items.name: Aaron Rodgers
items.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports league sources “don’t foresee” QB Aaron Rodgers playing again, barring an injury-driven emergency.
items.analysis: Rodgers cleared waivers Thursday and no immediate suitors emerged. The 42-year-old free agent QB torched what was left of his Steelers career earlier this week when he issued an ultimatum to Steelers HC Mike McCarthy, got benched, appeared on the Pat McAfee Show and was released. Plenty of teams are missing their starting quarterbacks, but Pelissero says it’ll take an injury-driven emergency for Rodgers to play again. At this point, no team is desperate enough to dance with the devil.

items.name: Bill Murray
items.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that Rams OG Bill Murray ruptured his Achilles tendon in the Rams’ Week 12 win over the Packers.
items.analysis: This is unfortunate. Murray, a backup, started at left guard and played well. He will now undergo surgery and begin rehab for the 2027 NFL season. The Rams’ offensive line is fairly banged up. Hopefully, the extra time off allows the unit to improve its health.

items.name: Brian Schottenheimer
items.headline: NFL on Prime’s James Palmer believes Brian Schottenheimer will remain the Cowboys’ head coach for the rest of the season.
items.analysis: Palmer’s report wasn’t entirely positive. He also believes that if the Cowboys’ performance does not improve, “there are going to be some decisions that Jerry Jones needs to make after the season.” It sounds like Schottenheimer may be coaching for his job for the rest of the year. Stay tuned.

items.name: Drew Lock
items.headline: Drew Lock (elbow) is not on the Seahawks’ final injury report for Week 12 against the 49ers.
items.analysis: Lock was limited again this week with tendinitis in his throwing arm’s elbow. With Sam Darnold (quad) back in action, Lock returns to his backup role.

items.name: Harold Fannin
items.headline: Harold Fannin (groin) is not on the Browns’ final injury report and will play in Week 12 against the Raiders.
items.analysis: Fannin upgraded to full participation on Thursday and remained at that level today. Fannin has dealt with this groin issue for a couple of weeks, but still posted a 7/91 receiving line last week. He is a locked-in TE1 against a soft Raiders defense.

items.name: Evan Engram
items.headline: Evan Engram didn’t catch either of his two targets in the Broncos’ Week 12 loss to the Steelers.
items.analysis: Engram was a complete non-factor, which is particularly disappointing after his six-catch, 74-yard effort in Week 11 against the Raiders. Unfortunately, this is much more inline with his previous production, and Engram can safely be ignored in Week 13 against the Dolphins.

items.name: Pat Freiermuth
items.headline: Pat Freiermuth caught his only target for one yard in the Steelers’ Week 12 win over the Broncos.
items.analysis: Freiermuth didn’t have his first target until the beginning of the fourth quarter. The 28-year-old was a consistent target of Aaron Rodgers, but he didn’t appear to have much of a rapport with Mason Rudolph in their first game together. Freiermuth can’t be trusted as more than a low-end TE2 for Week 13 against the Texans.

items.name: Pat Bryant
items.headline: Pat Bryant caught 4-of-7 targets for 42 yards in the Broncos’ Week 12 loss to the Steelers.
items.analysis: Bryant was able to make the most of an unfathomably bad day from Bo Nix, although it’s far from a fantasy stat line fantasy managers are clamoring for. Bryant has been one of the more consistent options for the Denver passing attack, but that’s not the compliment it should be. Bryant is at best a FLEX for Week 13 against the Dolphins.

items.name: Courtland Sutton
items.headline: Courtland Sutton caught 1-of-8 targets for four yards in the Broncos’ Week 12 loss to the Steelers.
items.analysis: To be fair to Sutton, Bo Nix was trying to get him the football. To be honest, he didn’t. Sutton was once among the better wideout options, but he’s been consistently putting up duds like this for too long in 2026 to count on him in fantasy. Even in a friendly matchup against the Dolphins in Week 13, fantasy managers should be looking elsewhere.

items.name: Rico Dowdle
items.headline: Rico Dowdle rushed 11 times for 71 yards in the Steelers’ Week 12 win over the Broncos while catching one pass for three yards.
items.analysis: Dowdle was the much more effective runner between he and Jaylen Warren, although the bulk of the yardage came on one 27-yard scoot. He also lost a fumble, but the Steelers still gave him some carries after that turnover. A solid yardage day, but fantasy managers shouldn’t expect similar production in Week 13 against the Texans.

items.name: Michael Pittman
items.headline: Michael Pittman caught 1-of-2 targets for seven yards in the Steelers’ Week 12 win over the Broncos.
items.analysis: Pittman was playing in his first game since Week 4, and he — and most of the Pittsburgh offense — didn’t have much chemistry with Mason Rudolph in a game where the Steelers’ defense was their best offense. The former Colt could be an option in the coming weeks, but shouldn’t be trusted in Week 13 against the Texans.

items.name: Jaylen Waddle
items.headline: Jaylen Waddle caught 5-of-8 targets for 53 yards in the Broncos’ Week 12 loss to the Steelers.
items.analysis: It’s far from one of Waddle’s best games of his career, but when you consider how atrocious Bo Nix was Friday, it’s considerably more impressive. He wasn’t able to get deep down the field, but he was without hyperbole the only relatively effective offensive option for the Broncos in Week 12. He’s a WR4 for the upcoming match against his former employer in the Dolphins in Week 13.

items.name: Germie Bernard
items.headline: Germie Bernard caught 1-of-2 targets for 58 yards in the Steelers’ Week 12 win over the Broncos.
items.analysis: Bernard set up the Steelers’ only offensive touchdown with his long connection with Mason Rudolph. That was his only contribution, however, as Pittsburgh relied heavily on the run game as they built a big lead and didn’t appear to have a ton of trust in Rudolph in the rainy weather. Bernard doesn’t have much fantasy upside for the remainder of the year, and that includes his Week 13 showdown against the Texans.

items.name: Jaylen Warren
items.headline: Jaylen Warren rushed 20 times for 46 yards in the Steelers’ Week 12 win over the Broncos.
items.analysis: Warren and Dowdle received all 31 rushing attempts as the Steelers relied heavily on the run game in Mason Rudolph’s first game as a starter. The 28-year-old tailback didn’t find much room, however, and this is back-to-back-to-back clunkers for Warren. He’ll try and get things going in Week 13 when Pittsburgh squares off against the Texans.

items.name: Jonah Coleman
items.headline: Jonah Coleman rushed 15 times for 26 yards in the Broncos’ Week 12 loss to the Steelers while adding eight catches for 46 yards.
items.analysis: Coleman was able to “save” his fantasy afternoon thanks to some checkdowns and screen passes, although outside of a 17-yard connection it was all for minimal yardage. The 23-year-old found zero room on the ground against the Steelers’ front seven, and plodding wouldn’t be an inaccurate description. Coleman has looked the part for most of the year and has a good chance to rebound in Week 13 against the lowly Dolphins, but this was ugly.

items.name: DK Metcalf
items.headline: DK Metcalf caught 3-of-4 targets for 36 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 12 win over the Broncos.
items.analysis: After being ejected from Week 11, Metcalf was able to find the end zone in his first game with Mason Rudolph as he won a one-on-one battle with Pat Surtain II on a 22-yard score. I

items.name: Bo Nix
items.headline: Bo Nix completed 22-of-40 passes for 169 yards with two interceptions in the Broncos’ 27-5, Week 12 loss to the Steelers.
items.analysis: Nix was atrocious in the first half and created two Pittsburgh touchdowns, one on a fumble returned for a score and one on an interception where it’s not clear who he was trying to throw the ball to. His third turnover was a desperation throw on 4th and forever in the middle of the final quarter. This was an ugly performance that showed Nix’s floor is among the lower of the quarterbacks fantasy managers would consider. He’ll be a QB2 for Week 13 in a matchup against the Dolphins.

items.name: Mason Rudolph
items.headline: Mason Rudolph completed 9-of-15 passes for 142 yards with a touchdown in the Steelers’ 27-5, Week 12 win over the Broncos.
items.analysis: Rudolph’s first start since the trainwreck that was the Aaron Rodgers dismissal was uneven, but it was better than the production Rodgers was giving the Steelers over the past few weeks. He found DK Metcalf for a touchdown on a solid throw that allowed Metcalf to take advantage of his size, and he kept the chains moving in the first half, for the most part. The second half was far less impressive, but good enough, especially with Bo Nix playing atrocious football. Rudolph will still be hard to trust as a fantasy option for Week 13 against the Texans.

items.name: Mike Evans
items.headline: Mike Evans (Achilles) is questionable to play in Week 12 against the Seahawks.
items.analysis: Evans sat out on Wednesday and practiced in a limited capacity on Thursday. We do not know today’s participation level, but he is clearly still rehabbing his Achilles tendinitis. Regardless, he is a high-end WR2 at worst whenever he is active. He will be catching passes thrown by capable backup Mac Jones against a tough Seahawks defense this week.

items.name: Mac Jones
items.headline: Mac Jones will start in Week 13 against the Seahawks.
items.analysis: Brock Purdy (ankle) has been ruled out, leaving Jones as the 49ers’ starter this week. Jones played very well in multiple starts last season, though he faces a tough Seahawks defense. Jones is a starter in two-quarterback leagues.

items.name: Brock Purdy
items.headline: 49ers ruled out Brock Purdy (ankle) for Week 12 against the Seahawks.
items.analysis: Mac Jones will start in Purdy’s stead. 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said Purdy is dealing with a mid-ankle sprain and that surgery is not necessary. The team is optimistic about his availability for Week 13 against the Giants. Jones piloted the offense efficiently last year and should be expected to do so again, albeit in a tough matchup this week.

items.name: David Njoku
items.headline: David Njoku (shoulder) is questionable for Week 12 against the Patriots.
items.analysis: Njoku’s potential absence would allow Charlie Kolar, and theoretically Oronde Gadsden, to play more, but neither tight end qualifies as a top-12 option in that scenario. Justin Herbert (concussion) is also out.

items.name: Keaton Mitchell
items.headline: Chargers ruled out Keaton Mitchell (knee) in Week 12 against the Patriots.
items.analysis: Losing Mitchell helpfully condenses the Chargers’ backfield for fantasy purposes, though the offense will suffer with Justin Herbert (concussion) sidelined. Omarion Hampton is a volume-based RB2. Kimani Vidal is an RB3/4.

items.name: Justin Herbert
items.headline: Chargers ruled out Justin Herbert (concussion) for Week 12 against the Patriots.
items.analysis: Chargers backup QB DJ Uiagalelei is expected to start in Herbert’s stead. He threw a touchdown pass when Herbert left early due to a hand injury a few weeks back, but he is tough to rely on as anything more than a volatile QB2. Hopefully, Herbert can return for Week 13 against the Buccaneers.

items.name: Jaxon Smith-Njigba
items.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba (ankle) is not on the Seahawks’ final injury report and will play in Week 12 against the 49ers.
items.analysis: The Seahawks have managed Smith-Njigba’s reps in practice all year, and this week was no different. He was limited on Wednesday and Thursday, but should be fine for Sunday. Smith-Njigba is an elite WR1, as always, and gets Sam Darnold (quad) back this week.

items.name: Sam Darnold
items.headline: Sam Darnold (quad) is not on the Seahawks’ final injury report and will play in Week 12 against the 49ers.
items.analysis: The Seahawks’ starting quarterback will make his return for a divisional showdown against the 49ers. Darnold has been fairly banged up this year, but hopefully the time off was good for him. He is a QB2 in Week 12.

items.name: Jackson Powers-Johnson
items.headline: Jackson Powers-Johnson (Achilles) will not play in Las Vegas’ Week 12 game against the Browns.
items.analysis: The instant rule-out and talk of a potentially serious injury has us believing Powers-Johnson will hit IR ahead of Sunday Night Football. Caleb Rogers and Trey Zuhn have played in Powers-Johnson’s absence this year and one of them will likely start against the Browns.

items.name: Raheim Sanders
items.headline: Raheim Sanders (hip) is questionable for Cleveland’s Week 12 game against the Raiders.
items.analysis: Todd Monken said he’s “hoping” to activate Sanders, who has only gotten in limited practices this week. He sounds truly questionable for Sunday Night Football. If active, Sanders will cut into Dylan Sampson’s backup workload a bit.

items.name: Rex Sunahara
items.headline: Browns signed LS Rex Sunahara to a four-year contract extension.
items.analysis: Sunahara, 30 years young, has been the Browns’ snapper of balls that go longer than the league average since 2024. He’s now inked through his age-34 season.

items.name: Abdul Carter
items.headline: Abdul Carter (calf/illness) is not on the Giants’ final injury report and will play in Week 12 against the Colts.
items.analysis: Carter is also no longer listed with an ankle injury, which is a good sign. Giants LB Arvell Reese (back) is also cleared to face a Colts offense now led by Anthony Richardson.

items.name: Isaiah Likely
items.headline: Isaiah Likely (groin) is not on the Giants’ final injury report for Week 12 against the Colts.
items.analysis: Likely injured his groin last Friday and caught one pass for 35 yards two days later. He was limited on Wednesday and Thursday before upgrading to full today, which is encouraging. Likely is a TE1 for Week 12 against the Colts.

items.name: Carlton Davis
items.headline: Carlton Davis (knee) won’t play in New England’s Week 12 game against the Chargers.
items.analysis: He didn’t practice at all this week and doesn’t seem especially close to playing at this point. Davis has not played since Week 9. The Patriots are having enough trouble struggling with the maximum number of IR-return slots that Drake Maye hasn’t been placed on IR either, so we won’t slag them for Davis not being there, but he doesn’t look close.

items.name: Jack Stoll
items.headline: Rams signed TE Jack Stoll off San Francisco’s practice squad.
items.analysis: With both Davis Allen and Tyler Higbee week-to-week, the Rams have brought in reinforcements behind Colby Parkinson and Max Klare. There’s no need to project Stoll to real fantasy work, but he could find some playing time if they continue to play 13-personnel sets.

items.name: Treylon Burks
items.headline: Treylon Burks (foot) is not on Washington’s final Week 12 injury report.
items.analysis: A rough Cardinals defense could get Burks into the deep league conversation, but he’s had just six targets in two games since returning from the bye week. If he doesn’t do something this week, Brandon Aiyuk might be knocking on the door of his starting spot come Week 13.

items.name: Jakobi Meyers
items.headline: Jakobi Meyers (ankle) is not on the Jaguars’ final injury report and will play in Week 12 against the Titans.
items.analysis: Meyers will expectedly function as the Jaguars’ No. 1 wide receiver with Parker Washington (shoulder) sidelined and considered week-to-week. Meyers accordingly vaults into the WR2/3 range and could deliver a big stat line against a soft Titans defense.

items.name: Rashod Bateman
items.headline: Rashod Bateman (groin) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 12 injury report.
items.analysis: You know what you’re getting into if you start Bateman, but he did manage a touchdown grab against the Panthers last week and the Ravens have generally pumped up their passing usage since Jacoby Brissett landed in Baltimore. He’s probably a bit below the FLEX line in standard leagues, but it wouldn’t shock us if he landed in that area this week against the Texans.

items.name: Bhayshul Tuten
items.headline: Jaguars ruled out Bhayshul Tuten (foot/ankle) for Week 12 against the Titans.
items.analysis: Chris Rodriguez should be added wherever he is available. Tuten will finally take a week off after playing through foot and ankle injuries for multiple weeks. He reportedly aggravated the issues in Week 11 against the Giants. Hopefully, Tuten will return for the Jaguars’ expectedly fantasy-friendly game against the Bears in Week 13.

items.name: Zay Flowers
items.headline: Zay Flowers (ankle) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 12 injury report.
items.analysis: He can be started as a low-end WR1 against a Texans outfit that has given up plenty of passing yards this year. Flowers has been a fixture on the injury report this year but hasn’t missed a game since Week 2.

items.name: Derrick Henry
items.headline: Derrick Henry (concussion) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 12 injury report.
items.analysis: He’ll get his normal workload, though he’s playing like more of a low-end RB1 or high-end RB2 since the Jacoby Brissett takeover, against the Texans.

items.name: Danielle Hunter
items.headline: Danielle Hunter (hamstring) will not play in Houston’s Week 12 game against the Ravens.
items.analysis: Hunter didn’t practice at any point this week. The hamstring injury has been described as short-term, but this is the third straight week he’ll miss with it. Perhaps he’ll have a chance to get back for Week 13.

items.name: Kayshon Boutte
items.headline: Kayshon Boutte (hip) will not play in Houston’s Week 12 game against the Ravens.
items.analysis: Boutte did not practice at any point this week and has essentially become a boom-bust FLEX threat at best on a limited snap count. He is likely questionable for Week 13 and can be dropped in shallow leagues.

items.name: Marvin Harrison
items.headline: Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) is not on Houston’s final Week 12 injury report.
items.analysis: With Kayshon Boutte out, it’s possible that Harrison could be Houston’s No. 3 wideout if they continue to manage things delicately with Tank Dell. He’ll be a tough FLEX play given his snap volume with the Texans even despite a nice matchup against the Ravens.

items.name: Brock Bowers
items.headline: Brock Bowers (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 12 against the Browns.
items.analysis: We can’t know for sure, but it looks like the Raiders might choose to hold Bowers out through their Week 13 bye. He was limited on Wednesday, and although he was limited again on Thursday, he practiced with his injured ankle heavily taped. Today, he sat out. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak tends to let his players take the field on game day, even if they are at less than 100 percent, but Bowers must be viewed as truly questionable at best. If active, he should be in fantasy football lineups. In the meantime, make a backup plan.

items.name: Jalen McMillan
items.headline: Jalen McMillan (knee/calf) was limited in Friday’s practice.
items.analysis: McMillan added the calf injury while trying to get off injured reserve with his knee, falling from a Thursday full session to a limited Friday. He’ll likely be questionable at best for Monday night.

items.name: Isaiah Williams
items.headline: Isaiah Williams (ribs) is not on New York’s final Week 12 injury report.
items.analysis: Williams got in two full sessions to close out the week and should have a decent role against the Dolphins with Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle/groin) sidelined. Still, we’d expect the Jets to try to ride their run game, so Williams isn’t a must-use FLEX play or anything like that.

items.name: Tee Higgins
items.headline: Tee Higgins (hamstring) is questionable to play in Week 12 against the Saints.
items.analysis: Higgins reportedly woke up with soreness in his hamstring today. He participated in the Bengals’ walkthrough, but left practice when team stretching began. He will be listed as a non-participant on the official injury report. Bengals coach Zac Taylor said Higgins should be fine for Sunday’s game. Higgins has a long history of hamstring strains, particularly in his left leg, and the Bengals have occasionally used him as a decoy when hurt in the past. That said, he is a very talented player, capable of producing efficiently even if used minimally. Higgins should be in fantasy football lineups if active.

items.name: Darren Waller
items.headline: Darren Waller (knee) was limited in Friday’s practice.
items.analysis: Waller now has back-to-back limited sessions. He has cobbled together four limited practices in a row and played through this injury last week. It’s possible he is held to 40 percent of the snaps again in Week 12 if we don’t see an upgrade on Friday, but with all three Panthers tight ends on the injury report, the whole situation will remain uncertain until Saturday. Mitchell Evans (Achilles) upgraded to a limited session after not practicing on Thursday, and Tommy Tremble (knee) also was limited for a second day in a row.

items.name: Tetairoa McMillan
items.headline: Tetairoa McMillan (foot) was limited in Friday’s practice.
items.analysis: McMillan was not spotted on Thursday, so this is a good sign for his chances of suiting up on Monday Night Football against the Buccaneers. Still, there’s a non-zero chance he winds up with a questionable tag on Saturday.

items.name: Taliese Fuaga
items.headline: Taliese Fuaga (knee) is questionable to play in Week 12 against the Bengals.
items.analysis: While Fuaga, the Saints’ right tackle, may or may not play, the team’s starting center, Erik McCoy (biceps), will make his return. Getting him back is good news for the Saints’ offense as a whole. Backup OT Asim Richards (knee) is also questionable.

items.name: Kyler Murray
items.headline: Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell said Kyler Murray will back up Kirk Cousins in Week 12.
items.analysis: Murray was removed from the injury report on Friday and will be active for the first time since suffering his hamstring strain. Carson Wentz will likely be an inactive third quarterback.

items.name: Noah Fant
items.headline: Noah Fant (calf) is questionable to play in Week 12 against the Bengals.
items.analysis: With Juwan Johnson (hamstring) sidelined, Fant had a chance to increase his role on Sunday. Getting hurt on Friday pretty much takes him off the TE2 radar. Jordyn Tyson could benefit as a go-to receiver in the short-to-intermediate area of the field.

items.name: Christian Darrisaw
items.headline: Christian Darrisaw (shoulder) will not play in Minnesota’s Week 12 game against the Falcons.
items.analysis: At no point did he practice after leaving Week 11’s game in Mexico City with the shoulder injury. Ryan Van Demark replaced Darrisaw in mop-up duty and would seem likely to start this week.

items.name: Jordan Addison
items.headline: Jordan Addison (thumb) will not play in Minnesota’s Week 12 game against the Falcons.
items.analysis: It’s his third straight absence. Kevin O’Connell seemed optimistic that Addison would have more of a shot to play this week, but he remains practiceless since suffering the thumb injury in a Friday practice ahead of Week 10.

items.name: Juwan Johnson
items.headline: Juwan Johnson (hamstring) will not play in New Orleans’ Week 12 game against the Bengals.
items.analysis: Perhaps this will give Kellen Moore an excuse to actually get Jordyn Tyson on the field this week. Noah Fant should also benefit from Johnson’s absence, and has a non-zero chance of a TE1 fantasy day given the Bengals strong track record of letting tight ends run wild under DC Al Golden.

items.name: Vega Ioane
items.headline: Ravens ruled out Vega Ioane (hand) for Week 12 against the Texans.
items.analysis: The Ravens’ stud rookie right guard has had unfortunate injury luck thus far. He was already playing through knee and shoulder injuries when he injured his hand in yesterday’s practice. Perhaps the time off will help the other two issues heal. The Ravens also ruled out DT Nnamdi Madubuike and S Jaylinn Hawkins.

items.name: Woody Marks
items.headline: Woody Marks cleared the NFL’s concussion protocol and will play in Week 12 against the Ravens.
items.analysis: Marks will return for No. 2 running back duties after a one-game absence. With zero teams on bye, Marks makes for a shaky FLEX option. He was unable to produce reliably while operating as the team’s starter, and should mostly be viewed as a bench stash at this time.

items.name: Brandon Aiyuk
items.headline: Commanders coach Dan Quinn said Brandon Aiyuk will not be elevated from the practice squad for Washington’s Week 12 game against the Cardinals.
items.analysis: No surprise or shame there — Aiyuk literally just signed on Wednesday. We are curious to see if he’ll be able to get active for Week 13, when the Commanders have a tasty matchup against the Jeffrey Simmons-less Titans.

items.name: Brock Bowers
items.headline: Brock Bowers (ankle) was not seen practicing on Friday.
items.analysis: Bowers was limited on Wednesday and Thursday. ESPN’s Ryan McFadden noted yesterday that Bowers’ right ankle was “heavily wrapped up” yesterday, which wasn’t the case on Wednesday. Hopefully, today’s absence during the portion of practice open to the media is only a precautionary, rest-related move. We should know more when the official injury report drops later. Stay tuned.

items.name: Jake Ferguson
items.headline: ESPN’s Todd Archer reports Jake Ferguson has partial tears in his MCL and PCL.
items.analysis: That explains why Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said Ferguson would likely be out “multiple weeks” after injuring his knee in Week 9 against the Colts. We haven’t had an official update in a while, but the Cowboys are on bye in Week 14. Perhaps a Week 15 return is possible.

items.name: Colston Loveland
items.headline: Bears announced Colston Loveland (knee) is “week to week.”
items.analysis: This was the same status they gave Caleb Williams ahead of him missing Weeks 3-5 with his hamstring injury, so fantasy managers should expect a multi-week absence even if this sprain isn’t something that will send him to injured reserve. Earlier reporting has focused on the idea that he could return before the end of the regular season. The Bears have a Friday game in Week 16 so if Loveland isn’t back for Week 15, it will be difficult to turn him around for that one.

items.name: Cole Holcomb
items.headline: Cole Holcomb (heel) will not play in the Steelers’ Week 12 game against the Broncos.
items.analysis: Holcomb was the only player listed as questionable entering the weekend, but the team has opted to sit him for this one after he suffered a heel injury in the previous week’s loss to the Eagles. In addition to Holcomb, the Steelers also declared WR Kaden Weten, QB Drew Allar, CB Sean Murphy-Bunting, RB Eli Heidenreich, LB Alex Highsmith, and DT Gabe Rubio inactive for this week. Will Howard will serve as the backup for starting QB Mason Rudolph.

items.name: Sam Ehlinger
items.headline: Broncos declared QB Sam Ehlinger, WR Lil’Jordan Humphrey S Taylor Rapp, OL Gavin Ortega, OL Kage Casey, and TE Dallen Bentley inactive for Week 12 against the Steelers.
items.analysis: The Broncos will be operating at close to full strength against the Steelers in a game that could feature some inclement weather and low temperatures. Rookie running back Jonah Coleman could be in line for a busy day, with J.K. Dobbins suspended by the team for this week. Coleman rushed 24 times for 111 yards and three touchdowns in last week’s win over the Raiders.

items.name: Zachariah Branch
items.headline: Zachariah Branch (hamstring) will not play in Atlanta’s Week 12 game against the Vikings.
items.analysis: Branch has now been sidelined each of the last four weeks, missing Week 9 and 10 before their Week 11 bye, and did not practice at any point this week. If only there were some sort of “injured reserve” list for players who weren’t close to playing.

items.name: Jahan Dotson
items.headline: Jahan Dotson (hamstring) won’t play in Atlanta’s Week 12 game against the Vikings.
items.analysis: Olmaide Zachcheaus will be Atlanta’s No. 2 receiver behind Drake London, and after that it turns to Chris Blair and Beaux Collins with Zachariah Branch also hurt. This will likely be a situation that forces the Falcons to condense the target tree and throw at their main three of Drake London, Bijan Robinson, and Kyle Pitts.

items.name: Denzel Boston
items.headline: Denzel Boston (quad) is questionable for the Browns’ Week 12 game against the Raiders.
items.analysis: According to Cabot, Boston was a DNP all week but still managed to draw the questionable tag. Given his week’s worth of DNPs, it’s hard to imagine the rookie suiting up on Sunday night, but it sounds like the Browns will give him some additional time to try and heal up before ruling him out. Fantasy managers planning to hold out until a decision is made would be wise to stash Jerry Jeudy or another player from Sunday or Monday night’s games as a pivot off Boston in the event he is ruled out.

items.name: Romeo Doubs
items.headline: Patriots coach Mike Vrabel said he “wouldn’t anticipate” Romeo Doubs (shoulder) being ready for action yet.
items.analysis: Doubs was ruled out when official designations come out. Most players on IR will get a questionable tag on their chances to return regardless of the surrounding data, so it’s not a great sign that Doubs couldn’t even muster that. He remains week-to-week and has little fantasy relevancy unless Drake Maye can muster a comeback.

items.name: Josh Cameron
items.headline: Jaguars coach Liam Coen said Parker Washington’s injury is “a big opportunity” for Josh Cameron.
items.analysis: You may have been thinking that Washington’s injury would create BTJ szn, but Coen singled out Cameron when asked about him, saying he’s “been trending. He’s made a lot of plays for this offense and for this team ... Trevor trusts him.” Cameron suddenly surfaces on the FLEX line as an expected Jaguars No. 2 target behind Jakobi Meyers against the Titans on Sunday.

items.name: Jeremiyah Love
items.headline: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said he had no update on Jeremiyah Love (ankle/IR) and would know more on Wednesday.
items.analysis: Love is eligible to come off injured reserve after this Sunday, but the fact that LaFleur won’t have a real update until Wednesday is probably foreshadowing that it will be at least another week. Love picked up a high-ankle sprain against the Cowboys in Week 8.

items.name: Carson Beck
items.headline: Carson Beck (back) will not play in Week 12 against the Commanders.
items.analysis: Beck will miss a second straight game with his back injury after missing all of practice this week. The rookie QB has dealt with back issues for the majority of the year, but will now set his sights on returning in Week 13 against the Eagles. That said, the Cardinals have a Week 14 bye, which could give them a reason to sideline Beck for at least one more week and let him heal up before returning for the final four games of the regular season.

items.name: Josh Johnson
items.headline: Josh Johnson will start for the Cardinals in Week 12 against the Commanders.
items.analysis: Johnson will get the start on Sunday against the Commanders in what will be a “revenge” game for the 40-year-old vet. Although, in fairness to Johnson, a lot of games are revenge games for the well-traveled vet. Things didn’t fare too well for Johnson in his first start of the season against the Chiefs, as he threw for 155 yards and one touchdown on the road, but did a good job of limiting turnovers. He’s nothing more than a QB3/desperation play in 2QB and superflex leagues.

items.name: Colston Loveland
items.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Colston Loveland (knee) is expected to land on injured reserve but “the current belief” is he could return later in the season.
items.analysis: The Bears are still running Loveland through additional testing and won’t make any final decisions to place him on IR until after those tests are complete, per Schefter. The early news of a sprained knee, however, is mostly good news for the second-year tight end. Loveland will be required to miss a minimum of four games on injured reserve and won’t be eligible to return until Week 18 at the earliest. Hopefully the final prognosis is as optimistic as things sound right now. That said, rookie Sam Roush looks to be in line for more work in the passing game after catching a season-high five passes for 31 yards in Thursday’s win over the Lions while leading all tight ends in routes run (35) and targets (5).

items.name: Tyler Higbee
items.headline: Rams TE Tyler Higbee is considered week-to-week with a chest injury he suffered in Week 12’s win over the Packers.
items.analysis: ESPN’s Adam Schefter was the first to report the news on Higbee. Higbee will reportedly have “a chance” to play in Week 13 against the Chiefs, but as Schefter reported, that decision will be based on “how he heals over the next week.” Where things stand right now, the Rams are currently down three tight ends, with Terrance Ferguson (ankle) out for the season and Davis Allen (ankle) also considered week-to-week after going down in Week 12. Colby Parkinson and Max Klare are expected to serve as the top two tight ends in Sean McVay’s 12-heavy personnel, but the team could look to add a free agent tight end or two in the days ahead.

items.name: Davis Allen
items.headline: Rams TE Davis Allen is considered week-to-week after suffering a high-ankle sprain in Week 12’s win over the Packers.
items.analysis: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport was the first to report the news. Allen will reportedly go to the Rams’ facilities today for a full evaluation to determine the approximate length of his absence, but with Terrance Ferguson (ankle) out for the season and Tyler Higbee (chest) also considered week-to-week, the Rams are suddenly very thin at tight end. Rookie second-rounder Max Klare and veteran Colby Parkinson are the only healthy tight ends currently on the roster, but it’s possible the Rams will look to add one or two more free agents to fill their needs at the position. It’s hard to imagine either Parkinson or Klare seeing enough of a role in the Rams’ passing game to become fantasy-viable players in the weeks ahead.

items.name: Omar Cooper
items.headline: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle/groin) will not play in Week 12 against the Dolphins.
items.analysis: With a Week 13 bye on tap for the Jets, the team is hoping two extra weeks of rest will be more than enough for Cooper to play in Week 14 against the Broncos. Cooper has not played since re-injuring his ankle in Week 10 against the Bills and has now missed six of a possible 12 games in his rookie season. It’s possible this is the last update we receive on Cooper until the Jets return from their bye week, but fantasy managers in need of help over the next two weeks can safely drop him where needed.

items.name: Bhayshul Tuten
items.headline: Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said he’s “not sure yet” if Bhayshul Tuten (foot/ankle) will play in Week 12 against the Titans.
items.analysis: Fantasy managers don’t need to panic just yet. The Jaguars have not taken the field for their Friday practice, and Coen said the team will assess how he looks on Friday before making any further decisions on his availability. Tuten has not practiced in either of the first two practices of the week, so a limited practice would be a slight upgrade for him heading into the weekend. We will check back in with a final update on his availability when the team announces it, but backup Chris Rodriguez could be in line for a busy week if Tuten were to be sidelined.

items.name: Parker Washington
items.headline: Parker Washington (shoulder) will not play in the Jaguars’ Week 12 game against the Titans.
items.analysis: According to head coach Liam Coen, Washington aggravated an AC joint injury in Thursday’s practice that will sideline him for at least one week. Speaking with the media on Friday, Coen said the team hopes to have him back “ASAP” but noted that it is a “week-to-week injury.” Jakobi Meyers could be first in line to benefit from Washington’s absence, but this certainly isn’t an ideal situation for fantasy managers with the fantasy playoffs just weeks away.

items.name: Dallas Goedert
items.headline: Dallas Goedert (shoulder) was spotted in a sling after the Eagles’ Week 12 win over the Cowboys.
items.analysis: Goedert exited Week 12’s win over the Cowboys with a shoulder injury on the first drive of the game. The veteran tight end did not return to the game, and the fact that he was wearing a sling after the game suggests this could be somewhat of a serious injury. Head coach Nick Sirianni did not comment on his injury after the game, so it’s possible we won’t learn until later next week what he’s dealing with and how much time he could miss, if any. Goedert has caught 33 passes for 355 yards and two touchdowns this season, with both of his scores coming in Week 1against the Commanders. Zach Ertz’s 39 offensive snaps and 19 routes run both led the Eagles’ tight end room on the day, and could point to him operating as Philly’s TE1 if Goedert were to miss any time.

items.name: Rashee Rice
items.headline: Rashee Rice caught 2-of-5 targets for 19 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 12 loss to the Bills.
items.analysis: Rice’s quiet day was made all the worse by the refs when they overturned his third catch to an incomplete pass after replay showed the ball hitting the ground. While the tip of the ball did touch the turf, the ball didn’t appear to move. While the controversial call eventually led to a Buffalo victory, calling it a catch would have changed little for fantasy managers. Rice has played five games since returning from his early-season hamstring injury. He had more than 53 yards in just one of them. Rice will get one final week in the WR2 ranks when the Chiefs take on the Rams next week. Another quiet performance will send him tumbling down the rankings.

items.name: Travis Kelce
items.headline: Travis Kelce caught 4-of-7 targets for 71 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 12 loss to the Bills.
items.analysis: Kelce was the only member of the Chiefs’ passing attack to find any success in this game. Being battered by the elements, Patrick Mahomes relied on his trusted tight end for a handful of big plays throughout the contest. One of them was a 21-yard toss to the nine-yard line at the end of the first half that set up a short field goal. Kelce, however, paid the price with a helmet to the back that left him on the ground in pain for a while. He ultimately played through the issue, though we expect to see him on the injury report next week. Kelce, unfortunately, did not go out on a high note, dropping a long pass that would have at least pushed the game into overtime. With a potential shootout on tap versus the Rams, Kelce will remain inside the top 12 fantasy tight ends next week.

items.name: Ty Johnson
items.headline: Ty Johnson caught both of his targets for 12 yards in the Bills’ Week 12 win over the Chiefs.
items.analysis: Johnson spiked for 55 yards on seven catches last week. That usage was nowhere to be found on Thanksgiving. It was a rain-soaked rock-fight of a game in which the Bills barely even tried to pass. Josh Allen threw the ball 21 times and only 10 were caught. The low volume axed any chance Johnson had of an encore. Facing a lowly Patriots team in Week 13, we don’t expect much work for Buffalo’s third-down back next week. Johnson will be buried in the RB5 ranks.

items.name: Khalil Shakir
items.headline: Khalil Shakir caught 3-of-6 targets for 33 yards in the Bills’ Week 12 win over the Chiefs.
items.analysis: Shakir led the Bills in targets, catches, and yards, but it was a memorable Thanksgiving for the worst kind of reason. Josh Allen tossed him a simple screen pass in the red zone late in the third quarter, but Shakir failed to corral the ball and bobbled it right into the hands of Chiefs corner Nohl Williams. The good news for Shakir is that the blunder didn’t land him in the doghouse. Allen’s very next attempt went to Shakir for a six-yard gain. Shakir has been a steady option out of the slot this year, but the spike weeks have been nonexistent. He has one touchdown and a single 100-yard game through 11 appearances. He will be stuck in the WR4 ranks when the Bills take on the Patriots next week.

items.name: Josh Downs
items.headline: Josh Downs caught 1-of-4 targets for 13 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 12 loss to the Bills.
items.analysis: This was by far Downs’ quietest game as a Chief, though his second half special teams play was rather loud. Downs made a pair of questionable decisions on fourth quarter punts, twice fielding the ball near the Chiefs’ own goal line. Neither gamble came close to working. The only good news was Downs did not cough the ball up. Downs’ snaps once again didn’t really kick up on offense, as he was on the field for just 16 plays. Perhaps that will finally, finally change in Week 13 against the Rams. For now, Downs is a boom/bust WR3 in fantasy football.

items.name: Xavier Worthy
items.headline: Xavier Worthy was held without a catch on three targets in the Chiefs’ Week 12 loss to the Bills.
items.analysis: It was a rainy, wind-swept night in Buffalo, but Patrick Mahomes still managed to have a decent evening. The same was not true for his former No. 2 receiver, who “zero balled” even as also-rans like Cyrus Allen and Jalen Royals caught passes. Held to just two catches in three games since Josh Downs’ Kansas City arrival, Worthy is turning into a tough hold even in 14-team leagues.

items.name: Dalton Kincaid
items.headline: Dalton Kincaid caught 2-of-2 targets for 13 yards in the Bills’ Week 12 win over the Chiefs.
items.analysis: Two catches looks bad until you realize Josh Allen completed only 10 throws in a rain-marred affair. It’s still sadly unsurprising Kincaid was one of the biggest victims of a run-heavy game environment. Rather amazingly, tonight was the fifth time in 10 2026 appearances Kincaid was held to three-or-fewer targets. He’s becoming more of a fringe TE1 than locked-in option, though the return of byes for Week 13 means he will probably still crack the top 12 against the Patriots.

items.name: Emmett Johnson
items.headline: Emmett Johnson rushed 17 times for 72 yards and a touchdown in the Chiefs’ Week 12 loss to the Bills, adding four catches for 24 yards.
items.analysis: Johnson made his third start in place of an injured Kenneth Walker this week. While the Bills did a far better job of bottling up the rookie than either of Johnson’s previous opponents, they still couldn’t shut him down entirely. After a quiet first half, Johnson punched in a goal line touchdown on the Chiefs’ opening drive of the third quarter. Johnson still managed 96 yards from scrimmage and what will almost certainly be another RB1 weekly finish, even with the Chiefs’ offense amounting to little in a torrential downpour. Walker practiced this week, but the Chiefs didn’t want to rush him back for a short turnaround to Thanksgiving. He now has seven days to get ready for the Chiefs’ Week 13 game against the Rams. We suspect he’ll be active, which will relegate Johnson to a change-of-pace role. Fantasy managers, however, won’t want to cut one of the league’s most valuable backups loose, even if his role is set to decline.

items.name: James Cook
items.headline: James Cook rushed 32 times for 117 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 12 win over the Chiefs.
items.analysis: Sportsbooks correctly cratered the total of this game throughout the week to account for gusting winds, pouring rain, and a chilly temperature. Joe Brady’s response to these miserable conditions was to feed his top back for all four quarters. Cook set a season-high in carries and scored his 10th straight rushing touchdown. Buffalo’s lead back didn’t score in Week 1 and has found the end zone in every subsequent game. Cook will be a good bet to find the end zone at least once when he takes on the downtrodden Patriots next week. Per usual, Cook will be a top-five fantasy option.

items.name: DJ Moore
items.headline: DJ Moore caught 2-of-6 targets for 15 yards in the Bills’ Week 12 win over the Chiefs.
items.analysis: On a rain-drenched, run-heavy night in Buffalo, Josh Allen completed only 10 passes. Translation, there wasn’t a whole lot for Moore to do even as he tied for the team lead in looks. That being said, volume has not been Moore’s strong suit this season, as he’s averaging just six targets. Although that number is skewed a bit by an injury-shortened Week 2, Moore hasn’t quite had the alpha role fantasy managers had in mind. He is still pacing as a solid option on the WR2/3 borderline, one whose best football could arguably still be ahead of him. The Patriots could go either way as a Week 13 road matchup.

items.name: Josh Allen
items.headline: Josh Allen completed 10-of-21 passes for 81 yards and two interceptions in the Bills’ 13-10, Week 12 win over the Chiefs, adding seven carries for 43 yards.
items.analysis: Playing in a cold downpour in Buffalo, it was a sloppy mess of a game for Allen, who posted his worst passing line of the year by every metric. The two interceptions, however, can’t be put entirely on him. The first was a tipped pass in the red zone that fell into the hands of a Chiefs defensive back. The second was a screen to Khalil Shakir, which was bobbled directly into the hands of Chiefs corner Nohl Williams. Even if you toss out the interceptions as bad luck, Week 12 was still the lowlight of his season and then some. The last time Allen completed fewer than half of his passes was Week 5 of the 2024 season. He averaged fewer than four yards per attempt for the first time since 2019. For fantasy purposes, Allen’s issues were compounded by a lack of volume, which has been a recurring theme for the Buffalo offense this year. While we aren’t expecting the team to air it out versus the struggling Patriots next week, Allen should at least be far more efficient in Week 13. He remains the QB1 overall with ease despite the Thanksgiving bust.

items.name: Patrick Mahomes
items.headline: Patrick Mahomes completed 16-of-29 passes for 174 yards in the Chiefs’ 13-10, Week 12 loss to the Bills.
items.analysis: Neither Mahomes nor Josh Allen was able to get much going in what was supposed to be the game of the season. With rain drenching the field and pelting players, there was simply no way for either team to consistently string together successful passes. The Chiefs also committed several special teams blunders, including but not limited to a botched snap and subsequent shank by punter Matt Araiza, a tipped punt, and yet another missed field goal by Harrison Butker. Not to be outdone, Mahomes bungled multiple snaps of his own. The elements and Buffalo’s resurgent defense combined to shut down Mahomes, who entered the week riding a two-game molten hot streak. The best he could do was avoid negative plays and live to fight another day. Mahomes was sacked just once and did not turn the ball over, though he had a close call in the fourth quarter with a throw-away gone awry. This game and its ugly conditions will ultimately go down as a write-off for fantasy managers who started either quarterback. Mahomes will get a QB1 redo in a week when he takes on the Rams.

items.name: Brian Schottenheimer
items.headline: Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said he is still confident in head coach Brian Schottenheimer.
items.analysis: Jones said he is not considering a head coaching change. This came just minutes after the Cowboys’ catastrophic meltdown against the Eagles on Thanksgiving. Dallas gave up 22 points in the fourth quarter and lost on a last-second field goal. Schottenheimer stripped DC Christian Parker of play-calling duties two weeks ago. The Cowboys gave up 79 points to Cam Ward and Joe Milton in senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine’s first two games calling plays on defense. Schottenheimer has had no issues getting points on the board, but his Cowboys have routinely found spectacular ways to snatch defeat from the jaws of victory. He is now 12-16-1 as the team’s head coach. He will need to turn things around in the final quarter of this season if he wants to keep his job beyond 2026.

items.name: Elijah Moore
items.headline: Elijah Moore caught 3-of-5 targets for 57 yards in the Eagles’ Week 12 win over the Cowboys.
items.analysis: Elijah Moore catching passes from Joe Milton makes a lot of sense on August 19, but is a little more surprising on Thanksgiving. Still, the 26-year-old was able to put together a solid day and helped set up the game-winning field goal with a couple of catches on the final drive. It’s hard to imagine Moore is fantasy relevant in Week 13 against the Cardinals, but he and Milton did appear to be on the same page.

items.name: Makai Lemon
items.headline: Makai Lemon caught 5-of-6 targets for 51 yards and a touchdown in the Eagles’ Week 12 win over the Cowboys.
items.analysis: Lemon was vastly improved from his disappointing one-catch against the Steelers the previous week. He brought in his first touchdown since Week 7 — also against the Cowboys — and it got the Eagles to within two points with just over two minutes left. The Eagles weren’t able to convert the two-point conversion, but still came up with the improbable victory. Lemon will try and build on this effort against the Cardinals in Week 13.

items.name: Will Shipley
items.headline: Will Shipley rushed 10 times for 46 yards in the Eagles’ Week 12 loss to the Cowboys.
items.analysis: Shipley took over after Saquon Barkley suffered a stinger, and while the Eagles were mostly in pass-mode because they fall behind 31-0, Shipley did a decent job in his limited touches. If Barkley can’t go in Week 13 against the Cardinals, Shipley is an interesting fill-in for that contest.

items.name: KaVontae Turpin
items.headline: KaVontae Turpin caught 1-of-3 targets for a 31-yard touchdown while adding a 10-yard rush in the Cowboys’ Week 12 win over the Eagles.
items.analysis: Turpin did most of the work on a dump-off from Dak Prescott. The 30-year-old remains an impact player on special teams, but despite the score, he offers very little fantasy upside for the remainder of the season. Or next season.

items.name: George Pickens
items.headline: George Pickens caught five-of-nine targets for 67 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 12 loss to the Eagles.
items.analysis: Pickens dropped what would have likely been a touchdown from Dak Prescott early in the game. He also had a catch that would have resulted in a first down, but after being hit hard, he went nine yards backwards and wasn’t given forward progress. After impressing the previous two weeks, this was a disappointing effort. He’ll get a chance to rebound in Week 13 against the Seahawks in a Monday Night Football showdown.

items.name: CeeDee Lamb
items.headline: CeeDee Lamb caught 7-of-11 targets for 134 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 12 loss to the Eagles.
items.analysis: Lamb also committed two pass interference penalties; one that wiped a touchdown off the board, although the Cowboys would end up scoring a few plays later. The 27-year-old was still able to fantasy day while going over 100 yards for the sixth time in the 2026 season. Lamb will remain a WR1 even with a tough matchup coming in Week 13 against the Seahawks.

items.name: DeVonta Smith
items.headline: DeVonta Smith caught 11-of-14 targets for 200 yards and two touchdowns in the Eagles’ Week 12 win over the Cowboys.
items.analysis: Smith was able to bring down an impressive 50-yard touchdown throw from Joe Milton to get the Eagles within two scores. He did the same on a 45-yarder a quarter later in what was easily his best game of the 2026 season. The hamstring issue that has limited Smith as of late did not appear to be an issue Thursday, and he appeared to have some quality chemistry with Milton. Smith is a WR2 on paper for a showdown in Week 13 against the Cardinals, but this effort shows the WR1 upside is palpable.

items.name: Javonte Williams
items.headline: Javonte Williams rushed 28 times for 101 yards and two touchdowns in the Cowboys’ Week 12 loss to the Eagles while adding three receptions for 22 yards and a receiving score.
items.analysis: Williams ran in for two scores in the first half, and then was able to just get into the end zone on a connection with Dak Prescott for his third score of the first half. The second-half was quiet for the tailback, but the damage was done while reaching 15 total scores on the season. Williams will be in the RB1 conversation, even with the sledding likely significantly tougher against the Seahawks in Week 13.

items.name: Joe Milton
items.headline: Joe Milton completed 21of-31 passes for 331 yards with three touchdowns and an interception in the Eagles’ 39-38, Week 12 win over the Cowboys while adding 15 yards and a touchdown on the ground.
items.analysis: Milton certainly isn’t boring. He even showed off some impressive touch at times, but the most impressive throw was a bomb that went 58 yards in the air for a score to DaVonta Smith. He nearly matched that dart with another 45-yarder to Smith in the third quarter as he lived up to the Bazooka Joe nickname. He even showed off some scrambling ability, particularly on a 15-yard scrambling into the end zone in the middle of the fourth quarter. The only real mistake was a forced throw with the Eagles down eight on the next possession, but he followed that up with a brilliant 24-yard throwing score to Makai Lemon. He made enough plays on the final drive to get the Eagles into field-goal range, and complete a three-touchdown comeback win. It was a vastly improved effort for Milton over the Week 11 contest versus the Steelers, albeit it against a significantly worse defense. Milton will likely get the start in Week 13 against the Cardinals, and offers a wide range of potential fantasy outcomes.

items.name: Dak Prescott
items.headline: Dak Prescott completed 19-of-27 passes for 291 yards and two touchdowns in the Cowboys’ 38-36, Week 12 win over the Eagles, adding 19 yards on the ground with a rushing score.
items.analysis: The NFC East is something, folks. Prescott had a big day even with a couple of long runs overturned due to penalty, and some “hidden yardage” due to pass interference that put the Cowboys into scoring position. He fired a pair of touchdowns to running backs in the first half and helped Dallas build a 28-10 lead going into the half. The Cowboys would blow that lead in spectacular fashion, and Prescott took a horrific sack to set up good field position before the game-winning field goal for Philadelphia. He will try and keep the good statistical run going in Week 13 against the Seahawks in a Monday Night Football matchup.

items.name: Kenneth Walker
items.headline: Chiefs declared RB Kenneth Walker, QB Garrett Nussmeier, CB Melvin Smith, DT Omarr Norman-Lott, T Diego Pounds, OL Jaylon Moore and DT Marcus Harris inactive for Week 13 against the Bills.
items.analysis: Walker will miss at least one more game while dealing with his groin strain, meaning Emmett Johnson should be the workhorse against the Buffalo defense. Nussmeier will be the emergency third quarterback.

items.name: Dalton Kincaid
items.headline: Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) is active for Week 12 against the Chiefs.
items.analysis: As expected, Kincaid will play after getting in a couple of limited practices ahead of the Thanksgiving showdown with the Chiefs. He should be treated as a lower-end TE1 for the contest. The Bills inactives versus Kansas City will be CB Christian Benford, WR Skyler Bell, S Jalon Kilgore, OLB Mike Danna, OT Jude Bowry and DL Greg Gaines.

items.name: Jahmyr Gibbs
items.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs rushed 21 times for 205 yards and three touchdowns in the Lions’ Week 12 loss to the Bears, adding five receptions for 47 yards.
items.analysis: Gibbs is the most valuable player in fantasy football, regardless of format. Since scoring twice from one yard out isn’t enough for him, Gibbs ripped off a clean 70-yard touchdown run on the Lions’ ninth drive — and that probably wasn’t his most impressive play. One drive earlier, Gibbs took a run to the right side, and multiple Bears defenders broke past the offensive line. One got a hand on him, but he changed direction and took off for a 32-yard gain down the sideline. The impending 2026 league-winner should be treated as the overall RB1 in Week 13 against the Falcons’ beatable run defense.

items.name: Sam LaPorta
items.headline: Sam LaPorta caught 4-of-5 targets for 44 yards and one touchdown in the Lions’ Week 12 loss to the Bears.
items.analysis: The Lions’ No. 1 tight end generated multiple double-digit gains today, including an 11-yard touchdown on a hitch-and-go just before halftime. He played through his ankle injury without issue after beginning the week limited in practice, notably diving to make a 17-yard catch. LaPorta is a TE1 against the Falcons next week.

items.name: Jameson Williams
items.headline: Jameson Williams caught 6-of-9 targets for 68 yards in the Lions’ Week 12 loss to the Bears, adding one rush for 12 yards.
items.analysis: The Lions got Williams involved on crossers, corners and screen passes today, but a few missed connections proved costly. Jared Goff targeted Williams in the end zone on the opening drive, but the pass fell incomplete. On the Lions’ fifth drive, Williams got behind the defense, but stumbled slightly, resulting in an overthrow instead of a long score. On the Lions’ 10th drive, Williams was unable to secure a third-down target at the Bears’ 25-yard line and accidentally tipped the pass to a Bears safety instead. That said, Williams deserves credit for generating a 39-yard gain on a corner route that helped set up Sam LaPorta’s touchdown just before halftime. Williams remains a volatile WR2 in Week 13 against the Jaguars.

items.name: Amon-Ra St. Brown
items.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown caught 7-of-10 targets for 146 yards in the Lions’ Week 12 loss to the Bears.
items.analysis: St. Brown shot out of the gates in this one, generating two explosive plays on the Lions’ opening drive. He needed a breather after being sandwiched between two Bears defenders on a deep completion on the Lions’ third drive. He played through a ribs issue a couple of weeks ago, and may reappear on the injury report with the same issue next week. Despite the hard hit, St. Brown stayed hot and continued ripping off long gains. A Bears defensive back committed pass interference against him on a target thrown to St. Brown right at the goal line. The ball fell incomplete, but the penalty setup one of Jahmyr Gibbs’ rushing touchdowns. St. Brown remains an elite WR1 against the Falcons in Week 13.

items.name: Dallas Goedert
items.headline: Dallas Goedert (shoulder) has been ruled out for the remainder of Week 12 against the Cowboys.
items.analysis: Goedert suffered a shoulder injury on the first drive of the game and was ruled out a quarter later. The 31-year-old will get a week-plus to get healthy for Week 13 against the Cardinals, but for now Zach Ertz and Johnny Mundt will be the uninspiring tight end options.

items.name: Jared Goff
items.headline: Jared Goff completed 25-of-36 passes for 313 yards, one touchdown and one interception in the Lions’ 35-39, Week 12 loss to the Bears, adding three rushes for 10 yards.
items.analysis: Goff’s first career Thanksgiving interception was not his fault. Jameson Williams tipped the pass right into Bears S Dillon Thieneman’s hands. Goff played very well on the day, and looked unstoppable whenever he targeted Amon-Ra St. Brown. Goff nearly tacked on a second passing touchdown on a trick-play pass to OL Larry Borom in the end zone, but the pass unfortunately fell incomplete. Goff remains a locked-in QB1 next week against the Falcons.

items.name: Salvon Ahmed
items.headline: Salvon Ahmed rushed three times for 50 yards in the Bears’ Week 12 win over the Lions, adding two receptions for 17 yards.
items.analysis: Ahmed provided the Bears with needed sparks on more than one occasion today, using his speed to initially rip off a 46-yard run on the Bears’ third drive. He later made a slick diving catch for a first down on the Bears’ 10th drive. He can be picked up in 14-team leagues at this time, though he is only a bench stash.

items.name: Kyle Monangai
items.headline: Kyle Monangai rushed eight times for 15 yards and two touchdowns in the Bears’ Week 12 win over the Lions, adding one reception for 14 yards.
items.analysis: Monangai ran inefficiently this week, but that did not stop him from bullying his way into the end zone for a pair of short touchdowns. The burly back may still be rounding into form after his lengthy turf toe-related absence, but he remains a featured player in the Bears’ elite offense. Monangai is an RB2/FLEX against the Jaguars next week.

items.name: D'Andre Swift
items.headline: D’Andre Swift rushed nine times for 65 yards and one touchdown in the Bears’ Week 12 win over the Lions, adding seven receptions for 97 yards.
items.analysis: Swift was extremely efficient on his touches against the Lions, which was good because the Bears got Kyle Monangai and Salvon Ahmed going in this one as well. Swift had two 30-plus-yard gains today. His first was a catch in the flats, which he took down the right sideline after juking two Lions defenders. The second was a clean touchdown run in which he faked right before cutting back to the left and outrunning the defense. He regularly operated as a needed checkdown option for Caleb Williams today. Swift is a borderline RB1/2 against the Jaguars next week.

items.name: Saquon Barkley
items.headline: Saquon Barkley is questionable to return in Week 12 against the Cowboys with a stinger.
items.analysis: Barkley has struggled with just seven yards on five attempts, and was seen grimacing on the sideline before exiting the contest. With Barkley unavailable, Will Shipley will likely see the majority of touches.

items.name: Caleb Williams
items.headline: Caleb WIlliams told reporters that he was “fine” after undergoing X-rays following the Week 12 win over the Lions.
items.analysis: Williams said that he thought there was just a bruise on his abdomen after taking a fall. The signal-caller will get a mini-bye before the Bears take on the Jaguars in Week 13, and should be good to go for that contest.

items.name: Denzel Boston
items.headline: Denzel Boston (quad) was listed as a non-participant for Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: That’s back-to-back missed practices for Boston. The 22-year-old still could be a go for Week 12 against the Raiders, but he’ll need to get in at least a limited session, and he doesn’t provide a ton of fantasy upside even if he does play for that matchup.

items.name: Dallas Goedert
items.headline: Dallas Goedert (shoulder) is questionable to return in Week 12 against the Cowboys.
items.analysis: Goedert was injured on the first drive of the game and headed to the locker room. Zack Ertz and Johnny Mundt will likely see the majority of the snaps if Goedert can’t return.

items.name: Zay Flowers
items.headline: Zay Flowers (ankle) was a full participant during Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: Flowers was limited Wednesday but was upgraded to a full-go a day later. He’ll be a WR2 for the showdown against the Texans in Week 12.

items.name: Brock Bowers
items.headline: Brock Bowers (ankle) was listed as a limited participant during Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: Bowers was also limited during Wednesday’s session. The team remains optimistic that their star tight end will play in Week 12 against the Browns, but fantasy managers should be prepared to turn to another option.

items.name: Jahdae Walker
items.headline: Jahdae Walker caught 0-of-1 targets in the Bears’ Week 12 win over the Lions.
items.analysis: Walker did not do himself any favors in this one. He got open on the Bears’ 10th drive, and Caleb Williams heaved a well-placed, desperate pass his way while evading pressure way downfield. Walker bobbled it, giving Lions S Kerby Joseph the chance to punch the ball out of his possession, resulting in a turnover on downs. Walker does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues.

items.name: Kalif Raymond
items.headline: Kalif Raymond caught 3-of-5 targets for 20 yards in the Bears’ Week 12 win over the Lions.
items.analysis: Raymond chipped in as needed in the Bears’ win. On his best play, he snagged a play-action pass and ran upfield for a first down on the Bears’ first drive. Raymond does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues.

items.name: Sam Roush
items.headline: Sam Roush caught 5-of-5 targets for 31 yards in the Bears’ Week 12 win over the Lions.
items.analysis: Roush’s role increased after Colston Loveland suffered a worrying knee injury early in the game. The rookie tight end showed off his physicality by running over a would-be tackler on an 11-yard gain on the Bears’ seventh drive. Backup TE Stephen Carlson caught 2-of-4 targets for 30 yards as well. Roush could be a TE1/2 against the Jaguars next week if Loveland is sidelined.

items.name: Luther Burden
items.headline: Luther Burden caught 3-of-7 targets for 44 yards in the Bears’ Week 12 win over the Lions.
items.analysis: Burden’s impact on the game was bigger than it was in the box score. He went in motion and helped block on the interior for Kyle Monangai’s first rushing touchdown. Aside from that, Burden generated a 25-yard gain on a slick post route and a 15-yard gain that helped set up Rome Odunze’s 41-yard score. Burden nearly hauled in a 46-yard pass on the Bears’ eighth drive, but Caleb Williams overthrew him. Burden was also flagged for offensive pass interference for what should have been considered justifiable handfighting. Burden took an end around for just one yard. Lions S Kerby Joseph delivered a helmet-to-helmet hit on the play, but was not flagged for it. Burden will be a WR2 against the Jaguars in Week 13.

items.name: Mike Evans
items.headline: Mike Evans (Achilles) was a limited participant during Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: Evans was a non-participant during Wednesday’s session, and seems very likely to be a solid option even against the tough Seahawks’ defense in Week 12. Jordan Watkins (groin) was listed as a non-participant for the Thanksgiving practice.

items.name: Tyler Badie
items.headline: Broncos activated Tyler Badie off injured reserve.
items.analysis: Badie is back after missing a month with his thumb ailment. He’ll get some touches behind Jonah Coleman during Friday’s contest against the Steelers.

items.name: Rome Odunze
items.headline: Rome Odunze caught 6-of-9 targets for 87 yards and two touchdowns in the Bears’ Week 12 win over the Lions.
items.analysis: Caleb Williams and Odunze nearly linked up for a 20-yard touchdown during the Bears’ sixth drive, but the pass was a little too far outside the end zone for Odunze to get his feet down. Williams began looking his way more and more as the game progressed, and things really kicked off partway through the fourth quarter, when Williams hit Odunze on consecutive plays for a 15-yard gain and a 41-yard touchdown. Williams went right back to him for the game-winning score, firing a dart to the Bears’ leaping wide receiver in the back-right corner of the end zone with nine seconds left in the game. Odunze is a WR3/FLEX against the Jaguars in Week 13.

items.name: Jaxon Smith-Njigba
items.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba (ankle) was limited during Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: That makes back-to-back limited sessions for JSN. The 24-year-old seems likely to go for the pivotal Week 12 matchup against the 49ers, but fantasy managers should pay a little closer attention to Friday’s report.

items.name: Sam Darnold
items.headline: Sam Darnold was listed as a full participant for Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: Darnold appears to be ready to go and will likely start Sunday’s Week 12 game against the 49ers. The question is how Darnold will play, as his 2026 season has been a mixed bag, at best. Drew Lock will be ready if Darnold struggles.

items.name: Aaron Rodgers
items.headline: Aaron Rodgers cleared waivers.
items.analysis: Rodgers is now officially a free agent. The quarterback could be a target of a team desperate for a quarterback who can contribute — it’s worth noting that Rodgers was not playing well prior to his blow-up —like the Patriots or the Ravens, but it’s just as feasible that this is the last time we’ve seen Rodgers on a football field.

items.name: Brock Purdy
items.headline: Brock Purdy (ankle) did not participate in Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: That makes back-to-back missed practices for Purdy. The 26-year-old is considered day-to-day with his ankle injury, but it’s at least a little concerning that Purdy hasn’t been able to practice this week. Fantasy managers should hope that he gets in at least a limited session Friday before the matchup against the Seahawks in Week 12.

items.name: Caleb Williams
items.headline: Caleb Williams completed 30-of-44 passes for 345 yards and two touchdowns in the Bears’ 39-35, Week 12 win over the Lions, adding three rushes for 15 yards.
items.analysis: The Bears trailed 24-35 when they got the ball back with a little over eight minutes remaining in the game. Williams then activated “Iceman” mode, linking up with Luther Burden and Rome Odunze (twice) for 71 yards, one passing touchdown and a successful QB keeper on the two-point conversion. A Lions interception and consecutive turnovers on downs for both teams resulted in the Bears getting the ball back with just over two minutes remaining in the game. Aided by a 15-yard facemask penalty on the Lions, Williams again led the offense down the field before firing a perfectly placed ball to Rome Odunze in the back-right corner of the end zone for a six-yard score, powering the Bears to a 39-35 fourth-quarter comeback. The Chicago Tribune’s Brad Biggs reports that although Williams participated in all post-game celebration activities, he was taken for an X-ray afterward. We await an update. Stay tuned.

items.name: Rashod Bateman
items.headline: Rashod Bateman (groin) was a full participant for Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: Bateman got a limited practice tag Wednesday, but appears to be just fine for the Week 12 matchup against the Texans. He’s still off the fantasy radar in the majority of formats for that contest.

items.name: Derrick Henry
items.headline: Derrick Henry (concussion) was listed as a full participant for Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: It’s excellent news for fantasy managers and for Henry, as he’s exited the concussion protocol. The 32-year-old should be ready to go for Week 12 against the Texans, assuming there are no setbacks.

items.name: Darren Waller
items.headline: Darren Waller (knee) was a limited participant in Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: Waller got in a limited session, as was Tommy Tremble with his own knee ailment. Mitchell Evans was not able to practice due to his Achilles injury, so the Carolina room could be in a bit of trouble for Week 12 against the Bucs.

items.name: Jonathon Brooks
items.headline: Jonathon Brooks (groin) practiced in full on Thursday.
items.analysis: Brooks has a chance to face the Buccaneers this week, though Panthers coach Dave Canales acknowledged earlier this week that it will be tough to find a spot on the roster for him, due to special teams needs. Brooks is only a bench stash at this point.

items.name: Tetairoa McMillan
items.headline: Tetairoa McMillan (foot) did not practice on Thursday.
items.analysis: McMillan was unable to participate in today’s walkthrough, which is a bad sign for his Week 12 availability. Jalen Coker would step into No. 1 wide receiver duties if McMillan cannot play this weekend against the Buccaneers.

items.name: Omar Cooper
items.headline: Omar Cooper (ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
items.analysis: Cooper is firmly on the wrong side of questionable for the Jets’ Week 12 game against the Dolphins. Isaiah Williams (ribs) is on track to return for No. 3 wide receiver duties, though only Garrett Wilson is reliable.

items.name: Isaiah Williams
items.headline: Isaiah Williams (ribs) practiced in full on Thursday.
items.analysis: Williams should be good to go for No. 3 wide receiver duties this week. The Jets’ wide receiver corps is a little too crowded for Williams to be a serious FLEX option against the Dolphins this week, though.

items.name: Carson Beck
items.headline: Carson Beck (back) did not practice on Thursday.
items.analysis: Beck is unlikely to recover in time to face the Commanders on Sunday. Journeyman in-season signee Josh Johnson will likely start. Johnson will be a low-end QB2 in this instance. The team brought back Kedon Slovis via waivers this week.

items.name: Romeo Doubs
items.headline: Romeo Doubs (shoulder) was limited on Thursday.
items.analysis: Doubs has a chance to return this week, in time to face the Chargers, but he is still in the questionable column. If he upgrades tomorrow, he should be good to go. Doubs would theoretically be the Patriots’ No. 1 wide receiver, but this situation is shaky. He can be stashed in 12-team leagues.

items.name: Bhayshul Tuten
items.headline: Bhayshul Tuten (foot/ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
items.analysis: Tuten aggravates his ankle and foot issues in Week 11 against the Giants. He has been playing through the ailments for multiple weeks, and still has a chance to face the Titans this week. He is an RB1 if active. Chris Rodriguez (hand) should be rostered just in case.

items.name: Jakobi Meyers
items.headline: Jakobi Meyers (ankle) was limited on Thursday.
items.analysis: Meyers has played through this injury for weeks now. We expect him to do the same against the Titans on Sunday. Parker Washington (shoulder) suffered an injury today. If Washington is inactive, Meyers would slide into the No. 1 wide receiver role. He should be added in 12-team leagues.

items.name: Parker Washington
items.headline: Parker Washington (shoulder) was added to the injury report as a limited participant on Thursday.
items.analysis: This suggests Washington injured his shoulder at today’s practice. Hopefully, it is only a mild issue and he suits up as planned in Week 12 against the Titans. He is a WR1 if active. Jakobi Meyers (ankle) would benefit if Washington sits out this week.

items.name: Jordan Addison
items.headline: Jordan Addison (thumb) did not practice on Thursday.
items.analysis: Addison seems unlikely to face the 49ers this week, though Myles Price (knee/ankle) has a chance to play, having logged two limited practices. Addison is still worth stashing as a potential FLEX option in 12-team leagues.

items.name: Jahan Dotson
items.headline: Jahan Dotson (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
items.analysis: Dotson does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues, nor does rookie Zachariah Branch (hamstring). The Falcons’ pass-catching corps is fairly condensed at this point.

items.name: Keaton Mitchell
items.headline: Keaton Mitchell (knee) did not practice on Thursday.
items.analysis: Mitchell and David Njoku (shoulder) remain sidelined through two practices. The tight end group is highly unlikely to produce reliably this week, even with Njoku sidelined. Mitchell’s likely absence gives Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal touch-count boosts.

items.name: Justin Herbert
items.headline: Justin Herbert (concussion) did not practice on Thursday.
items.analysis: Herbert is firmly on the wrong side of questionable at this time, likely leaving DJ Uiagalelei as the team’s starter against the Patriots this week. The Chargers also signed Jake Browning from the practice squad to the active roster, which bodes poorly for Herbert’s availability.

items.name: Quinyon Mitchell
items.headline: Quinyon Mitchell (hamstring) is active for Week 12 against the Cowboys.
items.analysis: The Eagles’ No. 1 cornerback is good to go this week. The Eagles declared EDGE Arnold Ebiketie, QB Cole Payton, CB Jonathan Jones, EDGE A.J. Epenesa, OT Ajani Cornelius and TE Grant Calcaterra inactive for Week 12 against the Cowboys. Payton is the emergency third quarterback.

items.name: Jake Ferguson
items.headline: Cowboys declared TE Jake Ferguson, RG Tyler Booker, WR Jonathan Mingo, S P.J. Locke, DT Jonathan Bullard and LB Jaishawn Barham inactive for Week 12 against the Eagles.
items.analysis: Ferguson will miss another game with knee and ankle injuries. Brevyn Spann-Ford is a touchdown-dependent fantasy TE2 in his stead. Ryan Flournoy will likely beneift from Ferguson’s absence. Losing Booker, the Cowboys’ starting right guard, for this one is unfortunate.

items.name: Juwan Johnson
items.headline: Saints coach Kellen Moore said Juwan Johnson (hamstring) is day-to-day.
items.analysis: Johnson was not seen practicing today, so we expect to see him listed as a non-participant on the Saints’ official injury report. He looks like a long shot for Week 12 against the Bengals. Noah Fant is a TE2 with Johnson sidelined.

items.name: Tyler Badie
items.headline: Tyler Badie (thumb) is questionable for Week 12 against the Steelers.
items.analysis: Badie could return from injured reserve this week. The Broncos need an RB2 with JK Dobbins suspended for one game, but Badie would not be worth rostering in 12-team leagues, even if he fills that role.

items.name: Nick Herbig
items.headline: Nick Herbig (hip/ribs) is not on the final injury report and will play in Week 12 against the Broncos.
items.analysis: Herbig is good to go. Steelers LB Alex Highsmith (ankle) and OG Gennings Dunker (knee) are ruled out. Steelers LB Cole Holcomb (heel) is questionable.

items.name: Ben Skowronek
items.headline: Steelers placed Ben Skowronek on injured reserve with a calf injury.
items.analysis: Skowronek leaves the active roster while Michael Pittman (foot) makes his return. The Steelers also signed Max Hurleman from the practice squad to the active roster.

items.name: Michael Pittman
items.headline: Steelers activated Michael Pittman (foot) from injured reserve.
items.analysis: Pittman is on track to play in Week 12 against the Broncos, catching passes thrown by Mason Rudolph. He is only a WR4/FLEX, given the circumstances. The Steelers’ offense might need a week or two to adjust to their new quarterback.

items.name: Colston Loveland
items.headline: Colston Loveland was ruled out in Week 12 against the Lions after suffering a knee injury.
items.analysis: This is concerning. A Lions defender tumbled into Loveland’s lower leg left while the Bears’ tight end was blocking on a run play. After a brief trip to the trainer’s table, he was taken to the locker room for further evaluation. It took only 15 minutes for the team to rule him out. Before exiting, Loveland caught 1-of-1 targets for five yards and lost one fumble. On his lone catch, a Lions defender tied up his legs while a second defender ran in and punched the ball out of his possession. Since they are playing on Thanksgiving, the Bears have a few extra rest days before their Week 13 game against the Jaguars.
