We should find out whether Loveland has a chance to play next week in the next day or so. Rookie TE Sam Roush is now the Bears’ top tight end.

items.name: Colston Loveland
items.headline: Colston Loveland was carted to the locker room in Week 12 against the Lions after suffering an apparent leg injury.
items.analysis: Loveland was tangled up, blocking against a Lions defender when another Lions defender tumbled into Loveland’s lower left leg in a classic roll-up mechanism. Both his ankle and knee could have been injured. Before getting onto the cart, Loveland sat on the trainer’s table with a towel over his head and appeared to be in considerable pain. We expect an update soon.

items.name: Aaron Rodgers
items.headline: Speaking with the Pittsburgh-Gazette’s Gerry Dulac, Steelers president Art Rooney II said Aaron Rodgers was not a “good teammate” following his release.
items.analysis: In a story published by Dulac on Thursday, Rooney said the Steelers are “100 percent” committed to head coach Mike McCarthy, while adding that “insubordination will not be tolerated” as far as Rodgers is concerned. According to Dulac, Rodgers and McCarthy met on Tuesday night, just hours before the QB’s benching, and presented McCarthy with an ultimatum: “let me call the plays or just release me.” What followed from there was Rodgers’ benching and eventual release after he went scorched earth on the Steelers and McCarthy on the Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday. Rodgers will be free to sign with any team when he inevitably clears waivers later in the day, but for now, no potential suitor has emerged for the soon-to-be retired QB, who has been among the least efficient in the league over the last few seasons.

items.name: Brock Purdy
items.headline: Speaking on NFL GameDay Morning, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said Brock Purdy is considered day-to-day with his ankle injury.
items.analysis: Purdy suffered a sprained ankle in the Niners’ Week 11 win over the Vikings and was a DNP on Wednesday. Rapoport reports the injury is thought to be “minor,” but noted that whether or not Purdy suits up for Week 12 against the Seahawks “remains to be seen.” Given the importance of the divisional matchup, it’s hard to imagine Purdy sitting at this point. We’ll see how his next two practices go to close out the week, but this doesn’t sound like something we need to be too concerned about just yet.

items.name: Kyler Gordon
items.headline: Bears declared QB Case Keenum, CB Kyler Gordon, CB Isaac Yiadom, CB Elijah Hicks, RB Roschon Johnson, OL Jordan McFadden, and DL Jayden Loving inactive for Week 12 against the Lions.
items.analysis: Gordon and Johnson were both ruled out before this one, but the Bears are at near full strength heading into Thursday’s Thanksgiving Day tilt against the Lions.

items.name: Ennis Rakestraw
items.headline: Lions declared CB Ennis Rakestraw, CB Keith Abney, S Chuck Clark, EDGE Tyrus Wheat, and EDGE DJ Wonnum inactive for Week 12 against the Bears.
items.analysis: Clark was questionable entering the week, but has officially been ruled out for Thursday’s game, putting Kerby Joseph in line to start. The Lions have most of their key players ready to go against the Bears as the two teams prepare to kick off this Thanksgiving Day.

items.name: Christian Watson
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Christian Watson has entered the league’s concussion protocol.
items.analysis: Watson exited in the second quarter of Wednesday’s game against the Rams after taking a helmet-to-helmet hit from Rams safety Kamren Kinchens. The hard hit left Watson on the ground for an extended period before he eventually got up on his own and went to the locker room. Watson was ruled out after halftime and now has to clear concussion protocol to play in Week 13’s game against the Saints. With extended time to clear protocol, Watson should have a decent chance of clearing protocol. We will be tracking his practice status throughout next week.

items.name: Colby Parkinson
items.headline: Colby Parkinson caught both targets for minus one yard in the Rams’ Week 12 win over the Packers.
items.analysis: Parkinson somehow lost a yard on two reception despite the team losing both Tyler Higbee and Davis Allen to injury, the latter of whom departed in the first half and the former of whom left at the beginning of the fourth quarter. The Rams completely controlled the flow of the game after Packers receiver Christian Watson departed with a concussion following a vicious targeting hit down the sideline just before the half, eventually leading to 47 total team carries to just 23 Matthew Stafford pass attempts. The Rams have some things to figure out given the sheer number of bodies missing after also losing two offensive linemen in the game. The long week hopefully affords them enough time to return to health ahead of a Week 13 meeting with the Chiefs.

items.name: Konata Mumpfield
items.headline: Konata Mumpfield caught 4-of-5 targets for 69 yards in the Rams’ Week 12 win over the Packers.
items.analysis: Mumpfield saw a team-high five targets and turned them into a team-leading 69 yards in one of the more dominant performances of the season. Despite the seemingly close score, the Rams jumped out to an early 13-3 lead while holding the Packers to only 44 total offensive plays run from scrimmage. The inability of the Packers to move the football resulted in additional time of possession for the Rams, which they used to notch 47 rush attempts to just 23 Matthew Stafford pass attempts, eight of which were directed at the backfield duo of Blake Corum and Kyren Williams. Mumpfield remains the player with the most weekly upside for as long as Davante Adams remains sidelined, of available pass catchers, a unit that took two more hits with the departures of tight ends Tyler Higbee and Davis Allen. Fantasy managers are likely better off leaving Mumpfield on the waiver wire or on their bench.

items.name: Kyren Williams
items.headline: Kyren Williams rushed 12 times for 46 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 12 win over the Packers, adding 19 yards on four receptions.
items.analysis: Williams now operates as the clear change of pace option and preferred back in passing situations, with recent reports pointing to consistent pain due to a turf toe injury likely the culprit in the shifting dynamics of the backfield in Los Angeles. Either way, Williams spent most of the second half on the sideline as Corum set career highs in attempts (32) and yards (184) while becoming the first back in the Sean McVay era to reach 30 carries. Given the nature of the injury, this could be the new norm for a Rams team that continues to push for a postseason bid following a 2-4 start to their 2026 season, leaving Williams a touchdown-driven RB3 for the time being.

items.name: Blake Corum
items.headline: Blake Corum rushed 32 times for 184 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 12 win over the Packers, adding 21 yards on two receptions.
items.analysis: The 184 yards on the ground easily set a new career high for the veteran back and his 32 carries marked the first time in the Sean McVay era where a single back ran the football 30 or more times, a mark that had not been reached since Todd Gurley over a decade ago. His trip to paint stretched his streak of touchdowns to five games while he also went over 100 yards for the second straight contest. The backfield split between Corum and Kyren Williams has taken a stark turn of late, with Corum now the preferred option on early downs and Kyren the preferred change of pace and clear passing situation back, a split that now leaves Corum the favorite for weekly production. He will remain an upside RB2 ahead of a Week 13 matchup against the Chiefs.

items.name: Matthew Stafford
items.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 16-of-23 passes for 140 yards and an interception in the Rams’ 26-13, Week 12 win over the Packers.
items.analysis: The two sides traded blows in the first half as the Packers came from behind to knot the game at 13 heading into the break, with Stafford leading three consecutive scoring drives to start the game for the first time this season. That was also the first time the Packers had allowed an opponent to score on three consecutive drives to start a game this season, but the departure of Christian Watson in the second quarter due to a concussion completely took the wind out of their sails in the second half. In total, the Rams attempted more runs than the Packers ran offensive plays (47 to 44), with this game marking the first game in the Sean McVay era in which a single back carried the football 30 or more times. It also marked the second consecutive game in which the Rams gained more than 200 yards on the ground, leaving Stafford with little volume as the reigning MVP failed to return a usable fantasy score for the fifth time this season while also failing to pass for a touchdown for the third time this season. The Rams saw two tight ends depart with injury as both Tyler Higbee and Davis Allen were unable to finish the game, potentially something to keep an eye on as the Rams prepare to face the Chiefs in Week 13, particularly in the absence of both Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. Stafford remains an upside QB2 in fantasy circles.

items.name: Tucker Kraft
items.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 3-of-5 targets for 24 yards in the Packers’ Week 12 loss to the Rams.
items.analysis: Kraft continues to look miles behind where he was during his breakout 2025 season before suffering a torn ACL, lacking burst out of routes while struggling through mental mistakes. Another such mistake appeared against the Rams when Kraft was stripped of the football in the first quarter following his longest reception in the game. The once-imposing Green Bay offense feel completely flat following the departure of Christian Watson in the second quarter due to a concussion, failing to score after the break while running just 44 total offensive plays. The Packers look to lick their wounds following back-to-back losses ahead of a Week 13 road meeting with the Saints, where Kraft will remain a frustrating TE2.

items.name: Matthew Golden
items.headline: Matthew Golden caught 1-of-5 targets for 39 yards in the Packers’ Week 12 loss to the Rams.
items.analysis: Golden found himself in lockdown coverage throughout, particularly following the departure of fellow receiver Christian Watson in the second quarter. The talented second-year receiver has seen double-digit targets in six of 11 games in his sophomore campaign and could be headed for another high-target game against the Saints in Week 13, pending Watson’s availability on a long week. Golden would be a legitimate WR1, should Watson miss, and an upside WR2, should Watson play.

items.name: Kaleb Johnson
items.headline: Kaleb Johnson rushed eight times for 13 yards in the Packers’ Week 12 loss to the Rams, adding 19 yards on one reception.
items.analysis: The Packers were completely unable to run the football effectively against the stout Los Angeles defensive front, running just 44 offensive plays as they struggled to get any offense going following the departure of Christian Watson due to a concussion. Lead back Josh Jacobs appeared close to suiting up coming out of their bye and could make his way back into the starting lineup on a long week ahead of a Week 13 meeting with the Saints.

items.name: Jordan Love
items.headline: Jordan Love completed 17-of-29 passes for 198 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions in the Packers’ 26-13, Week 12 loss to the Rams, adding seven yards on one carry.
items.analysis: it was the second consecutive game with three turnovers for the Packers as two second half interceptions thrown by Love were a microcosm of the team’s inability to hang with the Rams without their top option through the air. Christian Watson departed in the second quarter with a concussion after being knocked out on a vicious hit down the sideline, leaving the Packers in a hole they could not climb out of despite taking a tied game into the break. It is possible for Watson to clear concussion protocol in a long week of preparation, but Love could realistically be without his top option when the Packers travel to New Orleans to face the Saints in Week 13. In desperate need of a win following back-to-back losses to current playoff teams, the Packers head into the final two months of the regular season on the outside looking in at the NFC playoff picture.

items.name: Tyler Higbee
items.headline: Tyler Higbee (chest) was ruled out for the remainder of Week 12 against the Packers.
items.analysis: It is unknown when Higbee sustained the injury but he was shown walking to the locker room at the start of the fourth quarter, with the broadcast stating that he was ruled out for the remainder of the game. Higbee caught 1-of-3 targets for 14 yards prior to departing, with his absence of particular note considering fellow tight end Davis Allen was already ruled out in the second quarter with an ankle injury. Perhaps rookie Max Klare will see meaningful run in their absences.

items.name: Davis Allen
items.headline: Davis Allen (ankle) was ruled out for the remainder of Week 12 against the Packers.
items.analysis: Allen saw his ankle rolled up on in the first quarter, playing through the ailment to finish the drive before succumbing to the pain. He was ruled out at the half after catching both targets for 14 yards. Rookie Max Klare could see an uptick in opportunity in his absence.

items.name: Christian Watson
items.headline: Christian Watson (head) was taken to the locker room in the second quarter of Week 12 against the Rams.
items.analysis: Watson briefly departed the game after catching a pass on the first play from scrimmage, initially deemed questionable to return with a thigh injury. He would return without missing a play, catching a touchdown half way through the second quarter. Watson was then the target of a vicious hit down the sideline for which Kamren Kinchens was ejected from the game. He remained down on the field before walking to the locker room under hit own power. Watson caught all four targets for 65 yards and a touchdown prior to departing. Although no update has been passed from the team, it appears as if Watson will enter the league’s concussion protocol after appearing to be knocked out, making him worse than questionable to return.

items.name: Carlton Davis
items.headline: Carlton Davis (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
items.analysis: Davis has not played since Week 9, dealing with a knee injury. He stays sidelined coming out of the Patriots’ bye. Davis is trending in the wrong direction for Week 12 against the Chargers.

items.name: Romeo Doubs
items.headline: Romeo Doubs (shoulder) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
items.analysis: Doubs (shoulder) was listed as limited on the Patriots’ Wednesday practice report, indicating his 21-day practice window is now open for him to return from injured reserve. With A.J. Brown dealing with a hamstring issue, Doubs’ return will boost the wide receiver group, though a lack of Drake Maye will keep Doubs out of fantasy lineups when he returns.

items.name: Daiyan Henley
items.headline: Daiyan Henley (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
items.analysis: Henley missed Week 11 with a knee injury and continues to sit for the Chargers’ walk-through practice to open the week. Also missing the walk-through were DT Dalvin Tomlinson (knee), Tuli Tuipulotu (ankle), CB Tarheeb Still (ankle), EDGE Akheem Mesidor (ankle), S Kendall Williamson (calf), and DB Deane Leonard (groin). It’s hard to believe this many Chargers defenders will sit this week but the team released a practice report with 14 DNPs on Wednesday. We can expect a few of these players to return to practice later this week and play in Week 12 against the Patriots.

items.name: David Njoku
items.headline: David Njoku (shoulder) was held out of Wednesday’s practice.
items.analysis: Playing in his just his second game off I.R., Njoku suffered the upper-body injury against the Jets last Sunday. We already had practically nonexistent expectations for Njoku becoming TE2 relevant, but the new issue coupled with DJ Uiagalelei’s likely Week 12 start has him further from 12-team league lineups than ever.

items.name: Keaton Mitchell
items.headline: Keaton Mitchell (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
items.analysis: Mitchell was listed as a DNP for the Chargers’ Wednesday walk-through. He suffered the knee injury in the first half of the team’s Week 11 loss to the Jets, only playing on a kick return afterwards and exiting the game in the second half. Mitchell does not need to be in fantasy lineups, though a potential absence would further boost Omarion Hampton’s resurgence for Week 12 against the Patriots.

items.name: Quenton Nelson
items.headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Quenton Nelson (knee) and Abraham Lucas (ankle) are out for Week 12 against the 49ers.
items.analysis: Neither Nelson or Lucas practiced on Wednesday and Macdonald declared both offensive lineman out this week against the 49ers. The Seahawks will dig into their offensive line depth to deal with the 49ers pass rush this week.

items.name: Drew Lock
items.headline: Drew Lock (right elbow) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
items.analysis: Lock continues to deal with an elbow injury, getting in a limited session on Wednesday. Sam Darnold was practicing in full and already announced to start in Week 12, so Lock can go back to fantasy benches and be cut for other waiver wire adds or stashes.

items.name: Jaxon Smith-Njigba
items.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba (ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
items.analysis: Smith-Njigba was listed on the practice report with an ankle issue earlier this season, but has not missed a game. This is likely just load management for the 24-year-old receiver. Expect Smith-Njigba to still play in Week 12 against the 49ers.

items.name: Danielle Hunter
items.headline: Danielle Hunter (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday.
items.analysis: Hunter is dealing with a hamstring strain, missing the past two games for the Texans. He starts out this week not practicing and will need to practice in some capacity to have a shot at returning in Week 12 against the Ravens.

items.name: Kayshon Boutte
items.headline: Kayshon Boutte (hip) did not practice Wednesday.
items.analysis: Boutte popped up on the injury report with a hip issue and did not practice Wednesday. With Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) potentially returning this week, Boutte does not need to be on the fantasy radar for Week 12 against the Ravens.

items.name: Rashod Bateman
items.headline: Rashod Bateman (groin) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
items.analysis: Bateman was hobbled after taking a hard hit in the Ravens’ Week 11 loss to the Panthers. He pops up on the injury report with a groin issue to start the week, though he was still limited in practice. Bateman is hardly fantasy relevant at this point, but an absence would indicate more Ja’Kobi Lane targets for Week 12 against the Texans.

items.name: Zay Flowers
items.headline: Zay Flowers (ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
items.analysis: Flowers dealt with ankle issues earlier this season and now pops up on the injury report with a limited designation due to the ankle. He is still trending to play in Week 12, where he will operate as the Ravens’ WR1 for Jacoby Brissett against the Texans. Barring setbacks, the ankle should not limit Flowers too much as he sits in the fantasy WR2 rankings this week.

items.name: Ty Simpson
items.headline: Rams declared QB Ty Simpson, DE Larrell Murchison, OLB Darryl Peterson III, C Coleman Shelton, G Steve Avila, and OLB Desjuan Johnson inactive for Week 12 against the Packers.
items.analysis: Simpson will operate as the team’s emergency third quarterback. Avila and Shelton were declared out heading into the day, leaving the Rams offensive line short-handed against a Packers defensive line getting Micah Parsons back.

items.name: Micah Parsons
items.headline: Micah Parsons (knee) is active for Week 12 against the Rams.
items.analysis: Parsons is officially back after the Packers activated him off the PUP list this week. He is back nearly a year after suffering a torn ACL last season, making his debut on Thanksgiving eve against the Rams. The Packers pass rush gets a boost with the return of the five-time Pro Bowler this week.

items.name: Josh Jacobs
items.headline: Josh Jacobs (thumb) is inactive for Week 12 against the Rams.
items.analysis: Jacobs was limited in the Packers’ practices this week, but is not ready to return to play just yet. Kaleb Johnson and MarShawn Lloyd will split the backfield opportunities in his absence. The Packers also declared LB Zaire Franklin, OL Jager Burton, OL Donovan Jennings, and OL Mekhi Becton inactive for Week 12 against the Rams.

items.name: Kyren Williams
items.headline: NFL Insider Tom Pelissero reports Kyren Williams “has been battling turf toe for the past month.”
items.analysis: Williams was on the Rams’ injury report this week with a toe injury before getting cleared off the report before Wednesday. Pelissero reveals that Williams told him he has been battling turf toe for the past month. This stretch coincides with Blake Corum’s increased opportunities while Williams has seen his role reduced to more of a backfield split. Williams will continue to play through the injury, but expect Corum to still be heavily involved as a result.

items.name: Dalton Kincaid
items.headline: Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) is questionable for Week 12 against the Chiefs.
items.analysis: Kincaid was limited in practice all week but said he would most likely play. The Bills also listed Christian Benford (groin), T.J. Sanders (shoulder), O’Cyrus Torrence (ankle), and Dorian Williams (calf) as limited for Thursday night after a week of limited practices for each player.

items.name: Kyler Murray
items.headline: Kyler Murray (hamstring) was limited in Wednesday’s walk-through.
items.analysis: Murray was listed as a limited participant for the Vikings’ walk-through practice. Since going down with a hamstring injury, Murray’s starting role has been taken over by Kirk Cousins. Even if Murray is good to go for Week 12, he is likely to be in the backup role to Cousins against the Falcons.

items.name: Tai Felton
items.headline: Tai Felton (hip) was limited in Wednesday’s walk-through.
items.analysis: Felton pops up on the injury report with a limited listing as he deals with a hip injury. The second-year wide receiver saw a team-high 12 targets in Week 11 against the 49ers and has seen increased opportunities with Jordan Addison still dealing with a thumb injury. Also limited was Myles Price (knee/groin). Both Price and Felton offer limited deep-league upside with Addison out. Felton is the receiver to roster, if you must.

items.name: Christian Darrisaw
items.headline: Christian Darrisaw (shoulder) did not practice Wednesday.
items.analysis: Darrisaw seemingly re-injured his shoulder in the Vikings’ Week 11 loss to the 49ers. Minnesota just held a walk-through, but the franchise left tackle starts out not practicing. He is truly questionable ahead of Week 12 against the Falcons.

items.name: Jordan Addison
items.headline: Jordan Addison (thumb) did not practice Wednesday.
items.analysis: Addison has yet to practice since undergoing thumb surgery last week. Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell said Monday that the 24-year-old may not “necessarily” be back in Week 12 against the Falcons. Tai Felton will continue to get increased reps with Addison out.

items.name: Rachaad White
items.headline: Rachaad White (heel) is practicing in full for Week 12 against the Cardinals.
items.analysis: White dealt with this issue last week, but managed to be active on Monday night. He should be fine for backup duties in Week 1 2 against the Cardinals, though Jacory Croskey-Merritt is likely the only fantasy starter in this backfield.

items.name: Treylon Burks
items.headline: Treylon Burks (foot) was limited on Wednesday.
items.analysis: Burks continues to play through his foot injury, albeit mostly ineffectively. He is a boom-bust downfield wide receiver who faces a tremendously soft Cardinals pass defense this week. Burks does not need to be in 12-team lineups.

items.name: Jayden Daniels
items.headline: Jayden Daniels (left elbow/left hand) is practicing in full for Week 12 against the Cardinals.
items.analysis: Daniels’ left elbow issue is obviously not new, but the left hand injury is. That said, he is practicing in full and gets an exceptionally soft matchup against the Cardinals’ defense this week. Daniels is a high-end QB1, as usual.

items.name: Denzel Boston
items.headline: Denzel Boston (quad) did not practice on Wednesday.
items.analysis: Boston continues to rack up lower-body injuries, though he tends to play through them. He dealt with a toe injury last week, catching just one pass for 16 yards. His practice participation is worth tracking closely this week.

items.name: Harold Fannin
items.headline: Harold Fannin (groin) was limited on Wednesday.
items.analysis: Fannin has been dealing with this groin injury since Week 9, but it has not impacted his productivity. Fannin is a locked-in TE1 against the Raiders in Week 12. Ideally, he will upgrade to full participation by the end of the week.

items.name: Michael Mayer
items.headline: Michael Mayer (back) is practicing in full for Week 12 against the Browns.
items.analysis: Mayer injured his back in the Raiders’ Week 11 loss to the Broncos, but he is evidently good to go this week. Brock Bowers (ankle) was limited today, tentatively putting him on track to face the Browns this weekend.

items.name: Brock Bowers
items.headline: Brock Bowers (ankle) was limited on Wednesday.
items.analysis: Bowers closed last week with two limited sessions, listed with ankle and quad injuries. Fortunately, the quad injury is no longer an issue. He is tentatively on track to play in Week 12 against the Browns. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said he is optimistic that Bowers will play this weekend, adding that having a bye in Week 13 will not factor into whether Bowers suits up this week.

items.name: Jahan Dotson
items.headline: Jahan Dotson (hamstring) did not practice on Wednesday.
items.analysis: Dotson and Zachariah Branch (hamstring) both missed Wednesday’s practice. Dotson is not relevant in 12-team leagues, and Branch has earned just 12 targets this season. Neither player is consequential.

items.name: Mike McCarthy
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that coach Mike McCarthy “has the full support” of the Steelers’ organization and the team is “not planning to make any immediate changes.”
items.analysis: McCarthy can rest easy knowing that the organization fully backs him. Rapoport’s “immediate changes” phrasing does allow room for interpretation, though. Perhaps the team could move on in the offseason. Until then, McCarthy will roll with Mason Rudolph as his starting quarterback. They face the Broncos on Friday.

items.name: Carson Beck
items.headline: Carson Beck (back) did not practice on Wednesday.
items.analysis: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said Beck has been steadily improving since back spasms hit him late in Thursday’s practice. The team is taking it one day at a time with him. The team is preparing to start Josh Johnson in Week 12 against the Commanders this week.

items.name: Kedon Slovis
items.headline: Cardinals claimed QB Kedon Slovis off waivers.
items.analysis: The former Raven is now a Cardinal. He was notably on Arizona’s roster last summer. Slovis could end up taking live reps, pending Carson Beck’s (back) health and Josh Johnson’s performance, but he would only be a QB2/3 in that instance.

items.name: Avery Smith
items.headline: Chargers claimed CB Avery Smith off waivers.
items.analysis: The Chargers traded Smith to the Seahawks earlier this year. The Seahawks waived him on Tuesday. Whether Smith plays meaningful snaps remains to be seen, but he is familiar with the system.

items.name: Juwan Johnson
items.headline: Juwan Johnson (hamstring) was not seen practicing on Wednesday.
items.analysis: Johnson is unlikely to play in Week 12 against the Bengals at this point. The Saints’ No. 1 tight end injured his hamstring last week. Recovering in one week is a tall task for a player who needs to be able to stride while running routes.

items.name: Taliese Fuaga
items.headline: Taliese Fuaga (knee) was seen practicing on Wednesday.
items.analysis: Fuaga, the Saints’ right tackle, and C Erik McCoy (biceps) were both practicing on Wednesday. This is great news for the offense overall. Getting both players back would be helpful this week against the Bengals’ talented defensive line.

items.name: Jakobi Meyers
items.headline: Jakobi Meyers (ankle) was limited on Wednesday.
items.analysis: Meyers has been dealing with this ankle issue for weeks now, but it has not impacted his game-day availability. Meyers is FLEX-viable against a soft Titans pass defense in Week 12.

items.name: Carnell Tate
items.headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) is practicing in full for Week 12 against the Jaguars.
items.analysis: Tate returned from his multi-week absence last week, posting a 2/58/1 receiving line. He faces the Jaguars’ capable defense in Week 12, but his role and talent keep him in the WR3 tier. Tate looks like a classic rookie wide receiver set to produce late in the season.

items.name: Abdul Carter
items.headline: Abdul Carter (ankle/calf) did not practice on Wednesday.
items.analysis: Carter is firmly in the questionable camp for the Giants’ Week 12 game against the lowly Colts. Giants LB Arvell Reese (back) was limited at today’s practice. Hopefully, one or both of them are good to go this weekend.

items.name: Isaiah Williams
items.headline: Isaiah Williams (ribs) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
items.analysis: Williams missed last week with the rib issue. Omar Cooper was also out, allowing Sterling Shepard to take over the No. 3 receiver role. Shepard saw two targets and managed to get into the end zone on both of them. Cooper appears to be out again this week, but Williams is trending in the right direction. Needless to say, we can’t recommend Shepard (or Williams) in fantasy leagues this week.

items.name: Isaiah Likely
items.headline: Isaiah Likely (groin) was limited on Wednesday.
items.analysis: Likely injured his groin during practice last week and caught just one pass for 35 yards on Sunday against the Jaguars. His early-week participation is a good sign for his overall health. He will be in the TE1 ranks this week against the Colts.

items.name: D.J. Reed
items.headline: D.J. Reed (hip) is not on the final injury report and will play in Week 12 against the Bears.
items.analysis: Lions EDGE DJ Wonnum (back) and S Chuck Clark (hamstring) are both questionable to play on Thursday. The Lions’ defense was already a fantasy-friendly unit before losing Aidan Hutchinson (knee) for the year. Bears skill position players should be in fantasy football lineups this week.

items.name: Sam LaPorta
items.headline: Sam LaPorta (ankle) is not on the final injury report and will play in Week 12 against the Bears.
items.analysis: LaPorta began the week with a limited session before upgrading to full on Tuesday. The Lions’ No. 1 tight end should play a full complement of snaps in what will likely be a high-scoring game environment on Thursday. He should be in fantasy football lineups.

items.name: Michael Pittman
items.headline: Michael Pittman (foot) practiced in full on Wednesday.
items.analysis: Pittman is expected to return from injured reserve for Week 12 against the Broncos. Two full practices to open the week keep him on track to suit up on Friday. With Aaron Rodgers gone and the Steelers’ receiver room at full strength, Pittman will be a weak FLEX option if activated from IR.

items.name: Kobie Turner
items.headline: Rams activated DT Kobie Turner (groin) from injured reserve.
items.analysis: Turner missed a month while on IR because of the groin issue. He will be active tonight for a must-win game against the Packers. Turner made six starts this year. He has 22 combined tackles with two passbreakups.

items.name: De'Zhaun Stribling
items.headline: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said he thinks De’Zhaun Stribling (ankle) is “a couple of weeks away” from returning.
items.analysis: Exactly 10 weeks ago, it was reported that Stribling was expected to miss 10 weeks after undergoing surgery on his ankle. Unfortunately, it sounds like he needs more time to recover. ESPN’s Nick Wagoner believes Shanahan’s comments are in reference to Stribling “returning to practice, not necessarily playing.” Hopefully, Shanahan is actually referring to the latter timeframe. Regardless, Stribling should be stashed on fantasy football benches.

items.name: Jalen Thompson
items.headline: Cowboys activated S Jalen Thompson (hamstring) from injured reserve.
items.analysis: Running back Jashaun Corbin was elevated from the practice squad. He will back up Javonte Williams tomorrow against the Eagles. Thompson is back in the lineup after suffering a hamstring injury in Week 3. He will provide a small boost to a defense that will need an offseason overhaul to meaningfully improve.

items.name: Justin Herbert
items.headline: Justin Herbert (concussion) did not practice on Wednesday.
items.analysis: Herbert was placed in the NFL’s concussion protocol following the Chargers’ Week 11 loss to the Jets. He took eight hits and six sacks that day. Herbert is firmly in the questionable camp at this time. His backup, DJ Uiagalelei, would only be a low-end QB2 against the Patriots if he gets the start this weekend.

items.name: Tetairoa McMillan
items.headline: Panthers coach Dave Canales said he is optimistic that Tetairoa McMillan (foot) will play in Week 12 against the Bucs.
items.analysis: McMillan limped off the field in Week 11 with the foot issue but eventually returned to and finished the game. He did not practice today, though it’s not officially a DNP. The Panthers’ first practice of the week is tomorrow since they play on Monday, which will give McMillan an extra day to recover. Assuming all goes well in practice this week, McMillan will remain a fantasy WR2 for a must-win matchup with the Bucs.

items.name: Derrick Henry
items.headline: Ravens coach Jesse Minter said that Derrick Henry “had a couple of small symptoms” and is now in the NFL’s concussion protocol.
items.analysis: Minter adds that he expects Henry to play in Week 12 against the Texans. On Sunday, it was reported that Henry had cleared the concussion protocol after the Ravens’ Week 11 loss to the Panthers. Re-entering the concussion protocol mid-week seems like a bad sign. Justice Hill has played well in recent weeks and would presumably start in Henry’s stead if the burly back is unable to play. Hill is backed up by Rasheen Ali and rookie Adam Randall, the latter of whom could be worth adding in deep leagues. Henry was limited at practice today.

items.name: Aaron Rodgers
items.headline: The Pittsburgh Post-Gazette’s Gerry Dulac reports the Steelers are expected to release Aaron Rodgers.
items.analysis: The team announced his benching late Tuesday night. He then went on The Pat McAfee Show earlier today and burned every bridge in town by saying Mike McCarthy has been sleeping through meetings or missing them outright, among many other accusations. Per Dulac, the interview hastened Pittsburgh’s decision to get Rodgers off the roster. Once he clears waivers, Rodgers will be eligible to sign with another team. It’s unclear if any team will be interested in the Rodgers experience after how things ended in Pittsburgh, but a desperate playoff contender like the Patriots or Ravens could convince themselves of signing him.

items.name: Mike Evans
items.headline: Mike Evans (Achilles) did not practice on Wednesday.
items.analysis: This is almost certainly just load management for the superstar wide receiver. Evans returned ot action last week, posting a 6/109/1 receiving line. He should be viewed as a talent- and volume-based WR2 against the Seahawks’ top-tier defense. Jordan Watkins (groin) will also sit out on Wednesday.

items.name: Roschon Johnson
items.headline: Bears ruled out Roschon Johnson (ankle) for Week 12 against the Lions.
items.analysis: Johnson will be replaced by Salvon Ahmed as the Bears’ No. 3 running back. Ahmed does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats, with D’Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai splitting reps.

items.name: Kyler Gordon
items.headline: Bears ruled out Kyler Gordon (shoulder) for Week 12 against the Lions.
items.analysis: Bears No. 2 perimeter CB Tyrique Stevenson (groin) is questionable to play, which could mean that the Bears are without two of their top-three cornerbacks against the Lions’ elite offense. Tomorrow’s NFC North is looking like a fantasy-friendly environment.

items.name: Brock Purdy
items.headline: Brock Purdy (ankle) will not practice Wednesday.
items.analysis: Purdy sprained his ankle in the second quarter of his Week 11 win over the Vikings. He played through the issue but, according to Kyle Shanahan, is now considered day-to-day. With a NFC West bout versus Seattle on tap, we suspect Purdy will play in Week 12 despite the injury. On the other hand, Mac Jones was extremely successful under center last year, so the 49ers wouldn’t be in a terrible spot if they are forced to sit Purdy for a week. Between the injury and the nightmare matchup, Purdy will shuffle to the back of the QB1 ranks this week.

items.name: Colton McKivitz
items.headline: 49ers placed RT Colton McKivitz on injured reserve with an ankle injury.
items.analysis: This is extremely unfortunate. The 49ers’ talented right tackle is expected to miss the rest of the season after fracturing and dislocating his ankle. The 49ers remain an elite team, but McKivitz’s loss will likely be felt on the field from time to time. The 49ers also activated CB Nate Hobbs from injured reserve and re-signed WR Brandin Cooks to the practice squad.

items.name: Jake Ferguson
items.headline: Jake Ferguson (ankle/knee) will not play in Week 12 against the Eagles.
items.analysis: Ferguson failed to practice at any point this week and will miss his second straight game. Brevyn Spann-Ford will be the next man up versus Philly. He caught both of his targets for five yards and a touchdown last week. “BSF” will be a touchdown-or-bust TE2 for Week 12.

items.name: Aaron Rodgers
items.headline: Speaking on The Pat McAfee Show, Aaron Rodgers said he issued an ultimatum to Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy to give up play-calling duties.
items.analysis: Rodgers started off the conversation talking about McCarthy’s shortcomings this year, but he quickly shifted toward accusing McCarthy of being “unwell.” He mentioned several instances of McCarthy missing meetings while sleeping in his office or falling asleep during others. Rodgers also talked extensively about McCarthy failing to stay ahead on film sessions and even brought up a moment on the sidelines when McCarthy broke down the team at halftime with a “1, 2, 3, Packers”. Rodgers feigned concern for McCarthy’s health, though it felt rather disingenuous amidst his scorched-earth campaign. Rodgers told McAfee that he issued an ultimatum to the team to have McCarthy give up play-calling duties. That was seemingly the final straw. Notably, he also talked about being released by the Steelers, though it’s unclear if he has officially made that request. Either way, there’s no coming back from this. He has played his last snap in Pittsburgh. The fact that he’s going out on such a disastrous note means the Steelers won’t want to do him any favors by releasing him. He will likely be inactive and away from the team for the remainder of what Rodgers has said is his final year. If this is the end of his career, it’s a truly unbecoming and sad final chapter for one of the greatest to ever do it.

items.name: Woody Marks
items.headline: Woody Marks (concussion) resumed practicing on Wednesday.
items.analysis: Texans reporter Aaron Wilson later added that Marks is expected to return for the team’s Week 12 game against the Ravens. That said, he is unlikely to reliably return FLEX value playing behind David Montgomery. Marks was unable to be a fantasy football difference-maker even when he was operating as the Texans’ starter.

items.name: Marvin Harrison
items.headline: Marvin Harrison (hamstring) resumed practicing on Wednesday.
items.analysis: The Texans could get Harrison back in time for Sunday’s game against the Ravens. While his presence might help CJ Stroud, Harrison can only be viewed as a WR4/5, likely playing in a rotational role on the perimeter. Harrison does not need to be stashed in 12-team leagues at this time.

items.name: Sam Darnold
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Sam Darnold (oblique) is expected to start in Week 12 against the 49ers.
items.analysis: Speaking on The Pat McAfee Show, Schefter said Darnold is expected to practice in full today. He also noted that, as of right now, there’s no quarterback controversy in Seattle. On the other hand, he did mention that the idea of Drew Lock taking over will at least be a talking point if Darnold struggles. For now, it looks like Darnold is back in the QB2 mix for a must-win matchup with the 49ers. We should get confirmation on his health via the team’s injury report throughout the week.

items.name: Brandon Aiyuk
items.headline: Commanders signed Brandon Aiyuk, formerly of the 49ers, to the practice squad.
items.analysis: Aiyuk worked out for the Commanders earlier today and they didn’t let him leave the building without a deal. He’ll likely spend a week or two on the practice squad as he gets up to speed with the playbook before being elevated to the active roster. It’s anyone’s guess as to how much Aiyuk has left in the tank. He was struggling early in the 2024 season before suffering a season-ending ACL injury and hasn’t played a snap since. On the other hand, the Commanders need more firepower on offense with Terry McLaurin out for the season and Aiyuk played with Jayden Daniels at Arizona State. The floor is nonexistent, but Aiyuk is still worth adding in deeper fantasy formats.

items.name: Alec Pierce
items.headline: Colts coach Shane Steichen said Alec Pierce (Achilles) has not been ruled out for the season.
items.analysis: This contradicts a report from Ian Rapoport saying that the Colts have decided to shut him down. Pierce suffered a partially torn Achilles in Week 2. He underwent offseason surgery to address his heel/Achilles issues, but apparently it didn’t work. Now Pierce says he’s still hopeful to return later this year. The Colts have already thrown in the towel on the year, trading several big names and cutting Daniel Jones outright. There’s no reason to have Pierce try to play through the issue, so we’re still skeptical that he gets on the field again this year.

items.name: Denzel Boston
items.headline: Denzel Boston (toe) did not practice on Wednesday.
items.analysis: Boston was held out of the first two practices of Week 11 with the toe issue. He got in a limited session on Friday and played through a questionable tag on Sunday. It’s possible he gets a similar practice regimen this week. Even if he is active again, Boston will be a risky option for fantasy managers. He caught one pass for 16 yards last week and only earned two targets. It’s possible the toe issue is turning him into more of a decoy than a true downfield threat. KC Concepcion would be in line for more work if Boston can’t play at all this week.

items.name: Dallas Goedert
items.headline: Dallas Goedert (shin) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 12 against the Cowboys.
items.analysis: Goedert was upgraded to a full practice on Tuesday, meaning he was never at risk of missing tomorrow’s game. Coming off a one-catch bust against the Steelers, things get much better on Thanksgiving for the Eagles’ top tight end. Only four teams are allowing more passing yards per game than the Cowboys. Goedert will be on the TE1/2 border this week.

items.name: Brandon Aiyuk
items.headline: NFL agent Drew Rosenhaus said Brandon Aiyuk is having “ongoing and positive” conversations with the Commanders.
items.analysis: Rosenhaus conceded there would “probably” be “no decision today” about Aiyuk joining the Washington roster. That Aiyuk did not sign with the Commanders following Wednesday’s meeting could be bearish for his chances of playing in 2026 at all. Recently released by the 49ers after protracted contract disagreements, Aiyuk would likely start as a rotational player if he eventually signs with Washington.

items.name: Omar Cooper
items.headline: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) was held out of Wednesday’s practice.
items.analysis: It is obviously a poor start to Cooper’s week after he missed Week 11, though coach Aaron Glenn claimed his rookie wideout was “day to day.” That might actually be true, but with the Jets’ season once again lost, we doubt the No. 30 overall pick will be rushed back for a matchup with the lowly Dolphins. Were Cooper to somehow suit up, he would be more of a WR4 than WR3.

items.name: DeVonta Smith
items.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) practiced in full Wednesday.
items.analysis: Smith last week dominated air yards and targets in the Eagles offense in his first game back from a two-month hamstring injury. He should be locked into lineups for Thursday’s matchup against the Cowboys. Dallas has allowed the fourth highest EPA per target to wide receivers on the season. Only five defenses allow more expected fantasy points per game to the position.

items.name: Saquon Barkley
items.headline: Saquon Barkley (neck, illness) practiced in full Wednesday.
items.analysis: Barkley is good to go for Thanksgiving Day against the Cowboys. He left last week’s win over the Steelers with a stinger in the second half but seems OK a few days later. On Thursday he’ll face off against a Dallas defense allowing the second highest rate of fantasy points per touch to running backs, along with the league’s highest rush yards over expected per attempt. Barkley should be considered a locked-in top-12 option.

items.name: Bhayshul Tuten
items.headline: The Florida Times-Union’s Demetrius Harvey reports Bhayshul Tuten (ankle) was not seen at practice Wednesday.
items.analysis: Tuten was banged up last week against the Giants and clearly playing through considerable discomfort. That he hasn’t practiced much over the past couple weeks means Tuten could sit out a couple days of practice this week and still suit up for Week 12 against the Titans. The Jaguars would do well to rest their lead back in a game they should win comfortably. Chris Rodriguez, who bests Tuten in rushing success rate, rush yards over expected per attempt, and EPA per rush, would be in line for a big workload if Tuten is held out in Week 12.

items.name: Kenneth Walker
items.headline: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports Ken Walker (groin) is out for Week 12 against the Bills.
items.analysis: Walker was always going to be a long shot to suit up for KC’s Thanksgiving night game against Buffalo. This will be the third straight game in which Walker has been sidelined, leaving Emmett Johnson as the team’s workhorse back for at least one more week. Johnson over the past two weeks is fourth in rush yards, ninth in explosive run rate, 14th in rush yards over expected per attempt, and fourth in missed tackles forced per attempt. In other words, he’s good. Johnson will be a top-10 option against the Bills.

items.name: Caden Curry
items.headline: Colts DE Caden Curry (wrist) is out for the season.
items.analysis: Curry suffered the injury last week and will be sidelined for the rest of the season. His absence will be yet another blow for a crumbling Colts defense that has been bludgeoned over the past few weeks through the air and on the ground. Curry had 14 tackles and one tackle for loss over 11 games.

items.name: Jalen McMillan
items.headline: Bucs opened the 21-day practice window for Jalen McMillan (knee).
items.analysis: McMillan has been on injured reserve since late September with a PCL injury. His practice window opening today could mean McMillan will suit up in Week 12 against the Panthers. He would not be a fantasy option for now in a run-first Tampa offense with several wideouts ahead of McMillan in the pass-catching pecking order.

items.name: Josh Allen
items.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler said he expected the Bills offense to be “more complex” in Week 12 against the Chiefs.
items.analysis: Fowler suggested the Bills kept the game plan as simple as possible last week against the inferior Dolphins, with Josh Allen throwing 45 passes from the pocket and failing to log a single rushing attempt after averaging 7.1 rushes per game coming into Week 11. Fowler said the Bills might have wanted to hide offensive wrinkles ahead of their Thanksgiving night matchup against Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs. The Bills-Chiefs game offers a good fantasy environment and should feature plenty of scoring, though the KC defense allows the second lowest rate of fantasy points per drop back on the season.

items.name: Aaron Rodgers
items.headline: The Athletic’s Mike DeFabo said it “sounds like” the benching of Aaron Rodgers in favor of Mason Rudolph was “not a popular decision in the locker room.”
items.analysis: Rodgers was reportedly excused from meetings at the team facility on Wednesday, two days ahead of the Steelers’ Week 12 game against Denver. Rodgers’ benching comes after a series of down games and a proposed change from Rodgers about how plays are communicated to him during the game. Rudolph could be a slight upgrade for Pittsburgh pass catchers and should be rostered in supeflex formats for now.

items.name: Aaron Rodgers
items.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Aaron Rodgers was excused from a Wednesday morning meeting.
items.analysis: Schefter said the veteran was excused from showing up Wednesday morning so he could “process” being benched in favor of Mason Rudolph for Week 12 against the Broncos. That seems fair. Whatever happens from here, Rodgers has certainly taken his last snap as a Steeler. Rudolph, meanwhile, should be rostered in all superflex leagues for now.

items.name: Aaron Rodgers
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy made the decision to bench Aaron Rodgers.
items.analysis: Rapoport said McCarthy’s decision came after extensive meetings with coaches, players, and Rodgers himself following the Steelers’ Week 11 loss to the Joe Milton-led Eagles. Mason Rudolph is slated to get the start in Week 12 against the Broncos. NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo said the team was set to make a change in play calling, with QB coach Tom Arth relaying plays to Rodgers on game days “at the behest of Rodgers.” Hours later, the 42-year-old veteran was benched. Rodgers had reverted to his 2025 form in the weeks before the benching, ranking 23rd in EPA per drop back and 25th in drop back success rate from Week 8-11. The reuniting of McCarthy and Rodgers in Pittsburgh was always a bit odd considering their falling out in Green Bay. It’s unlikely Rodgers will be on the Steelers roster for much longer now that he has been pulled.

items.name: Mason Rudolph
items.headline: The Steelers have named Mason Rudolph their starter for Week 12 against the Broncos.
items.analysis: The news of Aaron Rodgers’ benching and Rudolph’s sudden promotion came in an 11:10 PM ET Tuesday evening press release. Normal stuff. While we wait for the next shoe to drop on the “Rodgers situation,” we can begin evaluating the “Rudolph development.” In short: Not much will change, though Rodgers’ recent immobility and subsequent inaccuracy had reached a boiling point. Rudolph will oversee an attack that figures to make a sudden swerve to the run, though the 31-year-old with 742 career pass attempts should be able to keep a wideout or two afloat in deeper fantasy leagues. The problem will be figuring out who, as DK Metcalf is having a poor season, Roman Wilson has just returned from injury, and Michael Pittman Jr. will soon join him. Rookie Germie Bernard has been coming in and out of fantasy usefulness, and Pat Freiermuth has caught some passes from Rudolph in the past. In the short term, Rudolph is not a Week 12 streaming option, and only Metcalf can be considered 12-team league viable as we wait to see how things shake out. It is possible, if not likely, the team eventually turns to second-year pro Will Howard or rookie Drew Allar for a late-season evaluation period.

items.name: Aaron Rodgers
items.headline: The Steelers they have announced they are benching Aaron Rodgers, with Mason Rudolph named the starter for Week 12 against the Broncos.
items.analysis: 42-year-old Rodgers’ play had taken a sudden, dramatic turn for the worst of late, but it’s still a stunning announcement, especially since it came via a terse team statement. It also comes one day after coach Mike McCarthy claimed he was not considering turning to one of his myriad other QB options (the team also has second-year pro Will Howard and rookie Drew Allar on the 53-man roster). Other information is scarce, except for the statement including Rodgers would be inactive for the Friday afternoon contest. With the Steelers playing on a short week, they are already issuing injury reports, and Rodgers was not on Tuesday’s edition. It would appear, rather unsurprisingly, the sides have simply soured of each other, an outcome that perhaps became inevitable following Rodgers’ recent downturn. Startlingly immobile, almost anyone would be an upgrade on Rodgers at this point, but Rudolph is really going to push the “almost anyone” framing. Needless to say, this is not an offense we are looking toward for Week 12 fantasy production. The next order of business could be Rodgers’ release. Stay tuned.

Needless to say, this is not an offense we are looking toward for Week 12 fantasy production. The next order of business could be Rodgers’ release. Stay tuned.

items.name: Bryce Young
items.headline: NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe reports there have “not been a lot of talks about an extension in-season” for Bryce Young.
items.analysis: Wolfe adds that Young and the Panthers are “on the same page for an offseason contract.” Young started out strong this season before a three-turnover loss to the Buccaneers in Week 7. The Panthers are still in first place atop the NFC South with a 5-5 record and a second bout with the Bucs on the horizon for Week 12. Young’s extension chances were highly reliant on his play this season but the Panthers need to see more before committing to the 25-year-old quarterback. With a 19-35 record and 67 passing touchdowns to 37 interceptions throughout his career thus far, Young’s performance the rest of this year will determine the status of a contract extension. If the Panthers choose to extend him, it will come in the offseason.

items.name: Alex Highsmith
items.headline: Alex Highsmith (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
items.analysis: Highsmith suffered an ankle injury in Week 11 and starts out the week not practicing. He was wearing an ankle brace in the team facility on Tuesday and head coach Mike McCarthy said it will be “tough” for Highsmith to play in a shortened Week 12 where the Steelers play the Broncos on Friday. Highsmith is trending in the wrong direction this week, but his ankle issue does not seem to be a major injury.

items.name: Quinyon Mitchell
items.headline: Quinyon Mitchell (hamstring) was limited in Tuesday’s practice.
items.analysis: Eagles DC Vic Fangio said today he believed Mitchell would be able to go, and it seems like he’s trending in the right direction after hitting the practice field today. It would certainly help anyone facing CeeDee Lamb or George Pickens this week if Mitchell were able to go.

items.name: Dallas Goedert
items.headline: Dallas Goedert (shin) practiced in full on Tuesday.
items.analysis: That makes us feel pretty confident that he’ll suit up for Thanksgiving’s game against the Cowboys after a limited session on Monday. The Eagles’ passing game is in pretty rough shape with Joe Milton under center, but Dallas’ issues invite a TE1-capable game script for Goedert if the Eagles can take advantage of it.

items.name: Will Shipley
items.headline: Will Shipley (foot/illness) was limited in Tuesday’s practice.
items.analysis: With the news that Saquon Barkley is practicing in full, Shipley’s waiver wire appeal has downgraded drastically. He’s a reasonable stash and little more at this point in 12-team leagues.

items.name: Saquon Barkley
items.headline: Saquon Barkley (neck/illness) practiced in full on Tuesday.
items.analysis: It’s an upgrade over his limited session on Monday. Barkley told reporters after Sunday’s game that he doesn’t think he’ll ever get to 100 percent again for the rest of the season, saying “That’s not how football works.” But it seems like he’s at least “football healthy” enough to go against the Cowboys on Thanksgiving.

items.name: Pat Bryant
items.headline: Pat Bryant (ankle) is practicing in full for Denver’s Week 12 game against the Steelers.
items.analysis: Bryant survived an injury scare on Sunday and this confirms that he should be in a good place to play on Friday. He took over as Denver’s No. 2 receiver against the Raiders, out-targeting Courtland Sutton 4-2, but wasn’t able to make much fantasy hay of the increased workload. Pittsburgh should be another game that mostly sees Bryant as a FLEX play at best.

items.name: Brandon Aiyuk
items.headline: Free agent WR Brandon Aiyuk will visit the Commanders on Wednesday.
items.analysis: Aiyuk’s last two days have gone pretty much exactly how you would have expected after the 49ers finally released him. He’ll likely sign with the Commanders practice squad officially tomorrow.

items.name: Tyler Badie
items.headline: Broncos designated Tyler Badie (thumb) to return from injured reserve.
items.analysis: His 21-day window opens with a full practice. Seems like perhaps J.K. Dobbins’ suspension has accelerated the timeline on this decision, so Badie may have a chance to be activated for Friday’s game against the Steelers.

items.name: Roschon Johnson
items.headline: Roschon Johnson (ankle) did not practice on Tuesday.
items.analysis: We wouldn’t be surprised if he was an IR candidate after he was carted off during Week 11’s win over the Saints. Salvon Ahmed will likely take over third-string duties for the Bears.

items.name: Sam LaPorta
items.headline: Sam LaPorta (ankle) practiced in full on Tuesday.
items.analysis: LaPorta profiles as a TE1 option in a game with a juicy 55.5 over/under on Thanksgiving. This full session should assure that he skips the questionable line and proceeds directly to a fun game script in the early window.

items.name: Christian Benford
items.headline: Christian Benford (groin) was limited in Tuesday’s practice.
items.analysis: It’s his first practice since suffering the groin injury in Week 10. We had a feeling the Bills would do all they could to have the full roster ready for the Chiefs and it appears Benford will indeed have a chance to suit up.

items.name: Dalton Kincaid
items.headline: Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) was limited in Tuesday’s practice.
items.analysis: Kincaid talked to reporters after practice and said he is “most likely” playing on Thanksgiving. Not a surprise after a pair of limited sessions, it seems like the Bills simply used their Week 11 game against the Dolphins as an exhibition to rest Kincaid ahead of the Chiefs game. He’ll be on the TE1 line if, as expected, he goes.

items.name: Brandon Aiyuk
items.headline: Brandon Aiyuk cleared waivers on Tuesday, making him a free agent.
items.analysis: Nobody claimed his 49ers contract. Our next blurb on Aiyuk will probably read something like “Commanders signed WR Brandon Aiyuk,” but until then we’re legally obligated to note that Adam Schefter reported he is expected to draw interest from “a few teams.”

items.name: Isaac Yiadom
items.headline: Bears claimed CB Isaac Yiadom off waivers from the Commanders.
items.analysis: Yiadom has been a decent depth corner for most of the last half-decade, but only played on special teams with the Commanders this year. Perhaps the Bears see more in him, or perhaps they just need a gunner.

items.name: J.K. Dobbins
items.headline: Broncos coach Sean Payton said he suspended J.K. Dobbins one game for conduct detrimental to the team.
items.analysis: For those of you who haven’t had the pleasure of rostering Dobbins anywhere, know that he played just one snap on Sunday. Whatever went down almost certainly has something to do with that low snap count, though Payton wouldn’t get into it publicly with reporters. If Dobbins could agitate enough to get released, maybe we’d get somewhere in fantasy circles, but as it stands there’s no reason to hold him in shallow leagues.

items.name: Kenneth Walker
items.headline: Kenneth Walker (groin) was limited in Tuesday’s practice.
items.analysis: This is at least the start of a movement for Walker to be active for Thanksgiving’s game against the Bills. It’s his first practice since suffering the groin injury. His status on Wednesday will be one of the biggest fantasy storylines of the week as it also underscores whether Emmett Johnson will be an RB1 or a contingency FLEX play. It’s hard to read too much into this one way or another, with Andy Reid saying early today that Walker “feels good” probably the best bellwether we have at this point.

items.name: Jake Ferguson
items.headline: Jake Ferguson did not practice on Tuesday.
items.analysis: He will almost certainly miss the Thanksgiving game against the Eagles after two more missed practices. It is perhaps feasible he could return for Week 13, which would be his fourth week since suffering this new knee injury.

items.name: Jake Ferguson
items.headline: Jake Ferguson (ankle/knee) did not practice on Tuesday.
items.analysis: He will almost certainly miss the Thanksgiving game against the Eagles after two more missed practices. It is perhaps feasible he could return for Week 13, which would be his fourth week since suffering this new knee injury.

items.name: Ben Skowronek
items.headline: Ben Skowronek (calf) did not practice on Tuesday.
items.analysis: This could open up more snaps for Pittsburgh’s ancillary receivers even if Skowronek is no fantasy force. He played 10 and 17 snaps in his first two weeks back from the calf injury after he was active for Week 10.

items.name: Michael Pittman
items.headline: Michael Pittman (foot) practiced in full on Tuesday.
items.analysis: Mike McCarthy has said he is “very confident” that Pittman will play in Week 12 and this listing does little to douse that. It’s hard to understand if Pittman’s return will actually make Aaron Rodgers target the middle of the field or not, but he would be a rough FLEX play either way in his first game off IR with all 32 teams playing in Week 12.

items.name: Shane Buechele
items.headline: Colts signed QB Shane Buechele off the Bills’ practice squad.
items.analysis: Buechele got his first NFL experience last year in Week 18, at age 27, when he completed 7-of-14 passes for 88 yards in a game the Chiefs were (probably) looking to lose against the Raiders. He was sacked five times. These last six Colts games will feel like they take five months.

items.name: LaJohntay Wester
items.headline: Ravens waived WR LaJohntay Wester.
items.analysis: Wester muffed two punts last week against the Panthers, which we’re told is “not a good way to keep your roster spot” when you are here to be the returner. The Ravens will shuffle the deck here.

items.name: Micah Parsons
items.headline: Packers activated Micah Parsons (knee/PUP) off the physically unable to perform list.
items.analysis: In other words, the questionable listing from an hour ago does not actually matter. Parsons is back after losing almost a year to a torn ACL. He’ll be directed to put some havoc on the field in his return against the Rams on Wednesday night.

items.name: Steve Avila
items.headline: Steve Avila (hamstring) will not play in Los Angeles’ Week 12 game against the Packers.
items.analysis: Avila did not play in Week 10 and did not practice at all this week coming out of a Week 11 bye. Perhaps the extra rest after this one will get him to a workable place in Week 13. Beaux Limmer started at guard in his place against the Cardinals in Week 10, but with Coleman Shelton (hamstring) also ruled out at center it’s possible that Limmer starts there instead. Bill Murray is the only other interior lineman on the 53-man roster currently, and it’s going to be almost Thanksgiving, not Groundhog Day.

items.name: Colby Parkinson
items.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) is not on Los Angeles’ final Week 11 injury report.
items.analysis: He and Tyler Higbee will both be featured parts of this offense as the Rams look to get by without Puka Nacua. The one that catches a touchdown will be the one that you don’t start.

items.name: Kyren Williams
items.headline: Kyren Williams (toe) is not on Los Angeles’ final Week 12 injury report.
items.analysis: He’ll be good to go against the Packers on Wednesday night. Williams should figure into the high RB2 mix as the Rams try to replace Puka Nacua once again with plenty of split back formations.

items.name: Wanya Morris
items.headline: Colts signed OL Wanya Morris off the Cowboys’ practice squad.
items.analysis: Jalen Travis and Bernhard Raimann are both dealing with injuries, and other names on the Colts 53-man roster at tackle include Luke Tenuta, Charlie Heck, and Matt Goncalves (a guard for almost the entirety of the year before shifting over in Week 10) as they try to see out the end of this disastrous season. Morris will attempt to see it with them.

items.name: Micah Parsons
items.headline: Micah Parsons (knee) is questionable for Green Bay’s Week 12 game against the Rams.
items.analysis: We have no doubts he’ll play — Rams EDGE Myles Garrett said he was able to give Parsons some tickets for the 27-year-old’s long-awaited return yesterday. But players returning from PUP and IR have frequently just gotten a questionable tag regardless of how likely they are to play. Parsons got in limited work in each of the three practices this week.

items.name: Josh Jacobs
items.headline: Josh Jacobs (thumb) is questionable for Green Bay’s Week 11 game against the Rams.
items.analysis: He got in limited work in each of Green Bay’s three practices this week, though some of them were “estimated” given the short week. Matt LaFleur said he was unlikely to play on Monday, so perhaps this is just a gamesmanship questionable. Obviously, if Jacobs does play, he’d be a suitable low-end RB2.

items.name: Kedon Slovis
items.headline: Ravens waived QB Kedon Slovis.
items.analysis: He’ll reportedly garner interest from the Arizona Cardinals for some reason. Slovis, 25, played for Arizona in the preseason and the Texans in the 2025 preseason. Over his three preseason stints he’s 86-of-126 for 816 yards, three touchdowns, and three interceptions while taking nine sacks.

items.name: Omarion Hampton
items.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh, asked about feeding Omarion Hampton more, said “in hindsight, we should have done that sooner.”
items.analysis: Many cases of fantasy managers who drafted Hampton in the first two rounds this past August nodding fervently at this news have been reported. Hampton had 15 touches last week and 23 against the Ravens in Week 10. With Justin Herbert (concussion protocol) uncertain for Week 12, it looks like Hampton will be a major part of the game plan yet again against the Patriots.

items.name: Raheim Sanders
items.headline: Browns designated RB Raheim Sanders (hip) to return from injured reserve.
items.analysis: His 21-day window will open today. Sanders probably won’t come back to a real role unless there are injuries ahead of him, but perhaps he’ll cut into Dylan Sampson’s No. 2 role and make both of them unrosterable.

items.name: Kenneth Walker
items.headline: Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said Ken Walker (ankle) will participate in practice Tuesday.
items.analysis: “I’m not anticipating a ton of work,” Reid said of Walker, who has missed two straight games and did not practice Monday ahead of the team’s Thanksgiving matchup against Buffalo. “Let’s see how does. He’s feeling pretty good.” If he practices today and Wednesday, Walker should be active for Thursday night. The Chiefs have committed to Walker as the team’s lead back despite Emmett Johnson putting up elite numbers in his absence. Johnson would be startable only in deeper fantasy leagues if Walker is good to go for Thursday.

items.name: Greg Newsome
items.headline: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports Greg Newsome (ankle) will miss 4-6 weeks.
items.analysis: He’s headed to injured reserve. Newsome will undergo surgery after sustaining a high ankle sprain in Week 11. His absence could be a blow to a Giants secondary that has played well in 2026, allowing the NFL’s 12th lowest drop back success rate and 11th lowest drop back EPA. Newsome through Week 11 had allowed the lowest EPA per target of any Giants cornerback.

items.name: DK Metcalf
items.headline: The Pittsburgh Post-Gazette’s Gerry Dulac reports DK Metcalf could face fines from the NFL following his Week 11 ejection.
items.analysis: Metcalf won’t be suspended for his repeated fights with Eagles defenders on Sunday but he could be fined for the behavior. Metcalf’s meltdown came after he had one catch for two yards in the first half. Among the most inefficient wide receivers in the game, Metcalf has had a disappointing 2026 campaign as the team’s No. 1 wideout. He’ll profile as a flex option in Week 12 against a Broncos defense allowing the fourth fewest fantasy points per target to boundary wideouts.

items.name: Sam Darnold
items.headline: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald would not say if Sam Darnold (oblique) would start in Week 12.
items.analysis: Darnold was able to return to practice on Monday ahead of the Seahawks’ Week 12 game against the division rival Niners. Macdonald suggested he wouldn’t make a call on a starting quarterback before Wednesday though. “I think before making any declarations with Sam, we’ll get through Wednesday, see how Wednesday goes,” Macdonald said. “So nothing official yet. He was able to train a little bit here, do some rehab here, he also was able to get away. He’s optimistic, but I think with today’s practice cadence and speed of today, it’s probably wise to wait to make any declarations until we get through Wednesday’s practice.” Drew Lock, the most efficient quarterback in the NFL this season, could get another start if Darnold isn’t quite ready. It’s an excellent matchup against a 49ers defense that profiles as a pass funnel.

items.name: Treylon Burks
items.headline: Treylon Burks caught 2-of-3 targets for 30 yards in the Commanders’ Week 11 win over the Bengals.
items.analysis: While Burks did little in the box score, he drew a defensive pass interference call in the end zone that set up the team’s only touchdown of the game on a Jacory Croskey-Merritt touchdown run on the following play. his three targets finished tied for fourth on the team behind Antonio Williams’ 12, Stefon Diggs’ six, and Chig Okonkwo’s five, leaving Burks in shaky fantasy territory as the team enters the final two months of play.

items.name: Stefon Diggs
items.headline: Stefon Diggs caught 4-of-6 targets for 45 yards in the Commanders’ Week 11 win over the Bengals.
items.analysis: Diggs was shown displaying clear frustration on multiple occasions, the two most glaring of which came on the sideline following a poorly thrown ball from quarterback Jayden Daniels. History would repeat in the second half when Daniels bounced a ball to Diggs in the end zone after escaping to his right, the former of whom had broken free of coverage over the middle of the field. Diggs’ veteran presence will need to persist through the uneven quarterback play if the Commanders are to make a push toward the postseason during the final two months of play, a road that was made that much easier with the walk off win over the Bengals. Up next are the downtrodden Cardinals in Week 12, where Diggs will remain a viable Flex play in fantasy.

items.name: Chig Okonkwo
items.headline: Chig Okonkwo caught 4-of-5 targets for 66 yards in the Commanders’ Week 11 win over the Bengals.
items.analysis: The veteran tight end’s five targets finished third on the team behind the 11 of Antonio Williams and six of veteran Stefon Diggs. Okonkwo remains unlikely to return elite volume in the more conservative Washington offense but can continue to return usable fantasy outings as a viable TE2. He’ll push for TE1 status in a plus matchup against the Cardinals in Week 12.

items.name: Antonio Williams
items.headline: Antonio Williams caught 9-of-11 targets for 122 yards in the Commanders’ Week 11 win over the Bengals.
items.analysis: Williams was the top option for quarterback Jayden Daniels throughout, seeing consistent volume throughout. He staked his mark on the game for good with a 42-yard reception to set up the game-winning field goal as time expired, effectively saving the Commanders’ season in the process. After teasing fantasy upside throughout the first half of his rookie season, Williams finally appears to have earned the top role through the air as he enters the final two months of the regular season as a viable WR3 with WR2 upside in fantasy circles. He gets a tantalizing matchup against the Cardinals in Week 12.

items.name: Austin Ekeler
items.headline: Austin Ekeler rushed seven times for 41 yards in the Commanders’ Week 11 win over the Bengals, adding three yards on two receptions.
items.analysis: The box score does little to jump off the page but it is notable that Ekeler played over Rachaad White as the primary change of pace option behind Jacory Croskey-Merritt. Whether that was due to White’s presence on the injury report throughout the week remains to be seen. Either way, the only fantasy-viable back currently on the roster appears to be Croskey-Merritt, leaving both Ekeler and White of little value moving forward.

items.name: Jacory Croskey-Merritt
items.headline: Jacory Croskey-Merritt rushed 13 times for 54 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 11 win over the Bengals, adding 23 yards on two receptions.
items.analysis: Croskey-Merritt immediately returned from injured reserve to handily lead the team in snaps and opportunities, despite veteran Austin Ekeler playing the team’s first series. More interesting was the fact that Rachaad White hardly had a role, with Ekeler serving as the primary change of pace option, something that could be due to White’s presence on the injury report throughout the week. Either way, Croskey-Merritt appears to have a stranglehold on lead duties moving forward, a role that keeps him as a viable RB2 in the immediate future. That holds true for a Week 12 meeting with the Cardinals.

items.name: Jayden Daniels
items.headline: Jayden Daniels completed 23-of-35 passes for 289 yards in the Commanders’ 22-20, Week 11 win over the Bengals, adding 55 yards on six carries.
items.analysis: Daniels and the Commanders were unable to get anything going offensively while playing through driving rain in the first half, going three-and-out on three of their first four possessions before their lone touchdown drive of the game on their final possessions before the break. Things would change in the second half as Daniels led five consecutive scoring drives, all of which ended in field goals, proving enough to eek out a victory that could have saved the team’s season. The 4-5-1 Commanders remain two games behind the division-leading Giants with two months remaining in the regular season, but a loss to the Bengals would have made a late-season push toward the playoffs almost insurmountable. Daniels and the Commanders now prepare to face the Cardinals on the road in Week 12, where the veteran signal caller will remain an upside QB2.

items.name: Ja'Marr Chase
items.headline: Ja’Marr Chase caught 5-of-9 targets for 31 yards in the Bengals’ Week 11 loss to the Commanders.
items.analysis: The two teams played to a scoreless first frame through driving rain in Maryland, with Chase appearing to come alive on the teams first possession of the second quarter. He would ultimately be locked up by sticky coverage heavily influenced by Washington’s ability to generate consistent pressure, narrowly missing a downfield shot in the second half in triple coverage that could have propelled his fantasy day toward a usable week. Chase’s next opportunity to flourish comes in a Week 12 meeting with the Saints, where his skillset sets up well to take advantage of one of the highest single-high rates in the league.

items.name: Tee Higgins
items.headline: Tee Higgins caught 2-of-3 targets for 43 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 11 loss to the Commanders.
items.analysis: Higgins got in the box score with a 31-yard touchdown reception late in the second quarter after the two teams played to a scoreless first frame in driving rain. The Bengals did not alter their typical pass-heavy ways despite the rain throughout the first half, with Higgins seeing modest volume while primarily matched up against Rasul Douglas on the perimeter. Joe Burrow fed the running backs and tight ends a massive 24 targets in the face of unrelenting pressure from the Commanders, a situation likely to correct against the single-high-heavy Saints in Week 12, where Higgins returns to WR2 status in fantasy.

items.name: Mike Gesicki
items.headline: Mike Gesicki caught 5-of-6 targets for 77 yards in the Bengals’ Week 11 loss to the Commanders.
items.analysis: Gesicki saw increased usage against an aggressive Commanders team that brought consistent pressure into the backfield, with the highlight of his game coming on a 32-yard reception over the middle of the field on the team’s final possession, ultimately ended in a field goal to take the lead with just over two minutes remaining. The Commanders would drive the field and kick the game-winning field goal on the subsequent possession to send the Bengals to 7-3. Gesicki’s weekly volume remains unlikely to approach elite territory, but his elite red zone usage and penchant for finding paint keeps him in the weekly TE1 discussion in the high-powered Cincinnati offense.

items.name: Samaje Perine
items.headline: Samaje Perine rushed six times for 26 yards in the Bengals’ Week 11 loss to the Commanders, adding 71 yards on four receptions.
items.analysis: The highlight of the game for Perine came on a 44-yard catch-and-run reception where he chipped into a leak route in the flat, springing free from linebacker coverage to give quarterback Joe Burrow an outlet in the face of pressure. He would outrun the secondary and pick up a key block from fellow running back Chase Brown as he sprung free down the sideline for the longest reception in the game. Perine’s 10 opportunities still ranked below the 14 of Brown but the former handily outproduced the presumed starter on his way to a usable fantasy outing. Up next are the ground-funnel Saints, where Perine will return to shaky Flex status in fantasy circles.

items.name: Chase Brown
items.headline: Chase Brown rushed six times for six yards in the Bengals’ Week 11 loss to the Commanders, adding 30 yards on five receptions.
