items.analysis: Brown saw minimal usage in the first half as the two teams played through driving rain, likely equal parts known tendencies as it was matchup-based. The bigger story here was the involvement of Samaje Perine, who did more than his standard change of pace role implied on his way to 97 total yards. There was no mention of injury or anything that would suggest Brown’s role was limited by necessity, likely best viewed as a small blip on the fantasy radar. Brown’s next opportunity to return a usable fantasy week comes in Week 12 against the Saints, where he will remain a fantasy RB2.

items.name: Joe Burrow
items.headline: Joe Burrow completed 28-of-40 passes for 300 yards and two touchdowns in the Bengals’ 22-20, Week 11 loss to the Commanders.
items.analysis: Burrow snapped a steak of five consecutive games in which he accounted for four or more touchdowns in the loss. He came into the game tied for the NFL record for consecutive games with four more touchdowns, ultimately unable to move into sole possession in game that played through driving rain throughout the first half. He leaned heavily on his running backs and tight ends against an aggressive Washington defense, feeding the two positions 24 targets on the evening. A defense that was able to stifle the Commanders in the first half allowed five consecutive scoring drives after the break, all of which were field goals, proving enough to send the Bengals to their third loss of the season. Now 7-3 and only one game ahead of the Browns and Steelers, the Bengals suddenly find themselves locked in one of the tighter divisional battles heading into the final two months of the regular season. Up next for Burrow and the Bengals are the Saints in Week 12, where Burrow will remain a top tier QB1.

items.name: Roschon Johnson
items.headline: Roschon Johnson (ankle) was listed as a “DNP” on Monday’s estimated practice report.
items.analysis: Johnson departed the team’s Week 11 win over the Saints with an ankle injury and did not return, making his absence Monday notable on the short week. Expect D’Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai to dominate snaps and opportunities out of the backfield for the Bears in one of the biggest games of the season, with the winner left standing alone atop the competitive NFC North.

items.name: Sam LaPorta
items.headline: Sam LaPorta (ankle) was listed as limited on Monday’s estimated practice report.
items.analysis: The ankle appears to be a non-issue, assuming LaPorta can manage to participate in practice Tuesday. The team will hold two more sessions ahead of Thursday’s divisional showdown against the Bears on Thanksgiving, a game that will decide which team stands alone atop the competitive NFC North with six weeks remaining in the regular season.

items.name: Sam Darnold
items.headline: Sam Darnold (quad/rib) was present at practice Monday.
items.analysis: The Seahawks held their “bonus” practice Monday as they prepare to face the 49ers on the road in Week 12. The level of participation of Darnold is not fully known considering the team does not owe a full practice report until Wednesday, but Darnold’s presence at practice appears to reinforce previous reports that the team expects him to return following their bye. A potential return would be a sizable boost to alpha wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba.

items.name: Ricky Barber
items.headline: Commanders declared CB Amik Robertson, QB Athan Kaliakmanis, RB Robert Henry Jr., Ricky Barber, and G Tanoa Togiai inactive for Week 11 against the Bengals.
items.analysis: The Commanders host one of the league’s hottest teams as they look to avoid falling further behind in the NFC East. They’ll need their defense to step up against a Bengals team averaging 36.2 points per game during their current five-game win streak.

items.name: Kyle Dugger
items.headline: Bengals declared S Kyle Dugger, OL Myles Hinton, DL Landon Robinson, OL Dalton Risner, and TE Cam Grandy inactive for Week 11 against the Commanders.
items.analysis: No real surprises here as the Bengals look to continue their string of recent offensive production against an inferior Washington defense. Joe Burrow gets his full compliment of offensive skill position players minus Andre Iosivas, who remains on injured reserve through Week 11.

items.name: Dallas Goedert
items.headline: Dallas Goedert (shin) was listed as a limited participant on Monday’s estimated practice report.
items.analysis: Likely nothing to see here as the veteran tight end prepares for a divisional matchup against the Cowboys on Thanksgiving. Goedert’s 38-yard reception last week against the Steelers was his longer catch since Week 1, although the fact it was his only grab is troubling considering it was the first game with a healthy DeVonta Smith in a month. Goedert has been relegated to a top end TE2 against the Cowboys.

items.name: Saquon Barkley
items.headline: Saquon Barkley (neck/illness) was listed as a limited participant on Monday’s estimated practice report.
items.analysis: Barkley should be good to go for the team’s Thanksgiving showdown against the Cowboys Thursday despite the dual-tag designation. The veteran workhorse is coming off one of his best performances of the season against the Steelers, leading the team to their first win in two calendar months.

items.name: Jake Ferguson
items.headline: Jake Ferguson was listed as a “DNP” on the estimated practice report Monday.
items.analysis: Even though the team held a walkthrough ahead of their Thanksgiving matchup against the Eagles, the fact that Ferguson has yet to practice after injuring his ankle two weeks ago spells trouble for his potential availability in Week 12. Brevyn Spann-Ford and Luke Schoonmaker appear to be looking at another game atop the depth chart, with volume through the air most likely to concentrate further on CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens.

items.name: George Holani
items.headline: Seahawks placed RB George Holani (knee) on injured reserve.
items.analysis: The move hurts far less than it would have earlier in the season when both Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price were unavailable. The change of pace option and special teams ace will now miss the next four games, at minimum, placing him in line to potentially return for Week 16 as the Seahawks make their final push toward the postseason.

items.name: Dalton Kincaid
items.headline: Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) was listed as limited on Monday’s estimated injury report.
items.analysis: Kincaid missed Week 11’s game against the Dolphins with the same set of injuries despite being questionable entering the weekend. It’s quite possible the decision to sit him against the one-win Dolphins was more of a precautionary one ahead of the Bills’ Week 12 matchup against the Chiefs. We’ll see how the rest of his week unfolds, but Kincaid practicing in any capacity this week should be viewed as a good sign for his availability.

items.name: Micah Parsons
items.headline: Micah Parson has been cleared to return for the Packers’ Week 12 game against the Rams.
items.analysis: This one game a bit earlier than expected. While the hope was Parsons would return on Wednesday, the star pass rusher was listed as a limited participant in Monday’s practice, leaving some doubt as to whether or not he would be cleared for a return. Now, the Packers get back their 2025 sack leader who last played in Week 15 of last season, when he suffered a torn ACL on the road against the Broncos. Parsons will provide an immediate boost to a defense that currently ranks 16th in points allowed but eighth in passing yards allowed per game. They are also tied for the seventh-most team sacks in the league (29), and should see that number creep up a bit with Parsons back in the mix.

items.name: Kenneth Walker
items.headline: Kenneth Walker (groin) was listed as DNP on Monday’s estimated injury report.
items.analysis: This wasn’t the news fantasy managers were looking for after going without Walker for each of the last two weeks. The Chiefs’ RB1 has been sidelined with a groin injury he suffered ahead of Week 10’s game against the Falcons, but there was early hope it would be a one-game absence. It was widely believed the decision to sit him against the woeful Cardinals was made to give him additional time to heal up before Week 12’s game against the Bills, but Monday’s DNP now draws his availability against Buffalo into question. The Chiefs didn’t officially practice today, but Walker would not have been present if they did. If he can’t get on the field in even a limited capacity on Tuesday, it would be fair to say he’s trending in the wrong direction ahead of Thursday’s marquee matchup. If Walker is unable to play, Emmett Johnson would be a fringe RB1 after strong performances in back-to-back weeks.

items.name: Daniel Jones
items.headline: Daniel Jones has cleared waivers and is now free to sign with any team.
items.analysis: Now that he has passed through waivers, Jones is officially a free agent and is free to sign with any team. While plenty of QB-needy teams could reach out for his services, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported early Monday that Jones will likely wait to sign with a new team and may leave the door open to signing with a contender later in the season that suddenly finds itself in need of a starting QB.

items.name: Quinyon Mitchell
items.headline: Quinyon Mitchell (hamstring) did not practice on Monday.
items.analysis: It was an estimated session. Mitchell talked with reporters after leaving Sunday’s game with the hamstring ailment, implying it wasn’t a super serious injury. Still, on a short week, his status is up in the air. If he were ruled out, it would only help CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens on Thanksgiving.

items.name: DeVonta Smith
items.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) is practicing in full ahead of Philadelphia’s Thursday game against the Cowboys.
items.analysis: We’re expecting the Eagles to force-feed Smith once more after his 57 percent target share on Sunday, leaving him as a plausible WR2 in an elevated matchup against the Cowboys defense.

items.name: Will Shipley
items.headline: Will Shipley (foot/illness) was limited in Monday’s practice.
items.analysis: It was an estimated session and exactly the same listing he had on Friday. As he was practicing on a limited basis before the illness (and before being activated off injured reserve last Saturday), we’ll assume he has a fairly good chance to suit up on Thursday.

items.name: Dallas Goedert
items.headline: Dallas Goedert (shin) was limited in Monday’s practice.
items.analysis: It’s a new (estimated) listing after his one-catch outing against the Steelers. Goedert was at least set up with a Joe Milton #RevengeGame script against a weak Cowboys defense this week to try to rebound, but it will be hard to rely on him as a streamer TE1 if healthy. We’ll see if he can get to the second part of that statement tomorrow.

items.name: Saquon Barkley
items.headline: Saquon Barkley (neck/illness) was limited in Monday’s practice.
items.analysis: We described Barkley as leaving the game in the fourth quarter with what “appeared to be a left arm” injury in Sunday’s blurb, it sounds like it may have been a stinger based on the neck listing. A limited (estimated) session is better than a DNP, but Tuesday’s report will loom large for Barkley’s chances of playing against the Cowboys on Thursday.

items.name: Micah Parsons
items.headline: Micah Parsons (knee) was limited in Monday’s practice.
items.analysis: Parsons has been limited in each of the Packers’ first two practices to start the week. It’s long been believed that the star pass-rusher could be activated for Wednesday’s game against the Rams, but the team has declined to say whether or not that will come to fruition. We will likely have an official word on Parsons’ Week 12 availability when the Packers release their final injury report on Tuesday.

items.name: Colby Parkinson
items.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) practiced in full on Monday.
items.analysis: He’s gotten in two full sessions coming off the bye and figures to remain one of the main figures in the Rams’ floating opera of tight end production that they’ll likely be relying on this week sans Puka Nacua and Davante Adams.

items.name: Josh Jacobs
items.headline: Josh Jacobs (thumb) was limited in Monday’s practice.
items.analysis: Jacobs has been limited in each of the Packers’ first two practices as they prepare to face the Rams on Wednesday. While a limited session would generally be viewed as an encouraging sign for a player, head coach Matt LaFleur said earlier that he doesn’t expect Jacobs to suit up this week. We will continue to track his status until he receives an official designation for the game, but we’re assuming based on LaFleur’s comments that Jacobs will miss at least one more week.

items.name: Kyren Williams
items.headline: Kyren Williams (toe) practiced in full on Monday.
items.analysis: It’s an upgrade from a limited session on Sunday and we’d be surprised if Williams was placed on the questionable line on Tuesday.

items.name: DK Metcalf
items.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports DK Metcalf will not be suspended following his ejection from Week 11’s game against the Eagles.
items.analysis: Metcalf allegedly tried to poke Eagles CB Cooper DeJean in the eye during an altercation. While Metcalf denies those allegations, whatever he was attempting to do certainly didn’t look good on tape. While the league has opted not to suspend Metcalf for his actions, he could still face fines for his conduct, which would be handed down later in the week. That said, Metcalf should be good to go for Week 12’s game against the Broncos.

items.name: Jacory Croskey-Merritt
items.headline: Commanders activated RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) off injured reserve.
items.analysis: “Bill” has missed the minimum four games and was designated as questionable; he has been removed from the injury report by the Commanders and should be their lead back. You likely already had plans to start him if you were holding up your FLEX spot or RB2 position for him, and now you officially can do so.

items.name: Jordan Addison
items.headline: Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell said he doesn’t “necessarily expect to have Jordan Addison (thumb)” back for Week 12 against the Falcons.
items.analysis: Addison underwent thumb surgery last week after suffering what was described as a “freak injury” in practice. While he wasn’t considered a candidate for injured reserve, O’Connell did say after the injury that he would likely miss multiple games before returning. If Addison is unable to play in Week 12, it would be the third straight game he has missed with the injury. His practice status will be one to monitor throughout the week.

items.name: RJ Harvey
items.headline: The Denver Post’s Parker Gabriel reports RJ Harvey (IR/knee) is “widely expected” to practice when first eligible to come off injured reserve.
items.analysis: Harvey will miss Black Friday’s game against the Steelers, but it sounds like that might be the last one he misses. Jonah Coleman has established a fiefdom at the top of the depth chart in Harvey’s absence, so the second-year back doesn’t necessarily return to a major role in Week 13, but he may be worth picking up in deeper leagues if he was dropped.

items.name: Greg Newsome
items.headline: Giants head coach John Harbaugh said CB Greg Newsome will miss multiple weeks with a high-ankle sprain.
items.analysis: Newsome’s injury comes just weeks after he signed a three-year, $46 million contract extension with the Giants. The 26-year-old corner has appeared on 483 defensive snaps this season, earning a PFF coverage grade of 71.2 while allowing opposing receivers to catch 19 passes for 209 scoreless yards. His absence will be a tough blow to a Giants secondary that ranks fourth in net yards allowed per attempt and fifth in overall passing yards allowed this season.

items.name: Michael Pittman
items.headline: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said he is “very confident” Michael Pittman (foot) will play in Week 12 against the Broncos.
items.analysis: Pittman hasn’t played since Week 4 and has put together a forgettable 7-89-0 line in the three games he has suited up for this season. His return comes as the Steelers are in the midst of an offensive slump, as they’ve averaged just 19.3 points per game in their last four games while going 1-3. They’ll need all hands on deck as they prepare to face a tough Broncos defense on Friday.

items.name: Nick Rallis
items.headline: Cardinals fired DC Nick Rallis.
items.analysis: Rallis, whose unit had allowed 323 points in 11 weeks, more than anyone but the Raiders, will give way to interim DC Teryl Austin. Still just 33, there’s a chance the ultra-aggressive Rallis will get another opportunity in this post down the line. Weirdly, the defense hasn’t been the No. 1 problem area in Arizona lately — though that’s certainly more about quarterback attrition than anything — but it’s hard to say that Rallis ever produced a notably above-average unit in three-and-a-half years in the desert. The Cardinals best finish over that span was 14th in DVOA in 2024.

items.name: Bhayshul Tuten
items.headline: Jaguars coach Liam Coen said Bhayshul Tuten (ankle) re-aggravated his injury against the Giants and it will be “business as usual” with him in practice this week.
items.analysis: In other words, look for a lot of DNPs and limited sessions that don’t really matter, then a Friday decision at the end of the week. The Jaguars certainly could decide they have the luxury of resting Tuten against the Titans in Week 12. Chris Rodriguez could be either a viable RB2 or a useless FLEX play by Friday, depending on how this situation shakes out.

items.name: Seth McGowan
items.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Seth McGowan (hamstring) “will miss some time.”
items.analysis: McGowan exited in Week 11’s loss to the Texans and did not return to the game. The rookie seventh-rounder had been seeing an increased role as of late, rushing 26 times for 158 yards and two touchdowns in his last four games while adding two receptions. His absence should create a slight uptick in opportunities for Jonathan Taylor, who has had no more than 16 rush attempts in his last four games. We’ll likely get a better sense of how long McGowan could be out in the coming days, but for now, DJ Giddens appears next in line behind Taylor.

items.name: Terrance Ferguson
items.headline: Rams head coach Sean McVay said Terrance Ferguson will undergo season-ending ankle surgery.
items.analysis: Ferguson tried multiple times to make his way back from the ankle injury that has sidelined him since Week 3. Initially expected to return in Week 9, Ferguson suffered a hamstring injury in practice that further delayed his return, but it doesn’t sound like his ankle ever fully healed in light of today’s news. Ferguson’s season comes to an end after just three games. The second-year tight end turned in an impressive 6-54-1 line in Week 2 against the Giants, but saw just three targets over his other two games. The former second-round pick is an explosive playmaker with the ball in his hand and could make for an intriguing late-round pick in fantasy leagues next year once healthy.

items.name: Marvin Harrison
items.headline: NBC Houston’s Aaron Wilson reports Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) is dealing with a short-term strain.
items.analysis: Danielle Hunter, too, is dealing with one of these. It seems like after the lengthy layoff following Thursday night’s win over the Colts, the Texans could be in line to get both players back for Week 12’s game against the Ravens.

items.name: Brandon Aiyuk
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Commanders are Brandon Aiyuk’s “most likely” landing spot.
items.analysis: The ink on the release wasn’t even given time to dry before Aiyuk was connected to the same team he was connected to all offseason. He’ll likely wind up with a spot on the Commanders practice squad. Given the lengthy layoff, we probably don’t need to imagine Aiyuk suiting up in Week 12 as a destined outcome, but it could be sooner rather than later.

items.name: Brandon Aiyuk
items.headline: 49ers released WR Brandon Aiyuk.
items.analysis: Took them long enough, you might say before you were pedanted by those who would tell you things like “Aiyuk had to report to actually be released.” It should be noted that Aiyuk must clear waivers since this is after the trade deadline, but nobody is expected to assume his contract. Anyway, Aiyuk will be free to pursue free agency and it sounds like we have another blurb to write about that almost instantly, funny how that works. The 28-year-old will look to continue his career elsewhere, perhaps somewhere in the greater Washington D.C. area.

items.name: Kenneth Walker
items.headline: Chiefs OC Eric Bieniemy said Kenneth Walker (groin) will “remain the starter” when he returns.
items.analysis: Rookie Emmett Johnson has rushed for 45-206-1 in two games without Walker this season, which has led some to wonder what role Walker could have when he returns from his groin injury. Walker, who currently ranks fifth in the league in rushing yards (872) and leads the league in yards per carry (5.5) could return as early as this Thursday when the Bills play host to the Chiefs on Thanksgiving, and from the sound of things, it would be safe to say he will be in line for plenty of work. Speaking Monday with the media, Bieniemy said that while Johnson has been impressive in his two games as a starter, the Chiefs “also understand the value [Walker] brings as well.” His practice status will be one to monitor this week, but if he’s active, Walker would be an easy must-start in what could be a high-scoring affair.

items.name: John Lynch
items.headline: FOX Sports’ Jay Glazer reports the 49ers signed President of Football Operations and GM John Lynch to an extension.
items.analysis: Lynch joined the Niners as general manager in 2017 and was promoted to President of Football Operations in 2023. Since his arrival, the Niners have emerged as one of the better-run organizations in the league. Under Lynch, the Niners have gone 91-68 in the regular season while making two trips to the Super Bowl and four trips to the NFC Championship Game. His selection of Brock Purdy as the final pick of the 2022 NFL Draft ended up giving head coach Kyle Shanahan his long-term QB of the future after previously failed attempts to address the position post Alex Smith and Colin Kaepernick, and in a season where the Niners have been dealt multiple injuries, specifically at receiver, San Francisco currently finds itself with a 9-1 record and three games ahead of the Seahawks and Rams in the NFC West. It’s a much-deserved extension for Lynch, who again has his team on track to make a deep run in the postseason.

items.name: Jalen Coker
items.headline: Panthers coach Dave Canales said Jalen Coker has cleared concussion protocol.
items.analysis: Coker was checked in the fourth quarter after taking a hard hit from Roquan Smith, but it looks like he’ll be fine to use against the Buccaneers on Monday night. With all 32 teams active, it may be time to capitulate and put Coker back on the WR3 line. He has not cleared 50 yards since Week 6.

items.name: Jonathon Brooks
items.headline: Panthers coach Dave Canales said Trevor Etienne’s production and Tre Tyus’ special teams value make it “challenging” to find a spot for Jonathon Brooks.
items.analysis: Brooks, who is on injured reserve due to a groin injury, has eight days to be activated or lost for the season. The 23-year-old back practiced in full last week all three times only to not be activated. It would be great news for Chuba Hubbard if this continued, as the team has shown little interest in using Etienne in a real role in the backfield.

items.name: Josh Jacobs
items.headline: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said Josh Jacobs (finger) is unlikely to play in Week 12 against the Rams.
items.analysis: Jacobs was listed as limited in Sunday’s practice as the Packers prepare to take on the Rams on Wednesday, but he’s still only nine days removed from the surgery to repair his fractured ring finger. It was reported shortly after his injury that Jacobs could miss 2-3 weeks, and a return in Week 13 would put him close to that three-week timetable. It doesn’t sound like we should expect to see him this week against the Rams, but a return against the Saints could be in the cards if all goes well.

items.name: Tommy DeVito
items.headline: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said “Tommy [DeVito is] our starter” when asked if the team plans to add a QB in the coming days.
items.analysis: After news broke last week of Drake Maye’s injury and impending absence of six-plus weeks, it was reported that the Patriots could explore QB options outside the building to take over for the Pats’ QB1. The recent release of Daniel Jones by the Colts makes that subject all the more interesting, but Vrabel, at least for now, seems committed to 28-year-old DeVito, who is set to make his first start as a Patriot in Week 12 against the Chargers. Vrabel praised DeVito for the improved play he showed in training camp and the preseason and expressed confidence in him to lead the offense and run the huddle. DeVito hasn’t started a game since the 2024 season with the Giants and has a career passing line of 1,490-9-4 in 15 career games. He threw for 81 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in relief if Maye in Week 10, but will be hard to trust as anything more than a desperation play in 2QB/Superflex leagues next week against the Chargers.

items.name: Malik Willis
items.headline: Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said “as of today” Malik Willis’ groin injury will not require surgery.
items.analysis: It sounds like this is subject to change, as Hafley also added that Willis will “be re-evaluated at the four-week mark” of his absence to see where things stand. Willis has already spent two weeks on injured reserve and will need to miss at least two more games before the Dolphins could consider bringing him back in Week 14 against the Bears. Kyle McCord has struggled in his two starts, completing 44.6 percent of his passes while throwing for 311-0-1, and will be under center again in Week 12 against the Jets.

items.name: Ja'Kobi Lane
items.headline: Ja’Kobi Lane was not targeted in the Ravens’ Week 11 loss to the Panthers.
items.analysis: After seeing a season-high 11 targets in Week 10’s loss to the Chargers, Lane went on to donut in Sunday’s loss to the Panthers. The rookie’s lack of targets wasn’t due to a shortage of playing time, as his 23 routes run were good for third most of any Ravens receiver, but the ball simply wasn’t finding him. With all 32 teams playing in Week 12, fantasy managers shouldn’t trust Lane in any capacity next week against the Texans.

items.name: Darren Waller
items.headline: Darren Waller caught 3-of-3 targets for 42 yards in the Panthers’ Week 11 win over the Ravens.
items.analysis: Waller’s biggest play came on a 27-yard reception in the third quarter. He caught one of three deep balls from Bryce Young, but fellow tight end Mitchell Evans outperformed him, posting a 5-44-1 line in what turned out to be a career day for the third-year tight end. Waller won’t be anything more than a boom-or-bust TE2 in Week 12 against the Buccaneers.

items.name: Daniel Jones
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said Daniel Jones could wait to sign with a new team if he goes unclaimed on waivers.
items.analysis: The belief is that Jones won’t be claimed on waivers, since any team that claims him would inherit his remaining contract with the Colts. Instead, Jones will likely pass through waivers and become a free agent, but he could delay signing with a new team immediately and instead opt to wait and see what other options may become available during the season. As Rapoport pointed out on Monday on NFL Network’s Good Morning Football, “someone, some playoff-ready team unfortunately is going to lose a quarterback at some point,” which could open the door for Jones to join a legitimate contender over the final stretch of the season and ahead of the playoffs. It was reported earlier that the Patriots and Ravens could be interested in Jones, but both teams would be on the outside looking in if the postseason began today. Jones struggled mightily in his second season with the Colts, throwing for 1,974-7-13 in 11 games, but he would likely be an upgrade over several teams’ backup QBs if a starter goes down.

items.name: Colton McKivitz
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports 49ers RT Colton McKivitz will likely miss the remainder of the season after suffering fracturing and dislocating his ankle in Week 11’s win over the Vikings.
items.analysis: If you saw this injury during the game, you immediately knew this would likely be a season-ender. McKivitz’s left leg twisted unnaturally after a play in the second quarter, and the 30-year-old tackle was carted off the field shortly after. While we hope for the best, we fully expect the team to announce McKivitz’s season is over at some point this week. McKivitz was replaced by Vederian Lowe, who will presumably be the Niners’ starting right tackle moving forward.

items.name: DK Metcalf
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports DK Metcalf’s actions will be “reviewed for potential additional discipline, including suspension” following his ejection in Week 11 against the Eagles.
items.analysis: Metcalf was ejected from Sunday’s game against the Eagles after receiving his second unsportsmanlike conduct penalty. The 28-year-old receiver ended the day with one catch for two yards and had two altercations with Eagles CB Cooper DeJean before he was sent to the locker room. Metcalf will almost certainly receive a fine from the league in the coming days, but a suspension could put him in line to miss Week 12’s game against the Broncos.

items.name: Deebo Samuel
items.headline: Deebo Samuel caught 3-of-4 targets for 20 yards in the 49ers’ Week 11 win over the Vikings, adding 27 yards on two carries.
items.analysis: Samuel continued to operate as the primary gadget player for a 49ers team now with Christian McCaffrey, Mike Evans, and George Kittle all fully healthy. While that role carries per-touch upside given the space he should have when receiving the ball, fantasy managers are likely forced to view Samuel more as a potential Flex than a viable weekly starter. That will remain true ahead of a Week 12 meeting with the Seahawks.

items.name: George Kittle
items.headline: George Kittle caught all three passes for 34 yards and two touchdowns in the 49ers’ Week 11 win over the Vikings.
items.analysis: Kittle got to work early, capping off the opening drive with a touchdown from 17 yards out before adding a second touchdown early in the second quarter. The team would score again on their subsequent possession before the defense tacked on a pick-six on the following play, capping passing volume and leading to the low target total for the veteran tight end in the process. Even so, Kittle continued to showcase his elite athleticism, body control, and strength on his two scores and remains a surefire TE1 heading into another difficult matchup against the Seahawks in Week 12.

items.name: Keenan Allen
items.headline: Keenan Allen caught 3-of-4 targets for 38 yards in the 49ers’ Week 11 win over the Vikings.
items.analysis: Allen was hardly used in the first half as George Kittle and Mike Evans did all the heavy lifting but came alive in the third quarter to get his name in the box score. The 49ers’ most recent addition provides yet another offensive weapon alongside Evans, Kittle, Christian McCaffrey, and Deebo Samuel, all of whom are now healthy as the team continues its press toward the only bye out of the NFC. Allen will be a difficult start in fantasy with the other supporting cast fully healthy as they prepare to face the Seahawks in Week 12.

items.name: Mike Evans
items.headline: Mike Evans caught 6-of-7 targets for 109 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 11 win over the Vikings.
items.analysis: Fantasy managers took a collective sigh of relief after Evans was shown on the sideline grimacing in the first quarter. The team would never pass an injury update for their veteran star, who would later connect with quarterback Brock Purdy in the second quarter from four yards out to push the team’s lead to 21-10. The defense would step up with a pick-six on Minnesota’s subsequent possession, allowing the 49ers to coast to the win in the second half. As is typically the case, Evans caught numerous key passes on third down to extend drives, using his large frame to great effect on both slants and on the perimeter. His touchdown was a fade to the corner of the end zone, highlighting the full range of his talents against a formidable opponent. Fantasy managers will want to track his practice availability in the coming days, but it appears likely Evans can be inserted into lineups as a viable WR1 when the 49ers take on the Seahawks in Week 12.

items.name: Christian McCaffrey
items.headline: Christian McCaffrey rushed 12 times for 49 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 11 win over the Vikings, adding 13 yards on two receptions.
items.analysis: McCaffrey found the end zone for the 14th time this season, marking his ninth consecutive game with a touchdown after failing to find paint in Week 1 against the Rams in Australia. The modest carry total and receiving total were more a comment on how much of a stranglehold the 49ers had on the game than anything else, coasting in the second half after jumping out to a 28-10 lead in the second quarter. The starters would then rest for the team’s final two possessions following McCaffrey’s fourth quarter touchdown. McCaffrey remains an elite RB1 ahead of a Week 12 meeting with the division rival Seahawks.

items.name: Brock Purdy
items.headline: Brock Purdy completed 21-of-26 passes for 255 yards and three touchdowns in the 49ers’ 35-10, Week 11 win over the Vikings.
items.analysis: Purdy and the 49ers controlled the tempo throughout against the aggressive Minnesota defense, expertly handling the blitz as the 49ers jumped out to a 21-10 lead in the second quarter by finding paint on three of their first four possessions. The lead was extended on a pick-six shortly thereafter, allowing the 49ers to coast to their ninth victory of the season. The team now has a stranglehold on the once-competitive NFC West and the inside track to the only bye out of the conference, with only the four teams in the NFC North threatening that claim. The former Mr. Irrelevant tossed three touchdowns for the second consecutive game and the fourth time this season, keeping him in the QB1 ranks in fantasy ahead of another stiff test against the Seahawks in Week 12.

items.name: Jauan Jennings
items.headline: Jauan Jennings caught 3-of-6 targets for 20 yards in the Vikings’ Week 11 loss to the 49ers.
items.analysis: Jennings operated in a familiar WR3 role for the Vikings despite the absence of Jordan Addison, with Tai Felton getting the start on the perimeter opposite Justin Jefferson. Fantasy managers that thought they were pulling a fast one by adding Jennings are likely better off scooping Felton as a viable Flex for as long as Addison remains sidelined.

items.name: Tai Felton
items.headline: Tai Felton caught 6-of-12 targets for 42 yards in the Vikings’ Week 11 loss to the 49ers.
items.analysis: Felton operated as a starter on the perimeter opposite Justin Jefferson but was unable to capitalize on a team-leading 12 targets. Even so, Felton should be expected to continue as a starter in the offense for as long as Jordan Addison remains sidelined due to a thumb injury, a role that could yield viable Flex status in the coming weeks. Fantasy managers in a bind could do worse than scooping Felton from waivers ahead of a Week 12 meeting with the Falcons.

items.name: T.J. Hockenson
items.headline: T.J. Hockenson caught 6-of-7 targets for 55 yards in the Vikings’ Week 11 loss to the 49ers.
items.analysis: The highlight of the game for the veteran tight end was a posterizing catch down the sideline for a 20-yard gain on the team’s opening possession, a drive that resulted in the first of two missed field goal attempts. Hockenson would play the role of Mr. Reliable from that point forward, although his seven targets finished third on the team behind Justin Jefferson and Tai Felton. The Vikings get the 3-7 Falcons at home in Week 12, where Hockenson will remain a volume-driven TE1.

items.name: Justin Jefferson
items.headline: Justin Jefferson caught 7-of-9 targets for 86 yards in the Vikings’ Week 11 loss to the 49ers, adding one yard on one carry.
items.analysis: Kirk Cousins and Kevin O’Connell did what they could to get Jefferson involved early and often, although his nine targets ended second on the team behind Tai Felton’s 12. His lone mistake in the game was a costly one, with Jefferson losing a fumble with the team driving on their first possession of the second half down 28-10. The team would not recover after the untimely error, failing to add additional scoring while turning the ball over twice on downs during their subsequent three possessions. Jefferson is clearly in better hands with Cousins under center, a situation that should hold moving forward despite the veteran signal caller being replaced late in a lost game. Fantasy managers can start Jefferson with confidence as an upside WR2 against the Falcons in Week 12.

items.name: Aaron Jones
items.headline: Aaron Jones rushed eight times for 30 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings’ Week 11 loss to the 49ers, adding 13 yards on one reception.
items.analysis: Jones continues to cede primary rushing duties between the 20s to Jordan Mason but scored for the second consecutive game. After serving as a workhorse back with Mason on the shelf, Jones has not seen more than 11 carries since Mason returned in Week 7, having been held to eight carries or fewer in four of five games. That leaves very little room for fantasy upside on the worse side of a true timeshare, meaning fantasy managers are better off leaving Jones on their bench ahead of a Week 12 meeting with the Falcons.

items.name: Jordan Mason
items.headline: Jordan Mason rushed 11 times for 38 yards in the Vikings’ Week 11 loss to the 49ers, losing one yard on one reception.
items.analysis: Mason led the team in rush attempts and yardage while ceding high-value touches to Aaron Jones for the second consecutive week, with the latter accounting for the only touchdown scored by the Vikings in the loss. The poor game environment and inability of the offense to sustain drives led to the modest touch total for the veteran back, who has become a difficult player to trust in fantasy circles given the current split in workload. Fantasy managers likely have better options ahead of a Week 12 meeting with the Falcons.

items.name: Kirk Cousins
items.headline: Kirk Cousins completed 26-of-38 passes for 235 yards and one interception in the Vikings’ 35-10, Week 11 loss to the 49ers.
items.analysis: This one started with all the makings of a true shootout, with the two teams trading blows early to push the score to 14-10 in favor of the 49ers through the first six possessions. That would be where the offensive production stopped for the Vikings, who turned the ball over twice and missed two field goals. We’ll give a pass on the second field goal attempt missed considering it came up just feet short of setting a new NFL record at 71 yards in the altitude in Mexico. The tires became entirely deflated for the Vikings after a Justin Jefferson fumble halted any momentum coming out of the half while trailing 28-10. A touchdown on that drive makes it a game, but the Vikings ultimately failed to muster any additional scoring after their third possession of the game. Cousins ended up giving way to Carson Wentz in the fourth quarter in a lost game after failing to throw for a touchdown for the first time this season. The 7-3 Vikings get a full week to prepare for the Falcons in Week 12, where Cousins will return as an upside QB2.

items.name: Jaylen Waddle
items.headline: Jaylen Waddle caught 3-of-6 targets for 61 yards in the Broncos’ Week 11 win over the Raiders.
items.analysis: Sean Payton tried to get Waddle going as a deep option today with mixed results. Waddle gained at least 18 yards on all three of his catches. He was also held to just three catches. Waddle has caught more than five passes in one game this year. Today was just his second outing over 50 yards. Waddle isn’t completely useless for fantasy purposes, but the case for him as a WR3 grows worse by the week. With no teams on bye in Week 12, Waddle will finally hit the WR4 ranks versus Pittsburgh.

items.name: Courtland Sutton
items.headline: Courtland Sutton did not catch either of his targets in the Broncos’ Week 11 win over the Raiders.
items.analysis: Sutton posted a solid 5-45-1 receiving line before the Broncos’ Week 10 bye, but it felt like the team was ready to move Pat Bryant into a larger role. Bryant only managed four targets, but it was his first time seeing more looks than Sutton all year. He caught three of them for 32 yards. Now facing increased competition for opportunities, Sutton’s fantasy outlook is going from bad to worse headed into Week 12. He will be a touchdown-or-bust WR5 versus the Steelers.

items.name: Jakobi Meyers
items.headline: Jakobi Meyers caught 4-of-10 targets for 84 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 11 loss against the Giants.
items.analysis: Meyers was second on the team in targets and receiving yards, trailing Parker Washington’s eight catches for 103 yards. Meyers’ 26-yard grab was the biggest play of the day for the Jaguars, who were forced into a pass-heavy chase script in the second half — a rarity for Jacksonville. Meyers will be a passable WR3 play in Week 12 against the Titans. He had 34 yards on three catches against the Titans in Week 10.

items.name: Pat Bryant
items.headline: Pat Bryant caught 3-of-4 targets for 32 yards in the Broncos’ Week 11 win over the Raiders.
items.analysis: Bryant got off to a hot start with a 20-yard grab on the Broncos’ opening drive. That would account for over half of his production on the day as Bo Nix could not get any of his receivers going. Bryant still finished second among the team’s wideouts in targets, though Evan Engram and Jonah Coleman both saw more opportunities in the passing game than him. Bryant also survived an injury scare late in the game. His leg got rolled on during a tackle in the fourth quarter. He tried to get up but went back down on the field. Bryant walked off under his own power, worked through the issue on the sideline, and returned a few plays later. We expect to see him on the injury report, but he should be available for Week 12. He will be in the WR4 mix versus Pittsburgh.

items.name: Chris Rodriguez
items.headline: Chris Rodriguez had four rushes for 28 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 11 loss to the Giants, adding one catch for 13 yards.
items.analysis: C-Rod handled a limited workload again, even despite Bhayshul Tuten coming on and off the field with ankle and knee injuries that have slowed him down of late. Tuten ended the game with ten carries and three receptions. Rodriguez could have a valuable workload in Week 12 against the Titans if the Jaguars rest Tuten for the stretch run. Rodriguez should be rostered in all formats as a solid contingency option.

items.name: Evan Engram
items.headline: Evan Engram caught 6-of-8 targets for 74 yards in the Broncos’ Week 11 win over the Raiders.
items.analysis: Engram was surprisingly involved in this game, and not just on check-downs. Four of his catches went for at least 10 yards, propelling him to a season-high in receiving yards. The only downside to his performance was the lack of a touchdown. That went to Adam Trautman on a short goal-line toss. While Engram’s pop-up game might help some best ball players, it’s not worth chasing headed into Week 12 against the Steelers.

items.name: Josh Cameron
items.headline: Josh Cameron caught 3-of-7 targets for 44 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 11 loss to the Giants.
items.analysis: Cameron ran only 22 routes on 56 Jacksonville drop backs but was second behind only Parker Washington (12) in targets. Cameron will be a borderline fantasy option next week against a terrible Titans secondary. Cameron had 67 yards on three catches against Tennessee in Week 10.

items.name: Brian Thomas
items.headline: Brian Thomas caught 1-of-3 targets for 18 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 11 loss against the Giants.
items.analysis: Thomas, who ran a pass route on 33 of the team’s 56 drop backs, caught his first touchdown since Week 8 and only his third score of the year. His route involvement saw a bump over Josh Cameron, who had been playing more than BTJ. Cameron had just 21 routes on the day and caught three balls for 44 yards. Thomas was among the Jacksonville pass catchers who benefited from the game’s inflated volume. He’ll be a high variance flex play in Week 12 against the Colts.

items.name: J.K. Dobbins
items.headline: J.K. Dobbins rushed one time for zero yards in the Broncos’ Week 11 win over the Raiders.
items.analysis: Jonah Coleman completed his takeover of the backfield today with 24 carries, four catches, and three touchdowns. Dobbins, meanwhile, saw as many carries as Cody Schrader. Dobbins’ carry total has gone from seven to four to one in his past three appearances. Sean Payton has decided that this is Coleman’s backfield and there’s not much Dobbins can do about it. Fantasy managers can cut ties with him on the next run of waivers.

items.name: Bo Nix
items.headline: Bo Nix completed 19-of-35 passes for 225 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Broncos’ 38-24, Week 11 win over the Raiders.
items.analysis: Nix got on the board early with a goal line toss to Adam Trautman, but it was all Jonah Coleman after that. The rookie running back punched in three rushing touchdowns, all from no farther than seven yards out. Nix did have several close calls on the day. He threw a well-placed deep ball to Troy Franklin, and the pass simply doinked off his helmet. Franklin was laying out for the ball, so it may not have been a touchdown, but it still would have juiced Nix’s box score. Nix also threw a dime to Marvin Mims on a flea-flicker that went down to the one-yard line. He was then stuffed on a sneak, after which Coleman made it into the end zone. All in, it was a better performance from Nix than the box score suggests. With no teams on bye next week, Nix will likely be relegated to the top of the QB2 ranks for his date with the Steelers.

items.name: Brenton Strange
items.headline: Brenton Strange caught all three of his targets for 16 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 11 loss against the Giants.
items.analysis: Strange didn’t see much involvement in a game that saw Trevor Lawrence attempt a season-high 47 passes, though he ran a route on 44 of the team’s 49 drop backs. Strange, who has more than five targets in five games this season, will be a fine fantasy option in Week 12 against a Colts defense that ranks among the most generous to enemy tight ends.

items.name: Michael Mayer
items.headline: Michael Mayer caught 1-of-4 targets for four yards in the Raiders’ Week 11 loss to the Broncos.
items.analysis: To add insult to injury for fantasy managers who streamed Mayer, Ian Thomas found the end zone on his only grab of the day. Mayer has typically played the inline tight end role with Brock Bowers operating as a de facto wide receiver. Because of that, Bowers’ absence today didn’t actually free up that many extra snaps or routes for Mayer. The targets also went to the team’s wide receivers instead of Mayer. Whether or not Bowers plays next week doesn’t make much of a difference for Mayer. He will be, at best, a low-end TE2.

items.name: J.J. McCarthy
items.headline: JJ McCarthy completed 18-of-38 attempts for 173 yards and a touchdown in the Giants’ Week 11 win against the Jaguars, adding seven rushes for 33 yards.
items.analysis: McCarthy looked out of sorts from start to finish. He airmailed a few routine throws and made some questionable decisions from the pocket against a stingy Jacksonville defense. He finished the game 15 percent below his expected completion rate and with a negative EPA per drop back. McCarthy fed Malik Nabers, who managed 55 yards on a dozen targets. He should be a decent streaming option in Week 12 against a Colts defense that has been among the league’s worst over the past month, though Jameis Winston’s tush push involvement has negatively impacted McCarthy’s weekly fantasy prospects.

items.name: Kimani Vidal
items.headline: Kimani Vidal rushed seven times for 36 yards in the Chargers’ Week 11 loss to the Jets, adding two receptions for 18 yards.
items.analysis: Keaton Mitchell’s knee and back injuries allowed Vidal to play a little more often on passing downs. Vidal had a five-yard catch called back due to a penalty, and he was given a carry from the Jets’ eight-yard line. He got open on 2nd-and-goal, a few yards shy of the end zone, late in the game, but Justin Herbert unsuccessfully tried to force a throw to Quentin Johnston in the back of the end zone. Herbert was placed in the NFL’s concussion protocol after the game. Vidal could warrant FLEX consideration against the Patriots next week, but Mitchell and Herbert’s health will factor into things.

items.name: Colton McKivitz
items.headline: Colton McKivitz (leg) was carted to the locker room in the second quarter of Week 11 against the Vikings.
items.analysis: McKivitz was rolled up on from behind and his leg did things it should not do, with the gruesome injury almost assuredly going to end his season. The veteran right tackle had become a staple for the 49ers before his injury, with the team now forced to shuffle things up front for the remainder of the season. Expect more word from the team in the coming days.

items.name: Jack Bech
items.headline: Jack Bech caught 8-of-9 targets for 89 yards and a touchdown in the Raiders’ Week 11 loss to the Broncos.
items.analysis: Bech quietly led the Raiders with seven targets last week but failed to do anything with the sizable role. Though he came up one target shy of the team lead this time around, Bech was the Raiders’ most productive wide receiver or tight end by a wide margin. Fernando Mendoza consistently found him for chunk gains, with four of his grabs resulting in either a first down or a touchdown. Bech’s second score of the year came on a seven-yard out near the goal line. He was initially ruled down at the one, but an expedited review put him on the board. Bech’s role will take a hit if Bowers is able to play in Week 12, but he’s at least challenging Tre Tucker for the WR1 role. He will be a high-risk FLEX play for his Week 12 game against Cleveland.

items.name: Devin Singletary
items.headline: Devin Singletary had one rush for five yards in the Giants’ Week 11 win against the Jaguars, adding one catch for five yards.
items.analysis: Singletary was strictly in a breather back role behind Cam Skattebo, who struggled to get anything going against the Jags. Singletary won’t have any fantasy value unless or until Skattebo misses time in the coming weeks.

items.name: Omarion Hampton
items.headline: Omarion Hampton rushed 14 times for 89 yards in the Chargers’ Week 11 loss to the Jets, adding one reception for four yards.
items.analysis: Hampton ripped off a 30-plus-yard run for the second time in three weeks today, averaging 6.4 yards per carry. He is the Chargers’ best runner, but frequent losing game scripts make his rushing workloads somewhat unreliable. The Chargers called an option run play for Justin Herbert in the red zone late in the game, with Hampton running a couple yards away from him, but Jets defenders recognized it and shut the play down, erasing Hampton’s potential opportunity to catch a pitch and run it in. Keaton Mitchell suffered back and knee injuries and departed early. Justin Herbert entered the NFL’s concussion protocol after the game. Hampton could warrant RB2 treatment against the Patriots next week, but both injuries will impact his projection.

items.name: Cam Skattebo
items.headline: Cam Skattebo had 14 rushes for 34 yards in the Giants’ Week 11 win against the Jaguars, adding three catches for 14 yards.
items.analysis: It was not the most efficient outing for the backflipping Skattebo, who averaged a meager 2.8 yards per touch and was regularly stuffed at or near the line of scrimmage against a stingy Jacksonville front seven. He did, however, manage 14 of the team’s 15 running back carries. Devin Singletary was limited to one carry on the day. Skattebo will be a solid RB2 option in Week 12 against a Cowboys defense allowing the second highest rate of fantasy points per touch to opposing running backs this season.

items.name: Tre Tucker
items.headline: Tre Tucker caught 2-of-10 targets for 50 yards in the Raiders’ Week 11 loss to the Broncos.
items.analysis: Tucker led the Raiders in targets, though several of his looks were uncatchable. He racked up plenty of prayer yards but didn’t do much in the way of actual receiving production. The bulk of his output came on a 39-yard toss from Fernando Mendoza in the fourth quarter. Jack Bech, on the other hand, went for 88 yards and a score on eight targets. With Brock Bowers potentially returning next week, even Tucker’s role as an air yards merchant could take a hit in Week 12. He is likely stuck in the WR5 mix for his upcoming game against the Browns.

items.name: Malachi Fields
items.headline: Malachi Fields caught 2-of-5 targets for 25 yards in the Giants’ Week 11 win against the Jaguars.
items.analysis: Fields logged a pass route on 42 of the team’s 47 drop backs and was third on the team in targets behind Malik Nabers and Cam Skattebo. He now has just three games with at least three receptions in 2026 as a tertiary part of the New York passing offense. Fields will be a deep league flex play in Week 12 against the Colts.

items.name: Keaton Mitchell
items.headline: Keaton Mitchell did not return to the Chargers’ Week 11 loss to the Jets after suffering a knee injury in the second quarter.
items.analysis: Mitchell also suffered a lower-back injury after catching a six-yard pass on the Chargers’ opening drive. He was announced as questionable with the back issue, but was available for kick return duties to begin the following drive. Mitchell disappeared after that and was later announced as questionable to return due to the knee injury in the third quarter. Mitchell does not need to be in 12-team lineups against the Patriots, if active, next week.

items.name: Malik Nabers
items.headline: Malik Nabers caught 7-of-12 targets for 55 yards and a touchdown in the Giants’ Week 11 win against the Jaguars.
items.analysis: Nabers again led the Giants in targets, with no other New York pass catcher seeing more than seven targets on the day. Nabers’ looks were mostly of the dink-and-dunk variety; JJ McCarthy missed his top wideout on a couple easy throws in the second half in a disastrously inaccurate outing for the Giants quarterback. Nabers’ 12 targets were the third most of his 2026 season. The near-total lack of target competition in the New York offense means Nabers has as stable a floor as any receiver in the game. He’ll once again be a top-10 option in Week 12 against the Colts.

items.name: Jalen Nailor
items.headline: Jalen Nailor caught 1-of-5 targets for 16 yards in the Raiders’ Week 11 loss to the Broncos.
items.analysis: Nailor was marginally more involved with Brock Bowers out this week, but it wasn’t enough for him to make a dent in the box score. He did score a touchdown late in the game, but Mendoza was well ahead of the line of scrimmage when the ball left his hands, killing the play. Nailor is still operating as the team’s No. 3 receiver behind Jack Bech and Tre Tucker. With a hard ceiling on his target volume, Nailor is not on the fantasy radar for Week 12.

items.name: David Njoku
items.headline: David Njoku caught 2-of-4 targets for 21 yards in the Chargers’ Week 11 loss to the Jets.
items.analysis: Njoku injured his shoulder on a 13-yard catch-and-run play on the Chargers’ opening drive, but he managed to play through it, leading his position group in targets along the way. The Chargers unsuccessfully tried to involve Njoku on play-action plays twice, including one at the Jets’ 20-yard line. Charlie Kolar caught one pass for eight yards. Oronde Gadsden did nothing. None of these three are on the fantasy football radar next week against the Patriots.

items.name: Mike Washington Jr.
items.headline: Mike Washington rushed nine times for 42 yards in the Raiders’ Week 11 loss to the Broncos.
items.analysis: Washington continued to operate as a change-of-pace back for the Raiders. He only saw two fewer carries than Ashton Jeanty, but the latter earned eight targets and led the team with 90 receiving yards. Washington was not targeted. Without any receiving work to fall back on, Washington is stuck in the RB4 ranks headed into a Week 12 matchup with Cleveland.

items.name: Quentin Johnston
items.headline: Quentin Johnston caught 1-of-2 targets for nine yards in the Chargers’ Week 11 loss to the Jets.
items.analysis: Johnston’s day was mostly quiet, although he did technically earn an end zone target on the Chargers’ sixth drive. The coaching staff tried to involve his post-catch skill set via a trick-play toss, but he was stuffed at the line of scrimmage. Johnston will be a shaky FLEX option against the Patriots next week, even if Justin Herbert clears the NFL’s concussion protocol.

items.name: Trevor Lawrence
items.headline: Trevor Lawrence completed 25-of-47 attempts for 300 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions in the Jaguars’ Week 11 loss to the Giants, adding three rushes for seven yards.
items.analysis: Lawrence finally had a high volume drop back game as the Jaguars chased points in the second half. Sunday was only the second game this season in which Lawrence has had more than 40 attempts. He targeted Parker Washington throughout, connecting with him eight times on 17 targets, including on a second half touchdown that was incorrectly called back on replay review. T-Law’s lone touchdown came on a fourth quarter touchdown toss to Brian Thomas. Lawrence will have a fantastic Week 12 matchup against a struggling Titans secondary that allowed 352 yards and three scores to Lawrence in Week 10.

items.name: Tre' Harris
items.headline: Tre’ Harris caught 2-of-2 targets for 28 yards in the Chargers’ Week 11 loss to the Jets.
items.analysis: Harris snagged a 22-yard pass against busted coverage in this one, but that was not his most consequential play. On the Chargers’ third drive, Harris ran a go route inside the red zone and managed to get behind his coverage defender. Justin Herbert uncorked it, and Harris dove for it, but unfortunately, the pass bounced off his hands in the back of the end zone. Jets EDGE David Bailey committed a roughing the passer penalty on the play, which the Chargers accepted, erasing it from the box score. Harris is a boom-bust FLEX against the Patriots next week, pending Justin Herbert’s (concussion) availability.

items.name: Ashton Jeanty
items.headline: Ashton Jeanty rushed 11 times for 79 yards in the Raiders’ Week 11 loss to the Broncos, adding five catches for 90 yards.
items.analysis: Jeanty broke his first carry of 20 or more yards on a 46-yard sprint into the red zone in the second quarter. The Raiders’ offensive line finally cleared a lane for the former No. 6 overall pick and he ran to daylight before being tracked down by a pair of Broncos defenders inside the five. Per Next Gen Stats, he hit 21.4 MPH on the run, which goes down as his highest top speed since being drafted. Jeanty was also productive through the air. His highlight of the day was a 68-yard receiving touchdown. He beat his man on a wheel route and Fernando Mendoza hit him in stride for a massive score. It was enough for Jeanty to lead the Raiders in receiving for the second straight week. Jeanty’s elite receiving role alone will keep him in the middle of the RB2 ranks for his Week 12 date with the Browns on Sunday Night Football.

items.name: Ladd McConkey
items.headline: Ladd McConkey caught 5-of-8 targets for 37 yards and two touchdowns in the Chargers’ Week 11 loss to the Jets.
items.analysis: McConkey mostly ran short-to-intermediate routes from the slot today. Although he dropped what might have been a first-down pickup on the first drive after halftime, he made the most of his other opportunities. McConkey scored an 11-yard touchdown via an out route early in the fourth quarter, faking an in-breaker that left his coverage defender in the dust. McConkey scored again with roughly two minutes left, shaking Jets LB DeMario Davis on a six-yard hitch-and-go before snagging Justin Herbert’s throw in the end zone. It was an encouraging performance for the Chargers’ No. 1 wide receiver. Unfortunately, the team announced post-game that Herbert has entered the NFL’s concussion protocol. If Herbert is active, McConkey will be back in the WR2 tier next week against the Patriots.

items.name: Braelon Allen
items.headline: Braelon Allen rushed 16 times for 75 yards in the Jets’ Week 11 win over the Chargers, adding one reception for nine yards.
items.analysis: Allen racked up 17 touches in the No. 2 role behind featured starter Breece Hall. The Jets leaned heavily on their backfield today, with Geno Smith playing through an ankle injury. The coaching staff repeatedly called Allen’s number on multiple drives, allowing their burly backup to wear out Chargers defenders. Allen sealed the game with a 15-yard run up the middle, barreling through contact along the way. Allen must be rostered in all fantasy football formats as an elite bench stash at worst. He warrants FLEX consideration next week against the Dolphins.

items.name: Breece Hall
items.headline: Breece Hall rushed 20 times for 86 yards in the Jets’ Week 11 win over the Chargers, adding three receptions for 14 yards and one touchdown.
items.analysis: The Jets’ coaching staff designed a run-heavy game plan with Geno Smith (ankle) playing through an injury. Hall and Braelon Allen split 40 touches between the two of them. Although Allen should be expected to remain regularly involved, and even got a little work inside the Chargers’ 20-yard line, the Jets made sure Hall was in the game when they got near, or inside, the Chargers’ 10-yard line. Hall scored on 2nd-and-goal from the Chargers’ seven-yard line by running a route across the backfield, behind the line, before catching a pass in the flats and turning upfield for the score. Hall is an RB1 against the Dolphins in Week 12.

items.name: Fernando Mendoza
items.headline: Fernando Mendoza completed 18-of-37 passes for 267 yards, three touchdowns, and an interception in the Raiders’ 38-24, Week 11 loss to the Broncos.
items.analysis: Mendoza got off to a dreadfully slow start. The Raiders’ first three drives amounted to 11 net yards and a trio of punts. Mendoza was already down 17 by the time he got the ball back for his fourth series. Mendoza then finally settled in and moved the ball well. His first career passing touchdown came on a well-thrown wheel route to Ashton Jeanty. He led his running back to space and Jeanty did the rest. Mendoza tossed two more scores in the second half, but his comeback bid came to a screeching halt with a fourth-quarter pick-six. Broncos corner Ja’Quan McMillan jumped the route and rather easily took the interception to the house. Things get much easier for Mendoza in Week 12 when he takes on the Browns next week. He will be near the back of the QB2 mix for his third start.

items.name: Mason Taylor
items.headline: Mason Taylor caught 2-of-2 targets for 25 yards in the Jets’ Week 11 win over the Chargers.
items.analysis: Taylor made a nice, leaping grab for 19 yards on the Jets’ third drive before chipping in with a six-yarder on the next drive. He is a reliable starter in real life, but tougher to trust in fantasy football. He is a touchdown-dependent TE2 against the Dolphins next week.

items.name: Kenyon Sadiq
items.headline: Kenyon Sadiq caught 3-of-3 targets for 30 yards in the Jets’ Week 11 win over the Chargers.
items.analysis: The rookie tight end got going with a nine-yard catch between the hashes on the Jets’ second drive. He showed up again on the third drive, snagging a sidearm throw from Geno Smith behind the line of scrimmage before turning upfield and weaving through traffic for a 10-yard gain, bringing the offense into the red zone. He made a similar play on the fourth drive, taking a shallow crosser for 11 yards. Sadiq continues to flash intriguing post-catch traits while splitting time with Mason Taylor. Sadiq is stuck in the TE2 tier, but should play efficiently against the Dolphins next week.

items.name: Brock Bowers
items.headline: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said he is optimistic about Brock Bowers’ (ankle/quad) availability for Week 12 against the Browns.
items.analysis: Kubiak told reporters post-game that Bowers continues to make progress as he rehabs his two injuries. Bowers’ backup, Michael Mayer, caught just one pass for four yards today and picked up a back injury along the way. Hopefully, one or both of them will be good to go next week. Stay tuned.

items.name: Parker Washington
items.headline: Parker Washington caught 8-of-17 targets for 103 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 11 loss to the Giants.
items.analysis: Washington should have been credited with a touchdown on a gorgeous end zone throw from Trevor Lawrence but the refs for some reason called it incomplete after a lengthy replay review. This was the rare negative game script in which Parker could flex his statistical muscles as the Jags’ clear WR1, as the usually-balanced Jacksonville offense tilted pass heavy while chasing points in the second half. No other Jacksonville pass catcher had more than ten targets on the day. Washington will be an elite fantasy option in Week 12 against a wretched Titans secondary that gave up 152 yards and a touchdown to Parker in Week 10.

items.name: Isaiah Likely
items.headline: Isaiah Likely caught 1-of-3 targets for 35 yards in the Giants’ Week 11 win against the Jaguars.
items.analysis: Likely was invisible for most of the game and finished fourth in targets on the day. Along with most other New York pass catchers, Likely suffered from JJ McCarthy’s stunningly inefficient outing in which he was 15 percent below his expected completion rate and averaged a mere 4.6 yards per attempt. Better days will are likely ahead for the Giants tight end, including in Week 12 against the Colts.

items.name: Sterling Shepard
items.headline: Sterling Shepard caught 2-of-2 targets for 24 yards and two touchdowns in the Jets’ Week 11 win over the Chargers.
items.analysis: The Jets’ practice squad veteran seized the moment with Omar Cooper (ankle) and Isaiah Williams (ribs) sidelined today, scoring twice against the Chargers. The first was a sliding scramble-drill snag in the front of the end zone. On the second, Sterling ran a shallow crossing route from the right slot, caught the pass, turned upfield and simply outran Chargers CB Donte Jackson. Shepard is not on the FLEX radar next week against the Dolphins.

items.name: Bhayshul Tuten
items.headline: Bhayshul Tuten had ten rushes for 33 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 11 loss against the Giants, adding three catches for 20 yards.
items.analysis: Tuten came into the game with ankle and knee injuries and was hobbled throughout. He was spotted on the stationary bike a couple times in the first half and limped to the sideline a few times in the third quarter. Clearly nowhere close to 100 percent healthy, Tuten ceded five backfield touches to Chris Rodriguez, who was much more efficient with his opportunities (averaging seven yards per carry). The Jaguars could consider resting their lead back in Week 12 against the Titans. If he plays, Tuten will be a top-15 option.

items.name: Adonai Mitchell
items.headline: Adonai Mitchell caught 2-of-3 targets for 30 yards in the Jets’ Week 11 win over the Chargers.
items.analysis: Mitchell bagged a 21-yard catch via a corner route on the opening drive. He should have bested it with a 40-plus-yard touchdown catch on the Jets’ fifth drive via another corner route, but Geno Smith overthrew him. Brutal. Mitchell’s downfield role lends itself to volatility, but there’s not much more he could have done there. He had his coverage defender beat. Mitchell remains a volatile yet capable FLEX option in Week 12 against the Dolphins.

items.name: Jonah Coleman
items.headline: Jonah Coleman rushed 24 times for 111 yards and three touchdowns in the Broncos’ Week 11 win over the Raiders.
items.analysis: The Coleman takeover was in full force today. He out-carried J.K. Dobbins 24-1 and added four catches for 18 yards. If you couldn’t tell, Coleman also saw all of the goal line work on top of his strong role through the air. He scored two of his touchdowns from inside the five and punched in the third from seven yards out. His longest carry of the day was a 14-yard scamper, but he still managed a respectable 4.6 yards per carry. Coleman fell forward on nearly every carry and broke plenty of tackles, boosting his efficiency numbers without needing a breakaway run. Coleman is a surefire RB1 for his Week 12 date with the Steelers the day after Thanksgiving.

items.name: Garrett Wilson
items.headline: Garrett Wilson caught 3-of-5 targets for 39 yards in the Jets’ Week 11 win over the Chargers.
items.analysis: Wilson generated a decent amount of his receiving yardage after the catch today. He spun off contact and broke another tackle on his 19-yard gain, and also added yards after the catch on a 12-yarder. His first incompletion was a shallow crosser on third down from the Chargers’ 32-yard line, which his coverage defender deserves credit for breaking up. The second incompletion was a desperation heave by Geno Smith under pressure from the Chargers’ six-yard line. The ball was badly overthrown to Wilson, just in front of the end zone, though. He had no chance of catching it. Wilson is a WR2 against the Dolphins in Week 12.

items.name: Geno Smith
items.headline: Geno Smith completed 17-of-21 passes for 176 yards and three touchdowns in the Jets’ 27-24, Week 11 win over the Chargers.
items.analysis: The Jets dialed up a run-heavy game plan with Smith playing through an ankle injury suffered last weekend. The ailment didn’t stop Smith from playing efficiently against the Chargers, though. Smith linked up with Breece Hall and Sterling Shepard (twice) for touchdowns today. Smith overthrew Adonai Mitchell on what could have been a 40-plus-yard end zone target, but luckily, Breece Hall ripped off a 26-yarder that set up one of Smith’s touchdown passes to Shepard, who was elevated from the practice squad this week. Smith warrants QB2 treatment against the Dolphins in Week 12.

items.name: Makai Lemon
items.headline: Makai Lemon caught 1-of-3 targets for one yard in the Eagles’ Week 11 win against the Steelers.
items.analysis: Lemon was a distant afterthought in the Philly offense with DeVonta Smith returning from a hamstring injury and leading the team with 12 targets (57 percent target share). Lemon should not be rostered in most fantasy leagues for the remainder of the season unless Smith again misses time.

items.name: Justin Herbert
items.headline: Justin Herbert completed 15-of-21 passes for 131 yards and two touchdowns in the Chargers’ 24-27, Week 11 loss to the Jets, adding eight rushes for 32 yards and one touchdown.
items.analysis: Immediately after the game, the Chargers announced that Herbert had entered the NFL’s concussion protocol. He took six sacks and eight hits, including one that resulted in a roughing-the-passer penalty after David Bailey hit him in the facemask while trying to disrupt a pass. Bailey had a field day aside from that, registering two quarterback hits and two sacks while forcing a fumble during one of the latter plays. Fortunately for Herbert, an offensive lineman recovered possession. Herbert’s connection with Ladd McConkey improved as the game progressed, leading to two fourth-quarter touchdown passes. Herbert also audibled to a quarterback-keeper from the Jets’ 10-yard line earlier in the game, which he successfully converted for a score. He notably had his left index finger taped up after halftime. If active next week against the Patriots, Herbert will be a high-end QB2. He is backed up by DJ Uiagalelei.

items.name: Jake Elliott
items.headline: Jake Elliott made all four of his field goal attempts in the Eagles’ Week 11 win against the Steelers.
items.analysis: Elliott also made his lone extra point attempt in the victory. Elliott drilled a couple long kicks through the wind in Philadelphia as he continued a solid 2026 campaign. He’s made 11 of his 12 field goal tries on the season. Sunday marked the first time in 2026 in which Elliott made more than two field goal attempts in a game. He’ll be a decent fantasy option in Week 12 against Dallas.

items.name: Jordan Addison
items.headline: Vikings declared QB Kyler Murray, WR Jordan Addison, CB Isaiah Rodgers, QB Max Brosmer, and S Jay Ward inactive for Week 11 against the 49ers.
items.analysis: Addison will miss his second consecutive game while the team gets Jauan Jennings back from his own two-game absence. Expect Tai Felton and Myles Price to fill in for Addison while addition volume remains most likely to concentrate on Justin Jefferson and T.J. Hockenson.

items.name: Mike Evans
items.headline: Mike Evans (Achilles) is active for Week 11 against the Vikings.
items.analysis: Evans returns from three missed games due to an aggravation of the Achilles injury that has plagued him throughout the season, and while he could see his snaps and routes managed, he brings a fantasy WR2 profile to the table in a difficult matchup against the Vikings. Fantasy managers likely did not start him considering the timing of the game this week, hoping he simply makes it through Week 11 healthy. Inactive for the 49ers are QB Kurtis Rourke, OT Enrique Cruz, DE Khalid Kareem, WR Demarcus Robinson, and LB Dre Greenlaw.

items.name: Adam Butler
items.headline: Adam Butler (concussion) will not return to the Raiders’ Week 11 game against the Broncos.
items.analysis: Fellow defensive tackle Tim Keenan (knee) is also done for the day. The Raiders were already one of the best matchups for running backs entering Week 11. Expect the Broncos to lean on Jonah Coleman to close this game out.

items.name: Gunnar Helm
items.headline: Gunnar Helm caught 2-of-3 targets for 14 yards in the Titans’ Week 11 loss to the Cowboys.
items.analysis: 14 of Helm’s 23 catches on the year have come in the past four weeks. It’s been a good start for a second-year pro trying to create some TE2 relevance but not really enough, even in a down year for the position. With all 32 teams active for Week 12 and bye weeks lingering on for only two more Sundays after that, Helm is facing long odds of becoming 12-team league relevant.

items.name: Elic Ayomanor
items.headline: Elic Ayomanor caught 3-of-3 targets for 27 yards in the Titans’ Week 11 loss to the Cowboys.
items.analysis: The three-catch effort was Ayomanor’s fourth straight, though he has exceeded three just once during that timespan. He is also averaging only 46 yards in the process, and has not found the end zone. Translation, Ayomanor’s play has been better, but not better enough you are seriously considering him as a WR4. That is especially true for slates like Week 12 where all 32 teams will be active.

items.name: Calvin Ridley
items.headline: Calvin Ridley caught 5-of-6 targets for 68 yards and a touchdown in the Titans’ Week 11 loss to the Cowboys.
items.analysis: Ridley entered the game with only six catches for 91 scoreless yards on the season, so he nearly doubled his 2026 production. The highlight was a 12-yard touchdown in garbage time that just happened to be one of the most insane throws of the year. Rolling near the sideline, Cam Ward made a cross-field, cross-body pass to find Ridley on the opposite side of the field in the end zone. It was an easy catch. Good stuff, though nearly all of Ridley’s production came with the Titans down multiple scores in the fourth quarter. The offense is playing better, but not better enough that Ridley is set to return to 12-team league relevance.

items.name: Darius Cooper
items.headline: Darius Cooper caught 4-of-5 targets for 59 yards in the Eagles’ Week 11 win against the Steelers.
items.analysis: Cooper led all Eagles pass catchers in catches and receiving yards on a day that saw Joe Milton throw just 21 passes in a run-heavy game. Cooper played a full-time role because Dontayvian Wicks remained sidelined after practicing over the past week. Cooper would profile as an interesting flex play next week against Dallas if Wicks remains out.

items.name: Juwan Johnson
items.headline: Juwan Johnson failed to catch his lone target in the Saints’ Week 11 loss to the Bears.
items.analysis: Johnson saw just one target before exiting in the second half of the Saints’ Week 11 game against the Bears. He did not return to the game and head coach Kellen Moore said the 30-year-old is still being evaluated with a hamstring injury. Johnson has not exceeded three targets for five straight weeks now. He can remain on waiver wires moving forward, though Noah Fant enters the streaming conversation if Johnson misses any time.

items.name: Chimere Dike
items.headline: Chimere Dike caught 6-of-7 targets for 69 yards in the Titans’ Week 11 loss to the Cowboys.
items.analysis: Dike notched a 22-yard gain on a flea flicker on the Titans’ first play from scrimmage and went on to lead the team in receiving as it put up 30 points in a road loss. Good stuff, and Dike’s second pop-up effort in as many weeks, though it was Carnell Tate and Calvin Ridley who made the biggest plays. Second-year fourth-rounder Dike has been one of the biggest beneficiaries as fellow sophomore Cam Ward has finally started to play better, but he’s still having a difficult time cracking the top 48 at receiver. That is going to be especially true for Week 12 against the Jaguars as we get a rare November week with all 32 teams actually playing football.

items.name: Noah Fant
items.headline: Noah Fant caught 2-of-5 targets for 19 yards in the Saints’ Week 11 loss to the Bears.
items.analysis: Fant was the Saints’ leading tight end on the day, seeing the most snaps, targets, and receptions in the tight end room. He saw a pair of red zone targets in the fourth quarter, though Tyler Shough could not connect with him and the drive ended in a turnover-on-downs. Juwan Johnson is his primary receiving competition, but Johnson saw just one target before exiting with a hamstring injury. No Saints tight end needs to be started for fantasy purposes at this point; Fant is in the streaming tight end conversation should Johnson miss any time.

items.name: Ted Hurst
items.headline: Ted Hurst caught 5-of-7 targets for 56 yards and two touchdowns in the Bucs’ Week 11 loss to the Lions.
items.analysis: Hurst brought down a beautiful deep shot right in the bread basket with four seconds left on the clock in the second quarter.
