He double-dipped near the end of the fourth quarter with a quick out at the goal line for his second touchdown of the day. Hurst led the Bucs in all receiving categories, including a 21 percent target share. Hurst has been a boom/bust receiver this year who mostly gives fantasy managers busts, but his Week 11 breakout gives him something to build on. He will be a high-risk FLEX play when the Bucs take on the Panthers next week.

items.name: Devaughn Vele
items.headline: Devaughn Vele caught 7-of-7 targets for 76 yards in the Saints’ Week 11 loss to the Bears.
items.analysis: Vele saw a decrease in opportunities last week with Jordyn Tyson’s activation off injured reserve. However, Tyson saw limited usage in Week 11 against the Bears, with Vele leading Saints receivers in snaps and ranking second in targets, receptions, and yards. Fantasy managers should wait to see if Tyson has any injury limitations moving forward, but Vele would be back in the WR3/4 ranks if Tyson is limited for Week 12 against the Bengals.

items.name: Brevyn Spann-Ford
items.headline: Brevyn Spann-Ford caught 2-of-2 targets for five yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 11 win over the Titans.
items.analysis: The closest thing the Cowboys have to a No. 1 tight end during Jake Ferguson’s ongoing absence, Spann-Ford’s two-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter was just the second of his career. It’s what got the Cowboys to 50 points, which is both cool and also tells you all you need to know about Spann-Ford’s fantasy value. It took the Cowboys running it up late against one of the worst teams in the league for Spann-Ford to find the paint. He remains outside the top 30 in the weekly tight end rankings.

items.name: Ryan Flournoy
items.headline: Ryan Flournoy caught an 11-yard pass in the Cowboys’ Week 11 win over the Titans.
items.analysis: Flournoy had his season-worst outing as the Cowboys had their season-best scoring effort. Go figure. Flournoy’s 11-yard grab came on the opening series only for him to draw zero more targets. That’s a rough development for WR3 desperados with six teams on bye. It is also a faceplant that is unlikely to repeat on Thanksgiving Day against the Eagles even with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens posting crazy usage numbers. The problem for Flournoy is, with all 32 teams active for Week 12, there’s simply no real way to get him into fantasy lineups.

items.name: Jordyn Tyson
items.headline: Jordan Tyson caught 1-of-2 targets for 6 yards in the Saints’ Week 11 loss to the Bears, adding one carry for four yards.
items.analysis: Tyson saw the first offensive touch for the Saints, getting four-yard carry to start things off. He saw just one more touch the rest of the game and was barely on the field for the Saints’ final offensive drive. Though he was cleared off the injury report heading into the weekend, Tyson was dealing with a chest injury last week. Also coming back from a hamstring injury this season, Tyson’s compounding injury list may have played a role in him seeing just half of the offensive snaps against the Bears after getting 13 targets last week. He saw just two targets as Chris Olave took the alpha receiver role back. Fantasy managers should monitor Tyson’s injury status heading into Week 12; he is in the WR3 ranks against the Bengals next week.

items.name: Chris Olave
items.headline: Chris Olave caught 9-of-15 targets for 102 yards in the Saints’ Week 11 loss to the Bears.
items.analysis: Olave saw 15 targets against the Bears, taking back over as the alpha receiver after four targets last week. Tyler Shough had a steady pass funnel to Olave in the intermediate area against a softened Bears secondary. The 26-year-old receiver reeled in nine catches for 102 yards but did not get any targets in the red zone. The Saints often find themselves in pass-heavy game scripts and Olave’s steady diet of targets keeps him in the low-end WR1 ranks for Week 12 against the Bengals.

items.name: Emeka Egbuka
items.headline: Emeka Egbuka caught 2-of-5 targets for 18 yards in the Bucs’ Week 11 loss to the Lions.
items.analysis: There’s not much to say here. It’s just not happening for Egbuka this year. He’s struggling to earn targets and doing nothing when the ball comes his way. Ted Hurst broke out with two scores and 56 yards on a team-high 56 yards today. Egbuka watched on with a measly 15 percent target share. He’s averaging a dismal five yards per target and has forced zero missed tackles. Egbuka will tumble into the WR4 ranks for his Week 12 game against Carolina. With no teams on bye, fantasy managers can feel comfortable sending him to the bench next week.

items.name: Darnell Washington
items.headline: Darnell Washington caught all three of his targets for 22 yards in the Steelers’ Week 11 loss to the Eagles.
items.analysis: Washington again ran fewer pass routes than Pat Freiermuth, who caught all five of his targets on the day. Washington won’t have much in the way of fantasy value until or unless Freiermuth misses time. Washington has five games this season with at least three catches.

items.name: Dallas Goedert
items.headline: Dallas Goedert caught his only target for 38 yards in the Eagles’ Week 11 win against the Steelers.
items.analysis: Goedert ran a pass route on 20 of the team’s 29 drop backs but only saw one look from Joe Milton, who attempted a meager 21 passes and threw for 141 scoreless yards. DeVonta Smith’s return to the Eagles lineup netted him a 57 percent target share. That kind of target domination won’t leave much opportunity for anyone else, including Goedert, who should not be played in 12-team formats for now. The Eagles play the Cowboys in Week 12.

items.name: Javonte Williams
items.headline: Javonte Williams rushed 18 times for 67 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 11 win over the Titans, adding three receptions for 24 yards and a second score.
items.analysis: Williams lost some mop-up work to someone named Jashaun Corbin but cleared 20 touches for the fourth time in five games. The touchdowns were his 11th and 12th of the season, and give him 25 in 27 appearances as a Cowboy. Williams continues to not provide efficiency, but that’s not what’s needed opposite the Cowboys’ elite receiver duo. Williams needs to finish drives at the goal line and do a little bit of everything else, and that’s what he has been doing. Williams will be a low-end RB1 for Thanksgiving Day against the Eagles.

items.name: CJ Donaldson
items.headline: CJ Donaldson rushed one time for five yards in the Saints’ Week 11 loss to the Bears, adding four receptions for 12 yards and a fumble.
items.analysis: Donaldson is head coach Kellen Moore’s pride and joy as a passing-down back in the backfield. The undrafted rookie continues to run routes despite a lack of efficiency and production all season. He was used as a pass blocker and ran 25 routes on the day, more than rookie wideout Jordyn Tyson. Donaldson fumbled on one of his receptions in the second quarter, totaling 12 yards through the air and five on the ground. He has no fantasy value heading into Week 12.

items.name: Chris Godwin
items.headline: Chris Godwin caught all three of his targets for 13 yards in the Bucs’ Week 11 loss to the Lions.
items.analysis: The Bucs leaned on Godwin on third downs, using him to move the chains on two of his three targets. That, however, is a cold comfort for fantasy managers. Godwin hasn’t hit 50 yards in a game this year and is still looking for his first touchdown. If you somehow made it this far into the season with Godwin on your roster, it’s past time to cut bait. He’s somewhere beyond the WR5 ranks heading into Week 12.

items.name: Will Shipley
items.headline: Will Shipley had four rushes for nine yards in the Eagles’ Week 11 win against the Steelers.
items.analysis: Shipley saw some decent fourth quarter run with Saquon Barkley nursing some sort of left arm injury. Shipley would likely take over the Eagles’ lead back if Barkley were to miss time. He should be rostered in most 12-team formats just in case, considering the Eagles take on the Cowboys in Week 12.

items.name: Pat Freiermuth
items.headline: Pat Freiermuth caught all five of his targets for 39 yards in the Steelers’ Week 11 loss to the Eagles.
items.analysis: Freiermuth ran 33 routes on the day while Darnell Washington logged 22 routes and had three targets from Aaron Rodgers. Freiermuth was fourth on the team in targets and receiving yards. Sunday was only the fourth time this season Freiermuth had more than four catches in a game. His waning route participation and the run heaviness of the Pittsburgh offense make Freiermuth nothing more than a desperation option for Week 12 against Denver.

items.name: Tony Pollard
items.headline: Tony Pollard rushed 21 times for 110 yards in the Titans’ Week 11 loss to the Cowboys.
items.analysis: Pollard was held without a catch on one target. Frustrating, though fantasy managers will take Pollard’s third 100-yard rushing effort in four weeks considering the Titans were down 27-9 at halftime. Pollard was “keeping the defense honest” as Cam Ward again showed increased play-making ability in the passing game. Pollard has now cleared 75 yards from scrimmage in five straight contests after doing so just once in the first five games of the season. He is amongst a number of Titans just genuinely playing better, though it is still not translating to victories. That will remain a pipe dream for Week 12, but Pollard will be rematching with a Jaguars defense he got for 99 yards from scrimmage in Week 10. It must be noted that was due in large part to a ridiculous eight receptions, which probably won’t be repeated seeing as Pollard has only 22 on the year.

items.name: Alvin Kamara
items.headline: Alvin Kamara rushed one time for one yard in the Saints’ Week 11 loss to the Bears, adding one reception for one yard and a touchdown.
items.analysis: Kamara was the third running back in the Saints backfield, seeing just six total snaps. He came in for a fourth-and-goal pay at the one-yard line and caught a Tyler Shough pass for the touchdown. Kamara only received one carry for one yard. The Saints have a frustrating backfield committee, with Travis Etienne getting the bulk of the carries, CJ Donaldson running routes, and Kamara coming in for the occasional red zone target. Three touchdowns in his last two games keeps Kamara on the fantasy radar, though he is close to a zero without the red zone opportunities. Kamara is best left on benches for Week 12 against the Bengals.

items.name: Travis Etienne
items.headline: Travis Etienne rushed 14 times for 76 yards in the Saints’ Week 11 loss to the Bears.
items.analysis: The good news is that Etienne started the game for the Saints backfield and received 14-of-16 running back carries. He led the backfield with 21 total snaps as Audric Estime was a healthy scratch against the Bears. Etienne’s best run of the day was a 46-yard carry in the second quarter, where he was chased down and tackled inside the five-yard line. He got two more opportunities and got the ball to the one-yard line, but did not get the touchdown on that drive. Etienne’s lack of passing-game usage and Alvin Kamara’s involvement as a touchdown scorer caps Etienne’s ceiling for fantasy purposes. He belongs in the RB3 ranks for Week 12 against the Bengals.

items.name: Cade Otton
items.headline: Cade Otton caught 1-of-3 targets for eight yards in the Bucs’ Week 11 loss to the Lions.
items.analysis: Otton popped up with a four-catch, eight-target game before the Bucs’ Week 10 bye. He was unable to build on that box score and all but disappeared today. Otton hasn’t topped five catches or 56 yards in a game this year. He has also been held without a touchdown through nearly three months of action. He’s barely even a TE2 for Week 12 against the Panthers.

items.name: George Pickens
items.headline: George Pickens caught 7-of-10 targets for 102 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 11 win over the Titans.
items.analysis: Pickens got off to a slow start this afternoon, seeming to not finish a route or two, but finished molten hot. He is now up to 18 catches for 247 yards and four touchdowns on 28 targets over the past two weeks. Ridiculous numbers, though somewhat sustainable in this narrow, explosive offense. For Thanksgiving Day he will be rematching with an Eagles defense he got for 4/57/1 last month. The Eagles have moved on to their No. 3 quarterback since then and traded a few key contributors. Even with all 32 teams active for Week 12, Pickens will remain in the low-end WR1 mix.

items.name: Kenny Gainwell
items.headline: Kenneth Gainwell rushed four times for 16 yards in the Bucs’ Week 11 loss to the Lions, adding four catches for 43 yards.
items.analysis: Bucs coach Todd Bowles told reporters on Monday that Gainwell could see more touches going forward to help keep Bucky Irving fresh. That couldn’t have been further from the truth today as Irving out-touched Gainwell 21-8. Gainwell did, however, post his second-best receiving line of the year. His only better game came two weeks ago, before Tampa’s bye, against the Bears. Gainwell might finally be developing a receptions-based floor, but a two-game sample can’t be taken as gospel. Gainwell will remain on the RB3/4 border when he takes on the Panthers next week.

items.name: Zavion Thomas
items.headline: Zavion Thomas caught 2-of-3 targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in the Bears’ Week 11 win over the Saints, adding one carry for 30 yards.
items.analysis: Thomas was the subject of multiple explosive plays against the Saints. He saw just offensive 10 snaps, but Ben Johnson schemed up multiple plays to utilize the rookie receiver’s speed. A 40-yard reception in the third quarter and 30-yard rush in the second quarter highlighted a career-best day for Thomas. He is still not fantasy relevant, but his usage should be monitored as the Bears scheme up more plays for him.

items.name: Jaylen Warren
items.headline: Jaylen Warren had nine rushes for 28 yards in the Steelers’ Week 11 loss to the Eagles, adding two catches for one yard.
items.analysis: Warren was snuffed out by a swarming Philadelphia defense that appeared committed to stopping the Pittsburgh rushing attack and forcing Aaron Rodgers to beat them (he did not). Warren ran 36 routes on the day to Rico Dowdle’s 16 routes, though it was Dowdle who led the backfield with five targets. Warren now has back-to-back down games in a collapsing Steelers offense. Things won’t get much easier in Week 12 against the Broncos.

items.name: Rico Dowdle
items.headline: Rico Dowdle had five rushes for 15 yards in the Steelers’ Week 11 loss to the Eagles, adding four catches for 19 yards.
items.analysis: Jaylen Warren, meanwhile, managed 29 yards on nine rushing attempts and caught one of his two targets. Dowdle got quite a lot of second half playing time, finishing the game with 16 pass routes to 36 routes for Warren. Dowdle is good for 7-10 touches per week in the low-octane Pittsburgh offense, making him a desperation flex option in deeper formats.

items.name: Kalif Raymond
items.headline: Kalif Raymond caught 1-of-4 targets for 14 yards in the Bears’ Week 11 win over the Saints.
items.analysis: Raymond was targeted four times, including an incomplete end zone target on fourth down in the first half. He caught one of his targets for 14 total yards, though he had the second-most wide receiver snaps on the team. Raymond is still involved as the starting outside receiver opposite Rome Odunze but has boom-or-bust WR5 viability at best heading into Week 12

items.name: Justice Hill
items.headline: Justice Hill rushed six times for 69 yards and a touchdown in the Ravens’ Week 11 loss to the Panthers, adding four receptions for 27 additional yards.
items.analysis: Hill fell victim to one of the worst rules in football when he fumbled inside the Panthers’ five-yard line on a 36-yard run and watched the ball run out of the end zone. The turnover resulted in a touchback that rewarded the Panthers with the ball at Baltimore’s 20-yard line, but Hill would get his revenge on the following drive when he ran in a 19-yard touchdown to put the Ravens up 26-22 before halftime. Despite the gaffe early in the game, Hill was very efficient in this one, averaging a solid 9.6 yards per touch while being a difference-maker both on the ground and through the air. He has now seen double-digit opportunities in four straight weeks, but he remains difficult to trust as anything more than an RB4/Flex play, especially with Derrick Henry around to vulture any short-yardage touchdowns.

items.name: Baker Mayfield
items.headline: Baker Mayfield completed 20-of-33 passes for 187 yards and two touchdowns in the Bucs’ 31-21, Week 11 loss to the Lions.
items.analysis: Mayfield appeared to be unlikely to suit up for today’s game when the week started, but a pair of limited practices was enough to get him on the field today. Things got off to a scary start when he was crushed for a sack-fumble on his first dropback of the day. He would go on to take four sacks for a total loss of 33 yards. Somehow, Mayfield looked more than willing as a runner, adding 36 yards on six carries. It was ultimately a solid fantasy outing from Mayfield, assisted by a garbage-time touchdown to Ted Hurst. A date with the Panthers next week will keep Mayfield in the QB2 mix next week, but he’s far from the best streaming option available to most fantasy managers.

items.name: Mitchell Evans
items.headline: Mitchell Evans caught 5-of-5 targets for 44 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 11 win over the Ravens.

items.name: CeeDee Lamb
items.headline: CeeDee Lamb caught 11-of-12 targets for 132 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 11 win over the Titans.
items.analysis: Lamb’s fifth 100-yard effort of the season and second in three weeks put him above 1,000 yards for the sixth consecutive season, good for a new Cowboys franchise record. Simply abusing overmatched Titans CB Cor’Dale Flott, it is barely an exaggeration to say Lamb was open at will against the Titans’ overmatched defense. The Eagles will be a slightly tougher Thanksgiving Day matchup, but not by much. Enjoy the holiday with your WR1.

items.name: Colston Loveland
items.headline: Colston Loveland caught 3-of-3 targets for 29 yards and a touchdown in the Bears’ Week 11 win over the Saints.
items.analysis: Loveland had the best fantasy day of all the Bears’ pass-catchers, catching all three of his targets and scoring a touchdown. He was primarily targeted in the flat, scoring his touchdown after catching a Caleb Williams pass and hurdling a Saints defender to walk in for the 15-yard score. The 22-year-old has recovered after a rough start to the season and belongs in the TE1 ranks for a Thanksgiving day matchup against the Lions.

items.name: Carnell Tate
items.headline: Carnell Tate caught 2-of-5 targets for 58 yards and a touchdown in the Titans’ Week 11 loss to the Cowboys.
items.analysis: Active for the first time since Week 7, the No. 4 overall pick caught a -1 yard pass in the first quarter before adding a 59-yard touchdown in the third. In between, he drew a 38-yard DPI in the end zone to set the Titans up at the one-yard line. On his score, Tate appeared to be down by contact near mid-field, but he realized he had not been touched and got up and sprinted to the end zone. Heady stuff, though we would have liked to see more targets. Tate thankfully avoided setbacks with his shoulder injury, and is now ready to slot into the WR24-30 range for a tough Week 12 matchup with the Jags. Tate would be a safer WR2 were it not a 32-team slate for the holiday week.

items.name: Jared Goff
items.headline: Jared Goff completed 20-of-28 passes for 279 yards and two touchdowns in the Lions’ 31-21, Week 11 win over the Bucs.
items.analysis: A long Bucs drive limited the Lions to one possession in the first quarter. Jake Bates missed his field goal try, resulting in a slow start for Detroit. They shook the rust off in the second quarter and cruised past the Bucs over the next three frames. Because Tampa’s offense didn’t put up much of a fight, Goff’s passing volume was limited once again. He hasn’t thrown for more than 32 passes in a game since Week 4. The good news for fantasy managers is that the Lions take on the Bears in what should be a Thanksgiving afternoon shootout next week. Goff topped 330 yards in both of his games against the Bears last year. He will be a top-half QB1 for Week 12.

items.name: Rome Odunze
items.headline: Rome Odunze caught 4-of-4 targets for 45 yards in the Bears’ Week 11 win over the Saints.
items.analysis: Odunze was involved in the intermediate area for the Bears, making a 19-yard grab on the first drive. He made a 16-yard catch later in the first half, getting tackled inside the five-yard line and setting up a touchdown. His four targets were tied for the most on the team, with Caleb Williams only attempting 23 passes against the Saints. Odunze’s downfield targets keep him in the FLEX conversation for fantasy purposes. He is in the WR3/FLEX ranks for Week 12 against the Lions.

items.name: Mark Andrews
items.headline: Mark Andrews caught 2-of-3 targets for 14 yards in the Ravens’ Week 11 loss to the Panthers.
items.analysis: Andrews’ disappointing performance comes a week after he caught eight targets for 82 yards in Jacoby Brissett’s debut with the Ravens. The Ravens worked to get all three tight ends involved in this one, as Andrews, Matthew Hibner, and Josh Cuevas combined to get eight targets, with Andrews and Cuevas both getting three looks. Andrews’ promising performance against the Chargers gave fantasy managers a reason to hope for more this week, especially with six teams on bye. With all 32 teams playing in Week 12, it’s safe to say Andrews shouldn’t be treated as anything more than a desperation play on the road against the Texans.

items.name: Rashod Bateman
items.headline: Rashod Bateman caught 2-of-6 targets for 67 yards and a touchdown in the Ravens’ Week 11 loss to the Panthers.
items.analysis: Bateman’s touchdown pass came on a play from the wildcat that started with Derrick Henry receiving the snap. While Henry handed the ball off to Justice Hill, who then pitched to Jacoby Brissett, Bateman streaked down the field, leaving every member of the Panthers’ secondary in the dust as they attempted to dissect the trick play called by Ravens OC Declan Doyle. Brissett delivered a slightly underthrown ball to Bateman, but it proved inconsequential given the distance between Bateman and the nearest defender. The 26-year-old receiver hauled in the pass without any trouble and made his way into the end zone to give the Ravens an early 9-0 lead. Bateman would only catch one more pass the rest of the day, but his six targets now give him 11 in his two games with Brissett under center. While it’s hard to imagine Bateman having any reliable fantasy value this season, he could be worth a desperation dart throw in deeper leagues in Week 12 against the Texans.

items.name: Zay Flowers
items.headline: Zay Flowers caught 8-of-11 targets for 97 yards in the Ravens’ Week 11 loss to the Panthers.
items.analysis: In two games with Jacoby Brissett, Flowers has caught 14-of-18 targets for 171 scoreless yards. This is great news for fantasy managers, who saw Flowers’ fantasy value in the tank when the duo of Tyler Huntley and Joe Fagnano led him to just six yards over a two-week stretch. Brissett’s arrival has been good news for Flowers, who ripped off two gains of 20-plus yards on the afternoon and led the Ravens in both targets and receiving yards. He will be a high-end WR2 next week against a Texans secondary that has proven vulnerable this season.

items.name: Luther Burden
items.headline: Luther Burden caught 2-of-3 targets for 10 yards in the Bears’ Week 11 win over the Saints, adding one carry for three yards.
items.analysis: Burden had little involvement in a low-volume passing day for the Bears. He saw three of Caleb Williams’ 23 passing attempts on a day where no Bears pass-catcher had more than four targets. Rookie Zavion Thomas saw the splash plays on the day as Burden had short-yardage usage to pick up quick first downs out of the slot. The first half game script did not favor Burden, but given his elite production in recent weeks, he is back in the low-end WR2 ranks for a Thanksgiving day game against the Lions.

items.name: Amon-Ra St. Brown
items.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown caught 5-of-6 targets for 37 yards and a touchdown in the Lions’ Week 11 win over the Bucs.
items.analysis: With only 28 attempts for Jared Goff, there simply wasn’t much receiving work to go around. St. Brown still led the Lions in targets alongside Sam LaPorta. Despite the quiet day, fantasy managers will be satisfied with St. Brown’s eighth touchdown of the year. He scored No. 8 on an easy strike over the middle of the field from 14 yards out. With a shootout versus the Bears scheduled for Thanksgiving, St. Brown is set for elite fantasy numbers in Week 12.

items.name: Cam Ward
items.headline: Cam Ward completed 21-of-30 passes for 248 yards and two touchdowns in the Titans’ 51-30, Week 11 loss to the Cowboys, adding two rushes for three yards and a third score.
items.analysis: Recalled from fantasy benches for streamer duties vs. the defense-less Cowboys, Ward had his first three-score game of the year. It was also his third straight multi-score effort after managing just one in first seven starts. No. 3 was a 12-yard garbage time connection with Calvin Ridley, but that description doesn’t really do it justice. Flushed from the pocket and seemingly running out of bounds, Ward instead made like prime Aaron Rodgers and threw the ball across his body, across the middle of the field into Ridley’s arms like it was a loaf of bread. It was the most impressive play of his young NFL career, and an exclamation point on his recent improved play. Today was a soft matchup, but that was not the case for the Jaguars in Week 10, with whom Ward must now rematch in Week 12. Despite his hot streak, Ward will find himself outside the top 20 for Thanksgiving week because of his tough setup and all 32 teams being active for the holiday slate.

items.name: Derrick Henry
items.headline: The Baltimore Banner’s Giana Han reports Derrick Henry cleared concussion protocol after Week 11’s loss to the Panthers.
items.analysis: Henry didn’t return to the field after exiting in the fourth quarter to be evaluated for a concussion, but it was reportedly shortly after that he cleared the league’s concussion protocol. Henry rushed 13 times for 94 yards and a touchdown in Sunday’s loss while catching another four passes for 17 yards. Barring any setback, we would expect him to be good to go for Week 12’s game against the Texans.

items.name: Tyler Bass
items.headline: Tyler Bass converted on 4-of-5 field goal attempts in the Bills’ Week 11 win over the Dolphins.
items.analysis: Bass was the beneficiary of the Bills’ offense continuing to stall out once they got into the Dolphins’ territory. Bass made field goals of 43, 54, 40, and 28 yards on the day. However, the 29-year-old did miss a 54-yarder in the third quarter, which was his first missed field goal of the season. He’s now 24-of-25 on the season after missing all of last year with an injury.

items.name: Kyle Monangai
items.headline: Kyle Monangai rushed eight times for 18 yards in the Bears’ Week 11 win over the Saints.
items.analysis: Monangai played for the first time since suffering a turf toe injury in Week 4, getting 17 snaps on the day. He had five less carries and nine less snaps than D’Andre Swift as Salvon Ahmed also got involved with six carries for 33 yards. Monangai’s first snap was to run a route on third-and-long on the Bears’ first possession while he started in the backfield on the second drive. The 24-year-old had no receptions and just one red zone carry on the day, though his snap share and touch split with Swift was at pre-injury levels. Fantasy managers should anticipate less Ahmed usage in future weeks; Monangai should be in the RB4 ranks for Week 12 against the Lions.

items.name: Greg Dulcich
items.headline: Greg Dulcich caught 2-of-7 targets for 12 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 11 loss to the Bills.
items.analysis: Dulcich saw the second-most targets on the team but ran a route on just 16 of the Dolphins’ 36 dropbacks. It’s nice to see Kyle McCord target him so often when he’s on the field, but Dulcich is not producing enough to be under consideration in fantasy leagues.

items.name: Joe Milton
items.headline: Joe Milton completed 11-of-21 attempts for 141 yards in the Eagles’ Week 11 win against the Steelers, adding five rushes for six yards.
items.analysis: Milton was in game manager mode as the Eagles maintained a lead throughout thanks to the team’s suffocating defense against Aaron Rodgers and the collapsing Steelers offense. Milton was not asked to do much, and he didn’t. He targeted DeVonta Smith — returning from a long injury absence — a team-high 12 times, missing him on a couple routine throws in the second half. Unless the Eagles face runaway negative game script, Milton won’t hold much fantasy value. He gets a good matchup next week against the Cowboys.

items.name: Chris Bell
items.headline: Chris Bell caught 1-of-4 targets for eight yards in the Dolphins’ Week 11 loss to the Bills.
items.analysis: Bell was questionable to return to the game after suffering a chest injury in the second quarter; however, he did return and ran 20 routes on 36 dropbacks, which was the third-most on the team. Bell still has a decent future given his pre-knee-injury upside, but it’s tough to roster him in redraft leagues right now.

items.name: Germie Bernard
items.headline: Germie Bernard caught 6-of-10 targets for 40 yards in the Steelers’ Week 11 loss to the Eagles.
items.analysis: Bernard led the team in both pass routes and targets. He didn’t do much with his opportunity, which mostly included quick check-down passes from Aaron Rodgers. Roman Wilson returned from a finger injury and caught three balls for 43 yards while DK Metcalf was ejected for unsportsmanlike conduct in the third quarter. Max Hurleman, meanwhile, led the Steelers in receiving yards and caught the team’s lone touchdown while running just 15 routes. Bernard, who has 97 yards over his past four games, will be a deep league PPR option next week against the Broncos.

items.name: Malik Washington
items.headline: Malik Washington caught 3-of-6 targets for 30 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 11 loss to the Bills.
items.analysis: He also added two rushes for 11 yards. Washington made a tremendous one-handed catch on a fourth-down conversion late in the game, but there wasn’t much else happening for him on the day. His six targets were the third-most on the team, but he ran a route on 32 of the team’s 36 dropbacks, which was the most on the team. He’s a risky FLEX play against the Jets next week.

items.name: Bhayshul Tuten
items.headline: Bhayshul Tuten exited the field in Week 11 against the Giants.
items.analysis: Tuten was dinged up on the first play of the game and was later seen riding the exercise bike on the sideline. He came into the game battling ankle and knee issues that limited him in practice this week. He may have aggravated the injuries. Chris Rodriguez would take over as the team’s lead back if Tuten misses time.

items.name: Jameson Williams
items.headline: Jameson Williams caught all four of his targets for 93 yards and a touchdown in the Lions’ Week 11 win over the Bucs.
items.analysis: Williams busted his two-game slump with a 57-yard score in the third quarter. As he tends to do, Williams simply blew by the Bucs’ defense on a deep shot and saw nothing but grass in front of him. Despite the strong fantasy outing, Williams still finished fourth on the team in targets, behind all of the usual suspects. Williams has been one of the most frustrating fantasy options this year, but managers have to stick with him through the lulls to find spike weeks like today. He will be in the WR2 mix for a potential shootout with the Bears next week.

items.name: D'Andre Swift
items.headline: D’Andre Swift rushed 13 times for 51 yards and a fumble in the Bears’ Week 11 win over the Saints, adding two receptions for eight yards and a touchdown.
items.analysis: Swift got the first three touches of the game for the Bears, operating as the lead back with Kyle Monangai back. His snaps took a dip, especially after a fourth quarter fumble. A shovel pass from Caleb Williams for receiving score in the first half saved his fantasy production as Bears drives stalled frequently against the Saints. The good news is that Swift is still the lead back, though Monangai’s return will eat into his workload. Swift belongs in the fantasy RB2 ranks for a Week 12 Thanksgiving matchup against the Lions.

items.name: Roman Wilson
items.headline: Roman Wilson caught 3-of-6 targets for 43 yards in the Steelers’ Week 11 loss to the Eagles.
items.analysis: Returning from a finger injury, Wilson ran a route on 41 of the team’s 59 drop backs and was second to Max Hurleman in receptions and receiving yards. Aaron Rodgers nearly connected with the speedy Wilson on a long ball in the second half. Wilson’s playing time may have been affected by DK Metcalf’s second half ejection after repeated fights with Philadelphia defenders. Wilson will have some deep league value in the run-first Steelers offense, including next week against the Broncos.

items.name: Dawson Knox
items.headline: Dawson Knox caught 2-of-3 targets for 31 yards in the Bills’ Week 11 win over the Dolphins.
items.analysis: Despite Dalton Kincaid not being active on Sunday, Knox was not a huge part of the passing game. He did run a route on 29 of 52 dropbacks, which was fourth-most on the team, but he simply wasn’t targeted much. Kincaid is expected to return on Thursday against the Chiefs, which keeps Knox off the fantasy radar.

items.name: Keon Coleman
items.headline: Keon Coleman caught 2-of-4 targets for 17 yards in the Bills’ Week 11 win over the Dolphins.
items.analysis: Despite the return of Tyrell Shavers, who is a strong blocking receiver, Coleman ran a route on 45 of the team’s 52 dropbacks and played on 63 of 78 snaps. Both of those were a team-high. It didn’t result in fantasy success, but it seems like Coleman has evolved into the “dirty work” receiver in Buffalo who can move the chains with tough catches and pick up key blocks in the running game. He’s not a fantasy option next week against the Chiefs.

items.name: Simi Fehoko
items.headline: Simi Fehoko caught 1-of-5 targets for two yards and a touchdown in Arizona’s Week 11 loss to the Chiefs.
items.analysis: He added three carries for seven yards. The 2021 fifth-round pick has suddenly become important at work, playing 47-of-49 snaps, but that does not mean he needs to be rostered in all but the deepest leagues given how poorly this offense is running.

items.name: Trey McBride
items.headline: Trey McBride caught 9-of-14 targets for 54 yards in Arizona’s Week 11 loss to the Chiefs.
items.analysis: It sure does feel hard to find overall TE1 upside the past few weeks with Michael Wilson on the shelf. McBride was peppered with targets in the blowout loss but was mostly just an underneath option. His long gain went for just nine yards. McBride will remain a TE1 next week against the Commanders, but it’s fair to question the ceiling.

items.name: DJ Moore
items.headline: DJ Moore caught 8-of-10 targets for 91 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 11 win over the Dolphins.
items.analysis: There was a scary moment in the second quarter when Moore jumped to try and break up an interception and came down hard, hyperextending his knee. He went right into the locker room, and it seemed like he might be done for the day, but he came back out in time for the next drive. There’s a chance the Bills give him a lighter week of practice with the Chiefs coming up on Thursday, but Moore will need to be a big part of the game plan if Buffalo is going to win that game.

items.name: Caleb Williams
items.headline: Caleb Williams completed 15-of-23 passes for 181 yards, two touchdowns, and an interception in the Bears’ 21-13, Week 11 win over the Saints.
items.analysis: The Bears offense had its usual explosiveness, but struggled to finish drives. Williams’ mobility was on full display, using his legs to buy time and find receivers while adding 13 rushing yards before a pair of end-of-game kneels. He lofted up a fourth down end zone target to Kalif Raymond that was broken up in the first quarter and threw an interception in the second quarter. The drives that did end in touchdowns for the Bears in the first half came on a Williams shovel pass to D’Andre Swift and a toss to Colston Loveland in the flat he ran in for the score. Williams had completions of over 10 yards to five different receivers as he continued to push the ball downfield. His high-risk, high-reward style of play lends it self to splash plays to boost fantasy production. Williams will be in the low-end QB1 ranks for a Thanksgiving day matchup against the Lions.

items.name: Harrison Wallace
items.headline: Harrison Wallace caught 4-of-7 targets for 57 yards in Arizona’s Week 11 loss to the Chiefs.
items.analysis: It was the 2026 UDFA’s third game in the pros. He played 29-of-49 snaps. Wallace caught Arizona’s longest gain of the day, a 25-yarder. We guess we have to take the idea that Wallace could move towards FLEX value seriously as they move on to the Commanders in Week 12, but it is hard to imagine much fantasy value coming out of this team for the rest of the year outside of Trey McBride.

items.name: Chuba Hubbard
items.headline: Chuba Hubbard rushed 27 times for 120 yards and two touchdowns in the Panthers’ Week 11 win over the Ravens.

items.name: Jahmyr Gibbs
items.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs rushed 23 times for 98 yards in the Lions’ Week 11 win over the Bucs, adding four catches for 20 yards.
items.analysis: The Lions did a good job bottling Gibbs up for three quarters, but you can only keep him out of the end zone for so long. Gibbs punched in a one-yard score late in the fourth quarter to functionally seal the game. After a quick turnover-on-downs from the Bucs, he put the final nail in the coffin with another goal line touchdown. Gibbs entered the game tied for the league lead in touchdowns from scrimmage at 13. Now Christian McCaffrey needs to find the end zone twice to keep pace. Still putting up gaudy numbers every week, Gibbs is the unquestioned RB1 overall for his Week 12 game against the Bears.

items.name: Khalil Shakir
items.headline: Khalil Shakir caught 5-of-9 targets for 101 yards in the Bills’ Week 11 win over the Dolphins.
items.analysis: Shakir led the team in receiving yards and was second on the team in targets. He hauled in a 38-yard reception and a 32-yard reception, which fueled his day. One of those was on a long catch-and-run, and the other was on a broken play where Josh Allen was rolling out of the pocket and found Shakir. The 26-year-old receiver has a knack for getting open in space and will always be a big producer for Buffalo when they play defenses that like to play a lot of zone.

items.name: Aaron Rodgers
items.headline: Aaron Rodgers completed 30-of-44 attempts for 227 yards and one touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 11 loss to the Eagles, adding five rushes for 29 yards.
items.analysis: Rodgers, as he has been for most of the season, was wildly inefficient against the Eagles. He posted a -4.1 EPA, barely better than Joe Milton. Rodgers again was in check-down mode, only trying a couple deep shots and holding the ball time and again. Rodgers took five sacks and narrowly avoided a handful of others as the Steelers offensive line was overwhelmed for the second straight week. Coming into Week 11, only Daniel Jones and Baker Mayfield had lower drop backs EPAs than Rodgers. He’ll be a superflex option in Week 12 against the Broncos.

items.name: Derrick Henry
items.headline: Derrick Henry rushed 13 times for 94 yards and a touchdown in the Ravens’ Week 11 loss to the Panthers, adding four receptions for 17 additional yards.

items.name: Jacoby Brissett
items.headline: Jacoby Brissett completed 24-of-37 passes for 276 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Ravens’ 35-33, Week 11 loss to the Panthers.

items.name: Tyler Allgeier
items.headline: Tyler Allgeier rushed seven times for 23 yards in Arizona’s Week 11 loss to the Chiefs.
items.analysis: He out-snapped Bam Knight 26-23 in a committee that has managed to keep even a slim amount of fantasy value from coming to fruition. Allgeier has 259 rushing yards on the season if you exclude the week they played the Dallas Cowboys.

items.name: Ty Johnson
items.headline: Ty Johnson caught 7-of-8 targets for 55 yards in the Bills’ Week 11 win over the Dolphins.
items.analysis: Despite his status as a running back, Johnson’s value to the Bills is as a receiver and pass blocker. He was a crucial option for Josh Allen when under pressure today, and Johnson consistently makes one or two big receptions in the screen game each week. His eight targets were third on the team this week, as were his 55 yards rushing. Still, it would be Ray Davis who would get a lot of rushing value if James Cook were ever to get hurt, which limits Johnson’s appeal as a stash option.

items.name: DeVonta Smith
items.headline: DeVonta Smith caught 5-of-12 targets for 41 yards in the Eagles’ Week 11 win against the Steelers.
items.analysis: Returning from a two-month hamstring injury, Smith led the Eagles with a 57 percent target share. No other Eagles pass catcher saw more than five targets. Joe Milton missed a couple easy completions to Smith, one of which would have led to a chunk gain. It was a tough run-out for Smith, who looked fully healthy. Smith will be a solid option next week against a terrible Dallas secondary that was carved up by Cam Ward in Week 11.

items.name: James Cook
items.headline: James Cook rushed 22 times for 89 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 11 win over the Dolphins.
items.analysis: With this effort, Cook has set an NFL record with nine consecutive games with 75+ rushing yards and a touchdown. Only two other players in NFL history had done it for eight games in a row. It’s the perfect encapsulation of Cook’s fantasy value on this Buffalo offense. The presence of Josh Allen will limit the number of touchdowns and ceiling games Cook puts together, but he remains one of the most consistent producers at the running back position in fantasy football. He remains an RB1, even in a tough matchup against the Chiefs.

items.name: Tyler Shough
items.headline: Tyler Shough completed 25-of-42 attempts for 222 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Saints’ 21-13 Week 11 loss to the Bears, adding three rushes for 34 yards.
items.analysis: Shough and the Saints offense got off to another slow start. After a scoreless first quarter, Shough threw an interception in New Orleans territory in the second quarter. He was able to later connect with Alvin Kamara for a fourth-and-goal touchdown pass while a 30-yard scramble in the two minute drill led to a Saints field goal at the end of the half. The second half saw little offense from the Saints as they scored just one field goal the rest of the game. Shough failed to connect with Noah Fant on a crucial red zone fourth down and took a 13-yard sack in the two-minute drill at the end of the game. He averaged 5.3 yards per attempt in another inefficient showing. Shough belongs in the fantasy QB2 ranks for a Week 12 matchup against the Bengals.

items.name: Bryce Young
items.headline: Bryce Young completed 22-of-30 passes for 254 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the Panthers’ 35-33, Week 11 win over the Ravens.
items.analysis: Young and the Panthers had a much-needed bounce-back performance in Sunday’s win over the Ravens. After struggling to move the ball in Week 10’s win over the Saints, Young and the Panthers overcame an early safety on their opening drive to string together a nice five-play, 79-yard drive in the first quarter that included a 35-yard completion to Jalen Coker, which was followed by a 23-yard touchdown pass to tight end Mitchell Evans. In the second quarter, Young connected with Tetairoa McMillan for a seven-yard touchdown pass in the end zone to put the Panthers up 22-19 after Chuba Hubbard ran in a two-point conversion. Young’s lone interception came on another end zone target to McMillan in the third quarter, but the mistake didn’t prove too costly, as the Ravens went three-and-out on the ensuing drive. Young took back-to-back sacks to start a drive in the fourth quarter after the Panthers’ defense forced a turnover of their own, spoiling a chance to go up by two possessions, but the Panthers’ defense held up its end of the bargain late when it forced an interception of Jacoby Brissett to end any hopes of a comeback attempt. With all 32 teams playing in Week 12, Young will be on the mid-to-high-end QB2 radar next week against the Buccaneers.

items.name: Zonovan Knight
items.headline: Bam Knight rushed seven times for 35 yards in Arizona’s Week 11 loss to the Chiefs, adding a catch on his only target for 10 yards.
items.analysis: Knight had three touches for three yards at halftime, but turned in a half-reasonable FLEX line once the Cardinals started running clock in the fourth quarter. He had 23 snaps to Tyler Allgeier’s 26. Even against the Commanders, this feels like a tough click in Week 12.

items.name: Bucky Irving
items.headline: Bucky Irving rushed 18 times for 68 yards and a touchdown in the Bucs’ Week 11 loss to the Lions, adding three catches for 32 yards.
items.analysis: It was a tumultuous day for fantasy managers who watched this one from start to finish. Irving broke off an 80-yard touchdown at the top of the third quarter, only for it to be called back via a holding penalty. Irving was leveled by Brian Banch a few plays later and appeared to suffer an injury. Trainers took the field to give him a look, but Irving eventually popped back up and was good to go a few plays later. Irving would go on to punch in a one-yard score later in the third quarter. Per usual, Irving operated as the unquestioned lead back, out-carrying Kenneth Gainwell 18-4. Irving has worked his way into the RB1 ranks ahead of his Week 12 game against the Panthers.

items.name: Kyle McCord
items.headline: Kyle McCord completed 12-of-33 passes for 102 yards and an interception in the Dolphins’ 26-9, Week 11 loss to the Bills.
items.analysis: McCord didn’t look as bad as the stats suggest, but it was not a great game. He overthrew some receivers on key plays, but his receivers also had some drops, and the Buffalo secondary looked good as well. The rookie should find things a little easier next week against the Jets, but he’s still not a recommended option in fantasy leagues.

items.name: Saquon Barkley
items.headline: Saquon Barkley had 17 rushes for 75 yards and a touchdown in the Eagles’ Week 11 win against the Steelers.
items.analysis: Barkley broke a few decent runs in the first half and was mostly bottled up in the second half against a tough Pittsburgh rush defense. He left the game in the fourth quarter with what appeared to be a left arm injury, though it’s unclear if the injury was serious. Barkley, who ran a route on 10 of 28 drop backs, did not see a target. With Joe Milton at QB, Barkley is nothing more than a touchdown-dependent RB2 going forward, including next week against the Cowboys.

items.name: Josh Johnson
items.headline: Josh Johnson completed 18-of-31 passes for 155 yards and a touchdown in Arizona’s 34-7, Week 11 loss to the Chiefs.
items.analysis: We watched this game and can say: It definitely happened. Johnson took three sacks and didn’t look laughably bad at any point, but he also could not get real fantasy production out of the motley crew around him. Assuming Carson Beck (back) can’t get off the mat next week, Johnson would seem to be in line to start against the Commanders next Sunday. That is not an endorsement of actually using him in fantasy football.

items.name: Noah Gray
items.headline: Noah Gray caught 3-of-5 targets for 21 yards in Kansas City’s Week 11 win over the Cardinals.
items.analysis: Gray played 45-of-70 snaps, more than any receiver or tight end but Travis Kelce and Rashee Rice. He remains just a low-end TE2 sort of bet, but it was Gray’s highest target total of the year.

items.name: Max Hurleman
items.headline: Max Hurleman caught 6-of-7 targets for 61 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 11 loss against the Eagles.
items.analysis: Hurleman, a converted quarterback who did not have a reception coming into Week 11, led all Steelers pass catchers in receptions and receiving yards, making an impressive touchdown grab late in the fourth quarter. Hurleman ran a route on just 15 of the team’s 58 drop backs on the day. He might have seen more playing time because DK Metcalf kept fighting with Eagles defenders until he was ejected in the third quarter. Hurleman remains a long way from fantasy relevance in any case.

items.name: Darius Alexander
items.headline: Giants declared DL Darius Alexander, S Jason Pinnock, OL Josh Sills, OT J.C. Davis, RB Greg Desrosiers, CB Nic Jones, and TE Thomas Fidone inactive for Week 11 against the Jaguars.
items.analysis: Alexander is a surprising healthy scratch for Week 11. The Giants will take on the ultra-efficient Jaguars offense with several defensive starters sidelined. It should be a good setup for every fantasy-relevant Jacksonville player.

items.name: Patrick Mahomes
items.headline: Patrick Mahomes completed 27-of-39 passes for 329 yards and three touchdowns before being pulled in the fourth quarter of Kansas City’s 34-7, Week 11 win over the Cardinals.
items.analysis: It was about what you would have expected. Mahomes continues to look like he has Young Mahomes Swagger with Josh Downs rejuvenating the offense. The Chiefs easily boatraced the Cardinals today and the game was never competitive after a 14-0 first-quarter start in which Arizona possessed the ball for just two of 15 minutes. Mahomes will be an easy QB1 in what should be a red-hot fantasy matchup against the Bills on Thanksgiving. Justin Fields relieved Mahomes.

items.name: Robert Hainsey
items.headline: Jaguars declared C Robert Hainsey, DE Danny Striggow, DT Matt Dickerson, WR CJ Williams, and S Jalen Huskey inactive for Week 11 against the Giants.
items.analysis: Hainsey will be out for a while with a knee issue, a blow for an otherwise-solid Jacksonville offensive line. The Jags are among the healthiest teams headed into Week 11. They face off today against a middling Giants pass rush.

items.name: Benjamin Morrison
items.headline: Benjamin Morrison (hamstring) will not return in Week 11 against the Lions.
items.analysis: Morrison went down late in the first half and was ruled out in the third quarter. Kevin Knowles has taken his place in the lineup. Knowles is primarily a special teamer, so we wouldn’t be surprised to see Jared Goff pick on him in the final 15 minutes of this game.

items.name: DK Metcalf
items.headline: DK Metcalf was ejected in Week 11 against the Eagles.
items.analysis: He had two unsportsmanlike conduct penalties called against them. Metcalf, who has one catch for two yards on the day, was thrown out in the third quarter after two melees with Eagles defenders. It’s unclear why Metcalf was so intent on fighting various Philadelphia players, including — most prominently — Cooper DeJean. Metcalf continues his poor play (and decision making) in a Steelers offense that can’t get anything going on the ground or through the air.

items.name: Brandon Jones
items.headline: Broncos declared S Brandon Jones, QB Sam Ehlinger, WR Lil’Jordan Humphrey, OL Gavin Ortega, OL Kage Casey, TE Dallen Bentley, and DL Jordan Jackson inactive for Week 11 against the Raiders.
items.analysis: Jones was the only Bronco listed as questionable for today’s game. The rest are healthy scratches. Jones has five pass breakups and two interceptions this year. He’s out with a hamstring issue.

items.name: Brock Bowers
items.headline: Brock Bowers (ankle/quad) is inactive for Week 11 against the Broncos.
items.analysis: Bowers wasn’t spotted on the field during warmups, so he may not have been that close to playing today after all. He’s now eyeing a Week 12 return against the Browns. Michael Mayer will pick up a few extra targets versus Denver, putting him on the TE1/2 border. Also inactive for the Raiders are WR Dont’e Thornton Jr., WR Malik Benson, S Tristin McCollum, S Dalton Johnson, OG Bryce Cabeldue, and DT Tonka Hemingway.

items.name: Omar Cooper
items.headline: The Jets declared Omar Cooper Jr., CB Jarvis Brownlee Jr., WR Isaiah Williams, LB Trevin Wallace, TE Jelani Woods and ED Nate Lynn inactive for Week 11 against the Chargers.
items.analysis: Removing Cooper and Williams leaves Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell as the team’s top two wide receivers. Kenyon Sadiq and Mason Taylor could benefit as well. Geno Smith will play through his ankle injury today, after beginning the week in the questionable column. A run-heavy, quick-passing game plan could be incoming, given Smith’s ailment.

items.name: Chris Bell
items.headline: Chris Bell is questionable to return to Week 11 against the Bills with a chest injury.
items.analysis: Bell and Bills safety Damar Hamlin collided on a Hamlin interception in the second quarter. It seemed like Bell and Hamlin slammed their helmets into one another, but Bell’s injury designation says chest. It’s been a season of tough injury luck for Bell, who has battled a knee injury all season after having offseason surgery.

items.name: Charlie Kolar
items.headline: Charlie Kolar (concussion) is active for Week 11 against the Jets.
items.analysis: Kolar, David Njoku and Oronde Gadsden will form a three-player committee this afternoon. None of them warrant TE1 treatment, though they provide Justin Herbert with safety-blanket options and should help out in the run game.

items.name: Ladd McConkey
items.headline: Ladd McConkey (back) is active for Week 11 against the Jets.
items.analysis: McConkey’s injuries have made him difficult to trust this season, but the Chargers have funneled targets his way when active. He should be viewed as a WR3 with volume-based upside, now evidently healthy enough to play. The Chargers declared LB Daiyan Henley, CB Tarheeb Still, WR Brenen Thompson, S Kendall Williamson, G Alex Harkey and WR KeAndre Lambert-Smith inactive for Week 11 against the Jets.

items.name: Roschon Johnson
items.headline: Roschon Johnson suffered an ankle injury in the Bears’ Week 11 game against the Saints and is doubtful to return.
items.analysis: Johnson was carted to the locker room in the first quarter against the Saints. He was announced to have an ankle injury and is doubtful to return. With Kyle Monangai back, the Bears had depth in the backfield again but lose a special teamer and third-string running back in Johnson against the Saints.

items.name: D.J. Reed
items.headline: Lions declared CB D.J. Reed, CB Ennis Rakestraw Jr., DB Ketih Abney II, LB Amen Ogbongbemiga, EDGE Tyrus Wheat, and DL Mekhi Wingo inactive for Week 11 against the Bucs.
items.analysis: Reed made seven starts this year before injuring his hip a few weeks ago. Rakestraw has been a depth option so far, but that would have been useful to have around with Reed out. The Lions’ defense will be as vulnerable as ever this week, though it’s anyone’s guess as to whether a hobbled Baker Mayfield will take advantage.

items.name: Dante Trader
items.headline: Dolphins declared S Dante Trader Jr., CB Jaylin Simpson, P Bradley Pinion, OL Christian Haynes, OL Caedan Wallace, TE Justin Joly, and WR Jared Wayne inactive for Week 11 against the Bills.
items.analysis: Trader Jr. is the Dolphins’ starting strong safety, but the rest of the inactives are depth pieces. Simpson does see the field as a backup cornerback, so the Dolphins will be down two members of the secondary in a game against Josh Allen, which is never great news.

items.name: Tyrell Shavers
items.headline: Tyrell Shavers (knee) is active and will make his season debut in Week 11 against the Dolphins.
items.analysis: Shavers has been sidelined all season after tearing his ACL in a playoff win over Jacksonville last year. The 27-year-old had emerged as the team’s best blocking wide receiver last year and had seen his snap count increase as the season went on. He’s unlikely to be a fantasy factor, but it would not be surprising to see him play a decent amount of snaps once he is fully ramped up because of the value he provides in the running game. This means rookie Skyler Bell is back to being a game-day inactive.

items.name: Dalton Kincaid
items.headline: Dalton Kincaid is inactive for Week 11 against the Dolphins.
items.analysis: Kincaid was listed as questionable with (thumb/ankle) injuries, but he will not suit up. This makes sense as a cautionary move for the Bills, who already ruled out starting cornerback Christian Benford and starting linebacker Dorian Williams. The Bills are nearly a 17-point favorite against the Dolphins on Sunday and then will face the Chiefs on Thursday night. Except Dawson Knox to be more involved in this game in Week 11, but we wouldn’t be surprised if the Bills are running the ball a lot in the second half. The Bills’ full inactives are: WR Skyler Bell, TE Dalton Kincaid, OT Jude Bowry, DL T.J. Sanders, ILB Dorian Williams, OLB Mike Danna, and CB Christian Benford.

items.name: Roman Wilson
items.headline: Roman Wilson (finger) is active for Week 11 against the Eagles.
items.analysis: Wilson, who accounted for 16 percent of the Steelers’ targets and 39 percent of the team’s air yards before sustaining a finger injury in Week 5, will make his return to the lineup and likely make Germie Bernard all but unplayable in 12-team leagues. Wilson can be slotted in as a high-variance flex or second flex against the Eagles. The Steelers declared WR Kaden Wetjen, QBs Drew Allar Will Howard, Sean Murphy-Bunting, RB Eli Heidenreich, OLB Nick Herbig, and DL Gabe Rubio inactive.

items.name: Kenneth Walker
items.headline: Chiefs declared RB Kenneth Walker (groin) inactive for Kansas City’s Week 11 game against the Cardinals.
items.analysis: It’s Emmett Johnson szn once more. Also inactive for the Chiefs are QB Garrett Nussmeier (third quarterback), OL Jaylon Moore (ankle), OL Trey Smith (concussion), DT Omarr Norman-Lott (knee), DT Peter Woods (neck) and CB Melvin Smith. Norman-Lott and Woods were both questionable and will not play. The others were ruled out on Friday.

items.name: Audric Estime
items.headline: Saints declared LB Pete Werner, CB Martin Emerson Jr., RB Audric Estime, OT Asim Richards, OT Taliese Fuaga, C Erik McCoy, and QB Zach Wilson inactive for Week 11 against the Bears.
items.analysis: Estime was seeing nearly half of the Saints’ backfield snaps up to last week. With Travis Etienne ramping back up from injury, the Saints choose to deactivate Estime, keeping Etienne as the primary back, Alvin Kamara as the pass-catching back, and rookie CJ Donaldson as the third-string in what has been a frustrating committee for fantasy purposes. Zach Wilson is the emergency third quarterback while Werner (hamstring), Emerson (concussion), Richards (knee), Fuaga (knee), and McCoy (biceps) are all out with injury, leaving the offensive line and defense short-handed against the Bears.

items.name: Nicholas Singleton
items.headline: Titans declared RB Nicholas Singleton, LB Mohamoud Diabate, CB Jaylon Jones, DT Jackie Marshall and OT Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson inactive for Week 11 against the Cowboys.
items.analysis: With Tyjae Spears on injured reserve, it’s a poor sign for fifth-round rookie Singleton that he is still getting healthy scratched in Week 11.

items.name: Darren Waller
items.headline: Darren Waller (knee) is active for the Panthers’ Week 11 against the Ravens.
items.analysis: Waller was questionable with a knee injury entering the weekend, but will be good to go in what is somewhat of a revenge game against the team that drafted him in the sixth round back in 2015. The 34-year old tight end profiles as a boom-or-bust TE2 against a Ravens defense that has allowed the 10th-most PPR points per game (14.1) to opposing tight ends over its last five games. In addition to Waller, fellow tight end Tommy Tremble (knee) is also active, while TE Ja’Tavion Sanders, QB Haynes King, RB AJ Dillon, LB Bobby Okereke, C Sam Hecht, and DT TeRah Edwards will all be inactive for this one.

items.name: Josh Johnson
items.headline: Cardinals declared QB Carson Beck, CB Starling Thomas V, OL Kingsley Eguakun, OL Jon Gaines (ankle) and DL Andrew Billings inactive for Arizona’s Week 11 game against the Chiefs.
items.analysis: Just in case you were off the grid Saturday: Josh Johnson will start for the Cardinals against the Chiefs, becoming the fourth quarterback in four weeks for a team critics are calling “one of mankind’s most awful crimes.” OK, not really, but they are 15.5-point dogs. Johnson is probably one of the three worst superflex quarterbacks to have to start this week on a short slate.

items.name: Jake Ferguson
items.headline: Cowboys declared TE Jake Ferguson, OG Tyler Booker, S P.J. Locke, WR Jonathan Mingo, LB Jaishawn Barham and DT Jonathan Bullard inactive for Week 11 against the Titans.
items.analysis: Ferguson has barely played since Week 7. Although he is merely week to week with his ankle and knee issues, the formerly fantasy relevant seam stretcher seems unlikely to be a 12-team league factor down the stretch.

items.name: DeVonta Smith
items.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) is active for Week 11 against the Steelers.
items.analysis: Smith will finally make his return to game action after a two-month hamstring injury. Before the injury, he had accounted for 30 percent of the team’s targets and 47 percent of the team’s air yards. Smith’s 40 percent first-read target share was among the highest in the NFL over the season’s first month. He should be a decent WR3 here with Joe Milton under center. Eagles declared QB Cole Payton, CB Mac McWilliams, LB Smael Mondon Jr., LB Ajani Cornelius, and OL Jake Majors inactive against the Steelers.

items.name: Sione Vaki
items.headline: Sione Vaki (ankle) is active for Week 11 against the Bucs.
items.analysis: Vaki will continue to back up Jahmyr Gibbs, though that role hasn’t produced much fantasy value this year. He will only see a meaningful amount of touches if the Lions blow out the Bucs, which could happen. Vaki is buried in the RB5 ranks for now.

items.name: Kyler Gordon
items.headline: Bears declared QB Case Keenum, OL Jordan McFadden, CB Kyler Gordon, DL Jayden Loving, and LB Keyshaun Elliott inactive for Week 11 against the Saints.
items.analysis: Gordon was already declared out with a shoulder injury heading into the weekend. Rookie wide receiver Zavion Thomas (ankle) entered the day questionable, but will be active after missing Friday’s practice. Case Keenum will be the team’s emergency third quarterback.

items.name: Marlon Humphrey
items.headline: Ravens declared CB Marlon Humphrey, FS Jaylinn Hawkins, RB Adam Randall, OG Emery Jones, DT Nnamdi Madubuike, and QB Kedon Slovis inactive for Week 11 against the Panthers.
items.analysis: Humphrey, Madubuike, and Hawkins were all ruled out before the weekend. The Ravens will look to end a five-game skid in Jacoby Brissett’s second start with the team and face a Panthers defense that is near the bottom of the league at stopping the run, which could bode well for Derrick Henry and a ground game that has been stagnant in recent weeks.

items.name: Baker Mayfield
items.headline: Baker Mayfield (foot) is active for Week 11 against the Lions.
items.analysis: Mayfield is going to try to play through the plantar fascia injury he suffered in Week 9 before the Bucs’ bye. Expect the Bucs to lean on their ground game for as long as possible to protect Mayfield. Even in a good matchup, it’s hard to treat him as anything better than a mid-range QB2. EDGE Yaya Diaby is also active. Inactive for the Bucs are DT DeMonte Capehart, CB Ayden Garnes, OG Trevor Keegan, OG Billy Schrauth, QB Easton Stick, and S Antoine Winfield Jr.

items.name: Brock Bowers
items.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports there is “not a lot of optimism” that Brock Bowers (ankle/quad) will play in Week 11 against the Broncos.
items.analysis: Bowers returned to practice earlier in the week and was listed as questionable on Friday. Schefter noted that Bowers is pushing to play, but we doubt the team will let him suit up after suffering another ankle injury. That’s on top of the quad issue, which seems to be minor compared to the ankle. Assuming Bowers is out, Michael Mayer should see an uptick in targets against a Denver defense that has bled fantasy points to tight ends this season. He would be a solid streaming option if Bowers is ruled out.

items.name: Drake Maye
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Drake Maye (fractured fibula) is expected to miss at least six weeks.
items.analysis: A six-week absence would technically allow Maye to return late in the regular season, but Rapoport then followed up by saying he has an “outside chance” at playing if the Pats make the playoffs. We suspect the Patriots would, at most, use the final weeks of the regular season to get Maye back on the practice field. Tommy DeVito is currently their starting quarterback and they’re sitting at 5-5, so a playoff berth doesn’t appear to be in the cards. Rapoport also mentioned Daniel Jones as an option in Maye’s absence. We doubt he saves New England’s season, but he would be an upgrade over DeVito.

items.name: Daniel Jones
items.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Ravens offered the Colts a fourth-round pick for Daniel Jones and a conditional fifth-round pick.
items.analysis: The fifth-round pick returned to the Colts if the Ravens made the playoffs. At worst, the Colts would have upgraded one of their Day Three picks. At best, they could have walked away with an extra fourth-round selection. They weren’t getting a king’s ransom for Jones, but it’s better than what they walked away with two weeks later when they cut him. The Colts’ mismanagement of the Jones situation will go down as a true blunder by a front office in disarray. Jones could still wind up in Baltimore as a free agent, assuming he clears waivers later this week.

items.name: Davante Adams
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Davante Adams sounds like a “long shot” to play in Week 13 against the Chiefs.
items.analysis: Adams isn’t expected to play in Week 12. The Rams get the Packers on Wednesday before Thanksgiving, and the tight turnaround makes a Week 12 return all but impossible. Head coach Sean McVay said Week 13 against Kansas City was a “possibility” earlier this week. That sounds unlikely now as well. Rapoport said Adams is eyeing a mid-December return. With Puka Nacua done for the year, the Rams are down to Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell as their top wide receivers for at least a few more weeks.

items.name: Micah Parsons
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Micah Parsons is “on track” to play in Week 12 against the Rams.
items.analysis: This isn’t a major surprise as head coach Matt LaFleur told reporters on Monday that he was hopeful Parsons would play in Week 12. It sounds like that timeline remains in the cards. Parsons has missed the first three months of the season while recovering from a torn ACL and meniscus injuries he suffered late last year. Getting Parsons back will be a huge boost for a Packers defense that hasn’t done much this year. Parsons had 12.5 sacks in 14 games with the Packers last year.

items.name: Daniel Jones
items.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter believes Daniel Jones will “draw interest” from the Patriots and Ravens.
items.analysis: Schefter didn’t directly cite his sources on this, so he may just be connecting dots. Still, the two teams make loads of sense for the downtrodden quarterback. The Patriots are expected to be without Drake Maye for at least the rest of the regular season. At 5-5, they’re still in the hunt for a Wild Card bid, though their odds of making the postseason will all but disappear if Tommy DeVito remains their starting quarterback. The Ravens are in a similar spot, though they’ve already addressed the quarterback position via Jacoby Brissett. Schefter notes that the most likely outcome is that Jones waits for a more attractive spot to open up. He is expected to clear waivers later this week, at which point he will become an unrestricted free agent.

items.name: Alec Pierce
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Colts are shutting down Alec Pierce (heel) for the remainder of the 2026 season.
items.analysis: Pierce signed a four-year, $114 million contract in the offseason. He almost immediately underwent surgery and was expected to miss three months, though it took a bit longer than that. There was also a mix-up about whether or not he underwent a second PRP injection, which at-the-time GM Chris Ballard denied. He was sidelined for a bit longer than that but did play in Week 1. Pierce then re-injured his heel in Week 2, functionally ending his season. The team has now chosen to shut him down to avoid any chance of further complications. It sounds like he will be good to go for 2027. Pierce’s season ends with five catches for 72 scoreless yards. He will return to a rebuilding Colts roster that is unlikely to support his WR3 fantasy case next year.

items.name: Ladd McConkey
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Ladd McConkey (back) is expected to play in Week 11 against the Jets.
items.analysis: McConkey experienced back spasms in pre-game warmups two weeks ago. The Chargers didn’t announce that until the game had started and he did not play a snap. The team had the courtesy to rule him out ahead of kickoff last week. He got in three limited sessions this week before being listed as questionable. McConkey has been the Chargers’ most effective wideout when healthy, but that has been an exceedingly rare occurrence this year. We suspect he’s still not at full strength. With the risk of a re-injury looming, fantasy managers should treat him as a WR3, even if his ceiling his much higher.

items.name: Baker Mayfield
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Baker Mayfield (foot) will play in Week 11 against the Lions.
items.analysis: Mayfield looked unlikely to play after missing Wednesday’s practice. He inexplicably returned for Thursday’s session before being listed as questionable the next day. He’s dealing with a plantar fascia injury that hobbled him in the team’s Week 9 loss to the Bears. A Week 10 bye was just enough time off to get him back on the field without any time missed. Even in a great matchup with the Lions, it’s hard to trust Mayfield as anything other than a mid-range QB2.

items.name: Mike Evans
items.headline: Mike Evans (Achilles) will play in Week 11 against the Vikings.
items.analysis: Evans’ agent posted a video on his Instagram that can only be described as the corniest thing you will see today. In it, he vaguely announced that Evans was back after missing a few weeks with Achilles tendinitis. Evans will likely be managing this injury for the rest of the season, so we wouldn’t be surprised if he returns on a bit of a pitch count. Still, Evans was operating as the team’s unquestioned WR1 before suffering the injury. He will be on the WR2/3 border for his first game back.

items.name: Puka Nacua
items.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Puka Nacua (MCL surgery) will be sidelined 4-5 months.
items.analysis: This confirms Nacua will not only miss the remainder of the regular season, but would be unavailable for any potential Super Bowl run for the pre-season favorites. Schefter did add that Nacua’s knee “checked out clean aside from the MCL.” That’s good news heading into Nacua’s potential free agency, though he is nevertheless at a low ebb in his up-and-down Rams tenure. The ups have been any time Nacua takes the field. The downs have been how often he has been sidelined, as well as his off-the-field issues. Going on 26, Nacua would make a lot of sense as a franchise tag candidate, or perhaps a tag-and-trade for the Rams.

items.name: Jonathon Brooks
items.headline: Panthers ruled out Jonathon Brooks (groin) for Week 11 against the Ravens.
items.analysis: Brooks will miss his seventh consecutive game in Week 11, leaving Chuba Hubbard to a true workhorse role for another week. The matchup is less than ideal against the Ravens but fantasy managers can continue riding the bump in volume to a high end RB2 profile for the veteran back.

items.name: Kyren Williams
items.headline: Kyren Williams (toe) was limited Saturday but is expected to play in Week 12 against the Packers.
items.analysis: Williams is reportedly dealing with “soreness” in his toe and was limited in practice Saturday as a result. ESPN’s Sarah Barshop added that Williams is expected to play on Wednesday against the Packers. Expect him to continue working in a strict timeshare with Blake Corum coming out of the team’s Week 11 bye.

items.name: Andrei Iosivas
items.headline: Andrei Iosivas (thumb) is doubtful for Week 11 against the Commanders.
items.analysis: Iosivas was practicing in full throughout the week, making his designation somewhat puzzling as he attempts to return from injured reserve. The team will have another week to activate the young wide receiver before he will be forced to remain on injured reserve for the remainder of the season.

items.name: Dontayvion Wicks
items.headline: Eagles placed WR Dontayvion Wicks (ankle/foot) on injured reserve.
items.analysis: Wicks has already missed the previous three games with an ankle injury and now finds himself sent to injured reserve, meaning he will miss at least seven games total with poorly timed injuries. He saw a “foot” designation added to his status during a week of limited showings, which is presumably the issue that lands him on injured reserve. DeVonta Smith, who returns from an extended absence this week, Makai Lemon, and Darius Cooper are likely to hold down the starting wide receiver positions in Wicks’ absence.

items.name: Treylon Burks
items.headline: Treylon Burks (foot) was removed from the injury report Saturday and will play in Week 11 against the Bengals.
items.analysis: Burks surprisingly went from a full session Thursday and a no-show Friday, prompting uncertainty regarding his expected availability for Monday Night Football against the Bengals. He quickly put those worries to rest with a full practice Saturday and was removed from the injury report. Expect Burks to continue operating in a featured role on the perimeter in the absence of Terry McLaurin.

items.name: Rachaad White
items.headline: Rachaad White (heel) is questionable for Week 11 against the Bengals.
items.analysis: White’s week of practice was troubling, first appearing on the injury report on Friday with a limited designation due to a heel ailment before being downgraded to a “DNP” Saturday. Even so, head coach Dan Quinn indicated the veteran back is “on track” for Monday Night Football. Assuming he is active, White is likely to slot back into the primary change of pace role behind Jacory Croskey-Merritt, the latter of whom appears set to be activated from injured reserve in time for Monday.

items.name: Jacory Croskey-Merritt
items.headline: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) is questionable for Week 11 against the Bengals.
items.analysis: Croskey-Merritt managed a week of full practices as he attempts to return from injured reserve, and while the team has not yet activated him, he appears to be trending in the right direction for his first game action since Week 5. Rachaad White, also listed as questionable, would likely shift back to a primary change of pace role, should Croskey-Merritt return.

items.name: Michael Pittman
items.headline: Steelers did not activate Michael Pittman (foot) ahead of Week 11.
items.analysis: Pittman will remain on injured reserve for at least another week. The team gets back fellow wide receiver Roman Wilson, who should join DK Metcalf and rookie Germie Bernard as the starters from 11-personnel. Fantasy managers are likely only able to confidently start Metcalf against the Eagles.

items.name: Roman Wilson
items.headline: Steelers activated WR Roman Wilson (hand) from injured reserve.
items.analysis: Wilson ended up staying on injured reserve for the minimum four games as he dealt with a hand injury, returning to a roster approaching full health, although fellow wide receiver Michael Pittman was not activated from injured reserve ahead of Week 11.Fantasy managers are likely only able to confidently start Metcalf against the Eagles on Sunday.

items.name: Carson Beck
items.headline: Cardinals ruled out Carson Beck (back) for Week 11 against the Chiefs.
items.analysis: That paves the way for 36-year-old journeyman quarterback Josh Johnson to draw the start under center for the Cardinals after being added to the team less than two weeks ago. Dynasty managers will be forced to wait longer for the first extended look at the third-round rookie as the Cardinals continue forward with insurmountable injuries up and down their roster in what has quickly become a lost season. Downgrade the primary skill position players in a difficult matchup against the Chiefs in Week 11.

items.name: Tyjae Spears
items.headline: Titans placed RB Tyjae Spears (knee) on injured reserve.
items.analysis: Spears will now miss the next four games, at minimum, as he tends to a knee injury that has plagued him in recent weeks. Spears previously missed two games in Week 7 and Week 8 before returning to a modest workload in Week 9 after the team’s bye. Tony Pollard should continue operating in a true workhorse role and gets one of the top matchups in the league against the Cowboys in Week 11. Fantasy managers can continue to treat Pollard as a volume-driven RB1 after a slow start to the season.

items.name: Jacory Croskey-Merritt
items.headline: Commanders HC Dan Quinn told reporters RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) is “trending the right way” ahead of the matchup with the Bengals in Week 11.
items.analysis: Quinn said Croskey-Merritt had a great week and is trending the right way for Monday’s game against the Bengals. It’s great news for fantasy managers and the Commanders as backup running back Rachaad White (heel) missed practice Saturday. Croskey-Merritt deserves FLEX consideration assuming he’s active against the Bengals this week.

items.name: Rachaad White
items.headline: Rachaad White (heel) missed practice on Saturday.
items.analysis: White was added to the injury report and was a limited participant in practice on Friday. His missed practice Saturday is another bad sign for the 27-year-old running back’s availability. With Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) trending towards being available, White doesn’t seem to have much fantasy value at the moment. CB Amik Robertson, who was seen limping in the locker room on Friday, also missed practice Saturday.

items.name: Carnell Tate
items.headline: CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reports Titans WR Carnell Tate (shoulder) is likely to return against the Cowboys in Week 11.
items.analysis: Tate hasn’t played since Week 7 due to a shoulder injury. Still officially questionable, Zenitz reports Tate is likely to play in Week 11.
