While he’s been out for over a month, Tate got in a full practice on Friday. He’ll be a high-end WR3 in a plus matchup against the brutal Cowboys defense.

items.name: Baker Mayfield
items.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Buccaneers QB Baker Mayfield (foot) is dealing with a plantar fascia injury.
items.analysis: While Mayfield remains on track to play against the Lions on Sunday, he’s dealing with a painful plantar fascia injury, according to Pelissero. If the 31-year-old gunslinger suits up in Week 11, he’ll wear a special orthotic and new cleats to help stabilize his foot. Mayfield looked doubtful to play earlier in the week and even missed practice Wednesday before getting in a pair of limited sessions. Jalon Daniels would start if Mayfield isn’t able to play this week.

items.name: Puka Nacua
items.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler described Rams WR Puka Nacua’s future with the team as “very uncertain.”
items.analysis: Nothing earth-shattering here from Fowler. Appearing on ESPN’s SportsCenter Saturday morning, the NFL Insider noted that Nacua is dealing with a significant MCL injury and a three-game suspension from the NFL. With Nacua unlikely to return this season, Fowler says this isn’t the kind of momentum the 25-year-old receiver wanted heading into free agency, where he’ll be the best player available. The Rams can extend him, franchise tag him or let him hit the open market this offseason. As Fowler says, it’s something the Rams have to sort out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports league sources “don’t foresee” QB Aaron Rodgers playing again, barring an injury-driven emergency.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.analysis: Rodgers cleared waivers Thursday and no immediate suitors emerged. The 42-year-old free agent QB torched what was left of his Steelers career earlier this week when he issued an ultimatum to Steelers HC Mike McCarthy, got benched, appeared on the Pat McAfee Show and was released. Plenty of teams are missing their starting quarterbacks, but Pelissero says it’ll take an injury-driven emergency for Rodgers to play again. At this point, no team is desperate enough to dance with the devil.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.headline: Aaron Rodgers cleared waivers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.analysis: Rodgers is now officially a free agent. The quarterback could be a target of a team desperate for a quarterback who can contribute — it’s worth noting that Rodgers was not playing well prior to his blow-up —like the Patriots or the Ravens, but it’s just as feasible that this is the last time we’ve seen Rodgers on a football field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.headline: Speaking with the Pittsburgh-Gazette’s Gerry Dulac, Steelers president Art Rooney II said Aaron Rodgers was not a “good teammate” following his release.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.analysis: In a story published by Dulac on Thursday, Rooney said the Steelers are “100 percent” committed to head coach Mike McCarthy, while adding that “insubordination will not be tolerated” as far as Rodgers is concerned. According to Dulac, Rodgers and McCarthy met on Tuesday night, just hours before the QB’s benching, and presented McCarthy with an ultimatum: “let me call the plays or just release me.” What followed from there was Rodgers’ benching and eventual release after he went scorched earth on the Steelers and McCarthy on the Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday. Rodgers will be free to sign with any team when he inevitably clears waivers later in the day, but for now, no potential suitor has emerged for the soon-to-be retired QB, who has been among the least efficient in the league over the last few seasons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.headline: The Pittsburgh Post-Gazette’s Gerry Dulac reports the Steelers are expected to release Aaron Rodgers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.analysis: The team announced his benching late Tuesday night. He then went on The Pat McAfee Show earlier today and burned every bridge in town by saying Mike McCarthy has been sleeping through meetings or missing them outright, among many other accusations. Per Dulac, the interview hastened Pittsburgh’s decision to get Rodgers off the roster. Once he clears waivers, Rodgers will be eligible to sign with another team. It’s unclear if any team will be interested in the Rodgers experience after how things ended in Pittsburgh, but a desperate playoff contender like the Patriots or Ravens could convince themselves of signing him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.headline: Speaking on The Pat McAfee Show, Aaron Rodgers said he issued an ultimatum to Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy to give up play-calling duties.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.analysis: Rodgers started off the conversation talking about McCarthy’s shortcomings this year, but he quickly shifted toward accusing McCarthy of being “unwell.” He mentioned several instances of McCarthy missing meetings while sleeping in his office or falling asleep during others. Rodgers also talked extensively about McCarthy failing to stay ahead on film sessions and even brought up a moment on the sidelines when McCarthy broke down the team at halftime with a “1, 2, 3, Packers”. Rodgers feigned concern for McCarthy’s health, though it felt rather disingenuous amidst his scorched-earth campaign. Rodgers told McAfee that he issued an ultimatum to the team to have McCarthy give up play-calling duties. That was seemingly the final straw. Notably, he also talked about being released by the Steelers, though it’s unclear if he has officially made that request. Either way, there’s no coming back from this. He has played his last snap in Pittsburgh. The fact that he’s going out on such a disastrous note means the Steelers won’t want to do him any favors by releasing him. He will likely be inactive and away from the team for the remainder of what Rodgers has said is his final year. If this is the end of his career, it’s a truly unbecoming and sad final chapter for one of the greatest to ever do it.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.headline: The Athletic’s Mike DeFabo said it “sounds like” the benching of Aaron Rodgers in favor of Mason Rudolph was “not a popular decision in the locker room.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.analysis: Rodgers was reportedly excused from meetings at the team facility on Wednesday, two days ahead of the Steelers’ Week 12 game against Denver. Rodgers’ benching comes after a series of down games and a proposed change from Rodgers about how plays are communicated to him during the game. Rudolph could be a slight upgrade for Pittsburgh pass catchers and should be rostered in supeflex formats for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Aaron Rodgers was excused from a Wednesday morning meeting.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.analysis: Schefter said the veteran was excused from showing up Wednesday morning so he could “process” being benched in favor of Mason Rudolph for Week 12 against the Broncos. That seems fair. Whatever happens from here, Rodgers has certainly taken his last snap as a Steeler. Rudolph, meanwhile, should be rostered in all superflex leagues for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy made the decision to bench Aaron Rodgers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.analysis: Rapoport said McCarthy’s decision came after extensive meetings with coaches, players, and Rodgers himself following the Steelers’ Week 11 loss to the Joe Milton-led Eagles. Mason Rudolph is slated to get the start in Week 12 against the Broncos. NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo said the team was set to make a change in play calling, with QB coach Tom Arth relaying plays to Rodgers on game days “at the behest of Rodgers.” Hours later, the 42-year-old veteran was benched. Rodgers had reverted to his 2025 form in the weeks before the benching, ranking 23rd in EPA per drop back and 25th in drop back success rate from Week 8-11. The reuniting of McCarthy and Rodgers in Pittsburgh was always a bit odd considering their falling out in Green Bay. It’s unlikely Rodgers will be on the Steelers roster for much longer now that he has been pulled.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.headline: The Steelers have announced they are benching Aaron Rodgers, with Mason Rudolph named the starter for Week 12 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.analysis: 42-year-old Rodgers’ play had taken a sudden, dramatic turn for the worse of late, but it’s still a stunning announcement, especially since it came via a terse team statement. It also comes one day after coach Mike McCarthy claimed he was not considering turning to one of his myriad other QB options (the team also has second-year pro Will Howard and rookie Drew Allar on the 53-man roster). Other information is scarce, except for the statement including Rodgers would be inactive for the Friday afternoon contest. With the Steelers playing on a short week, they are already issuing injury reports, and Rodgers was not on Tuesday’s edition. It would appear, rather unsurprisingly, the sides have simply soured on each other, an outcome that perhaps became inevitable following Rodgers’ recent downturn. Startlingly immobile, almost anyone would be an upgrade on Rodgers at this point, but Rudolph is really going to push the “almost anyone” framing. Needless to say, this is not an offense we are looking toward for Week 12 fantasy production. The next order of business could be Rodgers’ release. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.headline: Aaron Rodgers completed 30-of-44 attempts for 227 yards and one touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 11 loss to the Eagles, adding five rushes for 29 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.analysis: Rodgers, as he has been for most of the season, was wildly inefficient against the Eagles. He posted a -4.1 EPA, barely better than Joe Milton. Rodgers again was in check-down mode, only trying a couple deep shots and holding the ball time and again. Rodgers took five sacks and narrowly avoided a handful of others as the Steelers offensive line was overwhelmed for the second straight week. Coming into Week 11, only Daniel Jones and Baker Mayfield had lower drop backs EPAs than Rodgers. He’ll be a superflex option in Week 12 against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bill-murra.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that Rams OG Bill Murray ruptured his Achilles tendon in the Rams’ Week 12 win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bill-murra.analysis: This is unfortunate. Murray, a backup, started at left guard and played well. He will now undergo surgery and begin rehab for the 2027 NFL season. The Rams’ offensive line is fairly banged up. Hopefully, the extra time off allows the unit to improve its health.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bill-murra.headline: Colts waived DE Viliami Fehoko Jr.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bill-murra.analysis: Fehoko has played zero snaps since entering the league as a fourth-round pick in 2023. The Colts also waived LB Joseph Vaughn and released OG Bill Murray. OT Jack Wilson was waived as well, though he will revert to the Colts’ injured reserve list if he clears waivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bill-murra.headline: Colts signed LB Austin Ajiake to a one-year contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bill-murra.analysis: An exclusive rights free agent, Ajiake had 32 tackles and played 70 percent of the Colts special teams snaps this year. He also saw some sparse time at linebacker, with 157 defensive snaps over 16 games. The Colts also agreed to terms with RB Ulysses Bentley IV, CB Wyett Ekeler, DE Viliami Fehoko Jr., G LaDarius Henderson, QB Seth Henigan, T Bayron Matos, C Jimmy Morrissey, TE Sean McKeon, S Trey Washington, WR Coleman Owen, DT Tim Smith, G Bill Murray, DE Durell Nchami, S Ben Nikkel, WR Eli Pancol and G Josh Sills on reserve/future contracts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bill-murra.headline: Bears placed G Bill Murray (pectoral) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bill-murra.analysis: Pectoral injuries are usually season-enders for offensive linemen, but we’ll be kind and say “he’ll miss at least four weeks” as all players placed on injured reserve must. Murray had an 82.4 PFF grade in a small sample size, and the 27-year-old will be missed. The Bears will hope Teven Jenkins is able to go this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bill-murra.headline: Patriots released DT Bill Murray.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bill-murra.analysis: A practice-squad tackle in New England last year, Murray has yet to play a regular season snap since signing with the Patriots as undrafted free agent in May 2020. His career upside includes potential as a sub-package pass rusher off the bench if it all clicks at his next destination.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bill-murra.headline: Patriots placed practice squad DT Bill Murray on the reserve/COVID-19 list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bill-murra.analysis: Rotoworld isn’t usually in the business of writing up practice squad injuries, but New England’s second COVID-19 placement in the past four days is certainly noteworthy. A taxi squad tackle, Murray presumably has not had close contact with Cam Newton, but anything is possible. It’s yet another situation to monitor in these delicate football times.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-scho.headline: NFL on Prime’s James Palmer believes Brian Schottenheimer will remain the Cowboys’ head coach for the rest of the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-scho.analysis: Palmer’s report wasn’t entirely positive. He also believes that if the Cowboys’ performance does not improve, “there are going to be some decisions that Jerry Jones needs to make after the season.” It sounds like Schottenheimer may be coaching for his job for the rest of the year. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-scho.headline: Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said he is still confident in head coach Brian Schottenheimer.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-scho.analysis: Jones said he is not considering a head coaching change. This came just minutes after the Cowboys’ catastrophic meltdown against the Eagles on Thanksgiving. Dallas gave up 22 points in the fourth quarter and lost on a last-second field goal. Schottenheimer stripped DC Christian Parker of play-calling duties two weeks ago. The Cowboys gave up 79 points to Cam Ward and Joe Milton in senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine’s first two games calling plays on defense. Schottenheimer has had no issues getting points on the board, but his Cowboys have routinely found spectacular ways to snatch defeat from the jaws of victory. He is now 12-16-1 as the team’s head coach. He will need to turn things around in the final quarter of this season if he wants to keep his job beyond 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-scho.headline: NFL.com’s Kevin Patra reports Cowboys and HC Brian Schottenheimer had an “agreement” in place that would keep him with the team if not hired to be the head coach a season ago.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-scho.analysis: “We had made an agreement that I would stay here no matter what,” Schottenheimer revealed on the Twins Take Podcast. “And I didn’t want to leave. I really wanted to be the head coach and put our fingerprint, our blueprint on it.” While the “agreement” was not fully disclosed, it sounds like Jerry and Stephen Jones intended to keep Schottenheimer with the organization, most likely as a play calling offensive coordinator had the team hired a more defensive-minded head coach during the 2025 coaching cycle. Schottenheimer served in that position with the organization during the 2023 and 2024 seasons, although he was not tasked with play calling duties. Either way, Dallas landed their man and now look to return to offensive prominence in Schottenheimer’s second season as head coach.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-scho.headline: Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer believes the team is set up to draft “the best player available” in the first round of the 2026 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-scho.analysis: The Cowboys possess the 12th and 20th overall selections. They field an elite offense and a defense that could use more personnel upgrades, having allowed the most points in the NFL last season. The front office traded for EDGE Rashan Gary, and signed S Jalen Thompson and DT Otito Ogbonnia thus far this offseason, but the unit still has more needs. Regardless, Schottenheimer said that “if the best player on the board is clearly an offensive player, then we’ll certainly discuss that, and more than likely” draft that player, knowing Cowboys owner Jerry Jones. The Cowboys’ offense is already set up for fantasy success, but adding another capable offensive lineman and/or another pass catcher can only help QB Dak Prescott put up points.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-scho.headline: Cowboys QB Dak Prescott said the team is striving for offensive continuity by hiring Brian Schottenheimer as head coach.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-scho.analysis: Prescott said he was enthused to continue working under Schottenheimer, who has served as the Dallas offensive coordinator over the past two seasons. “The simple conversation I had with (owner) Jerry (Jones), post the decision of Mike walking, was simply that, the continuity,” Prescott said. “They wanted to keep continuity. Obviously had a lot of success with this group, with these men, and knew this was important to me. And Shotty has been a huge factor in that, setting up the game plan, creating the game plan. If you wanted to find continuity in place, look no further than Shotty.” Prescott struggled in 2024, throwing 11 touchdowns over eight games before suffering a season-ending hamstring injury that all but ended the Cowboys season. In 2023, Prescott posted 4,516 yards and 36 touchdowns in a Dallas offense that ranked third in success rate and second in EPA per play. The Cowboys in 2025 offense should look awfully familiar under Schottenheimer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-scho.headline: Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said he will call the offensive plays for the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-scho.analysis: “I’m really good with the X’s and O’s,” Schottenheimer said, “but I’m great with people.” Cool. This was expected after the hiring. Schottenheimer finished second in points scored with the Cowboys as offensive coordinator in 2023, but of course, he did not call those plays. He hasn’t called plays in the NFL since the 2020 season with Seattle. The Seahawks used play-action at a top-10 rate in that season and had Russell Wilson finishing second in the NFL in quarterback scrambles while tying for the league lead in time in the pocket. Those statistics are colored by the quarterback, of course, but they give a few clues as to what to expect from Schottenheimer’s offense. Without significant free-agent additions, it will be hard to believe in Dak Prescott or CeeDee Lamb to rebound all the way back to 2023 form.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-scho.headline: Cowboys hired offensive coordinator Brian Schottenheimer as their new head coach.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-scho.analysis: Schottenheimer held the Cowboys’ offensive coordinator position from 2023-2024, evidently earning Jerry Jones’ trust along the way. Schottenheimer was initially hired in former head coach Mike McCarthy’s third season at helm as a coaching analyst in 2022. Though Jones was unhappy with the Cowboys’ recent results, Schottenheimer somehow managed to escape Jones’ ire. Jones punctuated the hiring by saying “Brian Schottenheimer is known as a career assistant. He ain’t Brian no more. He is now known as the head coach of the Dallas Cowboys.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-scho.headline: Cowboys beat writer Clarence Hill Jr. reports the Cowboys could “cross the finish line on hiring Brian Schottenheimer no later than Friday, possibly today.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-scho.analysis: The betting markets appear to have known all along. Just days after it was reported that Schottenheimer was the odds-on favorite to land the Cowboys’ head coaching job, despite having never been interviewed beforehand, the current OC appears primed to turn head coach at any moment. Schottenheimer is the son of former NFL head coach Marty Schottenheimer, whose 200 career wins are good for eighth-most on the all-time wins list. Brian Schottenheimer, who first joined the NFL ranks as a QBs coach in 2001 has never held a head coaching position, and has underwhelmed at his last few stops as an offensive coordinator while with the Rams (2012-2014), Seahawks (2018-2020), and Jaguars (2021). He didn’t call offensive plays for the Cowboys in either of his two seasons as their offensive coordinator. Schottenheimer’s name didn’t emerge in the coaching conversations until people began linking him with the Cowboys. Now, it appears as if he’ll be the successor to Mike McCarthy barring an unforeseen change in plans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-scho.headline: Cowboys concluded a second interview with offensive coordinator Brian Schottenheimer on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-scho.analysis: After interviewing with the Cowboys Tuesday, Schottenheimer was brought in for a second interview, according to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport . As the Cowboys’ offensive coordinator for the past two seasons, he has a lot of familiarity with Jerry Jones and company. ESPN’s Todd Archer reports Schottenheimer’s second set of conversations with the team ended Wednesday night. The 51-year-old is still in the mix and is the only head coaching candidate to make it to two interviews for Dallas so far. Jones has been working with familiarity in head coaching candidates with former Cowboys and current Eagles OC Kellen Moore also in the mix. The Cowboys have shown the most interest in Schottenheimer thus far.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-scho.headline: Cowboys will interview offensive coordinator Brian Schottenheimer for the team’s head coaching vacancy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-scho.analysis: Schottenheimer has been with the Cowboys for three years, serving as the team’s OC for the past two seasons under former head coach Mike McCarthy. This would be his first head coaching job in the NFL after being offensive coordinator for four teams over the past 18 years. Schottenheimer, 51, led the Cowboys to the second most points and the third most yards in 2023 before injuries doomed the team’s 2024 campaign. His work with Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb could provide a seamless transition for the Dallas offense in the wake of McCarthy’s exit. Giving him the monumental task of replacing Mike McCarthy when he wasn’t even trusted to call offensive plays last year sounds like a dire idea.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: Drew Lock (elbow) is not on the Seahawks’ final injury report for Week 12 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: Lock was limited again this week with tendinitis in his throwing arm’s elbow. With Sam Darnold (quad) back in action, Lock returns to his backup role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: Drew Lock (right elbow) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: Lock continues to deal with an elbow injury, getting in a limited session on Wednesday. Sam Darnold was practicing in full and already announced to start in Week 12, so Lock can go back to fantasy benches and be cut for other waiver wire adds or stashes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Sam Darnold (quad) is expected to start in Week 12 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: Speaking on The Pat McAfee Show, Schefter said Darnold is expected to practice in full today. He also noted that, as of right now, there’s no quarterback controversy in Seattle. On the other hand, he did mention that the idea of Drew Lock taking over will at least be a talking point if Darnold struggles. For now, it looks like Darnold is back in the QB2 mix for a must-win matchup with the 49ers. We should get confirmation on his health via the team’s injury report throughout the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald would not say if Sam Darnold (quad) would start in Week 12.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: Darnold was able to return to practice on Monday ahead of the Seahawks’ Week 12 game against the division rival Niners. Macdonald suggested he wouldn’t make a call on a starting quarterback before Wednesday though. “I think before making any declarations with Sam, we’ll get through Wednesday, see how Wednesday goes,” Macdonald said. “So nothing official yet. He was able to train a little bit here, do some rehab here, he also was able to get away. He’s optimistic, but I think with today’s practice cadence and speed of today, it’s probably wise to wait to make any declarations until we get through Wednesday’s practice.” Drew Lock, the most efficient quarterback in the NFL this season, could get another start if Darnold isn’t quite ready. It’s an excellent matchup against a 49ers defense that profiles as a pass funnel.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said he is “really optimistic” that Sam Darnold (quad) will be able to start after the team’s Week 11 bye.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: Speaking on Monday with the media, Macdonald also reaffirmed Darnold as the starter after Drew Lock threw for 240 yards and two touchdowns in Week 10’s win over the Raiders. Lock has been solid for the Seahawks in four games this season, throwing for 837-7-0 while completing a career-high 73.1 percent of his passes. With the Seahawks now entering their bye, Macdonald said he his hopeful Darnold can log enough reps in time to play in Week 12 against the 49ers. We’ll see where things stand a week from now, but it’s clear there will be no QB controversey in Seattle whenever Darnold is ready to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: Drew Lock completed 14-of-17 attempts for 240 yards and two touchdowns in the Seahawks’ Week 10 win against the Raiders, adding six rushes for 20 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: Lock, as he has been in every spot start this season, was efficient in the run-first Seattle offense, averaging 14.1 yards per attempt and finishing 15 percent over his expected pass rate against a Raiders defense that ranks among the NFL’s worst. Lock fought through an elbow issue and an oblique injury in another win as Sam Darnold works his way back from injury. Visibly grimacing at time, Lock was his usual aggressive self, connecting with Cooper Kupp and Jaxson Smith-Njigba for touchdowns. Seattle has its bye in Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: Drew Lock (elbow/oblique) is not on Seattle’s final Week 10 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: Lock will step in as the starter again as Seattle takes on the Raiders, and he should profile as a reasonable superflex QB2. He was limited in all three practices this week, ceding some practice snaps to let Jalen Milroe run the show. The re-injury risk here does not quite appear to be zero.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: Drew Lock (elbow/oblique) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: Lock reportedly resumed throwing today, which is good to hear. He told reporters that the oblique injury is on the right side of his body, on the back of the muscle, which he thinks makes it easier to throw the football than when he had an oblique injury on the left side of his body two years ago. Lock is a QB2 this week against the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Drew Lock (elbow/oblique) will not “take every rep and throw” during Week 10 practices.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: Lock was a limited practice participant through Week 9 practices before starting on game day. We expect that to be the case again this week. Fellow backup QB Jalen Milroe will take some first-team reps to help preserve Lock for the Seahawks’ Week 10 game against the Raiders. Given the injuries, Lock is likely just a mid-to-low QB2 despite the soft matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said the team expects Drew Lock (oblique) to start in Week 10 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: Speaking on Monday, Macdonald said that tests on Lock’s oblique injury were “good” and that they believe his injury is something the team can manage. Lock has been solid in three games for the Seahawks this season, throwing for 597-5-0 while completing 71.1 percent of his passes. He draws a favorable Week 10 matchup against the Raiders and could be on the radar as a mid to low-end QB2 that may have some stream appeal in 2QB/Superflex leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.headline: Evan Engram didn’t catch either of his two targets in the Broncos’ Week 12 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.analysis: Engram was a complete non-factor, which is particularly disappointing after his six-catch, 74-yard effort in Week 11 against the Raiders. Unfortunately, this is much more inline with his previous production, and Engram can safely be ignored in Week 13 against the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.headline: Evan Engram caught 6-of-8 targets for 74 yards in the Broncos’ Week 11 win over the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.analysis: Engram was surprisingly involved in this game, and not just on check-downs. Four of his catches went for at least 10 yards, propelling him to a season-high in receiving yards. The only downside to his performance was the lack of a touchdown. That went to Adam Trautman on a short goal-line toss. While Engram’s pop-up game might help some best ball players, it’s not worth chasing headed into Week 12 against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.headline: Evan Engram failed to catch any of his three targets in the Broncos’ Week 8 win over the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.analysis: Engram was not a meaningful part of the Broncos’ offense, per usual. He has three catches for 15 yards over his past three appearances. It goes without saying, but Engram isn’t even on the TE2 radar for Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.headline: Evan Engram caught 1-of-3 targets for two yards in the Broncos’ Week 7 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.analysis: Engram popped up with four catches for 43 yards and a touchdown in Week 1. He has one game with more than two catches for 17 yards since. This week was no different. Engram isn’t even in the TE2 mix for Week 8 versus the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.headline: Evan Engram caught both targets for 13 yards in the Broncos’ Week 6 win over the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.analysis: Engram has not seen more than five targets in a game this season and has been held out of the end zone since Week 1, making him a difficult start in fantasy leagues of all sizes. He can safely remain on the bench in an enticing matchup against the Cardinals in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.headline: Evan Engram caught all four targets for 55 yards in the Broncos’ Week 5 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.analysis: Engram did a large portion of his damage on a busted coverage that allowed him to pick up 34 yards and come just short of a receiving score. The 55 yards are a season high, and it’s encouraging to see more involvement after being a non-factor in the previous two weeks. Engram will hope to build on this effort in Week 6 against the Seahawks, but fantasy managers shouldn’t bet on it.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.headline: Evan Engram caught 1-of-5 targets for six yards in the Broncos’ Week 4 loss against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.analysis: Engram again had a good route rate but didn’t make the most of his short targets from Bo Nix. Engram, who now has five receptions through four games, is not a fantasy option in any format and should remain on waiver wires for now. He’s been targeted on just 11 percent of his routes this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.headline: Evan Engram caught his lone target for 17 yards in the Broncos’ Week 2 win against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.analysis: Engram followed up his four catch, 43 yard, one touchdown Week 1 performance with a dud against his former team. Engram ran a route on just 15 of Bo Nix’s 34 drop backs, a far lower rate than he had in Week 1 against the Chiefs. That kind of role and usage would mean Engram is unusable in fantasy formats. He should remain on waiver wires ahead of the Broncos’ Week 3 matchup against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.headline: Evan Engram caught 4-of-5 targets for 43 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 1 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.analysis: Engram’s trip to paint came from 19 yards out on the team’s second possession to knot the score at seven in the first quarter, which would be the last time the team would be within striking distance for the remainder of the game. Nix’s timing was continually thrown off while under mounting pressure from Steve Spanguolo’s Kansas City defense, resulting in numerous off-target throws. Engram managed to corral two such throws and turn otherwise poor passes into completions for his young quarterback. Regardless of the low yardage total, Engram managed to score for the second time wearing the Denver blue and orange after notching just one touchdown in his first year with the team in 2025. Engram remains a low-upside TE2 ahead of a Week 2 matchup against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.headline: The Denver Post’s Parker Gabriel believes “it would be a surprise” if Adam Trautman didn’t outsnap Evan Engram again in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.analysis: There’s been some mild hype for Engram again in the early offseason, but it’s hard to understand why the Broncos would have brought in Jaylen Waddle if they thought getting Engram more involved in the offense would have been a notable upgrade. Engram belongs in TE2 purgatory for the time being.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.headline: Pat Freiermuth caught his only target for one yard in the Steelers’ Week 12 win over the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.analysis: Freiermuth didn’t have his first target until the beginning of the fourth quarter. The 28-year-old was a consistent target of Aaron Rodgers, but he didn’t appear to have much of a rapport with Mason Rudolph in their first game together. Freiermuth can’t be trusted as more than a low-end TE2 for Week 13 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.headline: Pat Freiermuth caught all five of his targets for 39 yards in the Steelers’ Week 11 loss to the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.analysis: Freiermuth ran 33 routes on the day while Darnell Washington logged 22 routes and had three targets from Aaron Rodgers. Freiermuth was fourth on the team in targets and receiving yards. Sunday was only the fourth time this season Freiermuth had more than four catches in a game. His waning route participation and the run heaviness of the Pittsburgh offense make Freiermuth nothing more than a desperation option for Week 12 against Denver.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.headline: Pat Freiermuth caught 2-of-3 targets for 35 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 10 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.analysis: This was one to forget for the entire Pittsburgh offense, who managed to gain just 23 yards of total offense through the first three quarters of play, limiting the fantasy production of all parties involved. Freiermuth was one of two fortunate ones to salvage his fantasy day with a fourth quarter touchdown when the game was already well out of reach, although the modest reception and yardage totals were far too familiar for Freiermuth’s fantasy managers. He’ll remain a touchdown-or-bust TE2 ahead of a Week 11 matchup with the Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.headline: Pat Freiermuth (illness) is questionable for Week 10 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.analysis: Freiermuth was added to the injury report Saturday as questionable with an illness. A mid-range TE2 when healthy, Freiermuth’s potential absence likely wouldn’t change much for Darnell Washington’s fantasy outlook. Fantasy managers counting on Freiermuth will need to be proactive about alternative options as the Steelers play the Bengals on Sunday Night Football, which airs on NBC and Peacock.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.headline: Pat Freirumuth caught both of his targets for 35 yards receiving and added a rushing touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 8 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.analysis: Freierumuth is the Steelers’ designated tush push option, which will give him a little added fantasy value here and there. Despite the fact that Darnell Washington outproduced Freiermuth today, Freiermuth ran a route on 11 of the team’s 26 dropbacks, compared to just five for Washington. This simply wasn’t a big day for the Steelers’ passing attack, but we’d expect Freiermuth to remain a mid-range TE2 option going forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.headline: Pat Freiermuth caught 2-of-4 targets for 20 yards in the Steelers’ Week 7 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.analysis: Freiermuth didn’t appear to be bothered by his calf injury, and he quadrupled the targets of Darnell Washington (4-to-1) in this game. Washington was able to convert his only target for a touchdown, however, and Freirmuth dropped what would have been a 20-yard gain in the third quarter. Freiermuth will likely get a similar amount of targets in Week 8 against the Browns, for better or worse.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.headline: Pat Freiermuth caught 2-of-3 targets for 11 yards in the Steelers’ Week 6 win over the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.analysis: The Muth was clearly limited by his nagging calf injury in this game. He was added to the injury report over the weekend and played through the issue despite being hit with a late questionable tag. He was spotted hobbling to the sidelines at least once during this game, though he ultimately gutted it out and played through the issue. He and Darnell Washington each played 54 of 76 offensive snaps. Better days should be ahead for Freiermuth once he’s healthy, but it will be hard to trust him as anything other than a TE2 flyer for his Week 7 game against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.headline: Pat Freiermuth (calf) is active for Week 6 against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.analysis: Muth was a late addition to the injury report, with the Steelers adding him on Saturday and listing him as questionable. With multiple starting receivers out this week, Muth will be asked to take on more work as a pass-catcher, moving him up the TE2 ranks. Inactive for the Steelers are WR Ben Skowronek, QB Drew Allar, QB Will Howard, CB Sean Murphy-Bunting, RB Eli Heidenreich, CB Terell Smith, and DL Kevin Jobity Jr.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Steelers are “optimistic” Pat Freiermuth (calf) will play in Week 6 against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.analysis: Freiermuth was added to the injury report on Saturday. The team listed him as questionable for Week 6. A last-minute addition to the injury report is never a good sign, so we wouldn’t be surprised if his snaps are limited even if he is active. On the other hand, with Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman out, the Steelers may have no choice but to play a banged-up Muth more than expected. He will be a high-risk TE2 if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.headline: Pat Freiermuth (calf) is questionable for Week 6 against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.analysis: Freiermuth popped up on the injury report Saturday afternoon with a calf injury. He’s questionable for this weekend against the Buccaneers. Freiermuth would’ve been in line for a sizable workload with the Steelers down multiple wide receivers. Coming off a two touchdown performance in Week 5, fantasy managers need a backup plan in case Freiermuth is ultimately ruled out against Tampa Bay.

https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.headline: Pat Bryant caught 4-of-7 targets for 42 yards in the Broncos’ Week 12 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.analysis: Bryant was able to make the most of an unfathomably bad day from Bo Nix, although it’s far from a fantasy stat line fantasy managers are clamoring for. Bryant has been one of the more consistent options for the Denver passing attack, but that’s not the compliment it should be. Bryant is at best a FLEX for Week 13 against the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.headline: Pat Bryant (ankle) is practicing in full for Denver’s Week 12 game against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.analysis: Bryant survived an injury scare on Sunday and this confirms that he should be in a good place to play on Friday. He took over as Denver’s No. 2 receiver against the Raiders, out-targeting Courtland Sutton 4-2, but wasn’t able to make much fantasy hay of the increased workload. Pittsburgh should be another game that mostly sees Bryant as a FLEX play at best.

https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.headline: Pat Bryant caught 3-of-4 targets for 32 yards in the Broncos’ Week 11 win over the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.analysis: Bryant got off to a hot start with a 20-yard grab on the Broncos’ opening drive. That would account for over half of his production on the day as Bo Nix could not get any of his receivers going. Bryant still finished second among the team’s wideouts in targets, though Evan Engram and Jonah Coleman both saw more opportunities in the passing game than him. Bryant also survived an injury scare late in the game. His leg got rolled on during a tackle in the fourth quarter. He tried to get up but went back down on the field. Bryant walked off under his own power, worked through the issue on the sideline, and returned a few plays later. We expect to see him on the injury report, but he should be available for Week 12. He will be in the WR4 mix versus Pittsburgh.

https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.headline: Pat Bryant caught 4-of-5 targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 9 win over the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.analysis: Active for the first time since Week 4, a returning Bryant (ankle) ended up leading the Broncos in receiving. Jaylen Waddle was forced to depart after only one target with a concussion. Bryant’s score, his second of the season, was a 26-yarder against broken coverage. Although his snaps were somewhat rationed following his month-long layoff, Bryant avoided setbacks and continues to look like a dark horse contender for No. 1 receiver duties in Denver. He’s a solid bench option heading into the Broncos’ Week 10 bye before their Week 11 return against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.headline: Broncos activated WR Pat Bryant (ankle) from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.analysis: The young receiver will make his return to the active game-day roster after missing the minimum four games after injuring his ankle in Week 4. He returns to a passing attack with no clear direction or upside, with no receiver other than Courtland Sutton playing in a near every-down role of late. Perhaps he can carve out a featured role, but it is more likely this team simply doesn’t have viable weekly fantasy assets through the air.

https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.headline: Pat Bryant (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.analysis: Bryant is expected to be activated from injured reserve by Saturday, but the team has officially listed him as questionable. He makes for a boom-bust FLEX in his first game back. The Broncos’ passing offense has struggled this season. Perhaps Bryant’s return lifts it up.

https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.headline: Pat Bryant (ankle) is practicing in full for Week 9 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.analysis: Bryant’s 21-day practice window has been opened, and it begins with a full session, putting him on track to play in Week 9 against the Panthers. The Broncos’ passing game has severely underperformed expectations. Bryant does not necessarily need to be added in 12-team formats, though he could ultimately compete for No. 2 wide receiver duties.

https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.headline: The Denver Gazette’s Chris Tomasson said “indications point to Broncos WR Pat Bryant returning to practice this week.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.analysis: Bryant has missed the Broncos’ last four games after being placed on injured reserve with an ankle injury. The 23-year-old receiver is eligible to return whenever the Broncos deem him ready to do so, and his practicing this week would mean the team has opened his 21-day return window. Bryant has caught nine passes for 133 yards and one touchdown and was third among Broncos receivers in routes run (91) through the first four weeks of the season. He could make for an interesting stash in deeper leagues, but fantasy managers shouldn’t rush to put him in their lineups whenever he does return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.headline: Broncos placed Pat Bryant on injured reserve with an ankle injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.analysis: Bryant will be eligible to return from injured reserve in Week 9, when the Broncos face the Panthers. The Broncos go on bye in Week 10, though, so if he isn’t feeling ready to play, they could hold him out until they face the division-rival Raiders in Week 11. Bryant’s absence could create more opportunities for Courtland Sutton and Marvin Mims, but Jaylen Waddle may end up hogging targets instead.

https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Broncos WR Pat Bryant will miss “a few weeks” after suffering a sprained ankle in Week 4’s loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.analysis: Bryant was carted from the field in the second half of Sunday’s game after taking a big hit over the middle. The 23-year-old receiver currently ranks third among Broncos receivers with 91 routes run and has played 55 percent of his snaps out wide. Troy Franklin or Marvin Mims could be in line to see more snaps while Bryant is sidelined, but it’s hard to imagine either player becoming valuable fantasy assets at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.headline: Courtland Sutton caught 1-of-8 targets for four yards in the Broncos’ Week 12 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.analysis: To be fair to Sutton, Bo Nix was trying to get him the football. To be honest, he didn’t. Sutton was once among the better wideout options, but he’s been consistently putting up duds like this for too long in 2026 to count on him in fantasy. Even in a friendly matchup against the Dolphins in Week 13, fantasy managers should be looking elsewhere.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.headline: Courtland Sutton did not catch either of his targets in the Broncos’ Week 11 win over the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.analysis: Sutton posted a solid 5-45-1 receiving line before the Broncos’ Week 10 bye, but it felt like the team was ready to move Pat Bryant into a larger role. Bryant only managed four targets, but it was his first time seeing more looks than Sutton all year. He caught three of them for 32 yards. Now facing increased competition for opportunities, Sutton’s fantasy outlook is going from bad to worse headed into Week 12. He will be a touchdown-or-bust WR5 versus the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.headline: Courtland Sutton caught 5-of-9 targets for 45 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 9 win over the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.analysis: Even with Pat Bryant (ankle) returning, Sutton posted new season highs for receptions and targets as Jaylen Waddle departed early with a concussion. He did get out-gained by Bryant, who also found the end zone. Sutton is a perfectly fine role player, but it is the bitter truth that he is no longer a featured option. With Waddle now having the Broncos’ bye week to get healthy, Sutton could be returning as the team’s No. 3 option. He’s a borderline WR4/5 hold in leagues with shallower benches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.headline: Courtland Sutton caught all four of his targets for 53 yards in the Broncos’ Week 8 win over the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.analysis: Sutton’s 53 yards today are now a season-high, as are his four receptions. That, however, largely speaks to how unproductive he has been this year. Sutton has more games under 20 yards than over 40. He also has just one touchdown through eight games. His signs of life versus the Chiefs will keep him in the WR5 ranks for Week 9, but the ceiling remains nonexistent.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said Jaylen Waddle suffered a chest injury and his Week 8 status has not been determined.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.analysis: Waddle left Sunday’s game against the Cardinals with the chest injury. It was, according to Rapoport, an “aggravation of his previous chest injury.” Waddle could try to practice later this week, but would appear to be iffy unless he can log a practice session by Friday. If Waddle is sidelined this week against the Chiefs, Courtland Sutton would likely see more targets and become an interesting flex option against a tough KC secondary. Sutton over the past four weeks leads Denver in air yards and has the second most targets behind Waddle.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.headline: Courtland Sutton caught 3-of-5 targets for 45 yards in the Broncos’ Week 7 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.analysis: Sutton’s 45 yards today were one shy of his season-high, which mostly speaks to how quiet the veteran wideout has been this year. He has only topped 25 yards twice and has just one touchdown to his name. Jaylen Waddle injured his chest late in this contest and could be out for Week 8. That would funnel a few more targets Sutton’s way, but it’s not like Waddle was putting up loads of counting stats that now shift to Sutton. Even if Waddle is out for Week 8 versus the Chiefs, Sutton would have a hard time pushing past the WR4 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.headline: Courtland Sutton caught 2-of-3 targets for 19 yards in the Broncos’ Week 6 win over the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.analysis: Nix’s only incompletion when targeting Sutton resulted in the veteran receiver getting rocked over the middle of the field on a ball Nix led him directly into oncoming contact. Sutton vented his frustration by repeatedly pounding the ground following the hit, with it unclear whether it was due to the hit or the incompletion on third down on a night the Broncos struggled to move the football to the tune of only 168 yards of total offense. Fantasy managers likely aren’t utilizing Sutton as a weekly option, but will want to track his practice status ahead of a Week 7 meeting with the Cardinals if bye week fill-ins are required.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.headline: Courtland Sutton caught 2-of-3 targets for 18 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 5 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.analysis: It’s the first touchdown for Sutton on the season, and it tied the game at 17-17. The 31-year-old was unable to find room versus the Chargers’ secondary, and for the fifth-straight week, Sutton was held under 50 yards. His size could give the smaller Seahawks’ defensive backs trouble, but he’s essentially a touchdown-dependent FLEX for Week 6 against Seattle.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.headline: Courtland Sutton caught 1-of-6 targets for four yards in the Broncos’ Week 4 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.analysis: Sutton was the recipient of a couple off-target intermediate looks from Bo Nix, who struggled to place the ball against the 49ers secondary. Sutton could see an expanded role in the Denver offense if Pat Bryant is out long term following his leg injury in Week 4. Sutton has been targeted on 16 percent of his pass routes this season; he has nine receptions through four games. Sutton should only be rostered in deeper leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.headline: Courtland Sutton caught 3-of-7 targets for 46 yards in the Broncos’ Week 3 win over the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.analysis: Sutton tied for the team lead in targets while pacing the offense in yards, which highlights the struggles that persist in Davis Webb’s offense through three games. He will be off the FLEX radar ahead of a Week 4 showdown against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.headline: Rico Dowdle rushed 11 times for 71 yards in the Steelers’ Week 12 win over the Broncos while catching one pass for three yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.analysis: Dowdle was the much more effective runner between he and Jaylen Warren, although the bulk of the yardage came on one 27-yard scoot. He also lost a fumble, but the Steelers still gave him some carries after that turnover. A solid yardage day, but fantasy managers shouldn’t expect similar production in Week 13 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.headline: Rico Dowdle had five rushes for 15 yards in the Steelers’ Week 11 loss to the Eagles, adding four catches for 19 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.analysis: Jaylen Warren, meanwhile, managed 29 yards on nine rushing attempts and caught one of his two targets. Dowdle got quite a lot of second half playing time, finishing the game with 16 pass routes to 36 routes for Warren. Dowdle is good for 7-10 touches per week in the low-octane Pittsburgh offense, making him a desperation flex option in deeper formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.headline: Rico Dowdle rushed five times for 26 yards in the Steelers’ Week 10 loss to the Bengals, adding eight yards on two receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.analysis: Dowdle played sparingly in the first half as the Steelers were completely incapable of moving the ball. In fact, Pittsburgh managed just 40 yards of total offense in the first half before losing 17 yards in the third quarter, leaving them with a putrid 23 yards of total offense through three quarters. The extremely negative game script clearly limited the backfield’s opportunities and production, with Dowdle unable to escape the onslaught. His next opportunity to return usable counting stats comes in Week 11 against the Eagles, where he’ll remain off the fantasy radar.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.headline: Rico Dowdle rushed 15 times for 56 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 8 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.analysis: Dowdle looked good in this one, and while he didn’t hit the home run play that Jaylen Warren did, he was ripping off big gains throughout the day. Dowdle played just six fewer snaps than Warren, ran four fewer routes, and had two fewer carries, so he needs to be rostered as an RB3 who would have low-end RB2 value if Warren were to get hurt.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.headline: Rico Dowdle rushed nine times for 48 yards in the Steelers’ Week 7 win over the Saints, adding six catches for 45 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.analysis: Dowdle was the clear backup to Jaylen Warren, but he was able to have a solid day thanks in large part to checkdowns from Aaron Rodgers. The 28-year-old had a long rush of 16 yards, and the toe injury that sidelined him earlier in the campaign doesn’t appear to be bothering him. Dowdle is a FLEX option for Week 8 against the Browns, at best.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.headline: Rico Dowdle (knee) is active for Week 7 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.analysis: The knee issue was new for Dowdle and limited him to three partial practices this week. He was listed as questionable for Week 7 on Friday. Dowdle will once again form the 1B portion of Pittsburgh’s backfield committee. He’s a low-end RB3 versus the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.headline: Rico Dowdle (knee) is questionable for Week 7 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.analysis: Dowdle was listed as limited throughout the week and will officially be questionable entering this week’s game with the Saints. This is a new injury he is dealing with but it doesn’t sound like he’s at serious risk of missing the game at this time. Dowdle played on just 17 percent of snaps in his return to action last week and saw 11 opportunities. He’ll profile as a low-end RB3 this week if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.headline: Rico Dowdle (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.analysis: It’s a new injury that popped up on Wednesday, but with two limited sessions we’re not overly concerned about Dowdle missing Sunday morning’s Civil Unrest Bowl in Paris. He’ll be in the RB3/FLEX discussion.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.headline: Rico Dowdle (toe) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.analysis: The Steelers will likely limit Dowdle’s reps for a few weeks as he manages the toe injury that cost him three games. He should be good to go for Sunday’s game by Friday. Dowdle saw 10 touches in his first game back and looked relatively explosive, running for 40 yards on seven attempts. He is in the RB3 mix for Week 7 versus the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.headline: Rico Dowdle rushed seven times for 40 yards in the Steelers’ Week 6 win over the Bucs, adding three catches for nine yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.analysis: Dowdle was active for the first time since injuring his toe in Week 2. He initially formed a near 50-50 committee with Jaylen Warren, but the latter pulled away in the fourth quarter and overtime. Warren racked up four carries and one catch in overtime alone, bringing his touch total from 11 to 16. Dowdle saw a single carry in the extra frame. Dowdle’s role should grow in the coming weeks, but it’s clear that Warren is the top option in the backfield, leaving Dowdle as a low-end RB3 for Week 7 versus the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.headline: Michael Pittman caught 1-of-2 targets for seven yards in the Steelers’ Week 12 win over the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.analysis: Pittman was playing in his first game since Week 4, and he — and most of the Pittsburgh offense — didn’t have much chemistry with Mason Rudolph in a game where the Steelers’ defense was their best offense. The former Colt could be an option in the coming weeks, but shouldn’t be trusted in Week 13 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.headline: Steelers activated Michael Pittman (foot) from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.analysis: Pittman is on track to play in Week 12 against the Broncos, catching passes thrown by Mason Rudolph. He is only a WR4/FLEX, given the circumstances. The Steelers’ offense might need a week or two to adjust to their new quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.headline: Michael Pittman (foot) practiced in full on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.analysis: Pittman is expected to return from injured reserve for Week 12 against the Broncos. Two full practices to open the week keep him on track to suit up on Friday. With Aaron Rodgers gone and the Steelers’ receiver room at full strength, Pittman will be a weak FLEX option if activated from IR.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.headline: Michael Pittman (foot) practiced in full on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.analysis: Mike McCarthy has said he is “very confident” that Pittman will play in Week 12 and this listing does little to douse that. It’s hard to understand if Pittman’s return will actually make Aaron Rodgers target the middle of the field or not, but he would be a rough FLEX play either way in his first game off IR with all 32 teams playing in Week 12.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.headline: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said he is “very confident” Michael Pittman (foot) will play in Week 12 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.analysis: Pittman hasn’t played since Week 4 and has put together a forgettable 7-89-0 line in the three games he has suited up for this season. His return comes as the Steelers are in the midst of an offensive slump, as they’ve averaged just 19.3 points per game in their last four games while going 1-3. They’ll need all hands on deck as they prepare to face a tough Broncos defense on Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.headline: Steelers did not activate Michael Pittman (foot) ahead of Week 11.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.analysis: Pittman will remain on injured reserve for at least another week. The team gets back fellow wide receiver Roman Wilson, who should join DK Metcalf and rookie Germie Bernard as the starters from 11-personnel. Fantasy managers are likely only able to confidently start Metcalf against the Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.headline: Michael Pittman (foot) is questionable for Pittsburgh’s Week 11 game against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.analysis: Pittman got in two full sessions on Thursday and Friday after a limited practice on Wednesday. It would not be surprising at all if he were activated for this game ahead of Sunday, though we wouldn’t quite call it a certainty. If he does come back, he may serve more as a governor for Germie Bernard than as someone you’re excited to start in fantasy right away.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.headline: Michael Pittman (foot) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.analysis: Pittman is tentatively on track to return in time for the Steelers’ Week 11 game against the Eagles. In his three games played from Weeks 1-3, Pittman caught seven passes for 89 yards. He will only be a WR4/5 when he returns to the field, though the Steelers do not currently have a starting wide receiver who is reliably producing. It is possible for him to carve out a role in the coming weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.headline: Steelers designated Michael Pittman (foot) to return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.analysis: Roman Wilson was also designated to return. Head coach Mike McCarthy told reporters earlier this week that he was hopeful both Pittman and Wilson would be able to return this week. Getting back on the practice field is a step in the right direction. Pittsburgh now has 21 days to officially activate both wideouts from IR. The return of either one will likely remove an already-slumping Germie Bernard from the FLEX mix. Pittman was officially limited on Wednesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.headline: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said he’s “hopeful” Roman Wilson (finger) and Michael Pittman, Jr. (foot) can return in Week 11.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.analysis: Wilson and Pittman, after being sidelined for about a month, could return to a Steelers offense in desperate need of pass-catching help. Before his finger injury, Wilson was interesting for fantasy purposes, seeing 14 percent of the team’s targets and 30 percent of the team’s air yards with a solid 23 percent targets per route rate. Pittman, meanwhile, was targeted on a lowly 13 percent of his routes over the season’s first few games. Their return could be a major issue for Germie Bernard, who’s had three straight quiet games, including a zero in Week 10 against the Bengals. Bernard won’t be playable in 12-team formats when Wilson returns to action.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle caught 5-of-8 targets for 53 yards in the Broncos’ Week 12 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: It’s far from one of Waddle’s best games of his career, but when you consider how atrocious Bo Nix was Friday, it’s considerably more impressive. He wasn’t able to get deep down the field, but he was without hyperbole the only relatively effective offensive option for the Broncos in Week 12. He’s a WR4 for the upcoming match against his former employer in the Dolphins in Week 13.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle caught 3-of-6 targets for 61 yards in the Broncos’ Week 11 win over the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Sean Payton tried to get Waddle going as a deep option today with mixed results. Waddle gained at least 18 yards on all three of his catches. He was also held to just three catches. Waddle has caught more than five passes in one game this year. Today was just his second outing over 50 yards. Waddle isn’t completely useless for fantasy purposes, but the case for him as a WR3 grows worse by the week. With no teams on bye in Week 12, Waddle will finally hit the WR4 ranks versus Pittsburgh.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle (concussion) was a full participant in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Waddle exited the Broncos’ Week 9 game against the Panthers with a concussion. He had time to work through the protocol with a Week 10 bye and is now back to practicing at the start of Week 11. Given his full participant listing, Waddle is trending to play this week against the Raiders. He has had a disappointing fantasy season and should be in the WR3 ranks for Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle suffered a concussion in the Broncos’ Week 9 game against the Panthers and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Waddle was listed as questionable in the first half but then ruled out to begin the third. It’s another nightmare development for Waddle in his first Broncos season, as he has struggled for both 100 percent health and productive box scores. Today’s injury came as Waddle skied for a target over the middle of the field and got high/lowed. He had just one grab for 22 yards before departing. The only good news is the Broncos are on bye for Week 10, meaning Waddle might not miss any game time beyond this afternoon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle (chest) is practicing in full for Week 9 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Waddle played through a questionable tag with this injury last week, catching 3-of-6 targets for 39 yards and one touchdown against the Chiefs. He apparently made it through the contest without re-injuring himself and can be started as a WR3 this week against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle caught 3-of-6 targets for 39 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 8 win over the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Starting with the positive, Waddle found the end zone for the second time this year and got going over the middle of the field with a 35-yard missile from Nix early in the second quarter. It’s his longest catch since Week 2, when he erupted for 138 yards on eight receptions, including a 49-yarder. On the downside, Waddle managed a pedestrian 19 percent target share and finished third on the team in receiving. He found the end zone and still scored a grand total of 12.9 PPR points. The Broncos’ offense is still a work in progress, even if today was a step in the right direction. Waddle will get another week in the WR3 mix when the Broncos take on the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle (shoulder) is active for Week 8 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Left tackle Garrett Boles and EDGE Zach Allen are also active. All Broncos players who were questionable for Week 8 are active. After a disappointing two months to start the year, Waddle is at the back of the WR3 ranks for Week 8. Inactive for the Broncos are S Talana Hufanga, QB Sam Ehlinger, OL Gavin Ortega, DL Jordan Jackson, DL Tyler Oneydim, OL Kage Casey, and TE Dallen Bentley.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Jaylen Waddle (chest) is “trending toward playing” in Week 8 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Waddle suffered the chest injury late in the Broncos’ Week 7 win over the Cardinals and a doomed trick play. He was leveled by Josh Sweat several yards behind the line of scrimmage. The Broncos held him out of Wednesday’s practice before giving him two limited sessions and a questionable tag. Though we suspect he is on some form of a snap count, it looks like Waddle is giving it a go. Already struggling to put up WR3 fantasy numbers, we’re regarding him as a high-risk FLEX play versus Kansas City.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle (chest) is questionable for Denver’s Week 8 game against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Waddle got in two limited sessions after missing practice on Wednesday. It feels like he’s on the optimistic side of questionable given the trend line, though of course you would have preferred to see a full session somewhere in here. It’s also possible he winds up on a snap count, so we’ll see if any insiders dig up anything on that this weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle (chest) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Waddle aggravated an existing chest injury on a trick play late in the fourth quarter of Week 7. A return to the practice field, in any capacity, Thursday keeps the door open for him to be available to play the Chiefs in Week 8, although fantasy managers are likely looking for an excuse to bench the over-hyped receiver. It would be prudent to look at other viable options in a difficult matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.headline: Germie Bernard caught 1-of-2 targets for 58 yards in the Steelers’ Week 12 win over the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.analysis: Bernard set up the Steelers’ only offensive touchdown with his long connection with Mason Rudolph. That was his only contribution, however, as Pittsburgh relied heavily on the run game as they built a big lead and didn’t appear to have a ton of trust in Rudolph in the rainy weather. Bernard doesn’t have much fantasy upside for the remainder of the year, and that includes his Week 13 showdown against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.headline: Germie Bernard caught 6-of-10 targets for 40 yards in the Steelers’ Week 11 loss to the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.analysis: Bernard led the team in both pass routes and targets. He didn’t do much with his opportunity, which mostly included quick check-down passes from Aaron Rodgers. Roman Wilson returned from a finger injury and caught three balls for 43 yards while DK Metcalf was ejected for unsportsmanlike conduct in the third quarter. Max Hurleman, meanwhile, led the Steelers in receiving yards and caught the team’s lone touchdown while running just 15 routes. Bernard, who has 97 yards over his past four games, will be a deep league PPR option next week against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.headline: Steelers designated Michael Pittman (foot) to return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.analysis: Roman Wilson was also designated to return. Head coach Mike McCarthy told reporters earlier this week that he was hopeful both Pittman and Wilson would be able to return this week. Getting back on the practice field is a step in the right direction. Pittsburgh now has 21 days to officially activate both wideouts from IR. The return of either one will likely remove an already-slumping Germie Bernard from the FLEX mix. Pittman was officially limited on Wednesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.headline: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said he’s “hopeful” Roman Wilson (finger) and Michael Pittman, Jr. (foot) can return in Week 11.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.analysis: Wilson and Pittman, after being sidelined for about a month, could return to a Steelers offense in desperate need of pass-catching help. Before his finger injury, Wilson was interesting for fantasy purposes, seeing 14 percent of the team’s targets and 30 percent of the team’s air yards with a solid 23 percent targets per route rate. Pittman, meanwhile, was targeted on a lowly 13 percent of his routes over the season’s first few games. Their return could be a major issue for Germie Bernard, who’s had three straight quiet games, including a zero in Week 10 against the Bengals. Bernard won’t be playable in 12-team formats when Wilson returns to action.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.headline: Germie Bernard did not catch any of his three targets in the Steelers’ Week 10 loss to the Bengals, gaining 10 yards on one carry.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.analysis: Bernard has now had three modest fantasy showings after his breakout game against the Buccaneers, failing to eclipse 30 yards in all three outings since Week 6. His output against the Bengals is more a microcosm of the performance from the entire Pittsburgh offense, a unit that gained only 23 yards of total offense through the first 45 minutes of play while losing 17 yards on two third quarter possessions. Fantasy managers that thought they found a hidden gem on the waiver wire a month ago have little to show for it and must question whether to start the rookie receiver in a middling matchup against the reeling Eagles in Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.headline: Steelers did not open Michael Pittman’s (foot) 21-day practice window.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.analysis: This is unfortunate, but it likely benefits Germie Bernard in the short term. Pittman told reporters that he had hoped to return following the Steelers’ Week 9 bye. The team will likely choose to ramp him up for at least one week once they open his 21-day practice window. Doing so tomorrow or Friday seems unlikely.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.headline: Germie Bernard caught all five of his targets for 30 yards in the Steelers’ Week 8 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.analysis: This wasn’t a big day for Bernard, but it wasn’t a big day for the Steelers’ passing attack either. Pittsburgh was able to control this game on the ground and with its defense. The good news for Bernard is that he was second on the team in targets and ran a route on 22 of Aaron Rodgers’ 26 dropbacks. Bernard is going to be more valuable in PPR leagues because of his shorter route tree, but he should be rostered in most formats given his ability and role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.headline: Germie Bernard caught 3-of-5 targets for 27 yards in the Steelers’ Week 7 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.analysis: Aaron Rodgers was focused on hitting his halfbacks out of the backfield much more than his wideouts, and Bernard was unable to get much done outside of a 20-yard reception. The rookie wideout had gone over 80 yards in his last two games, but this shows the volatility in Bernard’s fantasy profile as a rookie. He’ll look to bounce back against the Browns in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.headline: Germie Bernard caught 11-of-12 targets for 87 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 6 win over the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.analysis: Bernard began the game with a potentially catastrophic blunder by moving the chains on first down, only to run back behind the sticks in search of more yards. He was taken down behind the line to gain for a turnover on downs. Instead of banishing him to the bench, Aaron Rodgers continued to lean on the rookie throughout the contest for easy completions underneath. He tied DK Metcalf for a team-high in catches. Per the broadcast, it was the most catches by a rookie receiver of Rodgers since the grizzled veteran entered the league. Bernard went from a PPR scam to a full-blown breakout in overtime by extending the ball for a game-winning touchdown with two defenders draped over him. Bernard has 21 targets over the past two weeks. He also has at least 80 yards in back-to-back games. He is looking at a WR3 ranking for his Week 7 matchup with the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.headline: Steelers coach Mike McCarthy said Ben Skowronek (leg) has been ruled out for Week 6.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.analysis: We weren’t exactly worried about Skowronek siphoning many targets away, but with him out of the pecking order entirely Germie Bernard should be a wheels-up WR3 for Week 6 now that both Skowronek and Roman Wilson have been ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.headline: Jaylen Warren rushed 20 times for 46 yards in the Steelers’ Week 12 win over the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.analysis: Warren and Dowdle received all 31 rushing attempts as the Steelers relied heavily on the run game in Mason Rudolph’s first game as a starter. The 28-year-old tailback didn’t find much room, however, and this is back-to-back-to-back clunkers for Warren. He’ll try and get things going in Week 13 when Pittsburgh squares off against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.headline: Jaylen Warren had nine rushes for 28 yards in the Steelers’ Week 11 loss to the Eagles, adding two catches for one yard.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.analysis: Warren was snuffed out by a swarming Philadelphia defense that appeared committed to stopping the Pittsburgh rushing attack and forcing Aaron Rodgers to beat them (he did not). Warren ran 36 routes on the day to Rico Dowdle’s 16 routes, though it was Dowdle who led the backfield with five targets. Warren now has back-to-back down games in a collapsing Steelers offense.
