Things won’t get much easier in Week 12 against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.headline: Jaylen Warren rushed seven times for 15 yards in the Steelers’ Week 10 loss to the Bengals, adding 26 yards on five receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.analysis: The end results were obviously far from encouraging for the talented veteran, although they were overshadowed by the fact the Steelers managed just 23 yards of total offense through three quarters of play. Even worse, the team lost a total of 17 yards in the third quarter after gaining just 40 yards of total offense before the break. Warren has a solid opportunity to rebound in Week 11 against the hapless Eagles, where he’ll return to RB2 status in fantasy circles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.headline: Jaylen Warren rushed 17 times for 143 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 8 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.analysis: Warren tied a career-high in rushing, but the Steelers opted to try and run out the clock with Rico Dowdle, on Warren’s birthday no less, so Warren was unable to set a new personal best. Warren delivered plenty of chunk gains in this game, including a huge 51-yard run, but he split work pretty evenly with Dowdle. Warren had two more carries and ran four more routes, but this was as close to a split backfield as you can get, so Warren will really need to deliver on his touches to keep producing fantasy value. If you can get an RB1 in a deal for him, it might not be a bad idea to search for offers with Pittsburgh on a bye next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.headline: Jaylen Warren rushed 18 times for 101 yards in the Steelers’ Week 7 win over the Saints, adding three catches for 36 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.analysis: Warren got off to a hot start with 43 yards on the first drive, with 29 of those coming on a play that set up a short field goal. He totaled 78 yards in the first half, but found the sledding a little tougher in the final two periods with the Saints focused on stuffing the run. He outcarried Rico Dowdle 18-9, although Dowdle did add six catches to make the touches a little more even. Warren will look to impress again in Week 8 against the Browns’ front seven.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.headline: Jaylen Warren rushed 14 times for 50 yards in the Steelers’ Week 6 win over the Bucs, adding two catches for 28 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.analysis: Warren and Rico Dowdle, who was active after missing three games with a toe injury, split the backfield carries for the majority of this game. Warren finally pulled away from Dowdle late in the fourth quarter and overtime. Over the final 20 minutes of the contest, Warren out-carried Dowdle 7-2. He held a modest 7-5 carries advantage through three quarters. Dowdle was more efficient on the ground, but the Steelers clearly trust Warren more in all situations when push comes to shove. Warren will be in the RB2 mix when he takes on the Saints next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Rico Dowdle (toe) is expected to play in Week 6 against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.analysis: Dowdle has been out since Week 2 because of the toe issue. In the meantime, Jaylen Warren has looked like one of the league’s most dynamic backs on the ground and through the air. While his gargantuan workload will return to normal with Dowdle back, Warren should still operate as the team’s unquestioned RB1. Dowdle is just a mid-range FLEX play for his first game back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.headline: Steelers coach Mike McCarthy said “there’s a number you’d like to continue to give [Jaylen Warren],” even after Rico Dowdle (toe) returns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.analysis: “He’s produced, so it’s been heavy. It’d be great to get Rico back this week, too. ... Having him as a one-two punch was the vision of this offense, but Jaylen’s crushing it right now. He’s been awesome for us,” McCarthy continued. That’s a very telling “but.” Warren has to be regarded as the chair of a committee at this point rather than in a backfield split, and Dowdle probably doesn’t belong in the FLEX conversation coming off his injury until we see a good workload for him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.headline: Jaylen Warren rushed 15 times for 101 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 5 win over the Colts, adding six catches for 87 yards and another touchdown through the air.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.analysis: Warren got the Steelers on the board with an 80-yard catch-and-run, where he simply beat the Colts defenders down the sideline. He also ripped off a 50-yard touchdown run in the first quarter. The Steelers only had one other play go for longer than 17 yards on the day. Since Rico Dowdle has been out with a toe injury, Warren has emerged as a true RB1 in fantasy football. Even when Dowdle returns, you have to think that the Steelers have seen enough that they need to give Warren the lion’s share of the work.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.headline: Steelers declared RB Rico Dowdle, QB Will Howard, QB Drew Allar, CB Jamel Dean, RB Eli Heidenreich, CB Terell Smith, and DT Kevin Jobity Jr. inactive for Week 5 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.analysis: It was reported earlier in the day that Dowdle was unlikely to suit up due to his ongoing foot injury, so this doesn’t come as a major surprise. We could be looking at a big game for Jaylen Warren against an underperforming Colts defense. With Keenan Allen back for the Colts, the injury to Jamel Dean is a bit of a blow to this Pittsburgh secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.headline: Jonah Coleman rushed 15 times for 26 yards in the Broncos’ Week 12 loss to the Steelers while adding eight catches for 46 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.analysis: Coleman was able to “save” his fantasy afternoon thanks to some checkdowns and screen passes, although outside of a 17-yard connection it was all for minimal yardage. The 23-year-old found zero room on the ground against the Steelers’ front seven, and plodding wouldn’t be an inaccurate description. Coleman has looked the part for most of the year and has a good chance to rebound in Week 13 against the lowly Dolphins, but this was ugly.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.headline: Jonah Coleman rushed 24 times for 111 yards and three touchdowns in the Broncos’ Week 11 win over the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.analysis: The Coleman takeover was in full force today. He out-carried J.K. Dobbins 24-1 and added four catches for 18 yards. If you couldn’t tell, Coleman also saw all of the goal line work on top of his strong role through the air. He scored two of his touchdowns from inside the five and punched in the third from seven yards out. His longest carry of the day was a 14-yard scamper, but he still managed a respectable 4.6 yards per carry. Coleman fell forward on nearly every carry and broke plenty of tackles, boosting his efficiency numbers without needing a breakaway run. Coleman is a surefire RB1 for his Week 12 date with the Steelers the day after Thanksgiving.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.headline: Jonah Coleman rushed 17 times for 57 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 9 win over the Panthers, adding four receptions for 31 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.analysis: Coleman also put the ball on the ground near his own goal line on a Bo Nix pitch, but the Broncos were thankfully able to recover. Also thankfully for fantasy managers, coach Sean Payton continued to look Coleman’s way late after the miscue, including the very next play. Coleman experienced really strong usage in Charlotte, playing 58-of-75 snaps per PFF’s initial count while easily setting a new career high with his 21 touches. He has also now cleared 80 yards from scrimmage in back-to-back contests. It must be noted that today’s score was not a goal-line carry — it came from nine yards out — but he did receive a first quarter carry from the Panthers’ four-yard line. Coleman’s role continues to grow, thus far without setback. Hopefully that does not change when the Broncos come off bye in Week 11 against the Raiders’ soft defense. We will be ranking Coleman as a strong RB2 for that one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.headline: Jonah Coleman rushed 11 times for 41 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 8 win over the Chiefs, adding four catches for 63 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.analysis: Coleman out-carried Dobbins 11-7 and was the only Broncos running back to earn a target, of which he saw five. Most importantly, Coleman was on the field for goal line duties, and he cashed in with a touchdown late in the fourth quarter. Though he only averaged 3.7 yards per carry, Coleman was a handful for Chiefs defenders to bring down, routinely creating missed tackles while racking up yards after contact. Coleman’s best rep of the day was a 51-yard catch-and-run to set up his touchdown on the next play. Coleman saw all of the high-value touches in the backfield while leading the way in carries and targets. The takeover is all but complete, putting Coleman in the RB2 ranks for Week 9 against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.headline: RJ Harvey (knee) was ruled out for Week 8 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.analysis: Harvey was added to the injury report Thursday with a knee injury before being unable to practice Friday, ultimately ruled out for the team’s divisional clash against the Chiefs. Expect Jonah Coleman to serve as the primary rusher in addition to the possibility he sees his pass game involvement tick up in the absences of both Harvey and Tyler Badie, the latter of whom is on injured reserve. The increase in opportunity is enough to vault Coleman into viable FLEX territory for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.headline: Broncos coach Sean Payton, asked about Jonah Coleman, said touches were “something you earn and he’s done a good job of that.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.analysis: He also noted that Coleman’s touches were explosive. It’s hard to sit here with much certainty about what looks to be a three-headed Broncos running back room where every back has their niche, but Coleman probably enters Week 8 as the favorite of the three to crack 10 touches. Payton added, for the 17th time since he became Broncos coach, that he needed to get more touches for Marvin Mims on offense. We’ll believe that when we see it.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.headline: Jonah Coleman rushed nine times for 54 yards in the Broncos’ Week 7 win over the Cardinals, adding two catches for 15 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.analysis: Coleman returned to action after missing a month because of an ankle injury. He was immediately in the mix for touches and saw three opportunities before RJ Harvey got his first look. Coleman went on to lead the Broncos in carries. Both he and Harvey earned two targets apiece. Unfortunately for Coleman, he was the only Denver back who didn’t find the end zone in Week 7. Coleman has made a mess of a backfield that had just begun to stabilize. Now all three Denver backs will be low-end FLEX options for Week 8 versus the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.headline: Jonah Coleman (ankle) is active for Week 7 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.analysis: Outside linebacker Jonathon Cooper is also active. Coleman hasn’t played since Week 2, when he turned 10 carries into 39 yards and a score. The Broncos were banged up at running back that week. They have since established a stable two-man rotation with JK Dobbins operating between the tackles and RJ Harvey handling passing downs. Coleman will likely take a backseat to those two this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.headline: Broncos activated Jonah Coleman (ankle) from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.analysis: Coleman missed the minimum four games as he tended to an ankle injury suffered in Week 2. He led the team in snaps in that contest and could return to the primary rushing role considering the inefficient play of J.K. Dobbins in his absence, making him worthy of a start in fantasy circles in a plus matchup against the Cardinals in his first game back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.headline: Jonah Coleman (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.analysis: Coleman practiced in full all week, but the Broncos could technically give him another week to rehab the ankle. If active, there are too many unknowns regarding Coleman’s potential workload to start him in the FLEX, but he must be rostered in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.headline: DK Metcalf caught 3-of-4 targets for 36 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 12 win over the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.analysis: After being ejected from Week 11, Metcalf was able to find the end zone in his first game with Mason Rudolph as he won a one-on-one battle with Pat Surtain II on a 22-yard score. I

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.headline: The Pittsburgh Post-Gazette’s Gerry Dulac reports DK Metcalf could face fines from the NFL following his Week 11 ejection.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.analysis: Metcalf won’t be suspended for his repeated fights with Eagles defenders on Sunday but he could be fined for the behavior. Metcalf’s meltdown came after he had one catch for two yards in the first half. Among the most inefficient wide receivers in the game, Metcalf has had a disappointing 2026 campaign as the team’s No. 1 wideout. He’ll profile as a flex option in Week 12 against a Broncos defense allowing the fourth fewest fantasy points per target to boundary wideouts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports DK Metcalf will not be suspended following his ejection from Week 11’s game against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.analysis: Metcalf allegedly tried to poke Eagles CB Cooper DeJean in the eye during an altercation. While Metcalf denies those allegations, whatever he was attempting to do certainly didn’t look good on tape. While the league has opted not to suspend Metcalf for his actions, he could still face fines for his conduct, which would be handed down later in the week. That said, Metcalf should be good to go for Week 12’s game against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports DK Metcalf’s actions will be “reviewed for potential additional discipline, including suspension” following his ejection in Week 11 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.analysis: Metcalf was ejected from Sunday’s game against the Eagles after receiving his second unsportsmanlike conduct penalty. The 28-year-old receiver ended the day with one catch for two yards and had two altercations with Eagles CB Cooper DeJean before he was sent to the locker room. Metcalf will almost certainly receive a fine from the league in the coming days, but a suspension could put him in line to miss Week 12’s game against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.headline: DK Metcalf was ejected in Week 11 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.analysis: He had two unsportsmanlike conduct penalties called against them. Metcalf, who has one catch for two yards on the day, was thrown out in the third quarter after two melees with Eagles defenders. It’s unclear why Metcalf was so intent on fighting various Philadelphia players, including — most prominently — Cooper DeJean. Metcalf continues his poor play (and decision making) in a Steelers offense that can’t get anything going on the ground or through the air.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.headline: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said he’s “hopeful” Roman Wilson (finger) and Michael Pittman, Jr. (foot) can return in Week 11.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.analysis: Wilson and Pittman, after being sidelined for about a month, could return to a Steelers offense in desperate need of pass-catching help. Before his finger injury, Wilson was interesting for fantasy purposes, seeing 14 percent of the team’s targets and 30 percent of the team’s air yards with a solid 23 percent targets per route rate. Pittman, meanwhile, was targeted on a lowly 13 percent of his routes over the season’s first few games. Their return could be a major issue for Germie Bernard, who’s had three straight quiet games, including a zero in Week 10 against the Bengals. Bernard won’t be playable in 12-team formats when Wilson returns to action.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.headline: DK Metcalf caught 2-of-6 targets for 54 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 10 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.analysis: Metcalf was blanked through three quarters as the offense was held to a paltry 23 yards of total offense in the first 45 minutes of play. He salvaged his fantasy day with two receptions for 54 yards and a touchdown on the team’s first possession of the final frame, tacking on a two-point conversion for good measure. Even so, Metcalf has been one of fantasy’s bigger disappointments this season, with just 432 yards and two touchdowns through nine games played, while also catching under 50 percent of his targets. Even worse is the fact that he has only three receptions of 20 yards or more this season. Metcalf will remain a shaky FLEX ahead of a Week 11 meeting with the Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.headline: DK Metcalf caught 1-of-6 targets for four yards in the Steelers’ Week 8 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.analysis: This was not a great game for Metcalf. He and Rodgers struggled to connect all day, and one of Metcalf’s drops was a near-40-yard pass that hit him square in the chest. The receiver simply dropped the ball and wound up hitting it forward directly into the cornerback’s hands. The good news is that Metcalf ran a route on every single dropback today, but he and his quarterback are not on the same page. Maybe the bye week will help, so don’t drop him yet.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.headline: DK Metcalf caught 2-of-6 targets for 56 yards in the Steelers’ Week 7 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.analysis: After having a whopping 15 targets in the Week 6 win over the Bucs, Metcalf was essentially a non-factor in this one. He was able to haul in a 51-yard connection that set up the lone touchdown for the Steelers, but for the second time in three weeks, Metcalf was held under four catches. He’ll be a volatile WR2/3 for Week 8 in a matchup with the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.headline: DK Metcalf caught 11-of-15 targets for 93 yards in the Steelers’ Week 6 win over the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.analysis: Aaron Rodgers couldn’t get much going outside of check-downs for the better part of three quarters. Then, in desperation mode, Rodgers started forcing targets to his No. 1 receiver. Metcalf saw 12 targets in the fourth quarter and overtime. He turned that into 81 yards, otherwise known as nearly all of his production for the day. Metcalf’s ability to win downfield and on the boundary isn’t being maximized by Rodgers, but the team is throwing so often that Metcalf can still rack up fantasy points with ease. With a vulnerable Saints defense on deck for Week 7, Metcalf is on the WR2/3 border as we approach the midpoint of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Bo Nix completed 22-of-40 passes for 169 yards with two interceptions in the Broncos’ 27-5, Week 12 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Nix was atrocious in the first half and created two Pittsburgh touchdowns, one on a fumble returned for a score and one on an interception where it’s not clear who he was trying to throw the ball to. His third turnover was a desperation throw on 4th and forever in the middle of the final quarter. This was an ugly performance that showed Nix’s floor is among the lower of the quarterbacks fantasy managers would consider. He’ll be a QB2 for Week 13 in a matchup against the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Bo Nix completed 19-of-35 passes for 225 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Broncos’ 38-24, Week 11 win over the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Nix got on the board early with a goal line toss to Adam Trautman, but it was all Jonah Coleman after that. The rookie running back punched in three rushing touchdowns, all from no farther than seven yards out. Nix did have several close calls on the day. He threw a well-placed deep ball to Troy Franklin, and the pass simply doinked off his helmet. Franklin was laying out for the ball, so it may not have been a touchdown, but it still would have juiced Nix’s box score. Nix also threw a dime to Marvin Mims on a flea-flicker that went down to the one-yard line. He was then stuffed on a sneak, after which Coleman made it into the end zone. All in, it was a better performance from Nix than the box score suggests. With no teams on bye next week, Nix will likely be relegated to the top of the QB2 ranks for his date with the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Bo Nix completed 25-of-37 passes for 237 yards, two touchdowns and an interception in the Broncos’ 26-21, Week 9 win over the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Today was only Nix’s third multi-score start of the season through the air, though it was also his second in as many weeks. It came as No. 1 wideout Jaylen Waddle left with a first half concussion. Nix’s touchdowns were a three-yard precision dart to Courtland Sutton and 26-yard busted coverage strike to a returning Pat Bryant. He also extended a few key plays with his scrambling ability, most notably avoiding a massive third down sack on the Broncos’ opening drive. It was not a perfect day, but Nix has inarguably been playing better since his dismal Thursday Night Football outing three weeks ago. Now he must wait and see on Waddle’s status coming out of the Broncos’ Week 10 bye, but Bryant’s healthy return could be a massive development. Nix will be a solid QB2 streamer vs. Vegas in two weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Bo Nix completed 20-of-32 passes for 222 yards and two touchdowns in the Broncos’ 28-24, Week 8 win over the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Fittingly, Nix’s longest completion of the day was a dump-off to Jonah Coleman that the rookie turned into a 51-yard gain. Nix has two completions of 50+ yards this year. Both have gone to running backs on throws near or behind the line of scrimmage. On the other hand, when Nix did push the ball downfield versus Kansas City, he was largely effective. He completed 4-of-6 throws farther than nine yards downfield. It was a small step in the right direction after weeks of middling production on intermediate and downfield shots. Nix will look to build on this performance versus a beatable Carolina defense in Week 9. He will sit somewhere near the top of the QB2 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Bo Nix completed 15-of-29 passes for 222 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ 30-16, Week 7 win over the Cardinals, adding seven carries for 74 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Per usual, Nix had a quiet day through the air, which is doubly true when you realize 52 of his yards and his lone touchdown came on an RJ Harvey screen. Nix struggled to get his deep ball going, missing several long shots that would have padded out an otherwise lacking box score. On the other hand, fantasy managers won’t be complaining after seeing his rushing line, which was largely the result of a 62-yard rushing touchdown late in the first half. Denver sent nearly all of their eligible pass catchers to the right side of the field, opening up a running lane big enough for at least one 18-wheeler. Facing a much stingier Chiefs defense in Week 8, we don’t expect another elite fantasy showing from Nix next week. He will be on the QB1/2 border for the AFC West showdown.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Broncos coach Sean Payton said he has not considered removing Bo Nix from the starting job.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: “He is going to become the byproduct of all the finer things that get improved. The improved play from our offensive line; the more efficient we are relative to downs; running the football. That’s our job as coaches here,” Payton said. Nix has been one of the worst quarterbacks in the league through six starts and Jay Glazer passed along word yesterday that Payton changed the terminology that OC Davis Webb had put in this offseason back to what it was last season, which apparently did not help Nix out. He’ll be hard to trust even with a slapdash Cardinals defense on tap for Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Bo Nix completed 17-of-27 passes for 107 yards in the Broncos’ 17-14, Week 6 win over the Seahawks, adding two yards on four carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Broncos managed just 168 yards of total offense on a night their defense carried them to victory in overtime. Nine of the Broncos’ 11 possessions, excluding the two kneel downs to end each half, ended in punts on drives that lasted five plays or fewer. Two second quarter touchdown drives had the Broncos playing with a lead for much of the game but they were otherwise unable to move the football with any consistency. An overtime interception by nickel corner Ja’Quan McMillian allowed for a game-winning, 53-yard field goal from kicker Will Lutz after the Broncos again failed to gain a first down. The win sends Denver to 4-2 while averaging only 18.7 points per game through six weeks. The team gets a scheduling gift with the Cardinals on deck in Week 7, although Nix cannot be treated as a starter-worthy fantasy asset outside of the deepest leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Bo Nix completed 16-of-127 passes for 123 yards with a touchdown in the Broncos’ 23-17, Week 5 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Nix also added 10 yards on the ground on his four carries. He once again wasn’t able to get the ball downfield, with a long passing gain of 34 yards on a busted coverage. He was at least able to find Courtland Sutton for a short touchdown, but this was an ugly day for both signal-callers. Nix is no more than a QB2 for a matchup against the tough Seattle defense in Week 6, and it’s worth noting that game takes place Thursday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Bo Nix completed 25-of-42 attempts for 214 yards and one touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 4 loss to the 49ers, adding two rushes for ten yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Nix’s play — including missing easy intermediate throws in the first half — left Broncos offensive coordinator Davis Webb without answers, a common theme so far this season. His lone touchdown came on a garbage time score to Jaylen Waddle. Nix was in check-down mode throughout the game against the Niners, finishing with a 4.9 aDOT. He was 5 percent under his expected completion rate, targeting his running backs 12 times. Until Webb and Sean Payton figure out the offense, Nix will be a superflex-only fantasy option without much of a weekly ceiling. He gets the Chargers in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Bo Nix completed 17-of-34 passes for 186 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the Broncos’ 30-26, Week 3 win over the Rams, adding seven yards and a touchdown on four carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Broncos were shut out in the first half amidst consistent struggles from Nix, who, for his part, turned in solid production in a third quarter that saw the Broncos knot the game at 16 through two touchdowns and successful two-point conversions. Nix and the Broncos would struggle to move the football again in the fourth quarter but a pick-six from safety Talanoa Hufanga gave them the lead with under five minutes to play. Stafford returned blows to send the Rams to a three-point lead before Nix’s game-winning score from one yard out. That final drive was aided by three key penalties to go against the Rams, the final of which was questionable, to put it kindly. Josh Wallace appeared to intercept Nix for the second time in the fourth quarter but a defensive pass interference penalty was called, giving the Broncos renewed life. Hufanga would intercept Stafford for a second time in the fourth quarter, this time in the end zone, to seal the victory for the Broncos as time expired. Nix and offensive coordinator Davis Webb have not looked good through three games despite the team’s 2-1 record, and will need to clean things up ahead of another NFC West showdown against the 49ers in Week 4. Nix is currently nothing more than a middling QB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-rudo.headline: Mason Rudolph completed 9-of-15 passes for 142 yards with a touchdown in the Steelers’ 27-5, Week 12 win over the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-rudo.analysis: Rudolph’s first start since the trainwreck that was the Aaron Rodgers dismissal was uneven, but it was better than the production Rodgers was giving the Steelers over the past few weeks. He found DK Metcalf for a touchdown on a solid throw that allowed Metcalf to take advantage of his size, and he kept the chains moving in the first half, for the most part. The second half was far less impressive, but good enough, especially with Bo Nix playing atrocious football. Rudolph will still be hard to trust as a fantasy option for Week 13 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-rudo.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that coach Mike McCarthy “has the full support” of the Steelers’ organization and the team is “not planning to make any immediate changes.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-rudo.analysis: McCarthy can rest easy knowing that the organization fully backs him. Rapoport’s “immediate changes” phrasing does allow room for interpretation, though. Perhaps the team could move on in the offseason. Until then, McCarthy will roll with Mason Rudolph as his starting quarterback. They face the Broncos on Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-rudo.headline: The Steelers have named Mason Rudolph their starter for Week 12 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-rudo.analysis: The news of Aaron Rodgers’ benching and Rudolph’s sudden promotion came in an 11:10 PM ET Tuesday evening press release. Normal stuff. While we wait for the next shoe to drop on the “Rodgers situation,” we can begin evaluating the “Rudolph development.” In short: Not much will change, though Rodgers’ recent immobility and subsequent inaccuracy had reached a boiling point. Rudolph will oversee an attack that figures to make a sudden swerve to the run, though the 31-year-old with 742 career pass attempts should be able to keep a wideout or two afloat in deeper fantasy leagues. The problem will be figuring out who, as DK Metcalf is having a poor season, Roman Wilson has just returned from injury, and Michael Pittman Jr. will soon join him. Rookie Germie Bernard has been coming in and out of fantasy usefulness, and Pat Freiermuth has caught some passes from Rudolph in the past. In the short term, Rudolph is not a Week 12 streaming option, and only Metcalf can be considered 12-team league viable as we wait to see how things shake out. It is possible, if not likely, the team eventually turns to second-year pro Will Howard or rookie Drew Allar for a late-season evaluation period.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-rudo.headline: The Steelers have announced they are benching Aaron Rodgers, with Mason Rudolph named the starter for Week 12 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-rudo.analysis: 42-year-old Rodgers’ play had taken a sudden, dramatic turn for the worse of late, but it’s still a stunning announcement, especially since it came via a terse team statement. It also comes one day after coach Mike McCarthy claimed he was not considering turning to one of his myriad other QB options (the team also has second-year pro Will Howard and rookie Drew Allar on the 53-man roster). Other information is scarce, except for the statement including Rodgers would be inactive for the Friday afternoon contest. With the Steelers playing on a short week, they are already issuing injury reports, and Rodgers was not on Tuesday’s edition. It would appear, rather unsurprisingly, the sides have simply soured on each other, an outcome that perhaps became inevitable following Rodgers’ recent downturn. Startlingly immobile, almost anyone would be an upgrade on Rodgers at this point, but Rudolph is really going to push the “almost anyone” framing. Needless to say, this is not an offense we are looking toward for Week 12 fantasy production. The next order of business could be Rodgers’ release. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-rudo.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said Steelers QB Mason Rudolph and Chiefs QB Justin Fields are potential trade targets for the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-rudo.analysis: Rudolph has been discussed as a potential trade target in past seasons, and the Steelers notably kept four quarterbacks on the roster after cut-down day. Fields, we suppose, could be expendable if the Chiefs really like rookie QB Garrett Nussmeier.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-rudo.headline: Steelers kept all four quarterbacks for the team’s initial 53-man roster.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-rudo.analysis: The Steelers will head into the regular season with Aaron Rodgers, Mason Rudolph, Will Howard, and Drew Allar, who shined in training camp and during preseason outings in Mike McCarthy’s offense. If the 2026 season goes south for Pittsburgh, look for McCarthy to see what he has in Allar and perhaps Howard. Rudolph will likely back up Rodgers to start the regular season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-rudo.headline: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer believes Will Howard will get “the first crack” at being the Steelers’ backup QB.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-rudo.analysis: Howard is set to compete with veteran Mason Rudolph for backup duties to begin the season. Rudolph and Howard were splitting reps in the team’s offseason program last month. NFL Network reported in January that Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy “likes Will Howard a lot” and sees potential in his offensive system. “I’m not saying the Steelers believe Will Howard will be the quarterback for ten years after Aaron Rodgers is gone,” Breer said. “But I do think Mike McCarthy sees a little something there and wanted to take a closer look.” Howard, going into his age-25 season, threw for 4,010 yards, 35 touchdowns, and 10 interceptions during his final collegiate season at Ohio State in 2024. He ranked fourth among all CFB quarterbacks in adjusted yards per attempt that season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-rudo.headline: ESPN’s Brooke Pryor believes the Steelers could look to keep Mason Rudolph “as one of six veterans on the practice squad if Rudolph would be amenable to accepting a role.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-rudo.analysis: Aaron Rodgers’ return has left the Steelers with a four-quarterback room of Rodgers, Rudolph, 2025 sixth-rounder Will Howard, and 2026 third-rounder Drew Allar. Presumably the Steelers wouldn’t want to move on from Howard or Allar on their rookie contracts, which naturally leads to the idea of Rudolph’s roster spot being in jeopardy despite him likely being the backup with the highest floor. These things sometimes just work themselves out via injury, but if everyone makes it to the end of the preseason healthy, the Steelers will probably have to move on from someone rather than carrying four quarterbacks on their 53-man roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-rudo.headline: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said QBs Will Howard and Mason Rudolph are splitting reps in the Steelers’ offseason program.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-rudo.analysis: Howard and Rudolph have split reps so far in Pittsburgh’s offseason program. With Aaron Rodger still on radio silence, the Steelers are making do with their current quarterback room. Howard is a sixth-round pick from last year while Rudolph is a veteran backup who has started for the Steelers before. They are splitting reps, indicating Howard is getting developmental opportunities while the Steelers are keeping Rudolph ready with the offense in case the veteran needs to step in. Of course, all this could be moot if Rodgers returns, but for now Howard and Rudolph are getting equal starting opportunities early in the offseason program.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-rudo.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Steelers expect Aaron Rodgers to play in Week 13 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-rudo.analysis: Rodgers started the practice week as a DNP. We’ll see if his status changes at all come Thursday, but this isn’t the first time we’ve heard the Steelers expect Rodgers back for Week 13. His status remains one to watch until the team releases its final injury report on Friday, but Rodgers appears to be trending in the right direction by all accounts, despite Wednesday’s DNP.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: Mike Evans (Achilles) is questionable to play in Week 12 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: Evans sat out on Wednesday and practiced in a limited capacity on Thursday. We do not know today’s participation level, but he is clearly still rehabbing his Achilles tendinitis. Regardless, he is a high-end WR2 at worst whenever he is active. He will be catching passes thrown by capable backup Mac Jones against a tough Seahawks defense this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: Mike Evans (Achilles) was a limited participant during Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: Evans was a non-participant during Wednesday’s session, and seems very likely to be a solid option even against the tough Seahawks’ defense in Week 12. Jordan Watkins (groin) was listed as a non-participant for the Thanksgiving practice.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: Mike Evans (Achilles) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: This is almost certainly just load management for the superstar wide receiver. Evans returned ot action last week, posting a 6/109/1 receiving line. He should be viewed as a talent- and volume-based WR2 against the Seahawks’ top-tier defense. Jordan Watkins (groin) will also sit out on Wednesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: Mike Evans caught 6-of-7 targets for 109 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 11 win over the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: Fantasy managers took a collective sigh of relief after Evans was shown on the sideline grimacing in the first quarter. The team would never pass an injury update for their veteran star, who would later connect with quarterback Brock Purdy in the second quarter from four yards out to push the team’s lead to 21-10. The defense would step up with a pick-six on Minnesota’s subsequent possession, allowing the 49ers to coast to the win in the second half. As is typically the case, Evans caught numerous key passes on third down to extend drives, using his large frame to great effect on both slants and on the perimeter. His touchdown was a fade to the corner of the end zone, highlighting the full range of his talents against a formidable opponent. Fantasy managers will want to track his practice availability in the coming days, but it appears likely Evans can be inserted into lineups as a viable WR1 when the 49ers take on the Seahawks in Week 12.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: Mike Evans (Achilles) is active for Week 11 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: Evans returns from three missed games due to an aggravation of the Achilles injury that has plagued him throughout the season, and while he could see his snaps and routes managed, he brings a fantasy WR2 profile to the table in a difficult matchup against the Vikings. Fantasy managers likely did not start him considering the timing of the game this week, hoping he simply makes it through Week 11 healthy. Inactive for the 49ers are QB Kurtis Rourke, OT Enrique Cruz, DE Khalid Kareem, WR Demarcus Robinson, and LB Dre Greenlaw.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: Mike Evans (Achilles) will play in Week 11 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: Evans’ agent posted a video on his Instagram that can only be described as the corniest thing you will see today. In it, he vaguely announced that Evans was back after missing a few weeks with Achilles tendinitis. Evans will likely be managing this injury for the rest of the season, so we wouldn’t be surprised if he returns on a bit of a pitch count. Still, Evans was operating as the team’s unquestioned WR1 before suffering the injury. He will be on the WR2/3 border for his first game back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Mike Evans (Achilles) “is trending in the right direction” for Week 11 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: Rapoport does note, however, that Evans is “a little sore” after returning to practice on Thursday. The 49ers will make a decision on Evans’ Week 11 status on Saturday. If active, Evans will carry some re-injury risk, but reports have consistently indicated that the 49ers learned a lot from Christian McCaffrey’s bilateral Achilles tendinitis in 2024. It seems safe to assume that if Evans is active, his Achilles tendon is in good shape. Evans may not immediately return to his pre-injury form against the Vikings’ elite defense, but he should be in fantasy football lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: Kyle Shanahan said Mike Evans (Achilles) was questionable for San Francisco’s Week 11 game against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: We don’t have a practice status yet, but the 49ers said they’d make a decision on Evans’ status on Saturday. If active, he’ll be a reasonable WR3 bet due to the risk of in-game injury management risk and the tax the Vikings defense enacts on opposing passing games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: Mike Evans (Achilles) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: Evans has a chance to play in Week 11 against the Vikings. If active, Evans should be in fantasy football lineups. Re-injury risk is possible, but the 49ers have handled this issue smartly. We should have a decent indication as to whether he will make his return by tomorrow evening. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: 49ers GM John Lynch said “there’s a chance” Mike Evans (Achilles) practices on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: We’ll know more in a few hours, but even a chance at practicing is a small step in the right direction for Evans. The veteran wideout hasn’t played since Week 6 because of his Achilles tendinitis. We still expect this to be a ramp-up week of practice for him before returning in Week 12, but there’s at least an outside shot of him suiting up on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mac-jones/.headline: Mac Jones will start in Week 13 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mac-jones/.analysis: Brock Purdy (ankle) has been ruled out, leaving Jones as the 49ers’ starter this week. Jones played very well in multiple starts last season, though he faces a tough Seahawks defense. Jones is a starter in two-quarterback leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mac-jones/.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter named Gardner Minshew and Mac Jones as potential trade candidates for the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mac-jones/.analysis: Jaxson Dart will miss the rest of the regular season, though there’s hope he could return for a postseason run. Schefter noted that Minshew played under Giants OC Matt Nagy in Kansas City, giving him some familiarity with the team’s scheme. He also mentioned that it will not be cheap to pry Jones away from the 49ers. Jimmy Garoppolo is out there as well. He is a free agent and is reportedly still interested in playing, “in the right situation.” For now, the Giants are going to roll with Jameis Winston. Jake Haener will back him up. They will likely add someone as an extra backup option, but Winston is an interesting QB2 for fantasy purposes until they make a bigger addition.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mac-jones/.headline: Bleacher Report’s James Palmer believes that if a starting quarterback gets injured in training camp or in the regular season, 49ers QB Mac Jones would be the team’s top trade target.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mac-jones/.analysis: This is admittedly speculation, not breaking news, but the idea certainly makes sense. Palmer also believes that the 49ers could “probably” get the other team to “overpay a little bit.” Again, this tracks, especially if a playoff contender wants to keep their season alive. Palmer thinks Jones is also already aware of this being a potential scenario. That said, the 49ers added $300,000 in incentives to the final year of Jones’ contract, which happens to be this upcoming season. They wanted to keep him happy after how well he handled spot starts for QB Brock Purdy in 2025, and they could always choose to keep him in-house, given his reliability.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mac-jones/.headline: 49ers added $300,000 in incentives to Mac Jones’ contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mac-jones/.analysis: Jones, who could have started elsewhere this season if the Niners had found a trading partner, will now make $3.55 million in 2026, with another $2.25 million available in incentives. Jones will be a free agent after the 2026 season. The Niners reportedly wanted a first-round draft pick in exchange for Jones. The veteran threw for 2,151 yards, 13 touchdowns, and six interceptions last season over eight games as the Niners’ starter. Jones in 2025 was tenth in EPA per drop back, just behind Sam Darnold and Patrick Mahomes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mac-jones/.headline: 49ers HC Kyle Shanahan said he expects the team to keep Mac Jones for next season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mac-jones/.analysis: This comes after Lynch said he was surprised no teams made a trade offer for Jones during Day 1 of the 2026 NFL Draft. While Lynch may be surprised, the rest of the league may not be, as it was reported back in March that teams around the league believed the 49ers’ asking price for Jones was “astronomical” for the 27-year-old signal-caller. While anything remains possible, all signs seem to point to the Niners preferring to retain Jones for next season after he threw for 2,151-13-6 in just 11 games last season. Jones’ contract expires at the end of next season. It’s possible a few strong outings in 2026 could help generate a decent market for him in free agency during the 2027 offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mac-jones/.headline: The Athletic’s Dianna Russini reports teams calling on 49ers QB Mac Jones have described the asking price as “astronomical.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mac-jones/.analysis: The idea of Mac Jones starting somewhere in 2026 had a lot of gas in late January and February, but it has crashed in March as teams have been reluctant to meet San Francisco’s asking price. We’re not entirely sure why the 49ers would rather keep Jones as a backup than have, say, a third-round pick. Especially when they manufactured Jones’ value all on their own this past year after he was not exactly a first-wave free-agent signing in 2025. They could simply do that again with a different quarterback. But they seem to be anchored on keeping Jones.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mac-jones/.headline: The Athletic’s Jeff Howe believes the 49ers could demand a first-round draft pick in exchange for QB Mac Jones.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mac-jones/.analysis: Jones is signed through the 2026 season but could see significant interest from quarterback-needy teams this spring. Howe said “with that talented roster and coach Kyle Shanahan, the Niners don’t want a season to go to waste if Purdy goes down again. Since Jones was a major reason the Niners stayed afloat in 2025, they could rightfully be stubborn and hold out for a first-round offer.” This, along with a recent report that the market for Jones is not expected to be “robust,” suggests the veteran will remain in San Francisco for at least one more season. Jones in 2025 was fifth among all QBs in drop back success rate. Purdy, meanwhile, led the NFL in success rate.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mac-jones/.headline: The Athletic reports there is “not a robust market thus far for Mac Jones.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mac-jones/.analysis: These notes come from the Athletic’s Matt Barrows and Vic Tafur. In the article, they note that while the Niners aren’t looking to trade Jones, they “definitely expected to be tempted by a third-round-pick offer — if not higher.” In his first year with the 49ers Jones put together a solid 2151-13-6 line on 289 passes while posting a career-high 69.6 completion percentage. Given the current state of the quarterback market, it’s somewhat surprising to hear that a team hasn’t made a call about Jones, but there’s still time to let things unfold to see if a team whose free agency didn’t go as planned decides to extend an offer for the former No. 15 overall pick.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mac-jones/.headline: 49ers general manager John Lynch said, “somebody would have to come with something fairly strong for us to consider” trading QB Mac Jones.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mac-jones/.analysis: Jones started a few games for the 49ers in 2025, putting himself on the radar for quarterback-needy teams. However, Lynch said Jones has been “really good for us and we value that...I think we’re a better team with him on it.” The 49ers value Jones as a capable backup quarterback behind Brock Purdy, who has missed time due to injury over the last couple seasons. If a team values Jones as a starter and crafts a strong offer, Lynch and the 49ers would at least consider trading the 27-year-old.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mac-jones/.headline: The Athletic’s Matt Barrows believes the “stars could be aligning” for the 49ers to trade QB Mac Jones.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mac-jones/.analysis: Jones “didn’t just look like a starter in 2025 but someone who could lead an imperfect team.” Per Barrows, Quarterback-needy teams could be hoping that Jones becomes the next “Shanahan reclamation project” after watching Sam Darnold lead the Vikings to a 14-3 record in 2024 and the Seahawks to a Super Bowl victory in 2025. Darnold spent the 2023 season as a 49ers backup. The incoming rookie quarterback class is currently viewed as a thin group, which could spur teams to pursue Jones via a trade rather than rolling the dice on a questionable prospect. Barrows notes that the Dolphins, Cardinals and Vikings “are running Shanahan’s offense or something similar,” and views all three as potentially interested parties.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: 49ers ruled out Brock Purdy (ankle) for Week 12 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: Mac Jones will start in Purdy’s stead. 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said Purdy is dealing with a mid-ankle sprain, and the team is optimistic about his availability for Week 13 against the Giants. Jones piloted the offense efficiently last year and should be expected to do so again, albeit in a tough matchup this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: Brock Purdy (ankle) did not participate in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: That makes back-to-back missed practices for Purdy. The 26-year-old is considered day-to-day with his ankle injury, but it’s at least a little concerning that Purdy hasn’t been able to practice this week. Fantasy managers should hope that he gets in at least a limited session Friday before the matchup against the Seahawks in Week 12.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: Speaking on NFL GameDay Morning, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said Brock Purdy is considered day-to-day with his ankle injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: Purdy suffered a sprained ankle in the Niners’ Week 11 win over the Vikings and was a DNP on Wednesday. Rapoport reports the injury is thought to be “minor,” but noted that whether or not Purdy suits up for Week 12 against the Seahawks “remains to be seen.” Given the importance of the divisional matchup, it’s hard to imagine Purdy sitting at this point. We’ll see how his next two practices go to close out the week, but this doesn’t sound like something we need to be too concerned about just yet.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: Brock Purdy (ankle) will not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: Purdy sprained his ankle in the second quarter of his Week 11 win over the Vikings. He played through the issue but, according to Kyle Shanahan, is now considered day-to-day. With a NFC West bout versus Seattle on tap, we suspect Purdy will play in Week 12 despite the injury. On the other hand, Mac Jones was extremely successful under center last year, so the 49ers wouldn’t be in a terrible spot if they are forced to sit Purdy for a week. Between the injury and the nightmare matchup, Purdy will shuffle to the back of the QB1 ranks this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: Brock Purdy completed 21-of-26 passes for 255 yards and three touchdowns in the 49ers’ 35-10, Week 11 win over the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: Purdy and the 49ers controlled the tempo throughout against the aggressive Minnesota defense, expertly handling the blitz as the 49ers jumped out to a 21-10 lead in the second quarter by finding paint on three of their first four possessions. The lead was extended on a pick-six shortly thereafter, allowing the 49ers to coast to their ninth victory of the season. The team now has a stranglehold on the once-competitive NFC West and the inside track to the only bye out of the conference, with only the four teams in the NFC North threatening that claim. The former Mr. Irrelevant tossed three touchdowns for the second consecutive game and the fourth time this season, keeping him in the QB1 ranks in fantasy ahead of another stiff test against the Seahawks in Week 12.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: Brock Purdy completed 22-of-28 passes for 389 yards and three touchdowns in the 49ers’ 46-40, Week 10 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: Facing a porous Cowboys defense, Purdy and the Niners delivered just about everything fantasy managers could have hoped for in this one. Despite taking five sacks on the day, Purdy was nearly perfect, throwing just six incompletions while coming up with multiple big plays. Purdy’s first touchdown pass came on an 11-yard bubble screen to Deebo Samuel, with his other two coming on long catch-and-runs by Christian McCaffrey. In the second quarter, Purdy tossed a 14-yard pass to McCaffrey after evading pressure from several Cowboys defenders. CMC immediately turned upfield for a 74-yard score, and in the fourth quarter, another six-yard pass to CMC in the face of a blitz resulted in a 66-yard score after the Cowboys left Von Miller in coverage against McCaffrey. Purdy’s three touchdowns resulted in 151 passing yards, but came on passes that combined for just 20 air yards. That’s the benefit of playing with elite playmakers like CMC. Purdy and the Niners will get a true test in Week 11 when they take on the Vikings in Mexico City. We cautiously project Purdy as a QB1 despite the tough matchup on paper.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: Brock Purdy completed 17-of-25 attempts for 232 yards and two touchdowns in the 49ers’ Week 9 win against the Raiders, adding seven rushes for 40 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: Purdy made quick work of a Raiders defense that has ranked as one of the NFL’s worst over the past month. The Niners tormented the Vegas defense with well-timed screens and quick hits to the middle of the field. Purdy used his legs in a couple high leverage situations in the first half and scored his second rushing touchdown of the season. He connected with Christian McCaffrey and Jordan Watkins for his throwing scores. The ultra-efficient Purdy will take on the generationally bad Dallas defense in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: Brock Purdy completed 27-of-40 passes for 288 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions in the 49ers’ 29-20, Week 7 loss to the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: After losing seemingly every wide receiver to injury, it was only a matter of time before we finally had a down Purdy game. The truth is, he didn’t even play poorly. His first interception was on a pass that he was trying to throw away when safety Jesse Bates made an incredible toe-drag interception. The second pick was on a really nice play by linebacker Kendal Daniels over the middle. Purdy looked good and gave his team a chance to win despite a depleted offense. The 49ers will have a bye next week and then hopefully get back at least one of their primary receivers before a Week 9 game against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: Brock Purdy completed 21-of-29 passes for 264 yards and one touchdown in the 49ers’ 23-17, Week 6 win over the Commanders, adding 28 yards on five carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: Purdy and the 49ers absolutely dominated the first two quarters, gaining 303 yards of total offense on 41 plays before the break. The situation would alter course in a hurry after Purdy lost his top option through the air in the final minute of the second quarter as Mike Evans departed with an aggravation of the Achilles injury that had him listed as questionable entering the game. The team would go on to gain only 72 additional yards after the intermission, allowing the Commanders the ability to claw their way back into the game in the fourth quarter. Even so, Purdy now holds the NFL record for highest career passer rating after qualifying for the statistic with his 1,500th pass attempt in the win, which pushes the 49ers to a perfect 6-0 record ahead of a Week 7 meeting with the Falcons before their bye the following week. Purdy remains a surefire QB1 against the pass-funnel Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: Brock Purdy completed 19-of-29 passes for 189 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the 49ers’ 32-29, Week 5 win over the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: Purdy and the 49ers made the most of several short fields in this one. After an interception by Sam Darnold on the Seahawks’ first drive of the game, Purdy led a short 18-yard drive that he capped with a two-yard touchdown pass to Mike Evans to give the Niners an early lead. Purdy would orchestrate a long scoring drive in the fourth quarter, completing seven passes for 89 yards, with his final completion resulting in a seven-yard touchdown to Brandin Cooks. The Seahawks became the first team to sack Purdy this season, bringing him down three times in the backfield in the second half, but Purdy was able to evade pressure for the entire second half. Purdy and the Niners get a juicy Week 6 matchup next Monday against the Commanders, where he will profile as a solid QB1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.headline: David Njoku (shoulder) is questionable for Week 12 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.analysis: Njoku’s potential absence would allow Charlie Kolar, and theoretically Oronde Gadsden, to play more, but neither tight end qualifies as a top-12 option in that scenario. Justin Herbert (concussion) is also out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.headline: Keaton Mitchell (knee) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.analysis: Mitchell and David Njoku (shoulder) remain sidelined through two practices. The tight end group is highly unlikely to produce reliably this week, even with Njoku sidelined. Mitchell’s likely absence gives Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal touch-count boosts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.headline: David Njoku (shoulder) was held out of Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.analysis: Playing in his just his second game off I.R., Njoku suffered the upper-body injury against the Jets last Sunday. We already had practically nonexistent expectations for Njoku becoming TE2 relevant, but the new issue coupled with DJ Uiagalelei’s likely Week 12 start has him further from 12-team league lineups than ever.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.headline: David Njoku caught 2-of-4 targets for 21 yards in the Chargers’ Week 11 loss to the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.analysis: Njoku injured his shoulder on a 13-yard catch-and-run play on the Chargers’ opening drive, but he managed to play through it, leading his position group in targets along the way. The Chargers unsuccessfully tried to involve Njoku on play-action plays twice, including one at the Jets’ 20-yard line. Charlie Kolar caught one pass for eight yards. Oronde Gadsden did nothing. None of these three are on the fantasy football radar next week against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.headline: David Njoku was not targeted in the Chargers’ Week 10 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.analysis: Njoku briefly saw his role in the offense grow after fellow tight end Oronde Gadsden departed in the first quarter with an eye injury. Gadsden would return in the second half after the team deemed him questionable earlier, shifting Njoku back to a complementary role behind Gadsden and Charlie Kolar. Njoku’s next opportunity to return a usable fantasy score comes in Week 11 against the Jets, although fantasy managers are better off leaving him on waivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.headline: Chargers activated TE David Njoku from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.analysis: Njoku will try to fight for fantasy relevancy going forward, but there’s no need to pretend he has it at the moment with all three Chargers tight ends healthy. They also activated LB Denzel Perryman off the same list and sent G/T Branson Taylor to injured reserve in their place.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.headline: David Njoku (fibula) is questionable for Week 10 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.analysis: Njoku logged a week of limited sessions before drawing the questionable tag for Monday Night Football. He will need to be activated from injured reserve prior to Monday to play. Fantasy managers are likely better off making alternate plans considering the Chargers don’t play until Monday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.headline: David Njoku (fibula) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.analysis: Njoku is still within his 21-day practice window and has remained limited for five straight practices. He could end up playing on Monday night, but he does not need to be rostered.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.headline: David Njoku (fibula) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.analysis: Njoku is not worth rostering whenever he officially returns to the active roster, but he theoretically can contribute offensively. He will likely be a mildly productive member of the Chargers’ three-player tight end rotation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.headline: Chargers did not activate David Njoku (fibula) from injured reserve for Week 9 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.analysis: Njoku entered the contest listed as doubtful, although he practiced in a limited capacity all week. He might be able to return next week, but he does not need to be added in 12-team leagues. The Chargers declared LG Kayode Awosika (fibula), S Kendall Williamson (calf), CB Deane Leonard (concussion), WR Brenen Thompson (quad/hamstring) and WR Theo Wease inactive for Week 9 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.headline: Chargers ruled out Keaton Mitchell (knee) in Week 12 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.analysis: Losing Mitchell helpfully condenses the Chargers’ backfield for fantasy purposes, though the offense will suffer with Justin Herbert (concussion) sidelined. Omarion Hampton is a volume-based RB2. Kimani Vidal is an RB3/4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.headline: Keaton Mitchell (knee) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.analysis: Mitchell and David Njoku (shoulder) remain sidelined through two practices. The tight end group is highly unlikely to produce reliably this week, even with Njoku sidelined. Mitchell’s likely absence gives Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal touch-count boosts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.headline: Keaton Mitchell (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.analysis: Mitchell was listed as a DNP for the Chargers’ Wednesday walk-through. He suffered the knee injury in the first half of the team’s Week 11 loss to the Jets, only playing on a kick return afterwards and exiting the game in the second half. Mitchell does not need to be in fantasy lineups, though a potential absence would further boost Omarion Hampton’s resurgence for Week 12 against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.headline: Keaton Mitchell did not return to the Chargers’ Week 11 loss to the Jets after suffering a knee injury in the second quarter.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.analysis: Mitchell also suffered a lower-back injury after catching a six-yard pass on the Chargers’ opening drive. He was announced as questionable with the back issue, but was available for kick return duties to begin the following drive. Mitchell disappeared after that and was later announced as questionable to return due to the knee injury in the third quarter. Mitchell does not need to be in 12-team lineups against the Patriots, if active, next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said Omarion Hampton has reestablished himself as the team’s lead running back.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.analysis: The Athletic’s Noah Furtado asked Harbaugh why it took Hampton so long to reestablish himself as the team’s top running back. Harbaugh said, “he’s there (now). He’s showing it, proving it. And that’s all. That’s what’s important to me.” Hampton totaled 22 carries and one catch in Week 10. It sounds like he has a chance to continue handling a high-volume workload in the coming weeks, though the game script could hurt him if he fails to increase his passing game usage.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.headline: Keaton Mitchell (hip) was limited on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.analysis: Mitchell is trending in the right direction for the Chargers’ Week 10 game against the Ravens. The two teams play in this week’s Monday Night Football game. Mitchell is worth stashing in 12-team leagues, but he likely lacks RB2 upside.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.headline: Keaton Mitchell (hip) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.analysis: Mitchell should be good to go for Week 10’s Monday Night Football game against the Ravens. He and Omarion Hampton seemingly put a little distance between Kimani Vidal in the second half last week, though Mitchell only makes for a shaky bench stash.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.headline: Keaton Mitchell rushed seven times for 33 yards in the Chargers’ Week 9 loss to the Texans, adding three receptions for 34 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.analysis: Mitchell regularly rotated in and out as a member of the Chargers’ three-player backfield rotation, though he and Omarion Hampton remained far more involved than Kimani Vidal did in the second half. He looks spry as a rusher and receiver, ripping off double-digit gains in both facets of the game. Unfortunately, Mitchell’s biggest contribution was a fumble in enemy territory, which the Texans recovered inside the red zone. Mitchell is just a floor-based FLEX against his former Ravens team next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.headline: Keaton Mitchell had four rushes for six yards in the Chargers’ Week 8 loss to the Rams, adding three catches for 17 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.analysis: Mitchell, as usual, was third in rushing attempts, behind Omarion Hampton (9) and Kimani Vidal (8). His three targets led the backfield but didn’t amount to much. With the Bolts’ backfield being split three ways, Mitchell is going to struggle to get anything going without an explosive play or two. He should remain on most waiver wires ahead of Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.headline: Keaton Mitchell had two rushes for four yards in the Chargers’ Week 6 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.analysis: Mitchell did not catch his only target on the day. He was third among Bolts running backs in pass routes, behind Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal. The sad state of the Chargers offense and injuries to the team’s offensive line make it nearly impossible for Mitchell to post fantasy relevant numbers for now. The Chargers are on bye in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: Chargers ruled out Justin Herbert (concussion) for Week 12 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: Chargers backup QB DJ Uiagalelei is expected to start in Herbert’s stead. He threw a touchdown pass when Herbert left early due to a hand injury a few weeks back, but he is tough to rely on as anything more than a volatile QB2. Hopefully, Herbert can return for Week 13 against the Buccaneers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: Justin Herbert (concussion) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: Herbert is firmly on the wrong side of questionable at this time, likely leaving DJ Uiagalelei as the team’s starter against the Patriots this week. The Chargers also signed Jake Browning from the practice squad to the active roster, which bodes poorly for Herbert’s availability.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: Justin Herbert (concussion) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: Herbert was placed in the NFL’s concussion protocol following the Chargers’ Week 11 loss to the Jets. He took eight hits and six sacks that day. Herbert is firmly in the questionable camp at this time. His backup, DJ Uiagalelei, would only be a low-end QB2 against the Patriots if he gets the start this weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: Justin Herbert completed 15-of-21 passes for 131 yards and two touchdowns in the Chargers’ 24-27, Week 11 loss to the Jets, adding eight rushes for 32 yards and one touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: Immediately after the game, the Chargers announced that Herbert had entered the NFL’s concussion protocol. He took six sacks and eight hits, including one that resulted in a roughing-the-passer penalty after David Bailey hit him in the facemask while trying to disrupt a pass. Bailey had a field day aside from that, registering two quarterback hits and two sacks while forcing a fumble during one of the latter plays. Fortunately for Herbert, an offensive lineman recovered possession. Herbert’s connection with Ladd McConkey improved as the game progressed, leading to two fourth-quarter touchdown passes. Herbert also audibled to a quarterback-keeper from the Jets’ 10-yard line earlier in the game, which he successfully converted for a score. He notably had his left index finger taped up after halftime. If active next week against the Patriots, Herbert will be a high-end QB2. He is backed up by DJ Uiagalelei.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: Justin Herbert completed 12-of-18 passes for 129 yards in the Chargers’ 23-20, Week 10 win over the Ravens, adding 51 yards and a touchdown on seven carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: Herbert was not called on often after the Chargers jumped out to a 10-point lead in the first quarter, attempting under 30 passes for the fifth time this season. Two key turnovers were the difference in this one, the first a deflected pass off a Los Angeles defender that fell into the arms of linebacker Del’Shawn Phillips and the second a fourth quarter fumble recovery after Tarheeb Still stripped Zay Flowers with under three minutes to play. Herbert padded his counting stats with a 22-yard touchdown run on the team’s first possession but it still wasn’t enough for the veteran signal caller to return his first QB1 week of the season. Herbert remains a fantasy dud ahead of a Week 11 meeting with the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: Jordan Schultz reports the Chargers “immediately shut down all inquiries” for Justin Herbert at the trade deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: Schultz reports the Vikings called on Herbert, but the Chargers had no interest in moving on. It’s hard to understand what Herbert’s market value would have been — this has been one of the most disgusting outlier seasons for a previously good quarterback in recent memory — but the Chargers appear ready to move forward with him as their franchise quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said Justin Herbert may have suffered a left-hand fracture in the Chargers’ 22-44, Week 9 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: Last year, when Herbert injured his left, non-throwing hand, his trainers stabilized the hand, with extra padding and tape applied to his middle finger. The exact same thing happened today. Herbert fended off a pass rusher with his left hand before bracing himself with the same hand as he fell. Fortunately, he remained in the game long enough to complete a 58-yard touchdown pass to Quentin Johnston. After a trip to the blue medical tent, Herbert was on the sideline, helmet on, with his left hand and middle finger heavily taped and padded. However, he did not return. The Chargers’ pass protection remains a huge problem, allowing eight sacks on the day. Before exiting, Herbert completed 13-of-23 passes for 193 yards, one touchdown and one interception, rushing once for seven yards. Herbert told reporters post-game that he does not expect his left middle finger to be an issue going forward. We will know more once he undergoes imaging. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: Justin Herbert entered the blue medical tent in Week 9 against the Texans after suffering an apparent left hand injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: Herbert appeared to injure his left hand, and specifically his left middle finger, while fending off a pass rusher in the fourth quarter. He fractured the same hand, and seemingly the same digit, last year and underwent surgery to stabilize it in-season. We tentatively expect him to return after getting it taped up, but he will be playing hurt.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: Justin Herbert completed 24-of-32 attempts for 257 yards and two interceptions in the Chargers’ Week 8 loss to the Rams, adding four rushes for 15 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: Coming off their bye week, the Chargers looked worse than ever on offense, with Herbert apparently confused as to where to throw the ball or how to conduct OC Mike McDaniel’s complex pre-snap motion scheme. Herbert had a negative EPA per drop back. Both of his picks were of the mind blogging variety, thrown directly to Rams defenders in the open field. Frustrated and dejected, Herbert continues his worst pro season for the winless Bolts. As usual, Herbert — who ranks 33rd in fantasy points per game — won’t be a fantasy option in Week 9 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: The Athletic’s Noah Furtado reports the Chargers will try to “simplify” the team’s offense in the coming weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: Justin Herbert and the flailing Chargers skill position players have appeared almost comically confused about all the pre-snap motion OC Mike McDaniel uses. That came through in the team’s embarrassing Week 6 loss to the Chiefs when players were bumping into each other during pre-snap motion calls from Herbert. Head coach Jim Harbaugh acknowledged the team is considering narrowing the offensive playbook during their bye week. “Definitely looking at volume and where you can make it to where the players can understand,” Harbaugh said when asked about how Chargers players were adjusting to McDaniel’s complex offense. The Chargers have used pre-snap motion on 74 percent of their snaps, the fourth highest rate in the NFL. Last year they used motion on 56 percent of their snaps. Hopefully these adjustments lead to some production for the NFL’s worst offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba (ankle) is not on the Seahawks’ final injury report and will play in Week 12 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: The Seahawks have managed Smith-Njigba’s reps in practice all year, and this week was no different. He was limited on Wednesday and Thursday, but should be fine for Sunday. Smith-Njigba is an elite WR1, as always, and gets Sam Darnold (quad) back this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba (ankle) was limited during Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: That makes back-to-back limited sessions for JSN. The 24-year-old seems likely to go for the pivotal Week 12 matchup against the 49ers, but fantasy managers should pay a little closer attention to Friday’s report.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba (ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
