https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: Smith-Njigba was listed on the practice report with an ankle issue earlier this season, but has not missed a game. This is likely just load management for the 24-year-old receiver. Expect Smith-Njigba to still play in Week 12 against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 8-of-10 targets for 171 yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks’ Week 10 win against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: Smith-Njigba, as usual, accounted for well over half of the Seahawks’ receiving yardage, with no other Seattle pass catcher seeing more than three targets on the day. JSN’s catch-and-run touchdown came on a perfectly placed ball from Drew Lock after he was flushed out of the pocket. This marked JSN’s eighth 100-yard receiving performance in 2026; he has at least ten targets in all but two games this season. JSN has the strongest fantasy profile in quite some time. The Seahawks are on bye in Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 7-of-10 targets for 51 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 9 win over he Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: The fact that 54 yards is something to talk about says enough about the year Smith-Njigba is having, still handily leading the league in receiving despite the down performance. He remained the clear top dog through the air, receiving 10 targets on only 28 Lock pass attempts, largely confined to short area work as the Seahawks struggled to decipher the zone-heavy and two-high-heavy Arizona defense. Lock suffered an oblique injury in the third quarter that could place his Week 10 status in doubt, despite not missing an offensive snap, meaning fantasy managers of Smith-Njigba will want to monitor the situation ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Raiders considering Sam Darnold remains unlikely to play with a multi-week injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 6-of-11 targets for 118 yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks’ Week 8 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: Smith-Njigba was the entire offense in the first half, accumulating 92 yards through the air while the rest of the offense managed only two, including his receiving touchdown. Bears defensive coordinator Dennis Allen made adjustments after the break that confined JSN to only 26 additional yards the rest of the way. Smith-Njigba now has seven 100-yard receiving games in eight appearances as he extended his league-leading yardage totals, far and away the top overall wide receiver in fantasy circles. That position will not change ahead of a Week 9 meeting with the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 9-of-12 targets for 150 yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks’ Week 7 win over the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: Is there anyone in the league doing it better than Smith-Njigba at the moment? The reigning receiving leader put on an absolute show in this one, making two nearly identical bread basket catches down the left sideline in the second quarter, the first of which he snuck inside the pylon for his touchdown. He was forced out at the two on the second, resulting in an end zone interception from Sam Darnold two plays later. Those two long receptions before the break helped push Smith-Njigba to 126 yards and a touchdown before halftime, and he added an additional 24 yards on three more receptions in the final two frames as the Seahawks transitioned to a more ground-heavy attack while playing with the lead. Fantasy’s early-season cheat code has now gone over 100 yards in six of seven games while notching a league-leading eight receiving touchdowns. It goes without saying, but Smith-Njigba remains the overall WR1 in a solid matchup against the Bears in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 12-of-16 targets for 134 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 6 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: Smith-Njigba overcame a sluggish first half to extend his stranglehold on the overall WR1 in fantasy circles with a dominant second half and overtime period. While the 51 pass attempts from Sam Darnold were highly uncharacteristic of this Seattle offense, a complete inability to run the football paired with a negative script to form the perfect environment for Smith-Njigba to set a season high in targets and receptions. Smith-Njigba has now gone over 100 yards in five of six appearances to start the 2026 regular season and is in a good spot to continue that dominance when the Seahawks host the Chiefs in Week 7, where he remains a top-tier WR1 in fantasy circles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba (ankle) has no injury designation ahead of the Seahawks’ Week 6 game against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: Smith-Njigba played through an ankle injury in Week 5 and was limited in practice this week before getting a full designation on Wednesday. Despite the short week ahead of a Thursday matchup against the Broncos, he is off the injury report and good to go. Smith-Njigba is once again a top-three wide receiver option for Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Seahawks WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba (ankle) was listed as a limited practice participant on Tuesday’s estimated injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: Smith-Njigba gets a second-straight “limited” practice designation. The Seahawks have technically not practiced yet this week but it is notably the 24-year-old receiver gets back-to-back limited designations. With a Thursday matchup against the Broncos on the horizon for Week 6, the Seahawks are leaving the door open for Smith-Njigba to play; he battled the ankle injury in Week 5 and the short week makes this a tougher evaluation. For now, we still expect Smith-Njigba to play against the Broncos on Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Sam Darnold (quad) is not on the Seahawks’ final injury report and will play in Week 12 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: The Seahawks’ starting quarterback will make his return for a divisional showdown against the 49ers. Darnold has been fairly banged up this year, but hopefully the time off was good for him. He is a QB2 in Week 12.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Sam Darnold was listed as a full participant for Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: Darnold appears to be ready to go and will likely start Sunday’s Week 12 game against the 49ers. The question is how Darnold will play, as his 2026 season has been a mixed bag, at best. Drew Lock will be ready if Darnold struggles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Sam Darnold (quad) is expected to start in Week 12 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: Speaking on The Pat McAfee Show, Schefter said Darnold is expected to practice in full today. He also noted that, as of right now, there’s no quarterback controversy in Seattle. On the other hand, he did mention that the idea of Drew Lock taking over will at least be a talking point if Darnold struggles. For now, it looks like Darnold is back in the QB2 mix for a must-win matchup with the 49ers. We should get confirmation on his health via the team’s injury report throughout the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald would not say if Sam Darnold (quad) would start in Week 12.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: Darnold was able to return to practice on Monday ahead of the Seahawks’ Week 12 game against the division rival Niners. Macdonald suggested he wouldn’t make a call on a starting quarterback before Wednesday though. “I think before making any declarations with Sam, we’ll get through Wednesday, see how Wednesday goes,” Macdonald said. “So nothing official yet. He was able to train a little bit here, do some rehab here, he also was able to get away. He’s optimistic, but I think with today’s practice cadence and speed of today, it’s probably wise to wait to make any declarations until we get through Wednesday’s practice.” Drew Lock, the most efficient quarterback in the NFL this season, could get another start if Darnold isn’t quite ready. It’s an excellent matchup against a 49ers defense that profiles as a pass funnel.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Sam Darnold (quad/rib) was present at practice Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: The Seahawks held their “bonus” practice Monday as they prepare to face the 49ers on the road in Week 12. The level of participation of Darnold is not fully known considering the team does not owe a full practice report until Wednesday, but Darnold’s presence at practice appears to reinforce previous reports that the team expects him to return following their bye. A potential return would be a sizable boost to alpha wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said he is “really optimistic” that Sam Darnold (quad) will be able to start after the team’s Week 11 bye.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: Speaking on Monday with the media, Macdonald also reaffirmed Darnold as the starter after Drew Lock threw for 240 yards and two touchdowns in Week 10’s win over the Raiders. Lock has been solid for the Seahawks in four games this season, throwing for 837-7-0 while completing a career-high 73.1 percent of his passes. With the Seahawks now entering their bye, Macdonald said he his hopeful Darnold can log enough reps in time to play in Week 12 against the 49ers. We’ll see where things stand a week from now, but it’s clear there will be no QB controversey in Seattle whenever Darnold is ready to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said Sam Darnold (quad) will not play in Week 10 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: Macdonald said Darnold will need at least one more week to recover from the quad injury that sidelined him in Week 9. While Drew Lock (oblique) is dealing with his own injury, Macdonald said he believes the team can manage it and expects him to start next week against the Raiders. The Seahawks will have their bye in Week 11, so hopefully three straight weeks off will give him enough time to recover before Week 12’s game against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Drew Lock suffered an oblique injury today, and his status for Week 10 against the Raiders is “up in the air.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: Macdonald also said that he does not know whether Sam Darnold (quad/ribs) will be healthy enough to play. Lock has also been dealing with tendinitis in his throwing-arm elbow. If both Lock and Darnold are ruled out, it will be Jalen Milroe who leads the Seahawks’ offense against the Raiders next week. Milroe would warrant starting consideration in two-quarterback leagues thanks to his rushing abilities.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Seahawks declared QB Sam Darnold, WR Rashid Shaheed, T Charles Cross, G Quenton Nelson, LB Uchenna Nwosu, DT Brandon Pili, and DT Leonard Williams inactive for Week 9 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: Darnold was ruled out earlier in the week while Shaheed misses his second consecutive game with a knee injury. Drew Lock gets the start under center for the second time this season while veteran receiver Cooper Kupp could see a slight uptick in usage with Shaheed sidelined. Injury trouble along the offensive line could lead to a more ball-out-quick offensive game plan as the Seahawks look to keep pace in the NFC West.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Sam Darnold (quad) could “potentially” miss Week 10 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: Garafolo added that Darnold is dealing with a cracked rib, though it sounds like the quad issue is what’s preventing him from playing. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald called Darnold “week to week” on Wednesday. They get their bye in Week 11, so holding him out for one more game to get an extended break makes the most sense. Fantasy managers should plan on Darnold missing Week 10 in addition to today’s game against Arizona. Drew Lock will start today. As long as his elbow issue doesn’t flare up, he will be in line to start next week as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jackson-po.headline: Jackson Powers-Johnson (Achilles) will not play in Las Vegas’ Week 12 game against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jackson-po.analysis: The instant rule-out and talk of a potentially serious injury has us believing Powers-Johnson will hit IR ahead of Sunday Night Football. Caleb Rogers and Trey Zuhn have played in Powers-Johnson’s absence this year and one of them will likely start against the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jackson-po.headline: Raiders ruled out RG Jackson Powers-Johnson (groin) for Week 4 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jackson-po.analysis: The Raiders will be without their star right guard for this divisional showdown. It’s an unfortunate loss. The Chiefs’ defensive tackle group is talented. Hopefully, Powers-Johnson can return in time for the Raiders’ Week 5 game against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jackson-po.headline: Jackson Powers-Johnson (groin) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jackson-po.analysis: The Raiders’ stud right guard has now missed two practices in a row, putting him on the wrong side of questionable. The Raiders face a Chiefs defensive line led by DT Chris Jones this week. Playing without Powers-Johnson could be consequential.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jackson-po.headline: Jackson Powers-Johnson (groin) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jackson-po.analysis: Powers-Johnson was the only Raider who missed practice because of an injury. Former third-round pick Caleb Rogers filled in for JPJ on Sunday, though he was only needed for five snaps. Rogers would presumably draw the start if Powers-Johnson can’t go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jackson-po.headline: Raiders placed G Jackson Powers-Johnson (ankle) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jackson-po.analysis: It’s a blow to the Vegas offensive line. Powers-Johnson suffered his ankle injury in Week 10 against the Broncos and did not return to the game. Pro Football Focus has graded Powers-Johnson as the NFL’s 44th best pass blocking guard this season and the league’s 24th best run blocking guard. The Raiders have the fourth worst rushing success rate this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jackson-po.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Jackson Powers-Johnson’s ankle injury “could potentially end his season.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jackson-po.analysis: Powers-Johnson will land on injured reserve, but it sounds like he’ll be evaluated later in the season to see if he can return. Powers-Johnson has started every game at right guard for the Raiders this season, earning a PFF grade of 63.8 while being one of the few bright spots of an underwhelming group. Backup Alex Cappa replaced Powers-Johnson in Week 10’s loss and will likely take over as the starter for the foreseeable future.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jackson-po.headline: Raiders HC Pete Carroll said Jackson Powers-Johnson (ankle) will miss an extended period of time.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jackson-po.analysis: Powers-Johnson was carted off the field in Thursday night’s loss against the Broncos after having his ankle rolled up on. The second-year guard will now miss multiple weeks as a result of his injury and could be a candidate to land on injured reserve if the team believes he will miss four or more weeks. Veteran Alex Cappa took over in Powers-Johnson’s absence and will presumably be the starting right guard going forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jackson-po.headline: Jackson Powers-Johnson is questionable to return in Week 10 against the Raiders with an ankle injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jackson-po.analysis: Powers-Johnson got rolled up on a third-down sack, and after a quick look in the injury tent, the 22-year-old offensive lineman was carted off the field. Alex Cappa has taken Powers-Johnson’s spot at guard.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jackson-po.headline: Raiders DL Tyree Wilson (knee) will not play in Week 2 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jackson-po.analysis: Wilson is not yet a high-impact rotational player and losing valuable in-game repetitions will not help his development. Hopefully, he can return soon. Backup rookie G Jackson Powers-Johnson (illness) will be a game-time decision but fellow rookie LB Tommy Eichenberg (knee) will make his NFL debut.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jackson-po.headline: Raiders head coach Antonio Pierce confirmed QB Aidan O’Connell will not play in Friday’s preseason game against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jackson-po.analysis: Entering his second season, O’Connell will be the backup to Gardner Minshew heading into Week 1. With the quarterback pecking order now determined, Pierce is set to keep both guys on the bench without risk of further injury. It is an interesting approach as backup quarterbacks generally could use the extra reps, especially one entering his second season. However, this may indicate that O’Connell has a chance to start at some point in the season and the Raiders do not want to risk an injury to their viable “1b” quarterback. Carter Bradley and Nathan Peterman will split QB reps to finish the Raiders’ preseason. Pierce also added that rookie OL Jackson Powers-Johnson won’t play until the regular season as he was recently cleared from a stint on the PUP list due to a concussion.

https://www.nbcsports.com/raheim-sanders.headline: Raheim Sanders (hip) is questionable for Cleveland’s Week 12 game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/raheim-sanders.analysis: Todd Monken said he’s “hoping” to activate Sanders, who has only gotten in limited practices this week. He sounds truly questionable for Sunday Night Football. If active, Sanders will cut into Dylan Sampson’s backup workload a bit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/raheim-sanders.headline: Browns designated RB Raheim Sanders (hip) to return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/raheim-sanders.analysis: His 21-day window will open today. Sanders probably won’t come back to a real role unless there are injuries ahead of him, but perhaps he’ll cut into Dylan Sampson’s No. 2 role and make both of them unrosterable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/raheim-sanders.headline: Browns placed RB Raheim Sanders (hip) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/raheim-sanders.analysis: It’s unclear when he picked this injury up, but it does make the Audric Estime signing make some more sense. Sanders will miss at least four games. Assuming Quinshon Judkins (ankle) is good to go for Week 5, Jaleel McLaughlin and Estime will back him up.

https://www.nbcsports.com/raheim-sanders.headline: Browns head coach Todd Monken said Quinshon Judkins is considered day-to-day with an ankle injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/raheim-sanders.analysis: Monken was spotted in a walking boot after Sunday’s loss to the Jets, but Monken said his RB1 will have a chance to play in Week 6 against the Ravens. Judkins rushed 14 times for 44 yards last week and has a rushing line of 73-221-1 for the season, along with 18 receptions for 102 additional yards. Judkins’ practice status will be one to monitor throughout the week. If he’s not able to play, Raheim Sanders would likely handle the early-down work, with Jaleel McLaughlin mixing in as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/raheim-sanders.headline: Raheim Sanders rushed three times for 12 yards in the Browns’ Week 5 loss to the Jets, adding a one-yard reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/raheim-sanders.analysis: Sanders also lost a few snaps to Jaleel McLaughlin. 4-5 touches have been Sanders’ weekly norm, but that could change for Week 6 against the Ravens after Quinshon Judkins was spotted with his right foot in a boot following today’s contest. There have not been any indications Judkins is dealing with something serious, but it’s a situation worth monitoring ahead of Tuesday evening’s waiver wire run.

https://www.nbcsports.com/raheim-sanders.headline: Browns signed RB Jaleel McLaughlin to their active roster.
https://www.nbcsports.com/raheim-sanders.analysis: He gets the elevation after the Browns place Dylan Sampson on injured reserve. McLaughlin and Raheim Sanders will be behind Quinshon Judkins in Week 2. McLaughlin’s career shows him as a more reliable pure runner than Sanders, but we’re unsure of how the split behind Judkins will go from here.

https://www.nbcsports.com/raheim-sanders.headline: Raheim Sanders rushed one time for one yard in the Browns’ Week 1 loss to the Jaguars, adding 3 receptions for 25 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/raheim-sanders.analysis: Sanders entered the game after Dylan Sampson (knee) was ruled out. The 24-year-old had a couple explosive kickoff returns, including a 74-yard return in the second half. He caught three passes filling the Brown’s receiving back role and showcased some burst by taking those receptions for 25 total yards. Sanders is an intriguing handcuff to pick up off waivers, pending Sampson’s status heading into Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/raheim-sanders.headline: Browns RB Dylan Sampson (knee) is ruled out for Week 1 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/raheim-sanders.analysis: Sampson returned a kickoff and played on a third down play against the Jaguars before exiting in the first quarter. He left for the locker room with a knee injury and was promptly ruled out. Third-string running back Raheim Sanders will get more run with Sampson out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/raheim-sanders.headline: Raheim Sanders rushed five times for 26 yards in the Browns’ Week 18 win over the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/raheim-sanders.analysis: Sanders signed with the Chargers after going undrafted in April. He didn’t make their final roster, but the Browns scooped him up and gave him some short-yardage work in Week 1 with Quinshon Judkins unavailable. He scored a short touchdown and didn’t touch the ball again until Week 16, after Judkins went down with a season-ending injury. Sanders split work with fellow rookie Dylan Sampson over the final three weeks of the year. Judkins is locked in as the high-volume runner in Cleveland and Sampson can be penciled in for most of the work on passing downs in 2026. That doesn’t leave much room for Sanders, but he has made progress toward earning a roster spot next year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/raheim-sanders.headline: Raheim Sanders rushed eight times for 21 yards in the Browns’ Week 17 win over the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/raheim-sanders.analysis: Sanders drew the start in Sunday’s win over the Steelers, and handled six of his eight carries on the Browns’ first three possessions. His longest gain of the day came on a six-yard plunge on the first play of the game, and he also added a 10-yard reception in the fourth quarter. If Sanders finds himself in another split with Dylan Sampson next week, both backs will be hard to trust in Week 18 against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/rex-sunahara/0.headline: Browns signed LS Rex Sunahara to a four-year contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/rex-sunahara/0.analysis: Sunahara, 30 years young, has been the Browns’ snapper of balls that go longer than the league average since 2024. He’s now inked through his age-34 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.headline: Abdul Carter (calf/illness) is not on the Giants’ final injury report and will play in Week 12 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.analysis: Carter is also no longer listed with an ankle injury, which is a good sign. Giants LB Arvell Reese (back) is also cleared to face a Colts offense now led by Anthony Richardson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.headline: Abdul Carter (ankle/calf) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.analysis: Carter is firmly in the questionable camp for the Giants’ Week 12 game against the lowly Colts. Giants LB Arvell Reese (back) was limited at today’s practice. Hopefully, one or both of them are good to go this weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Abdul Carter (groin) is expected to play in Week 6 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.analysis: Carter got in one limited practice to close the week before being listed as questionable. That would normally make him a coin-flip at best to play today, head coach John Harbaugh was optimistic about Carter’s health early in the week. He is good to go, as is left tackle Andrew Thomas, who is dealing with a groin injury. He has played through the groin issue several times already and will do so again versus the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.headline: Andrew Thomas (groin) was seen working off to the side on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.analysis: Thomas, the Giants’ left tackle, RT Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) and EDGE Abdul Carter (calf) were all seen without jerseys, working on the side field with the training staff today. Expect to see all three listed as non-participants. Thomas has played through a couple of injuries this season, and seemingly has a good chance of suiting up in Week 6 against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.headline: Abdul Carter (calf) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.analysis: Giants coach John Harbaugh said Carter is doing well, so it doesn’t seem like he’s at much risk of missing Week 6. Rookie corner Colton Hood, on the other hand, is in concussion protocol and didn’t practice today. He will likely miss Week 6 while he works his way through the protocol.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.headline: Giants HC John Harbaugh said Abdul Carter’s ankle injury doesn’t appear to be too serious.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.analysis: Speaking after Monday’s minicamp, Harbaugh said Carter suffered a twisted ankle but downplayed any notion that it would be a serious injury. The Giants and their fans can breathe an early sigh of relief after the former No. 3 overall pick was seen limping off the field early in the first day of the team’s three-day minicamp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.headline: Giants beat writer Pat Leonard reports Abdul Carter suffered an apparent foot injury at Monday’s minicamp and could be seen limping to the sideline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.analysis: We’ll likely get an update on this soon, but it’s a concerning development for the second-year pass rusher who is hoping to build on a rookie season that included 43 tackles, four sacks, and seven TFLs. According to Leonard, Carter eventually made his way indoors and was seen leaving the field without his shoe. ESPN’s Jordan Raanan later reported that the “initial belief” is that Carter is okay, but we will provide an update when we receive one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.headline: Giants EDGE Abdul Carter (illness) is not on the injury report for Week 18 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.analysis: Carter returned to practice on Friday, logging a limited session. Giants DL Dexter Lawrence (illness) was also removed from the injury report, though he did not resume practicing. We tentatively expect both players to be on the field for Week 18, but projecting their snap counts is tough. The Giants and Cowboys have both been eliminated from playoff contention.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.headline: Giants EDGE Abdul Carter (illness) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.analysis: Carter’s absence is unsurprising. The coaching staff reportedly sent him and others home yesterday. The Athletic’s Dan Duggan noted DL Dexter Lawrence was also absent on Thursday. He believes Lawrence is “also in the illness category.” Both players have a chance to face the Cowboys this week, though the team notably kept TE Theo Johnson (illness) sidelined in Week 17, and he has not yet resumed practicing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.headline: Giants EDGE Abdul Carter (illness) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.analysis: Three Giants players “were sent home or not at practice as they deal with illnesses.” Carter is, unfortunately, among them. The Giants’ stud rookie has been playing very well as of late. An absence would make life far easier on the Cowboys this week. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely (groin) is not on the Giants’ final injury report for Week 12 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Likely injured his groin last Friday and caught one pass for 35 yards two days later. He was limited on Wednesday and Thursday before upgrading to full today, which is encouraging. Likely is a TE1 for Week 12 against the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely (groin) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Likely injured his groin during practice last week and caught just one pass for 35 yards on Sunday against the Jaguars. His early-week participation is a good sign for his overall health. He will be in the TE1 ranks this week against the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely caught 1-of-3 targets for 35 yards in the Giants’ Week 11 win against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Likely was invisible for most of the game and finished fourth in targets on the day. Along with most other New York pass catchers, Likely suffered from JJ McCarthy’s stunningly inefficient outing in which he was 15 percent below his expected completion rate and averaged a mere 4.6 yards per attempt. Better days are likely ahead for the Giants tight end, including in Week 12 against the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely (groin) is not on the Giants’ final injury report and will play in Week 11 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Likely sat out on Friday after practicing in full, injury-free, on Wednesday and Thursday. With six teams on bye and very few reliable tight end options in fantasy, Likely remains in the TE1 tier. Monitoring his status throughout the weekend will be worthwhile. Hopefully, we continue to get positive reports on his groin injury. Likely notably dealt with a groin injury back in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Giants head coach John Harbaugh said Isaiah Likely (undisclosed) is dealing with a “minor” injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Likely was noticeably absent from Friday’s practice, but Harbaugh said he expects his tight end to be okay. We assume that means he will be fine for Sunday’s game against the Jaguars, but we will need to wait to see where things stand when the team releases its final injury report on Friday. We should have a better sense of what he is dealing with soon, but in the event he can’t go, Theo Johnson would be the next man up to replace Likely.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely caught 9-of-11 targets for 127 yards and a touchdown in the Giants’ Week 10 loss to the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Likely as clearly the going-in game plan in a game expected to be heavily influenced by weather. The rain cleared in the first half but Likely remained the featured option through the air, likely influenced by heavy blitz rates and unrelenting pressure from the Washington defense. The 11-target game was the fifth time this season that the veteran tight end hit double-digit targets but the first time doing so with J.J. McCarthy under center. Likely remains a surefire TE1 ahead of a difficult matchup against the Jaguars in Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely caught 5-of-6 targets for 53 yards and a touchdown in the Giants’ Week 9 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Although it was another down day in the yardage department by his recent standards, Likely got the fantasy job done with his score and five receptions. It also wasn’t a bad outcome in a contest where J.J. McCarthy missed time with a hip injury and the Giants attempted only 27 throws vs. a reeling Eagles team. Likely’s touchdown was a five-yarder where he took advantage of mass defensive confusion at the goal line. It is unclear if McCarthy will be ready for Thursday’s short-week date with the Commanders, but Likely will remain a high-end QB1 even if Jameis Winston returns under center.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: The Athletic’s Dan Duggan reports Isaiah Likely (undisclosed) expressed confidence that he’ll be fine after the bye week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Likely was spotted limping at times during Week 7’s win over the Texans, which helps explain his subpar production. We’ll keep an eye on this one coming out of the bye, but we’re certainly not expecting anything serious here.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely caught 2-of-4 targets for 12 yards in New York’s Week 7 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: It was his first game with fewer than five targets all season. New York’s passing game simply targeted Houston outside the numbers and they ran the ball effectively enough that they didn’t need to feed Likely. He’ll be on the TE1 line in Week 9 against the Eagles once the Giants return from their bye week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: SNY TV’s Connor Hughes believes the Giants will stick with J.J. McCarthy as the starter “for the foreseeable future.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: According to Hughes, “this is the player they targeted and wanted” as their quarterback the minute Jaxson Dart (knee) got hurt. Hughes acknowledges that coach John Harbaugh could eventually bench McCarthy later in the year, but it will take more than a bad “game or two” for that to happen. In the meantime, the weekly fantasy football outlooks for Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely are more volatile than they were with Jameis Winston at the helm. Selling high could make sense. Hughes adds that McCarthy would have to play like a top-10 quarterback to make the coaching staff consider him for the starting role next season. That outcome seems highly unlikely.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.headline: Carlton Davis (knee) won’t play in New England’s Week 12 game against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.analysis: He didn’t practice at all this week and doesn’t seem especially close to playing at this point. Davis has not played since Week 9. The Patriots are having enough trouble struggling with the maximum number of IR-return slots that Drake Maye hasn’t been placed on IR either, so we won’t slag them for Davis not being there, but he doesn’t look close.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.headline: Carlton Davis (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.analysis: Davis has not played since Week 9, dealing with a knee injury. He stays sidelined coming out of the Patriots’ bye. Davis is trending in the wrong direction for Week 12 against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.headline: Carlton Davis (knee) will not play in Week 10 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.analysis: The Pats are traveling to Germany to take on the Lions. Davis was among several players who presumably didn’t make the trip overseas and were ruled out today. Davis has two pass breakups and 22 combined tackles across five appearances this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.headline: Carlton Davis (neck) is active for Week 8 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.analysis: The Patriots’ No. 2 perimeter cornerback makes his return from a multi-week neck injury for this divisional showdown. The Patriots declared CB Karon Prunty, S Elliott Davison, CB Channing Canada, QB Behren Morton, RB TreVeyon Henderson and WR A.J. Brown (knee/ankle) inactive for Week 8 against the Dolphins. Prunty and Canada have also missed multiple games, dealing with hamstring injuries. They are the Patriots’ primary backups on the perimeter. Both players practiced in full this week, so their absence is a little surprising.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.headline: Carlton Davis (neck) is questionable for New England’s Week 8 game against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.analysis: It’s a bit of a surprise questionable because Davis got in three full practice sessions this week. Still, he is coming off a long-term neck injury that has sidelined him most of the year so we understand the Patriots being cautious here. We’d consider Davis on the optimistic side of questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.headline: Carlton Davis (neck) is practicing in full for Week 8 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.analysis: Davis and both of the Patriots’ top perimeter backups, CB Channing Canada (hamstring) and CB Karon Prunty (hamstring) are practicing in full this week. This is very good news. The trio has been sidelined for some time, weakening the Patriots’ secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.headline: Patriots ruled out Carlton Davis (neck) for Week 7 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.analysis: The Patriots will also be without their top-two backup CBs, Karon Prunty (hamstring) and Channing Canada (hamstring). The Patriots listed S Kevin Byard (chest), S Craig Woodson (shoulder) and LB Christian Elliss (chest) as questionable. This is good news for the Bears’ passing attack.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.headline: Patriots CB Carlton Davis (neck) was limited in Tuesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.analysis: It was an upgrade from an estimated Monday DNP. Davis has missed Week 2, Week 3, Week 5 and Week 6 to the neck listing so far. Perhaps he’ll try to give it a go on Thursday night, but we’d be surprised if he did better than a questionable tag on Wednesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.headline: Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 6 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.analysis: Gonzalez has not played since Week 3, but he returns in time to cover Garrett Wilson in a divisional showdown. Gonzalez primarily lines up on the perimeter, but he has taken 15 combined snaps in the slot and in the box. He could take a few reps on the inside this week, but perimeter CB2 Carlton Davis (neck) is out, so Gonzalez could be asked to simply stay out wide.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.headline: Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez will not play in New England’s Week 5 game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.analysis: He has not practiced or played since Week 3. Nothing we’ve seen has suggested he’ll be a Saturday IR candidate, but it also wouldn’t necessarily be surprising if that happened. The Pats also ruled out fellow starting CB Carlton Davis (neck) for Week 5, leaving non-existent Raiders receivers with matchup upgrades. (Cody White is about to touch the end zone paint again.)

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-stoll.headline: Rams signed TE Jack Stoll off San Francisco’s practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-stoll.analysis: With both Davis Allen and Tyler Higbee week-to-week, the Rams have brought in reinforcements behind Colby Parkinson and Max Klare. There’s no need to project Stoll to real fantasy work, but he could find some playing time if they continue to play 13-personnel sets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-stoll.headline: 49ers signed TE Jack Stoll to their practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-stoll.analysis: With Jake Tonges dealing with an MCL injury, the 49ers added Stoll to the practice squad for depth. Stoll spent last season with the Saints, catching six passes for 46 yards in 15 games. He initially signed with the Eagles as an undrafted free agent in 2021 and has not surpassed 200 yards receiving in a single season over the course of his career. Stoll’s specialty is blocking and we could certainly see him contribute for the 49ers’ run game if Tonges is out for a while and George Kittle still working his way back to a full workload.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-stoll.headline: Browns released TE Jack Stoll.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-stoll.analysis: The Browns also released CB Tre Avery, CB Tyler Hall and OT Tyre Phillips. The Browns waived TE Drew Biber, OT Jeremiah Byers, P Nik Constantinou, S Christopher Edmonds, CB Nate Evans, DT Coziah Izzard, DT Patrick Jenkins, CB Jeremiah McClendon, T Izavion Miller, DE Jamil Muhammad, WR Ben Patterson and TE Jermaine Terry II.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-stoll.headline: Browns agreed to terms with TE Jack Stoll, formerly of the Saints, on a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-stoll.analysis: You better not wait on a blocking tight end in free agency, folks, the new meta is here. Stoll, 28, played 15 games for the Saints last year and was targeted 11 times in 209 snaps. He’s here to forge holes, not catch balls.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-stoll.headline: Saints signed TE Jack Stoll to a one-year, $1.362 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-stoll.analysis: After coming into the league with the Eagles, Stoll was a member of the Dolphins’ practice squad during the 2024 season but did not appear in a game. He’ll likely compete for a depth role behind Juwan Johnson, Foster Moreau, and (possibly?) Taysom Hill in New Orleans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-stoll.headline: Dolphins declared QB Tyler Huntley, LB Anthony Walker, CB Ethan Bonner, CB Kendall Fuller, TE Jack Stoll and WR Dee Eskridge inactive for Week 13 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-stoll.analysis: Huntley was activated off injured reserve Thursday, but he’ll be the emergency quarterback for Thursday’s bout against Green Bay. Skylar Thompson will be the backup for Tua Tagovailoa versus the Packers instead.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-stoll.headline: Grant Calcaterra caught 3-of-3 targets for 58 yards in the Eagles’ Week 8 win over the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-stoll.analysis: Calcaterra continued to fill in for the injured Dallas Goedert (hamstring) and caught a few deep targets on the day. He was the No. 3 pass-catching option, with a 28-yard catch his longest of the game. Jack Stoll also saw increased snaps with Goedert out, catching his only target for six targets, though he was primarily in for blocking. If Goedert continues to miss time, Calcaterra has low-end TE2 fantasy viability.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-stoll.headline: Giants released TE Jack Stoll.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-stoll.analysis: Stoll missed time during training camp with a brain injury and never made an impact upon his return, according to New York beat writers. The former Eagles tight end is likely to land with another team before Week 1. The Giants tight end depth chart includes Daniel Bellinger, Theo Johnson, and Lawrence Cager.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-stoll.headline: Giants signed TE Jack Stoll, formerly of the Eagles, to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-stoll.analysis: A 2021 UDFA, Stoll has spent his entire three-year career in Philly. Although he has just 20 career catches, Stoll could be part of the Giants’ pass-catching calculus if Darren Waller goes through with retirement. Already 26 years old, Stoll isn’t terribly projectable up the seam.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-stoll.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Dallas Goedert (arm) is expected to undergo surgery and will likely miss multiple weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-stoll.analysis: How many weeks Goedert misses will be determined after his MRI and surgery, but the veteran tight end will miss at least a few games. The veteran tight end has caught 38 passes for 410 yards and two touchdowns this season, and is a key piece of the Eagles’ offensive attack both on the air and on the ground. Jack Stoll, a UDFA from the 2021 draft class, is listed behind Goedert on the team’s unofficial depth chart, and played the second-most snaps among Eagles tight ends in Week 9. He would be the early favorite to start after the Week 10 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Treylon Burks (foot) is not on Washington’s final Week 12 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: A rough Cardinals defense could get Burks into the deep league conversation, but he’s had just six targets in two games since returning from the bye week. If he doesn’t do something this week, Brandon Aiyuk might be knocking on the door of his starting spot come Week 13.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Treylon Burks (foot) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: Burks continues to play through his foot injury, albeit mostly ineffectively. He is a boom-bust downfield wide receiver who faces a tremendously soft Cardinals pass defense this week. Burks does not need to be in 12-team lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Treylon Burks caught 2-of-3 targets for 30 yards in the Commanders’ Week 11 win over the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: While Burks did little in the box score, he drew a defensive pass interference call in the end zone that set up the team’s only touchdown of the game on a Jacory Croskey-Merritt touchdown run on the following play. His three targets finished tied for fourth on the team behind Antonio Williams’ 11, Stefon Diggs’ six, and Chig Okonkwo’s five, leaving Burks in shaky fantasy territory as the team enters the final two months of play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Treylon Burks (foot) was removed from the injury report Saturday and will play in Week 11 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: Burks surprisingly went from a full session Thursday and a no-show Friday, prompting uncertainty regarding his expected availability for Monday Night Football against the Bengals. He quickly put those worries to rest with a full practice Saturday and was removed from the injury report. Expect Burks to continue operating in a featured role on the perimeter in the absence of Terry McLaurin.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Treylon Burks (foot) did not practice on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: This could just be a rest day. Burks played through the injury last week, logging just one limited session, and he was clearly limited by the injury in-game. He still has a chance to play in this week’s Monday Night Football game against the Bengals, but he would be a terribly volatile FLEX if so.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Treylon Burks (foot) is practicing in full ahead of Washington’s Week 11 game with the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: Burks missed Week 9 and played through this injury in Week 10, and it seems like the extra rest after Thursday Night Football has done him some good. If he can overtake Chig Okonkwo as the No. 2 target in Washington’s passing game down the stretch, perhaps there’s some reasonable fantasy value to be had.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Treylon Burks caught 2-of-3 targets for 27 yards in the Commanders’ Week 10 win over the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: Burks fought through clear discomfort after coming into the game listed questionable following a Wednesday downgrade on the practice report, catching two early passes for 27 yards before succumbing to the inside-funnel nature of the New York defense. Quarterback Jayden Daniels directed 22 of his 33 pass attempts to the trio of Stefon Diggs, Chig Okonkwo, and Ben Sinnott over the middle of the field. Burks’ situation is unlikely to improve in Week 11 with lockdown perimeter corner DJ Turner on deck.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Treylon Burks (foot) is not on the final injury report and will play in Week 10 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: Burks got in a limited session on Tuesday, but was held out of practice on Monday and Wednesday. It is entirely possible that the Commanders are just exercising caution and Burks will play his normal allotment of snaps, but this sure seems like a scenario where he could end up being a decoy. Burks should be viewed as a boom-bust FLEX with a very low floor.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said he expected Treylon Burks (foot) to be active for Week 10 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: Burks, according to Quinn, did not practice Wednesday in preparation for Thursday night’s game against the Giants. He missed Week 9 against the Rams with a foot injury. The Commanders’ best downfield threat with Terry McLaurin sidelined, Burks profiles as a high-variance WR4 option this week. The Giants have faced deep passes at the league’s 16th highest rate this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Treylon Burks (foot) was limited in Tuesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: It’s an upgrade from an estimated DNP on Monday. Dan Quinn has previously said that he’s optimistic Burks will play, but it’s likely that he’ll hit the questionable line tomorrow barring a full practice.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (ankle) is not on the Jaguars’ final injury report and will play in Week 12 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Meyers will expectedly function as the Jaguars’ No. 1 wide receiver with Parker Washington (shoulder) sidelined and considered week-to-week. Meyers accordingly vaults into the WR2/3 range and could deliver a big stat line against a soft Titans defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (ankle) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Meyers has played through this injury for weeks now. We expect him to do the same against the Titans on Sunday. Parker Washington (shoulder) suffered an injury today. If Washington is inactive, Meyers would slide into the No. 1 wide receiver role. He should be added in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (ankle) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Meyers has been dealing with this ankle issue for weeks now, but it has not impacted his game-day availability. Meyers is FLEX-viable against a soft Titans pass defense in Week 12.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers caught 4-of-10 targets for 84 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 11 loss against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Meyers was second on the team in targets and receiving yards, trailing Parker Washington’s eight catches for 103 yards. Meyers’ 26-yard grab was the biggest play of the day for the Jaguars, who were forced into a pass-heavy chase script in the second half — a rarity for Jacksonville. Meyers will be a passable WR3 play in Week 12 against the Titans. He had 34 yards on three catches against the Titans in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (ankle) is not on Jacksonville’s final Week 11 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Meyers got in three limited sessions and will continue to play through this ailment. The Jaguars haven’t been tested enough to get him out of the WR4 ranks for the last few weeks, but if the Giants come to play on offense on Sunday, perhaps that will change.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (ankle) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Meyers has been rolling through this ankle issue the last few weeks and the fact that he remains limited shouldn’t be considered worrisome. He’ll be a fringe WR3 with six teams on bye in Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Meyers has been playing through the ankle issue for a few weeks. We expect the same for Week 11, though he hasn’t been a strong fantasy option at any point this year, healthy or not. He will remain in the WR4 ranks when the Jags take on the Giants on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers caught 3-of-6 targets for 34 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 10 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Week 10 will be one for Meyers to forget. He dropped a deep shot from Trevor Lawrence on a trick play. Lawrence, admittedly, underthrew the ball, forcing Meyers to turn around and fight through contact at the catch point. Meyers dropped another touchdown later in the game that was more than catchable. Meyers hasn’t scored since Week 3 and has caught more than five passes in two games this year. He’s struggling to provide even WR4 value ahead of the Jags’ Week 11 matchup with the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (ankle) is not on Jacksonville’s final Week 10 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Meyers will be in line for a FLEX-worthy workload against the Titans. The good news is that the over/under has climbed to 46.5 after last week’s date with Joey Fagnano, leaving Meyers as a more viable touchdown threat in Week 10 than he was in a limited passing workload against the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (ankle) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Meyers was limited at today’s practice. He is on track to play through the injury this week after doing so successfully last week, along with a hamstring injury. The Jaguars’ dominance has rendered Meyers somewhat of a touchdown-reliant FLEX starter, though this is a soft matchup against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman (groin) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 12 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: You know what you’re getting into if you start Bateman, but he did manage a touchdown grab against the Panthers last week and the Ravens have generally pumped up their passing usage since Jacoby Brissett landed in Baltimore. He’s probably a bit below the FLEX line in standard leagues, but it wouldn’t shock us if he landed in that area this week against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman (groin) was a full participant for Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: Bateman got a limited practice tag Wednesday, but appears to be just fine for the Week 12 matchup against the Texans. He’s still off the fantasy radar in the majority of formats for that contest.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman (groin) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: Bateman was hobbled after taking a hard hit in the Ravens’ Week 11 loss to the Panthers. He pops up on the injury report with a groin issue to start the week, though he was still limited in practice. Bateman is hardly fantasy relevant at this point, but an absence would indicate more Ja’Kobi Lane targets for Week 12 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman caught 2-of-6 targets for 67 yards and a touchdown in the Ravens’ Week 11 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: Bateman’s touchdown catch came on a play from the wildcat that started with Derrick Henry receiving the snap. While Henry handed the ball off to Justice Hill, who then pitched to Jacoby Brissett, Bateman streaked down the field, leaving every member of the Panthers’ secondary in the dust as they attempted to dissect the trick play called by Ravens OC Declan Doyle. Brissett delivered a slightly underthrown ball to Bateman, but it proved inconsequential given the distance between Bateman and the nearest defender. The 26-year-old receiver hauled in the pass without any trouble and made his way into the end zone to give the Ravens an early 9-0 lead. Bateman would only catch one more pass the rest of the day, but his six targets now give him 11 in his two games with Brissett under center. While it’s hard to imagine Bateman having any reliable fantasy value this season, he could be worth a desperation dart throw in deeper leagues in Week 12 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman caught 3-of-5 targets for 42 yards in the Ravens’ Week 10 loss to the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: Bateman saw his route structure altered with the change at quarterback, running a high percentage of his routes over the middle of the field. He was able to run free in the intermediate areas against the heavy zone coverage rates of the Chargers for much of the game, with Brissett instead targeting tight end Mark Andrews and alpha wide receiver Zay Flowers at elevated rates. Bateman remains a shaky Flex play ahead of a Week 11 meeting with the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman (calf) practiced in full on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: Bateman is firmly on track to play in the Ravens’ Monday Night Football game against the Chargers. Bateman will provide new QB Jacoby Brissett with a downfield option, but the veteran wide receiver is almost entirely reliant in ripping off one or two big plays, which has proven to be a difficult proposition for him on a weekly basis.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman (calf) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: The Ravens face the Chargers in Week 10’s Monday Night Football game, theoretically giving Bateman decent odds of suiting up. He does not need to be in starting lineups as a touchdown-dependent FLEX, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 7 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: He practiced in full twice on Thursday and Friday. With Ja’Kobi Lane eating into his targets and the Bengals ever-vulnerable through the air by tight ends, Bateman is probably only a deep-league play in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: Bateman has been playing through this shoulder injury for a while, though he was forced to leave early last week. Bateman should now be expected to play, but he is only a boom-bust FLEX option with Ja’Kobi Lane now back in the lineup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: Bateman left the Ravens’ Week 6 game against the Browns and did not return, though head coach Jesse Minter told reporters on Monday that he was going to be fine. Expect the team to manage his reps in practice this week with an eye on getting him ready for Sunday. Bateman has made a handful of splash plays this year, but his production is low-volume and high-variance. He will be a low-end FLEX option for Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Jaguars ruled out Bhayshul Tuten (foot/ankle) for Week 12 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: Chris Rodriguez should be added wherever he is available. Tuten will finally take a week off after playing through foot and ankle injuries for multiple weeks. He reportedly aggravated the issues in Week 11 against the Giants. Hopefully, Tuten will return for the Jaguars’ expectedly fantasy-friendly game against the Bears in Week 13.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said he’s “not sure yet” if Bhayshul Tuten (foot/ankle) will play in Week 12 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: Fantasy managers don’t need to panic just yet. The Jaguars have not taken the field for their Friday practice, and Coen said the team will assess how he looks on Friday before making any further decisions on his availability. Tuten has not practiced in either of the first two practices of the week, so a limited practice would be a slight upgrade for him heading into the weekend. We will check back in with a final update on his availability when the team announces it, but backup Chris Rodriguez could be in line for a busy week if Tuten were to be sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Bhayshul Tuten (foot/ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: Tuten aggravates his ankle and foot issues in Week 11 against the Giants. He has been playing through the ailments for multiple weeks, and still has a chance to face the Titans this week. He is an RB1 if active. Chris Rodriguez (hand) should be rostered just in case.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: The Florida Times-Union’s Demetrius Harvey reports Bhayshul Tuten (ankle) was not seen at practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: Tuten was banged up last week against the Giants and clearly playing through considerable discomfort. That he hasn’t practiced much over the past couple weeks means Tuten could sit out a couple days of practice this week and still suit up for Week 12 against the Titans. The Jaguars would do well to rest their lead back in a game they should win comfortably. Chris Rodriguez, who bests Tuten in rushing success rate, rush yards over expected per attempt, and EPA per rush, would be in line for a big workload if Tuten is held out in Week 12. Tuten was officially listed as a non-participant on Wednesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Jaguars coach Liam Coen said Bhayshul Tuten (ankle) re-aggravated his injury against the Giants and it will be “business as usual” with him in practice this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: In other words, look for a lot of DNPs and limited sessions that don’t really matter, then a Friday decision at the end of the week. The Jaguars certainly could decide they have the luxury of resting Tuten against the Titans in Week 12. Chris Rodriguez could be either a viable RB2 or a useless FLEX play by Friday, depending on how this situation shakes out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Bhayshul Tuten had ten rushes for 33 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 11 loss against the Giants, adding three catches for 20 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: Tuten came into the game with ankle and knee injuries and was hobbled throughout. He was spotted on the stationary bike a couple times in the first half and limped to the sideline a few times in the third quarter, including once with trainers after staying down for a few beats. Clearly nowhere close to 100 percent healthy, Tuten ceded five backfield touches to Chris Rodriguez, who was much more efficient with his opportunities (averaging seven yards per carry). The Jaguars could consider resting their lead back in Week 12 against the Titans. If he plays, Tuten will be a top-15 option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Bhayshul Tuten exited the field in Week 11 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: Tuten was dinged up on the first play of the game and was later seen riding the exercise bike on the sideline. He came into the game battling ankle and knee issues that limited him in practice this week. He may have aggravated the injuries. Chris Rodriguez would take over as the team’s lead back if Tuten misses time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) is not on Jacksonville’s final Week 11 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: Tuten got in a limited session on Wednesday, a DNP on Thursday while working with trainers, and appeared to do much the same on Friday before getting an official “limited” designation. Clearly gutting his way through the injury at this point, Tuten will remain a high-end RB2 against the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle) was seen practicing on the side field on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: This will presumably result in a DNP for Tuten this week, but we’ll see what the team announces when it releases its final injury report. According to Jaguars beat writer Ryan O’Halloran, Tuten was on the field with his helmet to stretch with teammates during warmups but then went to the side field. If he is listed as a DNP, it would be the second straight day Tuten failed to get on the practice field, but he could still receive a questionable designation entering the weekend. We will check back in with a final status update once the team announces it in a few hours.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: He was spotted on the sideline with trainers, and he has played through this injury each of the last two weeks. That makes us optimistic that a rug pull won’t be forthcoming on Friday. Still, the Friday practice participation line has yet to be written and it is a negative trend after Wednesday’s limited session.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: Zay Flowers (ankle) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 12 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: He can be started as a low-end WR1 against a Texans outfit that has given up plenty of passing yards this year. Flowers has been a fixture on the injury report this year but hasn’t missed a game since Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: Zay Flowers (ankle) was a full participant during Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Flowers was limited Wednesday but was upgraded to a full-go a day later. He’ll be a WR2 for the showdown against the Texans in Week 12.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: Zay Flowers (ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Flowers dealt with ankle issues earlier this season and now pops up on the injury report with a limited designation due to the ankle. He is still trending to play in Week 12, where he will operate as the Ravens’ WR1 for Jacoby Brissett against the Texans. Barring setbacks, the ankle should not limit Flowers too much as he sits in the fantasy WR2 rankings this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: Zay Flowers caught 8-of-11 targets for 97 yards in the Ravens’ Week 11 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: In two games with Jacoby Brissett, Flowers has caught 14-of-18 targets for 171 scoreless yards. This is great news for fantasy managers, who saw Flowers’ fantasy value in the tank when the duo of Tyler Huntley and Joe Fagnano led him to just six yards over a two-week stretch. Brissett’s arrival has been good news for Flowers, who ripped off two gains of 20-plus yards on the afternoon and led the Ravens in both targets and receiving yards. He will be a high-end WR2 next week against a Texans secondary that has proven vulnerable this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: Zay Flowers caught 6-of-7 targets for 74 yards in the Ravens’ Week 10 loss to the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Flowers carried only two receptions on two targets into the fourth quarter as the team struggled to move the football consistently, catching fire in the final frame before losing a costly fumble on the team’s penultimate possession with under three minutes remaining in a three-point game. Even so, it was a solid rebound effort after Flowers had struggled mightily with poor quarterback play the previous weeks, with veteran Jacoby Brissett providing enough stability for Flowers to remain an upside WR2 ahead of a Week 11 meeting with the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: Zay Flowers caught 3-of-6 targets for six yards in the Ravens’ Week 9 loss to the Jaguars, adding 17 yards on three carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Offensive coordinator Declan Doyle did what he could to overcome undrafted free agent rookie Joe Fagnano under center, routinely putting Flowers in Motion across the formation to generate some level of misdirection for an offense with zero ability to attack downfield. That included three rush attempts and a completion thrown by running back Derrick Henry, but it wasn’t enough to salvage a usable fantasy week for the electric receiver. Fantasy managers can rest easy knowing help is on the way in the form of veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett, who was signed earlier in the week and will likely make his team debut when the Ravens take on the Chargers in Week 10. Flowers will return to upside WR2 range with the change at quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: Zay Flowers caught 0-of-5 targets in the Ravens’ Week 8 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Lamar Jackson exited after one play due to a thumb injury. Midway through the second quarter, backup Tyler Huntley left the game with a toe injury, forcing Flowers into a nightmare situation with rookie UDFA Joe Fagnano under center. Flowers saw four of his five targets come from Fagnano but was unable to convert any of them into catches, even if they were within his range to do so. With the Ravens now set to face the Jaguars on a short week, and Fagnano possibly set to make his first career start, Flowers needs to be adjusted down to WR3 rankings. With a full week to install a game plan with Fagnano, it’s fair to assume he’ll offer more than the donut we saw here today, but the Ravens’ offense, which was already struggling with Huntley under center, is unlikely to fare any better with Fagnano.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: Zay Flowers caught 8-of-11 targets for 137 yards and one touchdown in the Ravens’ Week 7 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Flowers’ biggest play of the day came on the Ravens’ opening drive. The star receiver turned a screen pass on third-and-nine upfield for a 48-yard touchdown to give the Ravens an early lead on what would be their only touchdown drive of the day. Despite another low-scoring day for the Ravens’ offense, Flowers continues to be one of the most profitable wide receivers in fantasy. He’s averaged over 10 targets per game in three starts by Tyler Huntley and has caught six or more passes in his last four games. With Lamar Jackson (ankle) expected back for Week 8’s game against the Bills, things are looking up for Flowers and the Ravens’ offense as a whole. The good news for Flowers’ managers, however, is that he’s a must-start regardless of who is under center.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: Zay Flowers caught 6-of-11 targets for 66 yards in the Ravens’ Week 6 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Flowers has yet to find the end zone in back-to-back games with Tyler Huntley under center, but the 10 targets per game he has averaged over that span is still encouraging. Flowers led the Ravens in targets by a wide margin in this week’s loss, with his biggest play coming on a 31-yard reception in the third quarter. Scoring opportunities were scarce in this one, as the Ravens managed just 10 points on their first two drives and were shut out for the rest of the game. Flowers will be in the WR1 conversation next week against the Bengals if Lamar Jackson (ankle) makes the start, but would be more of a WR2 if Huntley gets the nod for a third straight week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: Zay Flowers (toe) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Perhaps feeling a bit wistful after spending a little of every week of the season on the injury report, Flowers got re-added Thursday with a limited session. He was limited again on Friday but is expected to play. There’s no further word on how serious this toe injury was, but he’s doing enough on the field in his limited time so far this year that nobody is seriously benching Flowers anyway.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.headline: Derrick Henry (concussion) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 12 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.analysis: He’ll get his normal workload, though he’s playing like more of a low-end RB1 or high-end RB2 since the Jacoby Brissett takeover, against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.headline: Derrick Henry (concussion) was listed as a full participant for Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.analysis: It’s excellent news for fantasy managers and for Henry, as he’s exited the concussion protocol. The 32-year-old should be ready to go for Week 12 against the Texans, assuming there are no setbacks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.headline: Ravens coach Jesse Minter said that Derrick Henry “had a couple of small symptoms” and is now in the NFL’s concussion protocol.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.analysis: Minter adds that he expects Henry to play in Week 12 against the Texans. On Sunday, it was reported that Henry had cleared the concussion protocol after the Ravens’ Week 11 loss to the Panthers. Re-entering the concussion protocol mid-week seems like a bad sign. Justice Hill has played well in recent weeks and would presumably start in Henry’s stead if the burly back is unable to play. Hill is backed up by Rasheen Ali and rookie Adam Randall, the latter of whom could be worth adding in deep leagues. Henry was limited at practice today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.headline: The Baltimore Banner’s Giana Han reports Derrick Henry cleared concussion protocol after Week 11’s loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.analysis: Henry didn’t return to the field after exiting in the fourth quarter to be evaluated for a concussion, but it was reportedly shortly after that he cleared the league’s concussion protocol. Henry rushed 13 times for 94 yards and a touchdown in Sunday’s loss while catching another four passes for 17 yards. Barring any setback, we would expect him to be good to go for Week 12’s game against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.headline: Derrick Henry rushed 13 times for 94 yards and a touchdown in the Ravens’ Week 11 loss to the Panthers, adding four receptions for 17 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.analysis: Henry made the most of a plus matchup against a porous Panthers rush defense. The Big Dog’s 94 rushing yards were his most in any game since Week 5 against the Falcons, and he found the end zone on a 15-yard rushing touchdown in the fourth quarter to put the Ravens up 33-32. Unfortunately, Henry landed hard on his head on the play and had to be taken to the locker room to be evaluated for a concussion. While he didn’t return to the field, it was reported after the game that he cleared concussion protocol, meaning he should be in good shape to take on the Texans in Week 12. He will remain in the mix as a fringe RB1/RB2 for next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.headline: Derrick Henry (concussion) was seen heading into the locker room in the Ravens’ Week 11 game against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.analysis: After a brief stint in the blue medical tent, Henry exited for the locker room. It was announced shortly after that he was being evaluated for a concussion after landing hard on his head on a 15-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter. We will check back in when we receive official word on his status.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.headline: Derrick Henry exited in the fourth quarter to be evaluated in the blue medical tent in Week 11’s game against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.analysis: Henry appeared to land hard on the back of his head while diving into the end zone for a 15-yard touchdown. He remained down for a moment before being helped up by teammates, but was immediately ushered into the tent for what we assume is a concussion evaluation. Henry has rushed 13 times for 94 yards and one touchdown on the day.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.headline: Derrick Henry rushed 10 times for 10 yards and two touchdowns in the Ravens’ Week 10 loss to the Chargers, adding 10 yards on five receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.analysis: It was the fifth straight game in which Henry was held to 58 yards on the ground or fewer, all five of which were Baltimore losses. Henry salvaged an otherwise poor showing with two rushing scores and a season-high five receptions, marking his 35th career game with multiple touchdowns in the loss. Now playing with Jacoby Brissett under center, Henry has fallen to a middling RB2 in fantasy circles, where he will remain ahead of a more enticing matchup against the Panthers in Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Ravens aren’t expected to trade RB Derrick Henry.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.analysis: Citing league sources, Schefter says the Ravens recently informed Henry that they have no intention of trading him. While speculation about a trade is understandable given Baltimore’s injuries at the quarterback position, the Ravens are said to have never even considered it, according to Schefter. With the newly acquired Jacoby Brissett likely to be under center in Week 10 against the Chargers, Henry will be in the RB1 mix.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.headline: Derrick Henry rushed 17 times for 57 yards in the Ravens’ Week 9 loss to the Jaguars.
