https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.analysis: Offensive coordinator Declan Doyle did everything in his power to overcome an undrafted free agent rookie quarterback in his first professional start, going so far as to call numerous direct snaps to Henry and a Henry pass attempt, but it ultimately proved futile. Things appeared to be trending in the right direction as the Ravens played the Jaguars to a tightly contested game through the first 29 minutes before Parker Washington broke the game open with a 50-yard touchdown in the final minute before the break. Things got nasty for Henry after the half as he managed only two additional yards after bruising his way to 55 first half yards. Henry will return to RB1 status in fantasy circles in Week 10 when the Ravens take on the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.headline: Danielle Hunter (hamstring) will not play in Houston’s Week 12 game against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.analysis: Hunter didn’t practice at any point this week. The hamstring injury has been described as short-term, but this is the third straight week he’ll miss with it. Perhaps he’ll have a chance to get back for Week 13.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.headline: Danielle Hunter (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.analysis: Hunter is dealing with a hamstring strain, missing the past two games for the Texans. He starts out this week not practicing and will need to practice in some capacity to have a shot at returning in Week 12 against the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.headline: NBC Houston’s Aaron Wilson reports Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) is dealing with a short-term strain.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.analysis: Danielle Hunter, too, is dealing with one of these. It seems like after the lengthy layoff following Thursday night’s win over the Colts, the Texans could be in line to get both players back for Week 12’s game against the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.headline: Texans ruled out Danielle Hunter (hamstring) for Week 11 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.analysis: Hunter will now miss his second game due to a hamstring injury. He is replaced in the lineup by veteran pass rusher Jadaveon Clowney. Fortunately, Will Anderson returned from his ankle injury last week. Kamari Lassiter (wrist) is expected to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.headline: Danielle Hunter (hamstring) will not play in Houston’s Week 10 game against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.analysis: Hunter popped up on the report with this injury on Thursday as limited and wound up ruled out after a DNP on Friday. Rough scenes for the $40 million-a-year edge rusher. This will be the first game he has missed since the 2021 season. Houston’s pass rush looks tenuous against the Browns with Will Anderson Jr. also on the questionable line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.headline: Texans signed EDGE Danielle Hunter to a one-year, $40.1 million contract extension through 2027.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.analysis: The two sides did the same thing last March via a $35.6 million deal. Hunter’s new one-year extension includes a $30.7 million signing bonus. Per PFF, Hunter totaled 83 quarterback pressures and 16 sacks last season. Both figures rank in the top five in the NFL.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.headline: Texans signed EDGE Danielle Hunter to a one-year, $35.6 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.analysis: NFL Network’s Tom Pelissero reports Hunter is now the NFL’s second-highest paid defensive end and will make $32 million this season, a $12.5 million bump from his previous contract. His deal becomes a two-year, $55.1 million agreement with $54.1 million guaranteed. Hunter initially signed a two-year deal with the Texans last offseason and now gets one more season in Houston with a pay bump after tallying 12 sacks and a Pro Bowl in 2024. With Will Anderson opposite Hunter, the Texans keep a menacing pass rush through 2026. This sets another price point in an expensive edge market with pass rushers like Trey Hendrickson and Micah Parsons next to cash in.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.headline: Texans agreed to terms with EDGE Danielle Hunter, formerly of the Vikings, on a two-year, $49 million deal.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.analysis: The Texans essentially swap edge rushers with the Vikings, adding the veteran Hunter after reportedly losing Jonathan Greenard to Minnesota. One of the top edge rushers on the market, Hunter totaled 16.5 sacks for the Vikings in 2023. The former third round pick will spend his first career snaps outside of Minnesota in 2024, lining up opposite of Defensive Rookie of the Year Will Anderson. It’s a reported two-year deal worth $49 million with a max value of $51 million.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.headline: ESPN’s Dan Graziano reports the Vikings “made an effort” to re-sign EDGE Danielle Hunter earlier this offseason.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.analysis: This doesn’t mean a deal with Hunter won’t get done before free agency opens up, but with the team also attempting to re-sign Kirk Cousins and extend Justin Jefferson, it’s possible Hunter at least makes it to the open market. Jeremy Fowler added that teams are expecting Hunter to seek a deal that pays “well north of $20 million per year,” which would make him amongst the highest paid EDGE rushers i the league. Hunter tallied a career-high 16.5 sacks with the Vikings last season and has totaled 87.5 sacks through his first eight seasons in the league. Hunter will be 29 at the start of next season, and should have no trouble fetching a lucrative deal should he and the Vikings not come to terms on a contract in the coming weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Vikings are “receiving calls” about EDGE Danielle Hunter.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/danielle-h.analysis: Hunter has been the subject of trade rumors for years, but the Vikings have always worked things out with their star pass-rusher. That includes giving him a one-year, $20 million contract that features a no-tag clause this offseason. Hunter leads the NFL with eight sacks but his team sits at 2-4. With Minnesota’s season circling the drain, it would be smart for them to get something for Hunter instead of holding onto him for a lost season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kayshon-bo.headline: Kayshon Boutte (hip) will not play in Houston’s Week 12 game against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kayshon-bo.analysis: Boutte did not practice at any point this week and has essentially become a boom-bust FLEX threat at best on a limited snap count. He is likely questionable for Week 13 and can be dropped in shallow leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kayshon-bo.headline: Kayshon Boutte (hip) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kayshon-bo.analysis: Boutte popped up on the injury report with a hip issue and did not practice Wednesday. With Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) potentially returning this week, Boutte does not need to be on the fantasy radar for Week 12 against the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kayshon-bo.headline: Kayshon Boutte caught both targets for 40 yards and a touchdown in the Texans’ Week 11 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kayshon-bo.analysis: Boutte’s two targets were a product of minimal pass volume in a game the Texans were able to control with their defense. He made the most of the modest volume by coming down with a touchdown in the second quarter on a dime delivered by quarterback C.J. Stroud to the middle of the end zone from 24 yards out, catching the ball with the defender draped around his midsection. Boutte remains a shaky fantasy bet as nothing more than the third option through the air, with the team expecting to get back newcomer Marvin Harrison Jr. from a hamstring injury in short order. That could come as early as Week 12 considering the Texans now get a long week of preparation ahead of a meeting with the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kayshon-bo.headline: Xavier Hutchinson caught 4-of-5 targets for 65 yards in Houston’s Week 5 win over the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kayshon-bo.analysis: He led the team in receiving and didn’t have any contested drops today, so that’s a step up from where he’s been most of the year. Still, he played just 27-of-65 snaps. Kayshon Boutte (39-of-65) would be our main target as Houston’s third receiver if we thought the offense was good enough to warrant that kind of respect; they aren’t.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kayshon-bo.headline: Kayshon Boutte caught 3-of-4 targets for 36 yards in Houston’s Week 4 loss to the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kayshon-bo.analysis: He managed to get his finger underneath a sideline ball for a 21-yarder, and the replay booth upheld the ruling of catch on the field. He also managed fewer targets than Xavier Hutchinson (five), as well as 10 fewer yards, despite Hutchinson playing 16 snaps to Boutte’s 32. The Nick Caley WR platoon will continue until morale improves, making nobody much of a FLEX play against the Titans in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kayshon-bo.headline: Kayshon Boutte caught 2-of-2 targets for 21 yards in Houston’s Week 3 loss to the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kayshon-bo.analysis: Boutte played 35-of-52 snaps, and if that sounds low, it actually lead the team in Nick Caley’s absolutely bizarre WR platoon situation where it seems like he is trying to find someone who he trusts. Boutte looks the best of the bunch, but we can’t recommend trying to eat these non-existent fantasy points. Jaylin Noel (2/17 on two targets) and Jared Wayne (1/20 on four targets including an inexcusable drop) continue to haunt the situation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kayshon-bo.headline: Kayshon Boutte caught 3-of-5 targets for 37 yards in Houston’s Week 2 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kayshon-bo.analysis: Expected to be “used a lot” by Ian Rapoport’s reporting, Boutte was on the field for 53-of-76 snaps. He either didn’t look completely comfortable with the offense yet or wasn’t fully integrated, depending on how nice you want to be about it — C.J. Stroud’s one near-pick was in his area on a ball he wasn’t expecting and it was clear he and Dalton Schultz weren’t on the same page. Boutte’s role should continue to grow next week assuming Nico Collins remains out but the Texans haven’t really embraced his talents yet.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kayshon-bo.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said Texans WR Kayshon Boutte could be used “a lot” in Week 2 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kayshon-bo.analysis: Rapoport’s full quote is winding and hyperbolic, but it sounds like Boutte will be a featured receiver if the Texans believe he is ready to handle that role with WR Nico Collins (hamstring) sidelined. Rapoport notes that Boutte played in “the same” offensive scheme during his time with the Patriots, so adjusting to his new team’s playbook theoretically should have been easy. That said, Boutte caught just one pass last week. He can be treated as a volatile but viable FLEX starter in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kayshon-bo.headline: Kayshon Boutte caught 1-of-2 targets for 21 yards in Houston’s Week 1 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kayshon-bo.analysis: Boutte managed just 36-of-79 snaps, third-most among Texans wideouts, as they ran weird platoons that had Jared Wayne, Jaylin Noel, and Xavier Hutchinson all on the field for at least 24 snaps. Until someone conclusively wins this job, or at least we start getting some juice that someone might win the job, it’ll be hard to start any of these receivers in fantasy football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kayshon-bo.headline: Texans HC DeMeco Ryans said Kayshon Boutte will play in Week 1 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kayshon-bo.analysis: Speaking on Monday, Ryans said Boutte has been “picking up the playbook really well.” The fourth-year receiver was acquired in a trade with the Patriots back on August 24th and is expected to have an immediate role in the offense after the Texans lost Jayden Higgins to a torn ACL earlier this offseason. Boutte has served primarily as a field stretcher during his first three years in the league and shouldn’t be trusted in start/sit leagues this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) is not on Houston’s final Week 12 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: With Kayshon Boutte out, it’s possible that Harrison could be Houston’s No. 3 wideout if they continue to manage things delicately with Tank Dell. He’ll be a tough FLEX play given his snap volume with the Texans even despite a nice matchup against the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Marvin Harrison (hamstring) resumed practicing on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: The Texans could get Harrison back in time for Sunday’s game against the Ravens. While his presence might help CJ Stroud, Harrison can only be viewed as a WR4/5, likely playing in a rotational role on the perimeter. Harrison does not need to be stashed in 12-team leagues at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: NBC Houston’s Aaron Wilson reports Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) is dealing with a short-term strain.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: Danielle Hunter, too, is dealing with one of these. It seems like after the lengthy layoff following Thursday night’s win over the Colts, the Texans could be in line to get both players back for Week 12’s game against the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Texans declared Marvin Harrison, EDGE Danielle Hunter, RB Woody Marks, TE Brevin Jordan, C Jake Andrews, OG Wyatt Teller and OT Nate Thomas inactive for Week 11 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: Harrison (hamstring) and Marks (concussion) are both out this week, condensing the Texans’ skill position corps for fantasy football purposes. Both players can be stashed on benches in 12-team leagues, though neither player is a must-stash option. David Montgomery should handle a sizable workload with Marks out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Texans ruled out Marvin Harrison (hamstring) for Week 11 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: Unfortunately, the Texans’ mid-season acquisition will miss another game. Harrison’s absence helpfully condenses the pass-catching corps for fantasy football purposes, though. Nico Collins and Xavier Hutchinson will likely lead their position group, followed by Kayshon Boutte and Tank Dell.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) did not practice on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: He’ll almost certainly be sidelined for Week 11’s TNF game after back-to-back missed practices. Xavier Hutchinson and Tank Dell should be the main fantasy beneficiaries of Harrison’s absence. This will make two weeks in a row on the shelf for Harrison and no practices since ahead of Week 9’s game, making it feel dicey that he’ll be able to get active for Week 12 as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) was listed as a “DNP” on Monday’s estimated practice report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: It appears highly likely that Harrison Jr. will miss his second consecutive game with a hamstring injury considering the team is on a short week. Xavier Hutchinson and Kayshon Boutte are likely to continue forward as the top two wide receivers behind Nico Collins, with Tank Dell likely to be held around half of the offensive snaps in this third game back from over a year of missed time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) won’t play in Houston’s Week 10 game against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: Harrison did not practice on Thursday or Friday and it’s possible this develops into a longer-term injury. Kayshon Boutte and Xavier Hutchinson will step in as reasonable FLEX plays with Harrison’s snaps off the table. The Texans probably won’t score 40 points again, but they have struggled to move the ball on the ground and should throw plenty against the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Marvin Harrison (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: Harrison was limited yesterday and sat out today. That series of events typically suggests that the player was injured in practice. Harrison is firmly on the wrong side of questionable at this time. He can be stashed in 12-team leagues, but it may take him a while to get back into form.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Marvin Harrison (hamstring) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: Harrison is tentatively on track to play in Week 10 against the Browns, but hamstring strains can be tough for wide receivers to immediately bounce back from, and we do not know whether the injury occurred today or last Sunday. Harrison’s practice participation tomorrow will tell us more. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.headline: Brock Bowers (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 12 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.analysis: We can’t know for sure, but it looks like the Raiders might choose to hold Bowers out through their Week 13 bye. He was limited on Wednesday, and although he was limited again on Thursday, he practiced with his injured ankle heavily taped. Today, he sat out. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak tends to let his players take the field on game day, even if they are at less than 100 percent, but Bowers must be viewed as truly questionable at best. If active, he should be in fantasy football lineups. In the meantime, make a backup plan.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.headline: Brock Bowers (ankle) was not seen practicing on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.analysis: Bowers was limited on Wednesday and Thursday. ESPN’s Ryan McFadden noted yesterday that Bowers’ right ankle was “heavily wrapped up” yesterday, which wasn’t the case on Wednesday. Hopefully, today’s absence during the portion of practice open to the media is only a precautionary, rest-related move. We should know more when the official injury report drops later. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.headline: Brock Bowers (ankle) was listed as a limited participant during Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.analysis: Bowers was also limited during Wednesday’s session. The team remains optimistic that their star tight end will play in Week 12 against the Browns, but fantasy managers should be prepared to turn to another option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.headline: Brock Bowers (ankle) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.analysis: Bowers closed last week with two limited sessions, listed with ankle and quad injuries. Fortunately, the quad injury is no longer an issue. He is tentatively on track to play in Week 12 against the Browns. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said he is optimistic that Bowers will play this weekend, adding that having a bye in Week 13 will not factor into whether Bowers suits up this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.headline: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said he is optimistic about Brock Bowers’ (ankle/quad) availability for Week 12 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.analysis: Kubiak told reporters post-game that Bowers continues to make progress as he rehabs his two injuries. Bowers’ backup, Michael Mayer, caught just one pass for four yards today and picked up a back injury along the way. Hopefully, one or both of them will be good to go next week. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.headline: Brock Bowers (ankle/quad) is inactive for Week 11 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.analysis: Bowers wasn’t spotted on the field during warmups, so he may not have been that close to playing today after all. He’s now eyeing a Week 12 return against the Browns. Michael Mayer will pick up a few extra targets versus Denver, putting him on the TE1/2 border. Also inactive for the Raiders are WR Dont’e Thornton Jr., WR Malik Benson, S Tristin McCollum, S Dalton Johnson, OG Bryce Cabeldue, and DT Tonka Hemingway.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports there is “not a lot of optimism” that Brock Bowers (ankle/quad) will play in Week 11 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.analysis: Bowers returned to practice earlier in the week and was listed as questionable on Friday. Schefter noted that Bowers is pushing to play, but we doubt the team will let him suit up after suffering another ankle injury. That’s on top of the quad issue, which seems to be minor compared to the ankle. Assuming Bowers is out, Michael Mayer should see an uptick in targets against a Denver defense that has bled fantasy points to tight ends this season. He would be a solid streaming option if Bowers is ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.headline: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Brock Bowers (ankle/quad) is questionable for Week 11 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.analysis: We do not yet know Bowers’ Friday participation level. He was seen at practice, and Kubiak told reporters that Bowers got “a lot of work in.” Some reports indicate that Bowers spent time away from his teammates, working with trainers, though, so he could end up being a limited participant. The Broncos struggle to cover tight ends effectively. If active, Bowers is an elite TE1, albeit with some re-injury risk.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.headline: Brock Bowers (ankle/quad) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.analysis: Bowers resumed practicing in a limited capacity today, and although his quad ailment was not reported early in the week, it is not new. The Raiders listed him with both ankle and quad injuries yesterday as well, which likely explains why Bowers had such a hard time returning to the Raiders’ Week 10 loss to the Seahawks. He is tentatively on track to face the Broncos this weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.headline: Brock Bowers (ankle) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.analysis: This is great to see. We expect Bowers to be listed as a limited participant, but his return to practice with an extra day to spare gives him a real chance to suit up in Week 11 against a Broncos defense that routinely surrenders catches and yardage to the tight end position. Bowers is an elite TE1 if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Jalen McMillan (knee/calf) was limited in Friday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: McMillan added the calf injury while trying to get off injured reserve with his knee, falling from a Thursday full session to a limited Friday. He’ll likely be questionable at best for Monday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Bucs opened the 21-day practice window for Jalen McMillan (knee).
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: McMillan has been on injured reserve since late September with a PCL injury. His practice window opening today could mean McMillan will suit up in Week 12 against the Panthers. He would not be a fantasy option for now in a run-first Tampa offense with several wideouts ahead of McMillan in the pass-catching pecking order.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Bucs WR Jalen McMillan is expected to miss 6-8 weeks with a knee injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Imaging Monday confirmed a PCL sprain for McMillan, who will soon move to injured reserve with a month-plus recovery timeline. The Buccaneers are also dealing with an injury to quarterback Baker Mayfield’s thumb on his throwing hand, although initial testing was positive. Now sitting at 0-3 and in last place in the NFC South, they’ll likely look to youth to attempt to save their season. On that note, no team in the division currently holds a winning record through three weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: ESPN’s Jenna Laine reports Jalen McMillan is having an MRI on his left knee.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: McMillan suffered a knee injury in the first quarter of Sunday’s loss to the Vikings and did not return to the game. The 24-year-old receiver has played in two games this season but has yet to register a catch on the nine offensive snaps he has played. It’s been a rough two seasons for McMillan, who missed nearly all of last season with a serious neck injury that sidelined him until Week 15.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Jalen McMillan did not catch his lone target in the Bucs’ Week 3 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: McMillan sustained a knee injury in the first quarter and did not return to the game. The Bucs said they would evaluate the injury on Sunday night. Ted Hurst ran almost every route in the Tampa offense with McMillan sidelined, catching a 40-yard touchdown in the first half. Hurst would continue to play significant snaps if McMillan is out for a while.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Jalen McMillan (knee) is practicing in full for Week 3 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: McMillan logged three full practices last week but was limited to just seven snaps on Sunday. He was not targeted once. His role should increase as he gets more practice reps under his belt, but fantasy managers can’t count on that happening this week specifically. He is not on the fantasy menu for Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles said Jalen McMillan (knee) is “healthy and he’s not all the way there yet, but he’s closer to getting there.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: That explains all the Ted Hurst from yesterday’s game. McMillan played just seven snaps and saw no targets. He enters Week 3 as a hard-to-trust FLEX even if he is healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Jalen McMillan (knee) is expected to play in Week 2 against the Browns, but not in a “full-time role just yet.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Bucs are going to ease McMillan back into the lineup after he missed Week 1 with the knee injury. McMillan will take rookie Ted Hurst’s spot in the lineup once healthy, but that might not happen until Week 3. Until we see what their split looks like, neither Hurst nor McMillan should be in fantasy lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Buccaneers WR Jalen McMillan (knee) is questionable to play in Week 2 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: This is a little surprising. The Buccaneers seem to be taking it very slowly as they bring McMillan back from his knee injury. At this point, he must be treated as being truly questionable to play. He is a boom-bust FLEX if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Jalen McMillan (knee) is practicing in full on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: McMillan missed Week 1 due to a knee issue, despite getting in three limited practices during the week. He was listed as doubtful and the team ruled him out ahead of kickoff. It seems like the team was taking a cautious approach with his return from the training camp injury, and he should be good for Week 2. McMillan is expected to take rookie Ted Hurst’s spot in the lineup at X. Hurst managed just three catches for 36 yards in the role. In his first game of the season, McMillan will be buried in the WR5 ranks for fantasy purposes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/isaiah-william.headline: Isaiah Williams (ribs) is not on New York’s final Week 12 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/isaiah-william.analysis: Williams got in two full sessions to close out the week and should have a decent role against the Dolphins with Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle/groin) sidelined. Still, we’d expect the Jets to try to ride their run game, so Williams isn’t a must-use FLEX play or anything like that.

https://www.nbcsports.com/isaiah-william.headline: Isaiah Williams (ribs) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/isaiah-william.analysis: Williams should be good to go for No. 3 wide receiver duties this week. The Jets’ wide receiver corps is a little too crowded for Williams to be a serious FLEX option against the Dolphins this week, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/isaiah-william.headline: Isaiah Williams (ribs) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/isaiah-william.analysis: Williams missed last week with the rib issue. Omar Cooper was also out, allowing Sterling Shepard to take over the No. 3 receiver role. Shepard saw two targets and managed to get into the end zone on both of them. Cooper appears to be out again this week, but Williams is trending in the right direction. Needless to say, we can’t recommend Shepard (or Williams) in fantasy leagues this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/isaiah-william.headline: Jets ruled out Isaiah Williams (ribs) for Week 11 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/isaiah-william.analysis: This is unfortunate. Williams had a chance to play a larger role with Omar Cooper (ankle) sidelined. Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell benefit from these players’ absences, though they will be catching passes thrown by a hobbled Geno Smith (ankle).

https://www.nbcsports.com/isaiah-william.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Isaiah Williams (ribs) will not play in Week 11 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/isaiah-william.analysis: Williams could have been in line for a decent workload given that Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle/hip) has been ruled out, but the 25-year-old receiver will join Cooper on the sidelines for this one. Veteran Tim Patrick, who ran 22-plus routes in Weeks 5 and 6 when the Jets were shorthanded at the position, could be next in line for playing time, but he should probably be avoided even on a week with six teams on bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/isaiah-william.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Omar Cooper (ankle) will not play in Week 11 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/isaiah-william.analysis: This was to be expected. Cooper was bounced from Week 10’s game against the Bills after one snap, after he had his ankle rolled up on, and has not gotten on the practice field this week. The 22-year-old receiver has had a challenging start to his career and is now slated to miss his fifth game of the season. Fellow receiver Isaiah Williams (ribs) has also been ruled out, paving the way for Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell to have busy days against the one-win Chargers. It doesn’t sound like Cooper is at risk of being placed on injured reserve, so we’ll see if things fare any differently for him entering Week 12.

https://www.nbcsports.com/isaiah-william.headline: Isaiah Williams (ribs) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/isaiah-william.analysis: Williams’ injury is unfortunate because Omar Cooper (ankle) is seemingly unlikely to play. If Williams were able to go this weekend, he would enter the boom-bust FLEX tier with six NFL teams on bye. Hopefully, he practices tomorrow.

https://www.nbcsports.com/isaiah-william.headline: Isaiah Williams (ribs) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/isaiah-william.analysis: Williams would not normally be a name to monitor, but he tallied seven targets in the Jets’ Week 10 loss to Buffalo. Williams was forced to take on more work after Omar Cooper Jr. went down with an ankle injury. We suspect the Jets would lean on their 12-personnel alignment if Williams and Cooper are out for Week 11. That would finally get first-round rookie Kenyon Sadiq on the field more.

https://www.nbcsports.com/isaiah-william.headline: Isaiah Williams caught 4-of-7 targets for 24 yards in the Jets’ Week 10 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/isaiah-william.analysis: Williams stepped into a bigger role with Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) leaving this game after the Jets’ first offensive play. The 25-year-old could have had a bigger day, but a long catch-and-run was called back due to offsetting penalties. If Cooper Jr. were to miss Week 11, Williams could be a deep league FLEX option against the Chargers, but he’s likely not in for a huge role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/isaiah-william.headline: Isaiah Williams caught 1-of-2 targets for 16 yards in the Jets’ Week 5 win over the Browns, adding a three-yard rush.
https://www.nbcsports.com/isaiah-william.analysis: Fill-in No. 2 wideout Williams is stuck on just four catches in three games during Adonai Mitchell’s surprisingly lengthy absence with a finger injury. The fact that Mitchell was not placed on I.R. suggests the Jets were not expecting more than a three-game absence, so Mitchell could be back as soon as Week 6 against the Patriots. Either way, Williams has not shown enough to earn a spot on 12-team league benches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: Tee Higgins (hamstring) is questionable to play in Week 12 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Higgins reportedly woke up with soreness in his hamstring today. He participated in the Bengals’ walkthrough, but left practice when team stretching began. He will be listed as a non-participant on the official injury report. Bengals coach Zac Taylor said Higgins should be fine for Sunday’s game. Higgins has a long history of hamstring strains, particularly in his left leg, and the Bengals have occasionally used him as a decoy when hurt in the past. That said, he is a very talented player, capable of producing efficiently even if used minimally. Higgins should be in fantasy football lineups if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: Tee Higgins caught 2-of-3 targets for 43 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 11 loss to the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Higgins got in the box score with a 31-yard touchdown reception late in the second quarter after the two teams played to a scoreless first frame in driving rain. The Bengals did not alter their typical pass-heavy ways despite the rain throughout the first half, with Higgins seeing modest volume while primarily matched up against Rasul Douglas on the perimeter. Joe Burrow fed the running backs and tight ends a massive 24 targets in the face of unrelenting pressure from the Commanders, a situation likely to correct against the single-high-heavy Saints in Week 12, where Higgins returns to WR2 status in fantasy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: Tee Higgins (knee) is practicing in full for Week 11 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Higgins injured his knee in Week 10 against the Steelers, but apparently it is only a minor injury. The Bengals’ No. 2 wide receiver is having an excellent season, and that top-tier performance should continue against a beatable Commanders’ pass defense. Higgins is a borderline WR1/2 with six teams on bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: Tee Higgins caught 5-of-6 targets for 66 yards in the Bengals’ Week 10 win over the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Higgins’ six targets finished third on the team behind Ja’Marr Chase (14) and Chase Brown (nine) while his receiving output was dwarfed by the 231 yards of Chase. The matchup against the zone-heavy Steelers likely played a significant role in the target breakout, with Higgins much more dangerous against man coverage this season. Higgins remains an elite WR2 ahead of a Week 11 meeting with the Commanders on Monday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: Tee Higgins caught 5-of-6 targets for 32 yards and two touchdowns in the Bengals’ Week 9 victory over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Higgins had recorded at least 148 receiving yards in three of his last four games. His 32 yards were a far cry from those gaudy totals, but he was able to save the day from a fantasy perspective by catching a four-yard touchdown and an eight-yard touchdown. Higgins still has 758 receiving yards on the season to Ja’Marr Chase’s 647, so he has that going for him. Higgins is technically the WR2 on the Bengals, but he’s a top-10 WR in fantasy heading into a matchup with the Steelers in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: Tee Higgins caught 10-of-11 targets for 155 yards and two touchdowns in the Bengals’ Week 8 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Higgins led the team in receiving yards while trailing Ja’Marr Chase in receptions and targets. He was Joe Burrow’s primary target over the middle of the field in the intermediate and deep areas. Higgins caught a pair of second half touchdowns, catching an 18-yard score to tie the game towards the end of regulation. Pass-heavy game scripts will lead to a high amount of fantasy production for Higgins and Chase, who saw a combined 56-percent target share from Joe Burrow. Higgins is a high-end WR2 for Week 9 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: Tee Higgins caught 6-of-7 targets for 148 yards and one touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 7 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Higgins came up big multiple times for the Bengals in the second half after they were shut out 13-0 in the first half. He hauled in passes of 10 and 19 yards on the Bengals’ opening drive in the second half to help set up an eventual six-yard touchdown pass to Mike Gesicki, and hauled in a 13-yard touchdown of his own on the following drive. He would also make two catches of 40-plus yards, and came up six yards short of a second touchdown on an impressive 44-yard grab — his longest play of the day. Higgins has gone for 140-plus yards in two of his last three games and has topped 90 yards in four of six games this season. He profiles as a high-end WR2 in next week’s game against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: Tee Higgins caught 2-of-4 targets for 22 yards in the Bengals’ Week 5 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Higgins saw just four targets against the Dolphins after seeing 16 targets in Week 4. The adductor/neck injuries didn’t limit his playing time as much, seeing 45 snaps on the day, No. 2 among Bengals receivers. With Ja’Marr Chase back on the field, Higgins’ target volume decreased considerably and he totaled just 22 yards in a more run-favorable game script. Despite the dud, Higgins still belongs in the WR2 ranks and gets a mediocre Ravens defense in Week 7 after a Week 6 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: Bengals WR Tee Higgins is active for Week 5 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Higgins suffered an adductor injury in Week 4 against the Jaguars and was a full practice participant Friday after DNPs the two days before. Higgins and Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) both declared active. Though NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe reports he will play mostly “meaningful plays”, Higgins is in the WR2 ranks while Chase is back in the WR1 ranks this week. The Bengals declared S Kyle Dugger, C Connor Lew, OT Myles Hinton, TE Jack Endries, WR Colbie Young, and DT Landon Robinson inactive for Week 5 against the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Tee Higgins (groin/neck) is expected to play in Week 5 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) will also play. Higgins is likely suiting up at less than full strength, but fantasy managers have to keep him in their lineups versus a Miami defense that is giving up explosive passing plays at the second-highest rate in the league this year. He will be a boom/bust WR2 for Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Darren Waller (knee) was limited in Friday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: Waller now has back-to-back limited sessions. He has cobbled together four limited practices in a row and played through this injury last week. It’s possible he is held to 40 percent of the snaps again in Week 12 if we don’t see an upgrade on Friday, but with all three Panthers tight ends on the injury report, the whole situation will remain uncertain until Saturday. Mitchell Evans (Achilles) upgraded to a limited session after not practicing on Thursday, and Tommy Tremble (knee) also was limited for a second day in a row.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Darren Waller (knee) was a limited participant in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: Waller got in a limited session, as was Tommy Tremble with his own knee ailment. Mitchell Evans was not able to practice due to his Achilles injury, so the Carolina room could be in a bit of trouble for Week 12 against the Bucs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Darren Waller caught 3-of-3 targets for 42 yards in the Panthers’ Week 11 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: Waller’s biggest play came on a 27-yard reception in the third quarter. He caught one of three deep balls from Bryce Young, but fellow tight end Mitchell Evans outperformed him, posting a 5-44-1 line in what turned out to be a career day for the third-year tight end. Waller won’t be anything more than a boom-or-bust TE2 in Week 12 against the Buccaneers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Darren Waller (knee) is active for the Panthers’ Week 11 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: Waller was questionable with a knee injury entering the weekend, but will be good to go in what is somewhat of a revenge game against the team that drafted him in the sixth round back in 2015. The 34-year old tight end profiles as a boom-or-bust TE2 against a Ravens defense that has allowed the 10th-most PPR points per game (14.1) to opposing tight ends over its last five games. In addition to Waller, fellow tight end Tommy Tremble (knee) is also active, while TE Ja’Tavion Sanders, QB Haynes King, RB AJ Dillon, LB Bobby Okereke, C Sam Hecht, and DT TeRah Edwards will all be inactive for this one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Darren Waller (knee) is questionable for Carolina’s Week 11 game against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: He got in two limited practices on Thursday and Friday. You’re probably not planning to play either he or fellow questionable tight end Tommy Tremble as anything more than a TE2 either way. If both players were somehow ruled out, Mitchell Evans would take their place in the pecking order.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Darren Waller (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: He didn’t practice Wednesday, so this is a good sign for his availability. With Tommy Tremble also practicing though, we may remain in the Panthers TE Stasis where both players are taking too much volume off the table for you to want to start either of them in fantasy leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Darren Waller (knee) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: Waller is sometimes given Wednesdays often, so this could just be precautionary. Panthers backup TE Tommy Tremble (knee) was also listed as a non-participant. Hopefully, one of them is good to go for this week’s game against the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Darren Waller caught 2-of-4 targets for 24 yards in the Panthers’ Week 10 win against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: Waller ran a route on 27 of the team’s 38 drop backs and should have caught what would have been a 30-yard touchdown in the first half. Coming off a big game in Week 9 against the Broncos, Waller was fourth on the team in targets as the Panthers turned hard toward the run. Tommy Tremble had more targets, receptions, and yards than Waller on the day. Waller’s red zone role and the Panthers usual pass heaviness should keep him viable as a streaming option in Week 11 against Baltimore.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Darren Waller caught 8-of-10 targets for 90 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 9 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: By far the best game of Waller’s first season in Carolina came as Tommy Tremble also found the end zone. The duo combined for 12 catches as Bryce Young flooded the middle of the field with looks. Good stuff if you were forced to take a TE2 dart throw, but this is the first time since Week 3 Waller has seen genuine volume. We would consider it a one-off spiked week heading into an admittedly plus Week 10 date in the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Darren Waller scored a 50-yard touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 7 loss to the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: Waller’s second quarter touchdown came after he beat a linebacker on a post route. It was also one of just two targets in a game the Panthers went on to lose 43-13. Waller’s score was the only black and teal tally before garbage time. Nice, though Waller had previously not found the end zone since Week 2. He has 14 total catches through six games. The limited overall workload has made Waller difficult to trust as a TE2 because of his zero-point floor. He will have some big-play potential Thursday against the Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.headline: Tetairoa McMillan (foot) was limited in Friday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.analysis: McMillan was not spotted on Thursday, so this is a good sign for his chances of suiting up on Monday Night Football against the Buccaneers. Still, there’s a non-zero chance he winds up with a questionable tag on Saturday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.headline: Tetairoa McMillan (foot) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.analysis: McMillan was unable to participate in today’s walkthrough, which is a bad sign for his Week 12 availability. Jalen Coker would step into No. 1 wide receiver duties if McMillan cannot play this weekend against the Buccaneers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.headline: Panthers coach Dave Canales said he is optimistic that Tetairoa McMillan (foot) will play in Week 12 against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.analysis: McMillan limped off the field in Week 11 with the foot issue but eventually returned to and finished the game. He did not practice today, though it’s not officially a DNP. The Panthers’ first practice of the week is tomorrow since they play on Monday, which will give McMillan an extra day to recover. Assuming all goes well in practice this week, McMillan will remain a fantasy WR2 for a must-win matchup with the Bucs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.headline: Tetairoa McMillan caught 6-of-9 targets for 71 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 11 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.analysis: McMillan has scored twice in his last three games and led the Panthers in both targets and receptions in this one. His lone score came on a seven-yard pass from Bryce Young in the second quarter, but it could have been a much bigger day for McMillan were it not for an interception by Young in the third quarter. Young attempted to find McMillan again in the end zone in the third quarter, but a diving interception by Ravens CB T.J. Tampa ended any hopes of points for McMillan. McMillan has gone for 50-plus yards in three of his last four games and will be a strong WR2 in Week 12’s game against the Buccaneers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.headline: Tetairoa McMillan caught 3-of-7 targets for 35 yards in the Panthers’ Week 10 win against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.analysis: None of the Carolina pass catchers did much in a game that saw the Panthers go ultra run-heavy. McMillan led the team in targets but was never on the same page with Bryce Young, who had one of his worst games of the season. On the season McMillan has four games with at least 75 yards, along with five games of at least five receptions. McMillan will be a WR2 option in Week 11 against a shaky Ravens secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.headline: Tetairoa McMillan caught 4-of-6 targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 9 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.analysis: McMillan’s four-yard touchdown with the Panthers attempting to complete a fourth quarter comeback was his first since Week 4 and only his third of the season. He has also now been held below 60 yards receiving in three straight games as Bryce Young has been mired in a slump. If there’s good news, it’s that McMillan has maintained a decent floor, and we know the next spiked week can’t be far away. It could come as early as Week 10 against the Saints’ soft defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.headline: Tetairoa McMillan caught 6-of-11 targets for 58 yards in the Panthers’ Week 8 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.analysis: McMillan had a long gain of just 14 yards, as Bryce Young just didn’t have time to get the ball down the field and wasn’t particularly accurate on the rare times he did. The wideout was targeted early and often, but it was an inefficient effort for the 23-year-old, at best. Even as the clear top option in this passing attack — all due respect to Jalen Coker — there’s a ton of volatility in McMillan’s fantasy profile, and that won’t change for Week 9 against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.headline: Tetairoa McMillan caught 4-of-6 targets for 40 yards in the Panthers’ Week 7 loss to the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.analysis: Feel lucky McMillan even reached those marks, as the Panthers simply did not compete in a game where they committed four turnovers and trailed 33-6 at halftime. The first-team offense sat for the game’s final 10 minutes. McMillan had a better go of it than Jalen Coker, who caught one pass and fell down to create an interception. A shambles, though one the Panthers have to move on from quickly, as they are headed to Green Bay for a potential short-week shootout on Thursday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.headline: Tetairoa McMillan caught 6-of-9 passes for 86 yards in the Panthers’ Week 6 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.analysis: McMillan saw a lot of Quinyon Mitchell in tight coverage on Sunday, but he had a solid day that could have been much better after a fourth-quarter pass went off his hands in the end zone. It would have been a difficult catch with Mitchell draped all over him, but it was a catchable pass. More importantly, it shows that McMillan remains a key piece of this passing game, and he did run the most routes of any receiver on the team.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.headline: Tetairoa McMillan caught 14-of-16 targets for 192 yards and two touchdowns in the Panthers’ Week 4 win over the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.analysis: McMillan set career highs in both receptions and yardage in the first half with nine catches for 147 yards before the break. He operated as the clear alpha in a pass attack without both Jalen Coker and Xavier Legette, routinely dusting everyone the Lions had at their disposal in an injury-ravaged secondary. While the receiving line surely turns heads, fantasy managers were left even more ecstatic about the way in which he was utilized, with the second-year receiver catching six passes for 94 yards and both touchdowns while aligned in the slot. Offensive coordinator Brad Idzik is providing structure, sequencing, and situational tendencies unlike anything fans had grown accustomed to when head coach Dave Canales was helming the offense, resulting in quarterback Bryce Young leading the league in passing while averaging more than 30 points per game through the first month of play. McMillan’s ceiling remains sky-high as a legitimate WR1 when the Panthers square off against the Eagles fin Week 6 following their bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.headline: Taliese Fuaga (knee) is questionable to play in Week 12 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.analysis: While Fuaga, the Saints’ right tackle, may or may not play, the team’s starting center, Erik McCoy (biceps), will make his return. Getting him back is good news for the Saints’ offense as a whole. Backup OT Asim Richards (knee) is also questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.headline: Taliese Fuaga (knee) was seen practicing on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.analysis: Fuaga, the Saints’ right tackle, and C Erik McCoy (biceps) were both practicing on Wednesday. This is great news for the offense overall. Getting both players back would be helpful this week against the Bengals’ talented defensive line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.headline: Saints coach Kellen Moore said Taliese Fuaga (knee) will not play in New Orleans’ Week 11 game against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.analysis: Asim Richards (knee) was also ruled out, leaving the Saints with 24-year-old UDFA Mason Murphy as a potential Week 11 starter at tackle.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.headline: Taliese Fuaga (knee) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.analysis: Fuaga, the Saints’ right tackle, and backup OT Asim Richards (knee) were both sidelined today. Saints C Erik McCoy (biceps) is sidelined as well, though he was already expected to miss time. Hopefully, Fuaga can return in time to face the Bears this weekend. Backup RB CJ Donaldson (shoulder) is practicing in full.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.headline: Tailese Fuaga (knee) won’t play in New Orleans’ Week 10 game against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.analysis: Fuaga has a knee sprain, per Kellen Moore. It sounds like a short-term thing and Moore has said he won’t need to go on injured reserve. Asim Richards and Mason Murphy are the backup tackles and Richards played left tackle while Kelvin Banks was sidelined earlier this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.headline: Taliese Fuaga (knee) was added to the injury report as a limited participant on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.analysis: The Saints’ right tackle was added to the injury report today, which is extremely unfortunate. The team is already without center Erik McCoy (biceps). Hopefully, this is only a minor issue for Fuaga.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.headline: Saints RT Taliese Fuaga (ankle) will not play in New Orleans’ Week 14 game against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.analysis: Fuaga played in Week 13, but appears to have injured his other ankle — this is not the same ankle he was on the report for earlier in the year — somewhere along the way despite playing 100 percent of the snaps.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.headline: Saints declared S Ugo Amadi, CB Rejzon Wright, RB Audric Estime, OT Taliese Fuaga, DT John Ridgeway III, and DT Khristian Boyd inactive for Week 12 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.analysis: Fuaga has been sidelined with an ankle injury for the last few weeks. He was a limited practice participant on Friday, but is still not yet ready to go. Estime is also inactive in the backfield with Alvin Kamara (ankle) good to go for Week 12 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.headline: Saints ruled out OT Taliese Fuaga (ankle) against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.analysis: The Saints’ depleted offensive line is in rough shape. Fuaga has a long way to go in his development, having allowed 22 quarterback pressures and three sacks this season, but downgrading to his backup, OT Asim Richards, won’t be any better. They face the Panthers this weekend, who field a solid defensive tackle unit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.headline: Saints coach Kellen Moore said RT Taliese Fuaga (ankle) has a high-ankle sprain and is unlikely to play this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taliese-fu.analysis: Ditto Jack Stoll. Fuaga has played through multiple injuries this year, with a knee and back listing. The second-year tackle has played up to his form last year, with a 65.0 PFF rating in 473 dropbacks. Asim Richards replaced him for the final two snaps of Week 9’s loss to the Rams and would be next man up.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.headline: Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell said Kyler Murray will back up Kirk Cousins in Week 12.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.analysis: Murray was removed from the injury report on Friday and will be active for the first time since suffering his hamstring strain. Carson Wentz will likely be an inactive third quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.headline: Kyler Murray (hamstring) was limited in Wednesday’s walk-through.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.analysis: Murray was listed as a limited participant for the Vikings’ walk-through practice. Since going down with a hamstring injury, Murray’s starting role has been taken over by Kirk Cousins. Even if Murray is good to go for Week 12, he is likely to be in the backup role to Cousins against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.headline: Kyler Murray (hamstring) will not play in Minnesota’s Week 11 game against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.analysis: It’s his third straight week on the shelf. Carson Wentz will again handle backup duties behind Kirk Cousins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.headline: Kyler Murray (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.analysis: Murray was out last week because of the hamstring issue and will likely miss Week 11 versus the 49ers. Carson Wentz will back up Kirk Cousins on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.headline: Kyler Murray (hamstring) won’t play in Minnesota’s Week 10 game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.analysis: He wouldn’t have played anyway with Kirk Cousins coming over. Murray will reclaim QB2 duties when healthy, but dealing with a grade 2 strain on his hamstring, that may not be for a few weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.headline: Carson Wentz (ankle) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.analysis: Wentz is tentatively on track to be available for backup duties. Kyler Murray (hamstring) remains sidelined. Neither Vikings quarterback needs to be rostered in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.headline: Kyler Murray (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.analysis: Murray is expected to miss more time with the Grade Two hamstring injury. With Kirk Cousins back in Minnesota, Murray’s health doesn’t change much for the offense. He will likely serve as Cousins’ backup once he gets past the hamstring issue.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.headline: NFL on Prime’s James Palmer reports Kyler Murray (hamstring) is dealing with a grade 2 strain, is “week to week” and is expected to miss more time.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.analysis: In other words, Kirk Cousins could immediately slide in as the starting quarterback. As for Murray, he appears safe to drop in most formats. Call of Duty released on October 23. Not sure why that appeared in this post, but we seem to be unable to backspace it.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.headline: Vikings acquired QB Kirk Cousins from the Raiders for a 2027 third-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.analysis: And where did that bring you? Back to me. Cousins will likely take over as Minnesota’s starting quarterback in the near future, if not immediately. When that happens, Kyler Murray will head back to the bench for a second straight season — he’s droppable in most leagues at this point. Fernando Mendoza will take over as starting quarterback for the Raiders. Mendoza is best approached cautiously at this point in fantasy leagues. Cousins’ value likely remains stagnant — Klint Kubiak was already getting quite a bit out of him — but he provides the Vikings with a better floor at quarterback than what they were getting so it’s obvious after watching Carson Wentz play last night why this is happening.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports the Vikings could trade for a quarterback before the NFL’s trade deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.analysis: “The word going into last night was the Vikings would be in the QB market ahead of the trade deadline if Carson Wentz didn’t play well,” Garafolo said. Narrator voice: He didn’t. Wentz was an utter disaster in Monday night’s loss to the Bills, completing 8-of-25 passes for 81 yards and two interceptions in the team’s second straight loss. Wentz in Week 9 had the league’s lowest drop back EPA and lowest success rate. He also appeared to sustain an ankle injury in the second half. With Kyler Murray (hamstring) struggling mightily in Kevin O’Connell’s offense, the Vikings could make a desperation move for Kirk Cousins or Daniel Jones ahead of today’s 4:00 p.m. eastern time trade deadline. Cousins, for one, would be a marked upgrade for Justin Jefferson and the Minnesota pass catchers. The Raiders have not expressed interest in parting with Cousins, however.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-fant/.headline: Noah Fant (calf) is questionable to play in Week 12 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-fant/.analysis: With Juwan Johnson (hamstring) sidelined, Fant had a chance to increase his role on Sunday. Getting hurt on Friday pretty much takes him off the TE2 radar. Jordyn Tyson could benefit as a go-to receiver in the short-to-intermediate area of the field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-fant/.headline: Saints coach Kellen Moore said Juwan Johnson (hamstring) is day-to-day.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-fant/.analysis: Johnson was not seen practicing today, so we expect to see him listed as a non-participant on the Saints’ official injury report. He looks like a long shot for Week 12 against the Bengals. Noah Fant is a TE2 with Johnson sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-fant/.headline: Noah Fant caught 2-of-5 targets for 19 yards in the Saints’ Week 11 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-fant/.analysis: Fant was the Saints’ leading tight end on the day, seeing the most snaps, targets, and receptions in the tight end room. He saw a pair of red zone targets in the fourth quarter, though Tyler Shough could not connect with him and the drive ended in a turnover-on-downs. Juwan Johnson is his primary receiving competition, but Johnson saw just one target before exiting with a hamstring injury. No Saints tight end needs to be started for fantasy purposes at this point; Fant is in the streaming tight end conversation should Johnson miss any time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-fant/.headline: Saints TE Noah Fant (abdomen) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 5 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-fant/.analysis: Fant sat out in Week 4 after scoring two touchdowns in Week 3. He is not fantasy-relevant on his own, but he can serve as a checkdown option for Tyler Shough. The Saints labeled WR Barion Brown (thigh) questionable to play this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-fant/.headline: Saints TE Noah Fant (abdominal) is inactive for Week 4 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-fant/.analysis: Fant was originally listed as questionable but is ultimately unable to go, shocking fantasy managers that took a gamble on him following his two-touchdown game a week ago. Rookie Oscar Delp appears most likely to serve as the next man up while starter Juwan Johnson could take on additional volume at the position. Also inactive for the Saints are QB Zach Wilson, CB Decamerion Richardson, EDGE Anfernee Jennings, DL Christen Miller, LB Kaden Elliss, and EDGE Carl Granderson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-fant/.headline: Saints TE Noah Fant (abdominal) is questionable for Week 4 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-fant/.analysis: So too is LB Pete Werner, while LB Kaden Elliss, DE Carl Granderson, and DEAnfernee Jennings have been ruled out. Rookie tight end Oscar Delp would be in line to see additional run alongside Juwan Johnson, should Fant be unable to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-fant/.headline: Saints WR Barion Brown (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-fant/.analysis: Both Brown and TE Noah Fant (abdomen) were limited today, putting them tentatively on track to play on Monday night against the Falcons. Neither player belongs in fantasy lineups, but their presence is helpful for QB Tyler Shough.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-fant/.headline: Noah Fant caught 4-of-4 targets for 33 yards and two touchdowns in the Saints’ Week 3 loss to the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-fant/.analysis: Fant chipped in two touchdowns in a game that tied an NFL record for tight end touchdowns with six. His first was on a three-yard slant. His second was an impressive catch-and-run play via play-action from 16 yards out. Fant is not on the starting radar next week against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-fant/.headline: Saints agreed to terms with TE Noah Fant, formerly of the Bengals, on a two-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-fant/.analysis: In his lone season with the Bengals, Fant posted career-lows in targets (41), receptions (34), and receiving yards (288) while playing behind Mike Gesicki. The 28-year-old tight end will now join the Saints in what will presumably be a TE2 role with Juwan Johnson still under contract through the 2027 season. Fant is a good enough athlete to create yards after the catch, but most of his plays come in the short areas of the field. He’ll make for a decent depth signing for the Saints but we wouldn’t expect a career resurgence at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-fant/.headline: Noah Fant caught his only target for five yards in the Bengals’ Week 18 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-fant/.analysis: He managed a fumble-six — somehow his third of the season — in a game that the Browns won on a last-second field goal. Fant was heavily involved in Cincinnati’s offense while Mike Gesicki was on injured reserve, but still finished with his lowest yardage output in seven NFL seasons at 33/283/3. A surprise July release by Seattle, Fant latched on with the Bengals quickly on a one-year deal. He’ll likely find a new spot as a veteran placeholder in this same sort of role in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Darrisaw (shoulder) will not play in Minnesota’s Week 12 game against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: At no point did he practice after leaving Week 11’s game in Mexico City with the shoulder injury. Ryan Van Demark replaced Darrisaw in mop-up duty and would seem likely to start this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Darrisaw (shoulder) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Darrisaw seemingly re-injured his shoulder in the Vikings’ Week 11 loss to the 49ers. Minnesota just held a walk-through, but the franchise left tackle starts out not practicing. He is truly questionable ahead of Week 12 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Darrisaw (shoulder) practiced in full on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Darrisaw is now firmly on track to play in Week 9’s Monday Night Football game against the Bills, who field a tough, talented defensive line. Having Darrisaw on the field will be helpful for pocket passer Carson Wentz.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Darrisaw (shoulder) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: The Vikings’ left tackle is on track to play in Week 9’s Monday Night Football game against the Bills. His likely presence is good news. The Bills field a fairly strong defensive line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Darrisaw (concussion) is practicing in full for Week 7 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Darrisaw suffered a concussion in Week 4 against the Dolphins and was unable to play in Week 5 against the Saints. The Vikings were on bye in Week 6, giving him more than two weeks to get ready for Week 7. Vikings RT Brian O’Neill (knee) was limited.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Vikings LT Christian Darrisaw (concussion) will not play in Minnesota’s Week 5 game against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: He did not practice all week with the concussion. Brian O’Neill is questionable. Ryan Van Demark will likely play left tackle for Darrisaw, while 2026 third-rounder Caleb Tiernan is the likely reserve if O’Neill can’t go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Vikings LT Christian Darrisaw (concussion) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Darrisaw is on the wrong side of questionable, having logged consecutive absences to begin Week 5. With Vikings LG Donovan Jackson (knee) out, Kyler Murray could be looking over his shoulder quite often against the Saints this weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell said LT Christian Darrisaw (concussion) will not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: O’Connell also said that RT Brian O’Neill (undisclosed) will be limited. The Vikings recently placed LG Donovan Jackson (knee) on injured reserve. The offensive line is very banged up at the moment.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell said LT Christian Darrisaw cleared the NFL’s concussion protocol in Week 4 against the Dolphins, but later experienced symptoms.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Darrisaw was in and out of the Vikings’ Week 4 win over the Dolphins. Now, we know why. The Vikings’ left tackle will have to clear it in order for him to play in Week 5 against the Saints. Vikings LG Donovan Jackson was forced from the game with a knee injury. This line is ailing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Vikings LT Christian Darrisaw (knee) said he feels “the best” he has felt in two years.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Darrisaw suffered a multi-ligament tear in his left knee in October 2024 and struggled in his return last year. He told reporters today that he thinks he “turned the corner this offseason.” The Vikings plan to give him regular rest days during training camp and the regular season, but he believes he is on track to be a full-time player once again.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: Jordan Addison (thumb) will not play in Minnesota’s Week 12 game against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: It’s his third straight absence. Kevin O’Connell seemed optimistic that Addison would have more of a shot to play this week, but he remains practiceless since suffering the thumb injury in a Friday practice ahead of Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: Jordan Addison (thumb) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: Addison seems unlikely to face the 49ers this week, though Myles Price (knee/ankle) has a chance to play, having logged two limited practices. Addison is still worth stashing as a potential FLEX option in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: Jordan Addison (thumb) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: Addison has yet to practice since undergoing thumb surgery last week. Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell said Monday that the 24-year-old may not “necessarily” be back in Week 12 against the Falcons. Tai Felton will continue to get increased reps with Addison out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell said he doesn’t “necessarily expect to have Jordan Addison (thumb)” back for Week 12 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: Addison underwent thumb surgery last week after suffering what was described as a “freak injury” in practice. While he wasn’t considered a candidate for injured reserve, O’Connell did say after the injury that he would likely miss multiple games before returning. If Addison is unable to play in Week 12, it would be the third straight game he has missed with the injury. His practice status will be one to monitor throughout the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: Vikings declared QB Kyler Murray, WR Jordan Addison, CB Isaiah Rodgers, QB Max Brosmer, and S Jay Ward inactive for Week 11 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: Addison will miss his second consecutive game while the team gets Jauan Jennings back from his own two-game absence. Expect Tai Felton and Myles Price to fill in for Addison while addition volume remains most likely to concentrate on Justin Jefferson and T.J. Hockenson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell said Jordan Addison (thumb) will not be placed on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: Addison underwent successful surgery on his thumb after suffering a “freak” injury in practice last week. He is still expected to miss multiple games, but not placing him on IR means the Vikings don’t foresee him missing an entire month. He will be out for Week 11 and likely Week 12, but fantasy managers should still try to hold onto him ahead of the fantasy postseason. Myles Price and Tai Felton will be in the mix for extra targets if Jauan Jennings remains out this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell said Jordan Addison (thumb) will undergo surgery and could miss “a few weeks.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: He called it a “freak” injury and didn’t dismiss the possibility of Addison heading to short-term injured reserve. Fantasy managers in a rough bye week squeeze without injured reserve spots can move on from Addison if need be. He hasn’t cleared 100 yards in a game all season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: Jordan Addison (thumb) will not play in Week 10 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: After injuring his thumb in Friday’s practice, Addison has officially been ruled out for Sunday’s pivotal NFC North tilt against the Packers. With Jauan Jennings (calf) and T.J. Hockenson (wrist/chest) also sidelined, Kirk Cousins will be forced to rely on Myles Price, Tai Felton, and Jeshaun and his other receivers behind Justin Jefferson. Jefferson could be in line for a big day in his first game with Cousins since 2023. The Vikings also ruled out QB Kyler Murray, QB Max Brosmer, LB Blake Cashman, and DL Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins for Sunday’s game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Jordan Addison (thumb) “will have his status determined closer to game time.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: Addison injured his thumb in practice on Friday and the team listed him as questionable for today’s game. The team elevated wide receiver Jeshaun Jones from the practice squad yesterday, casting some doubt on Addison’s availability. With Jauan Jennings also out, Tai Felton and Myles Price could be in line for larger roles today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: Jordan Addison (thumb) is questionable for Minnesota’s Week 10 game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: Kevin O’Connell described it as Addison getting “dinged” in practice today. Not ideal. Addison would have been in for a workload bump with T.J. Hockenson out, as it stands it looks like Kirk Cousins will just throw to Justin Jefferson 25 times like it’s 2022 again.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Juwan Johnson (hamstring) will not play in New Orleans’ Week 12 game against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Perhaps this will give Kellen Moore an excuse to actually get Jordyn Tyson on the field this week. Noah Fant should also benefit from Johnson’s absence, and has a non-zero chance of a TE1 fantasy day given the Bengals strong track record of letting tight ends run wild under DC Al Golden.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Saints coach Kellen Moore said Juwan Johnson (hamstring) is day-to-day.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Johnson was not seen practicing today, so we expect to see him listed as a non-participant on the Saints’ official injury report. He looks like a long shot for Week 12 against the Bengals. Noah Fant is a TE2 with Johnson sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Juwan Johnson (hamstring) was not seen practicing on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Johnson is unlikely to play in Week 12 against the Bengals at this point. The Saints’ No. 1 tight end injured his hamstring last week. Recovering in one week is a tall task for a player who needs to be able to stride while running routes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Juwan Johnson failed to catch his lone target in the Saints’ Week 11 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Johnson saw just one target before exiting in the second half of the Saints’ Week 11 game against the Bears. He did not return to the game and head coach Kellen Moore said the 30-year-old is still being evaluated with a hamstring injury. Johnson has not exceeded three targets for five straight weeks now. He can remain on waiver wires moving forward, though Noah Fant enters the streaming conversation if Johnson misses any time.
