https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Juwan Johnson caught 2-of-3 targets for 28 yards in the Saints’ Week 10 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: It was yet another down game for Johnson in the flailing New Orleans offense. Johnson, who doesn’t have more than 40 yards in a game since Week 4, ran a pass route on 31 of 46 Saints drop backs. His involvement hasn’t led to much in the way of production. Johnson should remain on waiver wires ahead of Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Juwan Johnson caught both of his targets for 34 yards and a touchdown in the Saints’ Week 9 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Johnson split reps with Noah Fant and Oscar Delp once again. He had one catch headed into overtime but made the most of the extra drive with a game-winning touchdown grab. It was his first touchdown since Week 3. This was also his first multi-catch game since Week 5. With Jordyn Tyson set to take on a larger role in the coming weeks, Johnson’s days as a high-end TE2 appear to be over. Fantasy managers can do better off the waiver wire in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: NFL Insider Jordan Schultz reports Saints WR Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) “should be good to go” against the Browns in Week 9.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: The oft-injured Tyson hurt his hamstring in training camp and is yet to make his NFL debut. According to Schultz, he should be good to go Sunday against the Browns. A limited participant in practice throughout the week, it’s unclear how much Tyson might play in his first game. Eventually, though, he should settle in as the Saints’ WR2 behind Chris Olave. Tyson’s return also puts a damper on the fantasy prospects of Devaughn Vele and Juwan Johnson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Juwan Johnson caught 1-of-3 targets for seven yards in the Saints’ Week 7 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Johnson was solid over the first four weeks of the season, but this was another clunker for the 30-year-old tight end. After going over 50 yards in his first four games and bringing in three touchdowns, Johnson has just 23 total yards without a score in the next three. Because of positional value Johnson can’t be completely ignored, but the Saints haven’t paid much attention to him lately, so it’s time to look for alternatives, at least.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Juwan Johnson failed to catch either of his two targets in the Saints’ Week 6 win over the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Johnson was silent in a low-efficiency passing day for the Saints offense. The tight end position in general was a non-factor as a pass-catching group on the day. As Tyler Shough deals with broken bones in his non-throwing hand, the Saints’ passing game is tightening up and has less room for Johnson. He is a fantasy TE2 for Week 7 against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Juwan Johnson caught 4-of-5 targets for 16 yards in the Saints’ Week 5 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Johnson had hovered around 50 yards in every game before today’s loss, but a shutdown Minnesota defense was more than enough to mute the production of every New Orleans pass-catcher. Things should improve for everyone when the Saints take on the Giants next week. Johnson will be a volume-based TE2 for Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: Ravens ruled out Vega Ioane (hand) for Week 12 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: The Ravens’ stud rookie right guard has had unfortunate injury luck thus far. He was already playing through knee and shoulder injuries when he injured his hand in yesterday’s practice. Perhaps the time off will help the other two issues heal. The Ravens also ruled out DT Nnamdi Madubuike and S Jaylinn Hawkins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: Vega Ioane (shoulder/knee) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 11 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: He got in two full sessions on Thursday and Friday. Hopefully his return will help calm down the interior of the Baltimore offensive line. The Ravens will need all the pass protection help they can get if they keep playing as they did on Monday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: Vega Ioane (shoulder/knee) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: The Ravens’ talented rookie guard continues to practice and play through two difficult injuries. Ravens DT Nnamdi Madubuike (hamstring) remains sidelined through two Week 11 practices. Ioane should be able to face the Panthers this weekend. Madubuike could be sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: Vega Ioane (shoulder/knee) practiced in full on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: Ioane should have no issue playing against the Chargers on Monday night, nor should S Kyle Hamilton (hip), who has practiced in full in each of the last two days. Having Ioane on the field will be a big help for Jacoby Brissett in his first start for Baltimore.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: Vega Ioane (shoulder/knee) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: The Ravens’ stud rookie guard is on track to play this week, albeit with a new shoulder issue. Running backs Rasheen Ali (ankle) and Adam Randall (neck/hamstring) are practicing in full. They should play as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: Ravens did not activate Adam Randall (neck) from injured reserve for Week 9 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: The Ravens’ rookie running back will have to wait to make his debut. The Ravens declared QB Kedon Slovis, WR Elijah Sarratt, OL Emery Jones Jr., DL Aeneas Peebles, CB Nate Wiggins and S Jaylinn Hawkins inactive. Hawkins is dealing with a knee injury and Wiggins, the Ravens’ No. 1 cornerback, is listed with a stinger and an illness. Slovis will serve as the emergency third quarterback. Austin Reed is the QB2. Ravens RG Vega Ioane (knee) will play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: Ravens declared WR Elija Sarratt FS Jaylinn Hawkins, CB Chandler Rivers, OG Emery Jones, OG Vega Ioane, DT Aeneas Peebles, and QB Joe Fagnano inactive for Week 8 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: The Ravens will be without rookie guard Vega Ioane, who suffered a knee injury in last week’s loss to the Bengals. While it’s yet another blow to an already banged-up offensive line, the Ravens do have Lamar Jackson returning from his three-game absence after he suffered a high-ankle sprain in Week 4. Hopefully, Jackson’s return can provide a much-needed spark to an offense that has managed just 23 points combined in its last two games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: Vega Ioane (knee) won’t play in Baltimore’s Week 8 game against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: Ioane got in limited sessions on Thursday and Friday but was evasive when asked if he’d go at his locker yesterday. In the end, it would have been very impressive for him to play through a sprained MCL one week later. Ioane’s practice augurs well for his chances of playing in Week 10, at the very least. Week 9, on Thursday Night, might be too big of an ask.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: Roquan Smith (knee) and Vega Ioane (knee) returned to practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: Both players missed practice Wednesday, with their return Thursday a good step in the right direction for their availability in a marquee matchup against the Bills in Week 8. Quarterback Lamar Jackson and safety-linebacker Kyle Hamilton were also present at practice Thursday as the team inches closer to full strength.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: Ravens coach Jesse Minter said he is not ruling out Vega Ioane (knee) for Week 8 against the Bills yet.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: The Ravens’ mauling rookie guard suffered an MCL sprain in Week 7 against the Bengals. He is likely on the wrong side of questionable for Week 8, but Minter said he has been impressed by Ioane’s resilience and thinks he could recover quickly. In the meantime, OL Emery Jones Jr. and OT Andrew Vorhees will compete for the potential starting role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: Woody Marks cleared the NFL’s concussion protocol and will play in Week 12 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: Marks will return for No. 2 running back duties after a one-game absence. With zero teams on bye, Marks makes for a shaky FLEX option. He was unable to produce reliably while operating as the team’s starter, and should mostly be viewed as a bench stash at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: Woody Marks (concussion) resumed practicing on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: Texans reporter Aaron Wilson later added that Marks is expected to return for the team’s Week 12 game against the Ravens. That said, he is unlikely to reliably return FLEX value playing behind David Montgomery. Marks was unable to be a fantasy football difference-maker even when he was operating as the Texans’ starter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: Texans ruled out Woody Marks (concussion) for Week 11 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: David Montgomery (groin) is expected to return for tomorrow’s game. Emari Demercardo will serve as Montgomery’s backup. The Texans’ run game has been unable to establish itself as a reliable unit, but Montgomery’s workload and matchup against the Colts’ defense put him in the RB2 tier. The Texans face the Ravens in Week 12. Should Marks return to action, he will likely be relegated to PPR FLEX status.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: Woody Marks (concussion) did not practice on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: His ruleout on Wednesday is basically just a formality at this point. David Montgomery looks likely to lead the Texans backfield against the Colts on Thursday night. Marks should have a real chance to suit up for Week 12.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: Woody Marks (concussion) was listed as a “DNP” on Monday’s estimated practice report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: It is highly unlikely that Marks will clear concussion protocol on a short week, likely leaving Emari Demercado to split work with David Montgomery, the latter of whom was listed as a full participant as he aims to return from his own injury. Fantasy managers can consider Demercado a viable waiver target in a plus matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: Woody Marks (concussion evaluation) left Houston’s Week 10 game against the Browns and was ruled out.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: He was sandwiched between a pair of defenders on a third-quarter run and eventually walked off between trainers. Marks had 65 total yards before leaving, including one catch for 15 yards. With the short week ahead of them, the Texans will likely not have Marks available on Thursday night, leaving fantasy managers ignoring Emari Demercado and Dare Obungowale unless David Montgomery can play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: Woody Marks (knee) is not on Houston’s final Week 10 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: Marks was cleared after a full practice on Friday. Unfortunately, David Montgomery also got in a full practice and is questionable. Marks will retain RB2 status if Montgomery sits, but would probably go back in the FLEX bin if both are active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: Woody Marks (knee) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: Per Aaron Wilson, he injured the knee in Wednesday’s practice and was experiencing discomfort. We don’t necessarily think Marks is in major trouble yet considering “discomfort” isn’t exactly a major injury, and he has been remarkably durable in game. But there is certainly a chance he’ll miss Week 10’s game against the Browns and fantasy managers should be prepared to pivot on Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: Woody Marks (knee) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: Marks should be good to go for the Texans’ Week 10 game against the Browns, though this backfield is awfully banged up. Marks totaled 18 carries and four targets last week, and should again handle a sizable workload this week. Unfortunately, he has not proven to be an efficient player and may need to score a touchdown to return RB2 value.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: David Montgomery (groin) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: It looks like Montgomery will miss another game because of the groin issue. Woody Marks has been seeing all the work in his absence. The role has yet to produce a meaningful fantasy outing. Still, fantasy managers can’t afford to fade a player seeing the bulk of the touches in an ascending offense. Marks remains a frustrating RB2 for Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.headline: Commanders coach Dan Quinn said Brandon Aiyuk will not be elevated from the practice squad for Washington’s Week 12 game against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.analysis: No surprise or shame there — Aiyuk literally just signed on Wednesday. We are curious to see if he’ll be able to get active for Week 13, when the Commanders have a tasty matchup against the Jeffrey Simmons-less Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.headline: Commanders signed Brandon Aiyuk, formerly of the 49ers, to the practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.analysis: Aiyuk worked out for the Commanders earlier today and they didn’t let him leave the building without a deal. He’ll likely spend a week or two on the practice squad as he gets up to speed with the playbook before being elevated to the active roster. It’s anyone’s guess as to how much Aiyuk has left in the tank. He was struggling early in the 2024 season before suffering a season-ending ACL injury and hasn’t played a snap since. On the other hand, the Commanders need more firepower on offense with Terry McLaurin out for the season and Aiyuk played with Jayden Daniels at Arizona State. The floor is nonexistent, but Aiyuk is still worth adding in deeper fantasy formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.headline: NFL agent Drew Rosenhaus said Brandon Aiyuk is having “ongoing and positive” conversations with the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.analysis: Rosenhaus conceded there would “probably” be “no decision today” about Aiyuk joining the Washington roster. That Aiyuk did not sign with the Commanders following Wednesday’s meeting could be bearish for his chances of playing in 2026 at all. Recently released by the 49ers after protracted contract disagreements, Aiyuk would likely start as a rotational player if he eventually signs with Washington.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.headline: Free agent WR Brandon Aiyuk will visit the Commanders on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.analysis: Aiyuk’s last two days have gone pretty much exactly how you would have expected after the 49ers finally released him. He’ll likely sign with the Commanders practice squad officially tomorrow.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.headline: Brandon Aiyuk cleared waivers on Tuesday, making him a free agent.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.analysis: Nobody claimed his 49ers contract. Our next blurb on Aiyuk will probably read something like “Commanders signed WR Brandon Aiyuk,” but until then we’re legally obligated to note that Adam Schefter reported he is expected to draw interest from “a few teams.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Commanders are Brandon Aiyuk’s “most likely” landing spot.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.analysis: The ink on the release wasn’t even given time to dry before Aiyuk was connected to the same team he was connected to all offseason. He’ll likely wind up with a spot on the Commanders practice squad. Given the lengthy layoff, we probably don’t need to imagine Aiyuk suiting up in Week 12 as a destined outcome, but it could be sooner rather than later.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.headline: 49ers released WR Brandon Aiyuk.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.analysis: Took them long enough, you might say before you were pedanted by those who would tell you things like “Aiyuk had to report to actually be released.” It should be noted that Aiyuk must clear waivers since this is after the trade deadline, but nobody is expected to assume his contract. Anyway, Aiyuk will be free to pursue free agency and it sounds like we have another blurb to write about that almost instantly, funny how that works. The 28-year-old will look to continue his career elsewhere, perhaps somewhere in the greater Washington D.C. area.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.headline: NFL insider Dianna Russini reports Brandon Aiyuk passed the 49ers’ physical.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.analysis: “He’s 100% healthy right now, in shape, and working out full force,” Drew Rosenhaus, Aiyuk’s agent, told Russini. Passing the team’s physical was a key step in the two sides parting ways after years of conflict. Aiyuk reportedly hopes to sign with another team once the 49ers release him. Whether that happens in the coming weeks is anyone’s guess. Aiyuk had been linked to the Commanders in the summer before a series of questionable social media posts from Aiyuk squelched those rumors.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.headline: The NFL reinstated 49ers WR Brandon Aiyuk from the reserve/left squad list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.analysis: According to The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero, the NFL has granted the 49ers a two-week roster exemption for Aiyuk as the two sides continue to negotiate his impending release. The 49ers will have until November 23rd to make a roster move, but once released, Aiyuk will be free to sign with any team. The 28-year-old receiver last played in 2024 and hasn’t taken a snap since tearing his ACL in Week 7 of that season. While there is a chance Aiyuk could suit up for a new team at some point this season, fantasy managers hoping to stash him shouldn’t expect anything meaningful until the fantasy playoffs at the earliest, as it could take him several weeks to find a new team and get up to speed with the season more than halfway over.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Commanders “haven’t completely abandoned” the idea of acquiring WR Brandon Aiyuk.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-ai.analysis: Aiyuk was rumored to end up in Washington all offseason and there seemingly could still be a fit there with Terry McLaurin out for the season. However, this report suggests the Commanders haven’t completely ruled it out rather than this being something they’re actively pursuing. Aiyuk met with 49ers brass Friday, though a resolution proved elusive. This saga is far from over.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.headline: ESPN’s Todd Archer reports Jake Ferguson has partial tears in his MCL and PCL.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.analysis: That explains why Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said Ferguson would likely be out “multiple weeks” after injuring his knee in Week 9 against the Colts. We haven’t had an official update in a while, but the Cowboys are on bye in Week 14. Perhaps a Week 15 return is possible.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.headline: Cowboys declared TE Jake Ferguson, RG Tyler Booker, WR Jonathan Mingo, S P.J. Locke, DT Jonathan Bullard and LB Jaishawn Barham inactive for Week 12 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.analysis: Ferguson will miss another game with knee and ankle injuries. Brevyn Spann-Ford is a touchdown-dependent fantasy TE2 in his stead. Ryan Flournoy will likely beneift from Ferguson’s absence. Losing Booker, the Cowboys’ starting right guard, for this one is unfortunate.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.headline: Jake Ferguson (ankle/knee) will not play in Week 12 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.analysis: Ferguson failed to practice at any point this week and will miss his second straight game. Brevyn Spann-Ford will be the next man up versus Philly. He caught both of his targets for five yards and a touchdown last week. “BSF” will be a touchdown-or-bust TE2 for Week 12.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.headline: Jake Ferguson (ankle/knee) did not practice on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.analysis: He will almost certainly miss the Thanksgiving game against the Eagles after two more missed practices. It is perhaps feasible he could return for Week 13, which would be his fourth week since suffering this new knee injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.headline: Jake Ferguson was listed as a “DNP” on the estimated practice report Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.analysis: Even though the team held a walkthrough ahead of their Thanksgiving matchup against the Eagles, the fact that Ferguson has yet to practice after injuring his ankle two weeks ago spells trouble for his potential availability in Week 12. Brevyn Spann-Ford and Luke Schoonmaker appear to be looking at another game atop the depth chart, with volume through the air most likely to concentrate further on CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.headline: Cowboys declared TE Jake Ferguson, OG Tyler Booker, S P.J. Locke, WR Jonathan Mingo, LB Jaishawn Barham and DT Jonathan Bullard inactive for Week 11 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.analysis: Ferguson has barely played since Week 7. Although he is merely week to week with his ankle and knee issues, the formerly fantasy relevant seam stretcher seems unlikely to be a 12-team league factor down the stretch.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.headline: Jake Ferguson (ankle/knee) will not play in Dallas’ Week 11 game against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.analysis: Ferguson has now missed two weeks with this injury and has not practiced at all in the interim, leaving his status for a short turnaround Week 12 highly questionable. It is wheels up in the TE2 ranks for Brevyn Spann-Ford.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.headline: Jake Ferguson (ankle/knee) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.analysis: Last Monday, Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer told reporters that Ferguson would likely miss “multiple weeks.” We do not expect him to play in Week 11 against the Titans. Check back on Friday for an official update.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.headline: Cowboys ruled out Jake Ferguson (knee/ankle) for Week 10 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.analysis: This was the expected outcome. Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer told reporters on Monday that Ferguson will likely be out for “multiple weeks” after suffering a knee injury. He was already dealing with an ankle injury when it happened. Ferguson does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.headline: Jake Ferguson (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.analysis: No surprises here as Ferguson is expected to miss multiple weeks, according to Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer. Ferguson was barely putting up TE2 numbers when healthy, so we’re not expecting much from Brevyn Spann-Ford as the next man up. Fantasy managers should aim higher on the waiver wire this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cole-holco.headline: Cole Holcomb (heel) will not play in the Steelers’ Week 12 game against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cole-holco.analysis: Holcomb was the only player listed as questionable entering the weekend, but the team has opted to sit him for this one after he suffered a heel injury in the previous week’s loss to the Eagles. In addition to Holcomb, the Steelers also declared WR Kaden Weten, QB Drew Allar, CB Sean Murphy-Bunting, RB Eli Heidenreich, LB Alex Highsmith, and DT Gabe Rubio inactive for this week. Will Howard will serve as the backup for starting QB Mason Rudolph.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cole-holco.headline: Nick Herbig (hip/ribs) is not on the final injury report and will play in Week 12 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cole-holco.analysis: Herbig is good to go. Steelers LB Alex Highsmith (ankle) and OG Gennings Dunker (knee) are ruled out. Steelers LB Cole Holcomb (heel) is questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cole-holco.headline: Steelers re-signed LB Cole Holcomb to a two-year, $5 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cole-holco.analysis: After missing all of 2024 due to a devastating knee injury he suffered in 2023, Holcomb returned in 2025 to play in 14 games for the Steelers. The veteran linebacker made three starts over that span and totaled 37 tackles and one forced fumble while playing on 198 defensive snaps. Holcomb also turned into a contributor on special teams last season, playing on the most special teams snaps (161) since his rookie year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cole-holco.headline: Steelers EDGE Alex Highsmith (pectoral) will not play in Pittsburgh’s Week 11 game against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cole-holco.analysis: Also ruled out on Pittsburgh’s defense are CB Darius Slay (concussion) and LB Cole Holcomb (illness), Highsmith had said he was optimistic about playing but the Steelers opted to hold their pass rusher out. These rule-outs are good news for Cincinnati’s offense in what projects to be a shootout on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cole-holco.headline: NFL Network’s Tom Pelissero reports the Steelers restructured LB Cole Holcomb’s contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cole-holco.analysis: According to Pelissero, the move will free up $4 million in cap space for the Steelers. Holcomb suffered a brutal dislocated knee injury in 2023 and did not take a snap last season. The sixth-year linebacker totaled 54 tackles and four TFLs in the eight games he appeared in back in 2023, and is expected to be fully healthy for the start of next season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cole-holco.headline: Steelers placed LB Cole Holcomb (knee) on the active/PUP list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cole-holco.analysis: Holcomb suffered a devastating knee injury in Week 9 of last season, ending his 2023 campaign. It’s no surprise to see him open camp on the PUP list, given the nature of his injury, but we don’t have a firm timeline on when we can expect him to return. Speaking earlier in the week, head coach Mike Tomlin said he thinks Holcomb will participate in camp sooner than later, leaving the door open for a return in a few weeks. In addition to Holcomb, the Steelers also placed EDGE Dean Lowry, whose 2023 was ended by a pectoral injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cole-holco.headline: Steelers LB Cole Holcomb will undergo knee surgery and has been ruled out for the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cole-holco.analysis: Holcomb suffered a gruesome knee injury in the Steelers’ Week 9 win over the Steelers after colliding with a teammate in the middle of the field. The veteran linebacker was kept in a hospital over night out of precaution, but has since been discharged. He’ll undergo surgery in the coming days, but his 2023 season is officially over after eight games. A free agent signing by the Steelers earlier this offseason, Holcomb has totaled 54 tackles, four TFLs, and two forced fumbles and will be sorely missed as a leader of the defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cole-holco.headline: Steelers LB Cole Holcomb (knee) was carted off the field in the first quarter of Week 9 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cole-holco.analysis: Holcomb appeared to collide with a teammate while attempted to make a tackle on Titans wide receiver DeAndre Hopkins over the middle of the field. The injury was of the “let’s not show that again” variety, meaning Holcomb is likely looking at an extended absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cole-holco.headline: Steelers signed LB Cole Holcomb, formerly of the Commanders, to a three-year, $18 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cole-holco.analysis: Holcomb, 26, has started 48 games for Washington over the past four seasons. His career year came in 2021, when Holcomb recorded 145 tackles. He has 4.5 sacks in his NFL career and will join a Steelers defensive making free agency moves to improve for 2023 and beyond.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cole-holco.headline: Commanders declared LB Cole Holcomb, CB Rachad Wildgoose, LB David Mayo and G Chris Paul inactive for Week 11 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cole-holco.analysis: The Commanders come into this game with a relatively healthy roster. Nothing too surprising to see here, as all key fantasy assets appear good to go against the Texans

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-ehling.headline: Broncos declared QB Sam Ehlinger, WR Lil’Jordan Humphrey S Taylor Rapp, OL Gavin Ortega, OL Kage Casey, and TE Dallen Bentley inactive for Week 12 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-ehling.analysis: The Broncos will be operating at close to full strength against the Steelers in a game that could feature some inclement weather and low temperatures. Rookie running back Jonah Coleman could be in line for a busy day, with J.K. Dobbins suspended by the team for this week. Coleman rushed 24 times for 111 yards and three touchdowns in last week’s win over the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-ehling.headline: Broncos declared S Talanoa Hufanga, CB Kris Abrams-Draine, S Brandon Jones, WR Lil’Jordan Humphrey, OG Kage Casey, TE Dallen Bentley, and QB Sam Ehlinger inactive for Week 9 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-ehling.analysis: Hufanga was questionable entering the weekend due to an ankle injury, but will officially be sidelined for this one. The 28-year-old safety hasn’t played since Week 5 but was limited in back-to-back practices to close out the week, so there’s a chance he could return after the Broncos’ Week 10 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-ehling.headline: The Denver Post’s Parker Gabriel believes Sam Ehlinger could beat out Jarrett Stidham for Denver’s backup quarterback job.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-ehling.analysis: He projects Ehlinger to win the job, too. “The notion that Ehlinger could beat him out is not rooted in Stidham’s performance in the AFC title game,” Gabriel writes, "...but rather just in the staff’s excitement about Ehlinger a year ago, his mobility and a potential jump in performance in his second summer with the Broncos.” First the NFL hands us a Joe Milton-Sam Howell backup battle, now this? Premium July entertainment. Neither player has any real upside, though whoever wins the job could argue for Sean Payton-based superflex QB2 consideration in a good matchup should Bo Nix miss time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-ehling.headline: Broncos re-signed QB Sam Ehlinger to a one-year, $2 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-ehling.analysis: Ehlinger signed with the Broncos last offseason but didn’t make their final roster. He chose to stay on the team’s practice squad despite receiving 53-man roster offers from other teams. He bounced between the practice squad and the active roster throughout the year. With teams reportedly calling Denver about Jarrett Stidham, the Broncos are keeping Ehlinger around as a potential QB2 option should they choose to move their current backup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-ehling.headline: Broncos declared QB Sam Ehlinger, TE Caleb Lohner, WR Elijah Moore, ILB Karene Reid, CB Reese Taylor, OLB Que Robinson, and DL Sai’Vion Jones inactive for the Divisional Round against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-ehling.analysis: The Broncos begin their path to the Super Bowl as one of the healthier teams in the league after their Wild Card bye as the No. 1 seed in the AFC, enough so that they appear to have elevated two practice squad members, Elijah Moore and Caleb Lohner, to receive a small roster bonus as thanks for their time on the practice squad this season. The home-favorite Broncos face a difficult challenge against the Josh Allen-led Bills as they aim to avoid the same postseason outcome as in 2024 when the Bills bounced the Broncos in a blowout loss.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-ehling.headline: Broncos signed QB Sam Ehlinger to the 53-man roster.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-ehling.analysis: Ehlinger was not elevated for Week 18 while still having one standard elevation remaining, but will now head into the postseason a member of the 53-man, game-day roster. It’ll give the Broncos additional maneuverability during what they hope is a long playoff run as the No. 1 seed in the AFC. The veteran backup chose not to sign with the Colts following the injury to Daniel Jones and was reported to have had discussions with the Broncos regarding their plans moving forward. “We’ve talked about some things for the playoffs,” Ehlinger said ahead of Week 18, hinting at the move made official Monday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-ehling.headline: Broncos signed QB Sam Ehlinger off the practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-ehling.analysis: Ehlinger will not be active for Week 16 against the Jaguars, but the quarterback will get a nicer paycheck will operating as the emergency signal-caller going forward. The 27-year-old was offered a chance to join the Colts’ active roster after the Daniel Jones’ injury, but he declined and chose to stick with Denver. One can’t help but think this is a reward for his loyalty.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-ehling.headline: The Denver Post’s Parker Gabriel reports Broncos QB Sam Ehlinger declined the Colts’ offer to sign him to their active roster.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-ehling.analysis: Ehlinger was originally drafted by the Colts and spent four seasons with the team. He told The Denver Post that he and his agent talked to the Colts for two days before turning down the offer and sticking with the Broncos’ practice squad. The Colts were going for familiarity to fill their quarterback role by trying to get Ehlinger while also getting Philip Rivers. Ehlinger chooses to stay with the Broncos, where he is the third quarterback behind Bo Nix and Jarrett Stidham.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-ehling.headline: Broncos signed QB Sam Ehlinger to the active roster.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-ehling.analysis: Ehlinger has bounced between the active roster and practice squad for the Broncos to start the season. He was briefly released and brought back to the practice squad last week and is now back on the active roster. Ehlinger will continue to sit behind Bo Nix and Jarrett Stidham amidst the Broncos’ roster management ping-ponging his roster status.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-ehling.headline: Broncos released QB Sam Ehlinger.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-ehling.analysis: Ehlinger was released from the team before being re-signed to the practice squad back in August, and later promoted to the active roster. He is expected to be re-signed to the practice squad again shortly, though he is free to pursue employment elsewhere. The Broncos recently activated LB Dre Greenlaw (quad) from injured reserve. Ehlinger’s release was likely done to create space for him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Zachariah Branch (hamstring) will not play in Atlanta’s Week 12 game against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: Branch has now been sidelined each of the last four weeks, missing Week 9 and 10 before their Week 11 bye, and did not practice at any point this week. If only there were some sort of “injured reserve” list for players who weren’t close to playing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Jahan Dotson (hamstring) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: Dotson and Zachariah Branch (hamstring) both missed Wednesday’s practice. Dotson is not relevant in 12-team leagues, and Branch has earned just 12 targets this season. Neither player is consequential.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Falcons declared WR Zachariah Branch, QB Andy Dalton, LB Divine Deablo, CB Avieon Terrell WR, QB Jack Strand, CB Robert Longerbeam and OL Cameron Williams inactive for Week 10 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: It has been a disappointing rookie season for third-rounder Branch, who seemed like he might be in line for some first-year targets. Instead he has under 100 yards receiving and is now injured. A first-year washout like this makes Branch something of a dicey long-term prospect in Dynasty leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Zachariah Branch (hamstring) will not play in Atlanta’s Week 10 game against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: He didn’t practice all week and enters Atlanta’s Week 11 bye off two completely lost weeks. The rookie hasn’t made much of an impact so far and doesn’t necessarily need to be kept on rosters in non-dynasty leagues at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Zachariah Branch (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: He was instantly ruled out ahead of Atlanta’s date in Madrid last Monday and has not practiced since. With the bye on tap in Week 11, we’d expect Branch to sit against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Zachariah Branch (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: Branch suffered the hamstring injury in Week 8 and missed last week’s game because of it. He appears to be on pace to miss another game. With just 10 catches to his name after nearly as many weeks, 2026 is shaping up to be an underwhelming start to Branch’s career.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Brian Robinson (hamstring) is questionable for the Falcons’ Week 9 game against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: Robinson was briefly listed as questionable only for head coach Kevin Stefanski to rule him out shortly after the initial report. Robinson was limited in practice throughout the week, but the Falcons are opting to play it safe, likely hoping another week on the sidelines will lower the chances of re-injury. Rookie WR Zachariah Branch (hamstring) has also been ruled out for the game after picking up an injury in last week’s loss to the Buccaneers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski said Zachariah Branch (hamstring) will not play in Week 9 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: Branch suffered a hamstring injury in Week 8’s shutout loss to the Buccaneers and will miss next week’s game against the Bengals in Madrid. The rookie third-rounder has caught just 10 passes for 64 scoreless yards this season and has also served as the Falcons’ primary kick and punt returner.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Zachariah Branch caught 1-of-2 targets for nine yards in the Falcons’ Week 7 win over the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: It seemed like Branch would be in for a bigger role in Week 7 with Olamide Zaccheaus out with a shoulder injury. However, Branch ran a route on just 18 of 37 dropbacks and was only targeted twice. It doesn’t seem like he’s anywhere close to playing a large enough role for fantasy value and doesn’t need to be held through the bye weeks in redraft leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Falcons declared WR Olamide Zaccheaus, QB Jack Strand, QB Andy Dalton, RB Brian Robinson Jr., LB Divine Deablo, CB Avieon Terrell, and DB Billy Bowman Jr. inactive for Week 7 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring) was ruled out earlier in the week, and Zaccheaus is dealing with a shoulder injury and will not be able to suit up for this one. That could mean more work in the receiving game for rookie Zachariah Branch, who might be worth a stash in deeper formats in case a solid game today earns him a bigger role moving forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson (hamstring) won’t play in Atlanta’s Week 12 game against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Olmaide Zachcheaus will be Atlanta’s No. 2 receiver behind Drake London, and after that it turns to Chris Blair and Beaux Collins with Zachariah Branch also hurt. This will likely be a situation that forces the Falcons to condense the target tree and throw at their main three of Drake London, Bijan Robinson, and Kyle Pitts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Dotson does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues, nor does rookie Zachariah Branch (hamstring). The Falcons’ pass-catching corps is fairly condensed at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson (hamstring) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Dotson and Zachariah Branch (hamstring) both missed Wednesday’s practice. Dotson is not relevant in 12-team leagues, and Branch has earned just 12 targets this season. Neither player is consequential.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 3-of-6 targets for 63 yards in the Falcons’ Week 10 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Although this was only Dotson’s second three-catch performance of the season, this has rather amazingly become something of his weekly statline. Not that it is amounting to anything in fantasy football. It definitely won’t when the Falcons come off bye to face the Vikings in Week 12. Dotson can remain firmly affixed to 12-team league waiver wires.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 2-of-2 targets for 16 yards in the Falcons’ Week 9 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: The Falcons passing attack was a mess against the Bengals in Week 9. Michael Penix threw 31 times, but for just 162 yards. Dotson was a non-factor by product, totaling just 16 yards on two receptions. He’s Atlanta’s WR2, but is merely a WR5/6 heading into Week 10 against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 2-of-5 targets for 95 yards in the Falcons’ Week 8 loss to the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: The bulk of Dotson’s production came on a single, 76-yard gain in the fourth quarter. Michael Penix lobbed him a ball on the boundary and two Bucs defensive backs collided, leaving Dotson uncovered with room to run. He bolted down the sideline but didn’t have the speed to take it to the house. That play alone accounted for over half of Penix’s passing output. Dotson has made the occasional splash play while running as Atlanta’s WR2, but his fantasy prospects are not that intriguing headed into Week 9. He will be in the WR5/6 range when the Falcons take on the Bengals next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 1-of-3 targets for six yards in the Falcons’ Week 7 win over the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Dotson was also targeted on three different deep passes that resulted in San Francisco penalties. That doesn’t help your fantasy team, but it is indicative of his role in this offense. Dotson did run the second-most routes of any receiver on the Falcons; however, he is really only targeted on deep shots down the field, which will make his production inconsistent.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 3-of-5 targets for 87 yards and a touchdown in the Falcons’ Week 6 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Dotson, whose season-high yardage coming into the week was 54 — his total in both of the past two weeks — got loose a couple times in this one, mostly when the Falcons ditched their usual run-heavy offense in favor of a fast-pace pass-heavy approach while facing a multiple touchdown second half deficit. Running a route on 32 of the Falcons’ 38 drop backs, Dotson led the team in receiving yards thanks largely to a 41-yard grab. Dotson could be a deep league play in Week 7 against the Niners.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 2-of-4 targets for 54 yards in the Falcons’ Week 5 loss to the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Dotson’s 54 yards finished second on the team behind alpha Drake London but his four targets finished behind London, Kyle Pitts, and Bijan Robinson. His status as the starting wide receiver opposite London likely means little in the wake of modest volume games that continue to stack up. He can safely be left on, or returned to, the waiver wire.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 2-of-3 targets for 54 yards and a touchdown in the Falcons’ Week 4 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Dotson continues to operate as the team’s WR2 opposite Drake London but remains unlikely to return consistent fantasy production in an offense heavily concentrated on its top two options in London and Bijan Robinson. Dotson’s touchdown came in the fourth quarter with the team cruising, pushing the lead to 21 points with under 10 minutes to play. Fantasy managers can safely keep Dotson on the bench ahead of a Week 5 meeting with the Ravens in Atlanta.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston (quad) is questionable for the Browns’ Week 12 game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: According to Cabot, Boston was a DNP all week but still managed to draw the questionable tag. Given his week’s worth of DNPs, it’s hard to imagine the rookie suiting up on Sunday night, but it sounds like the Browns will give him some additional time to try and heal up before ruling him out. Fantasy managers planning to hold out until a decision is made would be wise to stash Jerry Jeudy or another player from Sunday or Monday night’s games as a pivot off Boston in the event he is ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston (quad) was listed as a non-participant for Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: That’s back-to-back missed practices for Boston. The 22-year-old still could be a go for Week 12 against the Raiders, but he’ll need to get in at least a limited session, and he doesn’t provide a ton of fantasy upside even if he does play for that matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston (quad) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: Boston continues to rack up lower-body injuries, though he tends to play through them. He dealt with a toe injury last week, catching just one pass for 16 yards. His practice participation is worth tracking closely this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston (toe) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: Boston was held out of the first two practices of Week 11 with the toe issue. He got in a limited session on Friday and played through a questionable tag on Sunday. It’s possible he gets a similar practice regimen this week. Even if he is active again, Boston will be a risky option for fantasy managers. He caught one pass for 16 yards last week and only earned two targets. It’s possible the toe issue is turning him into more of a decoy than a true downfield threat. KC Concepcion would be in line for more work if Boston can’t play at all this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston caught 1-of-2 targets for 16 yards in Cleveland’s Week 10 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: He did manage some good punt returns, but the Browns weren’t able to get their deep-ball offense going and mostly let Derek Stingley take Boston out of the game. Boston isn’t necessarily a must-hold through shallow leagues at the bye, as he’s been held under 50 yards in five of his last six games, but the target count has been stronger than this dud generally, and he was likely playing hurt here.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston (toe) is active for Cleveland’s Week 10 game against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: He got in just one practice and was spotted in a boot at times before being dubbed questionable, but will be a reasonable WR3 play against a Texans defense missing a few pieces. Inactive for the Browns are S Ronnie Hickman (concussion), C Parker Brailsford, QB Dillon Gabriel (third quarterback), QB Taylen Green, CB Noah Ignioghene and LB Justin Jefferson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Denzel Boston (toe) is expected to play in Week 10 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: Boston will likely go through a workout in the morning to determine his status, but he appears to be on the right side of questionable for now. He was held out of the Browns’ first two practices of the week before getting in a limited session on Friday. Barring a setback ahead of kickoff, Boston is back in the WR3 mix for Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston (toe) is questionable for Cleveland’s Week 10 game against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: He made it back on to the practice field on Friday, so he’s probably on the optimistic side of questionable at this point. Todd Monken did say at his Friday presser that Boston is “trending in the right direction.” Boston did miss the first two sessions of the week but has been no stranger to the injury report this year and has tended to gut it out. Boston was seen wearing a walking boot as he left the locker room. He still has a chance to play, but his status is worth monitoring closely.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston (toe) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: This morning, Boston told reporters that he was hoping to resume practicing today. Unfortunately, he was unable to do so. That said, Boston’s toe injury is feeling better and things are “trending up” at the moment. It sounds like the rookie wide receiver has a chance to play in Week 10 against the Texans and would be a WR3/FLEX if so.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston (toe) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: Boston continues to pick up lower-leg injuries, but last week’s calf issue did not slow him down. The Browns have begun varying Boston’s usage, no longer limiting him to high-variance downfield work. Adding short-to-intermediate opportunities only enhances his outlook. If he can play this weekend, he will be a WR3/FLEX.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/romeo-doub.headline: Patriots coach Mike Vrabel said he “wouldn’t anticipate” Romeo Doubs (shoulder) being ready for action yet.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/romeo-doub.analysis: Doubs was limited in each of the first two practices this week, and we’re guessing he won’t do better than that today based on this statement. Most players on IR will get a questionable tag on their chances to return regardless of the surrounding data, but we’d be surprised if Doubs didn’t sit this week based on what his coach said.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/romeo-doub.headline: Romeo Doubs (shoulder) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/romeo-doub.analysis: Doubs has a chance to return this week, in time to face the Chargers, but he is still in the questionable column. If he upgrades tomorrow, he should be good to go. Doubs would theoretically be the Patriots’ No. 1 wide receiver, but this situation is shaky. He can be stashed in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/romeo-doub.headline: Romeo Doubs (shoulder) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/romeo-doub.analysis: Doubs (shoulder) was listed as limited on the Patriots’ Wednesday practice report, indicating his 21-day practice window is now open for him to return from injured reserve. With A.J. Brown dealing with a hamstring issue, Doubs’ return will boost the wide receiver group, though a lack of Drake Maye will keep Doubs out of fantasy lineups when he returns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/romeo-doub.headline: Patriots placed Romeo Doubs (shoulder) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/romeo-doub.analysis: Doubs was ruled out in the third quarter of Week 6’s win over the Jets and will now miss at least the next four games. With the Patriots’ bye not coming until Week 11, the earliest Doubs will be able to return to the field will be in Week 12 against the Chargers. Doubs has caught 14 passes for 261 yards and three touchdowns this season and has been targeted more than four times in just one game. Doubs can be dropped in leagues that don’t allow players to be stashed on IR.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/romeo-doub.headline: Romeo Doubs injured his shoulder in the Patriots’ Week 6 game against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/romeo-doub.analysis: Initially deemed questionable, Doubs was ruled out in the third quarter. Doubs landed hard on his shoulder on his first target, which just happened to be a 42-yard touchdown where he broke free along the back line of the defense. Most unfortunate, though he at least tallied the score first. Doubs was evaluated in the blue tent before heading to the locker room. It’s bad news for the Pats and fantasy managers, but at least comes as A.J. Brown is back in the lineup for the first time in five weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/romeo-doub.headline: Romeo Doubs caught 1-of-3 targets for 16 yards in the Patriots’ Week 5 win against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/romeo-doub.analysis: Drake Maye carved up the Vegas secondary to the tune of 376 yards and four touchdowns, with almost none of it going to be nominal No. 1 wideout. Doubs, who last week against the Bills had 58 yards and two touchdowns, nearly came down with a short touchdown grab in the third quarter on a nice touch throw from Maye. The potential return of A.J. Brown (ankle) in Week 6 against the Jets could limit Doubs’ targets going forward. With Maye cooking, Doubs remains a potential flex option in 14-team formats going forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/romeo-doub.headline: Romeo Doubs caught 6-of-9 targets for 58 yards and two touchdowns in the Patriots’ Week 4 win over the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/romeo-doub.analysis: Doubs simply beat Bills cornerback Maxwell Hairston all game long. He seemed to be open at will and almost had a bigger day when he failed to haul in a 40+ yard pass that went off his hands on a diving attempt in the fourth quarter. With Mack Hollins (calf) getting hurt in the first half, Doubs played on 47 of the team’s 70 snaps and ran a route on 30 of their 43 dropbacks, the most of any receiver on the team. It seems that Doubs is finally starting to click with Drake Maye, and now that Hollins is out and A.J. Brown (ankle) is still not ready to come back, Doubs could be in for a big role against the Raiders next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/romeo-doub.headline: Romeo Doubs caught 3-of-4 targets for 49 yards in the Patriots’ Week 3 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/romeo-doub.analysis: Doubs was again an every-down player and finished second behind Mack Hollins in receiving yards. Doubs continues to be an afterthought in the New England offense, even with A.J. Brown out with a severe ankle injury. Through three games Doubs now has just six catches in the low-wattage Pats offense. He’ll be a deep league option in Week 4 against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/romeo-doub.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports A.J. Brown (ankle) is expected to miss 6-8 weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/romeo-doub.analysis: Schefter and other reporters previously called it a 4-6 week injury, which now seems unlikely. Schefter did add that Brown is moving “pretty well” and could come back on the faster side of his updated timeline. Still, it looks like Brown will miss at least half of the regular season. Romeo Doubs will operate as the team’s No. 1 receiver until he returns, though it will likely be a group effort to replace Browns’ production. Mack Hollins and Demario Douglas will also be more involved.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/romeo-doub.headline: Romeo Doubs caught 3-of-4 targets for 96 yards in the Patriots’ Week 2 win over the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/romeo-doub.analysis: Doubs followed up a rough Week 1 with a productive Week 2, leading the Patriots wideouts in targets, receptions, and yards. With A.J. Brown out, Doubs started and tallied the second-most snaps among Pats wide receivers for the day. The bulk of his yardage came from a pair of third-quarter chunk gains, catching a 29-yard pass early in the quarter and breaking free for a 63-yard gain later in the quarter. Between Drake Maye’s early season struggles and a spread-the-wealth approach in the passing game, the Patriots receivers’ ceilings are capped. Doubs looks like the best pass-catching option and will be firmly in the WR4 ranks for Week 3 against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deion-burk.headline: Jaguars coach Liam Coen said Parker Washington’s injury is “a big opportunity” for Josh Cameron.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deion-burk.analysis: You may have been thinking that Washington’s injury would create BTJ szn, but Coen singled out Cameron when asked about him, saying he’s “been trending. He’s made a lot of plays for this offense and for this team ... Trevor trusts him.” Cameron suddenly surfaces on the FLEX line as an expected Jaguars No. 2 target behind Jakobi Meyers against the Titans on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deion-burk.headline: Josh Cameron caught 3-of-7 targets for 44 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 11 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deion-burk.analysis: Cameron ran only 22 routes on 56 Jacksonville drop backs but was second behind only Parker Washington (12) in targets. Cameron will be a borderline fantasy option next week against a terrible Titans secondary. Cameron had 67 yards on three catches against Tennessee in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deion-burk.headline: Josh Cameron caught all three of his targets for 67 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 10 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deion-burk.analysis: Cameron was on the receiving end of a pair of deep shots from Trevor Lawrence. The first was a long contested catch on the boundary and the second was a layup touchdown. Cameron was completely uncovered for a 25-yard touchdown strike. It was his third score of the year. Cameron is a better real-life player than a fantasy option, but he’ll at least be on the radar as a high-risk FLEX play for Week 11 against the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deion-burk.headline: Jaguars coach Liam Coen said Brian Thomas Jr. played only 23 snaps in Week 3 because the Jaguars “were playing in a little bit more 12 and also some of the things that we had Josh [Cameron] on specifically were things that we felt good about him doing within a role that he has.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deion-burk.analysis: Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley believes that Cameron’s usage (23 snaps) could make it “stand[s] to reason Thomas could quickly become the fourth option instead” in a column that says he believes a “new start would be best for both parties.” It sounds like there’s a non-zero chance that Thomas is on the trade block at the deadline, as weird as that seems given how good the Jaguars have been on offense. Thomas isn’t necessarily someone who has to be rostered in shallow leagues given how things are trending.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deion-burk.headline: Josh Cameron caught his lone target for 13 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 3 win against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deion-burk.analysis: He caught one of Trevor Lawrence’s three touchdown throws on the day. Cameron has begun to eat into Brian Thomas Jr.'s snap share. Against the Patriots Cameron logged ten routes to 16 routes for Thomas while Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers each ran 31 routes. If the Jaguars part ways with Thomas in the coming weeks, Cameron would likely step into a bigger role in the potent Jags passing attack.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deion-burk.headline: Josh Cameron caught 2-of-2 targets for 20 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 1 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deion-burk.analysis: Cameron was thought to be buried on the Jaguars depth chart as a rookie, but Liam Coen found opportunities for him in Week 1 nevertheless. He caught a touchdown pass in the first half and saw increased snaps with Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) exiting the game briefly in the first half. Despite the touchdown, fantasy managers still should not expect Cameron to get fantasy-relevant opportunities unless one of the Jaguars’ top three wide receivers are injured.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deion-burk.headline: Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley believes WR Josh Cameron would be the fill-in starter if a Jaguars starting wide receiver misses time.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deion-burk.analysis: This might not matter, but it is worth noting. The Florida Times-Union recently reported that Jaguars WR Jakobi Meyers ( thumb ) is sidelined, as is WR Brian Thomas (shoulder). Both picked up minor injuries recently, but according to Shipley, the team does not “seem overly concerned” about either issue. Cameron and fellow sixth-round rookie WR CJ Williams have had good training camps. Cameron is evidently the name to know for waiver wire purposes in-season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deion-burk.headline: Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley believes Jaguars WR Josh Cameron “has the size and traits to work his way into the outside receiver rotation sooner rather than later.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deion-burk.analysis: Cameron injured his ankle during the draft process, so he only recently began practicing with his new teammates. He participated in special teams drills last week and made his offense debut today, on Tuesday, at mandatory minicamp. Per Shipley, Cameron arguably had the best day of any receiver. The Jaguars’ wide receiver corps is very deep, so it is tough to see how Cameron could become a meaningful contributor in year one. He is probably worth adding in dynasty formats, though. Keep an eye on him this summer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deion-burk.headline: Jaguars selected Baylor WR Josh Cameron with the No. 191 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deion-burk.analysis: With a bulky frame, Cameron (6’1/220) profiles best as a physical, contested-catch receiver. He started almost exclusively on the outside at Baylor, operating as the Bears’ No. 1 wideout his last two seasons. Totaling 19 touchdowns over that span, Cameron also led the Big 12 with 5.8 receptions per game in 2025. Cameron lacks the burst and route-running skills to separate consistently and is not a yards-after-catch player. However, he possesses good ball skills, rarely tallying drops while his physical presence often bullied college cornerbacks. The Athletic’s Dane Brugler also notes Cameron is a “competitive blocker and can be an asset in the run game.” An NFL team can build upon Cameron’s physical toolset to develop him as a blocker and big-bodied receiver at the next level.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said he had no update on Jeremiyah Love (ankle/IR) and would know more on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: Love is eligible to come off injured reserve after this Sunday, but the fact that LaFleur won’t have a real update until Wednesday is probably foreshadowing that it will be at least another week. Love picked up a high-ankle sprain against the Cowboys in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Cardinals placed Jeremiyah Love (ankle) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: The new injury Love picked up in Week 8’s win over the Cowboys has been diagnosed as a high-ankle sprain and will sideline Love for a minimum of four weeks. Love, who has been dealing with multiple ankle injuries this season, has had a tough start to his NFL career. In six career games he’s rushed for 268 yards and one touchdown on 76 carries, while adding 11 receptions for 36 yards and another score. His injury comes as Bam Knight is in the league’s concussion protocol, leaving Tyler Allgeier and Evan Hull as the only two healthy backs on the Cardinals’ 53-man roster. Allgeier could be in line for a significant role in Week 9 against the Seahawks if Knight is unable to clear protocol, and veteran Jerome Ford could also be promoted from the practice squad in the coming days. Love will not be eligible to return until Week 13 against the Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Jeremiyah Love is dealing with a new ankle injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: According to LaFleur, the injury is to “a new portion of the ankle” that Love hadn’t previously injured. LaFleur didn’t dismiss the possibility of Love being placed on injured reserve, suggesting he would wait until Wednesday to decide if that is on the table. A tough rookie season only gets tougher for Love, who sounds like he will be at risk of missing more time even if he isn’t an IR candidate. Meanwhile, Bam Knight, who left Week 8’s game with a concussion, is in the league’s protocol, making Tyler Allgeier the only healthy back on the roster entering Week 9 against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) left Arizona’s Week 8 game against the Cowboys and is questionable to return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: His right ankle was rolled up on at the end of a running play and Love immediately slammed his helmet after walking off. He later went to the locker room with trainers and then was officially dubbed questionable. Not great. Love finished with nine carries for 23 yards, including a fourth-and-1 go at the goalline that he didn’t convert. We’ll see what reports say after the game but given Love has already missed time with ankle injuries this year, it’s hard to be optimistic about his status for next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Jeremiyah Love (ankle) will play in Week 8 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: After missing the last two games with an ankle injury, Love will return to the Cardinals in what could be a three-way split after the recent emergence of Bam Knight. Love was averaging 16.2 opportunities per game before being sidelined, with most of that work coming on the ground. With only two top-24 PPR performances to his name so far this season, he shouldn’t be viewed as anything more than a boom-or-bust RB2 against the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) was listed as a limited participant in practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: That’s a second straight limited session for Love. The Cardinals are taking this slowly with the 21-year-old ahead of a potential return in Week 8 against the Cowboys, but fantasy managers will obviously need to pay close attention to how much he practices Friday and his injury designation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) will be limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: We were hoping to see Love practice in full after taking two weeks off. While today’s limited session puts him on track to play in Week 8 against the Cowboys, Bam Knight and Tyler Allgeier are still worth stashing on benches, just in case. The Cardinals are finally handling Love’s recovery patiently, after giving him far too many touches early in the preseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is expected to practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: This news comes from head coach Mike LaFleur, who spoke with the media on Monday. After missing the last two games with a nagging ankle issue, Love’s return to the field in any capacity suggests he could have a chance to suit up in Week 8 against the Cowboys. Love’s ankle injury slowed his production through the first five weeks of the season, with the rookie saying at one point that he would “probably just hinder the team” if he had to play through it. Love’s status will be one to watch throughout the week, but even if he’s active, he’ll likely be forced to split touches with either Tyler Allgeier or Bam Knight, who has been solid in Love’s absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Jeremiyah Love (ankle) will not play in Week 7 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: Things have been trending in this direction all week, but LaFleur officially confirmed on Friday that Love will miss a second straight game. Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight will likely split duties again in Week 7 after seeing a near 50/50 split in the touch distribution last week, with Allgeier’s 19 touches narrowly edging out Knight’s 17. Both Allgeier and Knight are fringe RB2/RB3 plays against a stout Broncos defense. In addition to Love the Cardinals also ruled out DT Walter Nolen III (ankle), S Andrew Wiggins (ankle), and OG Jo Gaines II (ankle).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reports Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is not expected to play in Week 7 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: Love didn’t practice on Wednesday and Thursday after missing Week 6. It doesn’t sound like he will practice at all this week. Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight will split the backfield again this week. Allgeier out-carried Knight 18-15 last week, but Knight was far more effective, running for 80 yards in total. Allgeier posted just 38 yards. He still figures to be the lead runner this week, but Allgeier shine as a plug-and-play RB2 is waning headed into Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Carson Beck (back) will not play in Week 12 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: Beck will miss a second straight game with his back injury after missing all of practice this week. The rookie QB has dealt with back issues for the majority of the year, but will now set his sights on returning in Week 13 against the Eagles. That said, the Cardinals have a Week 14 bye, which could give them a reason to sideline Beck for at least one more week and let him heal up before returning for the final four games of the regular season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Carson Beck (back) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: Beck is unlikely to recover in time to face the Commanders on Sunday. Journeyman in-season signee Josh Johnson will likely start. Johnson will be a low-end QB2 in this instance. The team brought back Kedon Slovis via waivers this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Carson Beck (back) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said Beck has been steadily improving since back spasms hit him late in Thursday’s practice. The team is taking it one day at a time with him. The team is preparing to start Josh Johnson in Week 12 against the Commanders this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Cardinals ruled out Carson Beck (back) for Week 11 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: That paves the way for 36-year-old journeyman quarterback Josh Johnson to draw the start under center for the Cardinals after being added to the team less than two weeks ago. Dynasty managers will be forced to wait longer for the first extended look at the third-round rookie as the Cardinals continue forward with insurmountable injuries up and down their roster in what has quickly become a lost season. Downgrade the primary skill position players in a difficult matchup against the Chiefs in Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Carson Beck (back) is questionable to play in Week 11 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur told reporters earlier today that Beck is unlikely to start in Week 11 against the Chiefs, so this may just be a formality. If active, Beck would be a low-end QB2 this week despite six NFL teams being on bye. Josh Johnson is expected to start in his stead.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Carson Beck (back) is unlikely to start in Week 11 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: According to Cardinals beat writer Darren Urban, LaFleur “won’t close [the] door on Beck just yet,” but the team is preparing as if Josh Johnson will draw the start on Sunday against the Chiefs. This was already shaping up to be a disastrous matchup for the Cardinals, and an offense that is down its top three receivers, and this isn’t doing anything to help the situation. If they weren’t already doing it, fantasy managers everywhere should be scrambling to stream the Chiefs defense in what is shaping up to be a very favorable home matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Carson Beck (back) was added to the injury report as a limited participant on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: Beck’s back issues continue. The rookie quarterback has dealt with this for weeks now. He should be viewed as questionable to play in the Cardinals’ Week 11 game against the Chiefs. Journeyman QB Josh Johnson is his backup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Carson Beck completed 11-of-18 passes for 108 yards and two interceptions in the Cardinals’ 6-34, Week 10 loss to the Rams and lost one fumble.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: Beck’s performance wasn’t quite as bad as the box score suggests, but it wasn’t good either. The rookie quarterback went 7-of-9 through the Cardinals’ first three drives, but the game script suddenly became pass-heavy late in the second quarter, allowing the Rams’ defense to play single-mindedly. Reggie Virgil let what could have been a 29-yard touchdown pass go off his hands on a free play, and Zay Jones fell over backward while trying to secure what should have been an easy 40-yard reception. Beck’s first interception, on the Cardinals’ fifth drive, was not his fault. Devin Duvernay twirled to the ground as he attempted to secure the pass, but his momentum got the better of him and he accidentally flung the ball into Rams S Kam Kinchens’ hands. Beck’s second interception was a poorly timed checkdown attempt to Tyler Allgeier, which a Rams defender timed perfectly as he jumped the route, ripping the ball away from Allgeier’s outstretched hands on the Cardinals’ seventh drive. Beck’s lost fumble was the result of a clean punch-out from a Rams defender while Beck was attempting to scramble for a first down. Life won’t get any easier for Beck against the Chiefs next week. He’s a QB2/3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Carson Beck will start for the Cardinals in Week 10 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: With Jacoby Brissett in Baltimore and Gardner Minshew out because of a UCL injury, the Cardinals are already down to their third-string quarterback. It was almost a given that Beck would start at some point this year, though we imagine head coach Matt LaFleur didn’t think it would be this soon. Beck played well in his lone preseason appearance, throwing for 188 yards and a score. While he’s not much of a streaming option this week, he should be good enough to keep Trey McBride at the top of the TE1 ranks, especially with Michael Wilson done for the year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Cardinals fear Gardner Minshew may have suffered a torn UCL in Week 9’s loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: If this proves to be the case, then Minshew played the entire second half with the injury, gutting things out for the Cardinals against a top-notch Seahawks defense. Minshew will undergo more tests to confirm the severity of his injury, but it now looks as if the Cardinals will be turning things over to rookie third-round pick Carson Beck, who threw for 188 yards and one touchdown in his lone preseason game. Beck could be in for a rough few weeks, and the Cardinals’ receiving corps looks suddenly depleted with Marvin Harrison Jr. now on the Texans and Michael Wilson (neck) and Kendrick Bourne (leg) both done for the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.headline: Josh Johnson will start for the Cardinals in Week 12 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.analysis: Johnson will get the start on Sunday against the Commanders in what will be a “revenge” game for the 40-year-old vet. Although, in fairness to Johnson, a lot of games are revenge games for the well-traveled vet. Things didn’t fare too well for Johnson in his first start of the season against the Chiefs, as he threw for 155 yards and one touchdown on the road, but did a good job of limiting turnovers. He’s nothing more than a QB3/desperation play in 2QB and superflex leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.headline: Carson Beck (back) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.analysis: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said Beck has been steadily improving since back spasms hit him late in Thursday’s practice. The team is taking it one day at a time with him. The team is preparing to start Josh Johnson in Week 12 against the Commanders this week.
