https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.headline: Josh Johnson completed 18-of-31 passes for 155 yards and a touchdown in Arizona’s 34-7, Week 11 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.analysis: We watched this game and can say: It definitely happened. Johnson took three sacks and didn’t look laughably bad at any point, but he also could not get real fantasy production out of the motley crew around him. Assuming Carson Beck (back) can’t get off the mat next week, Johnson would seem to be in line to start against the Commanders next Sunday. That is not an endorsement of actually using him in fantasy football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.headline: Cardinals declared QB Carson Beck, CB Starling Thomas V, OL Kingsley Eguakun, OL Jon Gaines (ankle) and DL Andrew Billings inactive for Arizona’s Week 11 game against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.analysis: Just in case you were off the grid Saturday: Josh Johnson will start for the Cardinals against the Chiefs, becoming the fourth quarterback in four weeks for a team critics are calling “one of mankind’s most awful crimes.” OK, not really, but they are 15.5-point dogs. Johnson is probably one of the three worst superflex quarterbacks to have to start this week on a short slate.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.headline: Cardinals ruled out Carson Beck (back) for Week 11 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.analysis: That paves the way for 36-year-old journeyman quarterback Josh Johnson to draw the start under center for the Cardinals after being added to the team less than two weeks ago. Dynasty managers will be forced to wait longer for the first extended look at the third-round rookie as the Cardinals continue forward with insurmountable injuries up and down their roster in what has quickly become a lost season. Downgrade the primary skill position players in a difficult matchup against the Chiefs in Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.headline: Team reporter Darren Urban believes Josh Johnson will “probably” start in Week 11 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.analysis: Rookie Carson Beck is dealing with back spasms again, so recently signed journeyman Johnson will likely get the start this week. Urban notes that Johnson “played significant snaps for LaFleur in two games for the Jets in 2021, " completing 55-for-81 passes for 621 yards, five touchdowns and two interceptions. With six teams on bye, Johnson, 40, is in the low-end QB2 conversation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.headline: Carson Beck (back) is questionable to play in Week 11 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.analysis: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur told reporters earlier today that Beck is unlikely to start in Week 11 against the Chiefs, so this may just be a formality. If active, Beck would be a low-end QB2 this week despite six NFL teams being on bye. Josh Johnson is expected to start in his stead.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Carson Beck (back) is unlikely to start in Week 11 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.analysis: According to Cardinals beat writer Darren Urban, LaFleur “won’t close [the] door on Beck just yet,” but the team is preparing as if Josh Johnson will draw the start on Sunday against the Chiefs. This was already shaping up to be a disastrous matchup for the Cardinals, and an offense that is down its top three receivers, and this isn’t doing anything to help the situation. If they weren’t already doing it, fantasy managers everywhere should be scrambling to stream the Chiefs defense in what is shaping up to be a very favorable home matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.headline: Carson Beck (back) was added to the injury report as a limited participant on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.analysis: Beck’s back issues continue. The rookie quarterback has dealt with this for weeks now. He should be viewed as questionable to play in the Cardinals’ Week 11 game against the Chiefs. Journeyman QB Josh Johnson is his backup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.headline: Cardinals signed QB Josh Johnson from the Bengals’ practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-johns.analysis: In the wake of trading away Jacoby Brissett and the UCL injury to Gardner Minshew, the Cardinals spring into action to add veteran depth behind rookie third-round quarterback Carson Beck, the latter of whom is expected to start for the remainder of the season in Arizona. Beck will be thrust into action without the team’s starting left tackle and alpha wide receiver in Michael Wilson but will get much needed experience as the Cardinals decide the trajectory of their franchise in the final half of the 2026 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.headline: Rams TE Tyler Higbee is considered week-to-week with a chest injury he suffered in Week 12’s win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: ESPN’s Adam Schefter was the first to report the news on Higbee. Higbee will reportedly have “a chance” to play in Week 13 against the Chiefs, but as Schefter reported, that decision will be based on “how he heals over the next week.” Where things stand right now, the Rams are currently down three tight ends, with Terrance Ferguson (ankle) out for the season and Davis Allen (ankle) also considered week-to-week after going down in Week 12. Colby Parkinson and Max Klare are expected to serve as the top two tight ends in Sean McVay’s 12-heavy personnel, but the team could look to add a free agent tight end or two in the days ahead.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.headline: Tyler Higbee (chest) was ruled out for the remainder of Week 12 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: It is unknown when Higbee sustained the injury but he was shown walking to the locker room at the start of the fourth quarter, with the broadcast stating that he was ruled out for the remainder of the game. Higbee caught 1-of-3 targets for 14 yards prior to departing, with his absence of particular note considering fellow tight end Davis Allen was already ruled out in the second quarter with an ankle injury. Perhaps rookie Max Klare will see meaningful run in their absences.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.headline: Tyler Higbee caught 3-of-4 targets for 17 yards and one touchdown in the Rams’ Week 10 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: Higbee earned an end zone target on the Rams’ opening drive, but Matthew Stafford overthrew him, resulting in an incompletion. The two did manage to link up for a score on the Rams’ fourth drive, though. Rams coach Sean McVay dialed up a play where Higbee motioned from in-line to out wide on the left side. He ran right past his coverage defender, and Stafford hit him streaking toward the back of the end zone for a five-yard touchdown. Higbee will likely be a low-end TE1 against the Packers, following the Rams’ Week 11 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) is not on the Rams’ final injury report for Week 10 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: Parkinson upgraded to full participation today. Tyler Higbee (illness) was limited. Both players were cleared to play. Davis Allen (oblique) is questionable, sandwiching a Thursday absence between two limited sessions. The Rams must be smart with their skill position players’ health, while asking as much as they can from their available players.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: Parkinson should play through his injury again this week. Unfortunately, Tyler Higbee (illness) did not practice, as a new addition to the injury report, and Davis Allen (oblique) was downgraded to being a non-participant. The running backs are going to get all the work they can handle this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.headline: ESPN’s Dan Graziano reports Puka Nacua (knee, toe) will not miss the rest of the regular season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: Graziano said there’s an outside chance the Rams won’t put Nacua on injured reserve ahead of Week 10. Rams sources “were very adamant that Nacua’s injury isn’t season-ending and that they hope to get him back around that Week 14, Week 15 time.” With Davante Adams (hamstring) also sidelined, look for the Rams offense to be unusually run heavy in the coming weeks. That should mean more work for Kyren Williams and Blake Corum. Tyler Higbee and Colby Parkinson could see an uptick in targets too. If Terrance Ferguson (hamstring) is ever able to return to game action, he could profile as the team’s top target. Nacua had seen 44 percent of the Rams’ first-read targets this season, the highest rate in the NFL.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.headline: Rams ruled out Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring) for Week 9 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: Ferguson was set to make his return from injured reserve, having rehabilitated his early-season ankle injury. Unfortunately, he strained his hamstring in practice today and has now been ruled out. With Colby Parkinson (ribs) questionable, Tyler Higbee sneaks back into the TE1 conversation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.headline: Tyler Higbee caught 1-of-2 targets for 14 yards in the Rams’ Week 8 win against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: It was another disappointing outing for Higbee. This one came with Colby Parkinson (ribs) sidelined. Davis Allen had two catches on two targets for eight yards. Higbee now hasn’t had more than 25 yards receiving in a game since the beginning of October, and has lost opportunities with the Rams going run heavy in recent weeks. Higbee won’t be a fantasy option in Week 9 against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.headline: Rams declared TE Colby Parkinson, QB Ty Simpson, LS Joe Cardona, OT Keagan Trost, and DE Desjuan Johnson inactive for Week 8 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: Parkinson will miss at least one game with a rib injury he sustained last week against the Raiders. His absence could have a big impact on playing time for both Davis Allen — who had two touchdown grabs last week — and Tyler Higbee, the de facto TE1 in the LA offense. Both tight ends are better options against the Chargers with Parkinson sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: Parkinson will have one more chance to get back no the practice field Friday to avoid an injury designation entering the weekend. The veteran tight end was in and out of the team’s Week 7 game with the injury but managed to finish it, apparently feeling much worse after the adrenaline wore off. Fantasy managers of Parkinson and Tyler Higbee will want to track Parkinson’s status closely to end the week. An absence from Parkinson could also bring Davis Allen into the fantasy spotlight after the young tight end scored twice against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.headline: Rams TE Davis Allen is considered week-to-week after suffering a high-ankle sprain in Week 12’s win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.analysis: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport was the first to report the news. Allen will reportedly go to the Rams’ facilities today for a full evaluation to determine the approximate length of his absence, but with Terrance Ferguson (ankle) out for the season and Tyler Higbee (chest) also considered week-to-week, the Rams are suddenly very thin at tight end. Rookie second-rounder Max Klare and veteran Colby Parkinson are the only healthy tight ends currently on the roster, but it’s possible the Rams will look to add one or two more free agents to fill their needs at the position. It’s hard to imagine either Parkinson or Klare seeing enough of a role in the Rams’ passing game to become fantasy-viable players in the weeks ahead.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.headline: Davis Allen (ankle) was ruled out for the remainder of Week 12 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.analysis: Allen saw his ankle rolled up on in the first quarter, playing through the ailment to finish the drive before succumbing to the pain. He was ruled out at the half after catching both targets for 14 yards. Rookie Max Klare could see an uptick in opportunity in his absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.headline: Davis Allen caught 1-of-1 targets in the Rams’ Week 10 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.analysis: Allen played a small role, but made a big impact today, scoring from 19 yards out on a nice catch-and-run on the Rams’ seventh drive. Allen lined up in-line on the right side before slipping across the field mid-play, seemingly without any Cardinals defenders noticing. He easily hauled in the pass and turned upfield for the score. Allen will be a touchdown-dependent TE2 against the Packers, post-bye, in Week 12.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) is not on the Rams’ final injury report for Week 10 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.analysis: Parkinson upgraded to full participation today. Tyler Higbee (illness) was limited. Both players were cleared to play. Davis Allen (oblique) is questionable, sandwiching a Thursday absence between two limited sessions. The Rams must be smart with their skill position players’ health, while asking as much as they can from their available players.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.analysis: Parkinson should play through his injury again this week. Unfortunately, Tyler Higbee (illness) did not practice, as a new addition to the injury report, and Davis Allen (oblique) was downgraded to being a non-participant. The running backs are going to get all the work they can handle this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.headline: Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring) did not practice in Wednesday’s walk-through.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.analysis: Ferguson was listed as a DNP for the Rams’ Wednesday walk-through. Rams head coach Sean McVay said earlier this week that Ferguson is likely out a couple week, so this comes as no surprise. Meanwhile, fellow tight ends Davis Allen (oblique) and Colby Parkinson (ribs) were both listed as limited participants. Allen and Parkinson are trending towards playing in Week 10 against the Cardinals, with Parkinson operating more as a pass-catcher and Allen as a blocker.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.headline: Davis Allen caught both of his targets for eight yards in the Rams’ Week 8 win against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.analysis: With Colby Parkinson sidelined with a rib injury, Allen played behind Tyler Higbee and wasn’t all that involved in the Rams’ run-first offense. Fresh off catching two touchdowns from Matthew Stafford on just 12 routes in Week 7, Allen didn’t get so lucky in Week 8. He shouldn’t be rostered in 12-team formats for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.analysis: Parkinson will have one more chance to get back no the practice field Friday to avoid an injury designation entering the weekend. The veteran tight end was in and out of the team’s Week 7 game with the injury but managed to finish it, apparently feeling much worse after the adrenaline wore off. Fantasy managers of Parkinson and Tyler Higbee will want to track Parkinson’s status closely to end the week. An absence from Parkinson could also bring Davis Allen into the fantasy spotlight after the young tight end scored twice against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.headline: Davis Allen caught 4-of-5 targets for 20 yards and two touchdowns in the Rams’ Week 7 win against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.analysis: The Rams in Week 7 resorted to a heavy dose of three tight end sets with Davante Adams sidelined with a long-term hamstring injury. That led to 12 pass routes for Allen, fewer than both Colby Parkinson and Tyler Higbee. He caught two red zone touchdowns from Matthew Stafford, however, seeing a look on 33 percent of his routes. Allen will be tough to trust as a fantasy option unless or until his snaps and routes increase. He could be a deep league option in Week 8 against the Chargers, however.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.headline: Davis Allen (foot) is not on Los Angeles’ final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.analysis: He got in a limited session and the Rams apparently trust him to play despite a pair of missed practices on Wednesday and Thursday. Colby Parkinson (shoulder) also avoided the final report. Tyler Higbee is the Rams tight end you should be using at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle/groin) will not play in Week 12 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: With a Week 13 bye on tap for the Jets, the team is hoping two extra weeks of rest will be more than enough for Cooper to play in Week 14 against the Broncos. Cooper has not played since re-injuring his ankle in Week 10 against the Bills and has now missed six of a possible 12 games in his rookie season. It’s possible this is the last update we receive on Cooper until the Jets return from their bye week, but fantasy managers in need of help over the next two weeks can safely drop him where needed.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Omar Cooper (ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Cooper is firmly on the wrong side of questionable for the Jets’ Week 12 game against the Dolphins. Isaiah Williams (ribs) is on track to return for No. 3 wide receiver duties, though only Garrett Wilson is reliable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) was held out of Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: It is obviously a poor start to Cooper’s week after he missed Week 11, though coach Aaron Glenn claimed his rookie wideout was “day to day.” That might actually be true, but with the Jets’ season once again lost, we doubt the No. 30 overall pick will be rushed back for a matchup with the lowly Dolphins. Were Cooper to somehow suit up, he would be more of a WR4 than WR3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: The Jets declared Omar Cooper Jr., CB Jarvis Brownlee Jr., WR Isaiah Williams, LB Trevin Wallace, TE Jelani Woods and ED Nate Lynn inactive for Week 11 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Removing Cooper and Williams leaves Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell as the team’s top two wide receivers. Kenyon Sadiq and Mason Taylor could benefit as well. Geno Smith will play through his ankle injury today, after beginning the week in the questionable column. A run-heavy, quick-passing game plan could be incoming, given Smith’s ailment.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) has been ruled out for Week 11 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Cooper and Isaiah Williams (ribs) will both miss this week’s game, leaving Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell to lead the wide receiver corps. Both players’ target share projections should increase a tad. Cooper did not practice at all this week. He has dealt with multiple ankle injuries in his rookie season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Omar Cooper (ankle) will not play in Week 11 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: This was to be expected. Cooper was bounced from Week 10’s game against the Bills after one snap, after he had his ankle rolled up on, and has not gotten on the practice field this week. The 22-year-old receiver has had a challenging start to his career and is now slated to miss his fifth game of the season. Fellow receiver Isaiah Williams (ribs) has also been ruled out, paving the way for Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell to have busy days against the one-win Chargers. It doesn’t sound like Cooper is at risk of being placed on injured reserve, so we’ll see if things fare any differently for him entering Week 12.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Omar Cooper (ankle/hip) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: The Jets’ rookie wide receiver is on the wrong side of questionable. He appears to be likely to miss this week’s game against the Chargers. Ankle issues have bothered him for some time. Perhaps taking a week off would benefit him in the long run. He remains a worthwhile hold at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Omar Cooper, Jr. (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Cooper, who picked up his latest injury last week against the Bills, appears to be a long shot for Week 11 against the Chargers. That would leave Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell as the clear top targets for Geno Smith, if Smith is able to play through his own ankle injury. Wilson and Mitchell last week combined for 87 percent of the Jets’ air yards and 51 percent of the team’s targets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) has been downgraded to out for Week 10 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Cooper Jr. was injured on the Jets’ first play of the game when Breece Hall was tackled into the back of his leg. Cooper Jr. has been battling an ankle injury throughout the season, so there is some concern that this could lead to an extended absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Omar Cooper Jr. is questionable to return in Week 10 against the Bills due to an ankle injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: On the Jets’ first play of the game, Cooper Jr. was blocking for Breece Hall when Hall was tackled into the back of Cooper Jr.'s legs. The wide receiver bent back awkwardly and limped off the field before heading into the locker room. Cooper Jr. was on the IR earlier this season with an ankle injury and was questionable coming into this week with an ankle injury, so this is a tough break for the 22-year-old.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Parker Washington (shoulder) will not play in the Jaguars’ Week 12 game against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: According to head coach Liam Coen, Washington aggravated an AC joint injury in Thursday’s practice that will sideline him for at least one week. Speaking with the media on Friday, Coen said the team hopes to have him back “ASAP” but noted that it is a “week-to-week injury.” Jakobi Meyers could be first in line to benefit from Washington’s absence, but this certainly isn’t an ideal situation for fantasy managers with the fantasy playoffs just weeks away.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Parker Washington (shoulder) was added to the injury report as a limited participant on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: This suggests Washington injured his shoulder at today’s practice. Hopefully, it is only a mild issue and he suits up as planned in Week 12 against the Titans. He is a WR1 if active. Jakobi Meyers (ankle) would benefit if Washington sits out this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Parker Washington caught 8-of-17 targets for 103 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 11 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: Washington should have been credited with a touchdown on a gorgeous end zone throw from Trevor Lawrence but the refs for some reason called it incomplete after a lengthy replay review, befuddling even Gene Steratore. This was the rare negative game script in which Parker could flex his statistical muscles as the Jags’ clear WR1, as the usually-balanced Jacksonville offense tilted pass heavy while chasing points in the second half. No other Jacksonville pass catcher had more than ten targets on the day. Washington will be an elite fantasy option in Week 12 against a wretched Titans secondary that gave up 152 yards and a touchdown to Parker in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Parker Washington caught 7-of-9 targets for 152 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 10 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: Washington was unstoppable in the first half with three gains of 30 or more yards plus a short touchdown. He entered halftime with six grabs for 148 yards. The fact that he was on pace for nearly 300 yards and finished with “only” 152 is a slightly disappointing outcome, but there wasn’t much of a reason for the Jags to keep airing it out in the second half. The Titans weren’t putting up much of a fight on offense and the Jags leaned on their ground game, preventing Washington from having a truly insane day. Fantasy managers will have to live with their 28.2 PPR points. Washington is pushing for a WR1 ranking as he heads into a Week 11 matchup with the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Parker Washington caught 2-of-7 targets for 61 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: Both of Washington’s receptions came before the break, the second of which was a 50-yard touchdown on a double-move slant against Cover-0 with under one minute remaining before the half. Washington remains one of the most efficient receivers in the league but consistently positive game scripts have left the overall pass volume lacking, particularly in the second half this season. He remains an upside WR2 ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Parker Washington caught 1-of-2 targets for 16 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 8 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: Washington also added a 10-yard rush. Extremely disappointing volume coming out of the Jaguars’ bye week, but no Jag commanded more than three targets in a contest where Trevor Lawrence attempted only 14 throws before taking a fourth quarter breather in a 42-7 blowout. Washington is going to be subject to this kind of risk when the deep-and-dangerous Jags take on more overmatched foes, including now for Week 9 as the Ravens come to town for Thursday Night Football with their No. 2 or 3 quarterback under center. You always fire up Washington as a WR2, but he’s probably not going to stuff the stat sheet on Thursday evening.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Parker Washington caught 4-of-11 targets for 64 yards in Jacksonville’s Week 6 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: A lot of these incompletions were balls Washington got a hand on but couldn’t quite reel in as was breaking to the sideline. Washington displayed his speed and shiftiness on a 27-yard catch-and-run in the second quarter where he cut through both Texans linebackers for a big gain. He is a fantasy WR2 as the Jaguars enter their bye week. Washington is #onpace for a near-1,200 yard season with 14 touchdowns even after this dud.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Parker Washington caught 6-of-9 targets for 124 yards and two touchdowns in the Jaguars’ Week 5 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: Coming off a pair of quiet weeks, Washington paid off for fantasy managers early with a 51-yard score in the first quarter. It was somehow nowhere close to his best play of the day. Washington scored his second touchdown on a falling, one-handed grab in the end zone from 27 yards out near the end of the game. The grab was reminiscent of Odell Beckham’s famous touchdown catch. Washington remains the most talented and most involved receiver on the Jags. He will be a high-end WR2 versus the Texans next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Parker Washington caught 1-of-3 targets for 7 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 4 win over the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: Washington also added three yards with one carry on the ground. After a hot start to the season, Washington was relatively quiet against the Bengals. The Jaguars receivers combined for just 11 of Trevor Lawrence’s 23 targets and Washington saw three of those. His first reception came in the fourth quarter on a 40-yard catch-and-run that would have sealed the game, but was called back after replay showed he stepped out of bounds after seven yards. Game script and the Bengals’ tight end weaknesses played a factor in this game, with Brenton Strange the primary target on the day. Washington should still be the Jaguars’ No. 1 receiver and is a fantasy WR2 for Week 5 against the Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Parker Washington caught 3-of-5 targets for 40 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 3 win against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: It’s Washington’s second touchdown in the Jags’ first three games of the season. Washington caught his touchdown against the Patriots after having an acrobatic touchdown grab called back on a penalty. Having established himself as the team’s clear-cut WR1 — well ahead of Brian Thomas, who had one target in Week 3 — Washington will have a rock solid weekly floor with ceiling to spare in shootout game scripts. Washington should remain in all lineups next week against a middling Bengals defense, in what could be a high-scoring affair between two potent offenses.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert (shoulder) was spotted in a sling after the Eagles’ Week 12 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Goedert exited Week 12’s win over the Cowboys with a shoulder injury on the first drive of the game. The veteran tight end did not return to the game, and the fact that he was wearing a sling after the game suggests this could be somewhat of a serious injury. Head coach Nick Sirianni did not comment on his injury after the game, so it’s possible we won’t learn until later next week what he’s dealing with and how much time he could miss, if any. Goedert has caught 33 passes for 355 yards and two touchdowns this season, with both of his scores coming in Week 1against the Commanders. Zach Ertz’s 39 offensive snaps and 19 routes run both led the Eagles’ tight end room on the day, and could point to him operating as Philly’s TE1 if Goedert were to miss any time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert (shoulder) has been ruled out for the remainder of Week 12 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Goedert suffered a shoulder injury on the first drive of the game and was ruled out a quarter later. The 31-year-old will get a week-plus to get healthy for Week 13 against the Cardinals, but for now Zach Ertz and Johnny Mundt will be the uninspiring tight end options.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert (shoulder) is questionable to return in Week 12 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Goedert was injured on the first drive of the game and headed to the locker room. Zack Ertz and Johnny Mundt will likely see the majority of the snaps if Goedert can’t return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert (shin) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 12 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Goedert was upgraded to a full practice on Tuesday, meaning he was never at risk of missing tomorrow’s game. Coming off a one-catch bust against the Steelers, things get much better on Thanksgiving for the Eagles’ top tight end. Only four teams are allowing more passing yards per game than the Cowboys. Goedert will be on the TE1/2 border this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert (shin) practiced in full on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: That makes us feel pretty confident that he’ll suit up for Thanksgiving’s game against the Cowboys after a limited session on Monday. The Eagles’ passing game is in pretty rough shape with Joe Milton under center, but Dallas’ issues invite a TE1-capable game script for Goedert if the Eagles can take advantage of it.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert (shin) was limited in Monday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: It’s a new (estimated) listing after his one-catch outing against the Steelers. Goedert was at least set up with a Joe Milton #RevengeGame script against a weak Cowboys defense this week to try to rebound, but it will be hard to rely on him as a streamer TE1 if healthy. We’ll see if he can get to the second part of that statement tomorrow.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert caught his only target for 38 yards in the Eagles’ Week 11 win against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Goedert ran a pass route on 20 of the team’s 29 drop backs but only saw one look from Joe Milton, who attempted a meager 21 passes and threw for 141 scoreless yards. DeVonta Smith’s return to the Eagles lineup netted him a 57 percent target share. That kind of target domination won’t leave much opportunity for anyone else, including Goedert, who should not be played in 12-team formats for now. The Eagles play the Cowboys in Week 12.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert caught 5-of-6 targets for 50 yards in the Eagles’ Week 9 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: With No. 3 QB Joe Milton making his starting debut, Goedert padded the box score with some empty PPR production. Excellent, though there figures to be distressingly little difference between Goedert’s floor and ceiling for the time being. With the Eagles headed on bye for Week 10, how Goedert is valued upon the team’s return will depend on whether DeVonta Smith or Dontayvion Wicks finally get back in the lineup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert caught 3-of-4 targets for 30 yards in the Eagles’ Week 8 loss to the Commanders, adding two yards on one carry.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Goedert also committed a drop that was intercepted in the down performance, although the play in question was overturned through penalty. The veteran tight end continues to be limited by an ineffective offense with Tanner McKee under center in what has quickly become a lost season after the team’s sixth consecutive loss. Fantasy managers are likely better off looking for viable alternatives ahead of a Week 9 divisional clash with the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert caught 5-of-7 targets for 48 yards in the Eagles’ Week 7 loss to the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Goedert has now returned consecutive games of middling production with Tanner McKee under center, which is a somewhat troubling realization considering DeVonta Smith missed both games and Dontayvion Wicks departed Week 6 with an injury before missing Week 7. Goedert’s fantasy value appears strictly tied to the state of a sinking Philadelphia ball club, now fighting through declining quarterback play in addition to poor offensive structure and shoddy play calling. Fantasy managers are likely forced to endure the middling production for lack of better options.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Rashee Rice caught 2-of-5 targets for 19 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 12 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: Rice’s quiet day was made all the worse by the refs when they overturned his third catch to an incomplete pass after replay showed the ball hitting the ground. While the tip of the ball did touch the turf, the ball didn’t appear to move. While the controversial call eventually led to a Buffalo victory, calling it a catch would have changed little for fantasy managers. Rice has played five games since returning from his early-season hamstring injury. He had more than 53 yards in just one of them. Rice will get one final week in the WR2 ranks when the Chiefs take on the Rams next week. Another quiet performance will send him tumbling down the rankings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Rashee Rice caught 6-of-6 targets for 53 yards in Kansas City’s Week 11 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: He remains fully involved here, but with Travis Kelce stealing two scores, there wasn’t much here that Rice could do. Rice has cleared 60 yards just once since coming back from a hamstring injury and Josh Downs’ growing involvement probably won’t help his cause there. He’ll be a reasonable WR3 and remains in a good spot given the state of the offense against the Bills on Thursday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Rashee Rice (knee) is practicing in full for Week 10 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: For the first time since October 4th, the Chiefs listed Rice only with a knee issue. He had been managing a hamstring strain for more than a month, prior to today, and was typically limited early in the week. This is a great sign for his health moving forward. Rice is a WR2 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Rashee Rice caught 5-of-7 targets for 49 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 9 win against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: Rice, as usual, led the Chiefs in targets. It was an unusually run-heavy game plan for the Chiefs against a Jets defense that showed no real interest in stopping Ken Walker. This performance comes off last week’s 56-yard, one-touchdown outing for Rice, who missed significant time with a hamstring injury. Rice profiles as a high-floor WR2/3 in most formats. He’ll face the run-funnel Falcons defense in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) is not on the Chiefs’ final injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: Rice posted a 7/53/1 receiving line against the Broncos last week. He got in a limited session on Wednesday before upgrading to full on Thursday. He seems to be recovering effectively from his summer knee procedure and in-season hamstring injury. Rice is a borderline WR1/2 for this weekend’s game against the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: Rice is on track to face the Jets this weekend, as expected. The Chiefs’ embattled wide receiver also reportedly filed for bankruptcy this week, theoretically adding extra incentive to play well enough for a decent contract when he enters free agency next offseason. Rice is a fantasy football WR2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) was limited in Wednesday’s practice
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: Rice returned from a multi-game absence because of the hamstring injury last week and he’s been on the injury report with the knee issue for most of the year. It doesn’t sound like either injury will prevent him from playing in Week 9. The limited session was likely maintenance. Rice led the Chiefs with eight targets in his first game back on Sunday. He’s been the Chiefs’ only consistently productive pass-catcher when healthy. He will be in the WR1 mix when he takes on the Jets this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Rashee Rice caught 7-of-8 targets for 53 yards and a touchdown in the Chiefs’ Week 8 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: Rice was heavily involved early in the game, catching three passes for 26 yards and a score on the Chiefs’ opening drive. His role, however, took a backseat to running back targets in the second half. He caught three balls for 15 yards in the final two quarters combined. Rice briefly appeared to score the game-winning touchdown on the final play of the game, but refs had already blown the play dead because of a false start. Even without the second touchdown, fantasy managers can be confident in Rice as the team’s No. 1 receiver and a low-end WR2 for fantasy purposes going forward. He will sit just inside the WR1 ranks for his Week 9 date with the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Andy Reid said Rashee Rice (hamstring) will play in Week 8.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: Rice will make his return to the game-day roster after missing two games due to a hamstring injury sustained in Week 4, returning as the top option through the air for an offense that has struggled with him off the field. The Chiefs scored a combined 25 points against the Chargers and Seahawks without Rice, the latter of which tied the fewest points scored in quarterback Patrick Mahomes’ career. Fantasy managers can comfortably re-insert Rice into rosters as an upside WR2 against the Broncos, against whom Rice caught both targets for 19 yards and a touchdown in Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Rashee Rice (hamstring) was present at practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: That now marks consecutive days on the practice field for the veteran receiver whom has missed the previous two games. The Chiefs also had their bye in Week 5, giving Rice a full three weeks of recovery, which combines with his recent practice availability to make it likely he returns to face the Broncos. The Chiefs managed just 25 combined points in the two games without Rice.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.headline: Travis Kelce caught 4-of-7 targets for 71 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 12 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: Kelce was the only member of the Chiefs’ passing attack to find any success in this game. Being battered by the elements, Patrick Mahomes relied on his trusted tight end for a handful of big plays throughout the contest. One of them was a 21-yard toss to the nine-yard line at the end of the first half that set up a short field goal. Kelce, however, paid the price with a helmet to the back that left him on the ground in pain for a while. He ultimately played through the issue, though we expect to see him on the injury report next week. Kelce, unfortunately, did not go out on a high note, dropping a long pass that would have at least pushed the game into overtime. With a potential shootout on tap versus the Rams, Kelce will remain inside the top 12 fantasy tight ends next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.headline: Travis Kelce caught 6-of-7 targets for 74 yards and two touchdowns in Kansas City’s 34-7 Week 11 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: It was his first multi-receiving touchdown game since November of 2022, when he put up three on the Chargers. Kelce’s first score had him moving forward in the red zone and he added a nice post touchdown in the second quarter. Don’t expect this every week anymore, obviously, but Kelce will remain an easy TE1 against the Bills next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.headline: Travis Kelce caught 2-of-2 targets for 30 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 10 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: Kelce missed large chunks of the first and second quarter with injury, but returned to finish the game without incident. It initially appeared Kelce aggravated his pre-existing ankle issue, but coach Andy Reid said afterward it was a calf ailment. That likely means cramps. That also means it’s not a big concern for Week 11 against the Cardinals, but with Josh Downs in tow to finally provide another legitimate target for Patrick Mahomes, Kelce’s TE1 floor is probably lowering for the stretch run.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.headline: Travis Kelce (ankle, questionable) returned for the second quarter of Kansas City’s Week 10 game against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: Kelce ended up missing about a quarter of action. He figures to be on a snap count for the rest of the afternoon, but we would have to imagine he will be a point of targets emphasis when he is on the field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.headline: Travis Kelce suffered an ankle injury in Kansas City’s Week 10 game against the Falcons and is questionable to return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: Already nursing an ankle issue, Kelce got rolled up at the end of a first quarter reception and hobbled gingerly to the sideline. He tried to re-enter, but ran off the field after briefly checking back in. He then headed to the locker room. We would assume veteran Kelce is genuinely questionable, and that he could get taped up/receive a pain-killing injection and return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.headline: Travis Kelce (ankle) is practicing in full for Week 10 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: The Chiefs have been limiting Kelce’s participation on Wednesdays in recent weeks. His return to full participation to begin the week is great to see. Kelce, 37, remains a locked-in TE1 at this point in his career. Treat him accordingly against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.headline: Travis Kelce caught 4-of-6 targets for 72 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 9 win against the Jets, adding a rush for one yard and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: Kelce scored on a goal line tush push in the first half. It was a nice little treat for fantasy managers starting the old guy in Week 9. Kelce was second among KC pass catchers in targets, trailing Rashee Rice, who saw seven targets on the day. Kelce remains a reliable floor option in PPR formats. He’s had at least four receptions in five games this season, though his after the catch production has (predictably) cratered. Kelce should be in 12-team league lineups against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.headline: Travis Kelce (ankle) is not on the Chiefs’ final injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: Kelce caught 5-of-7 targets for 67 yards, playing through the ankle injury last week against the Broncos, looking slightly hobbled. Kelce was limited to begin the week, but got in two full practices over the last two days. He remains firmly in the TE1 tier for Week 9 against the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.headline: Travis Kelce (ankle) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: This time last week, Kelce was still a limited participant. Today’s upgraded status is a good sign for his overall health. The Chiefs’ stalwart tight end earned eight targets last week despite the ailment. He can be treated as a fantasy football TE1 against the Jets this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.headline: Travis Kelce (ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: Kelce looked slightly hobbled by the ankle issue in the Chiefs’ Week 8 loss to the Broncos, but he played through it and never missed a meaningful number of snaps. A limited session today means he should be good to go for Sunday’s game against the Jets. Kelce’s numbers are down over the past month, but he’s still seeing enough work to be considered a low-end TE1, especially against a weak Jets defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ty-johnson/000.headline: Ty Johnson caught both of his targets for 12 yards in the Bills’ Week 12 win over the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ty-johnson/000.analysis: Johnson spiked for 55 yards on seven catches last week. That usage was nowhere to be found on Thanksgiving. It was a rain-soaked rock-fight of a game in which the Bills barely even tried to pass. Josh Allen threw the ball 21 times and only 10 were caught. The low volume axed any chance Johnson had of an encore. Facing a lowly Patriots team in Week 13, we don’t expect much work for Buffalo’s third-down back next week. Johnson will be buried in the RB5 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ty-johnson/000.headline: Ty Johnson caught 7-of-8 targets for 55 yards in the Bills’ Week 11 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ty-johnson/000.analysis: Despite his status as a running back, Johnson’s value to the Bills is as a receiver and pass blocker. He was a crucial option for Josh Allen when under pressure today, and Johnson consistently makes one or two big receptions in the screen game each week. His eight targets were third on the team this week, as were his 55 yards rushing. Still, it would be Ray Davis who would get a lot of rushing value if James Cook were ever to get hurt, which limits Johnson’s appeal as a stash option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ty-johnson/000.headline: Ray Davis (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ty-johnson/000.analysis: Davis is still worth stashing on benches in 12-team leagues. He is James Cook’s primary backup. Passing down specialist Ty Johnson (knee) is practicing in full this week and should be good to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ty-johnson/000.headline: Ty Johnson caught all four of his targets for 50 yards in the Bills’ Week 3 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ty-johnson/000.analysis: Johnson missed the first two games after having his hamstring accessory tendon removed on August 11th. We’re not sure what that entails, but it doesn’t sound like a minor injury, and it makes sense why Johnson is only now able to return. Still, in his first game back, Johnson remains the clear passing game back in Buffalo’s offense. While he was second on the team in receiving, he played just 15 snaps, and 30 of his 50 receiving yards came on one catch. He’s not a recommended option in fantasy, and Ray Davis would remain the main beneficiary if James Cook were to get hurt.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ty-johnson/000.headline: Ty Johnson (hamstring) is not on Buffalo’s final Week 3 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ty-johnson/000.analysis: He practiced in full all week and will return to his third-down role against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ty-johnson/000.headline: Bills declared RB Ty Johnson (hamstring) inactive for Week 2 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ty-johnson/000.analysis: Johnson mainly serves as a third-down specialist, so his absence is not hugely consequential. The Bills promoted RB Frank Fore Jr. from the practice squad. He and RB Ray Davis will back up starting RB James Cook tonight.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ty-johnson/000.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the Bills “want to get that running game recharged” in Week 2 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ty-johnson/000.analysis: Bills RB James Cook totaled 57 yards on just 13 rushing attempts last week, adding three catches for 12 yards. Per Fowler, the Bills plan to use him a lot more in primetime this evening. Cook can be treated as a locked-in RB1 in what should be a fantasy-friendly game environment on Thursday Night Football. The Bills notably elevated RB Frank Gore Jr. from the practice squad, which could indicate that RB Ty Johnson (hamstring) will be inactive tonight.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ty-johnson/000.headline: Ty Johnson (hamstring) is questionable for week 2 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ty-johnson/000.analysis: Johnson was limited in practice throughout the week after missing the Bills’ opener versus Houston. James Cook’s receiving role didn’t change much with Johnson out. Instead, Ray Davis and Frank Gore Jr. picked up a few extra routes each. Neither player has much fantasy appeal, even if Johnson remains out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ty-johnson/000.headline: Bills RB Ty Johnson (hamstring) was limited in Tuesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ty-johnson/000.analysis: Johnson, the only offensive player on the Bills injury report ahead of Thursday’s clash with the Lions, could be trending in the right direction for Week 2. If he does return, he’ll take passing-game work off Frank Gore Jr.'s plate.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ty-johnson/000.headline: Bills RB Ty Johnson (hamstring) was limited in Monday’s estimated practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ty-johnson/000.analysis: We’ll have a better idea of if Johnson can go for Week 2 on Tuesday — when the Bills will run an actual practice. Johnson didn’t return to practice until the Friday ahead of Week 1 as he’s nursed this hamstring injury throughout most of training camp. If he does go, he’ll step in as Buffalo’s third-down back. The Bills mostly used Frank Gore Jr. there in the second half during Week 1’s win.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.headline: Khalil Shakir caught 3-of-6 targets for 33 yards in the Bills’ Week 12 win over the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.analysis: Shakir led the Bills in targets, catches, and yards, but it was a memorable Thanksgiving for the worst kind of reason. Josh Allen tossed him a simple screen pass in the red zone late in the third quarter, but Shakir failed to corral the ball and bobbled it right into the hands of Chiefs corner Nohl Williams. The good news for Shakir is that the blunder didn’t land him in the doghouse. Allen’s very next attempt went to Shakir for a six-yard gain. Shakir has been a steady option out of the slot this year, but the spike weeks have been nonexistent. He has one touchdown and a single 100-yard game through 11 appearances. He will be stuck in the WR4 ranks when the Bills take on the Patriots next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.headline: Khalil Shakir caught 5-of-9 targets for 101 yards in the Bills’ Week 11 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.analysis: Shakir led the team in receiving yards and was second on the team in targets. He hauled in a 38-yard reception and a 32-yard reception, which fueled his day. One of those was on a long catch-and-run, and the other was on a broken play where Josh Allen was rolling out of the pocket and found Shakir. The 26-year-old receiver has a knack for getting open in space and will always be a big producer for Buffalo when they play defenses that like to play a lot of zone.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.headline: Khalil Shakir caught 2-of-3 targets for 26 yards receiving in the Bills’ Week 10 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.analysis: Shakir also added 29 yards rushing on three carries, but two of those were simply screens thrown backwards, so they counted as runs. When you factor that in, Shakir had five targets in this one, which was the second-most of any receiver on the Bills. He remains a safe floor option because of his consistent role in the offense, but there isn’t a big fantasy ceiling here unless he breaks multiple tackles after a short completion.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.headline: Khalil Shakir caught all four targets for 58 yards in the Bills’ Week 9 win over the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.analysis: Shakir saw his routes capped against the tenacious Minnesota defense, with the Bills increasing their 12- and 13-personnel rates to combat the most blitz-heavy defense in NFL history. He made the most of his opportunities while catching all four targets for a team-leading 58 yards. Even so, Shakir remains unlikely to return usable weekly fantasy production as a near slot-only receiver in the run-first Buffalo offense. He will be nothing more than a bye-week FLEX when the Bilsl take on the Jets in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.headline: Khalil Shakir caught 5-of-6 targets for 64 yards in the Bills’ Week 8 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.analysis: Shakir came out cooking on the Bills’ opening drive, catching passes of 26 and 18 yards to immediately move the ball into Ravens territory. A few plays later, Shakir would haul in a five-yard pass that was initially ruled a touchdown, only to have the call overturned after review when Shakir was shown to have stepped out of bounds near the one-yard line. He would have a quiet afternoon after that first drive, as DJ Moore and Dalton Kincaid were the preferred targets of Josh Allen with both back healthy. Shakir, whose fantasy stock is already fairly low, can likely be left out of lineups in Week 9 against a stout Vikings defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.headline: Khalil Shakir caught 4-of-6 targets for 34 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 6 win over the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.analysis: Shakir didn’t have an overly productive day through the air in this one, but he did manage to find the end zone for his first touchdown of the season. Shakir scored on a nine-yard screen pass in the second quarter to put the Bills up 13-7. Shakir has now gone for double-digit PPR points in three straight games but will be hard to trust as anything more than a WR4/WR5 in Week 8 when the Bills return from their bye to face the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.headline: Khalil Shakir caught all three targets for 80 yards in the Bills’ Week 5 win over the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.analysis: Shakir’s modest target total was primarily a product of a ground-heavy approach from the Bills, who were playing without both DJ Moore and Joshua Palmer. His quiet fantasy outing was quickly remedied through a 57-yard, catch-and-run reception on the team’s second possession of overtime to set up the game-winning, Tyler Bass field goal. Shakir remains a shaky fantasy bet ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.headline: Khalil Shakir caught 7-of-8 targets for 82 yards and a fumble in the Bills’ Week 4 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.analysis: Shakir served as Josh Allen’s safety blanket for much of the first half, but he was quiet for much of the second half. Most of his production came on a 51-yard catch-and-run, where he broke a few tackles and got the Bills into the red zone. On another catch-and-run opportunity, he had the ball punched out by two Patriots defenders for a crucial fumble. Shakir and Allen were also not on the same page on a key third-down pass that led to a punt. The Bills are going to need more from Shakir if DJ Moore (Shoulder) misses any time, but Shakir did play the second-most snaps of any receiver and ran the most routes, so his role is still there.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.headline: Khalil Shakir caught 1-of-3 targets for six yards in the Bills’ Week 3 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.analysis: The Bills’ offense was totally out of sorts in this game, and Shakir was hurt by their inability to get anything going through the air. Still, he played on 45 of their 62 snaps and ran a route on 23 of their 33 dropbacks, the second-most of any wide receiver. He’ll be in for a better game against the Patriots next week, but he remains just a desperation FLEX play right now unless the Bills are headed for a shootout.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.headline: Khalil Shakir caught 3-of-6 targets for 38 yards in the Bills’ Week 2 win over the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.analysis: Shakir continued in a gadgety role for the Bills, primarily working the short areas of the field in addition to receiving snaps out of the backfield. That could change in the immediate future after lead receiver DJ Moore departed in the second quarter with what appeared to be a significant shoulder injury. Even so, Shakir is best left on the waiver wire in all but the deepest fantasy leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: Josh Downs caught 1-of-4 targets for 13 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 12 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: This was by far Downs’ quietest game as a Chief, though his second half special teams play was rather loud. Downs made a pair of questionable decisions on fourth quarter punts, twice fielding the ball near the Chiefs’ own goal line. Neither gamble came close to working. The only good news was Downs did not cough the ball up. Downs’ snaps once again didn’t really kick up on offense, as he was on the field for just 16 plays. Perhaps that will finally, finally change in Week 13 against the Rams. For now, Downs is a boom/bust WR3 in fantasy football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: Josh Downs caught 4-of-5 targets for 59 yards in Kansas City’s Week 11 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: He made it to 17 snaps this week, Andy Reid told CBS’ crew that he was targeting 22 snaps, but the Chiefs spent most of the fourth-quarter in kill-the-clock mode. He’ll be an upside WR3 play in a game that should require the Chiefs to keep pouring it on as they play the Bills on Thanksgiving.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: Josh Downs caught 4-of-5 targets for 53 yards and a touchdown in the Chiefs’ Week 10 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: Playing sporadic snaps for most of the first half, the Chiefs finally cut Downs loose on their final drive of the second quarter and were rewarded with an 18-yard score where Downs cooked Billy Bowman in coverage. He then proceeded to see only one look after halftime, but Downs’ presence sure seemed to be creating more space for all involved. Not that Downs is that good, but that the presence of any legitimate wideout was all that was needed to get this attack operating on a higher level again. With his involvement certain to ramp up quickly, Downs can be considered a solid WR3 for Week 11 against Arizona.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: Chiefs acquired WR Josh Downs and a 2027 seventh-round pick from the Colts for a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2027 fifth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: It was an obvious fit. Downs will slot in as Kansas City’s No. 2 wideout behind Rashee Rice and his fantasy stock receives a slight upgrade — though we felt like we’ve spent all year saying that and never seeing any actual returns for it — while Xavier Worthy moves back to the undesirable FLEX shadow zone. The Colts had to make this trade as Downs was a free agent at year’s end, but it has left them with a completely indecipherable wideout room. Ashton Dulin is perhaps the No. 1 target Daniel Jones has outside of Tyler Warren and Jonathan Taylor.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: ESPN’s Stephen Holder believes Josh Downs “is finding that he is best suited to play the role he has always played.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: The Colts have given Downs the opportunity to expand his offensive involvement this year, but he has struggled to capitalize on it without Alec Piece (heel) on the field to keep defenses honest. Downs reportedly asked for a trade roughly two weeks ago, and per Holder, the relationship between Downs and the Colts isn’t “the best” right now. If they can’t get adequate trade value, they may choose to keep him, while also using the lack of a substantial offer as a counterpoint to his recent disgruntlement. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: Josh Downs caught 3-of-6 targets for 24 yards in the Colts’ Week 9 loss to the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: Downs saw numerous snaps in coverage by his younger brother, Caleb Downs, and was unable to return a usable fantasy outing for the seventh time in nine appearances for the Colts this season. The subject of significant trade speculation ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline, Downs appears likely to be headed for a change of scenery in a contract year, with the Colts reportedly already holding an offer in hand. More to come from one of fantasy’s most disappointing mid-round selections.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Colts have told teams they’ve received an offer of a fourth-round pick for WR Josh Downs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: The Colts’ original asking price for Downs, who has requested a trade, was a third-round pick. Indianapolis has told teams they already have an offer of a fourth-round pick for the 25-year-old receiver, who is in the last year of his rookie contract. Downs is probably one of the more likelier players to be traded ahead of the deadline. Teams have also called the Colts about Keenan Allen, though he’s unlikely to bring back a similar trade return given his age.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer reports that Josh Downs “leads the wide receiver market” ahead of the NFL trade deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: Downs’ 2026 season has fallen short of expectations, but perhaps he has a chance to rebound. Breer believes acquiring Downs would “probably” cost a fourth-round pick. He is “one of a number of receivers on the market” at the moment, with the Chiefs and Steelers among the teams looking for help at the position. Breer adds that the 49ers are “open” to adding a wide receiver as well, but with their positional health improving, San Francisco is “less desperate than they were a couple of weeks ago.” The Steelers’ wide receiver corps might be too muddled for Downs to meaningfully increase his productivity, but landing in Kansas City or San Francisco would likely be good for him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins believes the Rams must find a way to trade for a wide receiver before the November 10th deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: The Rams’ resources are thin. They already traded away their 2027 first- and second-round picks, their 2028 second-round pick and their 2029 third-round pick. They also have just $8,000 in 2026 salary cap space, so restructuring the potential new add’s deal would be required. Atkins believes the Rams should consider Josh Downs as the top option due to his ability to beat man coverage and contribute as a returner. Other options, according to Atkins, include Calvin Ridley, Keenan Allen and Jauan Jennings, “for the likely cost of a Day 3 pick.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: A to Z Sports’ Charles Goldman reports that if the Chiefs trade for a wide receiver, the team “would like to acquire a long-term fixture rather than a one-year rental.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: Chiefs coach Andy Reid told reporters today that general manager Brett Veach has been constantly sharing potential trade targets with the coaching staff for about a month. According to Goldman, the Chiefs could also target additions along the offensive and defensive lines, but he believes the team would “likely have to acquire a receiver through other means” before focusing on the trenches. There aren’t many free agency options right now, though, so it is unclear how this scenario would play out. Goldman notes that Josh Downs and Brian Thomas Jr. “have surfaced in trade discussions.” He does not think the Chiefs will make a move before Sunday, though a move early next week, before the November 10th trade deadline, is still possible.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Xavier Worthy was held without a catch on three targets in the Chiefs’ Week 12 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: It was a rainy, wind-swept night in Buffalo, but Patrick Mahomes still managed to have a decent evening. The same was not true for his former No. 2 receiver, who “zero balled” even as also-rans like Cyrus Allen and Jalen Royals caught passes. Held to just two catches in three games since Josh Downs’ Kansas City arrival, Worthy is turning into a tough hold even in 14-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Xavier Worthy caught 2-of-4 targets for 38 yards and a touchdown in Kansas City’s Week 11 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: The touchdown had the feel of a vanity project as the Chiefs, who targeted him one time in the first half, peppered Worthy with targets up 27-7 in the second half. After dropping a deep ball (as per usual) earlier in the drive, Worthy found his way by tiptoeing the sideline on a short pass. It remains a hard-to-trust FLEX path for Worthy as even Cyrus Allen out-gained him here. Worthy played 47-of-72 snaps.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Xavier Worthy was held without a reception on three targets in the Chiefs’ Week 10 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: With Josh Downs making his Chiefs debut, Patrick Mahomes had his best game since 2022. Worthy, sadly, could not get in on the fun, turning in his first 2026 “zero ball” while only really popping up during the broadcast when he failed to corral a fourth quarter onside kick attempt. Worthy was playing through a hamstring injury, but he did not look much worse for the wear. Today was sad confirmation that what little WR4 value Worthy had left is probably now gone with Downs’ arrival. That includes even for plus dates like next week’s contest with the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Xavier Worthy (hamstring) is not on the Chiefs’ final injury report and will play in Week 10 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: Patrick Mahomes will have his speedy wide receiver on the field this weekend. Unfortunately for Worthy, he may be operating in a reduced role with Josh Downs now in Kansas City. Worthy can still be rostered in 12-team formats, but his play could be even more volatile.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Xavier Worthy (hamstring) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: We got word early on Wednesday that Worthy would suit up for practice. He ended up being a full participant and remained full today, putting him firmly on track to play in Week 10 against the Falcons. Worthy is down to being a touchdown-dependent FLEX with Josh Downs now on the roster, but his presence helps out Patrick Mahomes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Xavier Worthy (hamstring) practiced on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: Head coach Andy Reid told reporters Worthy is “actually feeling pretty good.” Worthy went down with a hamstring injury late in the Chiefs’ win over the Jets on Sunday. The fact that he’s able to practice in any capacity today suggests he will be good to go for Week 10 against the Falcons. With Josh Downs now in the mix for targets, Worthy’s days as a relevant fantasy option appear to be over.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Xavier Worthy sustained a hamstring injury in Week 9 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: Worthy hobbled off the field after a fourth quarter reception in the KC victory. It appeared to be the serious kind of hamstring injury but we won’t know the extent of it until the team tests the speedy receiver. Worthy had caught all six of his targets for 48 yards before exiting the game. An absence of Worthy would likely free up more targets for Travis Kelce and Rashee Rice. The team’s running backs could also see an uptick in targets if Worthy misses time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Xavier Worthy caught 3-of-6 targets for 13 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 8 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: With Rashee Rice back after missing two games because of a hamstring issue, Worthy was relegated to WR2 duties once again. Per usual, he didn’t do much while Rice racked up PPR-friendly receptions. Worthy was, however, the intended target on a pair of red zone attempts in the third quarter. Pat Surtain easily broke up one pass that was left a bit short and Worthy actually fought to knock another one down that should have been intercepted by Riley Moss. Worthy has topped 25 yards in one game with Rice again. He’s simply not a part of the Chiefs’ plans on offense when they’re at full strength. Fantasy managers can feel free to cut him loose on this week’s run of waivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Xavier Worthy caught 3-of-6 targets for 11 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 7 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: Worthy struggled to separate from primary coverage of the Seahawks throughout, also committing a drop in a crucial situation in the second half. The Chiefs continue to show hesitancy in utilizing Worthy in a downfield role, which is of particular concern for his fantasy managers considering the absence of Tyquan Thornton. Worthy is better left on fantasy benches ahead of a Week 8 meeting with the stingy Broncos, particularly if Rashee Rice returns from injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Xavier Worthy caught all seven of his targets for 73 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 6 win against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: The Chiefs, with Rashee Rice (hamstring) sidelined, made every effort to force feed Worthy near the line of scrimmage in this one. That resulted in Worthy leading the KC offense in both targets and receiving yards, with a long reception of 19 yards. Most of his Week 6 touches were of the gadget variety. Increased usage should give Worthy a sturdy PPR floor for now. He should be considered a flex play next week against the tough Seattle secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid caught 2-of-2 targets for 13 yards in the Bills’ Week 12 win over the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: Two catches looks bad until you realize Josh Allen completed only 10 throws in a rain-marred affair. It’s still sadly unsurprising Kincaid was one of the biggest victims of a run-heavy game environment. Rather amazingly, tonight was the fifth time in 10 2026 appearances Kincaid was held to three-or-fewer targets. He’s becoming more of a fringe TE1 than locked-in option, though the return of byes for Week 13 means he will probably still crack the top 12 against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) is active for Week 12 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: As expected, Kincaid will play after getting in a couple of limited practices ahead of the Thanksgiving showdown with the Chiefs. He should be treated as a lower-end TE1 for the contest. The Bills inactives versus Kansas City will be CB Christian Benford, WR Skyler Bell, S Jalon Kilgore, OLB Mike Danna, OT Jude Bowry and DL Greg Gaines.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) is questionable for Week 12 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: Kincaid was limited in practice all week but said he would most likely play. The Bills also listed Christian Benford (groin), T.J. Sanders (shoulder), O’Cyrus Torrence (ankle), and Dorian Williams (calf) as limited for Thursday night after a week of limited practices for each player.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) was limited in Tuesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: Kincaid talked to reporters after practice and said he is “most likely” playing on Thanksgiving. Not a surprise after a pair of limited sessions, it seems like the Bills simply used their Week 11 game against the Dolphins as an exhibition to rest Kincaid ahead of the Chiefs game. He’ll be on the TE1 line if, as expected, he goes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) was listed as limited on Monday’s estimated injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: Kincaid missed Week 11’s game against the Dolphins with the same set of injuries despite being questionable entering the weekend. It’s quite possible the decision to sit him against the one-win Dolphins was more of a precautionary one ahead of the Bills’ Week 12 matchup against the Chiefs. We’ll see how the rest of his week unfolds, but Kincaid practicing in any capacity this week should be viewed as a good sign for his availability.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid is inactive for Week 11 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: Kincaid was listed as questionable with (thumb/ankle) injuries, but he will not suit up. This makes sense as a cautionary move for the Bills, who already ruled out starting cornerback Christian Benford and starting linebacker Dorian Williams. The Bills are nearly a 17-point favorite against the Dolphins on Sunday and then will face the Chiefs on Thursday night. Except Dawson Knox to be more involved in this game in Week 11, but we wouldn’t be surprised if the Bills are running the ball a lot in the second half. The Bills’ full inactives are: WR Skyler Bell, TE Dalton Kincaid, OT Jude Bowry, DL T.J. Sanders, ILB Dorian Williams, OLB Mike Danna, and CB Christian Benford.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Bills coach Joe Brady said Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) is doubtful for Buffalo’s Week 11 game against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: Kincaid has not practiced yet this week and we’re guessing from this designation he won’t be heading to the field on Friday either. This has, sadly, become pretty standard for Kincaid as he simply has to be managed week-to-week on the injury report. Dawson Knox should join the TE2 ranks for Week 11 assuming Kincaid is out, though it’s plausible Kincaid’s fantasy managers can do better on the wire.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: This is a little concerning. Backup plans should be made at this time. Kincaid played through the ankle injury in Week 10 against the Jets, but evidently picked up a thumb injury along the way. Dawson Knox would only be a TE2 if Kincaid sits, but the Dolphins’ defense is hardly imposing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) did not practice on Wednesday.
