https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: Kincaid played through the ankle injury last week, catching two passes for 58 yards. The thumb injury is new and likely happened in-game. Kincaid has successfully played through multiple injuries this season, so we are optimistic about his availability for the Bills’ Week 11 game against the Dolphins, though Buffalo may be able to run out the clock with ease on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid caught 2-of-3 passes for 58 yards in the Bills’ Week 10 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: Kincaid had one huge play in the third quarter, with a 54-yard catch down the sideline. There wasn’t much else to his day, but he was targeted in the end zone on a play that wound up being called defensive pass interference. He remains more of a high-end TE2 in a crowded passing attack in Buffalo.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: Emmett Johnson rushed 17 times for 72 yards and a touchdown in the Chiefs’ Week 12 loss to the Bills, adding four catches for 24 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: Johnson made his third start in place of an injured Kenneth Walker this week. While the Bills did a far better job of bottling up the rookie than either of Johnson’s previous opponents, they still couldn’t shut him down entirely. After a quiet first half, Johnson punched in a goal line touchdown on the Chiefs’ opening drive of the third quarter. Johnson still managed 96 yards from scrimmage and what will almost certainly be another RB1 weekly finish, even with the Chiefs’ offense amounting to little in a torrential downpour. Walker practiced this week, but the Chiefs didn’t want to rush him back for a short turnaround to Thanksgiving. He now has seven days to get ready for the Chiefs’ Week 13 game against the Rams. We suspect he’ll be active, which will relegate Johnson to a change-of-pace role. Fantasy managers, however, won’t want to cut one of the league’s most valuable backups loose, even if his role is set to decline.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports Ken Walker (groin) is out for Week 12 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: Walker was always going to be a long shot to suit up for KC’s Thanksgiving night game against Buffalo. This will be the third straight game in which Walker has been sidelined, leaving Emmett Johnson as the team’s workhorse back for at least one more week. Johnson over the past two weeks is fourth in rush yards, ninth in explosive run rate, 14th in rush yards over expected per attempt, and fourth in missed tackles forced per attempt. In other words, he’s good. Johnson will be a top-10 option against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said Ken Walker (ankle) will participate in practice Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: “I’m not anticipating a ton of work,” Reid said of Walker, who has missed two straight games and did not practice Monday ahead of the team’s Thanksgiving matchup against Buffalo. “Let’s see how does. He’s feeling pretty good.” If he practices today and Wednesday, Walker should be active for Thursday night. The Chiefs have committed to Walker as the team’s lead back despite Emmett Johnson putting up elite numbers in his absence. Johnson would be startable only in deeper fantasy leagues if Walker is good to go for Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: Kenneth Walker (groin) was listed as DNP on Monday’s estimated injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: This wasn’t the news fantasy managers were looking for after going without Walker for each of the last two weeks. The Chiefs’ RB1 has been sidelined with a groin injury he suffered ahead of Week 10’s game against the Falcons, but there was early hope it would be a one-game absence. It was widely believed the decision to sit him against the woeful Cardinals was made to give him additional time to heal up before Week 12’s game against the Bills, but Monday’s DNP now draws his availability against Buffalo into question. The Chiefs didn’t officially practice today, but Walker would not have been present if they did. If he can’t get on the field in even a limited capacity on Tuesday, it would be fair to say he’s trending in the wrong direction ahead of Thursday’s marquee matchup. If Walker is unable to play, Emmett Johnson would be a fringe RB1 after strong performances in back-to-back weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: Chiefs OC Eric Bieniemy said Kenneth Walker (groin) will “remain the starter” when he returns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: Rookie Emmett Johnson has rushed for 45-206-1 in two games without Walker this season, which has led some to wonder what role Walker could have when he returns from his groin injury. Walker, who currently ranks fifth in the league in rushing yards (872) and leads the league in yards per carry (5.5) could return as early as this Thursday when the Bills play host to the Chiefs on Thanksgiving, and from the sound of things, it would be safe to say he will be in line for plenty of work. Speaking Monday with the media, Bieniemy said that while Johnson has been impressive in his two games as a starter, the Chiefs “also understand the value [Walker] brings as well.” His practice status will be one to monitor this week, but if he’s active, Walker would be an easy must-start in what could be a high-scoring affair.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: Emmett Johnson rushed 23 times for 105 yards and a touchdown in Kansas City’s Week 11 win over the Cardinals, adding four catches for 38 yards on four targets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: Frankly, they didn’t need him much after they established a 14-0 lead early. Johnson played 59-of-70 snaps, mostly ceding work to Jadyn Ott after the game was over. 92 of his total yards happened before halftime. With 171 total yards from scrimmage last game and 143 in this one, Johnson joins a pretty fun list of rookie runners since 2020 to pop 300 total yards in two games that includes Bucky Irving, Jahmyr Gibbs, De’Von Achane, Breece Hall, Najee Harris and Jonathan Taylor. He’s likely a reasonable FLEX starter next week even if Kenneth Walker (groin) is back. If Walker is not back, skip straight to smash RB1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: Chiefs ruled out Kenneth Walker (groin) for Week 11 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: The Chiefs face the lowly Cardinals this week, but they face the Bills next week. Allowing Walker to fully heal in time for that important matchup makes sense. Stud rookie Emmett Johnson remains a fantasy football RB1 after an explosive showing against the Falcons last week. Walker will vault back into the RB1 tier upon returning.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: Ken Walker (groin) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: It’s looking more and more like Walker will miss a second straight game with his groin issue. NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said Tuesday that he wouldn’t be surprised if Walker sat again in Week 11 against the Cardinals. “He had a sore groin (last week). It’s getting better,” head coach Andy Reid said. “We just don’t want to do something stupid. ... He’s feeling better.” Emmett Johnson, fresh off a monster outing in Week 10, would get another start and profile as a top-5 fantasy option. Johnson will face a Cardinals defense allowing the fifth lowest fantasy points per opportunity to running backs this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said he “wouldn’t be surprised” if Kenneth Walker sat in Week 11 to make sure that his groin is fully healed.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: The crux of this appears to be that Emmett Johnson did so well that there’s no need to rush Walker back to the field. We’ll see how the practice reports trend, but a pop-up groin injury on Friday to a rule-out Saturday never felt like something that assured Walker was playing in Week 11. This will be one to monitor on the practice reports all week, especially with six teams on bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: Emmett Johnson rushed 22 times for 101 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 10 win over the Falcons, adding six receptions for 70 yards and two touchdowns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: Making a spot start in place of Kenneth Walker III (groin), fifth-round rookie Johnson was electric from the opening whistle, routinely tacking on extra yardage by either dragging tacklers or simply juking them out of their cleats. Johnson almost never took a negative play, and was so, so slippery in the open field or with any steam whatsoever. He was the Chiefs’ No. 2 receiver with 6/70/2, and actually the most targeted with seven looks. It was the kind of all-around performance we knew was possible from Johnson’s pre-draft profile but that we just have not seen because of Walker’s dominance. With Walker truly questionable for Week 11 against the Cardinals until we hear otherwise, Johnson would be an RB1 if given another start against the lowly Birds. Even if Walker goes, Johnson’s FLEX standing is now on much firmer ground.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.headline: James Cook rushed 32 times for 117 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 12 win over the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.analysis: Sportsbooks correctly cratered the total of this game throughout the week to account for gusting winds, pouring rain, and a chilly temperature. Joe Brady’s response to these miserable conditions was to feed his top back for all four quarters. Cook set a season-high in carries and scored his 10th straight rushing touchdown. Buffalo’s lead back didn’t score in Week 1 and has found the end zone in every subsequent game. Cook will be a good bet to find the end zone at least once when he takes on the downtrodden Patriots next week. Per usual, Cook will be a top-five fantasy option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.headline: James Cook rushed 22 times for 89 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 11 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.analysis: With this effort, Cook has set an NFL record with nine consecutive games with 75+ rushing yards and a touchdown. Only two other players in NFL history had done it for eight games in a row. It’s the perfect encapsulation of Cook’s fantasy value on this Buffalo offense. The presence of Josh Allen will limit the number of touchdowns and ceiling games Cook puts together, but he remains one of the most consistent producers at the running back position in fantasy football. He remains an RB1, even in a tough matchup against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.headline: James Cook rushed 18 times for 157 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 10 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.analysis: The Bills leaned on Cook heavily in this one, not showing much of a belief that the Jets were going to pile up many points on offense. It was a solid day overall for Cook, but he then ripped off a career-high 74-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter that not only sealed the win for the Bills but also made it a big fantasy day for Cook. The 27-year-old could have had an even bigger day, but he dropped what likely would have been a 15-yard touchdown catch. Cook should be a rock-solid RB1 next week against the Dolphins as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.headline: James Cook rushed 31 times for 107 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 9 win over the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.analysis: Cook struggled to 2.7 yards per carry through the first three quarters but made his mark felt in the final frame, adding his lone rushing score in the fourth quarter to bring his season total to eight. The yardage total also pushed him over 5,000 career rush yards, doing so in the same game as Josh Allen to become the first quarterback and running back duo to achieve 5,000 career rush yards in the same season. Cook has now scored in seven straight games as he continues his bid for one of the top fantasy running backs in the league. He remains an elite RB1 ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.headline: James Cook rushed 21 times for 80 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 8 win over the Ravens, adding two receptions for 21 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.analysis: Cook paced the Bills on the ground all afternoon, picking up one key first down after another in a game where the offense struggled a bit in the first half. On the Bills’ first possession of the second half, Cook rushed three times for 20 yards, capping the drive with a five-yard rushing touchdown to bring his season total to seven scores on the ground. He exited briefly in the fourth quarter to be evaluated for a concussion, but was able to return. Cook will be in the RB1 conversation next week despite a tough road matchup against the Vikings in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.headline: James Cook rushed 22 times for 95 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 6 win over the Raiders, adding three receptions for 58 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.analysis: Cook had a much-needed bounce-back game in Sunday’s win over the Raiders. A week after he fumbled twice in an overtime win over the Rams, Cook secured the football for all four quarters and broke off multiple explosive plays while handling 22 of the Bills’ 24 running back carries. His lone rushing touchdown came on a three-yard run in the fourth quarter, and came one play after Cook ripped off a 26-yard reception on a third-and-three to keep the chains moving. Concerns about ball security may follow Cook for the remainder of the season, but his role in the Bills’ offense continues to provide valuable production in both real and fantasy football. He will be locked in as an RB1 in Week 8 against the Ravens when the Bills return from their Week 7 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.headline: Bills coach Joe Brady said James Cook needs to protect the ball or he’s going to get fewer carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.analysis: “At some point, there has to be consequences,” Brady said about his lead back, who has fumbled four times in five games this season, including twice on Monday night. Cook has played 67.3 percent of the team’s snaps, and this probably isn’t a threat to his lead back status, but it wouldn’t be surprising if he sat on the bench for a spell if he fumbled in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.headline: James Cook rushed 25 times for 111 yards and two touchdowns in the Bills’ Week 5 win over the Rams, adding seven yards on one reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.analysis: Cook’s elite rushing line was overshadowed by two fumbles, the second of which was a lost fumble on the team’s first possession of overtime, placing the Rams in position to complete the comeback and steal away the victory. A blocked field goal on what would have been the game-winning kick breathed new life into the Bills, who demonstrated confidence in their lead back by throwing him right back out there on the following possession to eventually win the game. The 26 touches go down as a season high for the veteran back, who found paint for the fourth consecutive game in the thrilling overtime win. Cook remains a top-tier RB1 for fantasy purposes ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Raiders in Las Vegas.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.headline: James Cook rushed 12 times for 75 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 4 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.analysis: He added two catches for either yards. This game was never more than a one-score game, so it’s pretty shocking that Cook only had 14 touches. The Patriots did a good job containing him early in the game, apart from his touchdown run, but the Bills simply moved away from the running game too quickly. Cook was gaining huge chunk yards in the second half and should have been fed more carries during the game. With the Bills having their second straight mediocre offensive performance, you have to wonder if they will make it a point to lean on Cook more next week against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.headline: James Cook rushed 24 times for 154 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 3 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.analysis: Cook was the only running back to get a carry on the day, and he ripped off over six yards per rush. He got the Bills down inside the two-yard line twice but watched as Josh Allen ran it into the end zone each time. On the third trip deep into the red zone, Cook rushed it in from four yards out. With Ty Johnson back, Cook did cede some passing game work; however, Cook also played 42 of the team’s 62 snaps, compared to just 15 snaps for Johnson. The lack of receiving may prevent Cook from being a top-five running back, but he’s a clear RB1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: DJ Moore caught 2-of-6 targets for 15 yards in the Bills’ Week 12 win over the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: On a rain-drenched, run-heavy night in Buffalo, Josh Allen completed only 10 passes. Translation, there wasn’t a whole lot for Moore to do even as he tied for the team lead in looks. That being said, volume has not been Moore’s strong suit this season, as he’s averaging just six targets. Although that number is skewed a bit by an injury-shortened Week 2, Moore hasn’t quite had the alpha role fantasy managers had in mind. He is still pacing as a solid option on the WR2/3 borderline, one whose best football could arguably still be ahead of him. The Patriots could go either way as a Week 13 road matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: DJ Moore caught 8-of-10 targets for 91 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 11 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: There was a scary moment in the second quarter when Moore jumped to try and break up an interception and came down hard, hyperextending his knee. He went right into the locker room, and it seemed like he might be done for the day, but he came back out in time for the next drive. There’s a chance the Bills give him a lighter week of practice with the Chiefs coming up on Thursday, but Moore will need to be a big part of the game plan if Buffalo is going to win that game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: DJ Moore caught 4-of-6 targets for 90 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 10 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: Bills saw twice as many targets as the next most-targeted player on the Bills, and connected with Josh Allen on a deep 45-yard touchdown pass in the third quarter. When he’s been healthy, Moore has been a really solid weapon in this Buffalo offense, and should be a high-end WR2 next week against the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: DJ Moore caught 3-of-5 targets for 25 yards in the Bills’ Week 9 win over the Vikings, adding 11 yards on one carry.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: The carry was really a pass that barely went backwards on a screen in the fourth quarter, bringing his yardage total on the evening to 36. Moore has struggled through injury during his first season in Buffalo and has returned a viable fantasy outing in two of five healthy games. His next opportunity comes in Week 10 against the Jets, where he will be a middling WR3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: DJ Moore (shoulder) was limited on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: The Bills are managing Moore’s AC joint sprain fairly well. He should be expected to play in Week 9’s Monday Night Football game against the Vikings. Although it is a tough matchup, Moore remains the WR2 tier in this week’s final game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: DJ Moore (shoulder) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: There was some concern that Moore may have injured his knee in Week 8 against the Ravens, but he is listed only with the same shoulder issue he has dealt with for weeks, which is good news. Moore should be treated as a WR2 in a very tough matchup against the Vikings on Monday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: DJ Moore caught 4-of-7 targets for 82 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 8 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: Moore’s 82 receiving yards trailed only Dalton Kincaid (86). Playing in his first game since Week 4, Moore did not appear to be slowed at all by his injured shoulder and bounced back quickly on a play where he appeared to land hard on the turf. Moore hauled in an impressive 49-yard grab in the third quarter on a drive that helped set up James Cook for a five-yard rushing touchdown, and found the end zone himself in the fourth quarter on an 11-yard score that gave Josh Allen the Bills’ franchise record for career touchdown passes. The seven targets Moore saw were on par with what have come to expect from him pre-injury, which is a good sign for him going forward. He appeared to suffer a minor knee injury near the end of the game, but said afterward it wasn’t too serious. That will be something to monitor, but assuming he’s good to go, Moore will be on the WR2 radar next week on the road against the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: DJ Moore (shoulder) is active for the Bills’ Week 8 game against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: Moore and TE Dalton Kincaid are both officially active, giving the Bills two of their top playmakers in what projects as one of the best matchups of the Week 8 slate against the Ravens. Moore returns for his first game since Week 4 and has caught 12 passes for 178 yards and one touchdown on 19 targets. He’ll profile as a fringe WR1/WR2 at home. The Bills declared WR Skyler Bell, CB Dee Alford, S Jalon Kilgore, LB Mike Danna, OG Ar’maj Reed-Adams, OT Spencer Brown, and DL Greg Gaines inactive for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports DJ Moore (shoulder) is expected to play in Week 8 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: Moore missed the Bills’ previous two games but had the bye week to get healthy. He was limited in practice throughout the week before being listed as questionable. He’s likely still not at full strength, but fantasy managers can’t be too concerned given the game environment. The Bills’ matchup with Baltimore has all of the makings of a shootout. Moore was also operating as Josh Allen’s clear No. 1 receiver before aggravating his shoulder injury. Moore is a strong WR2 option for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: Bills coach Joe Brady said DJ Moore (shoulder) is questionable for Buffalo’s Week 8 game against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: Moore has practiced with a non-contact jersey on, in a limited fashion, both of the first two days of the practice week after coming off bye. He got in a third limited session on Friday. This isn’t exactly an exciting run-out after the bye, but Moore probably is on the optimistic side of questionable and any fantasy player that is breathing should be elevated in a game projected to have Josh Allen and Lamar Jackson at quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.headline: Josh Allen completed 10-of-21 passes for 81 yards and two interceptions in the Bills’ 13-10, Week 12 win over the Chiefs, adding seven carries for 43 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.analysis: Playing in a cold downpour in Buffalo, it was a sloppy mess of a game for Allen, who posted his worst passing line of the year by every metric. The two interceptions, however, can’t be put entirely on him. The first was a tipped pass in the red zone that fell into the hands of a Chiefs defensive back. The second was a screen to Khalil Shakir, which was bobbled directly into the hands of Chiefs corner Nohl Williams. Even if you toss out the interceptions as bad luck, Week 12 was still the lowlight of his season and then some. The last time Allen completed fewer than half of his passes was Week 5 of the 2024 season. He averaged fewer than four yards per attempt for the first time since 2019. For fantasy purposes, Allen’s issues were compounded by a lack of volume, which has been a recurring theme for the Buffalo offense this year. While we aren’t expecting the team to air it out versus the struggling Patriots next week, Allen should at least be far more efficient in Week 13. He remains the QB1 overall with ease despite the Thanksgiving bust.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler said he expected the Bills offense to be “more complex” in Week 12 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.analysis: Fowler suggested the Bills kept the game plan as simple as possible last week against the inferior Dolphins, with Josh Allen throwing 45 passes from the pocket and failing to log a single rushing attempt after averaging 7.1 rushes per game coming into Week 11. Fowler said the Bills might have wanted to hide offensive wrinkles ahead of their Thanksgiving night matchup against Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs. The Bills-Chiefs game offers a good fantasy environment and should feature plenty of scoring, though the KC defense allows the second lowest rate of fantasy points per drop back on the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.headline: Josh Allen completed 27-of-45 passes for 304 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions in the Bills’ 26-9, Week 11 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.analysis: This was not Allen’s best effort in a game where the Bills were favored by 17 points. It almost seemed as though his coaches told him not to run, with the Bills set to face the Chiefs on Thursday. Allen didn’t run the ball a single time and passed up multiple chances to run when he rolled out. In his career, Allen has four games with zero rushing attempts. Three of them were season finales. The other was today. There were even opportunities for him to take off up the middle, but he actually backtracked into sacks. As a result, this was one of his worst games this season from a decision-making standpoint, and the Bills’ offense was very inconsistent. Still, Allen did throw for 300 yards, but the Bills will have to hope that he looks more in control on Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.headline: Josh Allen completed 11-of-21 passes for 196 yards with one touchdown and one interception in the Bills’ 31-12, Week 10 win over the Jets, adding two rushing touchdowns on the ground.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.analysis: The Bills leaned heavily on James Cook in this one, with Allen dropping back to pass just 21 times. When the Bills did pass, they took a few big shots down the field, which resulted in a long touchdown pass to D.J. Moore, but also a long interception on third down in what was ultimately an “arm punt.” Of Allen’s two rushing touchdowns, only one of them was on a tush push. The Bills quarterback has now rushed for 10+ touchdowns in four straight seasons, tying Jalen Hurts (2021-24) for the longest streak by a quarterback in NFL history, and he has 324 total touchdowns in his career, which is now the most by any player in their first 10 seasons in NFL history. He will look for another big fantasy day in Week 11 against the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.headline: Josh Allen completed 21-of-31 passes for 234 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Bills’ 23-6, Week 9 win over the Vikings, adding 15 yards on six carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.analysis: The career accolades continued to pile on for Allen, who became the fifth quarterback in NFL history to rush for 5,000 yards in his career with 15 yards on the ground against the Vikings. Furthermore, in one of the more wild statistics you will ever see, Allen and running back James Cook each surpassed 5,000 career rush yards on the same drive, becoming the first quarterback and running back duo to achieve 5,000 career rush yards in the same season. The Bills surge to 7-1 with the win and extend their lead on in the AFC East following the loss by the Patriots on Sunday. Allen and company earned every bit of it in this one, fighting through consistent pressure from the aggressive and tenacious Minnesota defense, the latter of whom kept the game within reason deep into the fourth quarter. Allen remains the top overall fantasy quarterback ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Jets on the road.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.headline: Josh Allen completed 21-of-34 passes for 289 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the Bills’ 36-10, Week 8 win over the Ravens, adding seven carries for 30 additional yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.analysis: Allen set the Bills’ franchise record for passing touchdowns in the fourth quarter when he completed an 11-yard pass to DJ Moore to put the Bills up 29-10. He added to his total a few minutes later when he connected with Dalton Kincaid down the right sideline for a 23-yard score, as the Bills trounced the hapless Ravens, who were down to their third QB midway through the second quarter. Allen and the Bills’ offense struggled at times, but eventually made the most of multiple possessions, thanks in part to three Ravens turnovers and multiple short drives. Allen also found the end zone on the ground in this one, and came up short of a second rushing score in the second quarter when he was tackled for a three-yard loss while trying to break a run to the outside. Allen and the Bills draw a tough road matchup against the Vikings in Week 9, but Allen is a must-start QB regardless of matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.headline: Josh Allen completed 23-of-33 passes for 255 yards and two touchdowns in the Bills’ 33-30, Week 6 win over the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.analysis: The Raiders did their part to keep Allen in the pocket in this one. He managed just one rushing yard on five carries, but did plenty of damage through the air to put the Bills in position to pull out their fifth win of the season. Allen threw his first touchdown of the day to Khalil Shakir in the second quarter on a nine-yard screen pass, and flipped an impressive shovel pass to Keon Coleman in the third quarter for his second touchdown pass of the day. Allen and the Bills have scored 30-plus points in four of their first six games this season, with Allen totaling four touchdowns in his last two games. The Bills punted just twice in this one, and Allen led his team on three straight scoring drives to start the game. While there’s plenty to figure out on defense, Allen and the offense are clicking on all cylinders even with DJ Moore (shoulder) sidelined. The Bills now head into their Week 7 bye week and will return in Week 8 to play host to the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.headline: Josh Allen completed 12-of-19 passes for 210 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Bills’ 37-34, Week 5 win over the Rams, adding 121 yards and a touchdown on 10 carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.analysis: The two teams mustered only 20 combined points in the first half as they felt each other out. There were only two punts after the break between the two sides, who combined for seven touchdowns on nine combined possessions including five straight touchdowns in the fourth quarter to send the game to overtime. Allen and the Bills took the ball first in the extra frame and quickly found themselves deep in enemy territory following a 57-yard, catch-and-run pass to Khalil Shakir. A James Cook fumble on the next play appeared to shatter Allen’s chances of earning his first career win in overtime, but a blocked 48-yard field goal attempt from Harrison Mevis gave the ball back to the Bills with a chance to win. Two Josh Allen scrambles set up a game-winning, 45-yard field goal for Tyler Bass. Allen ended with the second most yards on the ground of his career as the Bills moved to 4-1 with the wild win. Allen remains the top overall quarterback in fantasy circles ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Raiders on the road.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.headline: Josh Allen completed 23-of-33 passes for 253 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Bills’ 29-26 Week 4 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.analysis: Allen did score a rushing touchdown, but he had just four rushing yards on five carries, making this the second straight game that he was contained as a rusher. Every time Allen rolled out, the Patriots had a defender in the lane, and Allen wasn’t able to make his usual big plays with his arm. Once D.J. Moore left the game with a shoulder injury, it felt like none of the Bills’ receivers were able to create space with their defenders, much like we saw for all of 2025. Allen’s interception was an egregious decision on the final drive of the game, where he made an impressive spin move to avoid a sack and then chucked an unnecessary Hail Mary into double coverage. You’re still starting Allen in fantasy leagues, but it’s a bit concerning that we’ve seen the Bills’ offense look scattered and out of sync for two straight games. It won’t get easier on Monday against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.headline: Josh Allen completed 16-of-26 passes for 204 yards and two interceptions in the Bills’ 24-16, Week 3 win over the Chargers, adding 22 yards rushing and two touchdowns on the ground.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.analysis: Allen certainly wasn’t good in this one, but he wasn’t alone. The Bills turned the ball over five times, committed 10 penalties, and allowed four sacks and somehow won this game. His first interception was on a truly bad read over the middle of the field. The second was on a deep pass into coverage when Allen thought he had drawn an offside. The pass managed to hit the safety in the back and then land in his stomach when he rolled over after hitting the ground. Allen would also fumble on a sack later in the game. The Chargers did a good job of taking Allen’s scrambles away, and this entire Bills team was in disarray, so nobody was consistently open down the field. That being said, Allen’s two rushing touchdowns give him 85 for his career, which means he’s now tied with former Bill Marshawn Lynch for 17th on the NFL’s all-time list. The Bills and Allen will look to get things straightened out against the Patriots next week, and Allen will clearly be in your lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: Patrick Mahomes completed 16-of-29 passes for 174 yards in the Chiefs’ 13-10, Week 12 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: Neither Mahomes nor Josh Allen was able to get much going in what was supposed to be the game of the season. With rain drenching the field and pelting players, there was simply no way for either team to consistently string together successful passes. The Chiefs also committed several special teams blunders, including but not limited to a botched snap and subsequent shank by punter Matt Araiza, a tipped punt, and yet another missed field goal by Harrison Butker. Not to be outdone, Mahomes bungled multiple snaps of his own. The elements and Buffalo’s resurgent defense combined to shut down Mahomes, who entered the week riding a two-game molten hot streak. The best he could do was avoid negative plays and live to fight another day. Mahomes was sacked just once and did not turn the ball over, though he had a close call in the fourth quarter with a throw-away gone awry. This game and its ugly conditions will ultimately go down as a write-off for fantasy managers who started either quarterback. Mahomes will get a QB1 redo in a week when he takes on the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: Patrick Mahomes completed 27-of-39 passes for 329 yards and three touchdowns before being pulled in the fourth quarter of Kansas City’s 34-7, Week 11 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: It was about what you would have expected. Mahomes continues to look like he has Young Mahomes Swagger with Josh Downs rejuvenating the offense. The Chiefs easily boatraced the Cardinals today and the game was never competitive after a 14-0 first-quarter start in which Arizona possessed the ball for just two of 15 minutes. Mahomes will be an easy QB1 in what should be a red-hot fantasy matchup against the Bills on Thanksgiving. Justin Fields relieved Mahomes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: Patrick Mahomes completed 22-of-35 passes for 348 yards and five touchdowns in the Chiefs’ 35-13, Week 10 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: Breaking Josh Downs into the Chiefs’ undermanned receiver corps, Mahomes ended up having his first five-score passing effort since Week 1 of the 2022 season. Heavens to Betsy. The 348 yards were also his fourth most since that MVP campaign four years ago. All this when the only addition was Josh Downs. Of course, it helped that Mahomes was facing a downtrodden, disinterested Falcons side, but it really did seem like the presence of another legitimate wideout was creating more space for everybody. That even included Rashee Rice, who caught a legitimate down-field bomb, and Andrew Armstrong, who housed a late 43-yard score where Mahomes just kind of chucked it up. Two of Mahomes’ touchdowns went to spot-starting running back Emmett Johnson, who was electric in the open field. This had the feel of a sort of deliverance for the Kansas City side, and it should continue in Week 11 against the Cardinals. The schedule stiffens after that, if not really the opposing defenses. Mahomes is back to every-week QB1 status, and should frequently be a high-end option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Patrick Mahomes suffered a “very small sprain of his UCL” and a muscle strain in Week 9 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: Mahomes’ right arm was clobbered by a Jets defender while attempting to throw a pass late in the first half of Week 9. It looked like a serious issue at first, but he managed to finish the game and didn’t even miss any practice time this week. Per Schefter, the Chiefs consulted with physicians from the Rangers and Royals, who are among the world’s best doctors when it comes to shoulder and elbow injuries. Both doctors cleared him to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: Patrick Mahomes (elbow) is practicing in full for Week 10 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: This comes directly from Andy Reid, though we’ll have to wait until the team’s injury report officially drops to be sure it’s actually a full session. Either way, Mahomes is playing on Sunday despite suffering an ugly elbow injury in Week 9. He told reporters it’s simply a matter of pain management for now. The Chiefs may opt to lean on their ground game against the Falcons, but even that won’t knock Mahomes out of the QB1 mix after the addition of Josh Downs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said Patrick Mahomes (elbow) is considered “day-to-day.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: This news comes less than 24 hours after NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported that an MRI “did not reveal a major injury” to Mahomes, who was able to finish out the game in Sunday’s win over the Jets. Reid said Mahomes is dealing with some soreness that he will have to rehab a bit, but it doesn’t sound like he’s at risk of missing any time. Mahomes threw for 242 yards and two touchdowns against the Jets and will be on the QB1 radar next week against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Patrick Mahomes’ (elbow) MRI “did not reveal a major injury.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: Rapoport adds that Mahomes’ “elbow strain/sprain will be monitored over the next few days for pain and swelling.” Without getting too deep into the weeds, there are a few things to note. First off, Rapoport sometimes reports injury news optimistically. It would have been nice to see him actually report a “minor” injury, rather than not “major.” Secondly, “strain” typically refers to muscles and tendons, while “sprain” is often used for ligaments. Using both is a tad confusing. That said, Rapoport’s follow-up statement suggests Mahomes may have a chance to play in Week 10 against the Falcons. Updates will be provided as soon as news breaks. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: Patrick Mahomes completed 23-of-41 attempts for 242 yards and two touchdowns in the Chiefs’ Week 9 win against the Jets, adding two rushes for eight yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: Mahomes was pulled with a few minutes to go in the fourth quarter with the Chiefs up multiple scores and the Jets not all that interested in staging a comeback. Mahomes overcame an injury to his right forearm in this one. He sustained the injury on a hard hit from a blitzing New York defender who bent Mahomes’ arm back awkwardly. After getting some treatment on the sideline, Mahomes re-entered the game and seemed fine, though he was seen grimacing and shaking his arm at times. This marked Mahomes’ sixth multi-touchdown game of the season. He should remain in starting lineups as a top-12 option in Week 10 against the pass-funnel Atlanta defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: Patrick Mahomes completed 30-of-41 passes for 321 yards and three touchdowns in the Chiefs’ 28-24, Week 8 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: Mahomes posted a strong box score for fantasy managers and took care of the football with zero turnovers. He also took just two sacks, but the second was one that will haunt Chiefs fans for a while. After marching the offense down to the goal line under the two-minute warning, the Chiefs found themselves on fourth-and-goal. They initially got the score via a strike to Rashee Rice, but the play was blown dead via a false start. The Broncos’ pass-rush got to him on the second try, taking Mahomes down for a game-ending sack. On the whole, it was another dink-and-dunk game plan from Mahomes, who failed to get the deep ball going once again. Luckily for him, Emmett Johnson averaged 25.6 yards per catch and turned a short toss into a 73-yard touchdown in the first half. The Chiefs get a bounce-back spot against the Jets next week in a game where Mahomes will be just inside the QB1 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: Patrick Mahomes completed 19-of-33 passes for 165 yards and one interception in the Chiefs’ 20-3, Week 7 loss to the Seahawks, adding 14 yards on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: The three points tied the fewest scored in a start in Mahomes’ career as the Chiefs suffered their first defeat of the season. Mahomes faced consistent pressure and a shrinking pocket as the Seahawks held the Chiefs to just 213 yards of total offense. Mahomes also had an ill-advised turnover as he tried to escape pressure, over-throwing his intended receiver on the run. The Chiefs fall to 5-1 with the defeat, leaving only the Vikings as the lone unbeaten team through seven weeks. Mahomes gets little time to lick his wounds with the division rival Broncos on the horizon in Week 8, where he’ll be a low end QB1 in another difficult matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-moo.headline: Elijah Moore caught 3-of-5 targets for 57 yards in the Eagles’ Week 12 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-moo.analysis: Elijah Moore catching passes from Joe Milton makes a lot of sense on August 19, but is a little more surprising on Thanksgiving. Still, the 26-year-old was able to put together a solid day and helped set up the game-winning field goal with a couple of catches on the final drive. It’s hard to imagine Moore is fantasy relevant in Week 13 against the Cardinals, but he and Milton did appear to be on the same page.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-moo.headline: Eagles signed WR Elijah Moore to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-moo.analysis: Moore spent the majority of the 2025 season with the Bills, catching nine passes for 112 yards. The 25-year-old was released in November and later signed to the Broncos’ practice squad, catching one pass for four yards in the postseason for Denver. Initially drafted by the Jets, Moore tallied over 100 targets in back-to-back seasons with the Browns from 2023-2024. He will come in to compete for depth snaps in Philly. Moore is mostly off fantasy radars for 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-moo.headline: Broncos signed WR Elijah Moore, formerly of the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-moo.analysis: Moore will start with Denver’s practice squad ahead of the team’s Week 14 game against the Raiders. Moore appeared in nine games for the Bills this season and had nine catches for 112 yards. If he’s active for the Broncos in the coming weeks, Moore would likely be a rotational player who sees limited snaps and routes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-moo.headline: Bills waived WR Elijah Moore.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-moo.analysis: The Bills this week signed veteran journeyman Brandin Cooks, making Moore expendable after he appeared in nine games for the team this season and had nine catches for 112 yards. Moore could land with a receiver-needy team in the coming weeks, though he would likely remain a rotational player. Moore had 61 receptions for 538 yards and a touchdown last year in Cleveland.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-moo.headline: Bills made Keon Coleman a healthy inactive for Week 11 against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-moo.analysis: The Bills needed to shake things up after an embarrassing loss to the Dolphins last week, and they’re doing so in a big way with their receiver room. Josh Palmer is back after being out with a groin injury since Week 6, and he figures to take over much of Keon Coleman’s work which makes him a worthwhile stash in fantasy leagues. Mecole Hardman was also signed to the active roster on Saturday night and will likely serve primarily as a return man. The Bills also elevated Gabe Davis from the practice squad, so he will return to the Bills lineup after missing the start of the year while recovering from ACL surgery. The Bills other inactives are WR Elijah Moore, LB Shaq Thompson, CB Ja’Marcus Ingram, DT Phidarian Mathis, OL Chase Lundt and TE Dalton Kincaid.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-moo.headline: Josh Palmer (knee/ankle) will not play in Week 8 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-moo.analysis: Palmer did not log a practice this week and has been ruled out ahead of Friday’s practice. The veteran receiver has logged two or fewer catches in all but one game this season and wasn’t going to be on the fantasy radar in Week 8 even with six teams on bye. His replacements, Elijah Moore and/or Curtis Samuel (ribs) can also be left out of lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-moo.headline: Elijah Moore caught his only target for 31 yards and added a rushing touchdown in a Week 2 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-moo.analysis: The Bills involved Moore far more often this week than they did in Week 1. It may have been that the Jets play more man coverage than the Ravens, but it also could be that the Bills were up early and wanted to get Moore some yardage against his old team. The big catch was on a busted coverage, and the rushing touchdown was a reverse when the Bills were already up 23-3, so we wouldn’t read too much into his fantasy point total.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-moo.headline: Bills WR Keon Coleman (groin) is off Buffalo’s final injury report for Week 1.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-moo.analysis: He’ll be a WR3/FLEX dart in Week 1 against the Ravens, though recent reports from beats that have him leading the team in targets should be of interest to fantasy managers. Coleman got in a full practice on Friday for the first time all week. Elijah Moore (personal) was also cleared off the injury report for Buffalo.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-moo.headline: Bills WR Elijah Moore (personal) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-moo.analysis: Updating a previous item, Moore missed practice today for personal reasons. Unless it is a serious issue, he will likely be on the field for the Bills’ Sunday Night Football game against the Ravens. He does not need to be in re-draft lineups, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-moo.headline: Bills WR Elijah Moore (undisclosed) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-moo.analysis: Although Moore is just 25 years old, his erratic participation and performances have seemingly been ever-present for fantasy managers in football’s modern era. We do not know why he was sidelined today, but the official injury report should clarify things. He dealt with an ambiguous leg issue in July. Moore is not worth rostering at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Makai Lemon caught 5-of-6 targets for 51 yards and a touchdown in the Eagles’ Week 12 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: Lemon was vastly improved from his disappointing one-catch against the Steelers the previous week. He brought in his first touchdown since Week 7 — also against the Cowboys — and it got the Eagles to within two points with just over two minutes left. The Eagles weren’t able to convert the two-point conversion, but still came up with the improbable victory. Lemon will try and build on this effort against the Cardinals in Week 13.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Makai Lemon caught 1-of-3 targets for one yard in the Eagles’ Week 11 win against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: Lemon was a distant afterthought in the Philly offense with DeVonta Smith returning from a hamstring injury and leading the team with 12 targets and a 57 percent target share. Lemon should not be rostered in most fantasy leagues for the remainder of the season unless Smith again misses time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Makai Lemon caught 6-of-9 targets for 61 yards in the Eagles’ Week 9 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: Lemon again led this limited offense in receiving as Joe Milton made his first start under center, but he hurt the cause with a handful of drops, including a particularly brutal one with the Eagles desperately trying to tie the game late. Lemon now has at least six catches in three straight games but has not reached 70 yards in the process. In other words, he is posting empty PPR volume. That will remain the “thesis of the play” when the Eagles come off bye in Week 11, though the return of either DeVonta Smith or Dontayvion Wicks would take a major bite out of Lemon’s WR3 appeal.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Makai Lemon caught 6-of-9 targets for 57 yards in the Eagles’ Week 8 loss to the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: Lemon led the team in receiving for the second consecutive game without both DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks, although the returns were nothing to write home about in Week 8. Largely confined to a short area role, Lemon’s nine targets were mostly the product of the offense’s inability to attack downfield and carry weak per-target upside, a trend likely to continue for as long as Tanner McKee remains under center. That leaves fantasy managers in a precarious position heading into a Week 9 showdown against the Giants, where better options likely exist.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Makai Lemon caught 7-of-8 targets for 67 yards and a touchdown in the Eagles’ Week 7 loss to the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: Lemon showed out with the best game of his career in the absence of both DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks, operating as the top option through the air throughout the game against the Cowboys. He started his night off with a 21-yard reception on the team’s first possession before adding a fourth quarter touchdown on a quick slant from four yards out. The uncertainty surrounding Smith’s injury could leave Lemon as the de facto lead receiver for a Week 8 divisional tilt against the Commanders, where his fantasy value will be strictly tied to the availability of the other receivers on the roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Makai Lemon caught 3-of-6 targets for 19 yards in the Eagles’ Week 6 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: Despite not lighting up the box score, Lemon was third on the team in targets and finished fourth in receptions. Initial reports had him playing on 52 of the team’s 64 snaps and running a route on 47 of their 52 dropbacks. That was the most routes of any receiver on the team. Some of this was because the team seemed to be easing DeVonta Smith back from injury, and Dontayvsion Wicks briefly left the game with an injury scare, but we also wouldn’t be surprised to see Lemon get more work in what is looking like a bit of a lost season in Philadelphia.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Makai Lemon caught 5-of-7 targets for 43 yards in the Eagles’ Week 5 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: The good news is that Lemon set new season highs in targets, catches, and yards. The bad news: All of that resulted in a measly 9.3 PPR points. Lemon will hopefully continue to earn more opportunities as the season progresses, but DeVonta Smith’s return could just as easily stall the rookie’s progress. Lemon will be a WR4/5 if Smith remains out for Week 6 against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) was added to the injury report on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: Wicks was listed as a limited participant today, indicating that he strained his hamstring during Thursday’s practice. With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) still sidelined, rookie WR Makai Lemon could be the de facto top receiver, though the team has struggled to use him effectively thus far. Hollywood Brown (ankle) also remains sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Makai Lemon caught 3-of-6 targets for 27 yards in the Eagles’ Week 4 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: Lemon moved up a spot in the targets pecking order with DeVonta Smith sidelined, but it resulted in the same quiet box score he posted the first three weeks of his career. The No. 20 overall pick is now sitting on 10 receptions for a scoreless 65 yards through his first four NFL appearances. There has yet to be any light at the tunnel with regards to either his usage or the Eagles’ overall offensive environment. Even with byes beginning and injuries mounting, Lemon is not a recommended WR4 heading into Week 5 against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Makai Lemon caught 3-of-4 targets for 29 yards in the Eagles’ Week 3 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: Lemon was the target on the team’s first play from scrimmage, gaining a first down on a first down play for the Eagles for the first time all season. The offense would sputter throughout the game on their way to only 47 offensive plays run from scrimmage, capping the fantasy upside of all involved in the process. Lemon has yet to live up to his lofty draft capital through the first three games of his professional career, but he could be called on for heavier work with tight end Dallas Goedert nursing an MCL sprain. Things don’t get any easier with a matchup against the Rams on deck for Week 4, where Lemon can safely be left on fantasy benches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.headline: Will Shipley rushed 10 times for 46 yards in the Eagles’ Week 12 loss to the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.analysis: Shipley took over after Saquon Barkley suffered a stinger, and while the Eagles were mostly in pass-mode because they fall behind 31-0, Shipley did a decent job in his limited touches. If Barkley can’t go in Week 13 against the Cardinals, Shipley is an interesting fill-in for that contest.

https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.headline: Will Shipley (foot/illness) was limited in Tuesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.analysis: With the news that Saquon Barkley is practicing in full, Shipley’s waiver wire appeal has downgraded drastically. He’s a reasonable stash and little more at this point in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.headline: Will Shipley (foot/illness) was limited in Monday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.analysis: It was an estimated session and exactly the same listing he had on Friday. As he was practicing on a limited basis before the illness (and before being activated off injured reserve last Saturday), we’ll assume he has a fairly good chance to suit up on Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.headline: Will Shipley had four rushes for nine yards in the Eagles’ Week 11 win against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.analysis: Shipley saw some decent fourth quarter run with Saquon Barkley nursing some sort of left arm injury. Shipley would likely take over the Eagles’ lead back if Barkley were to miss time. He should be rostered in most 12-team formats just in case, considering the Eagles take on the Cowboys in Week 12.

https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.headline: Will Shipley (foot/illness) is questionable for Philadelphia’s Week 11 game against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.analysis: Illness was an added designation today. While it normally probably wouldn’t matter, since Shipley is already on injured reserve, the Eagles can afford to take it slow with him if they’d like to. If active, Shipley won’t be a FLEX play with Saquon Barkley healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.headline: Will Shipley (foot) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.analysis: Shipley could need another week to fully recover from his injured reserve-worthy foot injury. Shipley partially tore his plantar fascia just over a month ago. Once he is active, he will likely serve as the Eagles’ No. 2 running back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.headline: Will Shipley (foot) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.analysis: Shipley was designated to return from injured reserve on Monday. He can be officially activated at any time. Shipley will reclaim his RB2 role once healthy, though we don’t expect much fantasy value to come of it.

https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.headline: Eagles designated RB Will Shipley (foot) to return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.analysis: With Shipley’s 21-day return window officially opened, the third-year back can resume practicing with the team and is eligible to be activated from the injured reserve list at any time. It’s only Week 11, but this offense has struggled mightily without Jalen Hurts (blood clots), making it hard to imagine anybody offering much fantasy value at this point. Shipley has rushed 20 times for 57 yards and one touchdown this season and has caught five passes for 31 scoreless yards. There’s no reason to rush to add Shipley, even when he is activated. In another move, the Eagles also signed TE Zach Ertz to the and OT John Ojukwu to the 53-man roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.headline: Eagles placed Will Shipley (foot) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.analysis: He’ll miss at least the next four weeks. Shipley was diagnosed with a partially torn plantar fascia and was set to miss multiple weeks per reporting, so this makes sense. By the time he comes back, Saquon Barkley should be healthy, so he’s not a must-keep in short-bench leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Eagles RB Will Shipley (foot) suffered “a partial tear of his plantar fascia” in Week 5’s loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.analysis: The Eagles’ running backs room continues to take hits. After losing Tank Bigsby (core) last week to a multi-week injury, the team is now preparing to be without Shipley for multiple weeks. Saquon Barkley, who missed Week 5 with a hamstring injury, could be back as early as Week 6 against the Panthers, but if he’s unable to play, the Eagles could be looking at Dameon Pierce and Jaydon Blue as their top two backs. Shipley totaled 13 yards from scrimmage and a touchdown on six touches before going down yesterday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.headline: KaVontae Turpin caught 1-of-3 targets for a 31-yard touchdown while adding a 10-yard rush in the Cowboys’ Week 12 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.analysis: Turpin did most of the work on a dump-off from Dak Prescott. The 30-year-old remains an impact player on special teams, but despite the score, he offers very little fantasy upside for the remainder of the season. Or next season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.headline: KaVontae Turpin (ribs) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.analysis: Turpin has missed three weeks with the rib issue. He may need to be upgraded to a full practice before being cleared to return to action. Even if he is back this week, George Pickens appears to be healthy and Ryan Flournoy is locked in as the team’s WR3, so there isn’t any fantasy value to be had here.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.headline: KaVontae Turpin (ribs) was ruled out for Week 9 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.analysis: This will be a third-straight missed game for Turpin as he battles his rib issue. The 30-year-old has just seven targets on the season, but will again be missed by Dallas in the return game. Malachi Lawrence has also been ruled out by the Cowboys due to his ankle injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.headline: KaVontae Turpin (ribs) was ruled out for Week 8 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.analysis: Week 8 will mark the second consecutive absence for the veteran kick returner, with little-to-no impact on the offensive pieces around him considering he has played more than 12 offensive snaps only once all season. Fantasy managers are more interested in the potential status of George Pickens, who is listed as questionable. If Pickens can’t go, Ryan Flournoy could see a slight uptick in opportunities on the perimeter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.headline: George Pickens (shoulder/hamstring) was limited in Wednesday’s walkthrough practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.analysis: Pickens played through a minor shoulder injury last week, but the hamstring designation is new. He was still a limited practice participant, indicating neither injury should be an issue for his Week 8 status. Meanwhile, WR/KR KaVontae Turpin (ribs) was an estimated DNP in practice after not playing last week. The Cowboys may be missing Turpin again as a kick returner and gadget player on offense, but Pickens should still be the WR2 for Sunday against the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.headline: Cowboys ruled out KaVontae Turpin (ribs) for Week 7 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.analysis: Turpin’s absence will be felt most on special teams, with the team now forced to find a replacement on punt and kick returns. Otherwise, there is almost zero fantasy impact as the team’s WR4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.headline: KaVontae Turpin (ribs) is questionable to return to Week 6 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.analysis: Turpin departed before the first offensive play run from scrimmage after sustaining a ribs injury on the opening kickoff. He was taken to the locker room for x-rays and is listed as questionable to return by the team.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.headline: KaVonte Turpin failed to haul in his only target in Week 18.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.analysis: Turpin ends the season with 26 catches on 38 targets for 396 yards and two touchdowns. He also added 16 carries for 82 rushing yards, but his primary value was as a kick returner. On the season, he had 69 kick returns for 1,814 yards, which leads the league as of the end of this game. That will be his primary role in 2026 as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.headline: KaVontae Turpin caught his only target for an 86-yard touchdown in the Cowboy’s Week 17 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.analysis: It took all of one target for Turpin to make his mark felt in the win as he broke free of primary coverage and split the safeties deep down the middle for an 86-yard, catch-and-run score. Turpin continues to play behind Jalen Tolbert but his flashy touchdown demonstrates his big play ability.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.headline: Cowboys listed WR KaVontae Turpin (shoulder) as a full participant on Monday’s estimated practice report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.analysis: Turpin played through the same shoulder injury in Week 13’s win over the Chiefs. The Cowboys’ special teams ace has posted a meager 19-260-1 receiving line this season and isn’t on the fantasy radar for Week 14 against the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: George Pickens caught five-of-nine targets for 67 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 12 loss to the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: Pickens dropped what would have likely been a touchdown from Dak Prescott early in the game. He also had a catch that would have resulted in a first down, but after being hit hard, he went nine yards backwards and wasn’t given forward progress. After impressing the previous two weeks, this was a disappointing effort. He’ll get a chance to rebound in Week 13 against the Seahawks in a Monday Night Football showdown.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: George Pickens caught 7-of-10 targets for 102 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 11 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: Pickens got off to a slow start this afternoon, seeming to not finish a route or two, but finished molten hot. He is now up to 18 catches for 247 yards and four touchdowns on 28 targets over the past two weeks. Ridiculous numbers, though somewhat sustainable in this narrow, explosive offense. For Thanksgiving Day he will be rematching with an Eagles defense he got for 4/57/1 last month. The Eagles have moved on to their No. 3 quarterback since then and traded a few key contributors. Even with all 32 teams active for Week 12, Pickens will remain in the low-end WR1 mix.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: George Pickens caught 11-of-18 targets for 145 yards and three touchdowns in the Cowboys’ Week 10 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: In his first game since owner Jerry Jones said the Cowboys needed to focus more on getting the ball to Pickens, the 25-year-old receiver saw passes funneled to him early and often. Pickens was targeted six times on the Cowboys’ first two drives and capped the second drive with a 35-yard touchdown to give the Cowboys their first touchdown of the day. Pickens would find the end zone two more times in this one, with his second score coming on a 39-yard play on a long catch-and-run. His last score would come on a five-yard pass from Dak Prescott as the Cowboys aimed to keep pace with the Niners late in the fourth quarter, but it ultimately proved to not be enough in the end. Despite his struggles at various points this season, Pickens was far from an underutilized receiver, as he entered the day averaging a solid 7.8 targets per game. It goes without saying that we shouldn’t expect this kind of performance every week from Pickens, but he will be on the fantasy radar next week as a mid-to-high-end WR2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: George Pickens (hamstring) is not on the Cowboys’ final injury report and will play in Week 10 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: Pickens makes his return after sitting out in Week 9. He played through the injury in Week 8, which may have been the wrong decision. The Cowboys’ No. 2 wide receiver encouragingly upgraded from limited to full participation today and can be treated as a WR2 in what should be a high-scoring game against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: George Pickens (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: Pickens is still stuck in the questionable column, though his continued participation is a good sign. The team allowed him to play through the injury in Week 8 against the Cardinals, which was probably the wrong call. He sat out last week despite practicing in a limited capacity. Hopefully, he upgrades to full participation tomorrow. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said George Pickens (hamstring) is expected to practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: Pickens missed Week 9 with the hamstring issue. He was limited in practice throughout the week, but the team ultimately chose to hold him out for Sunday’s game. We expect one week off to be enough for the veteran wideout. Assuming things go well in practice, Pickens will be back in the WR2 ranks when the Cowboys take on the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: George Pickens (hamstring) is inactive for Week 9 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: Pickens played through the issue last week but will ultimately be held out in Week 9. Tight end Jake Ferguson is active after failing to practice until a limited showing Friday. Ryan Flournoy steps into a featured role for the Cowboys against the inside-funnel Colts defense. Fantasy managers can insert Flournoy into rosters as a viable FLEX considering he leads the team in slot rate through the first half of the season. Also inactive for the Cowboys are LB DeMarvion Overshown, WR KaVontae Turpin, CB Joey Porter Jr., LB Tyrus Wheat, OL Ajani Cornelius, and TE Luke Schoonmaker.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: George Pickens (hamstring) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: Earlier today, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said he is “hopeful” that Pickens will be available for this weekend’s game against the Colts. Pickens ended up being limited in practice all week and appears to be truly questionable to play. If active, he is a WR2 against a beatable Colts defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: Speaking on 105.3 The Fan, Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said he is “hopeful” George Pickens (hamstring) will play in Week 9 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: Pickens has been limited in each of the Cowboys’ first two practices to start the week, which would seem to be a good sign for his Week 9 availability. We’ll get a better sense of where things stand when the Cowboys release their final injury report on Friday and give Pickens a designation heading into the weekend, but Schottenheimer’s optimism is a good sign. Owner Jerry Jones advocated for Pickens getting the ball more this week after Week 8’s loss to the Cardinals, so if he is active, the star receiver could be primed for a bit of a squeaky wheel game in a plus matchup against the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: George Pickens (hamstring) was limited during Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: Pickens was also limited during Wednesday’s session. The 25-year-old still seems to be on target to play in Week 9 against the Colts, but fantasy managers would obviously like to see Pickens get in a full session before that contest.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: CeeDee Lamb caught 7-of-11 targets for 134 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 12 loss to the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: Lamb also committed two pass interference penalties; one that wiped a touchdown off the board, although the Cowboys would end up scoring a few plays later. The 27-year-old was still able to fantasy day while going over 100 yards for the sixth time in the 2026 season. Lamb will remain a WR1 even with a tough matchup coming in Week 13 against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: CeeDee Lamb caught 11-of-12 targets for 132 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 11 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: Lamb’s fifth 100-yard effort of the season and second in three weeks puts him above 1,000 yards for the sixth consecutive season, good for a new Cowboys franchise record. Simply abusing overmatched Titans CB Cor’Dale Flott, it is barely an exaggeration to say Lamb was open at will against the Titans’ overmatched defense. The Eagles will be a slightly tougher Thanksgiving Day matchup, but not by much. Enjoy the holiday with your WR1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: CeeDee Lamb caught 7-of-13 passes for 72 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 10 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: Fantasy managers won’t be disappointed with the end result, but this was a frustrating game for Lamb. It became apparent early on that he would be taking a backseat to George Pickens, who saw six targets on the Cowboys’ first two drives of the game. Lamb saw nine of his 13 targets in the second half, and he was particularly productive in the fourth quarter, catching five passes for 49 yards and hauling in a one-yard touchdown pass with less than a minute to go in regulation. Despite Lamb needing every last second of this one to hit his expectations from a fantasy perspective, we don’t expect that to be the case for him most weeks. He’ll remain in the high-end WR1 conversation next week against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: CeeDee Lamb caught 10-of-16 targets for 195 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 9 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: Lamb’s day was inches from being one of the top fantasy outings for any player this season, with the talented veteran unable to get his second foot down in the end zone in the third quarter, forcing the Cowboys to settle for a field goal. Even so, Lamb has now seen double-digit targets in each of his previous four games and five of his last six, averaging 13.8 targets per game in that span. His production in Week 9 also marked the third time this season in which Lamb has gone for more than 150 yards, handily leading the league in targets while trailing only Jaxon Smith-Njigba in yardage. Lamb and the Cowboys get a more difficult matchup against the 49ers in Week 10, where Lamb will remain an elite WR1 at home.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: CeeDee Lamb caught 7-of-11 targets for 58 yards in Dallas’ Week 8 loss to the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: Lamb’s most memorable play from this game was evading three tacklers on a screen to finally find a first down. He had two of Dallas’ six red zone targets but turned them into just one catch for four yards. Arizona’s aggressive defense simply clouded Lamb and dared the other receivers to win. He’ll remain on the WR1 line next week against the hapless Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: CeeDee Lamb caught 5-of-12 targets for 74 yards and two touchdowns in the Cowboys’ Week 7 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: It wasn’t a clean game for the alpha wide receiver by any stretch, who committed two drops and caught only five of his team-leading 12 targets. Despite the poor efficiency, Lamb made the plays he needed to when it mattered most, scoring from nine yards out on a fade to the back corner of the end zone and from 16 yards out on a similar play to the opposite sideline. Lamb has now seen 56 targets in his previous four games, with 12 or more in three of his last four. That level of volume keeps him in elite company near the top of rest-of-season wide receiver rankings in fantasy circles, where he will remain ahead of a Week 8 matchup against the Cardinals at home.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: CeeDee Lamb caught 9-of-18 targets for 70 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 6 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: Lamb was targeted relentlessly against the match-zone-based Green Bay defense but suffered through an up-and-down connection with quarterback Dak Prescott on his way to middling fantasy returns. The Cowboys managed under 100 yards in the first half and were victimized by two Prescott interceptions deep in Green Bay territory, leading to a game environment that required 55 Prescott dropbacks. Even with a second consecutive middling-to-poor performance from a fantasy first round pick, Lamb is still pacing for a 1,500-yard, 11-touchdown season, plenty to provide a solid return on investment for fantasy managers that used their top pick on his services. Lamb could be busy again in Week 7 against the inside-funnel nature of the Philadelphia defense, where he will once again be a fantasy WR1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: CeeDee Lamb (quad) is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: Lamb played through a quad bruise last week but exacerbated the issue and left the game late in the fourth quarter. The injury is not believed to be serious and a full practice today means Lamb isn’t at risk of missing Week 6. Despite burning fantasy managers with two catches for nine yards last time around, Lamb remains one of the best fantasy football wideouts in play this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports CeeDee Lamb’s quad injury is not believed to be serious after Week 5’s loss to the Buccaneers.
