https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: Skowronek leaves the active roster while Michael Pittman (foot) makes his return. The Steelers also signed Max Hurleman from the practice squad to the active roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Ben Skowronek (calf) did not practice on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: This could open up more snaps for Pittsburgh’s ancillary receivers even if Skowronek is no fantasy force. He played 10 and 17 snaps in his first two weeks back from the calf injury after he was active for Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Ben Skowronek (calf) is not on Pittsburgh’s final Week 10 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: We’ll see if he goes back to being a thorn in the ceiling cases for the remainder of the Steelers’ offensive players against the Bengals. Skowronek has no standalone value.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Ben Skowronek (calf) is inactive for Week 8 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: Steelers declared WR Ben Skowronek, QB Drew Allar, QB Will Howard, CB Brandin Echols, RB Eli Heidenreich, and CB Doneiko Slaughter inactive for Week 8 against the Browns. Skowronek will miss this game with a calf injury while Echols and Slaughter deal with hamstring injuries. Howard will serve as the emergency third quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Ben Skowronek (calf) is questionable for Pittsburgh’s Week 8 game against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: He was limited all three days. Skowronek carries no standalone value but could eat into snaps for the other Steelers receivers if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Ben Skowronek (calf) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: Skowronek is not fantasy-relevant and should not be picked up in 12-team formats. His potential return provides Aaron Rodgers with a trusted target. Skowronek also serves as a reliable run blocker.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Ben Skowronek (calf) will not play in Pittsburgh’s Week 7 game against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: Ruled out on Thursday before traveling, Skowronek probably has a real chance to get back in Week 8. With Marquez Valdes-Scantling now on the roster, Skowronek has likely lost whatever desperation fantasy value he might have had either way.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Steelers coach Mike McCarthy said Ben Skowronek (leg) has been ruled out for Week 6.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: We weren’t exactly worried about Skowronek siphoning many targets away, but with him out of the pecking order entirely Germie Bernard should be a wheels-up WR3 for Week 6 now that both Skowronek and Roman Wilson have been ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Ben Skowronek has been ruled out for Week 5 against the Colts with a calf injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: There hasn’t been a lot of word on what happened to Skowronek. He went into the blue medical tent in the second quarter to have his leg looked at and then headed into the locker room. When the Steelers returned the kickoff to start the second half, Skowronek, who is a key special teamer, was not on the field. He was ruled out shortly after. With Michael Pittman Jr. already out, the Steelers are getting a little thin with their wide receiver depth.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Ben Skowronek caught his only target for 22 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 1 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: It was a play-action pass where Skowronek went against the flow of the defense and it almost operated like a screen, with Steelers receivers blocking downfield to create an easy crease for the 28-year-old receiver. Skowronek doesn’t need to be chased in fantasy leagues after only playing 10 of 53 snaps for the Steelers in this one. He’s operating more-or-less in a timeshare for Pittsburgh’s third receiver role with Roman Wilson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-gord.headline: Bears declared QB Case Keenum, CB Kyler Gordon, CB Isaac Yiadom, CB Elijah Hicks, RB Roschon Johnson, OL Jordan McFadden, and DL Jayden Loving inactive for Week 12 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-gord.analysis: Gordon and Johnson were both ruled out before this one, but the Bears are at near full strength heading into Thursday’s Thanksgiving Day tilt against the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-gord.headline: Bears ruled out Kyler Gordon (shoulder) for Week 12 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-gord.analysis: Bears No. 2 perimeter CB Tyrique Stevenson (groin) is questionable to play, which could mean that the Bears are without two of their top-three cornerbacks against the Lions’ elite offense. Tomorrow’s NFC North is looking like a fantasy-friendly environment.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-gord.headline: Bears declared QB Case Keenum, OL Jordan McFadden, CB Kyler Gordon, DL Jayden Loving, and LB Keyshaun Elliott inactive for Week 11 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-gord.analysis: Gordon was already declared out with a shoulder injury heading into the weekend. Rookie wide receiver Zavion Thomas (ankle) entered the day questionable, but will be active after missing Friday’s practice. Case Keenum will be the team’s emergency third quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-gord.headline: Kyler Gordon (shoulder) will not play in Chicago’s Week 11 game against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-gord.analysis: He was ruled out after three straight missed practices following the Week 10 bye. It does not look especially likely he’ll be able to turn it around next week and play in Chicago’s Thanksgiving game against the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-gord.headline: Kyler Gordon (shoulder) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-gord.analysis: Gordon, the Bears’ starting slot cornerback, is on the wrong side of questionable for this week’s game against the Saints. Bears DT Jeffery Simmons was limited by a knee injury, but DC Dennis Allen said he does not expect the injury to impact Simmons’ availability.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-gord.headline: Kyler Gordon (shoulder) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-gord.analysis: Gordon missed time earlier this season with a calf issue. He played in Week 9 before the team’s bye but got banged up. Head coach Ben Johnson called him day-to-day earlier this week. Gordon has four sacks, two forced fumbles, and one pass breakup this year. Losing him would make this an easier matchup for Tyler Shough and the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-gord.headline: Kyler Gordon (calf) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-gord.analysis: Gordon, the team’s starting slot cornerback, and Tyrique Stevenson (hip), the team’s No. 2 perimeter cornerback, are both questionable. Bears LB T.J. Edwards (hamstring) has been ruled out. This defense is banged up, boding positively for the Falcons’ fantasy football outlook.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-gord.headline: Bears CB Kyler Gordon (calf) is questionable to play in Week 5 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-gord.analysis: Gordon practiced in full all week, so he is seemingly ready to play. The Bears could give it another week, though. Bears LB Noah Sewell (Achilles) and EDGE Shemar Stewart (knee) are also questionable this week. Both players practiced in full over the last two days and are likewise returning from the reserve/physically unable to perform list.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-gord.headline: Bears ruled out CB Kyler Gordon (calf) for Week 4 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-gord.analysis: Gordon, LB Noah Sewell (Achilles) and EDGE Shemar Stewart (knee) are all in the process of returning from the reserve/physically unable to perform list. None of them will play this week. Fill-in starting DB Cam Lewis (hip) is doubtful.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-gord.headline: Bears activated CB Kyler Gordon (calf) from the reserve/physically unable to perform list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-gord.analysis: This does not necessarily mean Gordon will play in Week 4 against the Jets, but he is certainly getting closer to making his 2026 debut. The Bears’ pass defense has been a fantasy-friendly unit thus far. If Gordon can return to form, he could help slow down opposing slot receivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ennis-rakestra.headline: Lions declared CB Ennis Rakestraw, CB Keith Abney, S Chuck Clark, EDGE Tyrus Wheat, and EDGE DJ Wonnum inactive for Week 12 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ennis-rakestra.analysis: Clark was questionable entering the week, but has officially been ruled out for Thursday’s game, putting Kerby Joseph in line to start. The Lions have most of their key players ready to go against the Bears as the two teams prepare to kick off this Thanksgiving Day.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ennis-rakestra.headline: Lions declared CB D.J. Reed, CB Ennis Rakestraw Jr., DB Ketih Abney II, LB Amen Ogbongbemiga, EDGE Tyrus Wheat, and DL Mekhi Wingo inactive for Week 11 against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ennis-rakestra.analysis: Reed made seven starts this year before injuring his hip a few weeks ago. Rakestraw has been a depth option so far, but that would have been useful to have around with Reed out. The Lions’ defense will be as vulnerable as ever this week, though it’s anyone’s guess as to whether a hobbled Baker Mayfield will take advantage.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ennis-rakestra.headline: Lions placed CB Ennis Rakestraw Jr. (shoulder) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ennis-rakestra.analysis: Rakestraw’s season is over. The injury’s specifics have not yet been released but it was severe enough to require surgery. Rakestraw’s 2024 rookie season was derailed by a hamstring injury as well. Hopefully, he can log a full season in 2026. The Lions correspondingly signed TE Steven Stilianos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ennis-rakestra.headline: Lions HC Dan Campbell said Ennis Rakestraw is undergoing evaluations on his injured shoulder.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ennis-rakestra.analysis: Speaking with the media, Campbell said of Rakestraw’s injury, “Hate it for the kid. It’s not his fault. Just one of those tough deals.” While Campbell stopped short of saying Rakestraw’s injury was considered a serious one, the tone he struck suggests the second-year corner may miss some time. We’ll know for sure when the team reports back with what they learned through the evaluations, but even if it’s a minor injury, it’s hard to ignore the myriad of injuries that have plagued Rakestraw since entering the league last year. We’ll check back in with an update on Rakestraw’s status when one is provided.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ennis-rakestra.headline: Lions HC Dan Campbell said Ennis Rakestraw “should be okay” after suffering a chest injury on Sunday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ennis-rakestra.analysis: Campbell said he expects Rakestraw to miss a few days after the X-rays on his chest came back negative. It’s the best outcome we could hope for at this stage of the season as players begin to ramp up practices in preparation for the season. Rakestraw appeared in eight games last season due to a hamstring injury and appeared on just 46 defensive snaps.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ennis-rakestra.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Lions CB Ennis Rakestraw Jr. “is believed” to have suffered a chest contusion.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ennis-rakestra.analysis: The second-year cornerback left practice earlier today, being supported by trainers. Rapoport describes the diagnosis as “a positive outcome.” Rakestraw appeared in just eight games as a rookie, plagued by a recurring hamstring strain suffered during Week 2 warmups. He ultimately landed on injured reserve in November. Rakestraw is trying to win a starting job from Amik Robertson in training camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ennis-rakestra.headline: David Montgomery is off the Lions’ injury report and will play in the Divisional Round against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ennis-rakestra.analysis: Montgomery was trending toward a return after being a full participant in practice all week. The thunder to Jahmyr Gibbs’ lightning will officially be good to go for Saturday’s game, with a right to host the NFC Championship Game on the line. Montgomery averaged 15.8 touches per game during the regular season and should see plenty of work against a Commanders defense that has struggled to slow opposing ground games. In addition to Montgomery, the Lions also listed CB Ennis Rakestraw as questionable for Saturday’s game while ruling out guard Kevin Zeitler (hamstring) and DE Pat O’Conner (calf).

https://www.nbcsports.com/ennis-rakestra.headline: Lions designated CB Ennis Rakestraw for return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ennis-rakestra.analysis: Rakestraw suffered a hamstring injury in November and hasn’t played since Week 11. The rookie second-rounder has appeared in eight games this season but has only played on 46 defensive snaps while earning a PFF coverage grade of 41.0. There’s a chance he could see more snaps in the postseason, however, as the Lions are dealing with multiple injuries on defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ennis-rakestra.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Lions CB Terrion Arnold is not expected to miss regular season time from a pec injury sustained in Monday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ennis-rakestra.analysis: The Lions selected Arnold with the No. 24 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft and hope to have the rookie as a starter in the secondary. However, Arnold suffered a pec injury in practice, briefly putting a wrench in those plans. Second-round rookie CB Ennis Rakestraw Jr. was also hurt in Monday’s practice with an apparent ankle injury. In addition to the two rookies, free agent signing Carlton Davis is also expected to contribute for a revamped Lions secondary that allowed the second-most passing yards per attempt last season. The good news is that Arnold is not expected to miss regular season time, while Rakestraw said he’s “perfectly fine” via an Instagram Live. The Lions will still be able to use the rookies next to Davis to improve the defense this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ennis-rakestra.headline: Lions selected Missouri CB Ennis Rakestraw with the No. 61 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ennis-rakestra.analysis: Rakestraw (5’11/183) was rated as a standard three-star prospect and the 70th cornerback from the 2020 recruiting class. Rakestraw diligently rehabbed an ACL injury and was able to return in time to start Missouri’s 2022 season opener against Louisiana Tech and play a career-high 725 snaps, 10 PBUs, and a 50% completion rate while forcing incompletions on 23% of his targets. He ran a respectable 4.51s 40-yard dash with a laudable 1.52s 10-yard split that ranks in the 90th percentile. Though spindly, Rakestraw has abnormally long 32-inch arms, which help him probe receivers and be disruptive at the catch point. Comfortable in press coverage and has legitimate mirroring skills that keep him in phase during breaks. Rakestraw is noticeably light and can get washed out when he doesn’t get an immediate read on the play, but he is more than happy to step up in run support and do his job on the outside. He had trouble staying on the field with injuries, which could add to concerns about his slight frame and questionable long speed. 205 snaps from the slot over the last two years shows his versatility to play inside or outside. He profiles like a less-athletic version of Washington Commanders CB Emmanuel Forbes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Christian Watson has entered the league’s concussion protocol.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Watson exited in the second quarter of Wednesday’s game against the Rams after taking a helmet-to-helmet hit from Rams safety Kamren Kinchens. The hard hit left Watson on the ground for an extended period before he eventually got up on his own and went to the locker room. Watson was ruled out after halftime and now has to clear concussion protocol to play in Week 13’s game against the Saints. With extended time to clear protocol, Watson should have a decent chance of clearing protocol. We will be tracking his practice status throughout next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson (head) was taken to the locker room in the second quarter of Week 12 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Watson briefly departed the game after catching a pass on the first play from scrimmage, initially deemed questionable to return with a thigh injury. He would return without missing a play, catching a touchdown half way through the second quarter. Watson was then the target of a vicious hit down the sideline for which Kamren Kinchens was ejected from the game. He remained down on the field before walking to the locker room under hit own power. Watson caught all four targets for 65 yards and a touchdown prior to departing. Although no update has been passed from the team, it appears as if Watson will enter the league’s concussion protocol after appearing to be knocked out, making him worse than questionable to return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson caught 3-of-5 targets for 37 yards in the Packers’ Week 10 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: A week after breaking out for 171 yards and a score, Watson and the rest of the Packers’ explosive passing game were grounded by the physical Vikings defense. Jordan Love and company failed to generate many downfield plays on the day and were instead forced to settle for more short and intermediate throws, which the Vikings immediately shut down. Watson’s biggest play came on a 15-yard reception in the first quarter on a drive that ended with a missed field goal by Trey Smack. He will be on the fantasy radar as a high-end WR2 in Week 12 when the Packers return from their bye week to face the Rams on Thanksgiving Eve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson caught 7-of-8 targets for 171 yards and one touchdown in the Packers’ Week 9 win over the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Watson and fellow receiver Matthew Golden combined to catch 14 passes for 335 yards and two touchdowns, as both receivers attacked downfield at will against an overmatched Patriots secondary. Watson saw four of his seven receptions go for 20-plus yards, and found the end zone on a 39-yard touchdown in the third quarter, one play after the Packers’ defense forced a turnover. Watson has now gone for 100-plus yards in back-to-back weeks and has four games of 100-plus-yard performances on his resumé this season. He draws a tough Week 10 matchup against the Vikings and will be in the mix as a high-end WR2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson is off the injury report for Week 9 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Watson got in a pair of limited practices after leaving in Week 8 against the Panthers with a rib injury that required a trip to the hospital. The 6-foot-4 wideout is a WR1 for the upcoming battle against New England.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson (rib) was limited during Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: It’s back-to-back limited sessions for Watson. It’ll likely be a pain-tolerance issue for the wideout, but assuming he doesn’t suffer a setback in practice, he appears to be good for Week 9 against the Patriots and deserves WR1 consideration.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson (rib) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Watson famously left for the hospital in the middle of Week 8’s win over the Panthers, only to return after halftime like a WWE performer. The fact that they’re letting him practice in any capacity today means he should be able to play through the issue in Week 9. We’d expect him to wear a flak jacket for at least a few weeks. Barring a setback in practice, Watson will be a high-variance WR1 for his matchup with the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson caught 8-of-10 targets for 113 yards in the Packers’ Week 8 win over the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: The fact that Watson was able to even play in the second half was incredible, as the 27-year-old was forced to be examined at the hospital following a chest injury. He didn’t do much after putting up 100 yards in the first half, but again, that’s not really the story here. Watson told reporters after the game that he was coughing up blood and suffered a fractured rib before returning. Assuming no setbacks, he’s a WR1 candidate for Week 9 against the Patriots, but keep in mind Christian Gonzalez — on top of this injury — can make things difficult.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson (chest) returned to action in Week 8 against the Panthers in the third quarter.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Watson went to the hospital to have his chest injury examined, but obviously checked out well if the Packers were willing to reinsert him into a game where they were leading by two scores. It’s a sigh of relief for fantasy managers, as Watson has been sensational Thursday night with six catches for 100 yards in just one half thus far.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson is questionable to return in Week 8 against the Panthers with a chest injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Watson was hurt on a deep pass in the middle of the second quarter, and went to the locker room to be evaluated and will head to the hospital to be further examined. The 27-year-old was playing well prior to the injury with six catches for 100 yards on his seven targets. Matthew Golden will be the primary wideout target for Jordan Love if Watson can’t return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Colby Parkinson caught both targets for minus one yard in the Rams’ Week 12 win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Parkinson somehow lost a yard on two reception despite the team losing both Tyler Higbee and Davis Allen to injury, the latter of whom departed in the first half and the former of whom left at the beginning of the fourth quarter. The Rams completely controlled the flow of the game after Packers receiver Christian Watson departed with a concussion following a vicious targeting hit down the sideline just before the half, eventually leading to 47 total team carries to just 23 Matthew Stafford pass attempts. The Rams have some things to figure out given the sheer number of bodies missing after also losing two offensive linemen in the game. The long week hopefully affords them enough time to return to health ahead of a Week 13 meeting with the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) is not on Los Angeles’ final Week 12 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: He and Tyler Higbee will both be featured parts of this offense as the Rams look to get by without Puka Nacua. The one that catches a touchdown will be the one that you don’t start.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) practiced in full on Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: He’s gotten in two full sessions coming off the bye and figures to remain one of the main figures in the Rams’ floating opera of tight end production that they’ll likely be relying on this week sans Puka Nacua and Davante Adams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Colby Parkinson caught 2-of-2 targets for 11 yards in the Rams’ Week 10 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Parkinson was barely involved today, though he nearly scored a touchdown on the Rams’ sixth drive. He successfully high-pointed a red zone pass, but tumbled out of bounds at the one-yard line, tangled up with a Cardinals defender. Parkinson will be a touchdown-dependent TE2 against the Packers, following the Rams’ Week 11 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) is not on the Rams’ final injury report for Week 10 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Parkinson upgraded to full participation today. Tyler Higbee (illness) was limited. Both players were cleared to play. Davis Allen (oblique) is questionable, sandwiching a Thursday absence between two limited sessions. The Rams must be smart with their skill position players’ health, while asking as much as they can from their available players.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Parkinson should play through his injury again this week. Unfortunately, Tyler Higbee (illness) did not practice, as a new addition to the injury report, and Davis Allen (oblique) was downgraded to being a non-participant. The running backs are going to get all the work they can handle this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring) did not practice in Wednesday’s walk-through.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Ferguson was listed as a DNP for the Rams’ Wednesday walk-through. Rams head coach Sean McVay said earlier this week that Ferguson is likely out a couple week, so this comes as no surprise. Meanwhile, fellow tight ends Davis Allen (oblique) and Colby Parkinson (ribs) were both listed as limited participants. Allen and Parkinson are trending towards playing in Week 10 against the Cardinals, with Parkinson operating more as a pass-catcher and Allen as a blocker.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: ESPN’s Dan Graziano reports Puka Nacua (knee, toe) will not miss the rest of the regular season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Graziano said there’s an outside chance the Rams won’t put Nacua on injured reserve ahead of Week 10. Rams sources “were very adamant that Nacua’s injury isn’t season-ending and that they hope to get him back around that Week 14, Week 15 time.” With Davante Adams (hamstring) also sidelined, look for the Rams offense to be unusually run heavy in the coming weeks. That should mean more work for Kyren Williams and Blake Corum. Tyler Higbee and Colby Parkinson could see an uptick in targets too. If Terrance Ferguson (hamstring) is ever able to return to game action, he could profile as the team’s top target. Nacua had seen 44 percent of the Rams’ first-read targets this season, the highest rate in the NFL.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) is active for the Rams’ Week 9 game against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Parkinson managed to draw a questionable tag entering the weekend after logging a limited practice on Friday. Despite being a DNP for two of the Rams’ three practices this week, he should be available to play his normal role in the Rams’ TE-heavy scheme. Parkinson has caught 14 passes for 103 yards and one touchdown this season and will not be on the fantasy radar this week. The Rams declared QB Ty Simpson, LS Joe Cardona, LB Darryl Peterson III, OL Bill Murray, OL Keagan Trost, and LB Desjuan Johnson inactive for Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Parkinson sat out on Wednesday and Thursday. His Friday participation level has not yet been released, but he is probably on the wrong side of questionable at this time. Parkinson does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues, especially with Terrance Ferguson (ankle) expected to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/konata-mumpfie.headline: Konata Mumpfield caught 4-of-5 targets for 69 yards in the Rams’ Week 12 win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/konata-mumpfie.analysis: Mumpfield saw a team-high five targets and turned them into a team-leading 69 yards in one of the more dominant performances of the season. Despite the seemingly close score, the Rams jumped out to an early 13-3 lead while holding the Packers to only 44 total offensive plays run from scrimmage. The inability of the Packers to move the football resulted in additional time of possession for the Rams, which they used to notch 47 rush attempts to just 23 Matthew Stafford pass attempts, eight of which were directed at the backfield duo of Blake Corum and Kyren Williams. Mumpfield remains the player with the most weekly upside for as long as Davante Adams remains sidelined, of available pass catchers, a unit that took two more hits with the departures of tight ends Tyler Higbee and Davis Allen. Fantasy managers are likely better off leaving Mumpfield on the waiver wire or on their bench.

https://www.nbcsports.com/konata-mumpfie.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Davante Adams sounds like a “long shot” to play in Week 13 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/konata-mumpfie.analysis: Adams isn’t expected to play in Week 12. The Rams get the Packers on Wednesday before Thanksgiving, and the tight turnaround makes a Week 12 return all but impossible. Head coach Sean McVay said Week 13 against Kansas City was a “possibility” earlier this week. That sounds unlikely now as well. Rapoport said Adams is eyeing a mid-December return. With Puka Nacua done for the year, the Rams are down to Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell as their top wide receivers for at least a few more weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/konata-mumpfie.headline: Konata Mumpfield caught 3-of-4 targets for 81 yards in the Rams’ Week 10 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/konata-mumpfie.analysis: Mumpfield had a decent game today, producing catches of 10, 27 and 45 yards, notably adding decent yardage post-catch on his two longest receptions. He was also targeted on Matthew Stafford’s interception, but it was simply an off-target throw. Mumpfield generated his longest gain with a slick hitch-and-go, leaving his defender in the dust on the false step. The Rams go on bye in Week 11 and face the Packers in Week 12. Davante Adams (hamstring) is targeting a Week 13 return. Mumpfield should be FLEX-viable in Week 12, though he will likely become quite volatile when Adams returns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/konata-mumpfie.headline: Konata Mumpfield caught 1-of-2 targets for 15 yards in the Rams’ Week 7 win against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/konata-mumpfie.analysis: Mumpfield saw a bump in snaps and routes but not so much in actual targets and receptions as the Rams went all in on three tight ends sets with Davante Adams (hamstring) sidelined for the foreseeable future. Mumpfield doesn’t need to be rostered in fantasy leagues for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/konata-mumpfie.headline: Puka Nacua left practice early after suffering a calf injury on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/konata-mumpfie.analysis: Brutal. The Rams lost Davante Adams to a hamstring tendon rupture in Week 6 against the Cardinals, and now they could be without Nacua in Week 7 against the Raiders. The Rams have handled star-player injuries smartly this season. Consider Nacua highly questionable to play, and seek out a backup plan. Konata Mumpfield would serve as the de facto No. 1 wide receiver if Nacua is unable to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/konata-mumpfie.headline: Konata Mumpfield caught 4-of-8 targets for 93 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 3 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/konata-mumpfie.analysis: Mumpfield managed just one grab before erupting for 78 yards and a touchdown on a single drive in the fourth quarter with the Rams trailing for the first time in the game. His touchdown came on a double move against Riley Moss down the sideline for a walk-in score from 48 yards out. Mumpfield stepped into a growing role the previous two weeks in the absence of Puka Nacua and could remain a starter at wide receiver should Nacua miss additional time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/konata-mumpfie.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Puka Nacua (groin) is considered a “pre-game decision” for the Rams’ Week 2 game against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/konata-mumpfie.analysis: Nacua was added to the injury report on Friday as a DNP. He failed to get in any reps on Saturday but still received the questionable designation. Given that the game is on Monday, fantasy managers won’t have many contingency options left. With Jordan Whittington also expected to miss Week 2, the Rams’ No. 2 receiver will be either Konata Mumpfield or Xavier Smith if Nacua doesn’t suit up. Both players would be WR5/6 options in the event of a Nacua absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/konata-mumpfie.headline: The Athletic’s Jourdan Rodrigue believes the Rams may take a committee approach to the WR3 role this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/konata-mumpfie.analysis: Rodrigue listed WR Konata Mumpfield and WR Jordan Whittington as candidates for the gig, notably excluding rookie WR CJ Daniels. Daniels was viewed as the potential WR3 due to his blocking ability earlier this year. Rodrigue says it is instead Whittington who could serve as the “3B” blocker. Mumpfield reportedly “looks the part” as the “3A” receiving component. Will he return fantasy value reliably? Probably not. Earlier this month, Rodrigue’s colleague, Nate Atkins, said Mumpfield could be the next man up on the perimeter if WRs Puka Nacua or Davante Adams miss time. Rodrigue’s comments seemingly confirm this.

https://www.nbcsports.com/konata-mumpfie.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins believes Rams WR Konata Mumpfield “could be the primary backup on the perimeter” if WR Puka Nacua or WR Davante Adams miss time.
https://www.nbcsports.com/konata-mumpfie.analysis: Mumpfield enters his second NFL season after posting a 10/92/1 receiving line in the regular season last year. He chipped in three catches for 22 yards in the playoffs. Were he to get a spot start, he is not guaranteed to be fantasy-relevant. Atkins lists sixth-round rookie WR CJ Daniels as the most likely player to assume No. 3 wide receiver duties, primarily due to his blocking. He also has some contested-catch ability. Mumpfield is a name to know for 2026, but he is unlikely to meaningfully contribute in the box score if Nacua and Adams are healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/konata-mumpfie.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins believes wideout could be “a strong spot for the No. 13 pick in the draft.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/konata-mumpfie.analysis: He also adds that a Day 2 selection is in play. Neither Davante Adams nor Puka Nacua are likely going to see their 2026 production threatened by a rookie wideout, but Adams is in the final year of his contract and the depth at the position hasn’t shown much for the Rams. Konata Mumpfield, who played outside while Adams was dealing with a hamstring injury late in the season, would figure to lose major dynasty stock if the Rams spent an early pick on a wideout.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.headline: Kyren Williams rushed 12 times for 46 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 12 win over the Packers, adding 19 yards on four receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.analysis: Williams now operates as the clear change of pace option and preferred back in passing situations, with recent reports pointing to consistent pain due to a turf toe injury likely the culprit in the shifting dynamics of the backfield in Los Angeles. Either way, Williams spent most of the second half on the sideline as Corum set career highs in attempts (32) and yards (184) while becoming the first back in the Sean McVay era to reach 30 carries. Given the nature of the injury, this could be the new norm for a Rams team that continues to push for a postseason bid following a 2-4 start to their 2026 season, leaving Williams a touchdown-driven RB3 for the time being.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.headline: NFL Insider Tom Pelissero reports Kyren Williams “has been battling turf toe for the past month.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.analysis: Williams was on the Rams’ injury report this week with a toe injury before getting cleared off the report before Wednesday. Pelissero reveals that Williams told him he has been battling turf toe for the past month. This stretch coincides with Blake Corum’s increased opportunities while Williams has seen his role reduced to more of a backfield split. Williams will continue to play through the injury, but expect Corum to still be heavily involved as a result.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.headline: Kyren Williams (toe) is not on Los Angeles’ final Week 12 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.analysis: He’ll be good to go against the Packers on Wednesday night. Williams should figure into the high RB2 mix as the Rams try to replace Puka Nacua once again with plenty of split back formations.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.headline: Kyren Williams (toe) practiced in full on Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.analysis: It’s an upgrade from a limited session on Sunday and we’d be surprised if Williams was placed on the questionable line on Tuesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.headline: Kyren Williams (toe) was limited Saturday but is expected to play in Week 12 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.analysis: Williams is reportedly dealing with “soreness” in his toe and was limited in practice Saturday as a result. ESPN’s Sarah Barshop added that Williams is expected to play on Wednesday against the Packers. Expect him to continue working in a strict timeshare with Blake Corum coming out of the team’s Week 11 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.headline: Kyren Williams rushed 12 times for 23 yards in the Rams’ Week 10 win over the Cardinals, adding two receptions for nine yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.analysis: Williams was the clear-cut starter, as usual, touching the ball on the first four plays, but Blake Corum played so well that Rams coach Sean McVay just kept calling his number. Williams had a five-yard receiving touchdown called back due to a false start committed by rookie WR CJ Daniels. Williams’ five targets also led the pass-catching corps. The Rams go on bye in Week 11, but Williams will be back in the RB1 ranks against the Packers in Week 12.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins believes Blake Corum’s development as a pass catcher has helped the Rams deal with increasing blitz rates.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.analysis: Leaning on Corum and No. 1 RB Kyren Williams has helped the Rams achieve a three-game winning streak, and Atkins notes that the Rams are 4-0 this season when Corum plays at least 30 percent of the offensive snaps. His development as a receiver and pass protector has erased run-pass tells pre-snap. Corum’s development as a weapon in the screen game, specifically, has allowed the Rams to beat the increasing blitz rates they have faced since Davante Adams (hamstring) was lost as a downfield receiving weapon. Corum belongs in starting lineups on a weekly basis at this point, as he establishes himself as a reliable RB2 in both real life and fantasy football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.headline: Kyren Williams rushed 15 times for 45 yards in the Rams’ Week 9 win over the Commanders, adding three receptions for 16 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.analysis: Williams was bottled up for most of the afternoon, with his longest gain coming on a nine-yard run. Williams’ 15 rush attempts narrowly edged out Blake Corum (11), but Corum found the end zone when he punched in a one-yard touchdown in the third quarter. Williams continues to see reliable work, but now that he’s in a near 50/50 split with Corum, the high-ceiling games could be few and far between compared to what we are used to seeing. He will profile as a fringe RB1 in next week’s game against the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.headline: Kyren Williams had 16 rushes for 56 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 8 win against the Chargers, adding one catch for three yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.analysis: The more efficient Blake Corum had 11 rushes for 73 yards and did not see a target in a run-heavy Rams offense. Williams led the LA backfield in routes but only had one look from Matthew Stafford. He was stuffed at the line of scrimmage a handful of times in the first half. The rushing volume in the Rams offense of late should make both Williams and Corum fantasy relevant every week, including next week against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.headline: Kyren Williams had 16 rushes for 99 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 7 win against the Raiders, adding two catches for 22 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.analysis: After complaining about the team’s backfield split last week, Williams was out-carried by Blake Corum, 17 to 16, with Corum scoring a touchdown and having two others called back on penalties. Though Williams lost a fumble in the second half, the Rams leaned on him late in the fourth quarter following a short-lived Vegas comeback. He ran 18 pass routes to eight routes for Corum — a season long trend that makes Williams less sensitive to game script than Corum. Williams will be a locked-in top-15 running back option next week against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Blake Corum rushed 32 times for 184 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 12 win over the Packers, adding 21 yards on two receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: The 184 yards on the ground easily set a new career high for the veteran back and his 32 carries marked the first time in the Sean McVay era where a single back ran the football 30 or more times, a mark that had not been reached since Todd Gurley over a decade ago. His trip to paint stretched his streak of touchdowns to five games while he also went over 100 yards for the second straight contest. The backfield split between Corum and Kyren Williams has taken a stark turn of late, with Corum now the preferred option on early downs and Kyren the preferred change of pace and clear passing situation back, a split that now leaves Corum the favorite for weekly production. He will remain an upside RB2 ahead of a Week 13 matchup against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Blake Corum rushed 17 times for 100 yards and one touchdown in the Rams’ Week 10 win over the Cardinals, adding three receptions for 19 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Corum was the star of today’s show. He got involved partway through the Rams’ first drive, lining up in a two-running back set alongside Kyren Williams. The Rams’ immediate successes out of this formation led to a whole lot of it for the rest of the game. The shifty third-year running back hogged touches for stretches, playing so well as a rusher and receiver that having an eight-yard run erased by a penalty was a non-issue for fantasy purposes. Corum is a locked-in RB2 with RB1 upside. Treat him accordingly against the Packers in Week 12, following the Rams’ Week 11 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins believes Blake Corum’s development as a pass catcher has helped the Rams deal with increasing blitz rates.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Leaning on Corum and No. 1 RB Kyren Williams has helped the Rams achieve a three-game winning streak, and Atkins notes that the Rams are 4-0 this season when Corum plays at least 30 percent of the offensive snaps. His development as a receiver and pass protector has erased run-pass tells pre-snap. Corum’s development as a weapon in the screen game, specifically, has allowed the Rams to beat the increasing blitz rates they have faced since Davante Adams (hamstring) was lost as a downfield receiving weapon. Corum belongs in starting lineups on a weekly basis at this point, as he establishes himself as a reliable RB2 in both real life and fantasy football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Blake Corum rushed 11 times for 58 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 9 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Corum continued to split drives with Kyren Williams, but he was easily the better back in Sunday’s win over the Commanders. Corum ripped off several strong runs on the opening drive of the third quarter and capped a 69-yard offensive drive with a two-yard score to put the Rams up 13-10. He failed to haul in either of the two targets that came his way, but this was the kind of fantasy week we have come to expect from Corum, who has now had double-digit carries in three straight games. He has also found the end zone in each of those games and will be a boom-or-bust RB2 in Week 10 against the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Kyren Williams had 16 rushes for 56 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 8 win against the Chargers, adding one catch for three yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: The more efficient Blake Corum had 11 rushes for 73 yards and did not see a target in a run-heavy Rams offense. Williams led the LA backfield in routes but only had one look from Matthew Stafford. He was stuffed at the line of scrimmage a handful of times in the first half. The rushing volume in the Rams offense of late should make both Williams and Corum fantasy relevant every week, including next week against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Blake Corum had 11 rushes for 73 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 8 win against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Kyren Williams led the LA backfield with 16 carries for 56 yards. Corum was much more efficient as a rusher against the Chargers, regularly bursting through the line of scrimmage and shedding tacklers on a couple second half runs. The Rams have been run heavy since Davante Adams went down with a serious hamstring injury a few weeks ago. That’s generated more opportunity for Corum, who last week had 17 rushes. He ranks 44th among running backs in expected fantasy points per game in 2026. That kind of usage should make Corum flex-viable for now. He gets the Commanders in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Blake Corum had 17 rushes for 93 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 7 win against the Raiders, adding one catch for eight yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Corum had the lead in carries until the final drive of the game, when the Rams turned to Kyren Williams to seal the victory following a short-lived Raiders comeback. Corum’s fantasy day could have been much bigger if he hadn’t had two touchdowns called back on penalties along with another chunk gain. Despite running cold on luck, Corum’s role continued to grow even after Williams complained publicly about the backfield workload split last week. Williams logged 18 routes against the Raiders while Corum ran just nine. Look for the Rams to be more run heavy in the coming weeks with Davante Adams out indefinitely with a hamstring injury, putting Corum in play as a weekly flex. He gets the Chargers in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Blake Corum rushed nine times for 42 yards in the Rams’ Week 6 loss to the Cardinals, adding two receptions, 18 yards and one touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Corum got the Rams’ second drive all to himself before re-entering the game on the fourth drive and splitting reps with Kyren Williams thereafter. Rams coach Sean McVay seemingly rewarded Corum for powering through contact on a third-down conversion from the Cardinals’ 19-yard line by allowing him to remain on the field for the scoring-position sequence. Two plays later, Corum was scampering upfield for a 15-yard receiving score after hauling in a pass in the flats. He ran hard the rest of the way, but the Rams got off just 20 rushing attempts today, surprisingly playing in a trailing game script for the entire second half, as the Cardinals achieved victory via voluminous field goals. Corum is an RB3/FLEX against the Raiders next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Blake Corum rushed five times for 19 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 5 loss to the Bills, adding 53 yards on three receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Corum provided a much needed spark in relief of lead back Kyren Williams, contributing three clutch receptions that kept drives alive in addition to a third quarter touchdown. That said, his modest volume continued while Williams turned in a third straight game with 20 or more opportunities, including 28 total targets in that stretch. Corum remains a top fantasy handcuff but is unlikely to return useful fantasy weeks for as long as Williams is healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Blake Corum rushed five times for 14 yards in the Rams’ Week 4 win over the Eagles, adding a seven-yard reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Corum was employed as a pure breather back this afternoon, as he got out-touched 26-6 by Kyren Williams. Four of Corum’s handles came on one first quarter series. With the 1-2 Rams staring down the barrel of 1-3 as they trailed by two scores for several quarters, they circled the wagons around their most established players, and that does not yet include Corum. The third-year pro will undoubtedly pop up for more 10-12 carry afternoons, but he’s fading from FLEX relevance as Williams gets re-established in the low-end RB1 mix.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 16-of-23 passes for 140 yards and an interception in the Rams’ 26-13, Week 12 win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: The two sides traded blows in the first half as the Packers came from behind to knot the game at 13 heading into the break, with Stafford leading three consecutive scoring drives to start the game for the first time this season. That was also the first time the Packers had allowed an opponent to score on three consecutive drives to start a game this season, but the departure of Christian Watson in the second quarter due to a concussion completely took the wind out of their sails in the second half. In total, the Rams attempted more runs than the Packers ran offensive plays (47 to 44), with this game marking the first game in the Sean McVay era in which a single back carried the football 30 or more times. It also marked the second consecutive game in which the Rams gained more than 200 yards on the ground, leaving Stafford with little volume as the reigning MVP failed to return a usable fantasy score for the fifth time this season while also failing to pass for a touchdown for the third time this season. The Rams saw two tight ends depart with injury as both Tyler Higbee and Davis Allen were unable to finish the game, potentially something to keep an eye on as the Rams prepare to face the Chiefs in Week 13, particularly in the absence of both Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. Stafford remains an upside QB2 in fantasy circles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 18-of-26 passes for 249 yards, three touchdowns and one interception in the Rams’ 34-6, Week 10 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: The Rams lost two centers to injury today, but Stafford navigated the resulting offensive line shuffling without issue, completing passes to nine different pass catchers. Stafford probably should have had a fourth touchdown added to his box score, but he overthrew Tyler Higbee and CJ Daniels in the end zone on the opening drive, which ultimately resulted in a field goal. A touchdown pass thrown to Kyren Williams was called back due to a false start on the Rams’ fourth drive, but Stafford linked up with Higbee for a score a couple of plays later. A similar sequence occurred in which Stafford threw a touchdown pass to Xavier Smith on the following drive, after Tutu Atwell failed to secure what should have been a 32-yard touchdown. Stafford’s second-drive interception was on him. He threw an off-target pass to Konatha Mumpfield, which a Cardinals defender easily caught. All in all, Stafford dealt with the Rams’ offensive personnel issues well. He will be a low-end QB1 against the Packers in Week 12, following the Rams’ Week 11 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 26-of-43 passes for 228 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Rams’ 20-13, Week 9 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: It was an uneven day for Stafford and the Rams, who managed just six points in the first half of this one. Stafford threw 19 of his 43 targets to Puka Nacua, who was unsurprisingly his most reliable receiver of the day, as the two connected 14 times for 150 yards and a touchdown. Stafford’s lone touchdown pass of the day came on a seven-yard pass to Nacua in the back of the end zone, which gave the Rams a 20-13 lead early in the fourth quarter. This marks back-to-back pedestrian outings for Stafford, who has thrown for 385 yards, two touchdowns, and two interceptions in his last two games. Stafford will be a fringe QB1/QB2 next week on the road against the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford (right elbow) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: Stafford has downplayed inquiries regarding his throwing-arm injury, saying he’s been icing his elbow post-game and post-practice for a while now — and he called out the beat reporters for missing it. Lingering elbow soreness isn’t exactly reassuring, but at least he is practicing fully. Stafford should be good to go for the Rams’ Week 9 game against the Commanders, but this is obviously worth monitoring.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 17-of-25 attempts for 157 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Rams’ Week 8 win against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: Stafford wasn’t asked to do much against the Chargers, as the Rams once again went ultra run-heavy with Davante Adams (hamstring) sidelined. Averaging a meager 6.3 yards per attempt, Stafford mostly checked down to his short-area targets. His touchdown came on a well-designed screen pass to Puka Nacua. Stafford will have some fantasy appeal in Week 9 against the pass-funnel Washington defense. Coming into Week 8, Stafford ranked 13th in expected fantasy points per game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 23-of-29 attempts for 195 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception in the Rams’ Week 7 win against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: It was a fairly clean game for Stafford against a Raiders defense that rarely pressures the passer and has proven vulnerable in the intermediate and deep areas of the field. Stafford picked apart the Vegas secondary in the first half, with heavy three tight end-set usage and a more run-heavy game plan than usual with Davante Adams (hamstring) sidelined. The Rams had 35 rushing attempts to 29 passes on the day. Stafford connected with Puka Nacua for one score and Davis Allen for two others. Though Stafford’s ceiling is going to be lower with Adams out, he profiles as a safe option in Week 8 against the Chargers. He now has six multi-touchdown games this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 25-of-33 passes for 222 yards and two touchdowns in the Rams’ 16-18, Week 6 loss to the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: The Cardinals’ pass rush was disruptive, hitting Stafford seven times and sacking him twice. Stafford lost a fumble on a two-point conversion, but the box score only shows a failed two-point try, evidently saving fantasy managers two fantasy points. Stafford later fumbled after getting spooked by a pass-rushing ghost. A Rams lineman recovered it, but it derailed an otherwise effective, tempo-based drive. Stafford engineered a touchdown drive at the tail end of the game, connecting with Puka Nacua on a 42-yarder and a 16-yarder, before Colby Parkinson barreled into the end zone for the score. Stafford should return to the QB1 tier against the Raiders in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 40-of-54 passes for 383 yards and three touchdowns in the Rams’ 37-34, Week 5 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: It was the third consecutive game in which Stafford attempted 51 passes or more in what has become the most voluminous passing offense in the league. The two powerhouses felt each other out throughout the first half as only 20 combined points per scored before the break. Things would get aggressive for the final 30 minutes as seven combined touchdowns were scored on nine second half possessions, four of which were accounted for by the Rams. Stafford directed a whopping 24 targets toward alpha wide receiver Puka Nacua, who set a career high with 17 receptions in a short-area role. The reigning MVP returned an instant classic performance against the 2024 MVP, ultimately coming up short in overtime following a blocked field goal attempt from Harrison Mevis. The Rams fall to 2-3 ahead of a home matchup against the more forgiving Cardinals in Week 6. Stafford is once again a fantasy QB1 in that matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 32-of-51 passes for 316 yards, zero touchdowns and two interceptions in the Rams’ 24-20, Week 4 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: Stafford put the Rams behind the eight ball with a pair of first half interceptions but was better after the break as the Rams slowly erased a 20-10 deficit. Not that he was amazing, but with the Eagles finishing an inconceivable 0-12 on third down, Stafford needed to make just enough plays, and that’s what he did despite leaving some meat on the bone. It was forgivable on a rainy day in Philly, though Stafford now has at least one interception in all four of his starts. In fact, he has as many scores (six) as picks. Hopefully that trend reverses with Puka Nacua back in the lineup, though the schedule is not lightening up with the Rams hosting the Bills for Monday Night Football in Week 5. That should nevertheless be a fantasy football bonanza.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 30-of-55 passes for 390 yards, two touchdowns, and two interceptions in the Rams’ 30-26, Week 3 loss to the Broncos, adding 13 yards on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: The Rams stormed out to a 16-0 lead they would take into the break but two unanswered scores and two-point conversions from the Broncos saw the game knotted at 16 heading into the fourth quarter, which is where the scoring really took off. Stafford and the Rams appeared to be in control of the game until a Talanoa Hufanga pick-six off Stafford, making 33 career pick-sixes thrown to give him a record he would otherwise not like to have on his ledger. Stafford answered on the following possession on a 48-yard strike to Konata Mumpfield, only for the Broncos to answer back with a Bo Nix rushing score with 47 seconds left to play. Stafford worked more magic to get the team into the red zone, marching the field with only one timeout with a chance to win on the final play of the game. Hufanga ultimately won the play with his second interception off Stafford, sending the Rams to a 1-2 record. Stafford also became the first quarterback in NFL history to throw for 20,000 yards for two different franchises in the loss. Stafford remains a locked-in QB1 in fantasy circles ahead of a Week 4 showdown with the Eagles on the road.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 3-of-5 targets for 24 yards in the Packers’ Week 12 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: Kraft continues to look miles behind where he was during his breakout 2025 season before suffering a torn ACL, lacking burst out of routes while struggling through mental mistakes. Another such mistake appeared against the Rams when Kraft was stripped of the football in the first quarter following his longest reception in the game. The once-imposing Green Bay offense feel completely flat following the departure of Christian Watson in the second quarter due to a concussion, failing to score after the break while running just 44 total offensive plays. The Packers look to lick their wounds following back-to-back losses ahead of a Week 13 road meeting with the Saints, where Kraft will remain a frustrating TE2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 1-of-4 targets for 19 yards in the Packers Week 10 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: That makes it back-to-back one-catch weeks for Kraft, who has totaled just two receptions for 20 yards on seven targets. While this can partly be blamed on a tough matchup against a stout Vikings defense, it’s worth remembering that Kraft often produces for fantasy managers despite lacking elite volume at times. His 52 routes run over the last week are tied with Dalton Schultz for 11th-most among tight ends, but the ball just hasn’t been finding him as of late. Despite the frustrating usage, he should be in the mix when the Packers return from their bye as a fringe TE1 in Week 12 against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 1-of-3 targets for one yard in the Packers’ Week 9 win over the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: Interestingly, Kraft had a more productive day on the ground (2-8-0) in what was a quiet day for the 26-year-old tight end. His quiet day can be partly blamed on a hyper-efficient passing attack that saw Matthew Golden and Christian Watson combine for 335 of the 372 receiving yards the Packers managed on the day. The three targets Kraft saw tied a season low, and he averaged 6.7 targets per game over his last six games. He will look to bounce back next week at home against the Vikings and will profile as a low-end TE1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 6-of-6 targets for 53 yards with a touchdown in the Packers’ Week 8 win over the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: Kraft was able to bring in a score between a pair of defenders to give the Pack a 6-0 lead in the first quarter. That’s back-to-back games for the tight end with a score, and three in the first half of 2026. Kraft has seen a similar amount of involvement throughout the campaign, and he’ll likely put up a similar statline — hopefully with a touchdown for fantasy managers who roster him — in Week 9 versus the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 4-of-6 targets for 48 yards and a touchdown in the Packers’ Week 7 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: Kraft found the end zone on a 14-yard touchdown near the end of the second quarter, giving him his second touchdown of the season and his first since Week 4 against the Buccaneers. Kraft has seen six or more targets in four of his last five games and has posted double-digit PPR points in three of his last four. Even when he isn’t finding the end zone, his volume, coupled with his big-play ability, is enough to keep him in the TE1 conversation. Kraft gets a nice matchup next week against the Panthers on Thursday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 5-of-8 targets for 37 yards in the Packers’ Week 6 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: Kraft was forced from the game in the second quarter after taking a scary hit to his thigh area that generated torsion on his knee while his foot was still planted. It was the opposite knee to the one he injured a season ago and the veteran tight end would miss only one drive before returning to the game after the half, providing a collective sigh of relief for fantasy managers that have tasted the despair of a major knee injury already. Kraft could be busy in Week 7 against the defense allowing the most fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends when the Packers face off against the division rival Lions in a potential shootout.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 5-of-5 targets for 64 yards in the Packers’ Week 5 win over the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: The five-catch effort was Kraft’s second straight after previously having zero. His 54 yards were also his most since Week 1. His 46-yard reception in the third quarter was his longest of the season. All of that is good, though it was still somewhat disappointing amidst a 367-yard Jordan Love outburst where Christian Watson and Matthew Golden both eased by 100 yards. Kraft is averaging a pedestrian six targets. He’s going to need both more looks and big plays to remain a higher-end TE1. It will nevertheless be impossible to bench him for Week 6 against the Cowboys’ shaky defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 6-of-7 targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in the Packers’ Week 4 win over the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: Jordan Love made it a point to get Kraft going in this game, peppering him with easy-button targets throughout the contest. Kraft led the team with a 23 percent target share. His six grabs also led the team and are a new season high. He found the end zone with an impressive toe-dragging catch at the goal line. Kraft is still looking for the explosive play, but the team is getting him more involved every week. He is back in the TE1 ranks after a slow couple of weeks to start the season. Kraft will look to stay hot versus the Bears next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 4-of-8 targets for 26 yards in the Packers’ Week 3 loss to the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: Kraft has not yet looked himself after recovering from a torn ACL suffered in 2025, this time committing two drops for the first time in his career. To add additional context, Kraft has never had more than three drops in an entire season entering his fourth year in the league. The game plan clearly consisted of getting Kraft involved early to circumvent the offensive line struggles, but the connection with Jordan Love was off throughout. Kraft appears likely to need time to get back to full speed for the Packers, although his snaps and route participation rate were back to normal for the second consecutive week. Fantasy managers are likely forced to ride through the turbulence considering the state of the tight end position throughout the league, but he is a shaky start ahead of a Week 4 matchup with the Buccaneers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 2-of-3 targets for 15 yards in the Packers’ Week 2 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: The good news is that Kraft played 52 of the team’s 53 snaps and ran a route on 32 of their 34 dropbacks. The bad news is that he wasn’t commanding targets, and he also fumbled one of his catches, but the replay review couldn’t determine for sure who recovered it, so the Packers were able to maintain possession. Perhaps we should have been a little less aggressive in expecting Kraft to return from tearing his ACL less than a year ago and go right back to being himself at the start of the season. His role remains elite, but it may take another couple of weeks before he’s physically able to play like we’re used to seeing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Matthew Golden caught 1-of-5 targets for 39 yards in the Packers’ Week 12 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: Golden found himself in lockdown coverage throughout, particularly following the departure of fellow receiver Christian Watson in the second quarter. The talented second-year receiver has seen double-digit targets in six of 11 games in his sophomore campaign and could be headed for another high-target game against the Saints in Week 13, pending Watson’s availability on a long week. Golden would be a legitimate WR1, should Watson miss, and an upside WR2, should Watson play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Matthew Golden caught 5-of-9 targets for 70 yards in the Packers’ Week 10 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: One of the Packers’ two three-and-outs in the first half can be blamed on Golden, who dropped back-to-back passes on second and third downs that would have resulted in first downs had he hauled them in. As one might expect, Golden was one of several players who was held in check in the Vikings’ 30-10 win, but he did manage to catch a few passes in the second half to salvage an otherwise forgettable fantasy day. Green Bay’s explosive passing game was nearly a non-factor in this one, as Jordan Love completed just one of his two pass attempts of 20-plus yards, after going 6-of-9 on deep attempts last week. Golden and the Packers now head into their bye week, but he will be in the fringe WR1/WR2 mix in Week 12 when the Packers return to take on the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Matthew Golden caught 10-of-10 targets for 164 yards and one touchdown in the Packers’ Week 9 win over the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: Golden appeared to be on pace for a historic performance after the first quarter. The second-year receiver hauled in two receptions of 40-plus yards, along with a five-yard touchdown, and ended the quarter with a 6-126-1 receiving line on six targets. Golden obviously didn’t sustain that pace for the remaining three quarters, but fantasy managers won’t be mad with the one highly productive quarter he offered up. Golden continues to dazzle in his second season and has now gone for 100-plus yards in four different games this season. He’s both a target hog and an air-yards king, which makes for a deadly combination as far as fantasy football is concerned. He will be a fringe WR1/WR2 next week against the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Matthew Golden caught 7-of-13 targets for 79 yards and a touchdown in the Packers’ Week 8 win over the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: Golden is rarely boring, that’s for sure. He dropped two passes, and one of those was a wide-open touchdown in the second quarter. The good news for Golden, Jordan Love and fantasy managers was that he was wide open again on the next play, and he was able to bring that pass in. Golden’s athleticism and ability to get down field is unquestionable, but to say the efficiency isn’t there is an understatement. He’ll be back at it in Week 9 against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Matthew Golden (shoulder/foot) is active for Week 8 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: Golden got in a lone limited session in preparation for the team’s Week 8 meeting with the Panthers on a short week, ultimately able to go as he looks to continue his recent hot stretch in fantasy production. No limitation in expected role has been passed by the team, meaning Golden should be good to go for a normal workload against the Panthers. Fantasy managers can confidently insert him into Week 8 rosters as an upside WR2. Inactive for the Packers are TE Jonnu Smith, RB Kaleb Johnson, LB Zaire Franklin, G Donovan Jennings, C Sean Rhyan, and G Travis Glover.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Matthew Golden (shoulder/foot) is “trending toward playing” in Week 8 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: Golden was estimated as a DNP for two walkthroughs this week before being limited in the Packers’ only real session. The short turnaround to Thursday Night Football likely forced the Packers to take an extra cautious approach with him in practice. While he almost certainly isn’t at 100 percent, Golden looks like a good bet to play in a sneaky shootout with the Panthers tonight. He will be on the WR1/2 border if he gets the green light.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Matthew Golden (shoulder/foot) is questionable for Week 8 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: The Packers held two walkthrough practices to start the week. Golden was estimated as a DNP for both. He was limited in the team’s final practice before being hit with the questionable tag. Fantasy managers should treat him as a true game-time decision for tomorrow’s game. Savion Williams has been operating as the team’s No. 3 receiver over the past two weeks. He would presumably be the next man up if Golden can’t go, though Williams would still be a high-risk FLEX bet for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said the team is “still working through it” when asked if WR Matthew Golden (shoulder/foot) will play Week 8 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: ESPN’s Rob Demovsky relayed LaFleur’s noncommittal response to questions on Golden’s status. LaFleur said the team hopes Golden plays, but the 23-year-old has been an estimated DNP for the first two practices of the week due to shoulder and foot injuries. With the Packers playing on a short week against the Panthers, Golden’s status will likely rely on the final practice report before a Week 8 Thursday showdown against Carolina.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Matthew Golden (shoulder/foot) did not practice on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: This does not have us optimistic that Golden will play on Thursday night. If he’s sidelined, Savion Williams will be a candidate for more work on offense and perhaps a worthwhile FLEX streamer, while Tucker Kraft will likely ascend to the No. 2 role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Packers listed Matthew Golden (shoulder/foot) as a DNP on Monday’s estimated injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: Golden has been dealing with the shoulder injury since last week, but the foot injury is a new one. While this is only an estimated injury report, the DNP is still mildly concerning for Golden, with the Packers playing on a short week. His status will be one to monitor in the coming days, but hopefully this is a minor issue. Golden played the entirety of the game in Week 7’s loss to the Lions and didn’t appear to be hampered by any nagging issues. We’ll see if he get upgraded to a limited participant on Tuesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaleb-john.headline: Kaleb Johnson rushed eight times for 13 yards in the Packers’ Week 12 loss to the Rams, adding 19 yards on one reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaleb-john.analysis: The Packers were completely unable to run the football effectively against the stout Los Angeles defensive front, running just 44 offensive plays as they struggled to get any offense going following the departure of Christian Watson due to a concussion. Lead back Josh Jacobs appeared close to suiting up coming out of their bye and could make his way back into the starting lineup on a long week ahead of a Week 13 meeting with the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaleb-john.headline: Kaleb Johnson rushed 10 times for 42 yards in the Packers’ Week 10 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaleb-john.analysis: Johnson’s 10 carries and 42 rushing yards both led the Packers, who also mixed in MarShawn Lloyd and Chris Brooks throughout the day. While Johnson failed to replicate the 14-68-1 performance he had in Week 9 against the Patriots, his 10 carries were more than double those of the next closest back. The Packers are now entering their Week 11 bye, but if Josh Jacobs (thumb) is unable to go in Week 12 against the Rams, Johnson could have some boom-or-bust RB3/Flex appeal.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaleb-john.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Packers RB Josh Jacobs (finger) underwent successful surgery on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaleb-john.analysis: Jacobs had surgery on his fractured right ring finger Friday in Los Angeles, according to Pelissero. The 28-year-old running back is expected to return in the next few weeks. In the meantime, Kaleb Johnson is the only usable Packers running back for fantasy purposes. He’s an RB3/FLEX play against the Vikings in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaleb-john.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Josh Jacobs (finger) could miss 2-3 weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaleb-john.analysis: In other words, the Packers might avoid placing Jacobs on injured reserve with his surgically-repaired finger. While he’s sidelined — including in Week 10 against the Vikings — some combination of Pierre Strong, Chris Brooks, Kaleb Johnson, and MarShawn Lloyd will handle backfield duties for the pass-heavy Packers. Johnson served as the nominal lead back in Week 9 against the Patriots, while Brooks is returning from injury and should slot in as the team’s pass-catching back. Johnson can be played as a touchdown-dependent RB3 option this week against a Minnesota defense that has shown recent vulnerabilities to the run.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaleb-john.headline: The Athletic’s Matt Schneidman believes Kaleb Johnson could have a chance to be the Packers’ lead rusher in the coming weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaleb-john.analysis: With Josh Jacobs out with a broken finger, Johnson led the Packers with 14 carries for 68 yards and a touchdown in the team’s Week 9 drubbing of the Patriots. Forty-four of those yards came on explosive rushes. Pierre Strong, meanwhile had eight carries on the day. MarShawn Lloyd was sidelined with a knee issue but could be back in the Green Bay lineup soon.
