Lloyd’s shocking lack of production this season could, according to Schneidman, give Johnson a real chance to seize lead back duties. Head coach Matt LaFleur after the team’s Week 9 win seemed to imply there are some pass protection concerns for Johnson. That would probably mean Chris Brooks, who’s expected to return from an ankle injury in Week 10, gets the third-down role while Jacobs is sidelined. The Packers this week take on an elite Minnesota offense that teams have run on in recent weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaleb-john.headline: CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reports Josh Jacobs will undergo surgery on his fractured finger and “is expected to miss a maximum of three weeks.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaleb-john.analysis: Less than 24 hours after it was reported that the team would see if Jacobs could play through his fractured finger, they have now opted for surgery. The decision to say Jacobs could be out “a maximum of three weeks” suggests he will avoid the injured reserve and that this will be more of a week-to-week thing, and that he could return before the end of the month. Jacobs has totaled 148 yards from scrimmage and three touchdowns on 47 touches since returning from the Commissioner’s Exempt list. Now, the Packers will likely take a bit of a committee approach in the weeks ahead and could lean more on Kaleb Johnson, who was solid against the Patriots (14-68-1), with Jacobs and MarShawn Lloyd (knee) both sidelined. That said, all Packers running backs will be hard to trust as anything more than desperation dart throws in Week 10 when they take on a stout Vikings defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaleb-john.headline: Kaleb Johnson rushed 14 times for 68 yards and a touchdown in the Packers’ Week 9 win over the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaleb-john.analysis: An early injury to Josh Jacobs (finger) opened the door for Johnson to have a career day. The former third-round pick rushed for a career-high 68 yards in this one while leading the Packers in carries and managed to find the end zone on a two-yard touchdown in the second quarter. In addition to Jacobs leaving the game early, Johnson also benefited from MarShawn Lloyd (knee) being inactive. Half of his rushing production came on a 34-yard run, and fantasy managers should exercise caution before adding him off of waivers this week. The Packers have already said that they are going to see if Jacobs can play through his fractured finger, and it’s possible Lloyd will be active next week after entering this weekend carrying a questionable tag. If both Jacobs and Lloyd are sidelined, Johnson could be worth a dart throw in deeper leagues as a boom-or-bust RB3 against the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaleb-john.headline: Pierre Strong rushed 11 times for 28 yards in the Packers’ Week 6 win over the Cowboys, adding 39 yards on five receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaleb-john.analysis: Strong’s 17 opportunities handily led the backfield on a night MarShawn Lloyd was in and out of the game due to an early injury scare. Even so, he managed only 2.8 yards per carry. With Josh Jacobs expected to be activated off the commissioner’s exempt list on Monday, Strong, Lloyd, and Kaleb Johnson can safely be returned to the waiver wire from whence they came.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaleb-john.headline: Kaleb Johnson rushed seven times for 26 yards in the Packers’ Week 5 win over the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaleb-john.analysis: Even with Chris Brooks (ankle) on injured reserve, Johnson remain mired in a three-man committee, as veteran journeyman Pierre Strong slid seamlessly into Brooks’ vacated “role.” In fact, it was worse than that, as Johnson could also only watch as MarShawn Lloyd and Strong formed an early 1-2 punch. Johnson wasn’t really involved before garbage time. Before that, Lloyd had the advantage in short-yardage situations, notching the first two rushing touchdowns of his star-crossed career. Yet to handle more than eight carries in a game, it just isn’t happening for Johnson in 12-team league fantasy. He’s a distant FLEX bet ahead of Week 6 against the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaleb-john.headline: Chris Brooks (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kaleb-john.analysis: Brooks suffered the ankle injury in Week 4. He went down in the first half and did not return. Brooks underwent testing on his ankle after the game, though the exact nature of his injury has yet to be reported. He does appear to be on the wrong side of questionable for Week 5. If he can’t go, MarShawn Lloyd and Kaleb Johnson will split the backfield. Johnson led the team in carries last week but also gave up a goal line fumble. We expect Lloyd to get the start versus Chicago on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Jordan Love completed 17-of-29 passes for 198 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions in the Packers’ 26-13, Week 12 loss to the Rams, adding seven yards on one carry.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: it was the second consecutive game with three turnovers for the Packers as two second half interceptions thrown by Love were a microcosm of the team’s inability to hang with the Rams without their top option through the air. Christian Watson departed in the second quarter with a concussion after being knocked out on a vicious hit down the sideline, leaving the Packers in a hole they could not climb out of despite taking a tied game into the break. It is possible for Watson to clear concussion protocol in a long week of preparation, but Love could realistically be without his top option when the Packers travel to New Orleans to face the Saints in Week 13. In desperate need of a win following back-to-back losses to current playoff teams, the Packers head into the final two months of the regular season on the outside looking in at the NFC playoff picture.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Jordan Love completed 17-of-27 passes for 220 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Packers’ 30-10, Week 10 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: Love was under relentless pressure for most of this one. According to the early data from PFF, Love was pressured 19 times on his 35 dropbacks, which feels about right for a player who was sacked a season-high eight times. Love and the Packers went three-and-out on two of their offensive drives and also saw a promising drive late in the second quarter end after giving up back-to-back sacks after two long completions to Matthew Golden. Love and the Packers would eventually string together a 10-play, 75-yard touchdown drive in the third quarter, with the lone touchdown coming on a 32-yard pass to rookie receiver J. Michael Sturdivant, but that was as close as the Packers would come to mounting any sort of a comeback. Love and the Packers now head into their bye week and will return in Week 12 to face the Rams on Thanksgiving Eve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Jordan Love completed 23-of-29 passes for 372 yards and three touchdowns in the Packers’ 45-27, Week 9 win over the Patriots, adding one carry for 13 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: As has been the case for much of the season, big plays were the name of the game for Love. Love aired the ball out at will against a helpless Patriots defense, going 6-for-9 on passes of 20-plus air yards for 235 yards and a touchdown. Love connected with Matthew Golden on multiple long plays in the first quarter, completing passes of 43 and 49 yards, and found him in the end zone for a five-yard score. Love’s longest touchdown pass of the day came in the third quarter when he connected with Christian Watson for a 39-yard-score immediately after the Packers recovered a fumble by Rhamondre Stevenson. Love and the Packers boast arguably the most explosive passing attack in the league, and both Watson and Golden continue to look like premier threats while also being versatile in other areas of the field. Love and the Vikings will have their work cut out for them next week at home against the Vikings, but he will remain in the QB1 mix.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Jordan Love completed 30-of-41 passes for 288 yards with three touchdowns and an interception in the Packers’ 27-19, Week 8 win over the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: Love completed 17 of his first 20 passes, and two of those incompletions were drops. He threw a seed to Tucker Kraft for his first touchdown between defenders, found Matthew Golden wide open in the end zone for his second score — one play after Golden dropped a touchdown — and connected with Josh Jacobs for his third score of the day. The interception was a heinous decision where he didn’t see the safety, but outside of that, it was an impressive evening for the 27-year-old. Love gets zero, well, love from the run game and doesn’t have a quality offensive line, but he’s still putting up respectable numbers. He’ll look to add to those numbers in Week 9 against the Patriots in what should be a fun matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Jordan Love completed 27-of-45 passes for 274 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the Packers’ 20-17, Week 7 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: Even with Josh Jacobs back in the mix, the Packers still struggled to get the ground game going. As a result, Love aired it out early and often, throwing a ridiculous 10 passes for 20-plus yards, but only three were completed. Love’s first touchdown pass came on a third-and-nine when he connected with Tucker Kraft for a 14-yard score, and in the third quarter, a short pass to Jacobs was turned upfield for a 25-yard touchdown after Jacobs tight-roped along the sideline to find pay dirt. Love nearly connected with Jacobs for another score late in the fourth quarter, but Jacobs was unable to complete the diving catch in the end zone for the go-ahead score. On the next play, Trey Smack had a 35-yard field goal blocked, which ultimately set the Lions up for the game-winning field goal on the ensuing drive. Love continues to play an aggressive style of football, airing it out to his speedsters in Matthew Golden and Christian Watson. He and the Packers now have a short turnaround to prepare for the Panthers in Week 8, where he will be on the QB1 radar.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Jordan Love (back) is not on the Packers’ final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: Love was limited on Wednesday before upgrading to full on Thursday. Packers coach Matt LaFleur told reporters that his starting quarterback was “pretty beat up” after the Packers’ Week 6 win over the Cowboys. Hopefully, he is feeling much better by now. This divisional showdown looks like one of the most fantasy-friendly game environments in Week 7. He’s a QB1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Jordan Love (back) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: It’s an upgrade from Wednesday’s limited session. Packers coach Matt LaFleur said Love was “pretty beat up” after Sunday night, but Love doesn’t appear to be in any danger of missing the game. He’ll likely be cleared off the injury report Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Packers coach Matt LaFleur said Jordan Love (back) was “pretty beat up” after the Packers’ Week 6 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: Love got checked out by the team’s chiropractor after the game and was listed as limited for yesterday’s practice. LaFleur told reporters they haven’t determined whether he will be limited for today’s session. Either way, he said yesterday that there is no chance Love misses Week 7, so the practice reports are a moot point. Love is a top-half QB1 for his date with Detroit this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Jordan Love (back) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: Wednesday’s session was a walkthrough, so this is just an estimate from the team. We don’t believe it will be much of an issue for Love in Week 7. Barring a setback, Love will remain in the QB1 mix for a likely shootout with the Lions on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Jordan Love completed 23-of-41 passes for 276 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Packers’ 23-13, Week 6 win over the Cowboys, adding 12 yards and a touchdown on four carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: Love isn’t typically a threat to punch in a touchdown with his legs, but the state of the backfield and flow of the game gave him that opportunity late in the second quarter, which he would cash in for his first rushing score since Week 11 of 2024. Fantasy managers shouldn’t get too excited about the touchdown on the ground considering running back Josh Jacobs is expected to be activated from the commissioner’s exempt list Monday. Even so, Love has now accounted for two touchdowns in all six games played through the first third of the season and has gone over 300 yards through the air in half his appearances to start the 2026 season, leaving plenty of meat on the bone for continued fantasy production as the Packers enter their most difficult stretch of the schedule. Love remains a locked-in QB1 ahead of a potential shootout against the division rival Lions in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.headline: Daiyan Henley (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.analysis: Henley missed Week 11 with a knee injury and continues to sit for the Chargers’ walk-through practice to open the week. Also missing the walk-through were DT Dalvin Tomlinson (knee), Tuli Tuipulotu (ankle), CB Tarheeb Still (ankle), EDGE Akheem Mesidor (ankle), S Kendall Williamson (calf), and DB Deane Leonard (groin). It’s hard to believe this many Chargers defenders will sit this week but the team released a practice report with 14 DNPs on Wednesday. We can expect a few of these players to return to practice later this week and play in Week 12 against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.headline: Daiyan Henley (knee) will not play in Los Angeles’ Week 11 game against the Jets.
Daiyan Henley (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.analysis: Henley infamously was sent back to the Chargers after a reported trade with Denver fell through due to a failed physical. He returned to play in the Chargers’ Week 10 win over the Ravens, but now misses the first practice of the week with a knee issue. Given he has been playing through soreness, Henley’s absence may just be load management after a Monday game. Henley still has a chance to play in Week 11 with practices later in the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Broncos have revoked their trade for Chargers LB Daiyan Henley because of a failed physical.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.analysis: The move, or lack thereof, was announced by Denver around midnight, and Rapoport later gave the reasoning. Henley has been playing through a knee issue for multiple weeks, though he has also dealt with other injuries that could have caused the Broncos to back out. Denver originally agreed to give fourth- and fifth-round picks to acquire Henley. He will now return to the Chargers. As Rapoport points out, the 0-8 Chargers now officially made zero trades ahead of the deadline.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.headline: Broncos acquired LB Daiyan Henley from the Chargers for a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.analysis: The Chargers finally make a move, dealing a player who was considered a burgeoning star a few years ago away for a light deadline return. Henley had a career-worst 38.3 PFF coverage grade this year but is still a good tackler and should give the Broncos some oomph on run defense down the stretch.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.headline: Chargers LB Daiyan Henley (illness) is questionable for Los Angeles’ Week 3 game against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.analysis: It’s kind of surprising that the illness has lasted this long — Henley drew another DNP in practice on Friday after also missing Wednesday — and even despite him playing through it on Monday Night it’s certainly possible he sits this game out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.headline: Chargers LB Daiyan Henley (illness) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.analysis: Henley was added to the Chargers’ injury report prior to their Monday night game with an illness. He played in the team’s win over the Raiders, so a missed practice two days later is a surprise, but not concerning yet. Henley is still on track to play in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.headline: Chargers LB Daiyan Henley (illness) is questionable for Week 2’s game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.analysis: The Chargers announced on Monday that Henley will be added to the injury report due to an illness. The third-year linebacker totaled eight tackles and a sack in the team’s Week 1 win over the Chiefs, and would join fellow linebacker Denzel Perryman on the sideline if he is unable to play. It’s not often we see players miss games due to illnesses, so we would still expect to see Henley suit up despite this late development.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.headline: Chargers LB Daiyan Henley said he has fully recovered from offseason shoulder surgery.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.analysis: Henley played through a torn labrum for four months while breaking out in his second NFL season last year. The 25-year-old totaled 92 tackles, 13 quarterback pressures, six pass breakups and one interception. He now has ample time to ramp up ahead of the 2025 NFL season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.headline: Chargers LB Daiyan Henley (shoulder) expects to be ready for training camp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daiyan-hen.analysis: Henley had surgery to repair a torn labrum that he played through for the final four months of the season. Henley told ESPN’s Kris Rhim that he expects to be “100 percent” before training camp. If for whatever reason Henley is slow coming back, it could be an opening for 2024 third-rounder Junior Colson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Quenton Nelson (knee) and Abraham Lucas (ankle) are out for Week 12 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: Neither Nelson or Lucas practiced on Wednesday and Macdonald declared both offensive lineman out this week against the 49ers. The Seahawks will dig into their offensive line depth to deal with the 49ers pass rush this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Quentin Nelson (knee) could play in Week 12 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: Macdonald also said that Nelson is “back” with the team this week. It’s unclear whether he means Nelson has simply returned to the facility to participate in team meetings, or if he actually has a chance to practice, though we assume Nelson will not practice until after the Seahawks’ Week 11 bye. Nelson underwent a procedure to remove cartilage fragments from his knee last week. If he indeed returns in Week 12, the surgery will have only cost him two games. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that “the plan” is for Quenton Nelson to avoid injured reserve after undergoing a procedure to remove cartilage fragments from his knee.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: If the Seahawks were to place Nelson on short-term injured reserve, he would be required to miss at least four games. The Seahawks face the Cardinals this week, the Raiders next and then go on bye. Nelson could have a chance to play in Week 12 against the 49ers. His availability that week will likely just come down to how the recovery is going. His loss is unfortunate.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Quenton Nelson (knee) will have a minor procedure and is week-to-week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: Apparently, Nelson was dealing with this knee issue when Seattle acquired for him, and he recently “aggravated it to some degree.” FOX 59’s Mike Chappell notes that Nelson was never listed on the Colts’ injury report this season. This is a bummer for the Seahawks, who acquired Nelson as a win-now move. Nelson will not play in Week 9 against the Cardinals, and the Seahawks also ruled out LT Charles Cross (ankle), DT Leonard Williams (stinger) and LB Uchenna Nwosu (ankle).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: Rashid Shaheed (knee) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: Shaheed seems likely to miss another week, though he could technically still turn things around tomorrow. Seahawks LT Charles Cross (ankle) also remains sidelined on Thursday, and LG Quenton Nelson (knee) was downgraded to a non-participant. Hopefully, Nelson’s absence is precautionary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: Seahawks acquired Quenton Nelson from the Colts in exchange for a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: With the Colts’ season all but over, the team could trade away a series of key player as they look toward a total tear down/rebuild scenario following the 2026 season. That includes Nelson, an eight-time Pro Bowler who now has a chance to compete for a title now that he’s out of Indianapolis. Nelson will join a Seattle offensive line that ranks 21st in pass blocking win rate and 27th in run blocking win rate. His addition should be a boon for Sam Darnold and the Seahawks’ pass catchers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Packers, Vikings, Seahawks, and Broncos are “among the teams interested” in trading for Jonathan Taylor.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: As Rap notes, the Colts view Taylor as a pillar of the franchise. Even if they are forced to rebuild the roster, they could want him there as the centerpiece of the next iteration of the offense. On the other hand, Taylor will turn 28 at the end of the season and the Colts face a lengthy teardown process without their 2027 first-round selection. Taylor will likely be past his prime by the time they are competitive again. Rapoport also named DeForest Buckner and Quenton Nelson as potential trade candidates if the Colts’ struggles continue.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: ESPN’s Stephen Holder listed QuentonNelson and DeForest Buckner as potential trade options for the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: Holder writes that “trade speculation is swirling” around Buckner and notes that Nelson is in the final year of his deal, potentially providing motivation for the Colts to move him. Neither player had much to say when asked about a potential trade, but per Holder, “it is widely expected that significant organizational changes might be coming after the eventual hire of a new general manager.” Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: Jonathan Taylor said he would “definitely love to be a Colt for life,” as he enters the final year of his contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: Taylor, 27, has totaled more than 320 offensive touches in each of the last two seasons. His current $14 million annual salary makes him the seventh-highest-paid running back in the league. Taylor has set multiple Colts records, operating as the centerpiece of Indianapolis’ offense for years. FOX 59’s Mike Chappell writes that it is “uncertain whether there’s a mutual desire to keep Taylor in Indy beyond 2025.” Multiple Colts stars, including DTs DeForest Buckner and Grover Stewart, OG Quenton Nelson and WR Josh Downs, are also entering the final year of their deal. Chappell believes owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon “might believe it’s more prudent to allow the upcoming season to run its course rather than reinvest in lucrative contracts.” Time will tell.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: Colts LG Quenton Nelson returned to Week 2 against the Broncos after suffering an apparent leg injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: Nelson was the downfield blocker on a delayed Tyler Warren screen pass when he was hurt. Broncos S Talanoa Hufanga went low on Nelson, which resulted in Nelson driving his quad-knee area into the diving Hufanga. Nelson immediately grabbed just above his knee as he went down. He then limped off the field under his own power and was seen talking to teammates with his helmet on, along the sideline. He returned on the following drive.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ty-simpson/000.headline: Rams declared QB Ty Simpson, DE Larrell Murchison, OLB Darryl Peterson III, C Coleman Shelton, G Steve Avila, and OLB Desjuan Johnson inactive for Week 12 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ty-simpson/000.analysis: Simpson will operate as the team’s emergency third quarterback. Avila and Shelton were declared out heading into the day, leaving the Rams offensive line short-handed against a Packers defensive line getting Micah Parsons back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ty-simpson/000.headline: Rams declared WR Tutu Atwell, WR CJ Daniels, OL Bill Murray, TE Max Klare and QB Ty Simpson inactive for Week 1 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ty-simpson/000.analysis: The Rams acquired Atwell via trade in August. Although he already knows the system, coach Sean McVay evidently feels that Atwell is unnecessary for this one. Incumbent QB Stetson Bennett has officially defeated Simpson for the QB2 job. Simpson is inactive, but has been labeled the emergency third quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ty-simpson/000.headline: Rams HC Sean McVay said he still hasn’t decided who the team’s backup will be to Matthew Stafford to start the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ty-simpson/000.analysis: After getting through the third and final dress rehearsal before the Rams kick off Week 1 in Australia, McVay said he won’t be “pigeon-holding” himself into any decision just yet. Rookie Ty Simpson and fourth-year vet Stetson Bennett have both performed well for the Rams this preseason, with Bennett sitting out Thursday’s game against the Chargers. The decision to sit Bennett on Thursday, coupled with the 62 snaps he saw in the preseason to Simpson’s 111, could be a signal as to which way McVay is leaning at this point, although he is on record saying we shouldn’t read too much into that. Regardless, the good news for McVay and Rams fans is that Matthew Stafford is healthy and will hopefully be under center for all 17 of the Rams’ games this season as he looks to defend his crown as the reigning league MVP.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ty-simpson/000.headline: Rams HC Sean McVay said he remains undecided on who Matthew Stafford’s backup will be to start the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ty-simpson/000.analysis: Rookie Ty Simpson and 2023 fourth-rounder Stetson Bennett have both turned in solid performances in the team’s first two preseason games. Bennett drew the start in the first preseason game and has thrown for 219 scoreless yards on 37 attempts, while Simpson has thrown for 263-2-0, also on 37 attempts. McVay has already said that Simpson will “definitely” play in the team’s preseason finale against the Chargers, but didn’t commit to Bennett seeing snaps as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ty-simpson/000.headline: Ty Simpson completed 8-of-12 passes for 73 yards in the Rams’ preseason win over the Saints on Saturday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ty-simpson/000.analysis: Simpson sat the entire first half of Saturday’s game and didn’t get on the field until midway through the third quarter, thanks to a long opening drive by the Saints after halftime that ended in a pick-six by the Rams’ defense that immediately gave the ball back to New Orleans. In the 34-0 win, Simpson wasn’t asked to do too much. He dropped back to pass on 14 of his 26 offensive snaps and stuck mostly to short completions, as only three of his attempts on the day traveled 10 or more air yards. Both Simpson and Stetson Bennett, who started this game, will see extensive work in next week’s game against the Chargers before the real games begin in Week 1 with the Rams playing “host” to the 49ers in Australia.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ty-simpson/000.headline: Ty Simpson completed 21-of-25 passes for 190 yards and two touchdowns in Saturday’s preseason game against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ty-simpson/000.analysis: Simpson played all but two drives for the Rams in this one, as Sean McVay gave his rookie first-rounder an extended first taste of NFL action. Simpson played about as clean of a game as one could have hoped for, avoiding sacks and turnovers while leading his team on three scoring drives. Simpson’s first touchdown pass came on a screen pass to running back Dean Conners, who took it into the end zone for the score. Later, Simpson connected with Conners on a two-yard score after he found a hole between two defenders to fit the ball into. We would expect Simpson to see another lengthy outing in next week’s game against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ty-simpson/000.headline: Rams HC Sean McVay told reporters QB Ty Simpson will “definitely play” in their first preseason game Saturday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ty-simpson/000.analysis: McVay added that he was undecided on whether presumed second-string quarterback Stetson Bennett would play in the team’s first preseason game, hinting at the potential for Simpson to see the bulk of the work against the Chiefs. The team selected Simpson with the No. 13 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft with a clear intent on developing him into an heir apparent under Matthew Stafford, meaning it could be another two years until he takes the field as the starting quarterback considering Stafford recently signed an extension that ties him to the Rams through the 2027 season. Either way, it appears likely that Simpson will get his first taste of play at the NFL level when the Rams face off against the Chiefs Saturday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ty-simpson/000.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins reports Steston Bennett is getting the “first crack” with the ones when Matthew Stafford rests.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ty-simpson/000.analysis: Atkins doesn’t seem impressed with Bennett (who has “fallen victim to a couple of greedy mistakes”) or Ty Simpson (“isn’t going downfield much”) early in camp and suggests that the unsigned Jimmy Garoppolo could just be a phone call away if Simpson isn’t able to win the QB2 job. We’ll see what happens, but Garoppolo lingering as a free agent could keep some upside injury runouts off the table for Simpson this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ty-simpson/000.headline: Rams signed QB Ty Simpson to a four-year, $25.4 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ty-simpson/000.analysis: The contract comes fully guaranteed and includes a $14.94 million signing bonus and a fifth-year option. Simpson should immediately challenge for the primary backup role behind veteran starter Matthew Stafford, the latter of whom recently signed a one-year extension that ties him to the Rams through the 2027 season. It appears as if Simpson will learn behind Stafford for a couple seasons before hopefully ascending to a franchise quarterback in a Sean McVay offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ty-simpson/000.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins says neither Ty Simpson or Stetson Bennett have been able to “stand out ahead of the other” in the Rams quarterback room.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ty-simpson/000.analysis: With Matthew Stafford likely to have another limited training camp as he manages a back issue for the second straight year, rookie No. 13 pick Ty Simpson and former fourth-round pick Stetson Bennett are battling for the backup role. Though the team wants Jimmy Garoppolo back, the vet is mulling retirement, leading to one of these two unproven arms to be thrust into the backup quarterback role. Atkins reports Bennett took reps first in Stafford’s two missed practices in minicamp but neither Bennett nor Simpson “were able to stand out ahead of the other.” The Rams consider the backup role a significant void “with Stafford’s need to take time off and with the risk from each time Stafford takes a hit”, according to Atkins. A season in which Stafford misses time due to injury already decreases the Rams’ contention odds and an unprepared Simpson or Bennett as QB2 would be costly. Both will have time for developmental reps in camp and Simpson is worth rostering in Dynasty fantasy football formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Micah Parsons (knee) is active for Week 12 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: Parsons is officially back after the Packers activated him off the PUP list this week. He is back nearly a year after suffering a torn ACL last season, making his debut on Thanksgiving eve against the Rams. The Packers pass rush gets a boost with the return of the five-time Pro Bowler this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Packers activated Micah Parsons (knee/PUP) off the physically unable to perform list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: In other words, the questionable listing from an hour ago does not actually matter. Parsons is back after losing almost a year to a torn ACL. He’ll be directed to put some havoc on the field in his return against the Rams on Wednesday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Micah Parsons (knee) is questionable for Green Bay’s Week 12 game against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: We have no doubts he’ll play — Rams EDGE Myles Garrett said he was able to give Parsons some tickets for the 27-year-old’s long-awaited return yesterday. But players returning from PUP and IR have frequently just gotten a questionable tag regardless of how likely they are to play. Parsons got in limited work in each of the three practices this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Micah Parson has been cleared to return for the Packers’ Week 12 game against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: This one game a bit earlier than expected. While the hope was Parsons would return on Wednesday, the star pass rusher was listed as a limited participant in Monday’s practice, leaving some doubt as to whether or not he would be cleared for a return. Now, the Packers get back their 2025 sack leader who last played in Week 15 of last season, when he suffered a torn ACL on the road against the Broncos. Parsons will provide an immediate boost to a defense that currently ranks 16th in points allowed but eighth in passing yards allowed per game. They are also tied for the seventh-most team sacks in the league (29), and should see that number creep up a bit with Parsons back in the mix.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Micah Parsons (knee) was limited in Monday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: Parsons has been limited in each of the Packers’ first two practices to start the week. It’s long been believed that the star pass-rusher could be activated for Wednesday’s game against the Rams, but the team has declined to say whether or not that will come to fruition. We will likely have an official word on Parsons’ Week 12 availability when the Packers release their final injury report on Tuesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Micah Parsons is “on track” to play in Week 12 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: This isn’t a major surprise as head coach Matt LaFleur told reporters on Monday that he was hopeful Parsons would play in Week 12. It sounds like that timeline remains in the cards. Parsons has missed the first three months of the season while recovering from a torn ACL and meniscus injuries he suffered late last year. Getting Parsons back will be a huge boost for a Packers defense that hasn’t done much this year. Parsons had 12.5 sacks in 14 games with the Packers last year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said “that’s my plan” when asked if Micah Parsons (knee) could return in Week 12 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: LaFleur did note that his plan has “been different than everybody else’s” throughout Parsons’ recovery, and said the star pass-rusher still has “a couple more hurdles” to clear before they can commit to him returning. Parsons has been practicing with the team since November 4th and would need to come off injured reserve by Week 12 in order to avoid being shut down for the season. With the Packers now entering their Week 11 bye, we will likely get more news on Parsons’ Week 12 status closer to the weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Micah Parsons (knee/illness) will not play in Green Bay’s Week 10 game against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: Parsons got in limited sessions all week and seems to be in line to play in Week 12 when the Packers return from their bye week, assuming he can upgrade to full work. The Packers have slow-played his return and have been rewarded, as their defense has been able to play quite well without him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Micah Parsons (knee/illness) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: Parsons seemingly has a chance to play in Week 10 against the Vikings, but he remains in the questionable column at this time. Packers DC Jonathan Gannon has done well with Parsons sidelined. Getting him back will only improve the unit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Micah Parsons (knee) was ruled out for Week 9 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: Parsons was cleared to resume individual activities but was never likely to play against the Pats this week. The next chance for Parsons to play will be Week 10 against the Vikings, and there’s at least a smidgen of optimism he could be back for that contest.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: Josh Jacobs (thumb) is inactive for Week 12 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: Jacobs was limited in the Packers’ practices this week, but is not ready to return to play just yet. Kaleb Johnson and MarShawn Lloyd will split the backfield opportunities in his absence. The Packers also declared LB Zaire Franklin, OL Jager Burton, OL Donovan Jennings, and OL Mekhi Becton inactive for Week 12 against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: Josh Jacobs (thumb) is questionable for Green Bay’s Week 12 game against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: He got in limited work in each of Green Bay’s three practices this week, though some of them were “estimated” given the short week. Matt LaFleur said he was unlikely to play on Monday, so perhaps this is just a gamesmanship questionable. Obviously, if Jacobs does play, he’d be a suitable low-end RB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: Josh Jacobs (thumb) was limited in Monday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: Jacobs has been limited in each of the Packers’ first two practices as they prepare to face the Rams on Wednesday. While a limited session would generally be viewed as an encouraging sign for a player, head coach Matt LaFleur said earlier that he doesn’t expect Jacobs to suit up this week. We will continue to track his status until he receives an official designation for the game, but we’re assuming based on LaFleur’s comments that Jacobs will miss at least one more week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said Josh Jacobs (finger) is unlikely to play in Week 12 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: Jacobs was listed as limited in Sunday’s practice as the Packers prepare to take on the Rams on Wednesday, but he’s still only nine days removed from the surgery to repair his fractured ring finger. It was reported shortly after his injury that Jacobs could miss 2-3 weeks, and a return in Week 13 would put him close to that three-week timetable. It doesn’t sound like we should expect to see him this week against the Rams, but a return against the Saints could be in the cards if all goes well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Packers RB Josh Jacobs (finger) underwent successful surgery on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: Jacobs had surgery on his fractured right ring finger Friday in Los Angeles, according to Pelissero. The 28-year-old running back is expected to return in the next few weeks. In the meantime, Kaleb Johnson is the only usable Packers running back for fantasy purposes. He’s an RB3/FLEX play against the Vikings in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Josh Jacobs (finger) could miss 2-3 weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: In other words, the Packers might avoid placing Jacobs on injured reserve with his surgically-repaired finger. While he’s sidelined — including in Week 10 against the Vikings — some combination of Pierre Strong, Chris Brooks, Kaleb Johnson, and MarShawn Lloyd will handle backfield duties for the pass-heavy Packers. Johnson served as the nominal lead back in Week 9 against the Patriots, while Brooks is returning from injury and should slot in as the team’s pass-catching back. Johnson can be played as a touchdown-dependent RB3 option this week against a Minnesota defense that has shown recent vulnerabilities to the run.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur confirmed Josh Jacobs will undergo surgery on his fractured finger and didn’t rule out a stint on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: LaFleur confirmed previous reports that Jacobs will undergo surgery, but it sounds like he could be at risk of missing more than the three-week “maximum” that was reported. LaFleur not only said a stint on injured reserve was possible, but also noted that Jacobs playing through the injury was never an option, saying he “had no grip strength.” We don’t yet know when Jacobs will undergo his surgery, but LaFleur did confirm that it will be some time this week. With Jacobs now sidelined for the foreseeable future, Green Bay will look to MarShawn Lloyd, Pierre Strong, and Kaleb Johnson to lead the backfield heading into Week 10 against the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reports Josh Jacobs will undergo surgery on his fractured finger and “is expected to miss a maximum of three weeks.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: Less than 24 hours after it was reported that the team would see if Jacobs could play through his fractured finger, they have now opted for surgery. The decision to say Jacobs could be out “a maximum of three weeks” suggests he will avoid the injured reserve and that this will be more of a week-to-week thing, and that he could return before the end of the month. Jacobs has totaled 148 yards from scrimmage and three touchdowns on 47 touches since returning from the Commissioner’s Exempt list. Now, the Packers will likely take a bit of a committee approach in the weeks ahead and could lean more on Kaleb Johnson, who was solid against the Patriots (14-68-1), with Jacobs and MarShawn Lloyd (knee) both sidelined. That said, all Packers running backs will be hard to trust as anything more than desperation dart throws in Week 10 when they take on a stout Vikings defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: Josh Jacobs suffered a fractured finger in the Packers’ Week 9 win over the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: Jacobs exited early in the first quarter after his finger got caught in a defender’s facemask while he attempted a stiff arm. While he was never officially ruled out, Jacobs never returned to the field and was instead on the sideline in full uniform. According to Schneidman, the Packers plan to find a way for Jacobs to play through the injury, but he was unable to return in this one. Although, to be fair, he also wasn’t needed, as the Packers’ offense was in control throughout the evening. We assume Jacobs would see close to a normal workload if he is active for Week 10 against the Vikings, meaning fantasy manager can treat him as a strong RB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: Josh Jacobs (hand) is questionable to return in Week 9 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: This news comes from the official team account. It was hard to tell when Jacobs suffered the injury, but star running back could be seen jogging to the locker room with trainers late in the first quarter. Jacobs leaves the game with five rushing yards on four carries and will be replaced by Pierre Strong with MarShawn Lloyd (knee) being inactive.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tai-felton.headline: Tai Felton (hip) was limited in Wednesday’s walk-through.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tai-felton.analysis: Felton pops up on the injury report with a limited listing as he deals with a hip injury. The second-year wide receiver saw a team-high 12 targets in Week 11 against the 49ers and has seen increased opportunities with Jordan Addison still dealing with a thumb injury. Also limited was Myles Price (knee/groin). Both Price and Felton offer limited deep-league upside with Addison out. Felton is the receiver to roster, if you must.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tai-felton.headline: Tai Felton caught 6-of-12 targets for 42 yards in the Vikings’ Week 11 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tai-felton.analysis: Felton operated as a starter on the perimeter opposite Justin Jefferson but was unable to capitalize on a team-leading 12 targets. Even so, Felton should be expected to continue as a starter in the offense for as long as Jordan Addison remains sidelined due to a thumb injury, a role that could yield viable Flex status in the coming weeks. Fantasy managers in a bind could do worse than scooping Felton from waivers ahead of a Week 12 meeting with the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tai-felton.headline: Tai Felton caught 2-of-3 targets for 27 yards in the Vikings’ Week 5 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tai-felton.analysis: Jordan Addison missed this game with an ankle injury and the Vikings deployed Felton as their WR2 over Jauan Jennings. Jennings ran fewer routes and failed to catch his only target. Felton wasn’t awfully productive either, but it’s good to see the former third-round pick picking up more work in his second season. He will return to a rotational role, assuming Addison is cleared to play after the Vikings’ Week 6 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tai-felton.headline: ESPN’s Kevin Seifert reports Vikings WRs Jordan Addison and Tai Felton will have “no issues going forward” after suffering arm injuries in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tai-felton.analysis: Seifert earlier reported that Addison and Felton had left with “what looked like hand/arm injuries.” Neither resumed practicing for Wednesday, but seem to be fine moving forward, according to Seifert. The Vikings avoid a major injury with Addison, but he is still set to miss the first three games of the season. Felton is the team’s third-round rookie and in line to compete with Jalen Nailor for the WR3 role this season. Both are still on track for Week 1, but with Nailor (hand) currently week-to-week, the Vikings may still look to acquire a veteran receiver.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tai-felton.headline: Vikings WRs Jordan Addison and Tai Felton left practice early on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tai-felton.analysis: We don’t have confirmed status updates from the team yet, but The Athletic’s Alec Lewis believes Addison jammed “something” and that Felton “looked like he dinged his arm.” Felton, per ESPN’s Kevin Seifert, walked off the field with a wrap on his left hand. If there’s one thing that would accelerate trade talks for wideouts ahead of last cuts, it’s more injuries to this room. The Vikings should update Addison’s (and Felton’s) status in the coming days.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tai-felton.headline: Vikings WR Jalen Nailor will undergo further evaluation after suffering a hand injury on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tai-felton.analysis: Nailor was expected to function as the Vikings’ fill-in No. 2 wide receiver with Jordan Addison suspended for the first three games of the season. Justin Jefferson is sidelined by a hamstring injury and Rondale Moore recently suffered a season-ending knee injury. The Nailor news leaves the wide receiver corps worryingly thin, and early-July reports on dynasty darling, rookie WR Tai Felton, indicated he may be best suited to special teams work in year one. The Vikings could make a move to acquire a proven, if unexciting, veteran to the mix.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tai-felton.headline: The Athletic’s Alec Lewis believes Vikings WR Tai Felton’s rookie season will be “spent mostly on special teams.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tai-felton.analysis: Lewis notes that Felton could see some snaps on offense if Jordan Addison is suspended in relation to his pending DUI trial. Otherwise, it sounds like Jalen Nailor will be back as the team’s third receiver. Nailor didn’t earn many targets in the WR3 role last year but did cash in with six touchdowns and 414 yards on 28 grabs. Nailor is on the menu as a dart throw in deep best ball formats while the third-round rookie is only intriguing as a dynasty stash.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tai-felton.headline: Vikings signed third-round pick WR Tai Felton to a four-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tai-felton.analysis: Felton is quietly in play to challenge Vikings No. 3 WR Jalen Nailor in training camp. Nailor (5'11/190) caught 28-of-42 targets for 414 yards and six touchdowns in his first season as a starter last year, with the latter category buoying his fantasy productivity. Felton (6'1/183), meanwhile, caught 96-of-143 targets for 1,119 yards and nine touchdowns while averaging 2.32 yards per route run in his final college season. Fantasy managers should monitor Felton’s training camp reports this summer, as he could have a matchup-based WR5 role if everything falls into place.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tai-felton.headline: Vikings selected Maryland WR Tai Felton with the No. 102 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tai-felton.analysis: Felton’s production steadily rose over four years at Maryland, culminating in a 96/1124/9 receiving line in his senior season. He’s a svelte outside receiver (6'1/183) who won after the catch and racked up 590 YAC in his final season and forced 26 missed tackles; the fifth-most among wide receivers last year. Unsurprisingly, Felton didn’t have the frame to win contested targets in college, bringing down 7-of-18 contested looks in his final season. Felton showed off his speed and burst at the combine with a 4.37 Forty followed by broad and vertical jumps above the 90th percentile. He left Indianapolis with a 9.2 RAS. Felton has the production of a potential NFL starter, but he may need to bulk up to be anything more than a volatile WR3 in the pros.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Rachaad White (heel) is practicing in full for Week 12 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: White dealt with this issue last week, but managed to be active on Monday night. He should be fine for backup duties in Week 1 2 against the Cardinals, though Jacory Croskey-Merritt is likely the only fantasy starter in this backfield.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Rachaad White (heel) is questionable for Week 11 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: White’s week of practice was troubling, first appearing on the injury report on Friday with a limited designation due to a heel ailment before being downgraded to a “DNP” Saturday. Even so, head coach Dan Quinn indicated the veteran back is “on track” for Monday Night Football. Assuming he is active, White is likely to slot back into the primary change of pace role behind Jacory Croskey-Merritt, the latter of whom appears set to be activated from injured reserve in time for Monday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Rachaad White (heel) missed practice on Saturday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: White was added to the injury report and was a limited participant in practice on Friday. His missed practice Saturday is another bad sign for the 27-year-old running back’s availability. With Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) trending towards being available, White doesn’t seem to have much fantasy value at the moment. CB Amik Robertson, who was seen limping in the locker room on Friday, also missed practice Saturday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Rachaad White (heel) was added to the injury report as a limited participant on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: Mid-week additions to the injury report are generally a bad sign for a player’s availability. Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) is also practicing in full, potentially pushing White into the droppable tier once tomorrow’s official injury report is released. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Rachaad White rushed 11 times for 47 yards in the Commanders’ Week 10 win over the Giants, adding five yards on one reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: White started in name only, playing the first two drives before splitting backfield duties with fellow veteran Austin Ekeler for the remainder of the game. The two backs ended with the same number of opportunities while also splitting red zone work, with White narrowly missing a touchdown in the second quarter on his second longest run of the evening, a seven-yard scamper up the gut that was stopped at the one. His lone explosive run went for 18 yards, with those two carries accounting for more than 50 percent of his yardage total on the ground. White has fallen into a strict timeshare in the absence of Jacory Croskey-Merritt and brings little fantasy upside ahead of a Week 11 meeting with the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Rachaad White rushed seven times for 28 yards in the Commanders’ Week 9 loss to the Rams, adding two receptions for 41 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: White’s 28 rushing yards led all Commanders running backs, but his biggest play of the game came through the air. In the second quarter, White turned a short screen pass upfield for a 45-yard gain, positioning the Commanders for a touchdown, which came on the following play when Van Jefferson found the end zone for a seven-yard score. White’s only other catch went for a four-yard loss, but the 41 receiving yards still set a new season-high for him. The 27-year-old free agent signee has three touchdowns this season and hasn’t totaled more than 80 yards from scrimmage in any game this season. He will be a fringe RB2/RB3 against the Giants, with Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) still sidelined for a few more weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Rachaad White rushed 11 times for 55 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 8 win over the Eagles, adding five yards on two receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: White averaged just over two yards per carry on his first eight attempts before breaking loose for a 33-yard gain entering the final two minutes of the fourth quarter. He would find the end zone two plays later to salvage an otherwise underwhelming fantasy outing while operating in a three-way timeshare with Austin Ekeler and Jeremy McNichols. Although White’s fantasy value is clearly higher in the absence of Jacory Croskey-Merritt, his performance in Week 8 goes down as his first fantasy-viable start through the first eight weeks of the 2026 season. Fantasy managers are likely better off exploring alternatives ahead of a poor matchup against the Rams in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Rachaad White rushed seven times for 27 yards in the Commanders’ Week 6 loss to the 49ers, adding 30 yards and a touchdown on four receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: The Commanders immediately found themselves in a negative game environment, managing just 17 offensive plays and 90 yards of total offense in the first half. While White found the end zone from nine yards out in the fourth quarter on an in-breaking route, the backfield split amongst White, Jeremy McNichols, and Austin Ekeler was troubling for fantasy managers looking to the former as a potential option with lead back Jacory Croskey-Merritt on injured reserve. White and the Commanders head to their bye week at a 1-4-1 record and some serious questions to answer, the least of which is the current state of their backfield.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Commanders ruled out RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) for Week 6 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: No surprise here. Croskey-Merritt has been dealing with a groin injury since the start of the season. This week he couldn’t practice and has since been officially ruled out for the Commanders’ Monday Night Football matchup against the 49ers. Croskey-Merritt will get a two-week break with Washington on bye in Week 7. Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler figure to handle the majority of the backfield touches in his absence with White being the preferred fantasy option between the two.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) did not practice on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: Croskey-Merritt has played through multiple injuries this year. We still think he has a chance to face the 49ers in Week 6’s Monday Night Football game. Rachaad White (shoulder) sported a red non-contact jersey for the first time this week, and was downgraded to limited today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.headline: Jayden Daniels (left elbow/left hand) is practicing in full for Week 12 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.analysis: Daniels’ left elbow issue is obviously not new, but the left hand injury is. That said, he is practicing in full and gets an exceptionally soft matchup against the Cardinals’ defense this week. Daniels is a high-end QB1, as usual.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.headline: Commanders signed Brandon Aiyuk, formerly of the 49ers, to the practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.analysis: Aiyuk worked out for the Commanders earlier today and they didn’t let him leave the building without a deal. He’ll likely spend a week or two on the practice squad as he gets up to speed with the playbook before being elevated to the active roster. It’s anyone’s guess as to how much Aiyuk has left in the tank. He was struggling early in the 2024 season before suffering a season-ending ACL injury and hasn’t played a snap since. On the other hand, the Commanders need more firepower on offense with Terry McLaurin out for the season and Aiyuk played with Jayden Daniels at Arizona State. The floor is nonexistent, but Aiyuk is still worth adding in deeper fantasy formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.headline: Jayden Daniels completed 23-of-35 passes for 289 yards in the Commanders’ 22-20, Week 11 win over the Bengals, adding 55 yards on six carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.analysis: Daniels and the Commanders were unable to get anything going offensively while playing through driving rain in the first half, going three-and-out on three of their first four possessions before their lone touchdown drive of the game on their final possession before the break. Things would change in the second half as Daniels led five consecutive scoring drives, all of which ended in field goals, proving enough to eke out a victory that could have saved the team’s season. The 4-5-1 Commanders remain two games behind the division-leading Giants with two months remaining in the regular season, but a loss to the Bengals would have made a late-season push toward the playoffs almost insurmountable. Daniels and the Commanders now prepare to face the Cardinals on the road in Week 12, where the veteran signal caller will remain an upside QB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.headline: Jayden Daniels completed 23-of-33 passes for 249 yards, three touchdowns, and two interceptions in the Commanders’ 24-21, Week 10 win over the Giants, adding 28 yards on 10 carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.analysis: A late second quarter touchdown drive that was sparked by a long reception by veteran wide receiver Stefon Diggs was capped off by tight end Ben Sinnott’s first touchdown of the season to send the Commanders into the half with a three-point lead. The two sides would trade touchdowns in the third quarter before the wheels appeared to fall off for Washington, with their first three possessions of the final frame going turnover on downs, interception, and interception, allowing the Giants to nurse a four-point lead inside the two-minute warning. Daniels drove the field in 49 seconds on just three plays, connecting with Diggs for a 32-yard touchdown with under a minute remaining. The Commanders would escape on the backs of a Rasul Douglas interception to send the team to a 3-5-1 record, now two games back of the Giants and with the first tie-breaker in hand following the previous tie. Daniels will look to keep the momentum going in a Week 11 meeting with the surging Bengals, where he will be an upside QB1 in another must-win game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.headline: Jayden Daniels completed 24-of-35 passes for 273 yards and one touchdown in the Commanders’ 20-13, Week 9 loss to the Rams, adding four runs for 16 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.analysis: Daniels played mostly mistake-free football in this one, but a lost fumble on a strip-sack by Myles Garrett near the end of the first half proved costly as the Commanders had a chance to add to their 10-3 lead before halftime. His lone touchdown pass of the day came on a seven-yard pass to Van Jefferson, who surprisingly ended up leading the Commanders with 58 receiving yards on the day, but Daniels and the offense struggled to generate much offense in the second half against a defensive front that featured both Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett together for the first time. Daniels saw 115 of his passing yards come on his final two drives of the game as he attempted to mount a comeback, but some off-target throws and two sacks on the game’s final drive all but buried any hopes of a comeback. Daniels’ disappointing showing on the ground marks the third straight week in which he has rushed for 23 or fewer yards, and he has managed only 10 rush attempts over that stretch. Now sitting at 2-5-1 on the season, Daniels and the Commanders will look to turn things around on a short week as they prepare to face the Giants on Thursday Night Football. He profiles more as a low-end QB1 until he begins to add more value in the rushing game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.headline: Jayden Daniels completed 16-of-29 passes for 217 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ 27-10, Week 8 win over the Eagles, adding 23 yards on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.analysis: Daniels started the game going 4-of-10 passing in the first quarter, which included an interception that was called back due to penalty, two false start penalties in the red zone, and a missed field goal, causing the Commanders to quickly fall into a 10-point deficit. They would clean things up from there as they rattled off 27 unanswered points to improve to 2-4-1 as they chase the division-leading Giants. A 53-yard completion to Treylon Burks and 30-yard completions to Antonio Williams and Stefon Diggs gave the offense explosive plays in key situations during the final three frames to boost Daniels’ counting stats despite poor efficiency. The win was the first victory in a Daniels start since 5 October of the 2025 season as the Commanders saved their season, at least for the moment. They get a difficult matchup against the Rams in Week 9, where Daniels will remain a middling QB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.headline: Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley believes it could make long-term sense for the Commanders to acquire Brian Thomas, Jr.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.analysis: Shipley mentions the Commanders and Rams as wideout-desperate teams who might be interested in trading for Thomas before the NFL’s trade deadline. The Jaguars have apparently soured on the one-time burgeoning star in recent weeks; against the Texans in Week 6, Thomas ran a pass route on just 28 percent of the Jags’ drop backs and saw two targets. The Commanders, meanwhile, lost Terry McLaurin to a potentially long-term knee injury on Monday night. Thomas, per Shipley, “is not a trade that would make a ton of sense for a Commanders team that might be losing a ton of games and needs their picks to rebuild ... but it would make sense for a general manager who needs to keep his job to give his quarterback a familiar and talented target. Daniels was Thomas’ quarterback during their final seasons at LSU, and the connection between the two could go a long-way toward solving some of Washington’s long-term issues at the wide receiver position.” BTJ’s fantasy prospects would get a big boost if he were to land in Washington in the coming weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.headline: Jayden Daniels completed 29-of-40 passes for 300 yards and two touchdowns in the Commanders’ 23-17, Week 6 loss to the 49ers, adding 10 yards on four carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.analysis: The Commanders gained just 90 yards of total offense and ran just 17 offensive plays in the first half, taking a 20-3 deficit into the break. Two quick touchdown drives to end the third quarter and begin the fourth quarter had the team in position to pull off an improbable comeback but two critical errors from Daniels sank that effort. The first error occurred on fourth down in the red zone with just over two minutes to play, when the team was late to break the huddle and ended up taking their first timeout down by six. They would fail to convert but would get the ball back with no timeouts and 52 seconds left. Daniels then committed an intentional grounding penalty from the San Francisco 28 with 16 seconds left, which incurred a loss of down and a 10-second runoff on the clock. The game would end on the following play. That now makes consecutive contests with late-game clock mismanagement that cost the Commanders potential wins. Rumors continue to swirl about a potential coaching change as the Commanders limp into their bye at a 1-4-1 record.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.headline: Jayden Daniels completed 17-of-25 passes for 199 yards in the Commanders’ 27-27, Week 5 tie with the Giants, adding nine carries for 103 additional yards and two touchdowns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.analysis: Daniels turned in one of the best games of his career on the ground on Sunday against the Giants. Daniels broke off an uncontested 38-yard touchdown run in the third quarter to put the Commanders up 19-6, and later broke free for a 26-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter to again extend the Commanders’ lead. Both runs came on scrambles where the Giants seemingly forgot Daniels was a threat to run at any moment, and Daniels made the most of his opportunities. With the Commanders in range for a game-winning field goal late in overtime, Daniels inexplicably took a sack with no timeouts left on what appeared to be an attempt to center the ball in time for the game-winning try. We’ll likely get an explanation from both Daniels and head coach Dan Quinn on that final play, but Washington snatched defeat from the jaws of victory to move to 1-3-1 on the season. Despite the late-game gaffe, Daniels looked on-point for most of the afternoon, but struggled at times against the blitz, as the Giants brought pressure in several key spots to force Daniels to get the ball out quick or throw it away. Daniels looked like the elite dual threat fantasy managers want to see, and will be firmly in the QB1 ranks in next week’s game against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports “there are doctors around the NFL who believe it’s a matter of when, not if, Jayden Daniels hurts his left elbow again.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.analysis: Schefter immediately added the caveat that the “overwhelming opinion” among doctors was that playing with a brace was a viable option. Daniels reportedly contemplated surgery after dislocating his elbow for the second time in less than a year. He opted against it and missed two games. Daniels is now set to return for Week 5 against the Giants. The Commanders could scale back his rushing for the time being, but OC David Blough already dismissed the idea that the playbook would be limited because of Daniels’ elbow injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Michael Mayer (back) is practicing in full for Week 12 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: Mayer injured his back in the Raiders’ Week 11 loss to the Broncos, but he is evidently good to go this week. Brock Bowers (ankle) was limited today, tentatively putting him on track to face the Browns this weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Michael Mayer caught 1-of-4 targets for four yards in the Raiders’ Week 11 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: To add insult to injury for fantasy managers who streamed Mayer, Ian Thomas found the end zone on his only grab of the day. Mayer has typically played the inline tight end role with Brock Bowers operating as a de facto wide receiver. Because of that, Bowers’ absence today didn’t actually free up that many extra snaps or routes for Mayer. The targets also went to the team’s wide receivers instead of Mayer. Whether or not Bowers plays next week doesn’t make much of a difference for Mayer. He will be, at best, a low-end TE2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports there is “not a lot of optimism” that Brock Bowers (ankle/quad) will play in Week 11 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: Bowers returned to practice earlier in the week and was listed as questionable on Friday. Schefter noted that Bowers is pushing to play, but we doubt the team will let him suit up after suffering another ankle injury. That’s on top of the quad issue, which seems to be minor compared to the ankle. Assuming Bowers is out, Michael Mayer should see an uptick in targets against a Denver defense that has bled fantasy points to tight ends this season. He would be a solid streaming option if Bowers is ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Raiders believe Brock Bowers (ankle) avoided a major injury in Week 10’s loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: Bowers is expected to undergo more tests to confirm the severity of his injury, but Rapoport said the Raiders believe they will have him back “sooner rather than later.” Bowers had his ankle rolled up in the first quarter of Sunday’s loss and did not return to the field after making a trip to the locker room. His absence will be felt by a Raiders offense that has relied heavily on him since drafting him in 2024, and leaves rookie QB Fernando Mendoza without a valuable outlet in the passing game. Backup tight end Michael Mayer, who is in the midst of a career year, could have some value as a fringe TE1/TE2 in any games Bowers misses.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Brock Bowers will be reevaluated on Monday after suffering an ankle injury in Las Vegas’ Week 10 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: Kubiak told reporters that the team has not yet determined the injury’s severity. Tomorrow’s tests will provide more info. Bowers injured his ankle in the first quarter and was taken into the blue medical for examination. He managed to return for Fernando Mendoza’s 10-yard touchdown run, but was taken to the locker room after that. Bowers then returned to the field early in the second quarter, catching a 12-yard pass on third down. Unfortunately, his ankle wasn’t feeling right and he was again taken back to the locker room before later being ruled out. His day ended with two catches for 18 yards. The Raiders face the Broncos and Browns before going on bye in Week 13. Hopefully, he is able to return before then. Michael Mayer will be a TE1 if Bowers misses time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Michael Mayer caught 2-of-3 targets for 16 yards in the Raiders’ Week 10 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: The Vegas passing attack was snuffed out from start to finish by an elite Seattle defense. Mayer could see a marked increase in targets if Brock Bowers misses time with the ankle injury he sustained in the first quarter. Mayer, who was productive earlier this season when Bowers was sidelined with injury, would be a legit streaming option in Week 11 against Denver if Bowers is out. The Broncos allow the tenth most fantasy points per target to tight ends this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Michael Mayer caught all three of his targets for 37 yards in the Raiders’ Week 9 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: Mayer was second on the team in pass routes behind Brock Bowers. He nearly had not one, but two touchdown catches on the day. Mayer had the ball knocked out of his hand as he reached for the goal line in the first half, and was called for pass interference on a short touchdown reception in the fourth quarter. It was a tough luck day for the Raiders’ TE2. With 15 receptions over the past three games coming into Week 9, Mayer is usable in deeper formats going forward. He gets the Seahawks in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Michael Mayer caught 5-of-6 targets for 53 yards in the Raiders’ Week 8 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: This was Mayer’s fourth five-catch outing of the season. Only Brock Bowers caught more passes this afternoon. It could have been a bigger day in fantasy, but Mayer’s unconverted look was an inaccurate goal-line pass he short-armed. Mayer has a reasonable enough PPR TE2 floor, but his spiked week potential remains limited enough that he is not a very exciting streamer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Michael Mayer caught all three of his targets for 32 yards in the Raiders’ Week 7 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: Mayer benefited from a pass-heavy second half for the Raiders as they once again faced a big deficit. He ran a pass route on 38 of the Raiders’ 49 drop backs. With four games of at least five targets, Mayer profiles as a desperation play in tight end premium games and a 12-team option if Brock Bowers misses time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Michael Mayer caught 7-of-9 targets for 95 yards in the Raiders’ Week 6 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: This is the second time in three weeks that Mayer has popped up for a big performance. With Brock Bowers blanketed for much of the first half, Mayer stepped up to catch five passes for 52 yards in the first half, and he ripped off an impressive 28-yard reception in the second half on a drive that ended with a Matt Gay field goal. Playing behind Bowers continues to make Mayer a risky fantasy bet, but he’s averaging 6.7 targets in his last three games, which is buoyed by this week’s nine-target game and a 10-target outing in Week 4 against the Chiefs. With a few reliable tight ends on bye in Week 7, Mayer could have some viability as a dart throw next week against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mccar.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that coach Mike McCarthy “has the full support” of the Steelers’ organization and the team is “not planning to make any immediate changes.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mccar.analysis: McCarthy can rest easy knowing that the organization fully backs him. Rapoport’s “immediate changes” phrasing does allow room for interpretation, though. Perhaps the team could move on in the offseason. Until then, McCarthy will roll with Mason Rudolph as his starting quarterback. They face the Broncos on Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mccar.headline: The Pittsburgh Post-Gazette’s Gerry Dulac believes the Steelers won’t draft a QB until round three at the earliest.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mccar.analysis: In his article, Dulac writes that the Steelers “have little if no intention of taking a quarterback with their top pick,” while adding “it’s more than likely it wouldn’t be until the third round” when they would consider drafting a QB. He also added that they would only take a QB if they believed he had a higher ceiling than Will Howard, who they selected in the sixth-round of last year’s draft. The Steelers met with Penn State’s Drew Allar, Miami’s Carson Beck, and Alabama’s Ty Simpson at last week’s combine, with Simpson being the only QB who is believed to have a chance at going in the first round. Whether or not Aaron Rodgers opts to return for another season will likely also factor into the team’s decision on if/when they should draft a QB, but regardless, it doesn’t sound like we should expect the Steelers to reach into the first-round to draft their quarterback of the future.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mccar.headline: Steelers HC Mike McCarthy said he believes the team has “a playoff roster” already assembled.
