https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mccar.analysis: There’s certainly no denying the Steelers made the playoffs in 2025, but with no quarterback of note on the team and no notable receiver behind DK Metcalf on the depth chart, it’s hard to definitively say the Steelers have a playoff roster in place for next season. Add in two aging veterans on the defensive side in Cam Heyward and T.J. Watt and things get even more complicated. That said, McCarthy said he does not view the Steelers’ job as “a start-over opportunity,” so it will be interesting to see what the team’s roster turnover looks like in the coming months. As was the case with Mike Tomlin for several years, the Steelers still have to find a quarterback who can be a mainstay on the roster for more than two seasons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mccar.headline: Steelers coach Mike McCarthy said he will call plays for Pittsburgh in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mccar.analysis: Not exactly earth-shattering news here, especially with no offensive coordinator tied to him yet. This should always have been the expectation for McCarthy. Steelers fans should get ready to get re-acquainted with slant/flat combination routes with Arthur Smith off to Ohio State.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mccar.headline: NFL Network’s Tom Pelissero reports Steelers are working to hire Mike McCarthy for their vacant head coaching position.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mccar.analysis: Pelissero reported yesterday that he believed that veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers would be most likely to play for one coach in 2026, naming Mike McCarthy as that coach. Not 24 hours later and the Steelers are reportedly working to hire McCarthy as their next head coach following the departure of Mike Tomlin. The dominoes certainly appear to be falling into place to get the franchise what they want, which appears to be Aaron Rodgers for another season. McCarthy last served as the head coach of the Dallas Cowboys between 2020 and 2024 but coached Rodgers for 13 years in Green Bay at the beginning of the aging veteran’s career. It also serves as a homecoming for the 62-year-old coach, who grew up in the Pittsburgh area.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mccar.headline: NFL Network’s Tom Pelissero believes “if Aaron Rodgers were coming back to play for one coach in 2026, it would be Mike McCarthy.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mccar.analysis: Pelissero noted that this wouldn’t be the Steelers “trying to lure” Rodgers to come back, but instead frames it as “a bonus” that might not be available if Pittsburgh hired a different head coach with no previous relationship with Rodgers. Given how the Steelers seem locked into a mindset of trying to win games rather than rip it down to the studs, you can squint and understand how they’d come to McCarthy as a good option compared to the more unproven coaches in this hiring class. We will be writing blurbs about Aaron Rodgers until the end of time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mccar.headline: Steelers completed an interview with former Cowboys head coach Mike McCarthy for their head-coaching vacancy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mccar.analysis: McCarthy took the year after being relieved of his duties with the Cowboys following the 2024 season. McCarthy also interviewed with the Giants and Titans, though both organizations chose to go with other candidates. McCarthy’s 2024 Cowboys squad averaged just 5.0 yards per play during the regular season, ranking 27th among NFL offenses.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mccar.headline: NFL Network’s Tom Pelissero reports the Steelers on Wednesday will interview former Cowboys head coach Mike McCarthy for the team’s head coaching vacancy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mccar.analysis: McCarthy had interviewed with the Titans, who filled their head coaching vacancy on Tuesday by hiring former 49ers defensive coordinator Robert Saleh. McCarthy, who was raised in the Pittsburgh area, would seem to be a natural fit for the Steelers as they look to keep their postseason streak alive even if they are not Super Bowl contenders. McCarthy has shown he can do just that during his stints in Green Bay and Dallas. McCarthy has won 61 percent of his games over 18 years as an NFL head coach. The Steelers are reportedly open to McCarthy’s former QB Aaron Rodgers returning in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mccar.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Mike McCarthy “has now interviewed twice in recent days for the Titans head coaching job.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mccar.analysis: It was reported over a week ago that McCarthy would interview with the Titans on January 17th, but according to Schefter, the team also spoke with McCarthy “once in late December in Green Bay,” while the season was still going on. This certainly throws a bit of a wrinkle in how we should view the Titans’ head-coaching vacancy, as the early decision to speak with McCarthy in-season could hint at him being the favorite in the clubhouse. McCarthy is also expected to speak with the Steelers in the coming days, giving him another potential suitor if things don’t work out with the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mccar.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Steelers “are expected to speak with former Cowboys HC Mike McCarthy about their head coach vacancy.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mccar.analysis: As Schefter notes, McCarthy was born in Pittsburgh and worked under Steelers GM Omar Khan during his time in New Orleans in the early 2000s. For a team that just moved on from Mike Tomlin because of his recent lack of playoff success, McCarthy would be a bit of an odd choice. He made the playoffs three times during five seasons in Dallas but managed to win just one postseason game. McCarthy was, however, more successful in Green Bay. He won a Super Bowl over the Steelers and made the NFC Championship three other times. His track record in the postseason is a mixed bag at best, but the Steelers could do worse in this head coaching cycle.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kedon-slovis/0.headline: Cardinals claimed QB Kedon Slovis off waivers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kedon-slovis/0.analysis: The former Raven is now a Cardinal. He was notably on Arizona’s roster last summer. Slovis could end up taking live reps, pending Carson Beck’s (back) health and Josh Johnson’s performance, but he would only be a QB2/3 in that instance.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kedon-slovis/0.headline: Ravens waived QB Kedon Slovis.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kedon-slovis/0.analysis: He’ll reportedly garner interest from the Arizona Cardinals for some reason. Slovis, 25, played for Arizona in the preseason and the Texans in the 2025 preseason. Over his three preseason stints he’s 86-of-126 for 816 yards, three touchdowns, and three interceptions while taking nine sacks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kedon-slovis/0.headline: Ravens signed QB Kedon Slovis from the Packers practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kedon-slovis/0.analysis: Slovis could, unbelievably, get the start Thursday night against the Jaguars with Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) out, and Joe Fagnano (ankle) iffy to suit up. If Fagnano can play, Slovis would presumably serve as Baltimore’s backup. Fagnano completed 48 percent of his passes for 91 yards and a pick last week against the Bills. Look for the Ravens to be ultra run-heavy against Jacksonville, one of the league’s best run defenses. It will be tough to trust anyone in the Ravens offense as a viable fantasy option for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kedon-slovis/0.headline: Cardinals waived QB Kedon Slovis.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kedon-slovis/0.analysis: Slovis needed to unseat QB Gardner Minshew or QB Carson Beck to make the roster. He was unable to do so. He could return to Arizona via the practice squad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kedon-slovis/0.headline: Cardinals ruled out QB Carson Beck (rib) for the team’s preseason Week 1 game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kedon-slovis/0.analysis: According to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, Beck suffered a rib injury in the Cardinals’ Hall of Fame game against the Panthers. Despite feeling “soreness,” he managed to practice this week. The Cardinals “decided to keep him out tonight as a precaution and to allow more time to heal.” This pours a little cold water on Beck’s moderate hype, but the reporting suggests that the injury is not overly concerning. Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett will start, and presumably be relieved by QB Kedon Slovis at some point. No word yet on QB Gardner Minshew’s potential involvement tonight.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kedon-slovis/0.headline: When asked about the Cardinals’ starting quarterback job, general manager Monti Ossenfort said, “we’ll see how that room looks by the time we get in August.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/kedon-slovis/0.analysis: This doesn’t tell us a whole lot. Readers might recall that the 2026 NFL Draft is next week, and the Cardinals hosted Alabama QB Ty Simpson for a top-30 visit yesterday. If the Cardinals do not draft a rookie quarterback, Jacoby Brissett will likely be the default starter, with only Gardner Minshew and Kedon Slovis joining him on the roster at this time. If that is the case, the pass catchers likely stand to benefit. Brissett was able to distribute the ball effectively last year. Rolling with a developmental rookie could hurt the receiving outlooks for TE Trey McBride, WR Michael Wilson and WR Marvin Harrison Jr.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kedon-slovis/0.headline: Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett exited Week 12 against the Jaguars after suffering an apparent injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kedon-slovis/0.analysis: Brissett was hurt on a third-quarter scramble. The Cardinals’ quarterback was trotting out of bounds after picking up a short gain on the ground when Jaguars LB Devin Lloyd lowered his shoulder, hitting Brissett hard, up high, from the left side. Brissett remained down after the play, and eventually made his way to the blue medical tent. He was replaced by QB Kedon Slovis.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kedon-slovis/0.headline: Cardinals signed QB Kedon Slovis.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kedon-slovis/0.analysis: Slovis returns to his home state of Arizona after three preseason appearances with the Texans. He completed 27-of-43 passes for 233 yards, one touchdown and one interception and rushed three times for seven yards.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kedon-slovis/0.headline: Texans released QB Kedon Slovis.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kedon-slovis/0.analysis: Slovis was unable to make the Texans to the surprise of absolutely no one. The 24-year-old is a candidate for the practice squad of Houston or another team looking for signal-caller depth.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kedon-slovis/0.headline: Texans signed OG Braeden Daniels, formerly of the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kedon-slovis/0.analysis: Daniels’ 2023 rookie season was derailed by a torn rotator cuff. His new landing spot will hopefully allow him to compete for a backup role for a Texans’ squad that was likewise hit by significant injuries last year. Also signed by the Texans on Thursday were TE Cole Fotheringham, WR Xavier Johnson, S Mark Perry and QB Kedon Slovis.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/avery-smit.headline: Chargers claimed CB Avery Smith off waivers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/avery-smit.analysis: The Chargers traded Smith to the Seahawks earlier this year. The Seahawks waived him on Tuesday. Whether Smith plays meaningful snaps remains to be seen, but he is familiar with the system.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/avery-smit.headline: ESPN’s Brady Henderson believes Seahawks LB Ernest Jones’ comments “seemed to convey doubt that” S Nick Emmanwori (ankle) will play in Week 1 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/avery-smit.analysis: Henderson’s assessment is reasonable. Jones’ comments on Emmanwori’s abilities meandered, but he closed by saying the team is “focused on who’s out there, who’s available right now.” Emmanwori underwent surgery to deal with a nagging ankle issue in July. Seahawks GM John Schneider said recent trade acquisition CB Avery Smith had a “phenomenal preseason” and can line up on the perimeter and over the slot, making him a potential fill-in for Emmanwori’s hybrid nickel/safety role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/avery-smit.headline: Seahawks acquired CB Avery Smith from the Chargers in exchange for a sixth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/avery-smit.analysis: The news was first reported by NFL Insider Tom Pelissero. It’s no secret that the Seahawks have been looking for cornerback depth this preseason. Seattle signed Trevon Diggs and Terrion Arnold in recent weeks. Now the Seahawks send out a sixth-round pick to bring in Smith, a UDFA from Toledo who was a standout in Chargers training camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) is practicing in full for Week 12 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: Tate returned from his multi-week absence last week, posting a 2/58/1 receiving line. He faces the Jaguars’ capable defense in Week 12, but his role and talent keep him in the WR3 tier. Tate looks like a classic rookie wide receiver set to produce late in the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate caught 2-of-5 targets for 58 yards and a touchdown in the Titans’ Week 11 loss to the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: Active for the first time since Week 7, the No. 4 overall pick caught a -1 yard pass in the first quarter before adding a 59-yard touchdown in the third. In between, he drew a 38-yard DPI in the end zone to set the Titans up at the one-yard line. On his score, Tate appeared to be down by contact near mid-field, but he realized he had not been touched and got up and sprinted to the end zone. Heady stuff, though we would have liked to see more targets. Tate thankfully avoided setbacks with his shoulder injury, and is now ready to slot into the WR24-30 range for a tough Week 12 matchup with the Jags. Tate would be a safer WR2 were it not a 32-team slate for the holiday week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reports Titans WR Carnell Tate (shoulder) is likely to return against the Cowboys in Week 11.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: Tate hasn’t played since Week 7 due to a shoulder injury. Still officially questionable, Zenitz reports Tate is likely to play in Week 11. While he’s been out for over a month, Tate got in a full practice on Friday. He’ll be a high-end WR3 in a plus matchup against the brutal Cowboys defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) is questionable for Tennessee’s Week 11 game against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: The big news here is that he got in a full session on Friday after being limited on Wednesday and Thursday. The long layoff is still a little bit concerning, but a full session likely inches him over to the optimistic side of questionable in what looks to be a shootout. Tate will have high-end WR3 appeal if he’s able to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: Tate has now gotten in back-to-back limited sessions, though the fact that he’s coming off three weeks lost (two games, bye) leaves us a little unsure if we should say he’s “trending” towards playing. A full session would be nice to see and we’d be surprised if he cleared the questionable line on Friday without one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) returned to practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: Tate missed Week 8 because of the shoulder issue. He got the bye week to recover but still wasn’t able to suit up in Week 10. Robert Saleh told reporters on Monday that he is hoping Tate is ready to go for Sunday’s game. Even a limited practice today puts him on track to play. With Wan’Dale Robinson on IR, Tate will return to an elite target share, even if he’s not fully healthy. He will be in the WR3 mix if the team clears him for Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Titans coach Robert Saleh said he’s “hoping” Carnell Tate (shoulder) returns for Sunday’s game against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: Tate last played in Week 7. Saleh made the disclosure at Monday morning’s press conference, one day before Wan’Dale Robinson (ankle) landed on injured reserve. Tate’s return would be just in the nick of time, as the Titans have a dream defensive matchup and Cam Ward is suddenly playing the best football of his career. Especially with six teams on bye and Robinson sidelined, Tate would immediately return to the WR2 ranks. We will get our first Titans practice report of the week on Wednesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) will not play in Week 10 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: Head coach Robert Saleh said he is hopeful Tate will be able to return in Week 11 when the Titans visit the Cowboys, but his availability for that game will be determined once the Titans begin prepping for Dallas. In the meantime, the Titans will likely go with Wan’Dale Robinson and Chimere Dike as their top two wideouts after the pair led the team in routes run in Week 8 against the Bengals, with Elic Ayomanor also seeing some work (30 routes). Playing against a stout Jaguars defense will make all of the Titans’ receivers hard to trust as anything more than WR3/WR4 plays, while TE Gunnar Helm could also see more work after earning a season-high eight targets vs. the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) worked out with trainers on the side during Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: He did not elevate beyond an official DNP today, but this is an actual step after Tate missed four consecutive practices and Week 8 sandwiched around their Week 9 bye. He’ll have a non-zero chance to play this week heading into Friday, but you have to imagine the best we’ll see on Friday is a questionable tag.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: It’s a little concerning considering the Titans are coming off their bye week. Tate suffered the shoulder injury three weeks ago, and unless he can log a practice tomorrow or Friday, he’s likely to miss this week’s game against the Jaguars. His absence would make Wan’Dale Robinson viable in PPR formats, along with Chimere Dike, who led the Titans in receiving against the Bengals in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.headline: D.J. Reed (hip) is not on the final injury report and will play in Week 12 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.analysis: Lions EDGE DJ Wonnum (back) and S Chuck Clark (hamstring) are both questionable to play on Thursday. The Lions’ defense was already a fantasy-friendly unit before losing Aidan Hutchinson (knee) for the year. Bears skill position players should be in fantasy football lineups this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.headline: Lions declared CB D.J. Reed, CB Ennis Rakestraw Jr., DB Ketih Abney II, LB Amen Ogbongbemiga, EDGE Tyrus Wheat, and DL Mekhi Wingo inactive for Week 11 against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.analysis: Reed made seven starts this year before injuring his hip a few weeks ago. Rakestraw has been a depth option so far, but that would have been useful to have around with Reed out. The Lions’ defense will be as vulnerable as ever this week, though it’s anyone’s guess as to whether a hobbled Baker Mayfield will take advantage.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.headline: D.J. Reed (hip) is questionable for Detroit’s Week 11 game against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.analysis: He got in limited sessions all three practice days this week and seems to be trending in a good direction after missing Week 9 and Week 10 with this hip injury. He’s probably best-regarded as a game-time decision.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.headline: D.J. Reed (hip) won’t play in Detroit’s Week 10 game against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.analysis: Reed has not practiced since injuring his hip in Week 8. The Lions’ secondary remains a patchwork effort against Drake Maye and the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.headline: Lions ruled out Cade Mays (ankle) for Week 9 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.analysis: Brutal. Mays returned from injured reserve in Week 7 due to a preseason wrist injury. He injured his ankle in Week 8. The Lions ruled out S Kerby Joseph (knee) and CB D.J. Reed (hip), yet S Brian Branch (concussion) will play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.headline: Lions declared RT Blake Miller, LG Christian Mahogany, CB Keith Abney, EDGE Ahmed Hassanein, CB Ennis Rakestraw, LB Jimmy Rolder and DL Mekhi Wingo inactive for Week 2 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.analysis: Losing Miller and Mahogany for this one is unfortunate, especially with C Cade Mays (wrist) on injured reserve. The Bills, however, lost DT Ed Oliver to a pre-game hip injury. This should be a high-scoring, fantasy-friendly game environment tonight. Lions CB D.J. Reed (foot) will play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.headline: D.J. Reed (foot) is questionable for Week 2 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.analysis: Reed was a mid-week addition to the injury report because of his foot issue. He was limited for the final two practices of the week. Reed is likely on the optimistic side of questionable, but we won’t know for sure until the Lions release their inactives 90 minutes before kickoff.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.headline: Lions CB D.J. Reed (foot) was limited in Tuesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.analysis: He was a surprise addition to the report on Tuesday. The Lions secondary, already starting a wave of low-level veteran free agents like Rock Ya-Sin, Avonte Maddox, and Chuck Clark, can ill-afford to lose Reed before taking on the Bills on Thursday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.headline: Lions CB D.J. Reed (hamstring) is active for Week 12 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.analysis: Reed, a critical part of the Detroit secondary, will suit up for the first time since sustaining a serious hamstring injury in early October and landing on injured reserve. It’s not the best development for Jameis Winston and the Giants pass catchers. The Giants were massively run heavy in Week 11 against the Packers. Lions declared CB Terrion Arnold, RB Craig Reynolds, CB Nick Whiteside, DL Quinton Jefferson, and DL Mekhi Wingo inactive against New York.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.headline: Lions EDGE Aidan Hutchinson (elbow) is not on Detroit’s final Week 11 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/d-j-reed-j.analysis: Good thing, too, because the entire rest of the Lions defense found their way on to this report. Terrion Arnold (concussion), Kerby Joseph (knee) and Josh Paschal (back) were all ruled out. D.J. Reed (hamstring) and Amik Robertson (hamstring) are questionable. Both A.J. Brown and DeVonta Smith should see slight matchup uggrades given the CB injuries.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kobie-turn.headline: Rams activated DT Kobie Turner (groin) from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kobie-turn.analysis: Turner missed a month while on IR because of the groin issue. He will be active tonight for a must-win game against the Packers. Turner made six starts this year. He has 22 combined tackles with two passbreakups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kobie-turn.headline: Rams placed DL Kobie Turner (groin) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kobie-turn.analysis: It’s a tough injury for Turner, who is in the final year of his rookie contract and will miss at least four weeks. He’s been a mainstay of Los Angeles’ defense over his first three years with several high-hurry seasons and stellar run defense. The Rams interior defense has taken a big hit today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kobie-turn.headline: Rams selected Wake Forest DL Kobie Turner with the No. 89 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kobie-turn.analysis: Turner (6’2.5/293) was a walk-on at FCS-subdivision Richmond out of high school, where he redshirted, then played for four years before graduate transferring to Wake Forest in 2022. After walking on at Richmond and earning a scholarship, Turner racked up 16 sacks and 33.5 tackles for loss in four years against FCS competition. While the Combine snub is only average in size and weight, if not a bit of a tweener, he overcomes his lack of arm length by being active with his hands. He has a bit of a bowling ball tendency, where his aggression and activity in small spaces creates more havoc than any single skill or technique. His feet are his asset when it comes to play leverage, as his short shuttle time of 4.49 shows great change of direction in the interior. His evaluation relies on his production at a lower level of competition as he only held a reserve role at Wake Forest. However, his good work ethic and non-traditional path to the NFL will make for a good story and win the favor of a coach once he can get into camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kobie-turn.headline: Wake Forest has received a verbal commitment from redshirt senior DT Kobie Turner, formerly of Richmond.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kobie-turn.analysis: Turner (6'3/285) has one year of eligibility remaining and will spend it at Wake Forest after being named an FCS All-American defensive tackle for his 2021 efforts. This season, Turner started eight games for Richmond, totaling 21 quarterback pressures and five sacks per Pro Football Focus to go with 27 tackles and two forced fumbles. In his three seasons as a starter at Richmond, Turner has totaled 11 sacks and 70 tackles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said he thinks De’Zhaun Stribling (ankle) is “a couple of weeks away” from returning.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Exactly 10 weeks ago, it was reported that Stribling was expected to miss 10 weeks after undergoing surgery on his ankle. Unfortunately, it sounds like he needs more time to recover. ESPN’s Nick Wagoner believes Shanahan’s comments are in reference to Stribling “returning to practice, not necessarily playing.” Hopefully, Shanahan is actually referring to the latter timeframe. Regardless, Stribling should be stashed on fantasy football benches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: De’Zhaun Stribling (ankle) was seen working off to the side with trainers on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: According to ESPN’s Nick Wagoner, this is the first time Stribling has worked off to the side at practice since injuring his ankle in Week 1. We expect to see him listed as a non-participant, but this is still a great sign for his availability in the coming weeks. Stribling must be rostered in 10-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: 49ers WR De’Zhaun Stribling (ankle) is expected to miss 10 weeks after undergoing surgery on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: According to NBC Sports Bay Area’s Matt Maiocco, the 49ers are “hopeful he can return this season,” which is a tad confusing, given the 10-week return timeline. Regardless, 10 weeks, plus a little wiggle room, should allow Stribling to return late in the regular season, potentially in time to help fantasy managers make a playoff push. That said, he should probably only be kept on managed re-draft rosters with an injured reserve spot. Veteran WR Demarcus Robinson filled in for Stribling last week and may be FLEX-viable moving forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the 49ers placed De’Zaun Stribling (ankle) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Stribling will be sidelined for at least four weeks after suffering a serious ankle injury in Week 1’s win over the Rams. It’s a disappointing start for the rookie, who can safely be dropped in most fantasy leagues. Deebo Samuel, who led the Niners in slot routes last week, could see an uptick in playing time and targets over the next month. Samuel had 48 yards on six receptions against the Rams. He should be rostered in 12-team PPR formats ahead of the Niners’ Week 2 game against the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports De’Zhaun Stribling (ankle) is out “at least a month.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Stribling suffered a deltoid sprain in his ankle. He is not expected to undergo surgery at this time, though Rapoport notes it is still a possibility. The fact that Rapoport noted that Stribling is “still seeking opinions” suggests surgery is very much on the table. With the rookie sidelined, Demarcus Robinson will slide into the three-receiver rotation. He scored a long touchdown versus the Rams in Week 1, though he profiles as a boom/bust WR6 going forward. Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel will see the majority of targets in most weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: 49ers HC Kyle Shanahan said De’Zhaun Stribling’s Achilles was intact after Week 1’s win over the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Stribling was carted from the game late in the second quarter after briefly attempting to play through the ankle injury he suffered earlier in the game. While there was some concern that his injury was Achilles-related, Shanahan’s comments after the game suggest there’s little reason to be concerned about his Achilles at this time. Stribling played 21 snaps in the first half of Thursday’s game but was held without a catch. We’ll likely get more clarity on his status in the coming days, but hopefully the worst was avoided here.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: De’Zhaun Stribling (ankle) has been ruled for the remainder of Week 1 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Stribling was carted off during Friday’s contest, and finished without a catch in his NFL debut. He’ll get a little longer to potentially return for Week 2 against the Dolphins, but obviously his status for that contest is very much in doubt.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: De’Zhaun Stribling (ankle) exited Week 1 against the Rams on a cart.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Stribling hurt the ankle earlier in the contest, and while he was able to return shortly after, the rookie wideout was unable to continue and exited on the vehicle. It’s likely he won’t return to Friday’s game, but there should be an update on his status soon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: The Athletic’s Matt Barrows believes “the plan” is for WR De’Zhaun Stribling to be the primary slot receiver and WR Mike Evans’ “understudy” at X-receiver.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: In his projected depth chart, Barrows lists Stribling as both the starting slot receiver and the No. 2 X-receiver. He does not place Stribling on the Z-receiver depth chart, which could mean the rookie wide receiver has not yet earned a role in two-wide receiver sets. Veteran WR Deebo Samuel is the starting Z-receiver, though Barrows already reported that Samuel will take only “a portion” of the overall Z-receiver snaps. It would be surprising to see Nos. 2-3 Z-receivers, Jordan Watkins and Jacob Cowing, play ahead of Stribling when Samuel needs a breather, but the season is long and Stribling can always change Barrows’ mind. Early in the year, Stribling is likely best treated as a WR4/FLEX candidate. Were Evans to miss time, Stribling would seemingly slide into a full-time starting role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: 49ers general manager John Lynch said he hopes Mike Evans (adductor) will practice next week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Evans’ Week 1 status is starting to look iffy after missing most of the past few weeks with various injuries. Entering his age-33 season, Evans will need to log at least a couple practices next week if he’s going to suit up against the Rams in the season opener. Niners head coach Kyle Shanahan said Evans is “ahead of schedule doing good. But we know with Mike and where he is at in his career, we’ll definitely have to treat him differently.” An Evans absence would be a marked boost for De’Zhaun Stribling and perhaps Deebo Samuel. Evans will be a name to watch in the coming days.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-thom.headline: Cowboys activated S Jalen Thompson (hamstring) from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-thom.analysis: Running back Jashaun Corbin was elevated from the practice squad. He will back up Javonte Williams tomorrow against the Eagles. Thompson is back in the lineup after suffering a hamstring injury in Week 3. He will provide a small boost to a defense that will need an offseason overhaul to meaningfully improve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-thom.headline: Cowboys placed Jonathan Bullard (calf) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-thom.analysis: The team also placed safety Jalen Thompson (hamstring) on IR. Thompson was already expected to miss at least four weeks, so the move doesn’t come as a surprise. Bullard signed a one-year deal with the Cowboys this offseason. He has three combined tackles and .5 sacks through three games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-thom.headline: Cowboys EVP Stephen Jones said Jalen Thompson (hamstring) is set to miss “four-plus weeks.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-thom.analysis: In other words, he’s headed to injured reserve. The Cowboys safety room has been besieged by injuries this year, with Malik Hooker also missing time. They don’t have another safety on their practice squad so they may be hunting the tryout circuit on Tuesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-thom.headline: Cowboys S Jalen Thompson (hamstring) is questionable to return in Week 3 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-thom.analysis: Thompson left the field after getting caught up in a scrum that initially looked like a potential head/neck injury. It was later reported as a hamstring injury, with sideline reporter Tracy Wolfson saying the 28-year-old safety was struggling to make his way to the locker room. It sounds like Thompson could face an uphill battle to return to the field in this one. The Cowboys’ defense continues to be dealt one injury after another. Markquese Bell is next in line to replace Thompson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-thom.headline: Cowbyos agreed to terms with S Jalen Thompson, formerly of the Cardinals, on a three-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-thom.analysis: The deal is worth as much as $36 million, though the full details have yet to be announced. Thompson has been with the Cardinals since they drafted him in 2019. He has appeared in and started 62 games over the past four seasons. Thompson broke up six passes, notched one sack, and forced a fumble in 2025. He will be penciled in for a starting role on a Dallas offense that desperately needs to improve in 20206.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-thom.headline: Cardinals selected Washington State S Jalen Thompson in Round 5 of the 2019 NFL Supplemental Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-thom.analysis: Thompson (5'10/186) was a very active slot corner at Washington State, showcasing enough man-coverage skills for the Cardinals to burn a 2020 5th round pick. The safety will be a depth option early in his career, but The Athletic’s Dane Brugler believes Thompson can earn a starting role with some development. Overall, Thompson’s upside is limited by his size and average athleticism and that’s likely why he “fell” to Round 5 after earning some Round 2 and Round 3 love.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-thom.headline: PFF’s Mike Renner “would be surprised” if Washington State S Jalen Thompson wasn’t drafted with a second-round pick in the NFL Supplemental Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-thom.analysis: This is Thompson’s (5'10/186) ceiling since he comes in undersized and as an average athlete. It’s more likely that Thompson slides in as a Round 3-5 pick. The safety prospect’s best attribute comes against slot receivers and tight ends, showing tight man-coverage skills with decent ball skills. A couple dozen teams showed up to Thompson’s workout and he’s been flown out to team headquarters for further evaluation since.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-thom.headline: Washington State S Jalen Thompson recorded an unofficial 4.47 40-yard dash at his private workout.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-thom.analysis: Thompson (5'10/186) also participated in the vertical (33.5 inches), broad (10-foot-4), short shuttle (4.16 seconds), three-cone (6.98 seconds), and bench press (11 reps). His measurables aren’t overly impressive, but he also didn’t have the multi-month lead up to practice for the tests. Still, Thompson is a Round 2, 3, or 4 supplemental draft prospect as a slot corner or safety.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-thom.headline: Washington State S Jalen Thompson lost his final season of college eligibility because he purchased a banned supplement.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-thom.analysis: The Spokesman Review’s Theo Lawson reports it was not a steroid, but it was a supplement that is a violation of NCAA rules. Ironically, the supplement made Thompson (6'0/191) enter the NFL’s Supplemental Draft, where all teams will have interest. Considered a Day 2 prospect, Thompson offers talent and versatility as a high-end slot corner and safety. Expect Thompson to be drafted despite this violation. He’s working out for teams on July 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-thom.headline: Washington State S Jalen Thompson entered the NFL Supplemental Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-thom.analysis: Thompson (6'0/191) learned he wasn’t going to be eligible to play college ball in 2019, so he’ll try his luck with the NFL’s other draft. After two strong seasons at Washington State, Thompson should end up being drafted as an intriguing slot corner and safety prospect. To crack an active roster as a rookie, he’ll need to show some special teams value, but he had some experience doing so in college. This is a big loss for the Cougars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roschon-jo.headline: Bears ruled out Roschon Johnson (ankle) for Week 12 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roschon-jo.analysis: Johnson will be replaced by Salvon Ahmed as the Bears’ No. 3 running back. Ahmed does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats, with D’Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai splitting reps.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roschon-jo.headline: Roschon Johnson (ankle) did not practice on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roschon-jo.analysis: We wouldn’t be surprised if he was an IR candidate after he was carted off during Week 11’s win over the Saints. Salvon Ahmed will likely take over third-string duties for the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roschon-jo.headline: Roschon Johnson (ankle) was listed as a “DNP” on Monday’s estimated practice report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roschon-jo.analysis: Johnson departed the team’s Week 11 win over the Saints with an ankle injury and did not return, making his absence Monday notable on the short week. Expect D’Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai to dominate snaps and opportunities out of the backfield for the Bears in one of the biggest games of the season, with the winner left standing alone atop the competitive NFC North.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roschon-jo.headline: Roschon Johnson suffered an ankle injury in the Bears’ Week 11 game against the Saints and is doubtful to return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roschon-jo.analysis: Johnson was carted to the locker room in the first quarter against the Saints. He was announced to have an ankle injury and is doubtful to return. With Kyle Monangai back, the Bears had depth in the backfield again but lose a special teamer and third-string running back in Johnson against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roschon-jo.headline: Bears ruled out Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) for Week 7 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roschon-jo.analysis: Monangai will miss his third game in a row this week. Exactly two weeks ago, ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reported that Monangai’s turf toe injury would be an issue for 1-2 weeks. Technically, his statement remains accurate. This week’s Thursday Night Football game complicates things. If the Bears thought Monangai would miss four games, they likely would have put him on injured reserve, so he should, theoretically, be able to play in Week 8 against the Seahawks. Of course, nothing is guaranteed, and for those wondering, the Bears go on bye in Week 10. D’Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson have been splitting touches with Monangai sidelined. We do not yet know if Johnson will be punished for last week’s fumble though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roschon-jo.headline: Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) did not practice on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roschon-jo.analysis: He hasn’t practiced yet this week and appears very unlikely to go on Thursday night. It would seem to be trending towards another week with Roschon Johnson as the backup runner for the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roschon-jo.headline: Roschon Johnson had 13 rushes for 53 yards and a touchdown in the Bears’ Week 6 win against the Falcons, adding two catches for 34 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roschon-jo.analysis: Johnson has been highly efficient as the Bears’ No. 2 back over the past two games, with Kyle Monangai (toe/hand) sidelined. Johnson saw much of his opportunity in the second half with the Bears up big. Johnson slid down at the two yard line late in the fourth quarter to allow the Bears to run out the clock and secure the victory. In Chicago’s run-first offense, Johnson in Week 7 against the Patriots will be a deep league flex play if Monangai remains sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roschon-jo.headline: Bears ruled out Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) for Week 6 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roschon-jo.analysis: Bears coach Ben Johnson said Monangai is “trending in the right direction,” but remains week-to-week. D’Andre Swift should handle a sizable workload with Monangai sidelined. Roschon Johnson may be able to catch a few passes, but he makes for a shaky FLEX bet. Monangai should be stashed safely on fantasy football benches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roschon-jo.headline: Roschon Johnson rushed five times for six yards in the Bears’ Week 5 loss to the Packers, adding five receptions for 34 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roschon-jo.analysis: Filling in for Kyle Monangai (toe), Johnson helped close out a blowout loss. Pro Football Focus charted him as playing the final 13 snaps over D’Andre Swift, goosing his touch totals with No. 3 QB Case Keenum under center. Johnson would perhaps be worth a desperation PPR flier if Monangai remains sidelined for Week 6 against the Falcons and Caleb Williams (hamstring) returns, but “desperation” would be the operative word there.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roschon-jo.headline: D’Andre Swift (hip/knee) is not on Chicago’s final Week 5 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/roschon-jo.analysis: Despite an early-week DNP, Swift heads into the week in arguably a better position than he started it. We’re not sure how much workload he’ll handle with Kyle Monangai (foot) out, but it will certainly be a large majority of what the Bears do. Roschon Johnson figures to handle whatever Swift can’t, but isn’t a priority free agency pickup so much as a stash at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colton-mck.headline: 49ers placed RT Colton McKivitz on injured reserve with an ankle injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colton-mck.analysis: This is extremely unfortunate. The 49ers’ talented right tackle is expected to miss the rest of the season after fracturing and dislocating his ankle. The 49ers remain an elite team, but McKivitz’s loss will likely be felt on the field from time to time. The 49ers also activated CB Nate Hobbs from injured reserve and re-signed WR Brandin Cooks to the practice squad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colton-mck.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports 49ers RT Colton McKivitz will likely miss the remainder of the season after fracturing and dislocating his ankle in Week 11’s win over the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colton-mck.analysis: If you saw this injury during the game, you immediately knew this would likely be a season-ender. McKivitz’s left leg twisted unnaturally after a play in the second quarter, and the 30-year-old tackle was carted off the field shortly after. While we hope for the best, we fully expect the team to announce McKivitz’s season is over at some point this week. McKivitz was replaced by Vederian Lowe, who will presumably be the Niners’ starting right tackle moving forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colton-mck.headline: Colton McKivitz (leg) was carted to the locker room in the second quarter of Week 11 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colton-mck.analysis: McKivitz was rolled up on from behind and his leg did things it should not do, with the gruesome injury almost assuredly going to end his season. The veteran right tackle had become a staple for the 49ers before his injury, with the team now forced to shuffle things up front for the remainder of the season. Expect updates from the team in the coming days.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colton-mck.headline: 49ers signed RT Colton McKivitz to a three-year, $45 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colton-mck.analysis: McKivitz was in the final year of his deal and is now tied to the Niners through the 2028 season. The sixth-year tackle cemented himself as a starter in 2023 and has started all 35 regular-season games he’s appeared in since then. McKivitz allowed just two sacks on 36 pressures last season, turning in arguably the best year while earning a PFF blocking grade of 72.2. His solid performances and availability over the years make McKivitz an easy player to invest in for the foreseeable future, and should solidify the Niners’ right side of the line for three more years.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colton-mck.headline: 49ers RT Colton McKivitz (knee) did not practice Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colton-mck.analysis: McKivitz was limited in Thursday’s practice, meaning he’s moving in the wrong direction heading into the weekend. The 49ers could be without three starting linemen this week if McKivitz sits. Left tackle Trent Williams and left guard Aaron Banks are both injured as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colton-mck.headline: 49ers signed RT Colton McKivitz to a one-year, $7 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colton-mck.analysis: Drafted in 2020, McKivitz spent the first three years of his career as a backup. He took over the starting right tackle job in 2023 after Mike McGlinchey left in free agency. McKivitz was solid in his first year, grading out as Pro Football Focus’s No. 47 tackle. The 49ers inked McKivitz to a two-year deal last offseason and he will now remain with the team through 2025 if he plays out the remainder of his new contract.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colton-mck.headline: 49ers GM John Lynch said “We believe in Colton” when asked if not drafting a tackle could be interpreted as a vote of confidence for RT Colton McKivitz.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colton-mck.analysis: It was the clear message sent after the 49ers didn’t draft a tackle this offseason nor sign a big-name free agent to replace the departed Mike McGlinchey. McKivitz signed a two-year contract this offseason and looks likely to start at right tackle for the 49ers in 2023. “The spirit, as we call it, really started to show,” Lynch added. “And Colton is sneaky talented, as well. We like him a lot as a player.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colton-mck.headline: 49ers re-signed OT Colton McKivitz to a two-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colton-mck.analysis: A 2020 fifth-rounder, McKivitz has just 446 career snaps to his name, though a decent chunk of them came in 2022 at both tackle spots. He provides in-house insurance in the increasingly likely event that RT Mike McGlinchey departs in free agency.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colton-mck.headline: 49ers OT Colton McKivitz suffered an MCL sprain in the Week 4 game against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colton-mck.analysis: Down already the best tackle football has to offer in Trent Williams, the 49ers now lose his replacement. McKivitz will be sidelined multiple weeks with the injury. Coach Kyle Shanahan described McKivitz’s injury as something similar to Elijah Mitchell’s injury which sidelined him for two months. The 49ers third-string tackle, Jaylon Moore replaced McKivitz against the Rams and will be expected to do so going forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colton-mck.headline: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said OT Colton McKivitz (knee) has a sprained MCL.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colton-mck.analysis: McKivitz left Week 4’s Monday Night win over the Rams with the injury and could miss 6-8 weeks; he’s likely an IR candidate. McKivitz was already the replacement for Trent Williams (ankle), leaving the 49ers left tackle duties to 2021 fifth-rounder Jaylon Moore. With a limited offensive line and Jimmy Garoppolo in the pocket, expect more screens from the 49ers offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.headline: Colts coach Shane Steichen said Alec Pierce (Achilles) has not been ruled out for the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.analysis: This contradicts a report from Ian Rapoport saying that the Colts have decided to shut him down. Pierce suffered a partially torn Achilles in Week 2. He underwent offseason surgery to address his heel/Achilles issues, but apparently it didn’t work. Now Pierce says he’s still hopeful to return later this year. The Colts have already thrown in the towel on the year, trading several big names and cutting Daniel Jones outright. There’s no reason to have Pierce try to play through the issue, so we’re still skeptical that he gets on the field again this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Colts are shutting down Alec Pierce (heel) for the remainder of the 2026 season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.analysis: Pierce signed a four-year, $114 million contract in the offseason. He almost immediately underwent surgery and was expected to miss three months, though it took a bit longer than that. There was also a mix-up about whether or not he underwent a second PRP injection, which at-the-time GM Chris Ballard denied. He was sidelined for a bit longer than that but did play in Week 1. Pierce then re-injured his heel in Week 2, functionally ending his season. The team has now chosen to shut him down to avoid any chance of further complications. It sounds like he will be good to go for 2027. Pierce’s season ends with five catches for 72 scoreless yards. He will return to a rebuilding Colts roster that is unlikely to support his WR3 fantasy case next year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said he wasn’t sure if Alec Pierce (heel) will play again this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.analysis: Pierce, who signed a massive new deal with the Colts last offseason, has been on injured reserve since Week 3. The Colts have little reason to rush him back in another lost season. “We’ll see. Like I said last week, he’s still in that rehab process, and I’m not going to put a timetable on return,” Steichen said Wednesday when asked about Pierce’s availability. Steichen mentioned Deion Burks and Anthony Gould as receivers who will see more playing time after the Colts traded Josh Downs and Keenan Allen this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Alec Pierce (heel) won’t practice this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.analysis: Pierce, dealing with a heel injury since mid-September, will continue rehabbing and remain on injured reserve ahead of the Colts’ Week 7 game against the Vikings. Since Week 3, Keenan Allen leads the Colts with a 24 percent target share, while Josh Downs has 17 percent of the team’s targets and 26 percent of the team’s air yards. Neither wideout is a great option in Week 7 against a marauding Minnesota defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Colts WR Alec Pierce (heel) is still a few weeks away from a return to game action.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.analysis: No surprise here. Pierce shed his cast earlier this week, but there was also a report from the Athletic’s James Boyd that he “didn’t get the sense” Pierce was close to a return. Pelissero reports that Pierce isn’t expected to return to practice next week when he’s eligible. It’s difficult to justify holding Pierce in leagues without IR spots given the circumstances.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.headline: The Athletic’s James Boyd reports Alec Pierce (heel) is no longer wearing a cast but is not close to a return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.analysis: Boyd said he “didn’t get the sense” that Pierce is close to a return. Pierce went on injured reserve with a heel injury after Week 2 and wore a cast on his left ankle/heel while rehabbing. It’s a sign of progress for Pierce, who will have his first chance to come back in the Colts’ Week 7 game against the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.headline: Colts placed Alec Pierce (heel) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.analysis: Pierce will be sidelined for at least four weeks after suffering the injury in Week 2 against Kansas City. Pierce had seen 19 percent of the Colts’ targets and 53 percent of the team’s air yards in Week 1 against the Ravens, resuming his role as a strictly-downfield pass catcher. With Pierce out, Josh Downs should have every chance to operate as the Colts’ No. 1 wideout while Tyler Warren sees a bump in targets. Laquon Treadwell is likely to take over as the team’s lone deep threat. Treadwell can be picked up in 14-team fantasy formats ahead of the Colts’ Week 3 matchup with the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Colts WR Alec Pierce (heel) will “attempt to rehab his injury rather than have surgery.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.analysis: Pierce will most certainly be out for numerous games after appearing to re-injure the heel that he had offseason surgery on in Week 2. Rapoport’s wording seems to indicate that additional surgery has not yet been ruled out, but Pierce will attempt to rehab the issue in the interim. It’s a disaster of a scenario for a team that extended Pierce while allowing Michael Pittman to walk in the offseason. Josh Downs appears most likely to become the focal point of the offense through the air in Pierce’s absence after amassing seven catches on nine targets in the team’s overtime loss to the Chiefs. When, or if, Pierce returns to the active roster in 2026 remains to be seen.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Alec Pierce (heel) aggravated the injury that required surgery in March and the Colts are “still gathering information.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.analysis: X-rays came back negative last night but Pierce couldn’t put weight on it last night and left on crutches with a boot on. The fact that it was an aggravation is not promising. It sounds like Pierce could be looking at an extended absence. If true, Josh Downs will get some WR3 hype ahead of Week 3’s date against the Texans. If you were wondering why Laquon Treadwell was on the field deep in the game on Sunday night, Pierce’s injury is the reason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that Colts WR Alec Pierce’s (heel) X-rays were negative.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.analysis: Pierce evidently avoided suffering a fracture. He will undergo more testing tomorrow to determine the remaining specifics and the injury’s severity. Hopefully, the Colts’ field-stretching wide receiver is not sidelined for long, if at all. Pierce underwent surgery on his ankle/heel this offseason and spent almost the entire spring and summer rehabbing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caden-curr.headline: Colts DE Caden Curry (wrist) is out for the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caden-curr.analysis: Curry suffered the injury last week and will be sidelined for the rest of the season. His absence will be yet another blow for a crumbling Colts defense that has been bludgeoned over the past few weeks through the air and on the ground. Curry had 14 tackles and one tackle for loss over 11 games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caden-curr.headline: Colts selected Ohio State EDGE Caden Curry with the No. 214 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caden-curr.analysis: Curry (6’2/257) finally got a chance to start in 2025, and he made the most of that opportunity. He was a Third-team All-American and Second-team All-Big Ten Conference performer while leading the loaded Buckeyes’ defense with 16.5 tackles for loss and finishing in the top 10 in all of college football with 11 sacks. While the production was impressive, there are concerns about his overall athleticism and fluidity, and his ability to shed blockers is a work-in-progress, to put it mildly. Still, those numbers in one of -- if not the -- best conference in college football is tough to ignore, and it’s not hard to see Curry developing into at least a situational pass-rusher at the highest level.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caden-curr.headline: Ohio State has received a verbal commitment from 2022 four-star DL Caden Curry.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caden-curr.analysis: Curry (6'3/250) made his announcement on CBS Sports HQ, passing on offers from his home state Indiana Hoosiers, along with Alabama, Clemson and Oregon to join head coach Ryan Day at Ohio State. Curry is the 14th ranked defensive lineman in the nation according to 247Sports composite rankings, and the 88th ranked player nationally. This past season at Center Grove High School, Curry totaled 65 tackles including 24 tackles for a loss and seven sacks. He finished his career with 290 tackles for 83.5 tackles for a loss and 28 sacks to go with three pass breakups, three forced fumbles and three fumble recoveries.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe reports there have “not been a lot of talks about an extension in-season” for Bryce Young.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: Wolfe adds that Young and the Panthers are “on the same page for an offseason contract.” Young started out strong this season before a three-turnover loss to the Buccaneers in Week 7. The Panthers are still in first place atop the NFC South with a 5-5 record and a second bout with the Bucs on the horizon for Week 12. Young’s extension chances were highly reliant on his play this season but the Panthers need to see more before committing to the 25-year-old quarterback. With a 19-35 record and 67 passing touchdowns to 37 interceptions throughout his career thus far, Young’s performance the rest of this year will determine the status of a contract extension. If the Panthers choose to extend him, it will come in the offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Bryce Young completed 22-of-30 passes for 254 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the Panthers’ 35-33, Week 11 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: Young and the Panthers had a much-needed bounce-back performance in Sunday’s win over the Ravens. After struggling to move the ball in Week 10’s win over the Saints, Young and the Panthers overcame an early safety on their opening drive to string together a nice five-play, 79-yard drive in the first quarter that included a 35-yard completion to Jalen Coker, which was followed by a 23-yard touchdown pass to tight end Mitchell Evans. In the second quarter, Young connected with Tetairoa McMillan for a seven-yard touchdown pass in the end zone to put the Panthers up 22-19 after Chuba Hubbard ran in a two-point conversion. Young’s lone interception came on another end zone target to McMillan in the third quarter, but the mistake didn’t prove too costly, as the Ravens went three-and-out on the ensuing drive. Young took back-to-back sacks to start a drive in the fourth quarter after the Panthers’ defense forced a turnover of their own, spoiling a chance to go up by two possessions, but the Panthers’ defense held up its end of the bargain late when it forced an interception of Jacoby Brissett to end any hopes of a comeback attempt. With all 32 teams playing in Week 12, Young will be on the mid-to-high-end QB2 radar next week against the Buccaneers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Bryce Young (foot) is practicing in full for Week 11 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: Young has played through lower-body injuries for much of the season already. Late in October, coach Dave Canales admitted that Young’s knee issue may be limiting his mobility. While we fully expect Young to play this week, he may be a little less likely to scramble than he normally would. Regardless, it doesn’t alter his ranking much. Today, Canales said Young’s “foot was sore coming out of the game Sunday, but it’s been getting better and better.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Bryce Young completed 17-of-30 attempts for 200 yards in the Panthers’ Week 10 win against the Saints, adding one rush for one yard.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: It was one of Young’s worst performances of the season considering the middling competition. He posted a negative EPA per drop back and was 10 percent under his expected completion rate against New Orleans. His statistical day would have been a little less bleak if Darren Waller had been able to hang on to what would have been a 30-yard score in the first half. Young, who regular missed open wideouts in the intermediate areas, has struggled for most of the past month. Young will be a superflex option in Week 11 against the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Bryce Young completed 28-of-39 passes for 276 yards, three touchdowns and an interception in the Panthers’ 26-21, Week 9 loss to the Broncos, also losing a fumble.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: Young’s three-score start was his first since Week 2, though the two turnovers really put a damper on things. Young’s fourth quarter fumble short-circuited a potential game-winning drive, while his interception came in the end zone. Now, it was one of the more unlucky plays we have ever seen in the NFL — a ball seemingly everyone thought bounced off the ground actually bounced off a player into Devon Key’s arms — but Young put too much on the negative side of the ledger for the Panthers to pull this one out. They’ve now lost three straight games to fall to 3-5 on the season. Young at least snapped a streak of three straight starts with a sub-60 completion percentage. He also converted a late 4th-and-18 with an amazing throw. Young remains a frustrating option on the QB1/2 borderline heading into a golden Week 10 matchup with the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said Bryce Young (ankle) will play in Week 9 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: Young never really felt like he was at risk of missing this week. Despite dealing with an ankle injury, the Panthers’ QB1 was listed as a full participant in practice throughout the week and will be good to go despite what appears to be a minor ankle injury. Young draws a tough Week 9 matchup at home against the Broncos and has thrown two touchdowns and three interceptions in his last two games, and has completed below 60 percent of his passes in his last three outings. He’ll be a risky QB2 this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Bryce Young (ankle) is practicing in full for Week 9 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said after Week 8’s loss to the Packers that Young’s knee injury could be limiting his mobility. The team didn’t list the knee issue on this week’'s injury report, instead adding an ankle injury to the mix. It’s not something that will prevent Young from playing on Sunday, but another lingering ailment could further hamper his mobility. Already in the midst of a two-game slump, Young is back in the middle of the QB2 ranks for Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said Bryce Young’s knee injury may be limiting his mobility.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: Young declined to get into details about his knee injury after Thursday night’s loss to the Packers, saying, “Everyone’s dealing with something; it’s no excuse,” when speaking with the media after the game. Canales didn’t seem overly concerned about Young’s injury after the game, but did acknowledge that he didn’t appear to have the “quick, make you miss” aspect to his game against the Packers. Young was listed on the Panthers’ injury report throughout the week, but was also a full participant in practice. Young’s knee could be partly to blame for the six sacks he took in Thursday’s loss, and his health will be one to monitor in the weeks ahead, especially with the team already past its Week 5 bye. Assuming he’s good to go in Week 9, Young will face an uphill battle against a stout Broncos defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Bryce Young completed 23-of-41 passes for 209 yards with a touchdown and an interception in the Panthers’ 27-19, Week 8 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: Those who believe that sacks are a quarterback stat might change their mind watching the Panthers block Thursday night. The 25-year-old had no time to throw and couldn’t get out of the pocket while taking six sacks and being pressured on what seemed like every throw. That’s not to say that Young was completely a victim of his circumstance; he struggled with accuracy and couldn’t get the ball downfield in another ugly performance for the 25-year-old sans a 26-yard passing score to Jalen Coker in the middle of the fourth. Things won’t get any easier on paper in Week 9, as Young and the Panthers face the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Panthers listed Bryce Young (knee) as a full participant on Monday’s estimated injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: Young was listed with the same knee injury last Friday but remained a full participant and was good to go in Week 7. Whatever issue he’s dealing with appears minor, especially if the team is still listing him as a full participant. At this point, there’s no reason to think he won’t be active for Week 8’s game against the Packers on Thursday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alex-highs.headline: Alex Highsmith (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alex-highs.analysis: Highsmith suffered an ankle injury in Week 11 and starts out the week not practicing. He was wearing an ankle brace in the team facility on Tuesday and head coach Mike McCarthy said it will be “tough” for Highsmith to play in a shortened Week 12 where the Steelers play the Broncos on Friday. Highsmith is trending in the wrong direction this week, but his ankle issue does not seem to be a major injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alex-highs.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport believes that the Steelers are likely to keep EDGE T.J. Watt and EDGE Alex Highsmith on the roster for 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alex-highs.analysis: Watt, 31, and Highsmith, 28, were the starting EDGE rushers last year. Their 24-year-old backup, LB Nick Herbig, signed a four-year, $100 million extension on Tuesday, prompting questions as to whether the Steelers could consider trading away one of their two veterans. Highsmith was not present at mandatory minicamp on Wednesday, but this was reportedly due to a stomach bug , not discontent over his backup’s big payday. Per Rapoport, Watt’s “enormous” contract, coupled with the amount of money the Steelers have invested elsewhere in their EDGE unit, means that they will probably “have a decision to make” in 2027.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alex-highs.headline: Steelers EDGE Alex Highsmith (pectoral) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 13 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alex-highs.analysis: Highsmith has not played since Week 10. Getting him back provides the Steelers’ pass rush with a big boost. The Steelers will also have CB Joey Porter Jr. (hip) on the field when they take on the Bills this weekend. Both Highsmith and Porter practiced full on Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alex-highs.headline: Steelers EDGE Alex Highsmith (pectoral) is doubtful to play in Week 12 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alex-highs.analysis: Highsmith sat out on Wednesday before getting in two limited sessions. The difference-making EDGE rusher boasts a 16.6 percent pass-rush win rate, 19 quarterback pressures and six sacks. Bears QB Caleb Williams should have a far easier time staying upright and comfortable in the pocket with Highsmith expectedly sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alex-highs.headline: Steelers EDGE Alex Highsmith (pectoral) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alex-highs.analysis: It’s the first practice he’s played in since injuring the pectoral in Week 10. It’s possible Highsmith will be out there against the Bears in Week 12, though we’d still bet on him hitting the questionable line at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alex-highs.headline: Steelers EDGE Alex Highsmith (pectoral) will not play in Pittsburgh’s Week 11 game against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alex-highs.analysis: Also ruled out on Pittsburgh’s defense are CB Darius Slay (concussion) and LB Cole Holcomb (illness), Highsmith had said he was optimistic about playing but the Steelers opted to hold their pass rusher out. These rule-outs are good news for Cincinnati’s offense in what projects to be a shootout on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alex-highs.headline: Steelers EDGE Alex Highsmith (pectoral) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alex-highs.analysis: He’s missed back-to-back practices, but told reporters he was optimistic about Friday. Highsmith always seems to be fighting through something, but he has played each of the last five weeks and should be considered questionable for this one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alex-highs.headline: Steelers EDGE Alex Highsmith (ankle) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 10 against the Chargers
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alex-highs.analysis: The Steelers will have their EDGE defender on the field in this one. Highsmith has totaled 15 quarterback pressures, four sacks and 16 tackles this year, while the Steelers attempt to restore their defense’s reputation. Doing so against the Chargers is no small feat, and should perhaps be viewed as unlikely to happen.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alex-highs.headline: Steelers EDGE Alex Highsmith (ankle) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alex-highs.analysis: Highsmith is now on track to play in Week 10 against the Chargers. The veteran pass rusher accounts for 15 quarterback pressures, four sacks and 16 tackles this season. The Steelers field a generally fantasy-friendly defense, though having Highsmith active is obviously a plus. His Friday participation level should clarify things.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alex-highs.headline: Steelers EDGE Alex Highsmith (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alex-highs.analysis: Highsmith missed two games earlier this year because of an ankle issue. It’s unclear if this is related or something new. Either way, his odds of playing in Week 10 are 50/50 at best right now. With Pittsburgh’s defense already struggling this year, the last thing they needed was to lose one of their best pass-rushers. Highsmith has 3.5 sacks and a forced fumble in six games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Benford (groin) was limited in Tuesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: It’s his first practice since suffering the groin injury in Week 10. We had a feeling the Bills would do all they could to have the full roster ready for the Chiefs and it appears Benford will indeed have a chance to suit up.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Bills coach Joe Brady said Christian Benford (groin) will not play in Buffalo’s Week 11 game against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Neither will Dorian Williams (calf) who also missed practice most of the week. Neither player is regarded as having a long-term injury, per Brady, so they should have a chance to get up for Week 12’s Thanksgiving game against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Benford (groin) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Benford and Bills LB Dorian Williams (calf) remained sidelined today. Bills slot CB Dee Alford (concussion) resumed practicing in a limited capacity, but he is still firmly in the questionable camp. The Bills can probably sneak past the Dolphins if a few of their defenders are absent, but having them on the field is obviously ideal.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Benford (groin) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Benford is the Bills’ No. 1 perimeter cornerback. Bills slot CB Dee Alford (concussion) and LB Dorian Williams (calf) were also sidelined to begin Week 11. The Bills face the Dolphins this weekend. Bills C Connor McGovern (neck) is practicing in full.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Benford has been ruled out for the remainder of Week 10 with a groin injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Benford was questionable to play in Week 10 with a wrist injury but was cleared to go. He then injured his groin in the fourth quarter and will not return to the game. The Bills are set to face the Dolphins in Week 11 before facing the Chiefs the following week, so there is a chance that they hold their top cornerback out for next week. We’ll have to see if he is able to practice at all during the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Benford (wrist) is active for Week 10 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Benford was questionable due to a wrist injury suffered in last week’s game against the Vikings. With Jordan Hancock also coming off the injured list, the Bills have a fully healthy secondary, including the addition of safety Amani Hooker. The Bills declared QB Shane Buechele, OT Jude Bowry, OL Ar’maj Reed-Adams, DL Greg Gaines, OLB Mike Danna, and S Jalon Kilgore inactive.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Dion Dawkins (ribs) is not on the Bills’ final injury report for Week 10 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Dawkins and LG Alec Anderson (ankle) are both good to go this weekend. Bills RT Spencer Brown (ankle) is unfortunately doubtful to play. Overall, the Bills’ offensive line health is trending in the right direction, though. Bills CB Christian Benford (wrist) is questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Benford (toe) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Benford has a chance to return for his team’s Monday Night Football game against the Rams. That said, his play declined last year, and it hasn’t exactly rebounded. If active, Benford should not dissuade anyone from treating the Rams’ wide receivers as they normally would.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Bills declared CB Christian Benford, WR Skyler Bell, OL Jude Bowry, OL Ar’maj Reed-Adams, DL T.J. Sanders, OLB Mike Danna, and S Jalon Kilgore inactive for Week 4 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: No real surprises here. Benford was listed as questionable heading into the day, but he didn’t practice at all this week so he was never likely to play. Rookie Davison Igbinosun is likely to step into his spot opposite Maxwell Hairston, which makes the Bills young and inexperienced on the boundary. Perhaps Drake Maye could finally take advantage of that on the way to his first truly good fantasy game of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Bills coach Joe Brady said CB Christian Benford (toe) is questionable for Buffalo’s Week 4 game against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Despite the questionable listing, Benford did not appear in the media portion of practice on Friday. At best, he’ll be listed as limited later today. Benford seems to be on the pessimistic side of questionable for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-yiad.headline: Bears claimed CB Isaac Yiadom off waivers from the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-yiad.analysis: Yiadom has been a decent depth corner for most of the last half-decade, but only played on special teams with the Commanders this year. Perhaps the Bears see more in him, or perhaps they just need a gunner.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-yiad.headline: Commanders declared QB Athan Kaliakmanis, CB Isaac Yiadom, DT Ricky Barber, G Tanoa Togiai, C Lucas Patrick and TE Colson Yankoff inactive for Week 10 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-yiad.analysis: Among the Commanders’ players who are currently healthy enough to practice, most of them will play. Treylon Burks (foot) could end up being a decoy, but Chig Okonkwo (hip) should be good to go. Only Yiadom and a few others are unable to go on Thursday night, though tonight’s kickoff could be delayed by weather.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-yiad.headline: Commanders waived DT Ricky Barber.
