https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-yiad.analysis: The second-year player is headed to waivers. The Commanders correspondingly promoted CB Isaac Yiadom to the active roster. Barber could be re-signed to the practice squad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-yiad.headline: Saints CB Isaac Yiadom (hamstring) is active for Week 8 against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-yiad.analysis: Yiadom has been sidelined since straining his hamstring in Week 4. Although the Buccaneers are without WRs Mike Evans (collarbone/concussion) and Chris Godwin (fibula), their deep receiving corps, led by rookies WR Emeka Egbuka and WR Tez Johnson, still poses problems for defenses. Yiadom’s return is helpful. The Saints declared OG Xavier Truss, TE Zaire Mitchell-Paden, DB Ugo Amadi, CB Rejzohn Wright, DL Jonah Williams and DT Khristian Boyd inactive for Week 8 against the Buccaneers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-yiad.headline: Saints signed CB Isaac Yiadom, formerly of the 49ers, to a three-year, $9 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-yiad.analysis: Yiadom returns to the Saints, who he played for in 2022 and 2023. The 29-year-old corner joined the 49ers on a one-year deal last offseason and appeared in all 17 games while making five starts. In those games, Yiadom totaled 46 tackles and one interception while also breaking up six passes and earning a PFF coverage grade of 55.3. One of Yiadom’s best seasons as a pro came in 2023 while with the Saints, where he broke up a career-high 13 passes. His signing doesn’t fully address the secondary problems the Saints had last season, but he’s a good depth signing who should be able to provide them plenty of snaps at a good value.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-yiad.headline: 49ers agreed to terms with CB Isaac Yiadom, formerly of the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-yiad.analysis: The 49ers will become Yiadom’s fifth team over the last five years, as the former third round pick has also spent time with the Texans, Packers, and Giants. Yiadom played on 517 defensive snaps last season, earning a PFF coverage grade of 80.4 while allowing 22 catches for 289 yards and three touchdowns on 44 targets. The veteran corner has started in 28 of the 87 games he’s appeared in for his career, and is likely more of a depth signing at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-yiad.headline: Texans declared TE Pharaoh Brown (shoulder) inactive for Week 4 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-yiad.analysis: Houston will only have O.J. Howard and Jordan Akins (an elevation) active at tight end with TE Brevin Jordan (ankle) also ruled out on Friday. WR Tyler Johnson is active for the first time this season. Also inactive for the Texans are OL Austin Deculus (ankle), CB Isaac Yiadom (thigh), LB Jake Hansen, DL Michael Dwumfour, and DL Demone Harris.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-yiad.headline: Texans TE Pharaoh Brown (shoulder) is active for Week 3 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-yiad.analysis: Brown going may cut into the viability of OJ Howard as a barebones TE streamer this week -- Brown bounced back from a Thursday DNP with a full practice on Friday. Both will have some freed up targets by the absence of Brevin Jordan (ankle), who was ruled out on Friday. Also inactive for the Texans are DL Kurt Hinish (foot), OL Austin Deculus (ankle), DB Isaac Yiadom (thigh), LB Jake Hansen, and WR Tyler Johnson. No practice squad elevation for Jeff Driskel means the Texans will actually use backup QB Kyle Allen for the first time all season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-yiad.headline: Texans signed CB Isaac Yiadom to an undisclosed contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-yiad.analysis: Yiadom spent last year as a Packers depth cornerback and didn’t impress. He’s yet to post a PFF Grade over 57 in any of his four seasons and allowed six touchdowns in 42 targets in 2020 per Sports Info Solutions charting. Nobody should ever be confident of where things stand with the Texans, but Yiadom is likely just fighting for a roster spot as a special teamer/depth player.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-yiad.headline: Pro Football Network’s Aaron Wilson reports that the Texans are working out free agent CB Isaac Yiadom.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-yiad.analysis: It appears to be cornerback workout day for the Texans with Malcolm Butler also in town. Yiadom played fewer than 100 defensive snaps last year for the Packers. He’s got outside cornerback traits, but has not been able to convert them into good results to this point. He’s still only 26 years old.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.headline: Broncos coach Sean Payton said he suspended J.K. Dobbins one game for conduct detrimental to the team.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.analysis: For those of you who haven’t had the pleasure of rostering Dobbins anywhere, know that he played just one snap on Sunday. Whatever went down almost certainly has something to do with that low snap count, though Payton wouldn’t get into it publicly with reporters. If Dobbins could agitate enough to get released, maybe we’d get somewhere in fantasy circles, but as it stands there’s no reason to hold him in shallow leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.headline: J.K. Dobbins rushed one time for zero yards in the Broncos’ Week 11 win over the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.analysis: Jonah Coleman completed his takeover of the backfield today with 24 carries, four catches, and three touchdowns. Dobbins, meanwhile, saw as many carries as Cody Schrader. Dobbins’ carry total has gone from seven to four to one in his past three appearances. Sean Payton has decided that this is Coleman’s backfield and there’s not much Dobbins can do about it. Fantasy managers can cut ties with him on the next run of waivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.headline: J.K. Dobbins rushed four times for 18 yards in the Broncos’ Week 9 win over the Panthers, adding a four-yard reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.analysis: Dobbins operated as a pure breather back for this one, getting out-touched 21-5 by Jonah Coleman and out-snapped 58-11. Dobbins did receive two touches inside the Panthers’ 20-yard line — one of which was nullified by penalty — but none inside the 10. It sure looks as if the Broncos are ready to ride rookie Coleman, making Dobbins a shaky 12-team league hold since the Broncos are now headed on bye. They return in Week 11 against the Raiders. The odds are strong Dobbins will not be in your starting lineup for that one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.headline: J.K. Dobbins rushed seven times for 13 yards in the Broncos’ Week 8 win over the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.analysis: Dobbins got the Bronocs’ first touch on offense and immediately took a backseat to Jonah Coleman. The rookie tallied 11 carries and five targets. He also became the first Bronocs running back to hit 100 yards from scrimmage in a game this year. Dobbins was not targeted and was not on the field at the goal line, where Coleman was heavily involved. Coleman ultimately punched in a goal line touchdown for the game-winning score after setting himself up with a 51-yard catch. The short-yardage role used to belong to Dobbins, but the rookie appears to have taken that as well. Without any high-value touches to work with, Dobbins is a between-the-20s grinder averaging a little over three yards per carry this season. He is falling back into the RB4 ranks for his Week 9 date with the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.headline: J.K. Dobbins rushed six times for 23 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 7 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.analysis: Dobbins was the team’s preferred option at the goal line, allowing him to save a bust of a fantasy day with a one-yard score in the second half. He was initially stood up at the goal line but made it in the paint by driving his legs through the contact for six. Dobbins was held under 10 points even with the touchdown. Jonah Coleman returned this week and led the team in carries with nine. Harvey ran the ball just three times. This backfield is a messy, three-man committee and Dobbins doesn’t get to pad the stats with PPR-friendly targets. He will shuffle to the back of the RB3 ranks for his Week 8 date with the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.headline: Broncos designated Jonah Coleman (ankle) to return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.analysis: Coleman can return to practice this week and the team now has 21 days to bring him off injured reserve. He could be back on the field as soon as Sunday. With the Broncos’ offense struggling and two backs already seeing work in the backfield, it’s hard to imagine Coleman having much fantasy value in his first game back. He’s worth stashing in deeper leagues, but it might be a while before fantasy managers want him in their lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.headline: J.K. Dobbins rushed 17 times for 41 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 6 win over the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.analysis: Dobbins found little room to run on a night the Broncos gained only 168 yards of total offense but handily led the backfield in opportunities in what was a consistently positive game script due to the dominance of their defense. Dobbins has now failed to eclipse a modest 50 yards on the ground in four of five appearances but might be useful as a bye week fill-in when the Broncos travel to Arizona to face the Cardinals in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.headline: J.K. Dobbins rushed 18 times for 68 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 5 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.analysis: Dobbins was the most effective offensive player for both teams, which isn’t quite the compliment you’d think it is. The 27-year-old was the bellcow for the Broncos, however, and he was able to keep the chains moving enough to give Denver the victory over the winless Chargers. Dobbins will likely find the sledding tougher in Week 6 when the Broncos face the Seahawks on Thursday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.headline: JK Dobbins had 11 rushes for 40 yards in the Broncos’ Week 4 loss to the 49ers, adding two catches for 12 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.analysis: Dobbins, as usual, led the Denver backfield in carries but lost out to RJ Harvey on pass routes and targets. In fact, Harvey led the Broncos with ten catches on ten targets in a check-down heavy game plan for Bo Nix and OC Davis Webb. Dobbins has been touchdown-reliant as the Broncos’ lead back, and sensitive to game script, as we saw in Week 4. Dobbins can be used as a flex next week against a vulnerable Chargers run defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.headline: J.K. Dobbins (hip) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 4 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.analysis: Dobbins practiced in full this week, so he should be ready to handle his typical workload against the 49ers this week. The Broncos’ lead rusher has played very unproductively this season, failing to hit 7.0 PPR points each week. The Broncos’ defensive line has been hit hard by injuries. Perhaps Dobbins can steady himself in the RB2/FLEX ranks against them.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shane-buec.headline: Colts signed QB Shane Buechele off the Bills’ practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shane-buec.analysis: Buechele got his first NFL experience last year in Week 18, at age 27, when he completed 7-of-14 passes for 88 yards in a game the Chiefs were (probably) looking to lose against the Raiders. He was sacked five times. These last six Colts games will feel like they take five months.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shane-buec.headline: Bills released QB Shane Buechele.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shane-buec.analysis: The news was first reported by ESPN’s Adam Schefter. Buechele, 28, has been a backup for years, spending time with the Chiefs and Bills. He was beat out by Kyle Allen, who will serve as the Bills’ QB2 this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shane-buec.headline: Bills signed QB Shane Buechele to a reserve-future contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shane-buec.analysis: Buechele, 28, has spent his NFL career bouncing between the Chiefs and Bills quarterback rooms, now returning to Buffalo for the offseason. The Bills also signed WR Jalen Virgil to a reserve-future deal; he spent the 2024 season with the team. Familiar faces return to Buffalo with reserve-future deals at the start of the offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shane-buec.headline: Chiefs waived QB Shane Buechele.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shane-buec.analysis: Buechele was signed off the Bills practice squad ahead of Week 18 and completed 7-of-14 passes for 88 yards against the Raiders in a game that neither team seemed to want to win. His reward was being waived. The Chiefs also signed LB Kam Arnold, DT Marcus Harris, WR Jimmy Holiday and T Matt Waletzko to reserve/future deals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shane-buec.headline: Chiefs QB Chris Oladokun completed 11-of-17 passes for 58 yards in Kansas City’s Week 18 game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shane-buec.analysis: Oladokun was lost throughout the first half, even in a clean pocket. He was sacked three times against a Raiders defense that ranks among the league’s worst against the pass and didn’t even have Maxx Crosby. Oladokun will revert to practice squad status for 2025 if he remains in Kansas City.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shane-buec.headline: Bills signed S Jordan Poyer to their practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shane-buec.analysis: Poyer made first-team All-Pro in 2021 and went to the Pro Bowl in 2022 while playing with the Bills. The 34-year-old safety spent 2024 with the Dolphins, where he started 16 games and had 98 tackles. The Bills already have Cole Bishop and Taylor Rapp as starting safeties, though Bishop has had a shaky training camp and preseason. The Bills also signed to their practice squad QB Shane Buechele, RB Frank Gore Jr., WR Stephen Gosnell, WR Kristian Wilkerson, TE Keleki Latu, OL Travis Clayton, OL Dan Feeney, OL Kendrick Green, DT Zion Logue, DT Jordan Phillips, LB Jimmy Ciarlo, LB Keonta Jenkins, CB Daequan Hardy, CB Dane Jackson and S Sam Franklin.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shane-buec.headline: Bills waived QB Shane Buechele.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shane-buec.analysis: Buechele is a strong candidate to end up on the Bills’ practice squad. He’s the second quarterback Buffalo has dropped Tuesday, as they also waived Mike White.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shane-buec.headline: Bills signed QB Ben DiNucci, formerly of the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shane-buec.analysis: DiNucci spent last season on the Broncos practice squad and hasn’t played a regular-season snap since 2020. The veteran backup joins a Bills team that lost Shane Buechele to a neck injury in their first preseason game and will likely see some snaps in the team’s upcoming preseason game against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shane-buec.headline: Chiefs waived RB Deneric Prince.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shane-buec.analysis: Prince ran and jumped his way into the hearts of fantasy managers earlier this offseason, only to fade away in camp/the preseason. The former Tulsa running back faced an uphill battle to crack a running back room that features Isiah Pacheco, Clyde Edwards-Helaire, and Jerick McKinnon and is now on the outside looking in. There’s a chance Prince clears waivers and ends up back on the Chiefs’ practice squad in the coming days. In addition to Prince, the Chiefs also released/waived DE Joshua Kaindoh, DT Phil Hoskins, S Deon Bush, DT Danny Shelton, CB Reese Taylor, CB Ekow Boye-Doe, LB Cole Christiansen, S Anthony Cook, QB Shane Buechele, QB Chris Oladokun, OL Sebastian Gutierrez, DT Daniel Wise, CB Kahlef Hailassie, RB La’Michal Perine, C Austin Reiter, and TE Kendall Blanton.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shane-buec.headline: Chiefs signed Southern Methodist QB Shane Buechele.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shane-buec.analysis: Chiefs gave Buechele (6'0/210) a $15,000 signing bonus and $160,000 guaranteed in base salary as multiple teams scrapped for his services the moment the draft ended. He was initially run out of Texas by Colts QB Sam Ehlinger but proved to be plenty capable as a passer at SMU, tossing a whopping 57 touchdown passes over those two seasons. Though his arm strength is uninspiring, Buechele has a knack for moving in and out of the pocket, as well as finding some interesting throws from uncomfortable platforms. Somewhere along the Austin Davis to Case Keenum spectrum is a fair expectation for him in the league as he learns behind Patrick Mahomes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Ravens waived WR LaJohntay Wester.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Wester muffed two punts last week against the Panthers, which we’re told is “not a good way to keep your roster spot” when you are here to be the returner. The Ravens will shuffle the deck here.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Ravens selected Colorado WR Lajohntay Wester with the No. 203 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Operating as the No. 2 wideout to Travis Hunter, Wester (5’10/163) totaled 74 receptions for 931 yards and 10 touchdowns for Colorado last season, adding a 76-yard punt return for a touchdown. He began his college career with four seasons at Florida Atlantic and made an impact as a returner, receiver, and occasional rusher. Wester has a small frame, but is impactful with the ball in his hands. As a slot receiver, he is elusive and can be used as a gadget piece on offense. He is a limited pass-catcher and lacks the strength to break tackles while a chunk of his college production was manufactured touches close to the line of scrimmage. Wester has the tools to be a returner and gadget receiver at the NFL level.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: FAU freshman WR LaJohntay Wester posted four grabs for a team-high 62 yards and a touchdown in Saturday’s 28-25 win against UTEP.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Wester (5'11/163) rolled up some big-time stat lines early in the season, going over 100 yards with a touchdown in wins over Georgia Southern and FCS Fordham. This line might be more impressive, however, as it came against a conference foe which will be bowl bound this season. Wester has four or more receptions in five of his eight games in 2021. FAU is back in action next Saturday at home against Marshall.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-avil.headline: Steve Avila (hamstring) will not play in Los Angeles’ Week 12 game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-avil.analysis: Avila did not play in Week 10 and did not practice at all this week coming out of a Week 11 bye. Perhaps the extra rest after this one will get him to a workable place in Week 13. Beaux Limmer started at guard in his place against the Cardinals in Week 10, but with Coleman Shelton (hamstring) also ruled out at center it’s possible that Limmer starts there instead. Bill Murray is the only other interior lineman on the 53-man roster currently, and it’s going to be almost Thanksgiving, not Groundhog Day.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-avil.headline: Trent McDuffie (back) is questionable for Week 10 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-avil.analysis: The Rams were optimistic about McDuffie practicing on Thursday and playing on Sunday. The former did not happen. It sounds like he has a chance to play this weekend, but his recovery appears to be going slightly slower than expected. Rams S Kam Curl (toe) is also questionable to play, though LG Steve Avila (hamstring) has been ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-avil.headline: Trent McDuffie (back) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-avil.analysis: Earlier today, we were told that McDuffie would resume practicing today. It turns out that report was wrong. McDuffie is on the wrong side of questionable. Myles Garrett (knee) was limited. Steve Avila (hamstring) and Kam Curl (toe) did not practice.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-avil.headline: Steve Avila (hamstring) did not practice in Wednesday’s walk-through.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-avil.analysis: Avila aggravated a hamstring injury and starts out the week not practicing. Rams head coach Sean McVay said Monday that Avila will miss some time, but may not go on injured reserve as the Rams are out of return slots. Expect Avila to miss Week 10 against the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-avil.headline: Rams declared OLB Nick Hampton, QB Stetson Bennett, TE Terrance Ferguson, OT DJ Humphries and LG Steve Avila active for Week 3’s game against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-avil.analysis: Ferguson is inactive with the Rams getting Parkinson back from a shoulder injury. Braden Fiske is also active after being considered questionable with an oblique issue.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-avil.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said OL Steve Avila (ankle) is doubtful for Week 3’s game against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-avil.analysis: It’ll likely be Justin Decich at guard for the Rams again on Sunday against Jalen Carter and company. McVay added that Colby Parkinson (ankle) is questionable for the contest. No Rams tight ends currently qualify as major fantasy plays.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-avil.headline: Eagles DT Jalen Carter (shoulder) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-avil.analysis: The Rams’ offensive line health is improving but LG Steve Avila remains sidelined by an ankle injury. His absence could be costly with Carter’s health improving. The Week 3 matchup between the Eagles and Rams might be a pass-heavy affair, which would bode positively for Carter’s sack productivity.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-avil.headline: Rams LG Steve Avila (ankle) and TE Colby Parkinson (shoulder) are doubtful for Week 2’s game against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-avil.analysis: The Rams will get one of their guards back after Kevin Dotson (also ankle) was cleared off the injury report for Week 2. Beaux Limmer figures to get Avila’s snaps at guard. Parkinson’s absence doesn’t majorly impact the Rams passing tree since it mostly condensed into Davante Adams and Puka Nacua in Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-avil.headline: Rams OL Rob Havenstein (ankle) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-avil.analysis: Havenstein sat out Wednesday’s practice, so his return is a great sign. The Rams also got back OL Kevin Dotson (ankle), who likewise practiced in a limited capacity. Fellow OL Steve Avila (ankle) remained sidelined. The Rams’ offensive line is banged up, but the unit is at least on the upswing, which bodes positively for Matthew Stafford’s ability to stay upright against the Titans in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-avil.headline: Rams OL Kevin Dotson, Rob Havenstein, and Steve Avila did not participate in Wednesday’s practice due to ankle injuries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-avil.analysis: Dotson, Havenstein, and Avila all popped up on the injury report with ankle issues to start Week 2. Head coach Sean McVay had said Dotson and Avila are week-to-week with their ankle injuries, but Havenstein’s status remains up in the air. Matthew Stafford’s protection will look slim should any or all of these three miss time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wanya-morr.headline: Colts signed OL Wanya Morris off the Cowboys’ practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wanya-morr.analysis: Jalen Travis and Bernhard Raimann are both dealing with injuries, and other names on the Colts 53-man roster at tackle include Luke Tenuta, Charlie Heck, and Matt Goncalves (a guard last year) as they try to see out the end of this disastrous season. Morris will attempt to see it with them.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wanya-morr.headline: Cowboys signed OT Wanya Morris, formerly of the Falcons, to their practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wanya-morr.analysis: Morris started several games for the Chiefs at left tackle over the past three seasons before the Falcons acquired him in the offseason. Atlanta chose to part ways and now the Cowboys add Morris as tackle depth heading into the season. Also signed to the Cowboys’ initial practice squad are RB Israel Abanikanda, WR Jordan Hudson, WR Anthony Smith, TE Michael Trigg, TE Mitchell Van Vooren, OT Marcellus Johnson, OL Nick Leverett, DT Tommy Dunn, DT Elijah Garcia, DT Adedayo Odeleye, LB Justin Barron, LB Isaiah Land, LB Curtis Robinson, CB Derion Kendrick, and CB Reddy Steward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wanya-morr.headline: Falcons waived OT Wanya Morris.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wanya-morr.analysis: Morris was in the final year of his rookie deal and came over in a June trade from the Chiefs. Apparently the Falcons weren’t enamored with what they saw in training camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wanya-morr.headline: Falcons acquired OT Wanya Morris and a 2027 seventh-round pick from the Chiefs in exchange for a 2027 sixth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wanya-morr.analysis: Two days ago, ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reported that the Chiefs and Morris had agreed to explore trade options because Morris wanted the chance to play more often. The 25-year-old, former third-round pick has logged 1,059 career snaps at left tackle and 88 at right tackle, though he has yet to stand out in pass protection. Despite his struggles, Morris provides at least mild insurance behind 34-year-old LT Jake Matthews.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wanya-morr.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the Chiefs and OT Wanya Morris have agreed to explore trade options.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wanya-morr.analysis: Per Fowler, Morris “would like the chance to play more and Kansas City has tackle depth.” Morris has 16 starts in three seasons and suffered a season-ending knee injury in December. An update on his rehab program was not provided. Morris earned a 57.1 PFF offense grade on 68 snaps last season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wanya-morr.headline: Chiefs OT Wanya Morris suffered a season-ending knee injury in Week 14’s loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wanya-morr.analysis: Morris suffered a gruesome knee injury early in the first quarter of Sunday’s game against the Texans and was ruled out shortly after. The third-year tackle was replaced by rookie UDFA Esa Pole, who allowed three pressures on 42 pass-blocking snaps against one of the top pass-rushing defenses in the league. It’s yet another massive blow to a Chiefs offensive line that was already missing its two starting tackles prior to Morris going down. Pole will likely draw the start in Week 15’s game against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wanya-morr.headline: Chiefs declared OT Wanya Morris inactive for Super Bowl LIX against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wanya-morr.analysis: The Chiefs enter Super Bowl LIX largely in good health. Morris struggled all season before being replaced in the starting lineup by D.J. Humphries and, later, guard Joe Thuney. The Chiefs also declared OL C.J. Hanson, OT Ethan Driskell, DE Malik Herring, DE Joshua Uche, CB Steven Nelson and CB Keith Taylor inactive.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wanya-morr.headline: Chiefs LT Wanya Morris (knee) left Kansas City’s Week 10 game versus the Broncos and is questionable to return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wanya-morr.analysis: He was struggling to put weight on his leg after he was rolled up on from behind, and reportedly had his hands on his helmet on the sideline before heading in to the locker room. Morris was replaced by Kingsley Suamataia, who is already struggling.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wanya-morr.headline: Chiefs backup T Wanya Morris exited preseason Week 3 against the Bears with a knee injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wanya-morr.analysis: Morris currently sits behind second-round rookie LT Kingsley Suamataia on the Chiefs’ depth chart. Though he ideally would play limited snaps, assuming a strong Week 1 debut for Suamataia, potentially losing depth at the offensive line’s most important position is an issue. Hopefully, the broadcast offers clarity as to the injury’s severity.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wanya-morr.headline: Chiefs OT Wanya Morris was arrested on Thursday and charged with misdemeanor marijuana possession in Johnson County, Kansas.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wanya-morr.analysis: Teammate Jason Godrick was also arrested with Morris, as the two were reportedly booked at the Johnson County Adult Detention Center around 2 A.M. Friday morning. Both players have since posted bond and were released, with their court appearances scheduled for May 23. It continues to be a rough offseason for the defending Super Bowl champions, who are dealing with the legal issues Rashee Rice has found himself in, and controversial comments recently made by kicker Harrison Butker. Morris is expected to compete with rookie Kingsley Suamataia for the starting left tackle job this offseason. Both players could be subject to discipline from the NFL depending on how the rest of this shakes out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh, asked about feeding Omarion Hampton more, said “in hindsight, we should have done that sooner.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: Many cases of fantasy managers who drafted Hampton in the first two rounds this past August nodding fervently at this news have been reported. Hampton had 15 touches last week and 23 against the Ravens in Week 10. With Justin Herbert (concussion protocol) uncertain for Week 12, it looks like Hampton will be a major part of the game plan yet again against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Omarion Hampton rushed 14 times for 89 yards in the Chargers’ Week 11 loss to the Jets, adding one reception for four yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: Hampton ripped off a 30-plus-yard run for the second time in three weeks today, averaging 6.4 yards per carry. He is the Chargers’ best runner, but frequent losing game scripts make his rushing workloads somewhat unreliable. The Chargers called an option run play for Justin Herbert in the red zone late in the game, with Hampton running a couple yards away from him, but Jets defenders recognized it and shut the play down, erasing Hampton’s potential opportunity to catch a pitch and run it in. Keaton Mitchell suffered back and knee injuries and departed early. Justin Herbert entered the NFL’s concussion protocol after the game. Hampton could warrant RB2 treatment against the Patriots next week, but both injuries will impact his projection.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said Omarion Hampton has reestablished himself as the team’s lead running back.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: The Athletic’s Noah Furtado asked Harbaugh why it took Hampton so long to reestablish himself as the team’s top running back. Harbaugh said, “he’s there (now). He’s showing it, proving it. And that’s all. That’s what’s important to me.” Hampton totaled 22 carries and one catch in Week 10. It sounds like he has a chance to continue handling a high-volume workload in the coming weeks, though the game script could hurt him if he fails to increase his passing game usage.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Omarion Hampton rushed 22 times for 105 yards and a touchdown in the Chargers’ Week 10 win over the Ravens, adding one reception for zero additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: Hampton tallied just his second game of 100 yards from scrimmage in the team’s first win of the season, which was also his first game this year hitting the century mark on the ground. The only other game in which Hampton surpassed 100 yards came against the Raiders way back in Week 2, which was also the only other game this season with 20 or more touches. The typically backfield timeshare tilted heavily in Hampton’s favor through positive game script, hinting at his upside potential in games the Chargers are able to control, something that has not been routine this season. Hampton could carry legitimate RB2 upside against the Jets in Week 11, pending the status of quarterback Geno Smith.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Omarion Hampton rushed 13 times for 60 yards in the Chargers’ Week 9 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh told reporters last Thursday that Omarion Hampton would get more touches. Surprise. The Chargers continued their three-player backfield rotation for much of the day, though Kimani Vidal was somewhat phased out in the second half. That said, Hampton at least totaled double-digit rushing attempts for the first time since Week 5. He clearly looked like the most powerful, explosive Chargers running back on a 32-yard run late in the game, jump-cutting his way into an open hole before exploding down the right side of the field. Hampton is a FLEX option against the Ravens in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh indicated that Omarion Hampton will get more touches.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: Harbaugh reportedly made comments to this effect earlier in the week. When asked for his thoughts on the matter, OC Mike McDaniel said he is “excited about someone dictating the rotation” and added that Hampton has “had a really great week of prep.” Hampton hasn’t scored double-digit half-PPR points since Week 4. Whether the potential usage increase can get him back to 10.0-plus points remains to be seen, but this week’s comments are at least somewhat encouraging.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Omarion Hampton had nine rushes for 20 yards in the Chargers’ Week 8 loss to the Rams, adding two catches for seven yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: It was business as usual for the plodding Hampton, who breaks no tackles and does nothing beyond what is blocked for him. Hampton, who now has less than 50 rushing yards in five games this season, was third in pass routes among LA running backs on the day and tied with Keaton Mitchell with three targets. Hampton’s role doesn’t offer much: Coming into Week 8, he ranked 31st among running backs in expected fantasy points per game (and 37th in actual fantasy points per game). With no ceiling of which to speak, Hampton should stay on benches in Week 9 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: The Athletic’s Noah Furtado reports the Chargers will try to “simplify” the team’s offense in the coming weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: Justin Herbert and the flailing Chargers skill position players have appeared almost comically confused about all the pre-snap motion OC Mike McDaniel uses. That came through in the team’s embarrassing Week 6 loss to the Chiefs when players were bumping into each other during pre-snap motion calls from Herbert. Head coach Jim Harbaugh acknowledged the team is considering narrowing the offensive playbook during their bye week. “Definitely looking at volume and where you can make it to where the players can understand,” Harbaugh said when asked about how Chargers players were adjusting to McDaniel’s complex offense. The Chargers have used pre-snap motion on 74 percent of their snaps, the fourth highest rate in the NFL. Last year they used motion on 56 percent of their snaps. Hopefully these adjustments lead to some production for the NFL’s worst offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Omarion Hampton had seven rushes for 18 yards in the Chargers’ Week 6 loss to the Chiefs, adding four catches for 21 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: Hampton was his usual plodding self in this one, with a long rush of four yards in another depressing outing for the LA offense. Kimani Vidal, meanwhile had seven rushes for 21 yards and got much of his work in the first quarter. Keaton Mitchell had just two carries and did not catch his lone target. Hampton led the backfield in routes and targets on the day. His diminishing role and his lack of efficiency has made Hampton nothing more than a touchdown-dependent desperation flex option this year. The Chargers have a bye in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Omarion Hampton rushed 14 times for 33 yards in the Chargers’ Week 5 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: Webster’s defines plodding as whatever this was. Hampton picked up a literal third of his yards on one 11-yard carry, and while much of the blame goes to the sheer lack of bodies on the offensive line, it was still mightily unimpressive. Hampton is at best a dart-throw FLEX for Week 6 against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-newso.headline: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports Greg Newsome (ankle) will miss 4-6 weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-newso.analysis: Newsome will undergo surgery after sustaining a high ankle sprain in Week 11. His absence could be a blow to a Giants secondary that has played well in 2026, allowing the NFL’s 12th lowest drop back success rate and 11th lowest drop back EPA. Newsome through Week 11 had allowed the lowest EPA per target of any Giants cornerback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-newso.headline: Giants head coach John Harbaugh said CB Greg Newsome will miss multiple weeks with a high-ankle sprain.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-newso.analysis: Newsome’s injury comes just weeks after he signed a three-year, $46 million contract extension with the Giants. The 26-year-old corner has appeared on 483 defensive snaps this season, earning a PFF coverage grade of 71.2 while allowing opposing receivers to catch 19 passes for 209 scoreless yards. His absence will be a tough blow to a Giants secondary that ranks fourth in net yards allowed per attempt and fifth in overall passing yards allowed this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-newso.headline: Giants signed CB Greg Newsome to a three-year, $46 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-newso.analysis: Newsome signed a one-year $8 million contract with the Giants this offseason and is now being rewarded for his strong play during the first half of this season. The 26-year-old corner has allowed just 174 receiving yards on 26 targets this season, per PFF, earning a coverage grade of 66.1. He has been one of the league’s better outside corners this season and will now be under contract with the Giants through the 2029 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-newso.headline: Jevón Holland (concussion) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-newso.analysis: Holland, the Giants’ starting free safety, and Tyler Nubin (neck), the Giants’ starting strong safety, are both questionable to play. Meanwhile, starting perimeter CB Greg Newsome (concussion) has been ruled out. Expect the Texans’ passing offense to stay hot this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-newso.headline: Jevón Holland (concussion) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-newso.analysis: Holland, the team’s top safety, and Greg Newsome (concussion), the team’s top cornerback, were both sidelined today. Giants LB Tremaine Edmunds (shoulder) was also sidelined. The Giants are tasked with containing a Texans’ passing offense that ties for the league lead in explosive pass plays this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-newso.headline: Giants agreed to terms with CB Greg Newsome, formerly of the Jaguars, on a one-year, $10 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-newso.analysis: Newsome was traded to the Jaguars last October and started 11 games for them. The former first-round pick allowed opposing receivers to go for 48-582-5 against him on 73 targets, and has struggled over the last two seasons after a strong first three years in the league. Newsome played almost exclusively on the outside last season, but has shown enough versatility throughout his career to play both outside and in the slot. Newsome will make for a nice addition to a secondary that just lost Cor’Dale Flott to the Titans on the first day of legal tampering.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-newso.headline: NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe reports that the Jaguars “plan to play” Travis Hunter as a full-time cornerback and part-time wide receiver in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-newso.analysis: Per Wolfe, the Jaguars believe Hunter can be an “elite” cornerback, while still being “an impact player” on offense. For fantasy purposes, this is unfortunate. Hunter may be stuck rotating in as a contributor in three-wide receiver sets, which would make him frustratingly unreliable, though head coach Liam Coen will likely try to scheme up ways to get the ball in his hands. On the plus side, Wolfe said Hunter will be “full-go” by Week 1. The Jaguars are reportedly expected to let one of their free agent cornerbacks, Montaric Brown or Greg Newsome, walk in free agency.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-newso.headline: Jaguars CB Greg Newsome suffered an ankle injury in Jacksonville’s Week 11 game against the Chargers and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-newso.analysis: Only recently back from injury, Newsome didn’t make it very long before landing back on the shelf. He has been replaced by Christian Braswell.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-newso.headline: Jaguars HC Liam Coen said Greg Newsome will have “an opportunity to play” in Week 6 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-newso.analysis: Speaking with the media on Friday, Coen said there’s some crossover between what the Jaguars do defensively and what Newsome did with the Browns that should put Newsome in line to see some snaps. Whether or not he draws the start is to be determined, but it doesn’t sound like the Jaguars will waste too much time getting Newsome on the field in a meaningful capacity, especially after they traded starting corner Tyson Campbell to acquire him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-newso.headline: Browns acquired CB Tyson Campbell and the Eagles’ 2026 seventh-round pick from the Jaguars in exchange for CB Greg Newsome and the Jets’ 2026 sixth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-newso.analysis: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Browns and Jaguars will be swapping late-round picks in addition to the cornerbacks. Campbell signed a four-year, $76.5 million extension in the 2024 offseason with the Jaguars and is now under contract through 2028 for Cleveland. He has six interceptions and 42 passes defended through his five-year career, but has missed 11 games over the last two seasons. The Jaguars swap him out for Greg Newsome, who is in the last season of his rookie deal. Newsome held a top-45 PFF coverage grade each of his first three seasons and has three interceptions and 37 passes defended through four total seasons. The Jags have flexibility at corner with Travis Hunter mixing in for snaps; his usage won’t decrease with Newsome joining him on the outside. Meanwhile, the Browns opt for Campbell’s long-term deal over negotiating a Newsome extension.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs caught 4-of-6 targets for 45 yards in the Commanders’ Week 11 win over the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: Diggs was shown displaying clear frustration on multiple occasions, the two most glaring of which came on the sideline following a poorly thrown ball from quarterback Jayden Daniels. History would repeat in the second half when Daniels bounced a ball to Diggs in the end zone after escaping to his right, the former of whom had broken free of coverage over the middle of the field. Diggs’ veteran presence will need to persist through the uneven quarterback play if the Commanders are to make a push toward the postseason during the final two months of play, a road that was made that much easier with the walk off win over the Bengals. Up next are the downtrodden Cardinals in Week 12, where Diggs will remain a viable Flex play in fantasy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs caught 6-of-10 targets for 83 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 10 win over the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: Diggs and the Washington pass offense went as Jayden Daniels went, with the dual threat quarterback mixing perfectly thrown passes with completely errant ones, two of which were directed toward Diggs. A third incompletion bounced off Diggs’ helmet as the veteran receiver should have drawn a defensive pass interference penalty, with the ball eventually ruled an incompletion upon further review after Treylon Burks appeared to come down with what would have been one of the wilder receptions of the season. Daniels’ best pass of the game came on the game-winning touchdown to Diggs in the flat on a crosser, threaded between two defenders. Diggs made a third miss as he took it into the end zone from 32 yards out to send the team to a 3-5-1 record, now two games behind the Giants with the first tie-breaker in hand. He will remain a volatile WR3 on capped routes against the Bengals in Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs caught 3-of-5 targets for 51 yards in the Commanders’ Week 9 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: With the Commanders down three receivers, Diggs appeared prime for a decent day against a Rams secondary that was down two corners. Instead, the 32-year-old receiver was outshone by journeyman Van Jefferson for most of the day until the final drive of the game. With the Commanders looking to mount a game-tying drive, Diggs broke free into the secondary to make a 42-yard reception, which accounted for nearly all of his receiving production. In two games without Terry McLaurin, Diggs has averaged just 5.5 targets per game and totaled 89 yards and a touchdown. He’s far from the target hog he was in his prime, and shouldn’t be treated as anything more than a WR3/WR4 on Thursday night against the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs caught 3-of-6 targets for 38 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 8 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: Offensive coordinator David Blough has made good on his promise not to increase the route participation or snap rate of the veteran receiver in the absence of Terry McLaurin, effectively keeping Diggs relegated to a situational role primarily from the slot. That has left Treylon Burks and rookie Antonio Williams to lead the team in routes the previous two weeks while limiting the true ceiling of Diggs in the process. Consider Diggs a touchdown-dependent FLEX option in a difficult matchup against the Rams in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs (hand/hamstring) is not on Washington’s final Week 8 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: He should be a mid-range WR3 with Terry McLaurin out of the picture in Washington. Diggs practiced in full each of the last two sessions of the week after a Wednesday DNP.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs (hand/hamstring) practiced in full Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: Diggs shook of the absence Wednesday with a full showing Thursday, indicating he is tracking well to suit up when the Commanders face off against the Eagles on Sunday Night Football. The tam previously indicated that Diggs’ modest role would not grow in the absence of Terry McLaurin, potentially paving the way for rookie Antonio Williams to see an increase in role and opportunity in the second half of the season. Fantasy managers will want to confirm Diggs’ status on the final injury report Friday, but it appears as if he will be available in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs (hand/hamstring/rest) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn already said Diggs won’t practice Wednesday, so this is not a surprise. Quinn also confirmed the veteran will return to practice Thursday and the additional rest designation should stave off concerns of Diggs dealing with a long-term injury. He should be in the WR3/FLEX mix for Week 8 against the Eagles. Also not practicing for the Commanders was TE John Bates (shoulder).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said Stefon Diggs will practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: Diggs won’t practice Wednesday with an undisclosed injury. He should be fine for Washington’s Week 8 matchup against the Eagles, however. Diggs could see a slightly bigger role in the Commanders offense with Terry McLaurin (knee) done for the year. Diggs drafters should keep an eye on the veteran’s practice status in the coming days. Diggs has been targeted on a team-high 28 percent of his pass routes in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Commanders coach Dan Quinn said he doesn’t anticipate Stefon Diggs taking on a larger role with Terry McLaurin lost for the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: Quinn did mention usage from “elsewhere” and the name “Antonio Williams” came up. Williams won’t be a buzzy waiver wire claim this week but could find himself in a reasonable WR3/WR4 sort of situation as the year unfolds.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Commanders coach Dan Quinn said Terry McLaurin (knee) tore his patellar tendon and will miss the rest of the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: It’s another rough blow for Washington’s No. 1 wideout, who will now have missed most of the last two seasons with injuries with the book closed on a 15-catch, 230-yard 2026 season in just five games. Entering his age-32 season in 2027, McLaurin will be a release or restructure candidate with a $34 million cap hit. The Commanders could save $16 million by releasing him without getting into post-June 1 antics. In the short term fantasy calculus, Stefon Diggs will slide in as Washington’s No. 1 receiver and Chig Okonkwo will also get a boost. Antonio Williams figures to see more snaps going forward as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Chig Okonkwo caught 4-of-5 targets for 66 yards in the Commanders’ Week 11 win over the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: The veteran tight end’s five targets finished third on the team behind the 11 of Antonio Williams and six of veteran Stefon Diggs. Okonkwo remains unlikely to return elite volume in the more conservative Washington offense but can continue to return usable fantasy outings as a viable TE2. He’ll push for TE1 status in a plus matchup against the Cardinals in Week 12.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Chig Okonkwo (back) is practicing in full ahead of Washington’s Week 11 game with the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: Okonkwo left last Thursday night’s game against the Giants briefly with an injury scare, but had returned by the end of the game. This listing tells us he’s in no danger of missing Monday Night Football and, assuming Ben Sinnott isn’t suddenly usurping him as the starter after his nice game, Okonkwo can be played as a fringe TE1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Chig Okonkwo (hip) is not on the final injury report and will play in Week 10 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: Okonkwo is one of many fringe TE1/2 candidates on any given week. He does not need to be in fantasy football lineups, but he can act as a serviceable fill-in, though his upside is most touchdown-dependent.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Chig Okonkwo (hip) practiced in full on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: That ought to put him firmly in the mix to play on Thursday against the Giants. Okonkwo is coming off a 6/57 game on seven targets against the Rams and figures to again be a reasonable low-end TE1 against the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Chig Okonkwo (hip) was listed as limited on Monday’s estimated injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: This is a new injury for Okonkwo, who caught a 16-yard pass on the final play of Sunday’s loss to the Rams as the Commanders were looking to tie the game. Okonkwo has gone for 57 or more yards in three of his last four games and would be on the streaming radar as a boom-or-bust TE2 on Thursday against the Giants if he can play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Chig Okonkwo caught 6-of-7 targets for 57 yards in the Commanders’ Week 9 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: Okonkwo’s seven targets tied Van Jefferson for the team high in this one. Okonkwo hauled in a 15-yard reception on the Commanders’ opening drive, and on the final play of the game, he caught a 16-yard pass and then tossed it to Rachaad White in hopes of keeping the play alive after time had already expired. Okonkwo has gone for 50-plus yards in three of his last four games and is seeing enough work in the passing game to be on the streaming radar for Week 10’s game against the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Chig Okonkwo caught 2-of-4 targets for 32 yards in the Commanders’ Week 8 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: Okonkwo flashed his athletic ability with a full-stretch reception in the second half but it was not enough to overshadow a first quarter fumble. The spry veteran has now been held to four receptions or fewer in four of five appearances in the low volume Washington pass offense, unable to return consistent fantasy value through the absence of Terry McLaurin. He is best left on fantasy benches in a Week 9 matchup against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Commanders coach Dan Quinn said Terry McLaurin (knee) tore his patellar tendon and will miss the rest of the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: It’s another rough blow for Washington’s No. 1 wideout, who will now have missed most of the last two seasons with injuries with the book closed on a 15-catch, 230-yard 2026 season in just five games. Entering his age-32 season in 2027, McLaurin will be a release or restructure candidate with a $34 million cap hit. The Commanders could save $16 million by releasing him without getting into post-June 1 antics. In the short term fantasy calculus, Stefon Diggs will slide in as Washington’s No. 1 receiver and Chig Okonkwo will also get a boost. Antonio Williams figures to see more snaps going forward as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: ESPN’s John Keim reports Terry McLaurin’s knee injury is considered “significant.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: Washington head coach Dan Quinn said after the team’s Monday night loss to the 49ers that there was “fear” McLaurin could be lost for the long-term after going down with a non-contact injury and was carted to the locker room. McLaurin has functioned as the team’s lone downfield threat for much of the season, and could be replaced with Treylon Burks, who on Monday night caught four balls for 66 yards before sustaining a late-game injury. Antonio Williams and Dyami Brown could also see an increase in routes and targets if McLaurin is sidelined for a while. Look for Chig Okonkwo to see an uptick in targets too. Okonkwo had seven grabs for 69 yards against the Niners.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Chig Okonkwo caught all seven targets for 69 yards in the Commanders’ Week 6 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: Okonkwo was thrust into an increased role with the departure of lead wide receiver Terry McLaurin in the first quarter, operating as the primary option through the air for much of the game. Veteran wide receiver Stefon Diggs continued to operate in a situational role, making Okonkwo a priority start when the Commanders come out of their Week 7 bye to face the Eagles in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.headline: Antonio Williams caught 9-of-11 targets for 122 yards in the Commanders’ Week 11 win over the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.analysis: Williams was the top option for quarterback Jayden Daniels throughout, seeing consistent volume throughout. He staked his mark on the game for good with a 42-yard reception to set up the game-winning field goal as time expired, effectively saving the Commanders’ season in the process. After teasing fantasy upside throughout the first half of his rookie season, Williams finally appears to have earned the top role through the air as he enters the final two months of the regular season as a viable WR3 with WR2 upside in fantasy circles. He gets a tantalizing matchup against the Cardinals in Week 12.

https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.headline: Antonio Williams caught both targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 10 win over the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.analysis: Williams cashed in on his first target of the game for a 31-yard score in the third quarter, adding one additional grab for 11 yards in the final frame. The electric rookie continues to play starters snaps and challenge for the team lead in route rate but had yet to get completely on the same page with quarterback Jayden Daniels, the latter of whom leaned heavily on Stefon Diggs and tight end Chig Okonkwo in this one. The talent is undeniable for Williams, but fantasy managers would love to see a bump in targets before feeling comfortable entering him into starting lineups. Williams’ next chance to return a usable fantasy outing comes in Week 11 against the inside-funnel Bengals, where he should avoid the primary coverage of lockdown corner DJ Turner.

https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.headline: Antonio Williams caught 3-of-6 targets for 25 yards in the Commanders’ Week 9 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.analysis: Fantasy managers hoping for a breakout performance from Williams, with Terry McLaurin (knee), Treylon Burks (foot), and Dyami Brown (calf) all sidelined, will be left wanting more. Instead, veteran journeyman Van Jefferson stepped up, catching five passes for 58 yards and a touchdown on a team-high seven targets, while Williams was largely an afterthought. Of the six targets Williams saw on Sunday, three came in the fourth quarter with the Commanders trailing 20-13. The rookie has caught 8-of-13 targets for 79 scoreless yards over the last two weeks and will be hard to trust as anything more than a WR3/WR4 in Week 10 against the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.headline: Antonio Williams caught 5-of-7 targets for 54 yards in the Commanders’ Week 8 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.analysis: Williams mostly operated in a short area role but added a 30-yard grab up the seam in the fourth quarter to pad his counting stats for fantasy managers hoping on a second-half rookie breakout. While the fantasy returns have yet to pop, managers can continue to hold the electric rookie in the hopes his role grows in the coming weeks. That said, he is likely best left on fantasy benches until his route structure improves.

https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.headline: Treylon Burks (foot) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.analysis: Burks downgraded from a limited showing Wednesday to a “DNP” Thursday, indicating he might be headed toward an absence when the Commanders take on the Eagles on Sunday Night Football. Considering the team is already without Terry McLaurin, who was lost for the season in Week 6, this would appear to be setting up for the best chance for rookie Antonio Williams to finally break out in Washington. Fantasy managers will want to confirm the status of Burks on the team’s final injury report Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.headline: Commanders coach Dan Quinn said he doesn’t anticipate Stefon Diggs taking on a larger role with Terry McLaurin lost for the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.analysis: Quinn did mention usage from “elsewhere” and the name “Antonio Williams” came up. Williams won’t be a buzzy waiver wire claim this week but could find himself in a reasonable WR3/WR4 sort of situation as the year unfolds.

https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.headline: Commanders coach Dan Quinn said Terry McLaurin (knee) tore his patellar tendon and will miss the rest of the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.analysis: It’s another rough blow for Washington’s No. 1 wideout, who will now have missed most of the last two seasons with injuries with the book closed on a 15-catch, 230-yard 2026 season in just five games. Entering his age-32 season in 2027, McLaurin will be a release or restructure candidate with a $34 million cap hit. The Commanders could save $16 million by releasing him without getting into post-June 1 antics. In the short term fantasy calculus, Stefon Diggs will slide in as Washington’s No. 1 receiver and Chig Okonkwo will also get a boost. Antonio Williams figures to see more snaps going forward as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.headline: Antonio Williams caught 3-of-4 targets for 50 yards in the Commanders’ Week 6 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.analysis: While the yardage total looks solid on paper, the fact that Williams had only four targets in a game in which veteran wide receiver Terry McLaurin departed in the first quarter and quarterback Jayden Daniels attempted 40 passes is concerning. Williams continues to flash big play upside through a multitude of injuries to teammates but has yet to fully take advantage of the increase in opportunity, something fantasy managers will hope corrects when the Commanders come out of their bye to face the Eagles in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that Terry McLaurin (hamstring) will “most likely” be a game-time decision for Week 5 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.analysis: Keep it locked to Rotoworld, folks. Hopefully, we get word on McLaurin’s status on Saturday, but it appears as though we may have to wait until Sunday morning. Fowler adds that rookie WR Antonio Williams “could be a factor in the passing game regardless of whether McLaurin plays.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.headline: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) will not play in Week 5 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.analysis: Diggs did not practice this week and was ruled out by the team shortly after Friday’s practice concluded. His absence will give rookie Antonio Williams, who ran 30 routes last week, a chance to take on a bigger role. Williams tied for the team lead with eight targets in Week 4’s game against the Colts and could be treated as a desperation WR4/FLEX play. Fantasy managers considering Williams for their lineups may want to check the weather, as rain and wind are currently forecasted for the area, which could create a suboptimal environment for Washington’s passing game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.headline: Austin Ekeler rushed seven times for 41 yards in the Commanders’ Week 11 win over the Bengals, adding three yards on two receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.analysis: The box score does little to jump off the page but it is notable that Ekeler played over Rachaad White as the primary change of pace option behind Jacory Croskey-Merritt. Whether that was due to White’s presence on the injury report throughout the week remains to be seen. Either way, the only fantasy-viable back currently on the roster appears to be Croskey-Merritt, leaving both Ekeler and White of little value moving forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.headline: Austin Ekeler rushed nine times for 26 yards in the Commanders’ Week 10 win over the Giants, adding 26 yards on four receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.analysis: The veteran in-season addition’s 13 opportunities matched that of starter Rachaad White, the latter of whom played the team’s first two drives before splitting the workload the rest of the way. Ekeler also split red zone work, although it was White that nearly missed a touchdown on a seven-yard run that was tackled at the one in the second quarter. Either way, the near-even split between the two caps the fantasy upside of both backs in the absence of Jacory Croskey-Merritt, with neither on the fantasy radar ahead of a Week 11 meeting with the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.headline: Commanders ruled out RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) for Week 6 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.analysis: No surprise here. Croskey-Merritt has been dealing with a groin injury since the start of the season. This week he couldn’t practice and has since been officially ruled out for the Commanders’ Monday Night Football matchup against the 49ers. Croskey-Merritt will get a two-week break with Washington on bye in Week 7. Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler figure to handle the majority of the backfield touches in his absence with White being the preferred fantasy option between the two.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.headline: Austin Ekeler (chest) was limited on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.analysis: Ekeler continues to practice in a limited capacity while wearing a red non-contact jersey. He has a chance to play on Monday night, but he is clearly hurting. Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) remains sidelined and Rachaad White (shoulder) has been downgraded to limited. It’s an ailing backfield.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.headline: Austin Ekeler (chest) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.analysis: Ekeler and Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) are both ailing, though the latter player sat out entirely. Rachaad White (shoulder) and Jeremy McNichols (quad) are both practicing in full. Croskey-Merritt is the only fantasy-relevant Commanders running back at this time, assuming he is good to go on Monday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.headline: Austin Ekeler rushed four times for 29 yards in the Commanders’ Week 4 loss to the Colts, adding one catch for 11 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.analysis: Ekeler made his 2026 debut in London and immediately operated as the Commanders’ backup with Rachaad White out. The team did, however, give four running backs multiple touches in this game. Ekeler’s role could grow as he gets more reps under his belt this year, but he could just as easily be made inactive once White is healthy. He’s only worth stashing in the deepest of leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.headline: Rachaad White (shoulder) will not play in Washington’s Week 4 game against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.analysis: He didn’t practice at any point this week after suffering a shoulder injury in Week 3. He has to be considered questionable for Week 5 at this point. ‘Bill’ Croskey-Merritt figures to shoulder the majority of the workload for the Commanders this week and is a reasonable FLEX play against the Colts. Freshly-signed Austin Ekeler figures to handle third-down work.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.headline: Rachaad White (shoulder) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.analysis: With two DNPs to start the week, White looks unlikely to suit up for Week 4 against the Colts. Austin Ekeler traveled with the team after signing with the team earlier this week, so he could ultimately take on White’s role. Backup running back Kayton Allen could also see more work, but Jacory Croskey-Merritt remains the clear lead back in Washington for now. He is on the RB2/3 border for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.headline: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said Rachaad White is receiving treatment for his shoulder injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.analysis: It sounds like White will be a question mark headed into Washington’s Week 4 game against the Colts in London. Quinn added that it’s too early to tell whether Austin Ekeler, who signed with the Commanders this week, will be active for Week 4. Jacory Croskey-Merritt could see a significant bump in carries and pass routes — and maybe targets — if White is sidelined this week. JCM, who has 58 percent of the team’s carries through three games, would be a nice flex option in that case.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.headline: Commanders re-signed RB Austin Ekeler.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.analysis: Ekeler is fully recovered from a torn Achilles that ended his 2025 season after just two games. The 31-year-old running back returns to a familiar place in Washington and will sign to the 53-man roster, making him immediately eligible to play in Week 4. We expect him to have a bit of a ramp-up period before being active on game days, but Ekeler could end up having a meaningful role in a backfield that has struggled to get going through the first three weeks. Ekeler may be worth a stash in deeper leagues, but we’ll have to see what kind of role he has before we can consider putting him in lineups. Ekeler met last week with the Panthers about possibly joining their practice squad but a deal was never reached.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.headline: Jacory Croskey-Merritt rushed 13 times for 54 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 11 win over the Bengals, adding 23 yards on two receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.analysis: Croskey-Merritt immediately returned from injured reserve to handily lead the team in snaps and opportunities, despite veteran Austin Ekeler playing the team’s first series. More interesting was the fact that Rachaad White hardly had a role, with Ekeler serving as the primary change of pace option, something that could be due to White’s presence on the injury report throughout the week. Either way, Croskey-Merritt appears to have a stranglehold on lead duties moving forward, a role that keeps him as a viable RB2 in the immediate future. That holds true for a Week 12 meeting with the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.headline: Commanders activated RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) off injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.analysis: “Bill” has missed the minimum four games and was designated as questionable; he has been removed from the injury report by the Commanders and should be their lead back. You likely already had plans to start him if you were holding up your FLEX spot or RB2 position for him, and now you officially can do so.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.headline: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) is questionable for Week 11 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.analysis: Croskey-Merritt managed a week of full practices as he attempts to return from injured reserve, and while the team has not yet activated him, he appears to be trending in the right direction for his first game action since Week 5. Rachaad White, also listed as questionable, would likely shift back to a primary change of pace role, should Croskey-Merritt return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.headline: Commanders HC Dan Quinn told reporters RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) is “trending the right way” ahead of the matchup with the Bengals in Week 11.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.analysis: Quinn said Croskey-Merritt had a great week and is trending the right way for Monday’s game against the Bengals. It’s great news for fantasy managers and the Commanders as backup running back Rachaad White (heel) missed practice Saturday. Croskey-Merritt deserves FLEX consideration assuming he’s active against the Bengals this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.headline: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) is practicing in full ahead of Washington’s Week 11 game with the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.analysis: Pretty much all the smoke here is that he’ll be activated and ready to go for Monday Night Football and the injury report does not disagree with that assertion. We’re expecting to see him as questionable on the final injury report because that is just generally how teams label players returning from IR, but ‘Bill’ is looking like a reasonable FLEX play against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.headline: Commanders designated RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) to return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.analysis: Ben Standig reports that he’s expecting Croskey-Merritt to be active for Monday night barring a setback. We’re expecting a pass-happy Commanders offense as they try to keep pace with Cincinnati’s high-flying offense, but given how many teams are on bye there’s certainly worse FLEX starts out there than a returning “Bill.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.headline: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) is “trending in the right direction” to practice this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.analysis: Quinn declined to commit to opening “Bill’s” 21-day return window, but sounded optimistic about doing so later in the week. The Commanders’ RB1 has missed the last four games with a groin injury he picked up in Week 5 and would be eligible to return as early as Week 11 if he were to be designated to return this week. The Commanders have struggled on the ground without JCM this season, as their running backs have combined to average just 3.7 YPC since Week 6 while finding the end zone once. If he’s able to play against the Bengals, JCM would have some appeal as an RB3/FLEX in a week that has six teams on bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.headline: Commanders placed Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.analysis: He’ll miss at least the next four weeks. Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler figure to get the majority of the work from Weeks 6-9. The Commanders also brought Jeremy McNichols off injured reserve and signed him to the active roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.headline: Commanders ruled out RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) for Week 6 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.analysis: No surprise here. Croskey-Merritt has been dealing with a groin injury since the start of the season. This week he couldn’t practice and has since been officially ruled out for the Commanders’ Monday Night Football matchup against the 49ers. Croskey-Merritt will get a two-week break with Washington on bye in Week 7. Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler figure to handle the majority of the backfield touches in his absence with White being the preferred fantasy option between the two.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.headline: Commanders beat writer Ben Standig reports RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) isn’t expected to play in Week 6 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.analysis: Croskey-Merritt has dealt with a groin injury all season despite playing in the Commanders’ first five games. He missed multiple practices this week and will now get two weeks off with missing the game against the 49ers ahead of Washington’s bye week. For now, expect Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler to handle the majority of the backfield touches for the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.headline: Ja’Marr Chase caught 5-of-9 targets for 31 yards in the Bengals’ Week 11 loss to the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.analysis: The two teams played to a scoreless first frame through driving rain in Maryland, with Chase appearing to come alive on the teams first possession of the second quarter. He would ultimately be locked up by sticky coverage heavily influenced by Washington’s ability to generate consistent pressure, narrowly missing a downfield shot in the second half in triple coverage that could have propelled his fantasy day toward a usable week. Chase’s next opportunity to flourish comes in a Week 12 meeting with the Saints, where his skillset sets up well to take advantage of one of the highest single-high rates in the league.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.headline: Ja’Marr Chase caught 11-of-14 targets for 231 yards in the Bengals’ Week 10 win over the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.analysis: It was the second consecutive game in which Chase went over 140 yards in the first half alone, eventually notching the third most receiving yards in a game in his illustrious career with 231 while blowing by the century mark for the third consecutive contest. Chase was the primary point of emphasis from the first kick against the Steelers, working mostly the short-to-intermediate areas of the field before bomb on a sluggo route in the second quarter. He worked behind primary coverage on three separate instances but was ushered out of bounds on all three occasions, any of which would have further inflated his counting stats had they turned into touchdowns. Chase and the Bengals now get a long week of preparation for the pass-funnel Commanders on Monday Night Football in Week 11, where he will remain an elite WR1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.headline: Ja’Marr Chase caught 10-of-12 targets for 155 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 9 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.analysis: Chase hadn’t had a game with 100 yards receiving until two weeks ago. Since then, he’s had at least 10 receptions, at least 141 yards and a touchdown in back-to-back games. Ho-hum. Chase absolutely toasted Falcons cornerback AJ Terrell for a 47-yard touchdown in the first quarter on a play that looked eerily similar to a touchdown he had against Terrell when the two were in college. Chase is up to 647 yards and seven touchdowns on the season. He’s a WR1 heading into Week 10’s matchup against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.headline: Ja’Marr Chase caught 11-of-16 targets for 141 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 8 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.analysis: Chase was heavily involved in a pass-heavy game script, seeing 16-of-48 Joe Burrow pass attempts. He was targeted downfield several times, catching a 30-yard touchdown but being the intended target on a pair of interceptions. It was Chase’s first 100-yard receiving day as he led the team in targets and receptions.
