The Bengals have a pass funnel to Chase and Tee Higgins, leading to extremely productive fantasy days in high scoring games. Chase is once again squarely in the fantasy WR1 ranks for Week 9 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.headline: Ja’Marr Chase is not on Cincinnati’s final Week 8 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.analysis: He will play and be on the overall WR1 line against the Titans. Zac Taylor spoke earlier today and said he had no concerns about Chase. Everyone has downplayed concerns about Chase’s ankle for the majority of the week. He will be a smash play against a Jeffrey Simmons-less Titans defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.headline: Ja’Marr Chase (ankle) practiced in full Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.analysis: Chase quickly puts his fantasy managers’ worries to rest, returning to a full session Thursday after being limited Wednesday. The Bengals will be playing without two tight ends and their WR3 in Andre Iosivas, but their primary contributors remain one of the healthier units as we approach the half way point in the regular season. Chase can be started as a top tier WR1 against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Ja’Marr Chase’s ankle injury “is not considered a major deal.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.analysis: Rap isn’t breaking much news here. Chase didn’t practice on Wednesday, but the Bengals listed him as getting a rest day on top of the ankle issue. It was just a maintenance day for one of the league’s best wideouts. Chase remains in the WR1 overall mix for his Week 8 game against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.headline: Ja’Marr Chase (NIR-rest/ankle) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.analysis: The rest aspect suggests Chase’s ankle injury can effectively be treated as a non-issue, but NFL teams have played games with the injury report at times this season, so we are cataloguing it here to be safe. Assuming Chase resumes practicing tomorrow, he can be started as an elite WR1, as usual, in Week 8 against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.headline: Ja’Marr Chase caught 5-of-7 targets for 62 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 7 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.analysis: Chase caught just two passes for 23 yards in the first half, but he popped up for a 30-yard gain in the fourth quarter on a drive that he capped with a two-yard touchdown to save the day for his fantasy managers. His seven targets tied Tee Higgins for the team-high this week, but Higgins had the far more productive day. He’s still in search of his first 100-yard performance of the year, but Chase has now found the end zone five times and has gone for 60-plus yards in four of six games this season. He’ll be on the WR1 radar next week against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.headline: Ja’Marr Chase caught 6-of-10 targets for 77 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 5 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.analysis: Chase returned from a concussion he suffered last week, seeing 10 targets in a productive fantasy day. He saw a goal-line fade target on the Bengals’ first drive and was later tackled at the one-yard line towards the end of the first half. Joe Burrow missed Chase for a 70-yard touchdown in the second half but Chase made a miraculous catch with his right arm for a 45-yard touchdown later in the half. He finishes with a successful fantasy day and is squarely in the WR1 ranks heading into the Bengals’ Week 6 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.headline: Mike Gesicki caught 5-of-6 targets for 77 yards in the Bengals’ Week 11 loss to the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.analysis: Gesicki saw increased usage against an aggressive Commanders team that brought consistent pressure into the backfield, with the highlight of his game coming on a 32-yard reception over the middle of the field on the team’s final possession, ultimately ended in a field goal to take the lead with just over two minutes remaining. The Commanders would drive the field and kick the game-winning field goal on the subsequent possession to send the Bengals to 7-3. Gesicki’s weekly volume remains unlikely to approach elite territory, but his elite red zone usage and penchant for finding paint keeps him in the weekly TE1 discussion in the high-powered Cincinnati offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.headline: Mike Gesicki caught 1-of-2 targets for nine yards in the Bengals’ Week 10 win over the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.analysis: Gesicki caught the first pass from scrimmage for nine yards before completely disappearing the rest of the game, which was easy to do considering Ja’Marr Chase erupted for the third highest receiving total in a game in his career with 231 yards. The Steelers just had no answer for the elite alpha receiver, leaving little scraps leftover for the rest of the Cincinnati offense. The only thing Chase didn’t do was find the end zone, with the touchdowns accounted for by Chase Brown (two), Samaje Perine, Dohnte Meyers, and Drew Sample. Gesicki remains a touchdown-dependent TE2 ahead of a Week 11 meeting with the Commanders on Monday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.headline: Mike Gesicki caught 2-of-2 targets for 11 yards in the Bengals’ Week 9 victory over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.analysis: Gesicki had caught a touchdown in each of his last six games, but was essentially a non-factor in the win over the Falcons in Madrid. The Bengals scored three times in the red zone, but those touchdowns went to Tee Higgins (twice) and Joe Burrow. Gesicki needs those scores to be fantasy-relevant. He’ll be a touchdown-dependent TE2 heading into Week 10’s matchup with the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.headline: Mike Gesicki caught 4-of-6 targets for 76 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 8 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.analysis: Gesicki has been a high-value red zone target for the Bengals all season long. His score against the Titans came from outside of the red zone, catching a 25-yard pass for the score in the fourth quarter. It’s Gesicki’s sixth-straight game with a touchdown and seventh score of the season. Pass-heavy game scripts will lift all boats in the Bengals offense but Gesicki remains a high-end fantasy TE2 due to his high amount of touchdown opportunities.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.headline: Mike Gesicki caught his lone target for six yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 7 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.analysis: Gesicki’s lone target came on an end zone target from Joe Burrow that resulted in a six-yard touchdown. The 31-year-old tight end has now scored in all five games he has appeared in this season, but has managed just 10 yards on two receptions in his last two games. Fellow tight ends Erick All and Drew Sample combined to catch five passes for 45 yards and one touchdown on five targets. Gesicki has run 15 routes in each of his last two games and is purely a touchdown-dependent option in Week 8 against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.headline: Mike Gesicki caught 1-of-2 targets for 4 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 5 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.analysis: The Bengals utilized all of their tight ends against the Dolphins, with Gesicki catching just one pass on the day. His sole reception was a touchdown on the Bengals’ opening drive, totaling four on the season and salvaging some fantasy value for those who streamed him at tight end this week. Gesicki’s value is lowered when Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are active; his red zone utilization makes Gesicki a low-end fantasy TE2 heading into the Bengals’ Week 6 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.headline: Mike Gesicki caught 3-of-5 targets for 40 yards in the Bengals’ Week 4 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.analysis: Gesicki caught a third quarter touchdown against the Jaguars, his third score of the year. He saw just five targets on a day where Joe Burrow threw 54 passes and Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) exited early. However, Gesicki has a clear red zone role and he led all Bengals tight ends in snaps on the day. If Chase and Tee Higgins (adductor) miss any time, Gesicki is a tight end streaming option for Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.headline: Mike Gesicki caught 3-of-3 targets for 37 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 3 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.analysis: After going without a target last week, Gesicki made the most of his three targets in this one. His most notable reception came in the fourth quarter on a fourth-and-two when he broke free across the middle of the field for a wide-open 25-yard touchdown to put the Bengals up 27-24. Gesicki has now scored in two of his first three games this season, but is averaging just 3.3 targets per game. Fantasy managers should be rushing to add him to their lineups for next week’s game against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.headline: Mike Gesicki was not targeted in Cincinnati’s Week 2 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.analysis: The rollercoaster ride that is “tertiary target in a Tee Higgins/Ja’Marr Chase-centric offense.” Erick All (2/5 on three targets) lead Bengals tight ends in receptions. Drew Sample (36 of 60) led Bengals tight ends in snaps. Starting Gesicki will pay off at times, but this wasn’t one of them. He’s a TE2 in Week 3 against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.headline: Mike Gesicki caught 5-of-7 targets for 78 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 1 win over the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.analysis: Gesicki led the Bengals in catches, targets and yards and was the only pass catcher to score on an afternoon where the Bucs’ defense was funneling Joe Burrow to the middle of the field. Gesicki’s score was a two-yarder where he rolled in to the end zone in the first quarter. Gesicki’s yardage total would have been his second highest of 2025. He’s a valuable real-life contributor, but he is going to have trouble cracking the top 18 tight ends on a regular basis with Ja’Marr Chase, Tee Higgins and Chase Brown all usage monsters for the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.headline: Samaje Perine rushed six times for 26 yards in the Bengals’ Week 11 loss to the Commanders, adding 71 yards on four receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.analysis: The highlight of the game for Perine came on a 44-yard catch-and-run reception where he chipped into a leak route in the flat, springing free from linebacker coverage to give quarterback Joe Burrow an outlet in the face of pressure. He would outrun the secondary and pick up a key block from fellow running back Chase Brown as he sprung free down the sideline for the longest reception in the game. Perine’s 10 opportunities still ranked below the 14 of Brown but the former handily outproduced the presumed starter on his way to a usable fantasy outing. Up next are the ground-funnel Saints, where Perine will return to shaky Flex status in fantasy circles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.headline: Samaje Perine rushed six times for 14 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 10 win over the Steelers, adding 25 yards on four receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.analysis: Perine’s 10 touches dwarfed in comparison to the 18 of lead back Chase Brown, the latter of whom found the end zone twice for his second and third scores of the season. Low weekly volume in the pass-first Cincinnati offense leaves Perine nothing more than a desperation Flex without an injury ahead of him on the depth chart.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.headline: Samaje Perine rushed 11 times for 43 yards in the Bengals’ Week 9 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.analysis: Perine had 43 yards on 11 carries, which was notable because he had two more rushing attempts than starter Chase Brown. While Brown continues to underwhelm, Perine is cutting into Brown’s ceiling (or lack thereof) more than he’s carving out a legitimate role for himself. Perine is one of the better handcuffs to stash, but he shouldn’t be in starting lineups in Week 10 against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.headline: Samaje Perine rushed 4 times for 10 yards in the Bengals’ Week 8 win over the Titans, adding one reception for nine yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.analysis: Perine took a backseat to Chase Brown against the Titans, seeing 26 snaps to Brown’s 50. He was still involved in the red zone, but was not utilized as much as Brown as a pass-catcher. Perine’s path to fantasy production will be touchdown opportunities. He is a fantasy handcuff with some desperation RB4 value in Week 9 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.headline: Samaje Perine rushed four times for 16 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 7 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.analysis: Perine saw only four carries in this one, but he turned his lone goal-line touch into a one-yard touchdown to barely salvage what was still a relatively disappointing day. Perine was out-snapped by Chase Brown 38-12, with Brown also leading the way with 11 rush attempts. Perine will be hard to trust as anything more than a desperation RB4 play next week against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.headline: Bengals OC Dan Pitcher said the team will “continually assess how that touch share between [Perine] and Chase Brown should play out.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.analysis: Pitcher suggested that when they run the ball more from shotgun — as they did last week against the Dolphins — Perine’s a better fit for those kinds of plays. The Bengals spent a lot of time this offseason working on an under center run game to get Brown more explosives, but that has gone for naught early on in the season. We may indeed see more Perine in Cincinnati’s running game after they return from the bye week, lowering Brown into the RB2 range.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.headline: Samaje Perine rushed 14 times for 68 yards in the Bengals’ Week 5 win over the Dolphins, adding 2 receptions for 10 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.analysis: Perine was involved heavily against the Dolphins, a surprising development given his lack of touches to open the season. He trailed Chase Brown by just five snaps on the day, getting involved in short-yardage situations and seeing an increase in red zone snaps after Brown’s red zone fumble in the second quarter. He caught a touchdown running a route out of the backfield and finished with 78 total yards. We don’t expect Perine to consistently see this kind of usage, but he is back on the radar as a deep-league FLEX value.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.headline: Samaje Perine rushed three times for seven yards in the Bengals’ Week 4 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.analysis: Perine only saw three touches on the day, though he had a rushing touchdown called back for holding in the second quarter. He has generally held a pass-catching role throughout his career but ceded all the backfield pass-catching opportunities to Chase Brown on the day. Perine remains a handcuff in the event of a Brown injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.headline: Samaje Perine rushed two times for six yards in Cincinnati’s Week 2 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.analysis: He added 16 yards on his only catch, making him the third-leading receiver for the game. Perine has 42 snaps in the first two games of the season and looks like a decent stash in case of a Chase Brown injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.headline: Samaje Perine rushed eight times for 42 yards in the Bengals’ Week 18 loss to the Browns, adding three catches for 10 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.analysis: Perine returned to Cincinnati on a two-year deal in the offseason. He easily took the RB2 gig over rookie Tahj Brooks and eventually parlayed that into a committee role. Perine didn’t log a single carry over the first two weeks but was stacking 10-touch games by November. He finished the year with 84 carries for 382 yards and three scores while adding 17 grabs for 87 yards. Perine was a staple of the RB4 ranks over the final two months of the year. He will likely keep his No. 2 role with the Bengals into the 2026 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.headline: Chase Brown rushed six times for six yards in the Bengals’ Week 11 loss to the Commanders, adding 30 yards on five receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.analysis: Brown saw minimal usage in the first half as the two teams played through driving rain, likely equal parts known tendencies as it was matchup-based. The bigger story here was the involvement of Samaje Perine, who did more than his standard change of pace role implied on his way to 97 total yards. There was no mention of injury or anything that would suggest Brown’s role was limited by necessity, likely best viewed as a small blip on the fantasy radar. Brown’s next opportunity to return a usable fantasy week comes in Week 12 against the Saints, where he will remain a fantasy RB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.headline: Chase Brown rushed 10 times for 44 yards in the Bengals’ Week 10 win over the Steelers, adding 39 yards and two touchdowns on eight receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.analysis: Brown continues to see a modest workload on the ground playing in the offense leading the league in pass rate over expectation while averaging almost 38 pass attempts per game. The pass game usage isn’t reliable on a weekly basis despite the veteran back seeing nine or more targets on three separate occasions this season. This was also his first game with a trip to the end zone since Week 1 despite working as a borderline workhorse this season, leaving Brown as an upside RB2 ahead of a Week 11 matchup against the pass-funnel Commanders, where he’ll likely require elite pass game utilization to return a usable score on that valuation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.headline: Chase Brown rushed nine times for 57 yards in the Bengals’ Week 9 win over the Falcons, adding three receptions for 18 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.analysis: While Brown struggled in Week 8, the silver lining was that he out-touched Samaje Perine 20-to-5. After fumbling against the Titans last week, Perine actually had more carries than Brown (11-to-9) in Madrid. Brown saw all three targets that went to running backs against the Falcons, but there’s no way to spin this positively for the 26-year-old who had a preseason ADP in the teens. Brown still hasn’t scored since Week 1 and he’ll be an RB2 at best against the Steelers in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.headline: Chase Brown rushed 12 times for 55 yards and a fumble in the Bengals’ Week 8 win over the Titans, adding eight receptions for 46 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.analysis: Brown saw most of his fantasy production come from the passing game, seeing nine targets in a pass-heavy game script. He fumbled on a handoff from Joe Burrow and also had a receiving touchdown called back for holding in the first half. Despite the dampened fantasy production, Brown saw most of the backfield opportunities for the Bengals, out-touching Samaje Perine 20-to-5. Brown’s production has been underwhelming the first half of the season but fantasy managers should hold tight given his large share of opportunities in pass-heavy game scripts. Brown’s production should regress to see more touchdowns the second half of the season. He is in the RB2 ranks for Week 9 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.headline: Chase Brown rushed 11 times for 39 yards in the Bengals’ Week 7 win over the Ravens, adding four receptions for 19 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.analysis: The Ravens held Brown in check both on the ground and through the air, with his longest play coming on an eight-yard reception. Even with the Bengals scoring 35 unanswered points in the second half alone, Brown was unable to find the end zone, and watched from the sidelines as Samaje Perine vultured a one-yard touchdown run from him down near the goal-line. Brown out-snapped Perine 7-to-3 in the red zone, but that won’t help fantasy managers much. This continues to be a tough season for Brown, who has just one touchdown on the year and has yet to surpass 82 yards from scrimmage in any game this season. He shouldn’t be considered as anything more than an RB2 next week against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.headline: Bengals OC Dan Pitcher said the team will “continually assess how that touch share between [Perine] and Chase Brown should play out.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.analysis: Pitcher suggested that when they run the ball more from shotgun — as they did last week against the Dolphins — Perine’s a better fit for those kinds of plays. The Bengals spent a lot of time this offseason working on an under center run game to get Brown more explosives, but that has gone for naught early on in the season. We may indeed see more Perine in Cincinnati’s running game after they return from the bye week, lowering Brown into the RB2 range.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.headline: Chase Brown rushed 13 times for 39 yards and a fumble in the Bengals’ Week 5 win over the Dolphins, adding 3 receptions for 21 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.analysis: Brown took a surprising backseat to Samaje Perine in the Bengals’ win over the Dolphins. He still out-snapped Perine 38-to-33, but a red zone fumble hurt his fantasy production while splitting backfield touches 50/50. There were a few snaps where Brown lined up as a receiver with Perine in the backfield; the Bengals used both backs heavily. Brown previously dominated all sorts of touches for the Bengals backfield, so this is a new development. Game script certainly played a factor but Brown’s ceiling as an RB1 may be considerably lessened if Perine’s usage sticks. He is a fantasy RB2 with a Week 7 matchup against the Ravens on the horizon after a Week 6 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.headline: Chase Brown rushed nine times for 10 yards in the Bengals’ Week 4 loss to the Jaguars, adding 11 receptions for 71 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.analysis: It was a big pass-catching day for Brown, who saw 11-of-54 total Bengals targets on the day. After Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) exited, Brown and Tee Higgins saw massive upticks in usage. Brown saw 57 backfield snaps, catching a series of checkdowns and wheel routes despite just 10 rushing yards on the day. He worked ahead of Samaje Perine on passing downs, a good sign for his fantasy production moving forward. We don’t expect Brown to consistently see this many targets but a high backfield share gives him a consistent fantasy floor. Brown is a fringe RB1 for Week 5 against the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.headline: Chase Brown rushed 13 times for 61 yards in the Bengals’ Week 3 loss to the Steelers, and two receptions for eight additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.analysis: Brown was effective with the opportunities he received, but the Bengals did all of their damage through the air in this one, as Joe Burrow and the company aimed to keep pace with a surprisingly explosive Steelers offense. As far as the Bengals’ backfield is concerned, Brown continues to be the only game in town. He handled 71.4 percent of the Bengals’ running back opportunities in this one but has only one touchdown to show for his efforts this season. He’ll be a fringe RB1/RB2 in next week’s game against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.headline: Chase Brown rushed 20 times for 80 yards in Cincinnati’s Week 2 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.analysis: He “added” three catches for two yards on five targets, getting absolutely exploded by Kamari Lassiter on one of them. He also had a 20-ish yard run called back for holding. Brown looked quick and able, but the Bengals ran just two plays inside the Texans red zone all game. He played on 42-of-60 snaps per PFF. Brown will be in the low-end RB1 ranks against the Steelers in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: Joe Burrow completed 28-of-40 passes for 300 yards and two touchdowns in the Bengals’ 22-20, Week 11 loss to the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: Burrow snapped a steak of five consecutive games in which he accounted for four or more touchdowns in the loss. He came into the game tied for the NFL record for consecutive games with four more touchdowns, ultimately unable to move into sole possession in game that played through driving rain throughout the first half. He leaned heavily on his running backs and tight ends against an aggressive Washington defense, feeding the two positions 24 targets on the evening. A defense that was able to stifle the Commanders in the first half allowed five consecutive scoring drives after the break, all of which were field goals, proving enough to send the Bengals to their third loss of the season. Now 7-3 and only one game ahead of the Browns and Steelers, the Bengals suddenly find themselves locked in one of the tighter divisional battles heading into the final two months of the regular season. Up next for Burrow and the Bengals are the Saints in Week 12, where Burrow will remain a top tier QB1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: Joe Burrow (illness) is practicing in full for Week 11 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: Burrow should be able to face the Commanders in this week’s Monday Night Football game without issue. Fortunately, his No. 2 wide receiver, Tee Higgins (knee), is also practicing in full this week. Burrow is an elite QB1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: Joe Burrow completed 35-of-44 passes for 409 yards and four touchdowns in the Bengals’ 38-18, Week 10 win over the Steelers, adding eight yards on one carry.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: Burrow cruised to his fifth consecutive game of four total touchdowns or more, passing for 302 yards and three scores in the first half alone. The Steelers were completely unable to move the ball consistently while managing only 23 yards of total offense through the first three quarters, allowing Burrow and the Bengals to build an insurmountable lead through the first 45 minutes of play. The win sends Cincinnati to the top of the AFC North with a 7-2 record after splitting the season series with the Steelers, now in the driver’s seat for the division title with two months remaining in the regular season. Burrow will look to keep the elite play going in a Week 11 meeting with the pass-funnel Commanders on Monday Night Football, where he remains a top tier QB1 in fantasy circles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: Joe Burrow completed 24-of-29 passes for 271 yards and three touchdowns in the Bengals’ 34-17 Week 9 win over the Falcons, adding three carries for seven yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: Burrow’s excellent run of play continued against the Falcons defense in Madrid in Week 9. The 29-year-old signal caller has amassed 16 passing touchdowns in the last four weeks and added two more touchdowns on the ground. Burrow’s production is unsurprisingly coming from playing through his top wide receivers as Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins combined for 187 yards receiving and all three receiving touchdowns against Atlanta. Burrow is likely to find himself on the shortlist for the MVP award the way things are going. He’s a locked in QB1 heading into a Week 10 matchup with the Steelers on Sunday Night Football, which airs on NBC and Peacock.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: Joe Burrow completed 38-of-48 passes for 462 yards, five touchdowns and three interceptions in the Bengals’ 43-36 win over the Titans, adding three carries for 10 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: Burrow and the Bengals passing offense started off slow, ending the first quarter scoreless. A first quarter interception from Burrow in Titans territory led to a Tennessee score the other way. He finished the half on a better note, tossing a 30-yard touchdown to Ja’Marr Chase and a one-yard score to Jack Endries. The second half saw many more possessions between both teams, with Burrow throwing two more interceptions to give the Titans increased opportunities. He was able to lead several scoring drives regardless, tossing three touchdowns in the second half and scrambling for the go-ahead touchdown in overtime. A high-scoring game script leads to very productive days for Burrow and the Bengals offense. Burrow profiles as a fantasy QB1 once again for Week 9 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: Joe Burrow completed 22-of-30 passes for 292 yards and four touchdowns in the Bengals’ 35-13, Week 7 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: After throwing for just 55 scoreless yards in the first half, Burrow and the Bengals came out firing on all cylinders in the second half. Trailing 13-0 at halftime, Burrow immediately orchestrated a nine-play, 66-yard drive that ended with a six-yard touchdown pass to Mike Gesicki, and followed that up with four more touchdown drives on his team’s next four possessions to jump out to a 35-13 lead. Burrow was as sharp as could be in the second half, completing 16-of-18 attempts while also completing two passes of 20-plus air yards. Burrow has now thrown four touchdowns in back-to-back games and has four multi-touchdown games this season. He’ll be on the QB1 radar next week when the Bengals play host to the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: Joe Burrow completed 23-of-32 passes for 190 yards and four touchdowns in the Bengals’ 31-24, Week 5 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: The Bengals offense mostly had a smooth-sailing day against the lackadaisical Dolphins defense. After a high-volume Week 4, Burrow threw 32 passes, tossing touchdowns to Mike Gesicki, Samaje Perine, and Tanner Hudson in the first half. He just missed Ja’Marr Chase for a 70-yard score in the second half, but later connected with Chase for a 45-yard score in the third quarter. Burrow was hardly under pressure and had plenty of time to make accurate throws and take deep shots against Miami. He is a fantasy QB1 heading into the Bengals’ bye and gets a middling defense in the Ravens for Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: Joe Burrow completed 39-of-54 passes for 428 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions in the Bengals’ 22-17, Week 4 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: The Bengals offense struggled to finish drives for much of this game, with Burrow throwing his first touchdown to Mike Gesicki in the third quarter. He also added a rushing touchdown on a fourth-quarter quarterback sneak. Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) leaving early didn’t help as Burrow threw two interceptions and nearly had a third. He threw one to Travis Hunter in the first quarter, though it was nullified by a roughing the passer penalty. He later threw one with under two minutes left in the first half, leading to a Jaguars score the other way. The final interception came in the fourth quarter in the red zone, ending a promising drive. Burrow made great plays under pressure, often finding Tee Higgins downfield. However, the interceptions proved to be back-breaking and the Bengals’ comeback attempt ultimately fell short. Burrow is a low-end fantasy QB1 for Week 5 against a soft Dolphins defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: Joe Burrow completed 28-of-37 passes for 281 yards and three touchdowns in the Bengals’ 30-27, Week 3 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: Burrow came out hot in this one, completing his first 14 passes while throwing a three-yard touchdown to Ja’Marr Chase on the Bengals’ opening drive. Burrow would throw his second touchdown of the day late in the second half when he connected with Tee Higgins for a 28-yard score and found Mike Gesicki 25 yards downfield on a fourth-and-two for his third touchdown of the day. Burrow led his offense on multiple long drives in this one, but with his team trailing 30-27 and driving late in the fourth quarter, he would cough up the ball on a strip-sack, which was recovered by Pittsburgh to seal the win for the Steelers. Burrow has attempted 30-plus passes in every game this season while throwing for six touchdowns to just one interception. He’ll be on the QB1 radar for next week’s game against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: Joe Burrow completed 20-of-31 passes for 207 yards and two touchdowns in Cincinnati’s 20-6, Week 2 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: Burrow was under pressure quite a bit in this one, as he took five sacks, but the Bengals were able to establish enough of a lead on a few incredible out-of-structure plays by Burrow that they took the air out of the ball in the middle of the third quarter. Both touchdown passes were to Ja’Marr Chase, the second as Burrow drifted out of his pocket to the right. It’s full-steam ahead in the QB1 tiers as Burrow heads to Pittsburgh in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Commanders declared CB Amik Robertson, QB Athan Kaliakmanis, RB Robert Henry Jr., Ricky Barber, and G Tanoa Togiai inactive for Week 11 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Commanders host one of the league’s hottest teams as they look to avoid falling further behind in the NFC East. They’ll need their defense to step up against a Bengals team averaging 36.2 points per game during their current five-game win streak.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Commanders waived DT Ricky Barber.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The second-year player is headed to waivers. The Commanders correspondingly promoted CB Isaac Yiadom to the active roster. Barber could be re-signed to the practice squad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Commanders signed WR Ja’Corey Brooks, CB Tre Hawkins, DE D.J. Johnson, WR Jacoby Jones, DE TJ Maguranyanga, S Rob McDaniel, T Tim McKay, CB Darius Rush, CB Car’lin Vigers, G Sala Aumavae-Laulu and DT Ricky Barber to reserve/future contracts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: In case you’re wondering, it’s not former Texans/Ravens wideout Jacoby Jones, but a wholly different Jacoby Jones who came out of UCF as an undrafted free agent in 2025. This Jones ran a 4.68s 40-yard-dash and is more of a special teamer who hangs around the roster. Glad we could clear that up for you. And us. But mainly you.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Former Western Kentucky redshirt freshman DL Ricky Barber Jr. transferred to UCF.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Barber Jr. (6'3/295) started every game last season, recording 51 tackles, 4.0 sacks, 27 hurries and one forced fumble, earning a strong PFF defensive grade of 80.2. A sure tackler, he only missed one potential tackle opportunity in 37 opportunities while recording 30 stops. He will be an immediate contributor on the defensive line for the Golden Knights and his presence will be sorely missed by WKU.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-dugge.headline: Bengals declared S Kyle Dugger, OL Myles Hinton, DL Landon Robinson, OL Dalton Risner, and TE Cam Grandy inactive for Week 11 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-dugge.analysis: No real surprises here as the Bengals look to continue their string of recent offensive production against an inferior Washington defense. Joe Burrow gets his full compliment of offensive skill position players minus Andre Iosivas, who remains on injured reserve through Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-dugge.headline: Andrei Iosivas (thumb) is doubtful to play in Week 10 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-dugge.analysis: Iosivas is still technically on injured reserve, although the team designated him to return this week. Fellow injured reserve players, CB Jalen Davis (hamstring) and OG Brian Parker (knee), are also listed as doubtful. Bengals S Kyle Dugger (quad) has been ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-dugge.headline: Bengals declared S Kyle Dugger, C Connor Lew, OT Myles Hinton, and DT Landon Robinson inactive for Week 9 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-dugge.analysis: The Bengals are surprisingly healthy headed into their date with the Falcons in Madrid, Spain. Dugger is the only one of their inactives who is out with an injury. The rest are healthy scratches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-dugge.headline: Bengals declared S Kyle Dugger, C Connor Lew, OT Myles Hinton, WR Mitch Tinsley, and DT Landon Robinson inactive for Week 8 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-dugge.analysis: Dugger is ruled out after not practicing all week due to a quad injury. The rest of the Bengals’ inactives consist of healthy scratches and they enter Week 8 against the Titans with a relatively clean bill of health.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-dugge.headline: Bengals signed S Kyle Dugger.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-dugge.analysis: Dugger was a full-time starter for years in New England before falling out of favor under new head coach Mike Vrabel, starting four of seven games before the Patriots traded him to the Steelers. Now the 30-year-old safety is on his way to Cincinnati, where he’ll presumably start once again. Dugger had 59 total tackles, five passes defended and two interceptions in 16 games (13 starts) in 2025.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-dugge.headline: Steelers acquired S Kyle Dugger and a 2026 seventh-round pick from the Patriots in exchange for a 2026 sixth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-dugge.analysis: The Patriots continue to deal defensive players that have fallen out of favor in their current scheme, sending Dugger to the Steelers just minutes after sending Keion White to the 49ers. Both deals were structured the same, with the Pats swapping late-round picks in exchange for giving up the defensive player. Dugger had started all 45 games played for the Patriots from 2022-2024, but started four out of seven games played this season. The veteran has nine career interceptions, 24 passes defended, and 25 tackles for loss over a six-year career. The Steelers had a need at safety with DeShon Elliott week-to-week due to a knee injury suffered in Week 8. Dugger will mix into a Steelers secondary that needs improvement if they are to make a playoff push.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-dugge.headline: Patriots declared DE Keion White, S Kyle Dugger, LB Caleb Murphy, DT Eric Gregory, OL Caedan Wallace, WR Efton Chism, and QB Tommy DeVito inactive for Week 8 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-dugge.analysis: Dugger is set to miss Week 8 with a knee issue that kept him limited in practice and landed him with a questionable tag heading into Sunday. Meanwhile, White is a surprise healthy scratch. Both White and Dugger could be on the trade block ahead of the November 4th trade deadline, but for now the Pats make both inactive against the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-dugge.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that the Patriots are “shopping” S Kyle Dugger.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-dugge.analysis: Rapoport’s report backs up what Jordan Schultz reported on August 20. The Patriots’ new coaching staff is hoping to move on from Dugger. Earlier today, ESPN’s Mike Reiss reported that it has been a “challenging year” for Dugger, who underwent offseason ankle surgery and has played “deep into preseason games” this month.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-dugge.headline: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports the Patriots are open to trading S Kyle Dugger.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-dugge.analysis: Schultz said the Patriots are keen on getting rid of Dugger ahead of the regular season, and are willing to eat part of his hefty contract to get a deal done. Dugger has been unhappy with his reduced role this offseason. There are several teams interested in acquiring Dugger, graded by Pro Football Focus in 2024 as the league’s fourth worst safety. Dugger last year allowed a completion on 79 percent of the passes that came his way. There’s a good chance he’s on another roster by Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-dugge.headline: The Athletic’s Chad Graff believes Patriots S Kyle Dugger “may not make the team.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-dugge.analysis: Dugger was playing deep into the fourth quarter with third-stringers in New England’s second preseason game, and he finished 2024 with a ghastly 34.8 PFF coverage grade — by far the worst of his five-year career. The Patriots wouldn’t get much cap relief from releasing Duggar, who is making $14.5 million a season, but Graff believes “they might do it anyway.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Seahawks placed RB George Holani (knee) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The move hurts far less than it would have earlier in the season when both Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price were unavailable. The change of pace option and special teams ace will now miss the next four games, at minimum, placing him in line to potentially return for Week 16 as the Seahawks make their final push toward the postseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports George Holani (knee) has an MCL sprain and is week-to-week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The “hope” is that Holani is not an IR candidate. His absence left Zach Charbonnet playing most of the third-down snaps yesterday, adding to his RB2 case going forward. Holani can be dropped in most leagues ahead of Seattle’s Week 11 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: George Holani (knee) has been ruled out in Week 10.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Holani picked up the knee injury in the first half against the Raiders and did not return. The Seattle rushing offense has revolved around Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price in recent weeks, leaving Holani out of the backfield fold. He can remain on waivers ahead of Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Seahawks ruled out Zach Charbonnet (knee) for Week 7 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald told reporters that Charbonnet has not suffered a setback. He just isn’t ready yet. Many teams might rush a player of his caliber back, now that he is practicing in full, but the Seahawks are smartly taking the long view with Charbonnet’s health. Emanuel Wilson will function as the team’s leading rusher while George Holani plays on passing downs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: George Holani rushed five times for 20 yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks’ Week 6 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Holani split primary change of pace duties with recent practice squad call-up Velus Jones Jr, the latter of whom turned four carries into 20 yards while losing one yard on his lone reception. Both backs appear unlikely to return fantasy value as Zach Charbonnet nears a return from injured reserve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: George Holani rushed four times for seven yards in the Seahawks’ Week 5 loss to the 49ers, adding four receptions for 24 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Holani put the ball on the turf twice in this one, but it was his fumble with 13 seconds left in the first half that proved to be one of the more costly mistakes of the game. With the Seahawks simply looking to get to halftime, Holani took a handoff from Sam Darnold for what should have been the final play of regulation. Instead, the third-year back had the ball knocked out and into his own end zone, which resulted in a Niners touchdown after it was recovered by DT Gracen Halton for the score. Holani hasn’t emerged as the late-round value fantasy managers hoped for this offseason and is fully off the fantasy radar for Week 6 against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: George Holani is active for Week 5 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Holani is good to go for Sunday’s game after entering the weekend as questionable. Holani rushed seven times for 18 scoreless yards last week and shouldn’t be relied on in any fantasy format this week. While Holani is active, the Seahawks declared QB Jalen Milroe, RB Robert Henry Jr., LB Chazz Surratt, WR Montorie Foster Jr., and TE Nick Kallerup inactive for Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Seahawks RB George Holani (ribs/knee) is questionable to play in Week 5 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Holani was nursing a ribs injury on Wednesday and Thursday, but he is now listed with a knee injury as well. This is concerning. He clearly picked up a new injury during the practice week. Velus Jones is the current RB3. Jones is not viable as a FLEX starter if Holani sits, but Emanuel Wilson should take on an RB2-worthy workload regardless.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Seahawks RB George Holani (ribs) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Holani should be good to go for the Seahawks’ Week 5 game against the 49ers, but he is certainly working through a decent little injury. The trusted passing game specialist should handle his normal workload, although he is only a touchdown-dependent PPR FLEX.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Seahawks RB George Holani (ribs) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Holani was listed as a limited practice participant due to a rib injury on Wednesday. The 26-year-old operated as a passing-down backup to Emanuel Wilson in Week 4 with Jadarian Price out. Unless he misses practice later this week, he is still on track to play in Week 5, though Holani does not have a large enough role to achieve fantasy relevance.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: Daniel Jones has cleared waivers and is now free to sign with any team.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: Now that he has passed through waivers, Jones is officially a free agent and is free to sign with any team. While plenty of QB-needy teams could reach out for his services, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported early Monday that Jones will likely wait to sign with a new team and may leave the door open to signing with a contender later in the season that suddenly finds itself in need of a starting QB.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said Daniel Jones could wait to sign with a new team if he goes unclaimed on waivers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: The belief is that Jones won’t be claimed on waivers, since any team that claims him would inherit his remaining contract with the Colts. Instead, Jones will likely pass through waivers and become a free agent, but he could delay signing with a new team immediately and instead opt to wait and see what other options may become available during the season. As Rapoport pointed out on Monday on NFL Network’s Good Morning Football, “someone, some playoff-ready team unfortunately is going to lose a quarterback at some point,” which could open the door for Jones to join a legitimate contender over the final stretch of the season and ahead of the playoffs. It was reported earlier that the Patriots and Ravens could be interested in Jones, but both teams would be on the outside looking in if the postseason began today. Jones struggled mightily in his second season with the Colts, throwing for 1,974-7-13 in 11 games, but he would likely be an upgrade over several teams’ backup QBs if a starter goes down.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Drake Maye (fractured fibula) is expected to miss at least six weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: A six-week absence would technically allow Maye to return late in the regular season, but Rapoport then followed up by saying he has an “outside chance” at playing if the Pats make the playoffs. We suspect the Patriots would, at most, use the final weeks of the regular season to get Maye back on the practice field. Tommy DeVito is currently their starting quarterback and they’re sitting at 5-5, so a playoff berth doesn’t appear to be in the cards. Rapoport also mentioned Daniel Jones as an option in Maye’s absence. We doubt he saves New England’s season, but he would be an upgrade over DeVito.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Ravens offered the Colts a fourth-round pick for Daniel Jones and a conditional fifth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: The fifth-round pick returned to the Colts if the Ravens made the playoffs. At worst, the Colts would have upgraded one of their Day Three picks. At best, they could have walked away with an extra fourth-round selection. They weren’t getting a king’s ransom for Jones, but it’s better than what they walked away with two weeks later when they cut him. The Colts’ mismanagement of the Jones situation will go down as a true blunder by a front office in disarray. Jones could still wind up in Baltimore as a free agent, assuming he clears waivers later this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter believes Daniel Jones will “draw interest” from the Patriots and Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: Schefter didn’t directly cite his sources on this, so he may just be connecting dots. Still, the two teams make loads of sense for the downtrodden quarterback. The Patriots are expected to be without Drake Maye for at least the rest of the regular season. At 5-5, they’re still in the hunt for a Wild Card bid, though their odds of making the postseason will all but disappear if Tommy DeVito remains their starting quarterback. The Ravens are in a similar spot, though they’ve already addressed the quarterback position via Jacoby Brissett. Schefter notes that the most likely outcome is that Jones waits for a more attractive spot to open up. He is expected to clear waivers later this week, at which point he will become an unrestricted free agent.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport believes the Patriots and Ravens are “potential landing spots” for Daniel Jones.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: Jones seemingly has decent odds of passing through waivers unclaimed, but he would be free to sign with any team after that. Rapoport adds that Jones is “still working his way back” from last year’s Achilles tendon rupture in his right, plant leg. Jones had a $10 million injury guarantee in his contract that is said to have been a factor in his release. Were he to sign with the Patriots, he could compete for the starting role with Tommy DeVito. Jacoby Brissett would probably be able to fend him off initially, were he to land in New England.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: ESPN’s Mike Reiss believes signing Daniel Jones could be an option for the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: Drake Maye has been diagnosed with a fractured fibula and is expected to be sidelined “deep” into the regular season. Tommy DeVito replaces him as the team’s starter. He is backed up by seventh-round rookie Behren Morton, who has reportedly “made a positive impression.” Jones has played poorly this year, prompting a surprise release earlier today. Despite the poor play, Jones still might be able to outplay DeVito and the late-Day 3 rookie. Assuming Jones passes through waivers, he could make sense as an affordable bridge option for the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: Colts waived QB Daniel Jones.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: Well, the Colts apparently evaluated everything, as they said they would last night. Wow. Jones makes it 11 games into a two-year, $88 million contract. He will be subject to waivers since the trade deadline has passed. It’s possible — though we’d be hard-pressed to say likely given the $2 million owed this season, $10 million next year and $38 million in non-guaranteed 2027 cash — that someone takes a chance on the deal. If not, he’ll be free to sign anywhere for the rest of the season. Minnesota would probably take a gamble on him again after they scooped him up in this same exact manner a few years ago, but that’s just speculation on our part. It’s stunning in the sense that it happened in-season, but this was obviously the way things had been trending as Indianapolis’ offense simply hasn’t been able to operate with Jones. Anthony Richardson will take over as the starting quarterback for the time being.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said he will “evaluate everything” at QB after Daniels Jones’ poor outing in Week 11’s loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: Steichen didn’t commit to Jones as the Colts’ Week 12 starter for next week’s game against the Giants. Anthony Richardson replaced Jones late in Thursday night’s loss to the Texans, but the Colts have been reluctant to bench Jones, despite a disastrous season in which he has thrown for 1,974 yards, seven touchdowns, and 13 interceptions. It feels like a switch to Richardson is inevitable at some point. With some extra time to prep him for next week’s game, now could be the time to make the move back to the former No. 4 overall pick.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: Daniel Jones completed 12-of-27 passes for 144 yards and an interception in the Colts’ 26-3, Week 11 loss to the Texans, adding three yards on one carry.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: Jones led the Colts to only 165 yards of total offense through almost 53 minutes of play against the Texans, also taking a sack in the end zone for a safety, before being replaced by Anthony Richardson with just over seven minutes remaining in the fourth quarter. This is the second game in the previous four weeks in which Richardson has come on in relief of an underperforming Jones in the fourth quarter. When you add that to the continuous questions fielded by head coach Shane Steichen surrounding the quarterback position moving forward, pressure appears to be mounting toward a potential change under center in a lost season. For what it’s worth, Richardson came on and immediately threw a pass that should have been intercepted during a quick three-and-out possession, which were the only three plays he ran as the Texans controlled the ball to run out the clock. Fantasy managers should not have held on for this long, but it is safe to say that Jones can be returned to the waiver wire from whence he came.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: The Denver Post’s Parker Gabriel reports RJ Harvey (IR/knee) is “widely expected” to practice when first eligible to come off injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harvey will miss Black Friday’s game against the Steelers, but it sounds like that might be the last one he misses. Jonah Coleman has established a fiefdom at the top of the depth chart in Harvey’s absence, so the second-year back doesn’t necessarily return to a major role in Week 13, but he may be worth picking up in deeper leagues if he was dropped.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Broncos placed RB RJ Harvey (knee) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Whoa, that escalated quickly. Harvey reportedly suffered a knee injury in practice this week that initially caused the Broncos to rule him out for Week 8, with the team then making the procedural move of placing him on injured reserve Saturday. Harvey will now miss the next four games, at minimum, as he rehabs the injury, leaving rookie Jonah Coleman and veteran J.K. Dobbins to handle primary backfield duties with Tyler Badie also on injured reserve. Coleman warrants weekly FLEX status, at minimum.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: RJ Harvey (knee) was ruled out for Week 8 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harvey was added to the injury report Thursday with a knee injury before being unable to practice Friday, ultimately ruled out for the team’s divisional clash against the Chiefs. Expect Jonah Coleman to serve as the primary rusher in addition to the possibility he sees his pass game involvement tick up in the absences of both Harvey and Tyler Badie, the latter of whom is on injured reserve. The increase in opportunity is enough to vault Coleman into viable FLEX territory for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: RJ Harvey (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harvey was added to the injury report Thursday after being limited in practice due to a knee injury, something fantasy managers will want to monitor as the weekend approaches. Either way, Harvey now has two healthy backs to compete with for touches with the return of Jonah Coleman in Week 7, keeping him on the fringes of FLEX consideration entering a difficult matchup against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: RJ Harvey caught two passes for 54 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 7 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harvey only ran the ball three times for six yards. Jonah Coleman, who was active for the first time since Week 2, ran nine times and also caught a pair of passes. Harvey’s role took a hit, but he made the most of his limited opportunities with a 52-yard screen in the third quarter. Sean Payton’s play-call schemed half of the Cardinals’ defense out of the play and Harvey blew by the other half on his way to the end zone. Despite the spike week for fantasy managers, Harvey’s declining role will have him tumbling down the running back ranks for Week 8. He will be on the RB3/4 border versus Kansas City next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Broncos designated Jonah Coleman (ankle) to return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Coleman can return to practice this week and the team now has 21 days to bring him off injured reserve. He could be back on the field as soon as Sunday. With the Broncos’ offense struggling and two backs already seeing work in the backfield, it’s hard to imagine Coleman having much fantasy value in his first game back. He’s worth stashing in deeper leagues, but it might be a while before fantasy managers want him in their lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: RJ Harvey rushed six times for 25 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 6 win over the Seahawks, adding 31 yards on three receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The fact that the 31 yards through the air led the team in receiving is a comment on the state of an offense that gained only 168 yards of total offense against the defending Super Bowl Champions. Even so, a relentlessly aggressive defense willed the team to victory behind a consistently positive game script, which allowed J.K. Dobbins to handily lead the backfield in opportunities. Harvey remains a matchup-dependent fantasy option best utilized in trailing game environments, which is unlikely to be the case when the Broncos face the struggling Cardinals in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: RJ Harvey picked up seven yards on three carries in the Broncos’ Week 5 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harvey was a non-factor in this one, and a week after his big receiving game, he was held without a catch with just one target. The second-year tailback was clearly the backup to JK Dobbins, and was unable to make the most of his limited opportunities. He’s off the radar for Week 6 versus the Seahawks on Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: JK Dobbins had 11 rushes for 40 yards in the Broncos’ Week 4 loss to the 49ers, adding two catches for 12 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Dobbins, as usual, led the Denver backfield in carries but lost out to RJ Harvey on pass routes and targets. In fact, Harvey led the Broncos with ten catches on ten targets in a check-down heavy game plan for Bo Nix and OC Davis Webb. Dobbins has been touchdown-reliant as the Broncos’ lead back, and sensitive to game script, as we saw in Week 4. Dobbins can be used as a flex next week against a vulnerable Chargers run defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: RJ Harvey had seven rushes for 25 yards in the Broncos’ Week 4 loss to the 49ers, adding ten catches for 68 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Playing against a 49ers defense allowing the league’s highest target share to running backs, Harvey led the Broncos in targets and receptions — thanks in part to negative game script that forced Denver to go pass heavy in the second half. It was a nice little PPR cheat code outing for Harvey, who now has 20 receptions in three games this year. JK Dobbins, meanwhile, led the Denver backfield with 11 rushes in Week 4. Harvey could be a PPR flex play next week against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-ralli.headline: Cardinals fired DC Nick Rallis.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-ralli.analysis: Rallis, whose unit had allowed 323 points in 11 weeks, more than anyone but the Raiders, will give way to interim DC Teryl Austin. Still just 33, there’s a chance the ultra-aggressive Rallis will get another opportunity in this post down the line. Weirdly, the defense hasn’t been the No. 1 problem area in Arizona lately — though that’s certainly more about quarterback attrition than anything — but it’s hard to say that Rallis ever produced a notably above-average unit in three-and-a-half years in the desert. The Cardinals best finish over that span was 14th in DVOA in 2024.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-ralli.headline: CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reports the Cardinals will retain DC Nick Rallis.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-ralli.analysis: The Cardinals’ defensive coordinator each of the past three seasons, 32-year-old Rallis was the youngest DC in the league when he was first hired three years ago. He’s had a rollercoaster ride in Arizona thus far, finishing bottom four in scoring defense two of the past three years. Discouraging, though former head coach Jonathan Gannon was largely responsible for his own defense. Rallis evidently impressed enough people inside the building to hang around under new head coach Mike LaFleur. It’s a gamble for a Cardinals team that arguably needed wholesale change, but also an olive branch to players who will at least now have one familiar face sticking around.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-ralli.headline: Cardinals hired Eagles LBs coach Nick Rallis as defensive coordinator.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-ralli.analysis: An up-and-comer on coach Nick Sirianni’s star-studded staff, Rallis has decided to follow Jonathan Gannon to the desert. At only 29 years old, Rallis will be the youngest coordinator, defensive or otherwise, in the entire league. A 2017 undrafted free agent out of Minnesota, Rallis immediately entered the coaching ranks. After one year at Wake Forest, he’s been in the NFL since 2018, and Philadelphia since 2021. It’s a gamble, but teams have been rewarded for going bold and young in the Sean McVay era.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Seth McGowan (hamstring) “will miss some time.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.analysis: McGowan exited in Week 11’s loss to the Texans and did not return to the game. The rookie seventh-rounder had been seeing an increased role as of late, rushing 26 times for 158 yards and two touchdowns in his last four games while adding two receptions. His absence should create a slight uptick in opportunities for Jonathan Taylor, who has had no more than 16 rush attempts in his last four games. We’ll likely get a better sense of how long McGowan could be out in the coming days, but for now, DJ Giddens appears next in line behind Taylor.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.headline: Seth McGowan (hamstring) is questionable to return to Week 11 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.analysis: McGowan pulled up lame following a kick return at the end of the first half and was deemed questionable to return when the two teams came out after the break. Jonathan Taylor appears to be in line to operate as a true workhorse for the remainder of the game after McGowan had carved out a meaningful role the previous two weeks. McGowan managed seven yards on three carries and caught his lone target for one yard prior to departing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.headline: The Athletic’s James Boyd believes Jonathan Taylor and Seth McGowan will see “heavy usage” in Week 11 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.analysis: A week after the Colts went ultra run-heavy in a win over the Dolphins — they were 9.3 percent below their expected pass rate — Boyd anticipates a similar approach on Thursday night against Houston. Taylor and McGowan over the past two games have split carries, 29-18, while Taylor takes on almost all the pass-catching work out of the backfield. “It doesn’t matter what I envision. It’s effective,” Taylor said of sharing the backfield workload with McGowan. “It helped us get a win. If we gotta win doing that and that’s what it takes, then I’m all for it. Seth has been growing each and every single day.” McGowan over the past two weeks has the highest EPA per rush in the NFL while Taylor ranks 44th. Unless the Colts face runaway negative game script against the Texans, look for McGowan to see around a dozen touches. Houston ranks 14th in running back fantasy points per opportunity allowed.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.headline: Seth McGowan rushed 12 times for 77 yards and a touchdown in the Colts’ Week 10 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.analysis: McGowan eclipsed his previous career-high with 12 carries in the Colts’ win. He continues to be involved, eating into Jonathan Taylor’s workload with a few red zone carries and a four-yard rushing touchdown to open the second quarter. McGowan was not involved in the passing game and Taylor still saw 23 more snaps. However, it seems like McGowan is here to stay as a playmaker for the Colts offense with a rushing score for the second straight game. He should be on fantasy rosters as a touchdown-dependent FLEX play for Week 11 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports the Colts won’t trade Jonathan Taylor before today’s trade deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.analysis: Multiple teams, per Pelissero, offered a second-round pick. It sounds like Indianapolis was holding out for a first. Playing out the season in Indy, Taylor will likely retain RB1 value despite a gross situation. It should be noted that Seth McGowan had begun to cut into Taylor’s playing time a bit, but with the Colts now committed to Taylor for the short-term, it’s plausible that he’ll operate at a 70-75 percent of snaps player for the remainder of the season. McGowan retains contingency value in fantasy leagues but will not stumble into a major role barring injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.headline: Seth McGowan rushed six times for 45 yards and a touchdown in the Colts’ Week 9 loss to the Cowboys, losing three yards on one reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.analysis: McGowan came on in relief of Jonathan Taylor on third-and-goal from the two late in the first quarter, cashing in on the opportunity for his first touchdown this season. a 36-yard scamper in the fourth quarter pushed his yards per carry mark to a healthy 7.5, dwarfing the 3.5 of Taylor. McGowan should not be on waiver wires ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline, with the looming possibility that Taylor has played his final snap for the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Jonathan Taylor remains on the Colts roster.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.analysis: Steichen mostly dodged questions about why the Colts would play Taylor in Week 9 if the team was in talks with contenders who might want to acquire the star running back before the NFL’s trade deadline. “Teams call all the time,” Steichen told reports. He said the team was focused on the Cowboys, their opponents in Week 9. Taylor seems more than likely to be dealt to another team in the coming weeks. That could be the Vikings, Bengals, Seahawks, or another contending team in need of backfield help.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.headline: Seth McGowan rushed five times for 29 yards in the Colts’ Week 8 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.analysis: McGowan actually out-gained Jonathan Taylor on the ground in a game the Colts trailed 28-0 at halftime and 42-7 heading into the fourth quarter. No. 3 back DJ Giddens was called upon for six carries, which he turned into 43 yards. Fantasy managers are stuck in a holding pattern as they await Taylor’s Colts fate ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline, but McGowan remains worth a speculative stash in most 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Colts are open to trading RB Jonathan Taylor.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.analysis: Multiple teams are interested in acquiring the 27-year-old Taylor and talks are active and ongoing, according to Schefter. The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reported that the Colts already turned down an offer for Taylor that included a 2027 second-round pick and another pick. While previous reports stated the Colts weren’t interested in trading Taylor, who signed an extension before the season, Indianapolis appears to be holding out for the best offer they can get. Taylor would see a slight boost in fantasy value if acquired by another team while Seth McGowan would likely take over the Colts’ backfield.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Jonathan Taylor has not requested a trade.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.analysis: The Colts this week dealt DeForest Buckner to the 49ers and Quenton Nelson to the Seahawks in what looks like a fire sale ahead of the NFL’s trade deadline. Taylor could be next if the Colts are ready to go all in on a rebuild in 2027 and beyond. A contender would likely have to part with a second round draft pick if they want Taylor in the coming weeks. Teams that could be suitors for Taylor include the Bengals, Vikings, and Seahawks, all of whom have backfield issues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rams head coach Sean McVay said Terrance Ferguson will undergo season-ending ankle surgery.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ferguson tried multiple times to make his way back from the ankle injury that has sidelined him since Week 3. Initially expected to return in Week 9, Ferguson suffered a hamstring injury in practice that further delayed his return, but it doesn’t sound like his ankle ever fully healed in light of today’s news. Ferguson’s season comes to an end after just three games. The second-year tight end turned in an impressive 6-54-1 line in Week 2 against the Giants, but saw just three targets over his other two games. The former second-round pick is an explosive playmaker with the ball in his hand and could make for an intriguing late-round pick in fantasy leagues next year once healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rams ruled out Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring) for Week 10 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ferguson is expected to be out for a couple of weeks, though the Rams are fortuitously on bye in Week 11. The rest of the Rams’ tight ends are in varying states of health. Colby Parkinson (ribs) will likely play through his injury again. Tyler Higbee (illness) and Davis Allen (oblique) did not practice on Thursday. Their game status has not been revealed.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring) did not practice in Wednesday’s walk-through.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ferguson was listed as a DNP for the Rams’ Wednesday walk-through. Rams head coach Sean McVay said earlier this week that Ferguson is likely out a couple week, so this comes as no surprise. Meanwhile, fellow tight ends Davis Allen (oblique) and Colby Parkinson (ribs) were both listed as limited participants. Allen and Parkinson are trending towards playing in Week 10 against the Cardinals, with Parkinson operating more as a pass-catcher and Allen as a blocker.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Speaking after Week 9’s win over the Commanders, Rams head coach Sean McVay said Terrance Ferguson (hamstring) will likely be out a “couple [of] weeks.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ferguson was set to return in Week 9 against the Commanders prior to suffering a pulled hamstring. According to McVay, the second-year tight end was going to be a “big part” of the Rams’ offensive game plan against the Commanders, which should be good news to fantasy managers still holding out hope for a return. Based on McVay’s comments, we can safely assume Ferguson won’t be playing in Week 10 against the Cardinals, and then the Rams head into their bye. If all goes well in his recovery, it’s possible he could return on a short week in Week 12 to play against the Packers, but we likely won’t have more clarity on that until after their bye. For now, Ferguson remains a worthwhile stash in leagues where you can afford to do so, but it’s hard to say with any confidence when we should expect him to be back on the field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rams ruled out Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring) for Week 9 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ferguson was set to make his return from injured reserve, having rehabilitated his early-season ankle injury. Unfortunately, he strained his hamstring in practice today and has now been ruled out. With Colby Parkinson (ribs) questionable, Tyler Higbee sneaks back into the TE1 conversation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rams HC Sean McVay told reporters that Terrance Ferguson (ankle) is expected to play in Week 9 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ferguson will be able to play for the first time since he suffered his medial ankle sprain in Week 3. The second-year tight end offers some volatility, but there’s no denying that there’s upside in his profile. Just don’t be shocked if it isn’t on full display just yet in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Terrance Ferguson (ankle) was spotted at practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ferguson had his 21-day practice window open up, and it’s a positive sign that he’s been able to practice on back-to-back days. There’s no guarantee he’ll play in Week 9 against the Commanders, but even if he misses that contest, it seems likely the second-year tight end will be back for the second half of the campaign.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rams opened Terrance Ferguson’s (ankle) 21-day practice window.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Rams coach Sean McVay told reporters that Ferguson will be limited today. The Rams could get their top receiving tight end back on the field this week, but they have slow-played his rehab thus far. It would be unsurprising to see him sit out this weekend. He should be added where available, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said Terrance Ferguson (ankle) will not be designated to return from injured reserve this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported last week that Ferguson’s return was still going to take “some time.” That doesn’t make it sound like he’s awfully close to getting back on the field. Tyler Higbee leads the Rams’ tight end room in routes since Ferguson went down, but his production has vanished over the past two weeks. Colby Parkinson scored in Week 6 and Davis Allen found the end zone twice last week. Higbee remains the best fantasy option of the bunch, but he’s nothing more than a low-end TE2 for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Terrance Ferguson (ankle) “will take some time” to come off injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ferguson is eligible to come off injured reserve next week, but Schefter reports that a source told him Ferguson’s recovery “will take some time.” The Rams placed Davante Adams on injured reserve this week and are in desperate need of pass-catching help behind Puka Nacua. Ferguson is a rising receiving tight end for the Rams, but has been on injured reserve since suffering an ankle injury in Week 3. Though he is a good IR stash for fantasy purposes, Ferguson is going to take longer than the minimum four weeks to return. Without a good timeline for return, he can be released from fantasy rosters in dire need of more immediate help during bye weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-lynch.headline: FOX Sports’ Jay Glazer reports the 49ers signed President of Football Operations and GM John Lynch to an extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-lynch.analysis: Lynch joined the Niners as general manager in 2017 and was promoted to President of Football Operations in 2023. Since his arrival, the Niners have emerged as one of the better-run organizations in the league. Under Lynch, the Niners have gone 91-68 in the regular season while making two trips to the Super Bowl and four trips to the NFC Championship Game.
