His selection of Brock Purdy as the final pick of the 2022 NFL Draft ended up giving head coach Kyle Shanahan his long-term QB of the future after previously failed attempts to address the position post Alex Smith and Colin Kaepernick, and in a season where the Niners have been dealt multiple injuries, specifically at receiver, San Francisco currently finds itself with a 9-1 record and three games ahead of the Seahawks and Rams in the NFC West. It’s a much-deserved extension for Lynch, who again has his team on track to make a deep run in the postseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-lynch.headline: NFL Network’s Tom Pelissero reports that the Dolphins, Saints, Browns and Jaguars have called the 49ers and other teams about trading up early in the second round.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-lynch.analysis: Pelissero echoed NFL insider Jordan Schultz’s phrasing from a report issued earlier today, saying it sounds like the 49ers are “very open” to fielding trade offers for the No. 33 overall pick. Pelissero mentions Ohio State DT Kayden McDonald, Washington WR Denzel Boston, Miami QB Carson Beck and Tennessee CBs Colton Hood and Jermod McCoy as possible targets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-lynch.headline: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports the 49ers “are considered ‘very open’ to moving back and continuing to acquire draft capital at (pick) No. 33.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-lynch.analysis: Schultz also reports that the Cardinals and Bills have “received calls about potential trades at the top of Round 2.” The Niners currently hold the first pick of the second round and enter the day with a total of eight picks left to make. They traded out of the first round on Thursday with the Jets, who used the 30th overall pick to select Indiana WR Omar Cooper Jr. In a draft that seems to lack notable talent after the first round, sliding back to acquire more picks could be a common theme on Day 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-lynch.headline: 49ers owner Jed York said 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan and general manager John Lynch are “not going anywhere.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-lynch.analysis: It’s the responsible move after the 49ers down year. The 49ers have been consistently messaging that nothing will happen, of course, but to get it straight from the owner’s mouth is notable. Shanahan has a career 70-61 record with the 49ers and has appeared in two Super Bowls while winning the division three times. The 49ers suffered an unfortunate run of bad injury luck this year and, with a fourth-place schedule, will probably be a good bet to rebound in 2025.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-lynch.headline: 49ers extended general manager John Lynch.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-lynch.analysis: The 49ers announced the extensions of Lynch and head coach Kyle Shanahan at the same time. Though Lynch has made a number of head-scratching picks in the draft, he has always found a way out of the holes he dug for himself. For Trey Lance, his most infamous pick that also featured a trade of multiple first-round selections, the life raft was hitting on Brock Purdy with the final pick in the draft. Lynch has also assembled an elite core of pass-catching weapons for Purdy with players tailored to his skill set and Kyle Shanahan’s scheme around every corner. A Super Bowl victory has eluded the duo for seven years, but they have been tantalizing close numerous times, including a Super Bowl berth and a pair of NFC Championship losses. Sitting at 3-0 to start the 2023 season, the hope will be that Purdy is just good enough to get the team over the hump.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-lynch.headline: The NFL announced the 2023 NFL Draft compensatory picks and the 49ers received three additional third-round picks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-lynch.analysis: The 49ers added No. 99, No. 101, and No. 102 overall while also being given picks in the fifth, sixth, and seventh rounds. Two of those third-round picks came from the Texans hiring DeMeco Ryans as head coach and the Titans hiring Ran Carthon as general manager. The Cardinals, Commanders, Browns, and Chiefs also added third-round picks, with the Patriots adding a fourth-round pick. The full list can be viewed in the link below.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-lynch.headline: 49ers GM John Lynch said he will continue to serve as the team’s general manager in 2023.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-lynch.analysis: Lynch had talks with Amazon to become an analyst for their Thursday Night Football programming last offseason. A deal never materialized and Lynch decided to return to the 49ers. His current contract runs through the 2024 season, though an extension could come as soon as this offseason. Having led the 49ers to three NFC Championships and a Super Bowl in the past four years, no one deserves a new deal more than Lynch right now. The only thing keeping him from re-upping with San Francisco for years to come is the allure of a cushy job on TV, though that won’t be happening this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-lynch.headline: The New York Post reports Amazon had talks with 49ers GM John Lynch for its Thursday Night Football package, but that it “did not lead to a deal.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-lynch.analysis: The tech colossus and football television neophyte is trying to throw money at its announcer problem — namely, it doesn’t have any — but could not lasso Troy Aikman and also struck out on Lynch. Talks with Al Michaels to serve as the play-by-play man have been at the “one-yard line,” but Michaels is reportedly waiting to see who his announcing partner might be. 50-year-old Lynch was delightful in the FOX booth before landing in the front office and will undoubtedly work in T.V. again one day.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-lynch.headline: When asked about the team’s trade for the No. 3 overall pick, 49ers GM John Lynch said Jimmy Garoppolo “likes competition.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-lynch.analysis: “We felt like we had a team that can compete,” Lynch said. “We went to ownership, said ‘hey things are looking good, we want to make this (trade), but we don’t want to say goodbye to Jimmy.’” Per Lynch, 49ers ownership signed off on keeping both a rookie and the 29-year-old veteran under contract for 2021. It confirms what was already known: the Niners will be adding someone under center at No. 3, and Garoppolo is in fact part of the team’s plans ... for now. (Coach Kyle Shanahan added that the team wouldn’t “rule out a trade” if they’re “absolutely blown away.”) Both Lynch and Shanahan are scheduled to be in attendance for Mac Jones’, Trey Lance’s, and Justin Fields’ (rescheduled) pro days.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-lynch.headline: 49ers promoted Adam Peters to assistant general manager.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-lynch.analysis: Peters, who was hired by the 49ers in 2017 as vice president of player personnel, is widely considered to be an up-and-coming general manager candidate. He’ll serve as the team’s assistant GM in 2021 alongside general manager John Lynch, who in a Friday statement called Peters a “tremendous asset” to the 49ers. Peters got his start as a scouting assistant for the Patriots in the early-2000s.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.headline: Panthers coach Dave Canales said Jalen Coker has cleared concussion protocol.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.analysis: Coker was checked in the fourth quarter after taking a hard hit from Roquan Smith, but it looks like he’ll be fine to use against the Buccaneers on Monday night. With all 32 teams active, it may be time to capitulate and put Coker back on the WR3 line. He has not cleared 50 yards since Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.headline: Jalen Coker caught 4-of-7 targets for 47 yards in the Panthers’ Week 11 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.analysis: Coker’s biggest play of the game came on a 35-yard reception in the first quarter, which precluded a 23-yard touchdown pass to tight end Mitchell Evans on the following play. Coker would muster just 12 yards on his other three catches, as he was used primarily in the short and intermediate areas of the field. He took a hard hit from Ravens LB Roquan Smith late in the fourth quarter and was placed in the league’s concussion protocol. Assuming he remains in the league’s concussion protocol on Monday, Coker will need to clear several hurdles if he hopes to suit up for Week 12 against the Buccaneers on Monday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.headline: Jalen Coker did not catch any of his four targets in the Panthers’ Week 10 win against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.analysis: Coker had one rush for three yards but was otherwise invisible. The usually pass-first Panthers went mega run-heavy against the Saints, limiting targets for every Carolina pass catcher. Coker, who ran a route on 33 of 36 Panthers drop backs, was seen yelling in frustration on the sideline in the second half. Coker has done almost nothing since his Week 1 explosion against the Bears. He has four or fewer receptions in five games this season. Coker will be a deep league flex in Week 11 against Baltimore.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.headline: Jalen Coker caught 4-of-5 targets for 29 yards in the Panthers’ Week 9 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.analysis: Coker is now really going through it over his past three games, managing just seven total catches for 74 yards and a touchdown. If there’s “good” news, it’s that it has been an offensive-wide slump in Carolina, not just Coker. He and everyone else has a premium Week 10 get-right spot in the Saints, though Coker is starting to look more like a WR3 than the WR2 he was showing out as earlier in the year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.headline: Jalen Coker caught 2-of-5 targets for 38 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 8 loss to the Packers while also losing a fumble.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.analysis: Coker’s fumble came on the last play of the game as the Panthers played pitchy woo woo in their attempt to tie the game. The 24-year-old didn’t have a catch in the first half, but salvaged his fantasy day — to a point, anyway — with a 26-yard touchdown from Bryce Young. The 24-year-old has just three catches over the last two games, and he’ll try and get things going against the Broncos in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.headline: Jalen Coker (shoulder) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 8 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.analysis: Coker was at little risk of missing tomorrow’s game after getting in a full practice on Tuesday. He was listed as a full participant again today before being cleared for action. Despite the quiet Week 7 showing, which saw Coker catch just one pass, fantasy managers should still treat him as a WR2 for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.headline: Jalen Coker (shoulder) practiced in full on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.analysis: Seems there’s little doubt that Coker will play on Thursday night. He’ll likely be removed from the injury report on Wednesday. Even after last week’s fiasco he likely belongs in the WR2 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.headline: Panthers listed Jalen Coker (shoulder) as limited on Monday’s estimated injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.analysis: The Panthers won’t have their first official practice until Tuesday, but Coker would have been limited on Monday had the team been on the field. Coker caught one pass for nine yards in Week 7’s loss to the Buccaneers. His struggles came on a day when the entire Panthers offense was stymied for much of the day, so hopefully he’ll be in line to bounce back against the Packers on Thursday if he is active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.headline: Jalen Coker caught 1-of-4 targets for nine yards in the Panthers’ Week 7 loss to the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.analysis: Coker was also the intended target on the first of Bryce Young’s two interceptions. The wideout fell down, leading to the miscue. It was simply a nightmarish day for the Panthers’ offense, who also watched Young cough up a fumble-six. With the Panthers trailing 33-6 at halftime and 43-6 at the 10:21 mark of the fourth, the first-team offense sat for the game’s final 10 minutes. A disaster for fantasy managers, but likely a short-lived one with the Panthers heading to Green Bay for a short-week Thursday night matchup with the Pack. Coker must still be fired up as a WR2 for that one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.headline: Jalen Coker caught 6-of-13 passes for 97 yards in the Panthers’ Week 6 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.analysis: Coker missed Week 4 with a quad injury but was able to heal up over the bye week and play a full complement of snaps in Week 6. Initial reports had him playing 59 of the team’s 79 snaps and running a route on 39 of 46 dropbacks, which was second most on the team. He also led the team in targets, catches, and receiving yards. He’s a rock-solid WR2 against the Bucs next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-devi.headline: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said “Tommy [DeVito is] our starter” when asked if the team plans to add a QB in the coming days.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-devi.analysis: After news broke last week of Drake Maye’s injury and impending absence of six-plus weeks, it was reported that the Patriots could explore QB options outside the building to take over for the Pats’ QB1. The recent release of Daniel Jones by the Colts makes that subject all the more interesting, but Vrabel, at least for now, seems committed to 28-year-old DeVito, who is set to make his first start as a Patriot in Week 12 against the Chargers. Vrabel praised DeVito for the improved play he showed in training camp and the preseason and expressed confidence in him to lead the offense and run the huddle. DeVito hasn’t started a game since the 2024 season with the Giants and has a career passing line of 1,490-9-4 in 15 career games. He threw for 81 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in relief if Maye in Week 10, but will be hard to trust as anything more than a desperation play in 2QB/Superflex leagues next week against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-devi.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Drake Maye (fractured fibula) is expected to miss at least six weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-devi.analysis: A six-week absence would technically allow Maye to return late in the regular season, but Rapoport then followed up by saying he has an “outside chance” at playing if the Pats make the playoffs. We suspect the Patriots would, at most, use the final weeks of the regular season to get Maye back on the practice field. Tommy DeVito is currently their starting quarterback and they’re sitting at 5-5, so a playoff berth doesn’t appear to be in the cards. Rapoport also mentioned Daniel Jones as an option in Maye’s absence. We doubt he saves New England’s season, but he would be an upgrade over DeVito.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-devi.headline: ESPN’s Mike Reiss believes signing Daniel Jones could be an option for the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-devi.analysis: Drake Maye has been diagnosed with a fractured fibula and is expected to be sidelined “deep” into the regular season. Tommy DeVito replaces him as the team’s starter. He is backed up by seventh-round rookie Behren Morton, who has reportedly “made a positive impression.” Jones has played poorly this year, prompting a surprise release earlier today. Despite the poor play, Jones still might be able to outplay DeVito and the late-Day 3 rookie. Assuming Jones passes through waivers, he could make sense as an affordable bridge option for the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-devi.headline: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports the Patriots “are expected to explore the QB market during the bye week.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-devi.analysis: According to Schultz, the Patriots could look into free agents like Jimmy Garoppolo and may also consider signing a QB from a team’s practice squad. Garoppolo, who last threw a regular-season pass in Week 18 of the 2024 season, worked with offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels from 2014 to 2017 during their time together in New England, and also spent the 2023 season with McDaniels during a brief stint with the Raiders. It’s hard to imagine Garoppolo coming off the couch to save the Patriots’ season, but he could offer a little more upside than Tommy DeVito did in relief of Drake Maye during Sunday’s loss to the Lions. For now, DeVito is expected to start in Week 12 when the Patriots return from their bye, but it wouldn’t be surprising if they considered an upgrade. Head coach Mike Vrabel said later that the team will “have conversations” about the possibility of bringing in outside help, but said he’s “ excited for the challenge ” of seeing what the team can do with DeVito under center.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-devi.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Drake Maye is believed to have suffered a fractured ankle in Week 10’s loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-devi.analysis: According to Schefter, Maye stayed overnight in Germany to undergo testing and determine whether or not he would need surgery. For now, Maye is out indefinitely, but the 24-year-old QB and 2025 MVP runner-up could be looking at missing the rest of the season for the now 5-5 Patriots. His absence would force the Patriots to start Tommy DeVito in Week 12 against the Chargers, which would all but spell disaster for all Patriots skill players from a fantasy perspective. DeVito completed 12-of-24 passes for 81 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in Sunday’s loss and has a career passing line of 1,450-9-4 in 15 career games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-devi.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports it’s “possible” Drake Maye (lower leg) misses the rest of the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-devi.analysis: Per Rapoport, Maye suffered a “significant lower leg injury that will keep him out an extended period of time.” It’s devastating news for Patriots fans and fantasy managers. While Maye has had his ups and downs this year, the team was nonfunctional without him on Sunday. Tommy DeVito took over for an injured Maye early in the first quarter and threw for 81 yards at 3.4 yards per attempt. The Pats also have seventh-round rookie Behren Morton on the roster. We suspect DeVito will get another shot at the starting job, but it wouldn’t be surprising to see Morton under center at some point this year. With A.J. Brown also banged up and Romeo Doubs still on IR, the Pats are shaping up to be a fantasy wasteland over the second half of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-devi.headline: Tommy DeVito completed 12-of-24 passes for 81 yards, a touchdown, and an interception in the Patriots’ 35-10, Week 10 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-devi.analysis: DeVito took over for an injured Drake Maye in the first quarter. He could not get anything going despite facing a Detroit defense that has been extremely beatable this year. DeVito threw a ghastly interception right at Roger McCreary late in the second quarter. He had Kyle Williams wide open for a touchdown but didn’t see him sprinting down the field uncovered. DeVito did eventually find the end zone on a check-down to Lan Larison late in the fourth quarter. DeVito would be the next man up if Drake Maye isn’t healthy after New England’s Week 11 bye, though we hope it doesn’t come to that.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-devi.headline: Drake Maye (ankle) will not return in Week 10 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-devi.analysis: Aidan Hutchinson hip-drop tackled Maye for a sack early in the first quarter. Maye limped off the field and made his way to the locker room shortly after going down. He was initially listed as questionable to return but has since been downgraded to out. A dreaded high-ankle sprain appears to be on the table right now. The good news is that the Patriots get their bye next week, which will give Maye some extra time to recover. Tommy DeVito will close out Week 10 under center.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-devi.headline: Patriots re-signed QB Tommy DeVito to a two-year, $7.4 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-devi.analysis: DeVito spent all of last season with the Patriots but never took a snap for the team. The former UDFA served as the team’s QB3 behind Joshua Dobbs and will likely have a chance to compete with Dobbs for the team’s QB2 spot now that both are slated to return in 2026. For his career, DeVito has thrown for 1,358-8-3 on 222 passes while completing 65.3 percent of his attempts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-devi.headline: Patriots declared WR Efton Chism, CB Kobee Minor, OLB Bradyn Swinson, OT Marcus Bryant, G Caedan Wallace, TE C.J. Dippre and QB Tommy DeVito inactive for Super Bowl LX against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-devi.analysis: Chism, an undrafted free agent rookie, was active in the Divisional Round and Wild Card Round but did not play in the AFC Championship Game. He caught 3-of-3 targets for 75 yards and one touchdown in the regular season and caught his lone postseason target for a 20-yard gain. DeVito will serve as the Patriots’ emergency third quarterback today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said “as of today” Malik Willis’ groin injury will not require surgery.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: It sounds like this is subject to change, as Hafley also added that Willis will “be re-evaluated at the four-week mark” of his absence to see where things stand. Willis has already spent two weeks on injured reserve and will need to miss at least two more games before the Dolphins could consider bringing him back in Week 14 against the Bears. Kyle McCord has struggled in his two starts, completing 44.6 percent of his passes while throwing for 311-0-1, and will be under center again in Week 12 against the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said Malik Willis (groin) is not having surgery at this time but a final decision has not been made on if he’ll have it.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: “We’ll see how he feels,” Hafley said. “If he needs surgery, he will have surgery.” Well, hard to make it less complex than that. Willis is definitely out for the next three games and it sounds like there’s at least a reasonable chance he’ll be done for the season. In the meantime, Kyle McCord will play the role of bottom-five superflex starter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said he hopes Malik Willis (groin) can return this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Hafley told reporters on Wednesday that Willis would seek second opinions on the groin injury that landed him on injured reserve. It sounds like season-ending surgery is a possibility for Willis, who would end his 2026 campaign. Through Week 9, Willis ranks 26th in passing yardage and 29th in passing touchdowns. He’s dead last in EPA per pass attempt and ranks 28th out of 38 qualifying QBs in EPA per drop back. Kyle McCord will get a chance at quarterback for the Dolphins in Week 10 against the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Dolphins placed Malik Willis (groin) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: He had clearly been laboring since the bye week and this will give Willis some time to heal. This is not regarded as a season-ending injury and Willis will be eligible to return in Week 14. In the mean time, it appears we’re all about to see how well the roster cutdown Kyle McCord trade works out for the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis completed 13-of-25 passes for 128 yards and an interception in the Dolphins’ 19-9, Week 9 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Willis only added seven yards on two carries. He was on the injury report with a groin injury this week. Despite practicing in full three times, Willis appeared to be severely limited by the issue. He turned down several opportunities to scramble, instead opting to throw the ball away when the Lions’ pass-rush got close. Without the rushing production to bail him out of tough spots, the offense collapsed despite facing one of the league’s worst defenses. His passing output was already weak, but a lack of rush attempts will pull him out of the QB2 ranks entirely. He will be downgraded to a low-end QB2 for his Week 10 matchup with the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis (groin) is practicing in full for Week 9 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Willis did the same during Week 8 practices and ended up running just once against the Patriots. Hopefully, the groin injury continues to improve and his rushing usage returns. Willis remains a QB2 this week against the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis completed 21-of-32 passes for 211 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in the Dolphins’ 19-24, Week 8 loss to the Patriots, adding one rush for two yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Willis practiced in full this week despite being listed with a groin injury. Perhaps the soft tissue issue made him play a little more restrained than we would have liked him to. The Dolphins’ quarterback continues to hold the ball too long. He took five sacks today. His interception was not totally his fault. He was hit by a pass rusher, altering the pass’s trajectory, which bounced off a defensive lineman’s helmet before flying 29 yards downfield, where a Patriots defender picked it off. Willis had another interception called back due to defensive offsides, which was lucky. The Dolphins’ young wide receivers are learning the ropes and could help him churn out usable fantasy line as the season progresses. Willis will be a high-end QB2 against the Lions in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis (groin) is practicing in full for Week 8 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: While we are happy to see Willis practicing in full, we are slightly unhappy to see that he has a new injury. The Dolphins’ quarterback has already dealt with toe and right thumb injuries this season. Willis remains a viable QB2 starter against the Patriots, but this is worth monitoring.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis completed 14-of-21 passes for 208 yards and two touchdowns in the Dolphins’ 28-28, Week 7 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Willis also added 37 yards and a touchdown on eight rush attempts. It was, by far, his best performance as a Dolphin. It was also the first win for both Willis and first-year head coach Jeff Hafley. Willis picked apart the Jets for chunk play after chunk play. His biggest play of the day was a 63-yard completion to Caleb Douglas, though nearly all of those yards came after the catch. He had already connected with Douglas earlier in the game for his first touchdown of the day. Things will be a lot tougher for Willis and the Miami offense when they take on the Patriots next week. Despite the strong showing today, Willis will remain buried in the QB2 ranks for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis (right thumb) is practicing in full for Week 7 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: ESPN’s Marcel Louis-Jacques reports that Willis received treatment for his thumb injury on his right, throwing hand, though he did not share what exactly the injury is. Hopefully, it is nothing serious. If his ball placement is impacted, the Jets’ D/ST would benefit. Willis is a volatile QB2 against them this week. Willis underwent surgery on his left thumb in August 2025.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: Ja’Kobi Lane was not targeted in the Ravens’ Week 11 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: After seeing a season-high 11 targets in Week 10’s loss to the Chargers, Lane went on to donut in Sunday’s loss to the Panthers. The rookie’s lack of targets wasn’t due to a shortage of playing time, as his 23 routes run were good for third most of any Ravens receiver, but the ball simply wasn’t finding him. With all 32 teams playing in Week 12, fantasy managers shouldn’t trust Lane in any capacity next week against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: Ja’Kobi Lane caught 3-of-11 targets for 61 yards in the Ravens’ Week 10 loss to the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: Lane handily led the team with 11 targets but struggled through inconsistent play, the most glaring of which came on a drop on a routine target inside the five. It won’t be often that lane leads the team in targets while playing alongside Zay Flowers and the recent resurgence of tight end Mark Andrews, the latter of whom should benefit greatly from the historically high tight end target rate from new quarterback Jacoby Brissett. Lane is an upside Flex ahead of a Week 11 meeting with the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: Ja’Kobi Lane caught his lone target for 13 yards in the Ravens’ Week 8 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: Lane hauled in a 13-yard reception from Joe Fagnano in the second quarter after Fagnano came in to replace Tyler Huntley (toe). Lane has yet to live up to the training camp hype he drew all offseason and seems even less likely to hit his stride with Lamar Jackson’s (thumb) in jeopardy. Fantasy managers stashing Lane in deeper leagues can move to drop him at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: Ja’Kobi Lane caught 3-of-5 targets for 25 yards in the Ravens’ Week 7 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: Lane had a relatively forgettable day through the air, but just missed finding the end zone on a short pass from Tyler Huntley in the second quarter. The rookie receiver ran 30 routes, which were second only to Zay Flowers, but he’s caught just seven passes for 65 scoreless yards in his two games since returning from injury. Lane’s involvement in the offense is encouraging, but there’s not enough here to warrant starting him in Week 8 against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: Ja’Kobi Lane caught 4-of-5 targets for 40 yards in the Ravens’ Week 6 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: Lane was immediately involved in the offense after missing the previous four weeks with a wrist injury. The rookie third-rounder caught two of his four passes on the Ravens’ opening drive that ended with a short touchdown pass to Josh Cuevas and ran 22 routes on the day. Zay Flowers (34) and Devontez Walker (26) both ran more routes than Lane on the afternoon, but Lane has been targeted on 21.1 percent of his routes in limited action this season. Fantasy managers shouldn’t be looking to start him in Week 7 against the Bengals, but the early volume is encouraging for a player who was hyped up throughout training camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Ravens WR Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) is “good to go” and should be activated for Week 6 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: While nothing is official yet, Lane practiced in full all week, which is another good sign for his availability against the Browns this weekend. Lane was one of the most impressive rookies this offseason and preseason. Rashod Bateman isn’t on the injury report, but missed practice during the week with a shoulder. Lane could conceivably operate as the second option in the Ravens passing game behind Zay Flowers as early as this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) is questionable for Baltimore’s Week 6 game against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: Lane practiced in full all week, lending credence to the idea that he’ll be activated. Ravens coach Jesse Minter stopped short of saying Lane would play when given a chance, saying they’d “figure that out,” but said he had a great week of practice.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: Bateman played through the shoulder injury last week. He was limited yesterday, but coach Jesse Minter said he wasn’t worried. Downgrading to a DNP is not a good sign. Meanwhile, Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) is practicing fully this week and could hop right into WR2 duties for the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: Earlier today, NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reported that Lane has “a shot” to face the Browns in Week 6. His full participation furthers that notion. The talented rookie drew rave reports all summer before suffering an unfortunate wrist fracture in Week 1. While he makes for a dicey FLEX if Tyler Huntley is under center, Lane should at least be safely stashed on fantasy football benches in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) has “a shot” to play in Week 6.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said Lane, who injured his wrist in the season opener against the Colts, will return to practice this week and could suit up this weekend against the Browns. Lane had impressed Ravens coaches and beat writers through training camp and in Week 1 he caught one of three targets for 11 yards before exiting with the wrist injury. Lane’s return to the Baltimore lineup could limit snaps and routes for Rashod Bateman Devontez Walker. Lane should be picked up in 14-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.headline: Deebo Samuel caught 3-of-4 targets for 20 yards in the 49ers’ Week 11 win over the Vikings, adding 27 yards on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.analysis: Samuel continued to operate as the primary gadget player for a 49ers team now with Christian McCaffrey, Mike Evans, and George Kittle all fully healthy. While that role carries per-touch upside given the space he should have when receiving the ball, fantasy managers are likely forced to view Samuel more as a potential Flex than a viable weekly starter. That will remain true ahead of a Week 12 meeting with the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.headline: Deebo Samuel caught 3-of-3 targets for 31 yards and a touchdown, adding three carries for 78 yards and one touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.analysis: Samuel, 30, turned back the clock to score not one, but two touchdowns in the Niners’ route of the Cowboys. Samuel would find the end zone on an 11-yard bubble screen in the first quarter to give the Niners their first points of the day. Then, in the third quarter, Samuel took an end around 70 yards upfield for a touchdown, and at one point had to walk a tightrope along the sidelines to stay in bounds before finding a clear path to the end zone. The run set a new career-high for Samuel, whose previous long was a 51-yard run back in 2022. Things went about as well as they could have for Samuel, who was playing in his first game since Week 5. Despite the strong outing, Samuel has averaged just 6.0 opportunities per game in his last three games, and his three targets in this one tied Jordan Watkins for fourth-most on the team. Fantasy managers shouldn’t view him as anything more than a WR4 next week against the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.headline: Deebo Samuel (hamstring) is not on the 49ers’ final injury report and will play in Week 10 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.analysis: The 49ers could end up limiting Samuel’s snaps in his first game back, but when he is on the field, he will likely be treated as the team’s No. 1 wide receiver. Samuel should be in fantasy football lineups as a WR3 with decent upside in what is expected to be a high-scoring game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.headline: Deebo Samuel (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.analysis: Samuel is still stuck in the questionable column, but his continued participation tentatively puts him on track to play in a fantasy-friendly matchup against the Cowboys in Week 10. If active, Samuel could end up serving as the 49ers’ No. 1 wide receiver. He would warrant WR3 treatment in this scenario.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.headline: Deebo Samuel (hamstring) will resume practicing in a limited capacity on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.analysis: Samuel now has a chance to play in Week 10 against the Cowboys’ fantasy-friendly defense. The 49ers could play things cautiously and give him more time off, but an early-week return is usually a good sign. With much of the 49ers’ pass-catching corps still banged up, Samuel could return to a WR3/flex-worthy workload right away. He should be added wherever he is available. Samuel later told reporters that he feels “ready” to play on game day.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.headline: 49ers ruled out Deebo Samuel (hamstring) for Week 9 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.analysis: Samuel, Mike Evans (Achilles) and Christian Kirk (knee) are all sidelined, potentially leaving Demarcus Robinson (ankle) as a featured receiver if he can play. Samuel can continue to be stashed on benches in 12-team leagues, though his return timeline remains somewhat opaque.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.headline: Deebo Samuel (hamstring) was not seen at Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.analysis: Neither Samuel nor Mike Evans (Achilles) was seen at the practice, and the same goes for Christian Kirk (knee). Kirk still has a chance to play, but it seems very unlikely that Brock Purdy will have Samuel lined out wide for Week 9 against the Raiders. His next chance to play will be Week 10 against the Cowboys, barring something unforeseeable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.headline: 49ers GM John Lynch said it’s likely that Deebo Samuel (hamstring) will not play in Week 9 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.analysis: Lynch said the same about Mike Evans. Samuel hasn’t played or practiced since going down with a hamstring injury in Week 5. It’s unclear when he will return to the field. The fact that the 49ers didn’t place him on injured reserve when he suffered the injury suggests they expected him to miss fewer than four games. Week 9 will be his third absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.headline: Deebo Samuel (hamstring) will not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.analysis: Samuel remains sidelined by his Week 5 hamstring strain. He still has a chance to resume practicing in time to face the Raiders this weekend, but it would have been nice to see him take the field today. The 49ers were on bye in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.headline: 49ers declared DE Nick Bosa, WR Mike Evans, WR Deebo Samuel, LB Luke Gifford, LB Garret Wallow, S Marques Sigle, and QB Kurtis Rourke inactive for Week 7 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.analysis: None of these comes as a surprise. All of Bosa, Evans, and Samuel were already ruled out earlier in the week, and Sigle has missed multiple weeks with an ankle injury. Brandin Cooks and Christian Kirk are likely to lead the 49ers’ pass catchers against the Falcons this week, and both are worth adding in deeper formats in case either emerges as a legit weapon while Evans (Achilles) and Samuel (hamstring) are sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: George Kittle caught all three passes for 34 yards and two touchdowns in the 49ers’ Week 11 win over the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: Kittle got to work early, capping off the opening drive with a touchdown from 17 yards out before adding a second touchdown early in the second quarter. The team would score again on their subsequent possession before the defense tacked on a pick-six on the following play, capping passing volume and leading to the low target total for the veteran tight end in the process. Even so, Kittle continued to showcase his elite athleticism, body control, and strength on his two scores and remains a surefire TE1 heading into another difficult matchup against the Seahawks in Week 12.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: George Kittle caught 6-of-9 targets for 74 yards in the 49ers’ Week 10 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: Kittle’s nine targets led all Niners players in this one. His 20-yard touchdown on the Niners’ opening drive set Deebo Samuel up nicely for an 11-yard touchdown on a screen pass on the following play, and in the fourth quarter, Kittle caught a 10-yard pass to move into the Cowboys’ red zone and positioned Christian McCaffrey for a 16-yard touchdown run soon after. Kittle continues to impress in his return from a late-season Achilles injury. He has gone for 58 or more yards in four straight games while averaging 8.5 targets per game over that span. He draws a tough Week 11 matchup against the Vikings, but will still profile as a low-end TE1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: George Kittle caught 4-of-7 targets for 58 yards in the 49ers’ Week 9 win against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: It was a fairly low volume day for Brock Purdy and the Niners passing offense. The team had 25 pass attempts to 34 designed rushes against a miserable Vegas defense. Kittle ran a route on 28 of the team’s 32 drop backs and led the Niners with seven targets. His biggest play came on a patented catch and run through the Vegas secondary — one of a few long YAC plays for the San Francisco offense. Kittle should remain in all lineups next week against a porous Dallas coverage unit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: George Kittle caught 8-of-10 passes for 88 yards in the 49ers’ Week 7 loss to the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: Unfortunately, Kittle also lost a fumble on the team’s final drive of the game as he was trying to earn extra yardage and set the team up for a better shot at the end zone. Even with that mistake, Kittle was tremendous on the day and the clear top option in the passing attack. The 49ers will be on a bye in Week 8, and then some of their injured receiving corps should return in Week 9, which might impact Kittle’s usage a bit. He will remain a rock-solid TE1 in fantasy leagues though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: George Kittle caught 5-of-8 targets for 69 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 6 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: Kittle got the scoring started with an 11-yard touchdown on a dime from Brock Purdy to the corner of the end zone, contributing to the offense steadily through a dominant first half before pushing his yardage totals with a 35-yard reception to start the third quarter. It was a tale of two halves for the San Francisco offense, which managed a staggering 303 yards of total offense in the first half and only 72 yards of total offense after the break, likely heavily influenced by the departure of Mike Evans at the end of the second quarter. Evans is expected to miss the team’s Week 7 contest against the Falcons, where Kittle could step into additional volume in his already-solid TE1 profile.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: George Kittle caught 5-of-6 targets for 24 yards in the 49ers’ Week 5 win over the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: After three straight big weeks, Kittle finally came back down to earth in Sunday’s win over the Seahawks. His longest reception came on a 13-yard gain in the third quarter, but proved inconsequential after Deebo Samuel lost a fumble on the following play to end the drive. Kittle has been targeted 19 times over the last three weeks and has gone for 70-plus yards in three of his last four games. He should be primed for a bounce-back next week when the Niners play host to the Commanders on Monday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: George Kittle (illness) is active for Week 5 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: It was reported earlier on Sunday that Kittle was dealing with an illness, but that he was still expecting to play. Kittle was not listed with the 49ers’ inactives when the team announced them 90 minutes before kickoff, meaning he is good to go and can be treated as a TE1 as usual.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: George Kittle caught 4-of-6 targets for 70 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 4 win against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: It was a quiet day for Kittle before a fourth quarter screen pass went for a 58-yard score that sealed the game for the Niners. Displaying explosiveness less than a year after tearing his Achilles tendon, Kittle outran the Broncos secondary for his second touchdown in as many weeks. His six looks from Brock Purdy was second most among Niners pass catcher, trailing only Mike Evans (eight targets). Kittle’s big play upside and his role in the red zone make him a potential matchup flipper in fantasy. He gets the Seahawks in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: George Kittle caught 6-of-7 targets for 82 yards and two touchdowns in the 49ers’ Week 3 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: Kittle saw a season-high seven targets in the 49ers’ win, becoming the team’s No. 1 pass-catcher after Mike Evans (rib) left the game. He caught a 10-yard touchdown at the start of the fourth quarter and later sealed the win with a 20-yard score with under two minutes left. Kittle seems to be all the way back from his Achilles tear, leading all 49ers offensive skill players in snaps, only trailing Brock Purdy and the offensive line. With Evans’ status in the air, Kittle is the team’s top receiver and is squarely in the fantasy TE1 conversation for Week 4 against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: 49ers ruled out WR Demarcus Robinson (ankle) for Week 3 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: This was the expected outcome for Week 3. Reports on Robinson’s injury indicate this could be a multi-week issue. With WR1 Mike Evans (hip) questionable, WR Deebo Samuel and TE George Kittle could take on sizable workloads, though the team will likely still try to limit Kittle’s snap count.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: Keenan Allen caught 3-of-4 targets for 38 yards in the 49ers’ Week 11 win over the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: Allen was hardly used in the first half as George Kittle and Mike Evans did all the heavy lifting but came alive in the third quarter to get his name in the box score. The 49ers’ most recent addition provides yet another offensive weapon alongside Evans, Kittle, Christian McCaffrey, and Deebo Samuel, all of whom are now healthy as the team continues its press toward the only bye out of the NFC. Allen will be a difficult start in fantasy with the other supporting cast fully healthy as they prepare to face the Seahawks in Week 12.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: Keenan Allen caught 5-of-7 targets for 61 yards in the 49ers’ Week 10 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: Despite a short week to acclimate himself to his new team, Allen made a seamless transition to his new team. He caught 2-of-3 targets on third down for 31 yards, with one of those plays resulting in a 23-yard gain while Brock Purdy was scrambling around to extend the play. Allen’s 21 routes run narrowly trailed Deebo Samuel (27) and Jordan Watkins (22), but it wouldn’t be surprising if he saw more involvement going forward. Still one of the premier receivers in the league when it comes to finding separation and getting open, Allen already looks like a perfect fit in Kyle Shanahan’s scheme. He will be a fringe WR3/WR4 next Week against the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: 49ers acquired WR Keenan Allen from the Colts for a 2027 sixth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: Just what the 49ers needed: To get older at the skill positions. With Christian Kirk gone, Allen figures to fill a role for the 49ers and could still be fantasy relevant depending on Mike Evans’ health. It does seem unlikely he’ll draw the same sort of targets as he had been handling for the Colts, but the targets should be more effective. The Colts signed Allen off the street in August and flipped him for something as they realized they were going nowhere, so they’ve done well for themselves here. The wideout vacuum in Indianapolis may draw players like Ashton Dulin into fantasy consideration, especially if Josh Downs also moves later today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: Keenan Allen caught 4-of-8 targets for 26 yards in the Colts’ Week 9 loss to the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: Allen wasn’t targeted until late in the second quarter but picked up two receptions on back-to-back plays to tease fantasy managers in an otherwise poor outing. Things can’t get much worse in Indianapolis, with their decisions in the coming days ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline potentially allowing Allen to step into a more featured role in the second half of the season. Stay tuned as the Colts limp into a Week 10 matchup against the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Colts have told teams they’ve received an offer of a fourth-round pick for WR Josh Downs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: The Colts’ original asking price for Downs, who has requested a trade, was a third-round pick. Indianapolis has told teams they already have an offer of a fourth-round pick for the 25-year-old receiver, who is in the last year of his rookie contract. Downs is probably one of the more likelier players to be traded ahead of the deadline. Teams have also called the Colts about Keenan Allen, though he’s unlikely to bring back a similar trade return given his age.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins believes the Rams must find a way to trade for a wide receiver before the November 10th deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: The Rams’ resources are thin. They already traded away their 2027 first- and second-round picks, their 2028 second-round pick and their 2029 third-round pick. They also have just $8,000 in 2026 salary cap space, so restructuring the potential new add’s deal would be required. Atkins believes the Rams should consider Josh Downs as the top option due to his ability to beat man coverage and contribute as a returner. Other options, according to Atkins, include Calvin Ridley, Keenan Allen and Jauan Jennings, “for the likely cost of a Day 3 pick.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: Keenan Allen caught 7-of-7 targets for 67 yards in the Colts’ Week 8 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: As is now the case every week, Allen easily lead the Colts in most every receiving category. That did not include targets — a returning Tyler Warren commanded 10 looks — but Allen out-gained him 67-18. Now Allen and fantasy managers must sit and wait to see what kind of moves the tanking Colts make ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline. That could include non-roster changes like the benching of Daniel Jones. For now a low-end WR3, Allen could be valued much differently 10 days from now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: Keenan Allen caught 3-of-3 targets for 31 yards in the Colts’ Week 7 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: Allen was second on the team in targets while leading in receptions and yards against the Vikings. He saw just 30 snaps but operated as a quick release valve over the middle of the field for Daniel Jones against a blitz-happy Vikings defense. In an otherwise low-volume day, Allen had another game with a high share of the Colts’ receiving output. He will be in the WR3 ranks ahead of a Week 8 matchup against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: Keenan Allen caught 8-of-11 targets for 82 yards in the Colts’ Week 6 loss to the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: Each of Allen’s targets, receptions and receiving yards were new personal bests for his embryonic Colts career. Allen is doing what he’s supposed to be doing in Indy, but that’s not true for many of his teammates. Then again, we don’t really care in fantasy football, as Allen’s WR3 checks are clearing all the same. Allen’s short-area looks will be in high demand in Week 7 as Daniel Jones tries to survive the Vikings’ onslaught of blitzes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: Keenan Allen caught 5-of-9 targets for 45 yards in the Colts’ Week 5 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: Allen did not play a full complement of snaps in his first week back from a groin injury. He played 32 of the team’s 71 snaps and ran a route on 28 of their 47 dropbacks. That makes him leading the team with nine targets even more impressive. Of course, the Colts were forced to throw almost 50 times because the Steelers made it a priority to contain Jonathan Taylor. It’s highly unlikely Daniel Jones throws that much going forward, but Allen remains the top target in the offense. The issue is that most of his targets are in the short-yardage areas of the field, so he is more of a fringe-FLEX option unless you’re in a full PPR league. Next week against the Titans is a good matchup for the Colts, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian McCaffrey rushed 12 times for 49 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 11 win over the Vikings, adding 13 yards on two receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: McCaffrey found the end zone for the 14th time this season, marking his ninth consecutive game with a touchdown after failing to find paint in Week 1 against the Rams in Australia. The modest carry total and receiving total were more a comment on how much of a stranglehold the 49ers had on the game than anything else, coasting in the second half after jumping out to a 28-10 lead in the second quarter. The starters would then rest for the team’s final two possessions following McCaffrey’s fourth quarter touchdown. McCaffrey remains an elite RB1 ahead of a Week 12 meeting with the division rival Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian McCaffrey rushed 13 times for 62 yards and one touchdowns in the 49ers’ Week 10 win over the Cowboys, adding four receptions for 161 yards and two touchdowns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: McCaffrey was at his best in what can only be described as a legacy game for the 30-year-old running back. A relatively pedestrian line on the ground (12-62-1) proved to be nothing but a footnote in the box score for McCaffrey, who needed just four catches to set a new career high with 161 receiving yards. McCaffrey ripped off scores of 74 and 66 yards through the air, doing most of his damage after the catch. Of his 161 receiving yards, 141 of those yards came after the ball was in his hands, and his second score went virtually uncontested by a helpless Von Miller in man coverage. McCaffrey’s 223 yards from scrimmage were just 14 off his career high, and marked the fifth time in his career that he has gone for 200-plus yards from scrimmage. He will look to follow up this elite performance in Week 11 when the Niners “host” the Vikings in Mexico City.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian McCaffrey had 18 rushes for 68 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 9 win against the Raiders, adding two catches for 19 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: McCaffrey didn’t have much trouble against a Vegas run defense that has been one of the league’s worst over the past month. His rushing score was his ninth of the season, while his receiving score was his first of 2026. CMC logged 28 routes on the day while Kaelon Black had just five routes and did not see a target from Brock Purdy. McCaffrey, with at least 15 carries in five games this year, has a spectacular Week 10 matchup against a miserable Dallas defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Kaelon Black had 11 rushes for 70 yards in the 49ers’ Week 9 win against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Christian McCaffrey, meanwhile, had 18 rushes on the day and scored two touchdowns. Black had just five pass routes against the Raiders while CMC ran 28 routes. Black’s 70 rushing yards marks a season high and shows he can be a fantasy factor when the Niners have game script in their favor. It didn’t help that he faced an abysmal Raiders front seven. Black should have some flex viability in deeper leagues next week against the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Christian McCaffrey (hamstring) will have a “full workload” in Week 9 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: McCaffrey went down with the hamstring injury in Week 7, but then got a well-timed bye week to recover. He was a full participant in Friday’s practice before being removed from the injury report entirely. Per usual, he will be near the top of the RB1 ranks for his date with the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian McCaffrey (hamstring) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: McCaffrey injured his hamstring in Week 7. The 49ers were on bye in Week 8, giving him extra time to rest. McCaffrey then sat out on Wednesday before practicing in a limited capacity on Thursday. He should be in fantasy football lineups this week, facing a soft Raiders run defense, but Kaelon Black could mix in for 8-10 touches, potentially warranting FLEX consideration.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian McCaffrey (hamstring) was able to participate in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: A rare bit of good news on the injury front for the 49ers. McCaffrey was given the day off Wednesday. Even though today’s activity only resulted in a limited session, it’s a good start for what could be a Week 9 date against the Raiders that sees the tailback get a smorgasbord of touches due to the issues involving several injured receivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian McCaffrey (hamstring) will not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said more than a week ago that McCaffrey has a “mild” hamstring strain. Hamstring strains can be finicky. If Kaelon Black is available, add him immediately. McCaffrey still has a chance to play in Week 9 against the Raiders’ soft run defense, but he is ever so slightly in the questionable column at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Kyle Shanahan said Christian McCaffrey has a “mild” hamstring strain.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: That explains McCaffrey’s brief departure in the team’s Week 7 loss to the Falcons, when the veteran alpha missed most of the second quarter but returned for the second half. 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan added that he believes McCaffrey will be fine when the team comes out of their Week 8 bye. “We’re pretty optimistic,” he said Monday. Fantasy managers appear to have dodged a bullet with the first-round fantasy powerhouse but will want to continue to monitor reports from the team through their bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian McCaffrey rushed seven times for 39 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 7 loss to the Falcons, adding 61 receiving yards on six catches.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: McCaffrey scored a touchdown on the first drive of the game and had six touches, which seemed to set the tone for a massive workload. However, he also picked up a thigh injury on that drive and didn’t return again until the third quarter. The 49ers seemed to give him a few extra breaks in the second half, but McCaffrey didn’t look any less explosive. He was also half a yard away from catching a touchdown pass in the fourth quarter, but he was ruled down short of the end zone, and then Brock Purdy threw a touchdown pass to Kyle Juszczyk on the next play. The 49ers have a bye next week, so we doubt McCaffrey’s thigh injury will be an issue when we see them next in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: Jauan Jennings caught 3-of-6 targets for 20 yards in the Vikings’ Week 11 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Jennings operated in a familiar WR3 role for the Vikings despite the absence of Jordan Addison, with Tai Felton getting the start on the perimeter opposite Justin Jefferson. Fantasy managers that thought they were pulling a fast one by adding Jennings are likely better off scooping Felton as a viable Flex for as long as Addison remains sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: Jauan Jennings (calf) is practicing in full for Week 11 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Jennings missed the past two games with the calf injury. A full practice today puts him on track to return for a revenge game against the 49ers. Jordan Addison is sidelined with a thumb injury, meaning Jennings will likely return to the No. 2 receiver role. He is worth a look in deeper formats, though he’s still a high-risk WR5 for Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: Jauan Jennings (calf) will not play in Minnesota’s Week 10 game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Jennings would have been useful additional depth to have with Jordan Addison suddenly questionable. Tai Felton will likely see more work in Week 10, and perhaps Odell Beckham Jr. will be elevated off the practice squad if Jordan Addison (thumb) also sits.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: Jauan Jennings (calf) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Jennings missed Week 9 against the Bills with the calf issue and looks likely to sit for at least one more game. Myles Price ran ahead of Tai Felton last week, putting him in line for another round of No. 3 duties in Week 10. He is not on the fantasy radar despite the uptick in snaps.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: Vikings ruled out Jauan Jennings (calf) for Week 9 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: The fantasy implications of Jennings’ absence are negligible, with the bigger boost to the passing offense being the absence of Kyler Murray, who is looking at a multi-game absence with a Grade 2 hamstring injury. Tai Felton appears to be in line for additional run as the team’s WR3, although he is not a recommended streaming option with both Jefferson and Jordan Addison healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: Jauan Jennings (calf) was not seen practicing on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Jennings was limited yesterday, which could mean he injured his calf during the Vikings’ Thursday practice. If this is the case, he is probably unlikely to suit up for his team’s Monday Night Football game against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: Jauan Jennings (calf) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Jennings has been the subject of trade rumors. Since is able to practice, even in a limited capacity, this injury is unlikely to alter a potential suitor’s interest. Regardless, Jennings is not on the FLEX radar this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins believes the Rams must find a way to trade for a wide receiver before the November 10th deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: The Rams’ resources are thin. They already traded away their 2027 first- and second-round picks, their 2028 second-round pick and their 2029 third-round pick. They also have just $8,000 in 2026 salary cap space, so restructuring the potential new add’s deal would be required. Atkins believes the Rams should consider Josh Downs as the top option due to his ability to beat man coverage and contribute as a returner. Other options, according to Atkins, include Calvin Ridley, Keenan Allen and Jauan Jennings, “for the likely cost of a Day 3 pick.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter named Calvin Ridley as a potential trade candidate.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Schefter threw out several names, many of whom have already been bandied about as trade candidates. Among the lesser-discussed options, he included Jerry Jeudy and Jauan Jennings in addition to Ridley. All three are veteran wideouts who have simply disappeared in the current iterations of their respective offenses. Even with new landing spots in the cards for the trio, none of them are worth holding onto in standard fantasy leagues. Ridley has five catches for 81 yards this year. He is expected to play through his hip injury today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: Juan Jennings caught 2-of-3 targets for 34 yards in the Vikings’ Week 7 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Jennings caught a 20-yard pass, his longest reception of the season. He was targeted three times, nearly catching a long touchdown from Kyler Murray in the second quarter, but failing to haul it in. Jennings is outside of the top-three pass-catching options for the Vikings and is irrelevant for fantasy purposes in this role. Fantasy managers should keep an eye on him in case he is traded, but Jennings does not need to be in fantasy lineups heading in to Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: T.J. Hockenson caught 6-of-7 targets for 55 yards in the Vikings’ Week 11 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: The highlight of the game for the veteran tight end was a posterizing catch down the sideline for a 20-yard gain on the team’s opening possession, a drive that resulted in the first of two missed field goal attempts. Hockenson would play the role of Mr. Reliable from that point forward, although his seven targets finished third on the team behind Justin Jefferson and Tai Felton. The Vikings get the 3-7 Falcons at home in Week 12, where Hockenson will remain a volume-driven TE1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: T.J. Hockenson is not on Minnesota’s final Week 11 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: He can be fired up as a low-end TE1 with Jordan Addison (finger) out for the foreseeable future. Hockenson got in limited practices on Wednesday and Thursday before a full session on Friday tipped him past the questionable line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: T.J. Hockenson (wrist) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: Hockenson has a chance to return from his wrist injury for the Vikings’ Week 11 game against the 49ers. It would be nice to see him upgrade to full participation tomorrow. If active, Hockenson will likely qualify as a low-end TE1 with six NFL teams on bye this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: T.J. Hockenson (wrist) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: Hockenson missed Week 10 with the wrist issue. He was also dealing with a chest injury, though the team didn’t bother listing that today. Hockenson will be reunited with Kirk Cousins on Sunday, and the Vikings will be without Jordan Addison. That could free up a few extra targets for the tight end. If healthy, Hockenson will be in the TE2 streaming conversation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell said the team expects TJ Hockenson (wrist/chest) “to progress” ahead of Minnesota’s Week 11 game against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: We’ll be monitoring practice participation for Hockenson after he missed all three practices last week. Should he miss another game, Gavin Bartholomew caught a touchdown in his absence and would be a reasonable TE2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: T.J. Hockenson (wrist/chest) will not play in Minnesota’s Week 10 game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: Hockenson didn’t practice at any point this week and his status for Week 11 is likely in question as well. Gavin Bartholomew has picked up the slack this year when Hockenson has sat and will be a reasonable low-end TE2 play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: T.J. Hockenson (wrist/chest) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: Hockenson still has a chance to play in Week 10 against the Packers, but at this point, it seems likely that he will miss at least one game. Hockenson’s potential absence would likely allow Jordan Addison to earn a little more work than he has in recent weeks. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: T.J. Hockenson (wrist/chest) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: Both injuries are new for the veteran tight end. He presumably suffered them in the Vikings’ Monday loss to the Bills, though it’s unclear exactly when in the game he got hurt. Gavin Bartholomew would be the next man up, though we doubt he’s the best option off the waiver wire in most fantasy leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: T.J. Hockenson caught 4-of-7 targets for 33 yards in the Vikings’ Week 9 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: Hockenson struggled along with the rest of a Minnesota offense that managed only 178 yards of total offense, only 126 of which were accounted for with Carson Wentz under center. Max Brosmer came on in relief of the beleaguered veteran on the team’s final possession an nearly led the only touchdown drive of the game, ultimately coming up short on fourth down in the red zone. Hockenson and the rest of the Minnesota pass catchers are surely better off with any other quarterback than is currently on the roster, and there is the potential for the team to address the poor under-center play in the coming hours ahead of Tuesday’s 4 pm ET trade deadline. Hockenson would be a tough fantasy start against the Packers in Week 10 if the situation remains the same.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: TJ Hockenson caught 4-of-5 targets for 58 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings’ Week 8 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: It was Hockenson’s third touchdown grab of the season, as he remains Kyler Murray’s most trusted target in the run-heavy Vikings offense. He now has at least four receptions in four games this year. Hockenson, who came into Week 8 ranked tenth among tight ends in expected fantasy points per game, should remain in all lineups next week against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: Justin Jefferson caught 7-of-9 targets for 86 yards in the Vikings’ Week 11 loss to the 49ers, adding one yard on one carry.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: Kirk Cousins and Kevin O’Connell did what they could to get Jefferson involved early and often, although his nine targets ended second on the team behind Tai Felton’s 12. His lone mistake in the game was a costly one, with Jefferson losing a fumble with the team driving on their first possession of the second half down 28-10. The team would not recover after the untimely error, failing to add additional scoring while turning the ball over twice on downs during their subsequent three possessions. Jefferson is clearly in better hands with Cousins under center, a situation that should hold moving forward despite the veteran signal caller being replaced late in a lost game. Fantasy managers can start Jefferson with confidence as an upside WR2 against the Falcons in Week 12.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: Justin Jefferson caught 9-of-13 targets for 74 yards in the Vikings’ Week 10 win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: Jefferson’s 13 targets wound up leading all Vikings players, but nearly half of them came in the fourth quarter when Jefferson caught 6-of-6 targets for 43 yards on a drive that ended with a 20-yard touchdown pass to tight end Gavin Bartholomew. Jefferson missed hauling in an end zone target earlier in the day that would have resulted in a much better fantasy outing, but his 16.40 fantasy points were his most since Week 5. The return of Kirk Cousins should provide an immediate spark to Jefferson’s fantasy stock and will be a mid-to-high-end WR2 in Week 11 against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports the Vikings could trade for a quarterback before the NFL’s trade deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: “The word going into last night was the Vikings would be in the QB market ahead of the trade deadline if Carson Wentz didn’t play well,” Garafolo said. Narrator voice: He didn’t. Wentz was an utter disaster in Monday night’s loss to the Bills, completing 8-of-25 passes for 81 yards and two interceptions in the team’s second straight loss. Wentz in Week 9 had the league’s lowest drop back EPA and lowest success rate. He also appeared to sustain an ankle injury in the second half. With Kyler Murray (hamstring) struggling mightily in Kevin O’Connell’s offense, the Vikings could make a desperation move for Kirk Cousins or Daniel Jones ahead of today’s 4:00 p.m. eastern time trade deadline. Cousins, for one, would be a marked upgrade for Justin Jefferson and the Minnesota pass catchers. The Raiders have not expressed interest in parting with Cousins, however.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: Justin Jefferson caught 3-of-11 targets for 58 yards in the Vikings’ Week 9 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: It was a game to forget for Jefferson and the Vikings, who gained only 178 yards of total offense on just over 17 minutes in time of possession. Jefferson also failed to secure what was initially ruled on incomplete pass on a screen attempt in the first half, later overturned to a Carson Wentz fumble after being ruled a backwards pass. Furthering the pain for Jefferson’s fantasy managers is the fact that 19 of his yards came on the team’s final possession with Max Brosmer under center, leaving arguably the most talented wide receiver in the league completely bereft of a viable option at quarterback considering Wentz’s struggles. His fantasy contingency are best off saying their prayers that the team decides to address the quarterback position in the next 17 hours ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline. Jefferson would be a middling WR2 if the position remains unchanged ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Carson Wentz is “trending toward” starting in Week 9 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: Kyler Murray suffered a hamstring injury in Week 8, but even Schefter alluded to the idea that this would be a soft benching for Murray. Schefter added that it “looks like there’s a question at the quarterback position” for Minnesota. Healthy or not, it sounds like Wentz is going to be under center versus Buffalo. Wentz made one start earlier in the season while Murray was sidelined with a concussion. He only threw for 133 yards on 19 attempts, but Wentz found the end zone three times. Murray hasn’t thrown three passing touchdowns in a game since the end of the 2024 season. Wentz’s gunslinging style will likely be a win for fantasy managers hoping to get more out of Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison, especially in a potential shootout with the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: Justin Jefferson caught 5-of-9 targets for 33 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings’ Week 8 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: Jefferson once again led the Minnesota offense in targets but it was Jordan Addison and TJ Hockenson who had bigger statistical days in what was Kyler Murray’s best game as a Viking. Jefferson secured a short touchdown in the first half and was mostly invisible in the second half. He was seen shouting at no one in particular on the Minnesota sideline late in the fourth quarter. With just two games of more than 60 receiving yards, Jefferson is somewhat touchdown-reliant in the low-volume, run-first Vikings offense. He’ll face a porous Bills secondary in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: Justin Jefferson caught 4-of-7 targets for 44 yards in the Vikings’ Week 7 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: Jefferson led the Vikings in targets and yards on a low-volume day for the passing game. He hit a career milestone, crossing 600 career catches with a four-catch day. The Vikings’ offense continues to post low-efficiency outings as the defense lifts the team to an undefeated record. Jefferson is still the No. 1 wide receiver but banks on high volume usage and touchdowns to be a fantasy WR1. A lack of touchdown opportunities and red zone usage will be an issue in the Vikings offense, but Jefferson has a soft matchup against the Lions for Week 8. He should be back in the WR1 rankings next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: Justin Jefferson (ankle) is not on the final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: Coming off the Vikings’ Week 6 bye, Jefferson got in a limited session on Wednesday before returning to full participation on Thursday.
