The star wide receiver posted a 6/79/1 receiving line in the Vikings’ Week 5 win over the Saints. He should be treated as an elite WR1 against a Colts pass defense that will be without CB Sauce Gardner (calf).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: Justin Jefferson (ankle) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: The Vikings’ No. 1 wide receiver posted a 6/79/1 receiving line in the Vikings’ Week 5 win over the Saints. He should be feeling even better at this point, coming off a Week 6 bye. The Colts will notably be without No. 1 cornerback Sauce Gardner (calf) this weekend, making life even easier on Jefferson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: Justin Jefferson (ankle) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: This is just a maintenance day for the Vikings’ No. 1 wide receiver. Jefferson has an excellent matchup this week against the struggling Colts’ defense. The unit will likely be without No. 1 CB Sauce Gardner (calf), further enhancing Jefferson’s WR1 outlook for Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.headline: Aaron Jones rushed eight times for 30 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings’ Week 11 loss to the 49ers, adding 13 yards on one reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.analysis: Jones continues to cede primary rushing duties between the 20s to Jordan Mason but scored for the second consecutive game. After serving as a workhorse back with Mason on the shelf, Jones has not seen more than 11 carries since Mason returned in Week 7, having been held to eight carries or fewer in four of fives games. That leaves very little room for fantasy upside on the worse side of a true timeshare, meaning fantasy managers are better off leaving Jones on their bench ahead of a Week 12 meeting with the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.headline: Aaron Jones rushed 11 times for 47 yards and one touchdown in the Vikings’ Week 10 win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.analysis: Jones was out-rushed by Jordan Mason in this one, but he still managed to get 12 touches and found the end zone on a one-yard touchdown run in the second quarter. It was the first touchdown for Jones since Week 5, which was also the last time he rushed for more than 26 yards in a game. His lone target in the passing game resulted in an eight-yard gain, but this was an otherwise forgettable performance for Jones were it not for the touchdown to get fantasy managers over the hump. Jones has not been the reliable pass-catcher fantasy managers have come to count on over the years and shouldn’t be viewed as anything more than a fringe RB2/RB3 in Week 11 against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.headline: Aaron Jones rushed five times for 16 yards in the Vikings’ Week 9 loss to the Bills, adding five yards on one reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.analysis: Jones’ six opportunities were three behind backfield-mate Jordan Mason, despite the former getting the start on paper. The Vikings were unable to move the football consistently with Carson Wentz under center, gaining just 178 yards of total offense on just over 17 minutes in time of possession, both of which heavily influenced the veteran back’s opportunities and output. Jones is far from a usable fantasy asset while sharing the workload with Mason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.headline: Aaron Jones had five rushes for 22 yards in the Vikings’ Week 8 loss to the Lions, adding two catches for 18 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.analysis: Jordan Mason led the Minnesota backfield with eight rushes (for 20 yards) while Jones remained the team’s preferred pass-catching option out of the backfield. Jones was battling a knee injury headed into the game and did not appear to be 100 percent against Detroit. He’ll be a deep league flex option in Week 9 against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.headline: Aaron Jones (knee) is active for Week 8 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.analysis: Jones was able to practice in full on Friday after battling the lingering knee issue all week. He could be somewhat limited against Detroit, creating a potentially bigger workload for Jordan Mason, who profiles as a flex option in 12-team leagues. Vikings declared Jakobe Thomas, Charles Demmings, Demond Claiborne, Caleb Tiernan, Elijah Williams, and Max Brosmer inactive against the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.headline: Aaron Jones (knee) will play in Week 8 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.analysis: Jones departed the team’s Week 7 win over the Colts after aggravating an existing knee issue. He was held out of practice Wednesday before retaking the practice field on consecutive days to end the week, ultimately deemed healthy enough to play against the division rival Lions in Week 8. Fantasy managers are likely best off finding a suitable alternative considering Jones is struggling through a sprained MCL and the team got Jordan Mason back a week ago, although managers in a bind can safely expect him to be on the field come Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.headline: Aaron Jones (knee) returned to practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.analysis: Jones was forced from the team’s Week 7 win over the Colts due to an aggravation of an existing knee injury. The fact he was able to return to the practice field in any capacity after missing Wednesday’s session is good news for his potential availability against the Lions. We would expect him to form a loose committee with Jordan Mason, if active Sunday. Fantasy managers will want to confirm his level of participation Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.headline: Aaron Jones (knee) will not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.analysis: Jones has reportedly been playing through a sprained MCL in one knee since Week 2. He seemingly aggravated it in Week 7 and left the game early in the fourth quarter. On Monday, ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported that Jones is considered “day-to-day.” Jones could once again play through the issue this week against the Lions. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Aaron Jones is considered “day-to-day” after suffering a knee injury in Week 7’s win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.analysis: Jones’ status will be one to watch this week as the Vikings prepare for their Week 8 matchup against the Lions. While the team calling him day-to-day is encouraging, Jones was already dealing with a knee injury entering Week 7, so it wouldn’t be surprising if the Vikings opted to sit him this week to give him some additional time to recover. Jordan Mason, who rushed 15 times for 68 yards in Sunday’s win over the Colts could be in line for a busy day against the Lions if Jones is unable to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.headline: Aaron Jones rushed eight times for 26 yards in the Vikings’ Week 7 win over the Colts, adding one reception for zero yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.analysis: Jones got the start in the Vikings backfield, ripping off four straight carries for nine yards on Minnesota’s first possession. Outside of the opening possession, Jones took a backseat to Jordan Mason, seeing a mix of passing-down snaps and short-yardage carries. He caught his only target in the red zone but had it punched out for a fumble out of bounds. Jones left in the fourth quarter with a knee injury; he had been playing through an MCL injury and may have aggravated the issue. Prior to the injury, Jones was getting out-snapped by Mason and ends with 15 snaps to Mason’s 38, while getting six fewer touches. Jones is a low-end fantasy RB2 if healthy for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: Jordan Mason rushed 11 times for 38 yards in the Vikings’ Week 11 loss to the 49ers, losing one yard on one reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: Mason led the team in rush attempts and yardage while ceding high-value touches to Jones for the second consecutive week, with the latter accounting for the only touchdown scored by the Vikings in the loss. The poor game environment and inability of the offense to sustain drives led to the modest touch total for the veteran back, who has become a difficult player to trust in fantasy circles given the current split in workload. Fantasy managers likely have better options ahead of a Week 12 meeting with the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: Jordan Mason rushed 16 times for 59 yards in the Vikings’ Week 10 win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: Mason’s 16 carries and 59 yards both led all Vikings players. It was his first double-digit touch game since Week 7 against the Colts, but despite the encouraging touch share, he still lacked the high-value touches near the goal line. Aaron Jones handled all four of the Vikings’ goal-to-go rush attempts, leaving Mason to rely on long scores. Mason will be hard to trust as anything more than a boom-or-bust RB3 in Week 11 against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: Jordan Mason rushed six times for 35 yards in the Vikings’ Week 9 loss to the Bills, adding seven yards on two receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: The Vikings managed only 178 yards of total offense on just over 17 minutes in time of possession, completely incapable of moving the football with Carson Wentz under center. Those shortcomings confined Mason to only eight touches for the second consecutive week. Mason is not a starter-worthy fantasy asset until, or unless, the quarterback situation in Minnesota drastically improves ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: Jordan Mason had eight rushes for 20 yards in the Vikings’ Week 8 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: Mason led the team in carries, as Aaron Jones — who came into the game with a knee issue — saw five rushing attempts on the day. Jones remained the team’s pass-catching option out of the backfield while Mason could not get anything going on the ground against a middling Lions rush defense. Mason, who had 15 carries last week, will remain a touchdown-dependent RB3 option in Week 9 against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Aaron Jones is considered “day-to-day” after suffering a knee injury in Week 7’s win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: Jones’ status will be one to watch this week as the Vikings prepare for their Week 8 matchup against the Lions. While the team calling him day-to-day is encouraging, Jones was already dealing with a knee injury entering Week 7, so it wouldn’t be surprising if the Vikings opted to sit him this week to give him some additional time to recover. Jordan Mason, who rushed 15 times for 68 yards in Sunday’s win over the Colts could be in line for a busy day against the Lions if Jones is unable to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: Jordan Mason rushed 15 times for 68 yards in the Vikings’ Week 7 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: Mason did not start for the Vikings, but out-touched and out-snapped Aaron Jones. He was the primary early-down back and saw two targets as well, though he did not catch either of them. Jones (knee) exited the game in the fourth quarter, leading to Mason finishing out the game for the Vikings. Even before the Jones injury, Mason was the the back with the highest utilization. Mason is a low-end fantasy RB2 heading into a soft Week 8 matchup against the Lions; he could emerge as a top-15 option if Jones misses time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: Jordan Mason (thumb) is active for Week 7 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: The Vikings activated Mason off injured reserve and he is officially active for the first time since suffering a thumb injury in Week 1. He will split backfield touches with Aaron Jones, with Jones likely getting more of the passing-down work and Mason more the early-down work. Mason is a fantasy RB3 in his return. The Vikings declared S Jakobe Thomas, QB Max Brosmer, CB Chuck Demmings, RB Demond Claiborne, DL Elijah Willliams and OT Caleb Tiernan inactive for Week 7 against the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: Mason is firmly on track to play in Week 7 against the Colts. The Colts’ defense is not an imposing unit, so both running backs are FLEX-viable this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.headline: Kirk Cousins completed 26-of-38 passes for 235 yards and one interception in the Vikings’ 35-10, Week 11 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.analysis: This one started with all the makings of a true shootout, with the two teams trading blows early to push the score to 14-10 in favor of the 49ers through the first three possessions each. That would be where the offensive production stopped for the Vikings, who also turned the ball over twice and missed two field goals. We’ll give a pass on the second field goal attempt missed considering it came up just feet short of setting a new NFL record at 71 yards in the altitude in Mexico. The tires became entirely deflated for the Vikings after a Justin Jefferson fumble halted any momentum coming out of the half while trailing 28-10. A touchdown on that drive makes it a game, but the Vikings ultimately failed to muster any additional scoring after their third possession of the game. Cousins ended up giving way to Carson Wentz in the fourth quarter in a lost game after failing to throw for a touchdown for the first time this season. The 7-3 Vikings get a full week to prepare for the Falcons in Week 12, where Cousins will return as an upside QB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.headline: Kirk Cousins completed 21-of-31 passes for 207 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the Vikings’ 30-10, Week 10 win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.analysis: Cousins didn’t exactly stuff the box score in this one, but his performance provided a noticeable upgrade for the Vikings’ passing game. Getting the start on a short week following his trade to the Vikings, Cousins struggled early on, but eventually found his footing on the road against a solid Packers defense. His first big play of the game came on a 38-yard touchdown pass to Myles Price, where he placed the ball perfectly between three defenders to find Price, who then turned the ball upfield for the long score. In the fourth quarter, Cousins would connect with Gavin Bartholomew for his second touchdown pass of the day, which all but put the game out of reach for the Packers. With a full week to get ready for Week 11’s game against the Niners, we would expect Cousins and the offense to look a little more in sync. Cousins profiles as a mid-QB2 next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Vikings have talked to Kirk Cousins “about returning to Minnesota for the 2027 season.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.analysis: Rapoport notes that the Vikings told Cousins they wanted him around beyond this year before their trade for him was complete. They would go on to pay a third-round pick to reunite with their former starter. Even if Cousins is far from a superstar quarterback, head coach Kevin O’Connell is clearly sick of the weekly carousel under center. The Vikings will be legitimate Super Bowl contenders if Cousins can just play as well as he did in Vegas. A deep playoff run will all but guarantee him a spot on the roster next year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.headline: Vikings GM Nolan Teasley said there is “always potential” for Kirk Cousins to remain in Minnesota beyond 2026, but acquiring him was about this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.analysis: It seems that the Vikings just love to move on from quarterbacks who successfully adapt to their system. It is fair to wonder how much Cousins, 38, has left in the tank, but the fact that Teasley actually said this out loud is a little perplexing. At worst, Cousins should be able to serve as a mentor for whichever young quarterback coach Kevin O’Connell decides he wants to whisper to in 2027. Cousins is currently playing on a one-year, $11.3 million contract and could likely be retained on a one- or two-year deal at a similar value.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.headline: Vikings acquired QB Kirk Cousins from the Raiders for a 2027 third-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.analysis: And where did that bring you? Back to me. Cousins will likely take over as Minnesota’s starting quarterback in the near future, if not immediately. When that happens, Kyler Murray will head back to the bench for a second straight season — he’s droppable in most leagues at this point. Fernando Mendoza will take over as starting quarterback for the Raiders. Mendoza is best approached cautiously at this point in fantasy leagues. Cousins’ value likely remains stagnant — Klint Kubiak was already getting quite a bit out of him — but he provides the Vikings with a better floor at quarterback than what they were getting so it’s obvious after watching Carson Wentz play last night why this is happening.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Kirk Cousins is a “prime trade candidate” for the Vikings ahead of today’s trade deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.analysis: This would, of course, have multiple fantasy impacts. Fernando Mendoza would take over as Las Vegas’ starting quarterback if Cousins were traded, and Kyler Murray would likely take a backseat to Cousins sooner rather than later in Minnesota. We unfortunately must recommend that you stay tuned for the next couple of hours. Click the ads, too.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.headline: Kirk Cousins completed 22-of-32 attempts for 216 yards, one touchdown, and three interceptions in the Raiders’ Week 9 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.analysis: The statuesque Cousins was under duress from start to finish, often falling back as he threw the ball into tight windows. That led to three picks, which should have been four or five picks if 49ers defenders had been a little more sure handed. As usual, Cousins targeted Brock Bowers relentlessly, once again connecting with the superstar tight end for a touchdown. He nearly threw a second touchdown to Bowers in the second half. Cousins also had a touchdown to Michael Mayer called back on an offensive pass interference penalty. This was only Cousins’ second game of the year with less than two TD passes. Cousins will be a superflex option in Week 10 against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.headline: Kirk Cousins completed 19-of-26 passes for 247 yards and three touchdowns in the Raiders’ 38-33, Week 8 win over the Jets, adding a rushing score.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.analysis: With the Fernando Mendoza chatter increasing as the Raiders were mired in a four-game losing streak, Cousins responded with his fourth three-touchdown effort through the air, albeit his first since Week 3. Cousins has now provided multiple scores in 7-of-8 starts, and is up to 20 overall on the season. This, with Tre Tucker as his No. 1 receiver. Of course, Tucker is merely Cousins’ No. 1 wideout. Brock Bowers is his No. 1 pass catcher, and the elite tight end stacked up 7/92/2 in the new Meadowlands. Cousins seemed to look Bowers’ way on all the most critical downs, and he was richly rewarded. Fantasy managers also continue to be rewarded with Cousins in streamer spots, though that will be put to the test in Week 9 against the 49ers on the road. With only two teams on bye, we would be looking elsewhere in our quarterback spots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Raiders plan to start Kirk Cousins “as long as possible.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.analysis: Schefter added that the team does not feel their current four-game losing streak is the fault of Cousins. He threw for nine touchdowns in the first three games, all of which the Raiders won. Cousins has just seven touchdowns over his past four outings, though he has only thrown two interceptions and taken just five sacks during that stretch. The Raiders are probably right to lay the blame elsewhere. Still, No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza is waiting in the wings. He is the future of the franchise, and his time grows closer with every Raiders loss. Vegas takes on the Jets this week. They then get a gauntlet of San Francisco, Seattle, and Denver. A 0-3 run that late in the season would likely spell the end of Cousins as their starter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.headline: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said “Kirk Cousins is our quarterback,” when asked about the possibility of making a change at QB ahead of Week 8.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.analysis: Rather than let any speculation linger, Kubiak was quick to shut down any idea of a switch at quarterback heading into Week 8’s game against the Jets. Kubiak said, “There is no controversy” at quarterback at this time, while also adding that “Fernando [Mendoza] is going to play football” at some point this season. Kubiak said the team does not have a timeline for when Mendoza could eventually make a start, and said Cousins continues to play well despite the team’s recent struggles. Cousins will be firmly on the streaming radar this week against a Jets team that just allowed 28 points to the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Chris Rodriguez had four rushes for 28 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 11 loss to the Giants, adding one catch for 13 yards.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: ESPN’s Jordan Raanan reports the Giants inquired about Bijan Robinson’s availability before the NFL’s trade deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: “They were certainly big game hunting,” Raanan said. Though the thought of the Falcons parting ways with the centerpiece of their offense sounds ridiculous, it’s clear John Harbaugh and the Giants see themselves as a postseason team that won’t be content with a playoff berth. The inquiry on Bijan speaks to the Giants’ ongoing skepticism of Cam Skattebo as a true lead back. The team has done everything they can to prevent Skattebo from taking on a big backfield workload. In Week 10 against the Commanders, with a flurry of backfield injuries and Devin Singletary coming off one of the worst running back performances in NFL history, the Giants might have no choice but to feed Skattebo, who should be started in all 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: Cam Skattebo (hamstring) practiced in full on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: He should be good to go and handle low-end RB2 duties against the Commanders. Seemingly always at his best after a week off — which makes sense due to how physical he plays — don’t be surprised if Skattebo puts up some major fantasy points on Thursday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: Cam Skattebo (hamstring) was listed as limited on Monday’s estimated practice report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: Head coach John Harbaugh said earlier Monday that Skattebo would be “full go” for Thursday night’s game against the Commanders. It’s good news for a New York football team that struggled mightily to run the football consistently with veteran journeyman Devin Singletary spearheading the backfield against the Eagles in Week 9. Skattebo appears likely to reclaim lead back duties moving forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: Giants head coach John Harbaugh said Cam Skattebo (hamstring) will be “full go” in Week 10 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: Harbaugh said Skattebo was “very close” to playing in Week 9 against the Eagles, but they opted to sideline him, focusing on the second game they would play four days later. With the Giants set to face the Commanders on Thursday, Skattebo should be well rested and ready to play in his first game since Week 7, when he first suffered his injury. Skattebo totaled 71 scoreless yards on 15 touches in Week 5 against the Commanders and will be in the RB2 mix upon returning this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: Cam Skattebo (hamstring) is inactive for Week 9 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: With Skattebo down, the G-Men have been forced into a Devin Singletary start. Someone named “Gregory Desrosiers” appears to be the RB2. Expect a pass-focused game plan vs. Philly’s crumbling defense. Also inactive for the Giants are CB Colton Hood, CB Nikko Reed, OL Josh Sills, OL Marcus Mbow, TE Thomas Fidone II and DL C.J. Okoye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.headline: Tre Tucker caught 2-of-10 targets for 50 yards in the Raiders’ Week 11 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.analysis: Tucker led the Raiders in targets, though several of his looks were uncatchable. He racked up plenty of prayer yards but didn’t do much in the way of actual receiving production. The bulk of his output came on a 39-yard toss from Fernando Mendoza in the fourth quarter. Jack Bech, on the other hand, went for 88 yards and a score on eight targets. With Brock Bowers potentially returning next week, even Tucker’s role as an air yards merchant could take a hit in Week 12. He is likely stuck in the WR5 mix for his upcoming game against the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.headline: Tre Tucker caught 1-of-2 targets for nine yards in the Raiders’ Week 10 loss against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.analysis: The Raiders had a meager 146 passing yards in Fernando Mendoza’s first NFL start. Tucker, the leading Vegas wideout headed into Week 10, wasn’t targeted until the fourth quarter against the elite Seahawks secondary. The loss of Kirk Cousins in a trade to the Vikings last week might be the end of Tucker’s fleeting fantasy relevance unless Mendoza improves in the coming weeks. If Brock Bowers (ankle) misses time, Tucker could see a slight uptick in targets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.headline: Tre Tucker caught 4-of-8 targets for 55 yards in the Raiders’ Week 9 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.analysis: Tucker occupied his usual role as the team’s de facto No. 1 wideout, almost connecting with Kirk Cousins in the second half for what likely would have been a long touchdown. Tucker was tied for the team lead in targets with Brock Bowers. His air yards domination gives Tucker a fairly high weekly ceiling in a Vegas offense usually chasing points in the second half. Tucker will be an iffy option next week against Seattle.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.headline: Tre Tucker was held without a catch in the Raiders’ Week 8 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.analysis: Coming off 10/200/3 over the past two weeks, Tucker somehow commanded only one target in a game where the Raiders scored 38 points. It was the first time since the opener he caught fewer than four passes. Tucker has definitely benefitted from some garbage time production, but he is not typically going to be a zero waiting to happen. He can still be trotted out there as a low-end WR3 for a Week 9 matchup where the Raiders are going to have to pass to compete with the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.headline: Tre Tucker caught 5-of-12 targets for 103 yards and a touchdown in the Raiders’ Week 7 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.analysis: It was a quiet day for Tucker until the Raiders once again found themselves down by three scores in the fourth quarter. Kirk Cousins — as he did last week against Buffalo — let it rip and peppered Tucker with late downfield targets, one of them resulting in an impressive 37-yard touchdown. Tucker led all Vegas pass catchers with a dozen targets and dominated air yards as usual. Last week against the Bills, Tucker went for 97 yards and two scores on five receptions. The miserable Raiders defense should lead to plenty of runaway negative game script for the team’s offense in the coming weeks, and Tucker’s role as the team’s lone deep ball option gives him weekly upside. He’ll be a WR3 option in Week 8 against the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.headline: Tre Tucker caught 5-of-7 targets for 97 yards and two touchdowns in the Raiders’ Week 6 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.analysis: Tucker found the end zone on an 11-yard touchdown pass from Kirk Cousins in the fourth quarter to tie the game at 23-23. Later in the game, with the Raiders down by 10, Tucker found himself on the receiving end of a Kirk Cousins moon ball in the end zone, which he hauled in for a 44-yard touchdown to cut the Bills’ lead to 33-30 with just over a minute left in the game. Tucker is the closest thing the Raiders have to a fantasy-viable wide receiver, and he has proven to be a volatile player throughout his four-year career. Fantasy managers shouldn’t view him as anything more than a boom-or-bust WR4 in next week’s game against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.headline: Tre Tucker caught 4-of-5 targets for 41 yards in the Raiders’ Week 5 loss to the Patriots, adding two rushes for -7 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.analysis: Tucker’s two rushing attempts were blown up in the backfield. He was third on the team in targets, trailing Brock Bowers and Ashton Jeanty. Tucker, who usually operates as the team’s primary downfield option, should have some appeal in Week 6 against Buffalo in what could be a high-scoring game. He has at least four receptions in four of five games this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.headline: Tre Tucker caught 4-of-8 targets for 44 yards in the Raiders’ Week 4 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.analysis: Tucker’s longest catch came on a 23-yard reception late in the fourth quarter as the Raiders looked to drive and tie up the game. Had the replay officials called for a review of the play in time, the catch likely would have been overturned, but the play was upheld, much to the disappointment of the Chiefs and head coach Andy Reid. The eight targets Tucker saw in this one set a new season high. He’s totaled 44 or fewer yards in three of four games this season and will be hard to trust as anything more than a dart-throw WR4 in Week 5 against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.headline: Tre Tucker caught 4-of-4 targets for 43 yards in the Raiders’ Week 3 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.analysis: Tucker had a bigger impact in real life than he did in fantasy. On the plus side, he helped set up a field goal and a touchdown, first by finding the soft spot in the Saints’ zone coverage in the two-minute drill. Later, his 15-yard gain on a deep crossing route helped set up the Raiders. He also committed a holding penalty, which erased a short gain for RB Ashton Jeanty. Tucker is a WR4/FLEX against the Chiefs next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.headline: Tre Tucker caught 5-of-7 targets for 119 yards and a touchdown in the Raiders’ Week 2 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.analysis: Kirk Cousins got the deep ball going in this game after settling for mostly check-downs in Week 1. Tucker caught two passes of 40+ yards, the first of which was a second-quarter touchdown. He also tied Ashton Jeanty with a team-high seven targets, so it wasn’t just a one-off deep shot for the veteran wideout. Brock Bowers is expected to return next week, meaning Tucker’s target share should take a hit the next time we see him. Even if he is relegated to field-stretching duties in Week 3, Tucker will remain a high-ceiling FLEX bet versus the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.headline: Malachi Fields caught 2-of-5 targets for 25 yards in the Giants’ Week 11 win against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.analysis: Fields logged a pass route on 42 of the team’s 47 drop backs and was third on the team in targets behind Malik Nabers and Cam Skattebo. He now has just three games with at least three receptions in 2026 as a tertiary part of the New York passing offense. Fields will be a deep league flex play in Week 12 against the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.headline: Malachi Fields caught 3-of-4 targets for 62 yards in the Giants’ Week 10 loss to the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.analysis: The New York wide receivers were clearly limited by a game plan to feature tight end Isaiah Likely, with the starting trio of Malik Nabers, Fields, and Darnell Mooney combining for just 10 receptions, one more than the nine of Likely. Even so, Fields continued to demonstrate a strong connection with quarterback J.J. McCarthy as the rookie finished second on the team in receiving despite seeing only four targets. The highlight of the game came in the second half when McCarthy threaded a ball over one defender and underneath two more down the left sideline for a 25-yard gain to Fields. Although his weekly volume likely won’t be vast enough to return consistent fantasy production without an injury to Nabers or Likely, Fields continues to show the growth dynasty managers were hoping for.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.headline: Malachi Fields caught 3-of-5 targets for 40 yards in the Giants’ Week 9 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.analysis: Although this was a step back on Fields’ pre-bye performance of 4/83, it was actually only the second time all season he caught more than two passes. He continues to head in the right direction as J.J. McCarthy provides some upside hope for this offense. That being said, McCarthy’s (hip) status is questionable for Thursday against the Commanders, while Fields has still not proven his WR4 bonafides. He mostly remains an end-of-bench stash in conventional 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.headline: Malachi Fields caught 4-of-5 targets for 83 yards in New York’s Week 7 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.analysis: It should be noted that the Texans defense is giving up points to wideouts by the bushel this year, but in J.J. McCarthy’s first start, Fields was heavily involved. This bested his career-best yardage total by 31 yards and he added a career-high 47-yard catch-and-run. Fields doesn’t necessarily need to be added in most fantasy leagues at this point but he’s definitely making inroads towards WR4 status.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.headline: Malachi Fields caught 2-of-8 targets for 19 yards and a touchdown in the Giants’ Week 6 loss to the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.analysis: Fields saw a season-high eight targets, but caught just two of those passes for 19 yards. The Giants passing game behind Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely isn’t productive for fantasy purposes. Darnell Mooney had a carry for 20 yards while Charlie Jones caught 2-of-3 passes for 66 yards. Fields is the best option past Nabers and Likely, but he can be left on fantasy benches for Week 7 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.headline: Malachi Fields caught 2-of-3 targets for 52 yards and a touchdown in the Giants’ Week 4 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.analysis: Fields has now caught exactly two passes in each of his first four NFL appearances. His 12-yard touchdown was the first of his career. Jameis Winston was flushed from the pocket and found Fields on the run. The duo later connected on a similar play for a non-scoring 40-yard grab. Today was the first time Winston showed any signs of life in place of Jaxson Dart, though Fields is still going to be a tough sell WR4 in this depressed offensive environment.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.headline: Malachi Fields caught both of his targets for 19 yards in the Giants’ Week 3 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.analysis: Fields hasn’t caught more than two passes in a game this year. He finished third on the team in targets in Week 3. Fields is on the field plenty, he just isn’t earning that many opportunities. He is not a viable fantasy option for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.headline: Malachi Fields caught 2-of-6 targets for 30 yards in the Giants’ Week 2 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.analysis: Fields struggled alongside the rest of the Giants in a game played mostly with backup quarterback Jameis Winston under center. Jaxson Dart departed after the team’s first possession with what looked like an MCL sprain based on the mechanism of the injury, something that could force missed contests from the normal starter. That would position Fields in a difficult spot to return usable counting stats in the short term. He gets the struggling Titans in Week 3, where he’ll be best left on fantasy benches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.headline: Malachi Fields caught 2-of-4 targets for 25 yards in the Giants’ Week 1 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.analysis: The rookie wide receiver showcased a polished all-around skillset, reinforcing offseason reports that he had locked down the WR2 role opposite Malik Nabers. His 6'4, 220-pound frame was on full display as he was continually utilized as both a down-blocker and blocker in the second level on runs, something that should allow him to continue to operate as the clear-cut WR2 for the Giants throughout his rookie campaign. That said, the box scores highlights the obvious distinction that his snap rate — he led all Giants wideouts with 50 — won’t always translate to fantasy production while playing alongside Nabers and tight end Isaiah Likely, the latter two of whom commanded 17 targets on 29 Jaxson Dart pass attempts. The good news is that he played well ahead of veterans Darnell Mooney and Odell Beckham Jr., with Mooney having 39 snaps and Beckham just 11. Fantasy managers are best off viewing Fields as a high-end stash at the end of benches for the time being.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.headline: ESPN’s Jordan Raanan believes WR Malachi Fields “will likely start as the Giants’ No. 2 receiver opposite Malik Nabers.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.analysis: This isn’t the first time Raanan has suggested Fields could have the inside edge as the Giants’ WR2. Earlier this month, he said the rookie third-rounder was making an “early claim” for the role, which doesn’t come as much of a surprise given the thin receiving corps the Giants are currently working with. The 6-foot-4, 220-plus-pound receiver has an excellent catch radius and made a name for himself with his ability to haul in contested targets during his days at Virginia and Notre Dame. It seems highly unlikely that Fields would make enough of an impact to be considered a reliable fantasy contributor, but he could be worth a late-round/stash in drafts to see how things unfold for him in the weeks to come.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Malik Nabers caught 7-of-12 targets for 55 yards and a touchdown in the Giants’ Week 11 win against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: Nabers again led the Giants in targets, with no other New York pass catcher seeing more than seven targets on the day. Nabers’ looks were mostly of the dink-and-dunk variety; JJ McCarthy missed his top wideout on a couple easy throws in the second half in a disastrously inaccurate outing for the Giants quarterback. Nabers’ 12 targets were the third most of his 2026 season. The near-total lack of target competition in the New York offense means Nabers has as stable a floor as any receiver in the game. He’ll once again be a top-10 option in Week 12 against the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Malik Nabers caught 5-of-7 targets for 44 yards in the Giants’ Week 10 loss to the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: Nabers was clearly not a point of emphasis in a game expected to carry significant weather impacts. Despite the weather subsiding in the second half, McCarthy remained fixed on Isaiah Likely, feeding the veteran tight end 11 targets. The matchup also played a role in the game plan, with the Commanders missing numerous key linebackers while blitzing at an above average rate. Nabers is in a good spot to bounce back against the Jaguars in Week 11, where he’ll return to WR1 status in fantasy circles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Malik Nabers caught 5-of-8 targets for 43 yards in the Giants’ Week 9 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: Entering the game with four straight 100-yard performances, Nabers had a day of what ifs. Banged up early but no worse for the wear, Nabers played snaps with two different QBs as J.J. McCarthy missed part of the third quarter with a hip issue. McCarthy returned only for Nabers to drop a should-have-been 20-yard touchdown in the end zone. Frustrating, but 9.43 PPR points on a “down” day is not the worst outcome. Nabers and McCarthy have only four days to heal up for Thursday’s short-week date with the Commanders, but Nabers’ status is not in doubt, while he will remain a high-end WR1 even if Jameis Winston returns under center for the G-Men.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Malik Nabers (knee) is not on the final injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: The Giants have smartly limited Nabers’ practice participation levels at times this season, allowing him to play very well while returning from last year’s season-ending knee injury. Nabers belongs in fantasy football lineups in this divisional showdown, as usual.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Malik Nabers (knee) returned to practice on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: Nabers was a surprise DNP with a knee injury on Thursday, but said after practice that he expected to play. His return to the field on Friday suggests he will be good to go for Sunday’s game against the Eagles, but we will still check in with a final status when the Giants announce player designations for the weekend. Assuming he is good to go, Nabers should be treated as a normal must-start receiver against a down-bad Eagles team.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Malik Nabers (knee) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: Nabers worked with trainers today instead of practicing with his teammates. He told reporters after practicing that he is “good” to go for Week 9 against the Eagles. We believe him. The Giants have managed his reps at times during the practice week this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Malik Nabers (undisclosed) was seen working off to the side with trainers on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: The Giants have limited Nabers’ practice reps from time to time this season. Although he may end up being listed as a non-participant, we are not currently concerned about his Week 9 availability. The Giants’ No. 1 wide receiver is fully dressed in his typical practice attire. An update will be provided when more info is released.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Malik Nabers caught 7-of-11 targets for 111 yards in New York’s Week 7 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: He toasted Derek Stingley Jr. a few times and found a 42-yarder early on in the proceedings. Nabers didn’t come close to scoring, but that was mostly a result of Houston’s bad run defense being an easy mark. He’ll retain WR1 status once he’s back from New York’s Week 8 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: SNY TV’s Connor Hughes believes the Giants will stick with J.J. McCarthy as the starter “for the foreseeable future.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: According to Hughes, “this is the player they targeted and wanted” as their quarterback the minute Jaxson Dart (knee) got hurt. Hughes acknowledges that coach John Harbaugh could eventually bench McCarthy later in the year, but it will take more than a bad “game or two” for that to happen. In the meantime, the weekly fantasy football outlooks for Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely are more volatile than they were with Jameis Winston at the helm. Selling high could make sense. Hughes adds that McCarthy would have to play like a top-10 quarterback to make the coaching staff consider him for the starting role next season. That outcome seems highly unlikely.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Malik Nabers caught 12-of-15 targets for 165 yards in the Giants’ Week 6 loss to the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: Nabers was once again heavily involved in the Giants’ passing game, getting the first offensive touch for New York. He saw 15 targets and tallied 165 scoreless yards on the day, with over half of this yardage coming with J.J. McCarthy in the fourth quarter. It’s the third straight 100-yard game for Nabers, who is now fully ramped up from his torn ACL last year. The Giants may be debating between Jameis Winston and J.J. McCarthy as the starting quarterback for next week. Regardless of the starter, Nabers sees enough volume to be a borderline WR1 for Week 7 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.headline: Jalen Nailor caught 1-of-5 targets for 16 yards in the Raiders’ Week 11 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.analysis: Nailor was marginally more involved with Brock Bowers out this week, but it wasn’t enough for him to make a dent in the box score. He did score a touchdown late in the game, but Mendoza was well ahead of the line of scrimmage when the ball left his hands, killing the play. Nailor is still operating as the team’s No. 3 receiver behind Jack Bech and Tre Tucker. With a hard ceiling on his target volume, Nailor is not on the fantasy radar for Week 12.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.headline: Jalen Nailor caught 4-of-4 targets for 38 yards and a touchdown in the Raiders’ Week 8 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.analysis: Nailor’s touchdown was his first as a Raider. It went down for all of two yards. In addition to the score, Nailor posted new season highs in yards and receptions, which obviously tells you all you need to know about his WR4 value: He doesn’t have any heading into Week 9 against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.headline: Jalen Nailor caught 2-of-5 targets for 14 yards in the Raiders’ Week 7 loss against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.analysis: Nailor ran a route on 42 of the team’s 49 drop backs but wasn’t all that involved. Tre Tucker remains the Raiders’ top wideout, leaving Nailor without much in the way of air yards or targets. He should remain on waiver wires ahead of the Raiders’ Week 8 game against the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.headline: Jalen Nailor caught 1-of-4 targets for nine yards in the Raiders’ Week 6 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.analysis: After missing Week 5’s game against the Patriots due to a concussion, Nailor was back on the field this week to face the Bills. Unfortunately for the 2026 free-agent signee, the results looked all too familiar. Nailor managed only one reception for nine yards and is now sitting on a 6-61-0 receiving line through his first five games of the season. Fantasy managers shouldn’t be counting on him to provide anything in next week’s game against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.headline: Jalen Nailor (concussion) will play in Las Vegas’ Week 6 game against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.analysis: This per coach Klint Kubiak, so we assume Nailor has passed protocol. He’s only a FLEX play at this point as it’s hard to trust any weapons in the Vegas offense beyond Brock Bowers, even in a good matchup against a struggling Bills defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.headline: Jalen Nailor (concussion) resumed practicing in a red non-contact jersey.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.analysis: Nailor will likely end up being listed as a limited participant today. He has a chance to play in Week 6 against the Bills, but his odds would be better if he had returned yesterday. If active, Nailor would only be a boom-bust WR5/FLEX.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.headline: Jalen Nailor (concussion) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.analysis: Nailor suffered a concussion in the Raiders’ Week 4 loss to the Chiefs, missing Week 5 against the Patriots while still in the protocol. He starts out the week not practicing, indicating he is not close to clearing protocol. Though he still has a chance to play this week, Nailor does not need to be stashed for fantasy purposes amid a murky wide receiver corps.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.headline: Raiders ruled out Jalen Nailor (concussion) for Week 5 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.analysis: The Raiders entered the season with a thin wide receiver corps, and the unit just got thinner. Tre Tucker will continue functioning as the team’s top wide receiver and second pass catcher, backed up by Cody White (ankle) and rookie Malik Benson. Nailor does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.headline: Raiders WR Jalen Nailor (concussion) did not participate in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.analysis: Nailor will almost assuredly sit out the Raiders’ Week 5 game against the Patriots. Fellow WR Dont’e Thornton (hamstring) is practicing in full, and WR Cody White (ankle) remains limited.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.headline: Raiders WR Jalen Nailor (concussion) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.analysis: Nailor suffered a concussion against the Chiefs in Week 4 and starts out the week not practicing. This indicates he is on the wrong side of questionable for Week 5 against the Patriots. Fellow WR Cody White (ankle) was limited as well, though Dont’e Thornton (hamstring) returned to practice, giving the Raiders some reinforcement with Nailor still in concussion protocol.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Mike Washington rushed nine times for 42 yards in the Raiders’ Week 11 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Washington continued to operate as a change-of-pace back for the Raiders. He only saw two fewer carries than Ashton Jeanty, but the latter earned eight targets and led the team with 90 receiving yards. Washington was not targeted. Without any receiving work to fall back on, Washington is stuck in the RB4 ranks headed into a Week 12 matchup with Cleveland.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Mike Washington, Jr. had eight rushes for 23 yards in the Raiders’ Week 10 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Meanwhile, Ashton Jeanty had nine rushes for a meager 18 yards and again took all the pass-catching work out of the Raiders backfield. Washington will see decent rush volume when the Raiders see neutral or positive game script. How often that will happen in the coming weeks is another matter entirely. Washington should not be played in most fantasy formats next week against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Mike Washington, Jr. had six rushes for -3 yards in the Raiders’ Week 9 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: A week after getting 25 rushes, Washington was relegated to six carries in this one, as the Niners raced out to a big lead and never relented. Washington tied Ashton Jeanty for the team lead in rushing attempts. Neither back got it going against a tough 49ers front seven. Washington, who ran five routes against San Francisco, will continue to be a prototypical early-down bruiser who is sensitive to weekly game script. He should be benched in almost every format next week against the brutal Seahawks defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Ashton Jeanty had six rushes for 25 yards in the Raiders’ Week 9 loss to the 49ers, adding five catches for -5 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Jeanty and Mike Washington were scripted out in the second half, with the Raiders — as usual — falling behind by multiple scores. Jeanty was swallowed up by Niners defenders almost every time he caught the ball in the backfield. The plodding Jeanty couldn’t get anything going against a swarming 49ers defense. This was Jenaty’s sixth game of the season with at least four catches. It’s a role that has made him playable in 12-team leagues this season. Washington, meanwhile, had six carries for -3 yards. Jeanty might have some flex value in Week 10 against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said the team’s backfield touch distribution will be a “moving target.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Mike Washington, Jr. in Week 8 against the Jets took over as the team’s lead rusher, logging 25 carries to just two carries for Ashton Jeanty. While Kubiak said after the game that Jeanty would remain a part of the offense, it’s clear the Raiders are willing to experiment with backfield touches. “You see where your team is at and who’s playing the best ball at the time. It’s a 17-game regular season where things change every week. They’ve been changing at guard, they change up front defensively, they change at corner,” Kubiak said. “That’s the NFL. We have a young roster and we’re going to give guys opportunities and see what fits us best. But your 11, whether you’re playing really well or not playing well at all, it’s always going to change a little bit.” The Raiders through Week 8 rank dead last in EPA per rush and second to last in rushing success rate. Jeanty should remain viable as long as he’s the team’s primary pass catcher out of the backfield. Jeanty ranks fifth among all RBs in expected fantasy points per game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Mike Washington rushed 25 times for 83 yards in the Raiders’ Week 8 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: At least for one week, the Raiders formalized Washington’s early-down takeover, as the rookie out-carried a doghoused Ashton Jeanty 25-2. However, Washington got routinely stood up on his ample goal-line opportunities, and only out-gained Jeanty 83-73 thanks to Jeanty’s involvement in the passing game. A 45-yard reception where Jeanty literally fell down to catch an inaccurate Kirk Cousins pass only to get up and rumble nearly half the length of the field was by far the biggest play by a Raiders running back in this one. Although Washington now has to be considered the favorite for early-down work, he was uninspiring enough this afternoon that it’s not going to be an open-and-shut case against the 49ers. We would still rather start Jeanty in fantasy because of his pass catching.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Mike Washington, Jr. had six rushes for 27 yards in the Raiders’ Week 7 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: As usual, Washington was far more efficient than lead back Ashton Jeanty, who had 15 yards on eight carries while catching eight passes for 61 yards and a touchdown. Washington can be stashed for now in case Jeanty misses time in the second half of the season. Washington likely won’t get the pass-catching work if Jeanty misses time, however.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Mike Washington (foot/back) is active for Week 7 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Whether Washington plays all that much remains to be seen. He is not a recommended FLEX starter. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak has misdirected at times with injury-related comments. The Raiders declared DT Thomas Booker IV, DE Cian Slone, S Dalton Johnson, DT Jonah Laulu, G Bryan Cabeldue, S Tristin McCollum and QB Aidan O’Connell inactive for Week 7 against the Rams. O’Connell will serve as the emergency third quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Mike Washington (foot/back) is a game-time decision for Week 7 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Washington Jr. didn’t practice on Thursday or Friday but still received a questionable designation for Week 7. Fowler added that there is “some optimism” that he plays this week, but the pre-game workout will be the determining factor. Washington saw an uptick in carries last week with nine totes for 43 yards. We don’t expect as much work to go this way given the injury situation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Mike Washington (foot/back) is questionable for Las Vegas’ Week 7 game against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Washington didn’t practice on Thursday and was not spotted at practice on Friday. It would seem that he’s a very tenuous questionable at this point. Dylan Laube would be next up for backup duties behind Ashton Jeanty if Washington were ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Quentin Johnston caught 1-of-2 targets for nine yards in the Chargers’ Week 11 loss to the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: Johnston’s day was mostly quiet, although he did technically earn an end zone target on the Chargers’ sixth drive. The coaching staff tried to involve his post-catch skill set via a trick-play toss, but he was stuffed at the line of scrimmage. Johnston will be a shaky FLEX option against the Patriots next week, even if Justin Herbert clears the NFL’s concussion protocol.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Quentin Johnston caught his only target for six yards in the Chargers’ Week 10 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: Johnston was a complete afterthought in a game quarterback Justin Herbert attempted only 18 passes, with the team playing with a lead throughout for the first time all season. Fellow receiver Tre’ Harris handily led the team with five targets, five receptions, and 86 yards, with no other pass catcher seeing more than three looks, catching more than two passes, or going for more than 16 yards. Johnston is completely off the fantasy radar ahead of a Week 11 meeting with the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Quentin Johnston caught 1-of-4 targets for 58 yards and one touchdown in the Chargers’ Week 9 loss to the Texans, adding one rush for five yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: If you didn’t start Johnston, we can’t blame you. It’s been a rough go. Johnston deserves credit for his long score. He caught a pass on a slant route and took off downfield via a post pattern, churning his legs through a shoestring tackle attempt. It’s the type of play we expected Johnston to be featured on in OC Mike McDaniel’s offense, rather than the deep routes he is frequently stuck running. Johnston also earned an end zone target, but was unable to secure it. With Justin Herbert (left hand) ailing, Johnston is tough to trust as a FLEX against the Ravens next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Quentin Johnston caught all four of his targets for 37 yards in the Chargers’ Week 8 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: It was yet another down game for Johnston, who did his work underneath in this one. He now has one game this season with more than two receptions in a Chargers offense that can be described as utterly dysfunctional on every level. Johnston should not be rostered in most fantasy formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Quentin Johnston caught 1-of-3 targets for 57 yards in the Chargers’ Week 6 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: Johnston’s lone catch was a fantastic grab over tight coverage in the fourth quarter. He nearly scored on the play. Even with Ladd McConkey out with a head injury, Johnston did not function as the Chargers’ top wideout, as DeAndre Lambert-Smith led the team with ten targets. Johnston will be nothing more than a deep league flex option going forward. He should not be rostered in most 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Quentin Johnston (chest) is not on Los Angeles’ final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: Stark difference from last week’s limited-limited-rule out. Jim Harbaugh would not commit to putting it on the record that Johnston would be on a snap count. Playing through the injury with Los Angeles’ sad sack offensive line would seem to have Johnston as more of a sketchy FLEX play than a WR3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Quentin Johnston (chest) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: Johnston is on track to play, but this wide receiver corps is very banged up. KeAndre Lambert-Smith (hamstring) and Brenen Thompson (quad) remained limited as well. Marquez Valdes-Scantling (ribs) upgraded to full.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Quentin Johnston (chest) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: Johnston, KeAndre Lambert-Smith (hamstring), Brenen Thompson (quad), and Marquez Valdes-Scantling (rib) were all limited Wednesday. Lambert-Smith currently has his practice window for return from IR open while the others are dealing with a varying level of ailments. Johnston is the best fantasy option out of this group, but he is only worth FLEX consideration in the deepest of leagues. With Ladd McConkey (foot) also limited, the Chargers have several “maybes” ahead of a Week 6 matchup against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said Quentin Johnston (chest) will “probably be limited this week like last for the practice.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: “We’ll see where he’s at the end of the week,” Harbaugh added. Johnston practiced on both Thursday and Friday so he likely has the best chance of being active among Los Angeles’ main three wideouts. Unfortunately this passing game is in rough shape, and even a higher volume, healthy load probably wouldn’t get Johnston above the FLEX line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Quentin Johnston (chest) won’t play in Los Angeles’ Week 5 game against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: Johnston got in limited sessions on Thursday and Friday, so it was surprising to see him sent straight to “not playing.” Tre’ Harris figures to step in as Los Angeles’ top outside receiver by snaps this week and is a worthwhile FLEX play, even against a formidable Broncos defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.headline: Trevor Lawrence completed 25-of-47 attempts for 300 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions in the Jaguars’ Week 11 loss to the Giants, adding three rushes for seven yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.analysis: Lawrence finally had a high volume drop back game as the Jaguars chased points in the second half. Sunday was only the second game this season in which Lawrence has had more than 40 attempts. He targeted Parker Washington throughout, connecting with him eight times on 17 targets, including on a second half touchdown that was incorrectly called back on replay review. T-Law’s lone touchdown came on a fourth quarter touchdown toss to Brian Thomas. Lawrence will have a fantastic Week 12 matchup against a struggling Titans secondary that allowed 352 yards and three scores to Lawrence in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.headline: Trevor Lawrence completed 25-of-35 passes for 352 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception in the Jaguars’ 40-23, Week 10 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.analysis: Lawrence added 27 yards with his legs. He picked apart the Titans’ defense in the first half, finding big completion after big completion via Parker Washington. With the Titans failing to do that much on offense, things slowed down in the second half, but two of Lawrence’s touchdowns did come after the break. The interception was the result of a batted pass that popped up and into the hands of Titans linebacker Cedric Gray. Lawrence’s 352 yards are his highest total since Week 5 of the 2024 season. Playing nearly MVP-caliber football, Lawrence will be a top-half QB1 for his Week 11 game against the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.headline: Trevor Lawrence completed 16-of-26 passes for 242 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ 33-10, Week 9 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.analysis: It was business as usual for Lawrence and the Jaguars, who won their eighth game by 20 or more points since the start of the 2025 season, the most in the league during that span. Lawrence looked sharp throughout, starting things off with a touchdown drive on their opening possession that was sparked by a 52-yard completion to tight end Nate Boerkircher. He would hit Parker Washington on a slant for a 50-yard touchdown in the final minute before the half to push the lead to 17-3, with a flurry of second half field goals enough to chase the reeling Ravens from the field. In standard Jacksonville fashion, positive game script capped Lawrence’s aerial volume, something fantasy managers have both gotten used to through the mid way point in the season and will likely see continue considering the Jaguars hold the league’s softest remaining strength of schedule. The win pushes the Jaguars to 6-2 and extends their lead in the AFC South ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the one-win Titans, where Lawrence will remain a back end QB1 due to lack of volume.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.headline: Trevor Lawrence completed 10-of-14 passes for 210 yards and three touchdowns in the Jaguars’ 42-7, Week 8 win over the Colts, adding three rushes for 10 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.analysis: This came in only three quarters of work, as Lawrence spent the fourth frame on the bench with the Jags demolishing the quitting Colts. Unfortunately for fantasy managers, early breathers have been a theme for Lawrence this season as his well-rounded team keeps blowing out less impressive sides. Rather unbelievably, that could now include the Ravens for Week 9, as Baltimore appears down to its No. 3 quarterback for the sides’ short-week Thursday night tilt. That won’t be enough to force Lawrence out of starting lineups, but he can’t be expected to single-handedly win matchups in that environment.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.headline: Trevor Lawrence completed 24-of-41 passes for 306 yards, four touchdowns and one interception in Jacksonville’s 34-31, Week 6 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.analysis: It could have been more, had Liam Coen not settled for a game-tying field goal on fourth-and-short with less than four minutes left in the game. It also could have been more had Lawrence not thrown an end-zone pick to Calen Bullock. At the end of the day, the screen game was dealing and Lawrence was hitting all sorts of in-breakers against a beleaguered Texans secondary. He enters the bye week as a sure-fire QB1 with 1,174 passing yards and 10 throwing touchdowns in his first five games. Last year’s rushing touchdowns appear to have vanished as the Jaguars have gotten better in the red zone, but Lawrence is still playing exceptional football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.headline: Trevor Lawrence completed 24-of-39 passes for 331 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the Jaguars’ 19-17, Week 5 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.analysis: Lawrence gave fantasy managers what they needed with a solid box score, but he was not the reason the Jags won this game. Lawrence struggled under pressure, throwing one ugly interception while putting the ball on the ground twice via sack-fumbles. Both were recovered by the Jags. The offense was also a catastrophe in the red zone, though a series of penalties and bizarre play calls are largely to blame there. Down by one with eight seconds left, it looked like the team’s struggles on offense would be too much to overcome. Instead, Ameer Abdullah returned a kickoff 53 yards to set up a walkoff field goal from Cam Little. If the Jags can clean things up after an uncharacteristically sloppy game, Lawrence will remain a mid-range QB1 for Week 6 versus the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.headline: Trevor Lawrence completed 18-of-23 passes for 227 yards and one touchdown in the Jaguars’ 22-17, Week 4 win over the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.analysis: The Jaguars offensive operation was far from clean against the Bengals; the team as a whole tallied 10 penalties for 100 yards by halftime. Lawrence was sacked four times behind a struggling offensive line but still put together an efficient game. He found Brian Thomas Jr. for the game’s first touchdown as time wound down in the first half and found tight end Brenton Strange for seven of his 18 completions. Despite a relatively pedestrian showing, Lawrence comes away with zero turnovers and the win. He will be a top-12 fantasy option for Week 5 against the Eagles in London.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.headline: Trevor Lawrence completed 19-of-29 attempts for 182 yards and three touchdowns in the Jaguars’ Week 3 win against the Patriots, adding four rushes for 25 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.analysis: Lawrence’s big statistical day could have been bigger if he hadn’t inexplicably taken a knee at the one yard line on a QB rush with about eight minutes left in the fourth quarter. Bhayshul Tuten would go on to score a rushing touchdown a few plays later. Lawrence picked apart of the New England secondary with very little pressure in his face, targeting former Patriots WR Jakobi Meyers heavily and connecting with three different pass catchers for touchdowns — including Parker Washington, who had another score called back. Lawrence, with one of the highest weekly floors in the game, will again be a top-12 QB option in Week 4 against Bengals in what should be a high-scoring game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.headline: Trevor Lawrence completed 17-of-29 attempts for 189 yards and one interception in the Jaguars’ Week 2 loss against the Broncos, adding two rushes for six yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.analysis: The Jaguars were relatively run-heavy against Denver a week after the Broncos were shredded by Ken Walker and the Chiefs. Lawrence mostly checked down in this one, targeting Parker Washington a team-high 12 times. Brian Thomas, Jr., meanwhile, had two untimely drops, one that appeared to frustrate Lawrence. Lawrence’s interception came on a poor throw to Washington near the sideline. He’ll look to bounce back next week against a stingy New England secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.headline: Trevor Lawrence completed 18-of-23 passes for 245 yards and four touchdowns in the Jaguars’ 34-10, Week 1 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.analysis: It was a monstrous offensive showing from the Jaguars, led by Lawrence and his four passing touchdowns. He opened scoring with a 30-yard touchdown throw to Parker Washington in the first quarter, tossing two more scores in the first half. Lawrence flexed his mobility with a lob on the run to Jakobi Meyers for a 32-yard touchdown in the third quarter. With a comfortable lead, Lawrence rested in the fourth quarter, finishing with a whopping 0.72 EPA per play. Nick Mullens tallied three kneel-downs in relief. Liam Coen’s offense will generate many fantasy opportunities across the board, especially when operating as efficiently as it did Week 1. Lawrence built upon his solid 2025 season with an all-star showing Week 1 against the Browns and should be a low-end fantasy QB1 for Week 2 against a tougher Broncos defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre’ Harris caught 2-of-2 targets for 28 yards in the Chargers’ Week 11 loss to the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harris snagged a 22-yard pass against busted coverage in this one, but that was not his most consequential play. On the Chargers’ third drive, Harris ran a go route inside the red zone and managed to get behind his coverage defender. Justin Herbert uncorked it, and Harris dove for it, but unfortunately, the pass bounced off his hands in the back of the end zone. Jets EDGE David Bailey committed a roughing the passer penalty on the play, which the Chargers accepted, erasing it from the box score. Harris is a boom-bust FLEX against the Patriots next week, pending Justin Herbert’s (concussion) availability.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre’ Harris caught all five targets for 86 yards in the Chargers’ Week 10 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harris’ five targets, five receptions, and 86 yards were all team highs on a night quarterback Justin Herbert attempted only 18 passes, with the Chargers playing with a lead throughout for the first time all season. The highlight of the game on either side was Harris’ 31-yard reception in the first quarter, with the veteran receiver shaking free on a deep crosser and getting his hand under the ball on a sliding catch. Fantasy managers will want to track the status of Ladd McConkey entering a Week 11 meeting with the Jets as a return to action could send Harris back to the nether realm as far as fantasy value is concerned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre’ Harris (shoulder) practiced in full on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harris led the team in targets last week, but somehow managed just six yards on three catches. With Ladd McConkey (back) ailing, Harris could lead the team in targets again. He would only be a boom-bust FLEX in this case, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre’ Harris (shoulder) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harris led the team with seven targets last week, catching just three of them for six yards. Although he is not fantasy-relevant on his own, his presence theoretically helps Justin Herbert and Harris is on track to play in this week’s Monday Night Football game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre’ Harris caught 3-of-7 targets for six yards in the Chargers’ Week 9 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Being this inefficient ain’t easy. Trainers examined Harris’ lower left leg after an eighth-drive incompletion in which Harris twisted as he unsuccessfully tried to high-point a pass and came down hard on his feet. Harris does not need to be in fantasy football lineups against the Ravens next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre Harris caught all three of his targets for 31 yards in the Chargers’ Week 8 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harris was the team’s WR3 behind Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston, as usual. When McConkey is healthy, Harris operates as a part-time player without much of a fantasy floor. He should remain on waiver wires ahead of LA’s Week 9 game against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre’ Harris (hamstring) will play in Week 8 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harris returns to the lineup after missing Week 6, with the team’s bye week providing enough time for the veteran receiver to get back to the active game-day roster. That doesn’t mean he should be inserted into fantasy lineups after such a slow start to the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre’ Harris (hamstring) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harris missed Week 6 before the team’s Week 7 bye but could be held out for an additional week given the nature of his injury. Fantasy managers will want to confirm his status on the team’s final injury report Friday to gauge the viability of entering him back into lineups for Week 8. Fellow wide receiver Ladd McConkey (concussion) got in his second consecutive full session and should be good to go for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre’ Harris (hamstring) will practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harris was labeled week-to-week early in Week 6 and was unable to face the Chiefs that weekend. After resting and rehabbing through the Chargers’ Week 7 bye, Harris has a chance to resume playing in Week 8. We expect to see him listed as a limited participant, but an update will be provided if he practices in full. Brenen Thompson (quad) remains sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre’ Harris (hamstring) will not play in Los Angeles’ Week 6 game against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: He did not practice this week and Jim Harbaugh called him “week to week.” Harris stands a chance at returning after Los Angeles’ Week 7 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Ashton Jeanty rushed 11 times for 79 yards in the Raiders’ Week 11 loss to the Broncos, adding five catches for 90 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: Jeanty broke his first carry of 20 or more yards on a 46-yard sprint into the red zone in the second quarter. The Raiders’ offensive line finally cleared a lane for the former No. 6 overall pick and he ran to daylight before being tracked down by a pair of Broncos defenders inside the five. Per Next Gen Stats, he hit 21.4 MPH on the run, which goes down as his highest top speed since being drafted. Jeanty was also productive through the air. His highlight of the day was a 68-yard receiving touchdown. He beat his man on a wheel route and Fernando Mendoza hit him in stride for a massive score. It was enough for Jeanty to lead the Raiders in receiving for the second straight week. Jeanty’s elite receiving role alone will keep him in the middle of the RB2 ranks for his Week 12 date with the Browns on Sunday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Ashton Jeanty had nine rushes for 18 yards in the Raiders’ Week 10 loss to the Seahawks, adding four catches for 46 yards.
