https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: Jeanty was the Raiders’ leading receiver with Brock Bowers sidelined with an ankle injury. His 38-yard catch and run was by far the biggest play of the day for a lifeless Vegas offense with Fernando Mendoza under center for his first start of his NFL career. As usual, Jeanty operated as the primary pass catcher out of the backfield, running 26 routes to just eight routes for Mike Washington, who had a meager 23 yards on eight carries. Jeanty will be a top-24 PPR option next week against Denver.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Mike Washington, Jr. had six rushes for -3 yards in the Raiders’ Week 9 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: A week after getting 25 rushes, Washington was relegated to six carries in this one, as the Niners raced out to a big lead and never relented. Washington tied Ashton Jeanty for the team lead in rushing attempts. Neither back got it going against a tough 49ers front seven. Washington, who ran five routes against San Francisco, will continue to be a prototypical early-down bruiser who is sensitive to weekly game script. He should be benched in almost every format next week against the brutal Seahawks defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Ashton Jeanty had six rushes for 25 yards in the Raiders’ Week 9 loss to the 49ers, adding five catches for -5 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: Jeanty and Mike Washington were scripted out in the second half, with the Raiders — as usual — falling behind by multiple scores. Jeanty was swallowed up by Niners defenders almost every time he caught the ball in the backfield. The plodding Jeanty couldn’t get anything going against a swarming 49ers defense. This was Jenaty’s sixth game of the season with at least four catches. It’s a role that has made him playable in 12-team leagues this season. Washington, meanwhile, had six carries for -3 yards. Jeanty might have some flex value in Week 10 against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said the team’s backfield touch distribution will be a “moving target.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: Mike Washington, Jr. in Week 8 against the Jets took over as the team’s lead rusher, logging 25 carries to just two carries for Ashton Jeanty. While Kubiak said after the game that Jeanty would remain a part of the offense, it’s clear the Raiders are willing to experiment with backfield touches. “You see where your team is at and who’s playing the best ball at the time. It’s a 17-game regular season where things change every week. They’ve been changing at guard, they change up front defensively, they change at corner,” Kubiak said. “That’s the NFL. We have a young roster and we’re going to give guys opportunities and see what fits us best. But your 11, whether you’re playing really well or not playing well at all, it’s always going to change a little bit.” The Raiders through Week 8 rank dead last in EPA per rush and second to last in rushing success rate. Jeanty should remain viable as long as he’s the team’s primary pass catcher out of the backfield. Jeanty ranks fifth among all RBs in expected fantasy points per game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Ashton Jeanty rushed two times for nine yards in the Raiders’ Week 8 win over the Jets, adding three receptions for 64 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: Jeanty was benched as the Raiders’ early-down back, getting out-carried 25-2 by Mike Washington Jr. For his part, Washington was not effective, churning up just 3.3 yards per carry and getting stoned on a bevy of goal-line handles. Speaking afterward, coach Klint Kubiak said the move was his call but that "(Jeanty) is still going to be a big part of our team.” Jeanty made waves during the week when he said the Jets could not tackle. Rather than let the struggling second-year back prove his theory on the field, the Raiders made the takedown themselves for the Jets. While it’s clear Jeanty is now in a true timeshare, we do also take Kubiak at his word that Jeanty will remain a “big part” of the team, almost certainly with double-digit carries more weeks than not. The question is if he can keep catching enough passes to hold RB2 status. Washington is now the preferred short-yardage back, but his failures in Sunday’s highest-leverage spots could keep the door ajar for Jeanty.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Ashton Jeanty had eight rushes for 15 yards in the Raiders’ Week 7 loss to the Rams, adding eight catches for 61 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: Among the least efficient rushers in the game, Jeanty again struggled to get anything going on the ground behind a middling Vegas offensive line. He did almost all of his damage through the air, turning eight targets into 61 yards and a late score in garbage time. He ran a route on 20 of the team’s 35 drop backs against the Rams and ranked second among Raiders pass catchers in targets. Mike Washington had six carries on the day. Jeanty, with at least six targets in six of his seven games this season, can maintain RB2 status as long as he’s catching passes out of the backfield. He gets the Jets in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Mike Washington (foot/back) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: Dang. This suggests Washington suffered one or both injuries yesterday in practice. He is firmly in the questionable camp and may have only a long shot at suiting up in Week 7 against the Rams. Without him, Ashton Jeanty should handle a solid workload. Dylan Laube could end up serving as the No. 2 running back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Ashton Jeanty rushed 10 times for 22 yards and a touchdown in the Raiders’ Week 6 loss to the Bills, adding four receptions for 36 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: Jeanty, who is dealing with a foot/ankle injury, wasn’t effective on the ground, but that didn’t stop him from scoring his first rushing touchdown of the season. Jeanty punched in a one-yard score in the first quarter of Sunday’s game to give the Raiders an early 7-3 lead, but averaged a disappointing 2.2 YPC overall. He did manage a solid 4-36-0 receiving line on six targets, with two of his four receptions coming on the Raiders’ third drive of the game. Jeanty appeared on 15 more snaps than Mike Washington and out-touched him 14 to 10. While he continues to struggle from an efficiency standpoint, Jeanty’s volume will make him a low-end RB1 next week against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Ashton Jeanty (foot) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 6 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: The Raiders’ starting running back is good to go for what should be a fantasy-friendly game environment. The Raiders encouragingly stopped listing Jeanty with an ankle injury this week. Hopefully, his remaining plantar fasciitis issue subsides before long as well. Jeanty is a low-end RB1 in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Ladd McConkey caught 5-of-8 targets for 37 yards and two touchdowns in the Chargers’ Week 11 loss to the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: McConkey mostly ran short-to-intermediate routes from the slot today. Although he dropped what might have been a first-down pickup on the first drive after halftime, he made the most of his other opportunities. McConkey scored an 11-yard touchdown via an out route early in the fourth quarter, faking an in-breaker that left his coverage defender in the dust. McConkey scored again with roughly two minutes left, shaking Jets LB DeMario Davis on a six-yard hitch-and-go before snagging Justin Herbert’s throw in the end zone. It was an encouraging performance for the Chargers’ No. 1 wide receiver. Unfortunately, the team announced post-game that Herbert has entered the NFL’s concussion protocol. If Herbert is active, McConkey will be back in the WR2 tier next week against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Ladd McConkey (back) is active for Week 11 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: McConkey’s injuries have made him difficult to trust this season, but the Chargers have funneled targets his way when active. He should be viewed as a WR3 with volume-based upside, now evidently healthy enough to play. The Chargers declared LB Daiyan Henley, CB Tarheeb Still, WR Brenen Thompson, S Kendall Williamson, G Alex Harkey and WR KeAndre Lambert-Smith inactive for Week 11 against the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Ladd McConkey (back) is expected to play in Week 11 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: McConkey experienced back spasms in pre-game warmups two weeks ago. The Chargers didn’t announce that until the game had started and he did not play a snap. The team had the courtesy to rule him out ahead of kickoff last week. He got in three limited sessions this week before being listed as questionable. McConkey has been the Chargers’ most effective wideout when healthy, but that has been an exceedingly rare occurrence this year. We suspect he’s still not at full strength. With the risk of a re-injury looming, fantasy managers should treat him as a WR3, even if his ceiling his much higher.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Ladd McConkey (back) is questionable for Los Angeles’ Week 11 game against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: McConkey was limited in all three sessions this week and was a shadow docket rule out in Week 9 while being a straight inactive in Week 10. Actually practicing ahead of this game is a sign things are better, but he’ll be no more than a WR3 in this dilapidated passing attack between the re-injury risk and the lack of upside. Yes, even against the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Ladd McConkey (back) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: The Chargers’ No. 1 wide receiver is tentatively on track to play in Week 11 against the Jets, but ideally he will upgrade to full participation tomorrow. The Chargers have been willing to run the passing offense through McConkey when he is active. He is a WR2, albeit with some re-injury risk, if he suits up.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Ladd McConkey (back) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: McConkey has been dealing with the back injury for two weeks now, sitting out the Chargers’ last two games. He continues to deal with a various set of injuries and is a wild card when it comes to playing on game days. A limited designation at least gives fantasy managers hope that he will play in Week 11 against the Jets, though McConkey has fallen to unreliable WR3 status at this point of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Chargers declared WR Ladd McConkey, S Kendall Williamson, CB Isas Waxter, OLB Bud Dupree, WR Brenen Thompson, and DL Justin Eboigbe inactive for Week 10 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: McConkey entered the weekend listed as questionable but was downgraded to out Saturday, while rookie Brenan Thompson will miss his seventh consecutive game. The reeling Chargers look to pick up their first win through an upset of a Ravens team without its top two quarterbacks, having recently signed veteran Jacoby Brissett for the final half of the regular season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Ladd McConkey (back) has been downgraded to out for Week 10 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: McConkey is not taking the team flight to Baltimore, hence the Sunday rule-out. This has become a(nother) lost season for McConkey, who has gone from supposedly not even being injured entering Week 9 pre-game warmups to now missing back-to-back contests. McConkey’s own poor health coupled with Justin Herbert’s stunningly dreadful play is conspiring to make Ladd a WR4 we are no longer even sure about keeping around on our 12-team league benches. He’s a tough drop because of how little talent there is behind him in L.A., but it’s so difficult to envision McConkey contributing when it matters most during the fantasy playoffs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Ladd McConkey (back) is questionable for Week 10 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: McConkey heads into Monday Night Football listed as questionable after failing to practice through Friday. The veteran receiver missed Week 9 when it was revealed he had been dealing with back spasms during warmups. Fantasy managers are likely better off making alternate plans considering the Chargers play in the final game of the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Ladd McConkey (back) did not practice on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: This is unfortunate. McConkey is no stranger to playing through injury, but his availability for Week 10’s Monday Night Football game appears to be in jeopardy. If active, McConkey would be a WR2, but backup plans should be made at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: Braelon Allen rushed 16 times for 75 yards in the Jets’ Week 11 win over the Chargers, adding one reception for nine yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: Allen racked up 17 touches in the No. 2 role behind featured starter Breece Hall. The Jets leaned heavily on their backfield today, with Geno Smith playing through an ankle injury. The coaching staff repeatedly called Allen’s number on multiple drives, allowing their burly backup to wear out Chargers defenders. Allen sealed the game with a 15-yard run up the middle, barreling through contact along the way. Allen must be rostered in all fantasy football formats as an elite bench stash at worst. He warrants FLEX consideration next week against the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: Braelon Allen rushed eight times for 40 yards in the Jets’ Week 10 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: Allen looked pretty good as a runner but didn’t get a lot of opportunities with the Jets trailing most of the game. Allen played eight fewer snaps than Breece Hall, took three fewer carries, and ran a route on four fewer dropbacks, but he didn’t command nearly as many targets. It’s hard to trust Allen in fantasy next week against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: Braelon Allen had eight rushes for 23 yards in the Jets’ Week 9 loss to the Chiefs, adding two catches for 21 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: Breece Hall, returning from his quad injury, led the New York backfield with 15 carries while adding three grabs out of the backfield. It was Allen, however, who led the Jets backfield in pass routes, 21 to 10. That sort of pass game usage could keep Allen viable in deeper formats since the Jets are going to be chasing points more weeks than not. Both Jets running backs average 4.1 yards per carry against an elite KC front seven. Allen plays the Bills in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: Breece Hall had 15 rushes for 61 yards in the Jets’ Week 9 loss to the Chiefs, adding three catches for 26 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: Finally returning from his multi-month quad injury, Hall took over as the Jets’ lead back even after Braelon Allen had a nice run as the team’s RB1. Allen ended up with 10 touches on the day, including eight carries. Hall looked spry, dodging would-be tacklers and creating yards after first contact on a handful of his touches. It seems Jets coaches were serious when they said Hall would resume lead back duties upon his return. Hall’s role in the Jets offense should make him a locked-in top-24 option, including next week against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Breece Hall (quad) will play in Week 9 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: This comes a day after Hall said he expects to play, so this news isn’t all too surprising. Hall’s return could somewhat complicate the Jets’ backfield situation on Sunday, however, as Braelon Allen has played well in Hall’s absence, making a strong case for more touches even when Hall is healthy. Glenn declined to get into how he plans to divvy up his running backs’ touches next week, saying “both guys will play,” when asked about his plans. This was already shaping up to be a tough fantasy matchup on the road against the Chiefs, but a potential backfield split would only further complicate matters. Until we see how things shake out, both Hall and Allen should be viewed as mid-to-low-end RB2s.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: Breece Hall (quad) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: Hall is expected to return this week, but a full practice might be required before the team gives him the go-ahead. Hall logged three limited practices last week before being ruled out on Sunday. Barring a setback, we’re still expecting Hall to ramp up to a full session over the next two days. Assuming he does, Hall will likely split work with Braelon Allen, who has been extremely effective as the Jets’ workhorse running back in his absence. Both backs will sit in the RB3 ranks for their Week 9 date with the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Breece Hall (quad) is “trending in the right direction.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: Hall, barring setbacks in practice, should be OK for Week 9 against the Chiefs. What his workload will look like is another question entirely. Braelon Allen has established himself as an efficient, tough runner over the past few weeks, and could remain the Jets’ lead rusher while Hall takes on most pass-catching opportunities. Though Hall should have some kind of floor in Week 9, he probably doesn’t have much of a ceiling unless the Jets decided to phase out Allen.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: Jets offensive coordinator Frank Reich said he “assumes” Breece Hall will remain the team’s lead back when he returns from injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn has knocked down suggestions that the Jets would trade Hall before the league’s trade deadline, as Braelon Allen continues as one of the NFL’s most productive rushers. When asked about how the backfield might look when Hall returns from his quad injury, Reich seemed to say Hall would remain the de facto lead runner. “Well, that’s obviously coach’s decision, but they’re both the guy … I mean, that’s a good problem to have,” Reich said. “That’s coach’s decision, but to me … Breece is our guy. I’m assuming Breece is our guy, you know what I mean? He’s one of the best in the NFL, but I think what’s been so excited is like, oh my gosh, we’ve got two of them. I mean, we’ve got two. This Braelon guy, he’s a beast as well.” Allen this season ranks third among running backs in rushing success rate; 11th in rush yards over expected per attempt; eighth in yards after contact per rush; and over the past three weeks he ranks eighth among RBs in expected fantasy points per game, proving the haters wrong along the way. Hall is expected to return to action this week against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: Braelon Allen rushed 21 times for 147 yards and a touchdown in the Jets’ Week 8 loss to the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: Allen added two receptions for six yards. With Breece Hall a surprising weekend ruleout with an aggravation of his long-running quad injury, Allen got another start and once again made the most of it. Allen’s career-high 147 yards on the ground included a 24-yard rush and 21-yard touchdown where he got the edge and was then not touched en route to the house. In between, he got shaken up on a big hit but appeared no worse for the wear. Although Hall is supposedly in play for Week 9, he was never even supposed to be in doubt for Week 8. For now we will consider Hall on the wrong side of questionable to face the Chiefs’ strong defense on the road. Even if Hall goes, Allen will maintain FLEX appeal. If Hall sits, Allen will be a must-start RB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: Breece Hall (quad) is inactive for Week 8 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: Hall seems to have suffered a rather serious setback with the quad injury that has been dogging him since September. This is easily said in hindsight, but it would seem Gang Green did not handle the issue particularly well. Hall is supposedly “hoping for next week,” but we would consider him on the wrong side of questionable until further notice. Isaiah Davis will serve as Braelon Allen’s breather back. Joining Hall on the shelf are EDGE David Bailey, WR Tim Patrick, CB Nahshon Wright, ED David Bailey, OL Kohl Levao and OL Max Mitchell.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: Breece Hall rushed 20 times for 86 yards in the Jets’ Week 11 win over the Chargers, adding three receptions for 14 yards and one touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: The Jets’ coaching staff designed a run-heavy game plan with Geno Smith (ankle) playing through an injury. Hall and Braelon Allen split 40 touches between the two of them. Although Allen should be expected to remain regularly involved, and even got a little work inside the Chargers’ 20-yard line, the Jets made sure Hall was in the game when they got near, or inside, the Chargers’ 10-yard line. Hall scored on 2nd-and-goal from the Chargers’ seven-yard line by running a route across the backfield, behind the line, before catching a pass in the flats and turning upfield for the score. Hall is an RB1 against the Dolphins in Week 12.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: Breece Hall rushed 11 times for 40 yards in the Jets’ Week 10 loss to the Bills, adding 67 yards receiving on four catches.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: Hall wasn’t able to get much going on the ground against the Bills, but he did look good as a receiver. Hall played eight more snaps than Braelon Allen, including running a route on 19 dropbacks to 16 for Allen, but the timeshare on a bad offense is going to limit both of their fantasy upside. Hall is more of a high-end FLEX option or RB3 next week against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones reports the Jets have no desire or intention to trade RB Breece Hall.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: While the Jets traded young players for draft picks last season, don’t expect New York to do that again this year. A team source told Jones the Jets moving Hall is “very unlikely to happen.” Hall appears ready to return from a quad injury in Week 9 against the Chiefs, but is difficult to trust in fantasy with Braelon Allen potentially cutting into his workload after a strong showing in Hall’s absence in recent weeks.

Until we see how things shake out, both Hall and Allen should be viewed as mid-to-low-end RB2s.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: Breece Hall (quad) said he is ready to go for Week 9 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: We expect to see Hall listed as a full participant on today’s injury report. An update will be provided if that is not the case. Earlier today, Jets OC Frank Reich discussed Hall and Braelon Allen’s expected usage, saying having the two players is “a great problem to have,” referring to the duo as “two No. 1 backs.” That said, Reich added that Hall “is obviously the bell cow,” but the backfield usage will be a “mix” of both players. Jets coach Aaron Glenn will reportedly share his ideal backfield split with Reich, who will work with the position coaches to make it happen. Hall likely belongs in the high-end RB2 tier while Allen remains FLEX-viable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Fernando Mendoza completed 18-of-37 passes for 267 yards, three touchdowns, and an interception in the Raiders’ 38-24, Week 11 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Mendoza got off to a dreadfully slow start. The Raiders’ first three drives amounted to 11 net yards and a trio of punts. Mendoza was already down 17 by the time he got the ball back for his fourth series. Mendoza then finally settled in and moved the ball well. His first career passing touchdown came on a well-thrown wheel route to Ashton Jeanty. He led his running back to space and Jeanty did the rest. Mendoza tossed two more scores in the second half, but his comeback bid came to a screeching halt with a fourth-quarter pick-six. Broncos corner Ja’Quan McMillan jumped the route and rather easily took the interception to the house. Things get much easier for Mendoza in Week 12 when he takes on the Browns next week. He will be near the back of the QB2 mix for his third start.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Fernando Mendoza completed 17-of-29 attempts for 143 yards in the Raiders’ Week 10 loss to the Seahawks, adding six rushes for 22 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Mendoza was thrown directly into the meat grinder of the elite Seahawks defense and lost his superstar tight end, Brock Bowers, to a potentially serious ankle injury in the first quarter. After a first quarter rushing score on a draw play, Mendoza and the Raiders couldn’t get anything going against Seattle. Mendoza, who was sacked six times, posted a -6.8 EPA while Drew Lock had an EPA of 7. Mendoza was about 7 percent under his expected completion rate. Things won’t get much easier for the 2026 No. 1 overall pick in Week 11 when the Raiders take on the Broncos. Mendoza for now is strictly a superflex option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Raiders planned to start Fernando Mendoza “in the next few weeks” even if Kirk Cousins had not been traded.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: With games against the Seahawks and Broncos on tap for Mendoza’s first two starts, the Raiders may have wanted to throw Cousins to the wolves for those games before getting the No. 1 overall pick under center against Cleveland. Instead, the Vikings offered Vegas a third-round pick for Cousins and the Raiders couldn’t say no. Mendoza will make his first NFL start at home versus Seattle today. We expect him to be in the QB2 mix at some point this year, but it might take a few weeks given Vegas’s tough schedule.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Fernando Mendoza will take over as Raiders starter following the trade of Kirk Cousins to Minnesota.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: We’re sure we’ll get something more official from the team once Klint Kubiak has a press conference, but this is the obvious move. The No. 1 overall pick will face a gauntlet in his first three games, starting with the defending champion Seahawks in Week 10. It’s not an immediate re-draft add situations outside of deep leagues, but Mendoza could eventually factor into the re-draft formula this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Vikings acquired QB Kirk Cousins from the Raiders for a 2027 third-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: And where did that bring you? Back to me. Cousins will likely take over as Minnesota’s starting quarterback in the near future, if not immediately. When that happens, Kyler Murray will head back to the bench for a second straight season — he’s droppable in most leagues at this point. Fernando Mendoza will take over as starting quarterback for the Raiders. Mendoza is best approached cautiously at this point in fantasy leagues. Cousins’ value likely remains stagnant — Klint Kubiak was already getting quite a bit out of him — but he provides the Vikings with a better floor at quarterback than what they were getting so it’s obvious after watching Carson Wentz play last night why this is happening.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Raiders plan to start Kirk Cousins “as long as possible.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Schefter added that the team does not feel their current four-game losing streak is the fault of Cousins. He threw for nine touchdowns in the first three games, all of which the Raiders won. Cousins has just seven touchdowns over his past four outings, though he has only thrown two interceptions and taken just five sacks during that stretch. The Raiders are probably right to lay the blame elsewhere. Still, No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza is waiting in the wings. He is the future of the franchise, and his time grows closer with every Raiders loss. Vegas takes on the Jets this week. They then get a gauntlet of San Francisco, Seattle, and Denver. A 0-3 run that late in the season would likely spell the end of Cousins as their starter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said “Kirk Cousins is our quarterback,” when asked about the possibility of making a change at QB ahead of Week 8.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Rather than let any speculation linger, Kubiak was quick to shut down any idea of a switch at quarterback heading into Week 8’s game against the Jets. Kubiak said, “There is no controversy” at quarterback at this time, while also adding that “Fernando [Mendoza] is going to play football” at some point this season. Kubiak said the team does not have a timeline for when Mendoza could eventually make a start, and said Cousins continues to play well despite the team’s recent struggles. Cousins will be firmly on the streaming radar this week against a Jets team that just allowed 28 points to the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Raiders’ head coach Klint Kubiak said the team is “thinking about everything” in regards to the team’s QB situation after Week 7’s loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Kubiak was asked about the possibility of switching from Kirk Cousins to rookie No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza, and said the team is considering “everything” while also making it sound like their struggles were more of a team issue. Cousins struggled in the early part of Sunday’s loss to the Rams, but managed some late touchdowns in garbage time to save his stat line. If the Raiders are considering a switch, it’s possible we’ll learn their decision by Wednesday, when they begin preparing for their Week 8 game against the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Kirk Cousins is the starter “but if Fernando [Mendoza]'s number is called we have confidence in him.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: No real surprise after Mendoza’s mop-up appearance in Week 5. It doesn’t appear that he’s taken a major step towards unseating Cousins — who has played well — just yet. But it remains a reasonable bet to happen in the near future.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Fernando Mendoza completed 6-of-8 passes for 48 yards in relief of Kirk Cousins in Las Vegas’ Week 5 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: This doesn’t necessarily mean that Mendoza is going to take the reins this week; we expect Cousins to continue starting even if Raiders coach Klint Kubiak didn’t affirmatively get ahead of the situation in Sunday’s post-game. But Mendoza looked reasonable and this will obviously be something that will bubble up eventually. No. 1 overall picks don’t typically stay on benches too long.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor caught 2-of-2 targets for 25 yards in the Jets’ Week 11 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Taylor made a nice, leaping grab for 19 yards on the Jets’ third drive before chipping in with a six-yarder on the next drive. He is a reliable starter in real life, but tougher to trust in fantasy football. He is a touchdown-dependent TE2 against the Dolphins next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor caught all four of his targets for 20 yards in the Jets’ Week 10 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Taylor played 52 of the team’s 70 snaps in this game, with Kenyon Sadiq only playing 29. Sadiq did run a route on 23 dropbacks compared to 28 for Taylor, but it’s clear that Taylor is the top tight end on the Jets. It just doesn’t amount to a lot of volume on a bad offense with a trio of good wide receivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor caught 1-of-2 targets for 11 yards in the Jets’ Week 9 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Taylor ran a route on 22 of the team’s 39 drop backs while Kenyon Sadiq has 21 routes and caught all four of his targets. Splitting the TE1 role with Sadiq, Taylor won’t be fantasy viable in most formats next week against the Bills. He has four receptions over his past two games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Kenyon Sadiq caught all four of his targets for 49 yards in the Jets’ Week 9 loss against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Sadiq logged 21 pass routes on the day to Mason Taylor’s 22 routes. The two tight ends have largely split the TE1 role in the New York offense in recent weeks. Taylor had just one catch on two targets against Kansas City, while Sadiq got open down the seam a couple times and found himself wide open for Geno Smith. Sadiq, who had five receptions over his previous four outings, won’t be usable in most fantasy formats next week against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor (back) is not on the final injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Taylor’s contributions are far too volatile for him to be trusted in 12-team formats, but his presence hurts rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq’s fantasy-scoring outlook. Taylor does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor (back) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Taylor is firmly on track to play in Week 9 against the Chiefs. He will operate as the team’s top tight end, keeping intriguing rookie Kenyon Sadiq in the TE2 tier.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor (back) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: It’s likely a maintenance day for Taylor, who tallied three catches on five targets in Week 8. He has been running ahead of rookie Kenyon Sadiq in recent weeks, though his own fantasy has been hit or miss. Taylor has been held under 40 yards in three of his past four appearances. He erupted for 62 yards and two scores in the fourth. Barring a setback in practice, Taylor will be a low-end TE2 for Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor caught 3-of-5 targets for 19 yards in the Jets’ Week 8 loss to the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Taylor’s five targets were third on the team behind Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell, while fellow seam stretcher Kenyon Sadiq mustered only two looks. Taylor has become a weekly volume presence in an offense that attempts a lot of passes, but he has not established a particularly high floor while his spiked week odds remain practically nonexistent. He’s a TE2 by the letter of the law but not one we would be looking to start in Week 9 against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor caught 5-of-6 targets for 62 yards and two touchdowns in the Jets’ Week 7 loss to the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Taylor got off to a hot start on National Tight Ends Day by mossing Dolphins cornerback Jason Marshall Jr in the end zone. Not content with just one score, Taylor double-dipped with a leaping touchdown catch late in the fourth quarter. He also scored the two-point conversion after the play. Taylor is running well ahead of first-round rookie Kenyon Sadiq right now and there’s no reason to expect anything different in Week 8 versus the Raiders. Taylor will be in the TE2 mix next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor caught 4-of-6 targets for 33 yards in the Jets’ Week 6 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Taylor is now up to 7/57 in two games since returning from his thumb injury. First-round rookie Kenyon Sadiq, who missed most of Week 5 with a concussion, is 3/15 during the same timespan. This Jets tight end targets battle figures to oscillate back and forth, but Taylor is the preferred option for the time being. It’s still not resulting in more than desperation TE2 value.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq caught 3-of-3 targets for 30 yards in the Jets’ Week 11 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: The rookie tight end got going with a nine-yard catch between the hashes on the Jets’ second drive. He showed up again on the third drive, snagging a sidearm throw from Geno Smith behind the line of scrimmage before turning upfield and weaving through traffic for a 10-yard gain, bringing the offense into the red zone. He made a similar play on the fourth drive, taking a shallow crosser for 11 yards. Sadiq continues to flash intriguing post-catch traits while splitting time with Mason Taylor. Sadiq is stuck in the TE2 tier, but should play efficiently against the Dolphins next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq caught 1-of-2 targets for 3 yards in the Jets’ Week 10 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: Sadiq is becoming buried on the Jets’ depth chart. He did run a route on 23 dropbacks in this one, compared to 28 for Mason Taylor, but Taylor played 23 more snaps, and Sadiq also has to compete with three receivers for targets. He can’t be trusted in fantasy leagues right now and should not be on redraft rosters unless there’s an injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Mason Taylor caught all four of his targets for 20 yards in the Jets’ Week 10 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: Taylor played 52 of the team’s 70 snaps in this game, with Kenyon Sadiq only playing 29. Sadiq did run a route on 23 dropbacks compared to 28 for Taylor, but it’s clear that Taylor is the top tight end on the Jets. It just doesn’t amount to a lot of volume on a bad offense with a trio of good wide receivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Mason Taylor caught 1-of-2 targets for 11 yards in the Jets’ Week 9 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: Taylor ran a route on 22 of the team’s 39 drop backs while Kenyon Sadiq has 21 routes and caught all four of his targets. Splitting the TE1 role with Sadiq, Taylor won’t be fantasy viable in most formats next week against the Bills. He has four receptions over his past two games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq caught all four of his targets for 49 yards in the Jets’ Week 9 loss against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: Sadiq logged 21 pass routes on the day to Mason Taylor’s 22 routes. The two tight ends have largely split the TE1 role in the New York offense in recent weeks. Taylor had just one catch on two targets against Kansas City, while Sadiq got open down the seam a couple times and found himself wide open for Geno Smith. Sadiq, who had five receptions over his previous four outings, won’t be usable in most fantasy formats next week against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Mason Taylor (back) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: Taylor is firmly on track to play in Week 9 against the Chiefs. He will operate as the team’s top tight end, keeping intriguing rookie Kenyon Sadiq in the TE2 tier.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq caught a 22-yard pass in the Jets’ Week 8 loss to the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: Sadiq’s third quarter reception went down as one of just two targets for the rookie tight end. He was once again out-caught by Mason Taylor, though Taylor provided just 19 yards across his three grabs. Sadiq’s reception was an impressive, leaping catch against single coverage, but therein lies part of the problem: It’s taking spectacular acts for Sadiq to create fantasy value. He is sadly off the radar for the time being in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq caught his only target for six yards in the Jets’ Week 7 loss to the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: The first-round rookie was held to one catch for the second week in a row. He has four catches over his past four games. It wouldn’t be surprising for his role to expand as the season wears on, but there were no signs of that happening this week. He isn’t worth holding onto in most fantasy formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq caught 1-of-3 targets for 12 yards in the Jets’ Week 6 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: Although there was an injury-shortened appearance mixed in, Sadiq now has just three catches for 15 yards over his past three games. This, as Mason Taylor has caught nine balls for 57 yards over the past two weeks. Sadiq’s big-play ability is going to come back into play sooner rather than later, but he is unsurprisingly maxing out as a zero-floor TE2 in fantasy for the time being.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) is active for Week 6 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: Sadiq made quick work of the league’s concussion protocol, for better or worse. With Omar Cooper Jr. also active vs. the Pats, Sadiq isn’t much more than a low-end TE2 prayer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sterling-s.headline: Sterling Shepard caught 2-of-2 targets for 24 yards and two touchdowns in the Jets’ Week 11 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sterling-s.analysis: The Jets’ practice squad veteran seized the moment with Omar Cooper (ankle) and Isaiah Williams (ribs) sidelined today, scoring twice against the Chargers. The first was a sliding scramble-drill snag in the front of the end zone. On the second, Sterling ran a shallow crossing route from the right slot, caught the pass, turned upfield and simply outran Chargers CB Donte Jackson. Shepard is not on the FLEX radar next week against the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sterling-s.headline: Jets signed WR Sterling Shepard to their practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sterling-s.analysis: The 33-year-old will be a short-term hedge against losing Omar Cooper Jr. and it sounds like he will be given a chance to come up as an elevation over the next two weeks if the Jets like what they see in practice.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sterling-s.headline: Texans released WR Sterling Shepard.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sterling-s.analysis: He lasted just nine days with the team. Shepard was signed before the Kayshon Boutte trade and the Boutte trade can be looked at as the end of any real chance for him to make the team. Shepard’s free agency was fairly slow and at 33 years old it wouldn’t be surprising if he had to sign to a practice squad if he wanted to keep playing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sterling-s.headline: Texans signed WR Zay Jones, formerly of the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sterling-s.analysis: Jones and former Buccaneers WR Sterling Shepard have been brought in to help shore up the Texans’ wide receiver corps. Second-year WR Jayden Higgins (knee) was placed on injured reserve today. The Texans are also still trying to figure out what they have in WR Tank Dell (knee), and WR Jaylin Noel (finger/hamstring) missed time in training camp with a pair of injuries. Jones is coming off a season-ending Achilles tendon rupture. Neither he nor Shepard are worth drafting.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sterling-s.headline: Free agent WR Josh Reynolds worked out for the Texans on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sterling-s.analysis: Reynolds, 31, was joined by WR Sterling Shepard, 33, today. Reynolds caught 11 passes for 101 yards with the Jets last year. Shepard caught 39 passes for 371 yards and one touchdown with the Buccaneers last year. Neither player would be on the fantasy radar if they were signed.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sterling-s.headline: Ravens signed WR Chris Moore, formerly of the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sterling-s.analysis: Moore caught 11 passes with the Commanders last season. He initially entered the NFL as a 2016 fourth-round pick with the Ravens, and spent five seasons in Baltimore. The Ravens brought him aboard today after a workout that also included free agent WRs Sterling Shepard and Dante Pettis.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sterling-s.headline: Buccaneers declared QB Connor Bazelak, TE Devin Culp, G Elijah Klein, WR Sterling Shepard, DL Elijah Simmons, LB Anthony Walker, and S Rashad Wisdom inactive for Week 16 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sterling-s.analysis: Shepard and Culp headline the Bucs’ healthy scratch list for Week 16. With a fully healthy wide receiver group and Cade Otton back in the lineup, neither are needed against the Panthers. There are no injury inactives for the Bucs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sterling-s.headline: Buccaneers WR Sterling Shepard (shoulder) is not on Tampa Bay’s final Week 12 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sterling-s.analysis: He got in full sessions on both Thursday and Friday. Shepard would retain some low-end PPR scam juice if Chris Godwin remains sidelined this weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sterling-s.headline: Buccaneers WR Sterling Shepard (shoulder) was limited in Wednesday’s walk-through practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sterling-s.analysis: Shepard and OT Tristan Wirfs popped up on the injury report with shoulder injuries on Wednesday. The Bucs held a walk-through, so practice designations were estimates, but still important to note. Shepard has a role as long as Chris Godwin (fibula) remains out, while Wirfs is the team’s franchise left tackle. Neither are in danger of missing Week 12 yet, barring setbacks later in the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sterling-s.headline: Sterling Shepard caught 4-of-5 targets for 54 yards in a Week 11 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sterling-s.analysis: Shepard was tied for second on the team in targets and led the team in receiving yards. Much of his work was done on third-and-long, where he was able to find soft spots in the Bills’ overly soft zone defense. Shepard has stepped into a bigger role with Mike Evans and Chris Godwin injured, but it hasn’t led to much fantasy value.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Adonai Mitchell caught 2-of-3 targets for 30 yards in the Jets’ Week 11 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: Mitchell bagged a 21-yard catch via a corner route on the opening drive. He should have bested it with a 40-plus-yard touchdown catch on the Jets’ fifth drive via another corner route, but Geno Smith overthrew him. Brutal. Mitchell’s downfield role lends itself to volatility, but there’s not much more he could have done there. He had his coverage defender beat. Mitchell remains a volatile yet capable FLEX option in Week 12 against the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Omar Cooper, Jr. (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: Cooper, who picked up his latest injury last week against the Bills, appears to be a long shot for Week 11 against the Chargers. That would leave Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell as the clear top targets for Geno Smith, if Smith is able to play through his own ankle injury. Wilson and Mitchell last week combined for 87 percent of the Jets’ air yards and 51 percent of the team’s targets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Adonai Mitchell caught 3-of-8 targets for 59 yards in the Jets’ Week 10 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: One of the incomplete passes was one that hit Mitchell in the hands, and he had two feet in bounds, but he let go of the ball to readjust his grip and was unable to remain in bounds, wiping out a 15-yard gain. With Omar Cooper Jr. leaving this game with an ankle injury, Mitchell could have a more dependable role next week against the Chargers, which would put him on the FLEX radar.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Adonai Mitchell (knee) is active for Week 10 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: Mitchell was expected to play, but now we have confirmation that he will. With Garrett Wilson (concussion) and Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) also active, it’s unclear which Jets receiver will be most productive in a good matchup. That makes Mitchell a boom-or-bust FLEX option in fantasy leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reports Adonai Mitchell (knee) is expected to play in Week 10 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: Mitchell remains questionable with a knee injury that put him on the injury report after getting in a full practice Friday. However concerning Mitchell’s new injury seemed, he’s expected to play, according to Zenitz. With Garrett Wilson (concussion) and Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) also expected to play, Mitchell is a boom-or-bust dart throw at best in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Adonai Mitchell (knee) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: Mitchell practiced in full today, but was added to the injury report with a new knee issue. This is a little concerning. The team could be trying to collect more info right now. We expect to hear more later today or at some point tomorrow. At this point, Mitchell must be viewed as firmly in the questionable column.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Adonai Mitchell didn’t catch any of his seven targets in the Jets’ Week 9 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: A week after going ballistic against the Raiders, the high-variance Mitchell couldn’t come up with a grab in an embarrassing effort for a Jets offense that was without Garrett Wilson (concussion). If your fantasy league awards points for air yards, Mitchell would have been a week winner against Kansas City. Alas, he could not convert any of that opportunity into real-life production, though he came awfully close on a couple well-thrown Geno Smith downfield balls. He was second on the team in targets, trailing Omar Cooper (11). Mitchell next week against the Bills will remain a boom-bust WR3 option. Buffalo has struggled against boundary receivers all season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Adonai Mitchell caught 7-of-9 targets for 142 yards and a touchdown in the Jets’ Week 8 loss to the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: Looking to bounce back from a Week 7 doughnut in his return from a marathon injury absence, Mitchell responded with by far the best game of his career. This, even as one of his two missed connections was a heinous deep drop. Geno Smith never stopped looking his way, and the quarterback was rewarded with multiple chunk gains. Smith once again failed to get fully in sync with Garrett Wilson. Smith also targeted Omar Cooper Jr. zero times. That was hard to see coming, and will be difficult to sustain going forward, keeping Mitchell as more of a boom/bust WR3/4 than weekly must start. This blow-up effort confirmed he still has life in 12-team leagues, however. That will include for Week 9 against a Chiefs defense that is admittedly much better than Vegas’ porous unit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Adonai Mitchell failed to catch any of his three targets in the Jets’ Week 7 loss to the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: To add insult to injury, Mitchell had a two-point conversion catch called back because of a penalty. Omar Cooper Jr. once again stole the show, reeling in several long catches en route to his second 100-yard game in a row. Playing in his first game in over a month, Mitchell did not appear awfully involved in the team’s game plan. The hope will be that he earns more opportunities next week, but Cooper Jr. may have already cemented himself as the team’s No. 2 receiver. Mitchell will be stuck in the WR5 ranks when he takes on the Raiders next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Adonai Mitchell (finger) will play in Week 7 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: Mitchell has been sidelined since injuring his finger in preparation for the Jets’ Week 3 game against the Lions. It was incredibly unfortunate time for Mitchell and his fantasy managers, as his injury came just days after he went for 6-63-0 on 12 targets against the Packers. Mitchell’s return could complicate things for Omar Cooper’s fantasy managers after Cooper broke out for 6-103-1 against the Patriots last week. The Jets rank 13th in the league in plays run from 11-personnel (209) through the first six weeks of the season, which means both Mitchell and Cooper should see plenty of snaps. That said, neither player should be viewed as anything more than a WR3/FLEX play until we see how the target distribution looks with both players active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Garrett Wilson caught 3-of-5 targets for 39 yards in the Jets’ Week 11 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: Wilson generated a decent amount of his receiving yardage after the catch today. He spun off contact and broke another tackle on his 19-yard gain, and also added yards after the catch on a 12-yarder. His first incompletion was a shallow crosser on third down from the Chargers’ 32-yard line, which his coverage defender deserves credit for breaking up. The second incompletion was a desperation heave by Geno Smith under pressure from the Chargers’ six-yard line. The ball was badly overthrown to Wilson, just in front of the end zone, though. He had no chance of catching it. Wilson is a WR2 against the Dolphins in Week 12.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Garrett Wilson caught 7-of-14 targets for 106 yards in the Jets’ Week 10 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: No other Jets player had more than seven targets, so Wilson was the clear focus of the passing attack. That continued when Cade Klubnik came into the game as well. Wilson made a few tough catches and was targeted twice in the end zone as well. Unfortunately, the wide receiver was also charged with a fumble on a botched hook-and-ladder play where he was hit as he was attempting the pitch, which went astray and was recovered by the Bills. Wilson remains the clear top option in this passing attack and could still be a low-end WR2 with Klubnik under center next week against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Garrett Wilson cleared the NFL’s concussion protocol and will play in Week 10 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: Wilson missed Week 9 because of the concussion but has cleared the league’s concussion protocol ahead of today’s game. Jets coach Aaron Glenn told reporters on Friday he expected Wilson to play, so this doesn’t come as much of a surprise. In a potential shootout with the Bills, Wilson will push for a high-end WR2 designation this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Garrett Wilson (concussion) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: All three of the Jets’ starting wide receivers are questionable to play, though Wilson practiced in full practice and is expected to play. Wilson could handle a hefty workload if he is indeed cleared to play, as expected, and one or two of the others are limited or ruled out. Wilson is a WR2 this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said he is “confident” that Garrett Wilson (concussion) will play in Week 10 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: Glenn said Wilson has one more step to clear before he is out of the league’s concussion protocol. Wilson missed last week’s game against the Chiefs due to his brain injury, but has practiced in a limited capacity twice this week and is trending toward a return. We will get a final update on Wilson once he has officially cleared the protocol, but fantasy managers can start him as a mid-to-high-end WR2 in a game that could feature plenty of points against a high-powered Bills offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Garrett Wilson (concussion) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: Wilson still needs to be officially cleared from concussion protocol to play, but two limited sessions have him with a real chance to be active in Week 10 after missing Week 9. If he can play, Wilson will likely be an upside fantasy WR2 against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: ESPN’s Rich Cimini reports the 49ers and Chiefs “were interested” in Garrett Wilson ahead of the trade deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: The Jets made it clear they were not moving Wilson early in the process, so we can’t imagine trade talks between them and either team made it very far. Cimini notes that the Jets could revisit a Wilson trade in the offseason. Wilson told reporters earlier this year that he loves it in New York, but he loves winning more. The Jets haven’t done much of that since Wilson was drafted. This will be a storyline to watch in the offseason, though we suspect he’ll remain in New York for the foreseeable future.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said he’s “very hopeful” Garrett Wilson (concussion) will play in Week 10 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: Wilson was sidelined in last week’s loss to Kansas City with the head injury he sustained in Week 8. Omar Cooper, Jr. functioned as the team’s top receiver with Wilson sidelined while Adonai Mitchell couldn’t reel in any of his seven targets from Geno Smith. Wilson would be a top-24 option in Week 10 against Buffalo if he can return to action. The Bills secondary allows the 13th highest fantasy points per target to boundary wideouts this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Jets declared Garrett Wilson, Tim Patrick, Nahshon Wright, Joseph Ossai, Trevin Wallace, Kohl Levao, and Blake Freeland inactive for Week 9 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: Wilson suffered a head injury last week and did not practice this week as he remained in the NFL’s concussion protocol. Look for Omar Cooper, Jr. and Adonai Mitchell to see more routes and targets against a tough KC secondary. Mitchell is likely to function as the team’s top wideout with Wilson sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Garrett Wilson (concussion) will not play in Week 9 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: Wilson has not practiced this week and has now been ruled out for Sunday’s game against the Chiefs. Wilson has caught 43 passes for 527 yards and three touchdowns this season and saw 12 targets in last week’s loss to the Raiders. His absence means both Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper should see expanded roles, but both players will be hard to trust as anything more than WR3s against a stout Chiefs defense. In addition to Wilson, the Jets also ruled out LB Trevin Wallace (groin) for Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.headline: Geno Smith completed 17-of-21 passes for 176 yards and three touchdowns in the Jets’ 27-24, Week 11 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.analysis: The Jets dialed up a run-heavy game plan with Smith playing through an ankle injury suffered last weekend. The ailment didn’t stop Smith from playing efficiently against the Chargers, though. Smith linked up with Breece Hall and Sterling Shepard (twice) for touchdowns today. Smith overthrew Adonai Mitchell on what could have been a 40-plus-yard end zone target, but luckily, Breece Hall ripped off a 26-yarder that set up one of Smith’s touchdown passes to Shepard, who was elevated from the practice squad this week. Smith warrants QB2 treatment against the Dolphins in Week 12.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.headline: Geno Smith (ankle) is not on the Jets’ final injury report and will play in Week 11 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.analysis: The Jets’ starting quarterback was limited on Wednesday and Thursday before upgrading to full participation on Friday. Smith has turned in a couple of decent games this season, but he’s currently on a two-game skid in which he has failed to beat 165 passing yards and/or throw a touchdown. He is stuck in the QB2 tier despite six teams being on bye this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Geno Smith (ankle) is trending toward playing in Week 11 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.analysis: We should have the final word on Smith’s status shortly, but Glenn said his QB1 will log another practice on Friday, which should be enough for him to play on Sunday against the Chargers. Smith has struggled in recent weeks, throwing for 313 scoreless yards, but could have a chance to bounce back against a woeful Chargers defense that has allowed the 10th-most passing yards and the fifth-most net yards per attempt this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.headline: Geno Smith (ankle) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.analysis: Smith is tentatively on track to play in the Jets’ Week 11 game against the Chargers, though his mobility could be somewhat impacted if this is indeed the case. Smith would warrant QB2 treatment if active. He is backed up by Cade Klubnik.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn would not say if Geno Smith (ankle) will start in Week 11.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.analysis: Smith suffered the ankle injury in last week’s loss to Buffalo and appears to be iffy for Sunday against the Chargers. Smith on Wednesday was a limited participant in practice, which is usually good news for a player’s Sunday availability. If Smith is sidelined against the Bolts, look for Cade Klubnik to get the start. Klubnik last week completed 11 of his 20 attempts for 137 yards and an interception. His aDOT was 11.3, the third highest of Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Geno Smith (ankle) will start in Week 11 against the Chargers if he is healthy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.analysis: Smith is having tests on his ankle after getting banged up in Week 10’s loss to the Bills. Smith was briefly evaluated for a concussion in Sunday’s game, only to return to the field and be knocked out in the third quarter with his ankle injury. Smith has struggled as of late, failing to throw a touchdown in his last two games while throwing for just 313 yards. Rookie Cade Klubnik, who threw for 137 yards and one interception while also taking three sacks, didn’t fare much better in Smith’s absence, but Smith is undoubtedly the better of the two QBs on the roster. All Jets pass-catchers would receive a slight downgrade next week if Smith is sidelined against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.headline: Geno Smith went to the locker room with an ankle injury during Week 10 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.analysis: Smith was evaluated for a concussion during halftime but cleared to return. On his first drive back in the third quarter, he took another big hit from safety Cole Bishop and limped off the field into the blue medical tent. He then went into the locker room, which will leave Cade Klubnik as the Jets’ only healthy quarterback on the roster. If Smith is done for the day, he will have completed 12-for-21 passes for 148 yards during his two quarters of play. The Jets will hope he can return next week against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.headline: Geno Smith cleared concussion protocol and returned to Week 10 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.analysis: Smith took a big hit on the Jets’ last play of the first half and was evaluated for a concussion at halftime. Rookie Cade Klubnik played the first drive and led the Jets on a 61-yard drive that ended in a field goal. However, with Smith cleared to return, Klubnik will head back to the bench.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.headline: Geno Smith is being evaluated for a concussion in Week 10 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.analysis: Smith took a huge hit on the final offensive play of the second quarter when he was rolling out of the pocket. He was down on the field for a while before heading into the medical tent. Cade Klubnik is in the game for the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.headline: Geno Smith completed 18-of-32 attempts for 162 yards in the Jets’ Week 9 loss to the Chiefs, adding one rush for eight yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.analysis: The 36-year-old Smith was as immobile as ever, taking five sacks on the day and narrowly avoiding a half dozen others. Some of that was the Jets offensive line being overwhelmed against an elite KC pass rush; some of it was Smith refusing to get rid of the ball as the pocket collapsed. Smith playing without Garrett Wilson (concussion) was irate on the sideline in the fourth quarter with the Jets down multiple scores, barking at coaches and teammates alike. He had a negative EPA per drop back on the day. Smith should be seen as a matchup-dependent fantasy play. He will be streamable in Week 10 against a vulnerable Buffalo secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-ellio.headline: Jake Elliott made all four of his field goal attempts in the Eagles’ Week 11 win against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-ellio.analysis: Elliott also made his lone extra point attempt in the victory. Elliott drilled a couple long kicks through the wind in Philadelphia as he continued a solid 2026 campaign. He’s made 11 of his 12 field goal tries on the season. Sunday marked the first time in 2026 in which Elliott made more than two field goal attempts in a game. He’ll be a decent fantasy option in Week 12 against Dallas.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-ellio.headline: Jake Elliott (ankle) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-ellio.analysis: The Eagles’ kicker practiced in full today, which was good to see. Given the state of the Eagles’ offense, he may not have many field goal attempts this week, though. Kickers tend to benefit from playing on teams with stellar offenses. The Eagles no longer have one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-ellio.headline: Jake Elliott (ankle) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-ellio.analysis: Even if Elliott is active for the Eagles’ Week 9 game against the Giants, he makes for an uncomfortable start. The offense is struggling with so many starters ailing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-ellio.headline: Jake Elliot (ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-ellio.analysis: Elliot was listed as a limited participant for the Eagles’ Wednesday practice. The 31-year-old has made 6-of-7 field goals this season and all 17 extra points. He is still trending to play in Week 9, but if the Eagles add another kicker sometime this week, that would indicate Elliot’s ankle injury is a real issue.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-ellio.headline: Eagles and K Jake Elliott agreed to a reworked contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-ellio.analysis: Per NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo, Elliott’s base salary went down from $6 million to $5 million. In turn, the Eagles guaranteed all of the money. Elliott struggled in 2025, hitting on just 20-of-27 field goal attempts. Four of his misses came from 50+ yards out. This season could be a make-or-break campaign for Elliott.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-ellio.headline: Jake Elliott missed his only field goal attempt and made all three of his extra point attempts in the Eagles’ Week 12 loss against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-ellio.analysis: Elliott narrowly missed on a 52-yard attempt in the second half as the Eagles choked away a big lead to the Cowboys. He’s now missed three of his 14 field goal tries on the season. The Eagles’ red zone aggressiveness and use of the tush push near the goal line makes Elliott a dicey weekly bet for fantasy purposes. Elliott has one or zero field goal attempts in eight games this season. He should remain on waiver wires in Week 13 against Chicago.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-ellio.headline: Eagles signed K Jake Elliott to a four-year, $24 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-ellio.analysis: Per ESPN’s Adam Schefter, the deal ties Elliott with Justin Tucker for the crown of highest-paid kicker in NFL history. Elliott went 30-of-32 on field goal tries this year, with only one of his two misses coming from inside 50 yards. He hit all but one of his 46 PATs. The veteran kicker also takes kickoffs for Philly. Despite the Eagles’ downturn in 2023, Elliott was a top-five fantasy kicker. He will rank among the league’s top fantasy options at the position heading into 2024.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-ellio.headline: Eagles restructured K Jake Elliott’s contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-ellio.analysis: The Eagles save $2.492 million against the cap with the restructuring of Elliott’s deal. The veteran kicker converted on 20-of-23 field goal attempts for the Eagles last season and has converted on 89.3% of his field goal attempts since 2021.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-ellio.headline: K Jake Elliott (ankle) is off Philadelphia’s final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-ellio.analysis: He’ll be Philadelphia’s kicker for Week 6’s game against the Cowboys after missing Week 5. He’s not a terrible streamer, but Dallas’ defense has been imposing enough that it’s hard to call him an easy streamer for Week 6 if he was dropped in your league.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-ellio.headline: Jake Elliott (ankle) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-ellio.analysis: Elliott did kick at Eagles practice per several reporters on the scene with video evidence. There’s been no mention of Elliott’s status in interviews so far. Cameron Dicker is the backup Eagles kicker and would get another go against the Cowboys if Elliott can’t go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adam-butle.headline: Adam Butler (concussion) will not return to the Raiders’ Week 11 game against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adam-butle.analysis: Fellow defensive tackle Tim Keenan (knee) is also done for the day. The Raiders were already one of the best matchups for running backs entering Week 11. Expect the Broncos to lean on Jonah Coleman to close this game out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adam-butle.headline: Raiders declared TE Michael Mayer, RB Zamir White, QB Aidan O’Connell, CB Darnay Holmes, LB Jamin Davis, OG Jordan Meredith and DT Tonka Hemingway inactive for Week 13 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adam-butle.analysis: Mayer was unable to practice all week, rehabbing an ankle injury. He has had bouts of fantasy relevance this year when Brock Bowers has been sidelined, but the Raiders haven’t built a consistent enough passing game for anyone but Bowers to be an easy start. O’Connell will be available to the team as the emergency third quarterback. Holmes’ illness-induced absence against a talented Chargers passing attack is unfortunate. Raiders DT Adam Butler (illness) is active, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adam-butle.headline: Raiders re-signed DT Adam Butler to a three-year, $16.5 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adam-butle.analysis: The deal includes $11 million guaranteed. Although it was his first season on the wrong side of 30, Butler became a weekly starter for the first time in his career last year. He was more than just a two-down run stuffer, though that was his primary objective. Butler has nevertheless managed five sacks each of the past two seasons. He’s a dependable interior option for new coach Pete Carroll even if he ultimately doesn’t match last year’s 856 snaps.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adam-butle.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports the Raiders have re-signed DT Adam Butler to a one-year deal.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adam-butle.analysis: Butler returns to Las Vegas where he had nice season in 2023 season racking up five sacks. He’ll team up with Maxx Crosby and newly acquired Christian Wilkins for what should be one of the most dominant fronts in the NFL.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adam-butle.headline: Dolphins signed DL Adam Butler, formerly of the Patriots, to a two-year contract worth up to $9.5 million.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adam-butle.analysis: Butler is the latest former Pat to join Brian Flores in Miami. He was durable in New England, playing all 16 regular season games in three of his four years there. Butler will join a Dolphins defensive line graded by Pro Football Focus as the league’s 13th best rush defense and 14th best pass rushing unit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adam-butle.headline: Patriots DT Adam Butler officially signed his second-round tender.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adam-butle.analysis: The tender is worth $3.26 million. The Patriots added Beau Allen to their defensive trenches but still figure to lean on Butler, fresh off career-highs in sacks (6) and tackles (26) in his third year with the team, following the loss of Danny Shelton to Detroit. Byron Cowart could also rotate in on occasion.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adam-butle.headline: Patriots extended a second-round tender to restricted free agent DT Adam Butler.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adam-butle.analysis: 26 in April, Butler notched career-highs in tackles (26) and sacks (6) in his third year off the bench with the Patriots last season. He’ll make $3.251 million in 2020 — a questionable amount to gift the former undrafted defensive tackle given his likely lack of interest if New England had extended an original-round tender.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adam-butle.headline: ESPN Boston reports the Patriots are expected to tender restricted free agent DT Adam Butler at the second-round level.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adam-butle.analysis: Butler set season highs with six sacks in a sub-package role last year. Undrafted in 2017, the Patriots would risk not getting any compensation if they didn’t tender Butler at the second-round level. There’s unlikely to be interest in 25-year-old Butler for that price.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Gunnar Helm caught 2-of-3 targets for 14 yards in the Titans’ Week 11 loss to the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: 14 of Helm’s 23 catches on the year have come in the past four weeks. It’s been a good start for a second-year pro trying to create some TE2 relevance but not really enough, even in a down year for the position. With all 32 teams active for Week 12 and bye weeks lingering on for only two more Sundays after that, Helm is facing long odds of becoming 12-team league relevant.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Gunnar Helm caught all four of his targets for 23 yards in the Titans’ Week 10 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Helm is up to 16 catches over his past four games, but he’s still looking for his first touchdown of the year. Daniel Bellinger stole a short score in this game. Helm also has just one game over 30 yards to his name. He’s developed a modest PPR floor, but there’s no ceiling to be had headed into his Week 11 date with the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) will not play in Week 10 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Head coach Robert Saleh said he is hopeful Tate will be able to return in Week 11 when the Titans visit the Cowboys, but his availability for that game will be determined once the Titans begin prepping for Dallas. In the meantime, the Titans will likely go with Wan’Dale Robinson and Chimere Dike as their top two wideouts after the pair led the team in routes run in Week 8 against the Bengals, with Elic Ayomanor also seeing some work (30 routes). Playing against a stout Jaguars defense will make all of the Titans’ receivers hard to trust as anything more than WR3/WR4 plays, while TE Gunnar Helm could also see more work after earning a season-high eight targets vs. the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Gunnar Helm caught 5-of-9 targets for 76 yards in the Titans’ Week 8 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Helm saw career-highs in targets and receiving yards in a high-scoring game against the Bengals. He saw a few targets in the flats but was targeted downfield multiple times, catching two passes of at least 24 yards. Helm also caught a two-point conversion in the fourth quarter. He is the Titans primary pass-catching tight end and saw heavy usage in a pass-heavy game script. Fantasy managers should not anticipate more game scripts like this for the Titans but Helm is a deep league streaming tight end option once the Titans come out of a Week 9 bye week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Gunnar Helm caught 3-of-4 targets for 24 yards in the Titans’ Week 7 loss to the Browns.
