https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Running a route on 23 of the team’s 34 drop backs, Helm was a little more involved than usual in the Titans’ low-octane passing attack. With fewer than 30 receiving yards in every game this season, Helm should not be rostered in any fantasy format for now. He’s been targeted on just 12 percent of his routes in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Gunnar Helm failed to catch his only target in Tennessee’s Week 5 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: 45 snaps, one target. Helm has somehow grown less relevant than his 4/28 Week 1 showing would have even suggested. He can be dropped in most leagues at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Gunnar Helm caught 2-of-4 targets for 14 yards in the Titans’ Week 3 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Helm continued to split reps with Daniel Bellinger, who also caught two passes today. Helm hasn’t topped 30 yards in a game this year and his four catches in Week 1 remain a high-water mark. He isn’t even in the TE2 mix for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Gunnar Helm caught 2-of-2 targets for 13 yards in the Titans’ Week 2 loss to the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Helm is now sitting on a scoreless 6/41 through the Titans’ first two contests. Helm is an intriguing second-year pro, but there’s not going to be much intrigue in the Titans’ offense for the time being. 24-year-old Helm is best left on 12-team league waiver wires head of Week 3 vs. the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Gunnar Helm caught 4-of-5 targets for 28 yards in the Titans’ Week 1 loss to the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Helm gobbled up snaps as he tied Carnell Tate for the second most Titans receptions on an afternoon where Cam Ward completed just 19 passes. Helm is looking heavily involved in the offense, it’s just unclear if that will even amount to anything in this situation. Week 2 is going to be tough against the Eagles before a slightly more forgiving Week 3 date with the Giants. For now, Helm is not a recommended TE2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Titans TE Gunnar Helm (toe) will not play in Tennessee’s Week 18 game against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Helm finishes a successful rookie season with a 44/357/2 slash line, and looked to be making a climb up Tennessee’s target pecking order before injuries largely derailed his final month. It’s hard to rely on anything in Tennessee’s offense until we see exactly what happens with the coaching staff, but there are offseason runouts that will put Helm as a high-end TE2 with Chig Oknokwo slated for free agency.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.headline: Elic Ayomanor caught 3-of-3 targets for 27 yards in the Titans’ Week 11 loss to the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.analysis: The three-catch effort was Ayomanor’s fourth straight, though he has exceeded three just once during that timespan. He is also averaging only 46 yards in the process, and has not found the end zone. Translation, Ayomanor’s play has been better, but not better enough you are seriously considering him as a WR4. That is especially true for slates like Week 12 where all 32 teams will be active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.headline: Titans head coach Robert Saleh said Wan’Dale Robinson (ankle) is out for the remainder of the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.analysis: Robinson’s Week 10 ankle injury will end a disappointing 2026 campaign in a low-octane Tennessee offense. Robinson over nine games managed 32 receptions for 272 yards and three touchdowns. He had just three games with more than 50 receiving yards. His absence will open up more snaps and routes from Xavier Restrepo, while Elic Ayomanor and Carnell Tate — who could be back soon from a shoulder issue — remain the team’s top two wideouts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.headline: Elic Ayomanor caught 5-of-10 targets for 79 yards in the Titans’ Week 10 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.analysis: Ayomanor didn’t do much in Carnell Tate’s absence the last time he took the field. He stepped up as the Titans’ clear WR1 in this game. Ayomanor led the team in all receiving categories except touchdowns. He nearly led the way in scoring as well, but the Jags tracked him down inside the five-yard line on his 50-yard catch. Ayomanor will move into the FLEX mix if Tate remains out for Week 11 against the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) will not play in Week 10 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.analysis: Head coach Robert Saleh said he is hopeful Tate will be able to return in Week 11 when the Titans visit the Cowboys, but his availability for that game will be determined once the Titans begin prepping for Dallas. In the meantime, the Titans will likely go with Wan’Dale Robinson and Chimere Dike as their top two wideouts after the pair led the team in routes run in Week 8 against the Bengals, with Elic Ayomanor also seeing some work (30 routes). Playing against a stout Jaguars defense will make all of the Titans’ receivers hard to trust as anything more than WR3/WR4 plays, while TE Gunnar Helm could also see more work after earning a season-high eight targets vs. the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.headline: Calvin Ridley (hip) is questionable for Tennessee’s Week 8 game against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.analysis: He got in a full session on Friday and would seem to be trending towards playing. With Carnell Tate down this week, Elic Ayomanor is probably the Titans dart throw wideout for the desperate against the Bengals if you’re choosing between him or Ridley.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.headline: Elic Ayomanor caught 3-of-7 targets for 44 yards in the Titans’ Week 7 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.analysis: Ayomanor has shown signs of life of late in a Titans offense operating quickly in recent weeks. Against the Browns he tied Carnell Tate for the team lead in targets while running a route on nearly 90 percent of the team’s drop backs; it seems that Cam Ward trusts him more than Calvin Ridley (hip), who missed this game. Even with more involvement in the Tennessee offense, Ayomanor should remain on the waiver wire in most fantasy formats ahead of the Titans’ Week 8 matchup against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.headline: Elic Ayomanor caught 1-of-3 targets for 11 yards in the Titans’ Week 3 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.analysis: It goes down as his second one-catch, three-target, 11-yard game of the season. He posted those exact numbers in Week 1, though with a touchdown for good measure. Ayomanor popped for 69 yards in Week 2 but failed to find the big play in this game, cratering his numbers. As the WR3 on one of the worst offenses in football, he is not on the fantasy radar for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.headline: Elic Ayomanor caught 2-of-3 targets for 69 yards in the Titans’ Week 2 loss to the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.analysis: One week after finding the end zone, Ayomanor led the Titans in receiving as they nearly upset the Birds. 41 of his yards came on an impressive leaping grab over Marcus Epps. Good stuff, but there’s not going to be much “good stuff” in this limited attack. Ayomanor should also routinely be out-targeted and out-gained by both Carnell Tate and Wan’Dale Robinson. Even in 14-team leagues, Ayomanor is probably off the re-draft radar.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.headline: Elic Ayomanor caught 1-of-3 targets for an 11-yard touchdown in the Titans’ Week 1 loss to the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.analysis: Ayomanor’s score came deep into garbage time with the Titans trailing 23-3. 23-year-old Ayomanor had an impressive rookie year for a fourth-round pick in 2025, but he’s now buried behind Carnell Tate and Wan’Dale Robinson in the Titans’ receiver corps. This is not an offense that is going to be producing consistent production out of the No. 3 receiver spot. We’ll let you know if Ayomanor becomes 12-team league relevant, but don’t count on it.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.headline: Titans WR Elic Ayomanor (shoulder) resumed practicing on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elic-ayomanor/.analysis: Per ESPN’s Turron Davenport, Ayomanor was in the huddle early at today’s practice, which is a good sign. The second-year wide receiver left practice early yesterday after seemingly injuring his left shoulder. He appears to be good to go and will now resume competing for a starting role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Calvin Ridley caught 5-of-6 targets for 68 yards and a touchdown in the Titans’ Week 11 loss to the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: Ridley entered the game with only six catches for 91 scoreless yards on the season, so he nearly doubled his 2026 production. The highlight was a 12-yard touchdown in garbage time that just happened to be one of the most insane throws of the year. Rolling near the sideline, Cam Ward made a cross-field, cross-body pass to find Ridley on the opposite side of the field in the end zone. It was an easy catch. Good stuff, though nearly all of Ridley’s production came with the Titans down multiple scores in the fourth quarter. The offense is playing better, but not better enough that Ridley is set to return to 12-team league relevance.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Calvin Ridley said he does not know if he will face charges related to his altercation at the Nashville International Airport.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: Ridley told reporters that he was trying to get his keys from the valet at the airport. They were giving him a hard time, so he took the keys out of the valet’s hands. The valet claims the altercation broke his finger. Ridley was at practice today and head coach Robert Saleh called it a “very minor miscommunication.” It doesn’t sound like the incident will keep Ridley off the field for now, though he hasn’t made much of an impact this year anyway.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Titans head coach Robert Saleh said Calvin Ridley was involved in an “unfortunate” incident at Nashville airport.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: Saleh didn’t get into the details of the matter, instead opting to say it was a “very minor miscommunication” that is “now in the hands of law enforcement.” Ridley, 31, has caught 6-of-12 targets for 91 scoreless yards this season and could find himself on the move ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline. That said, he’s far from the difference-making player he was early in his career and is fourth among Titans receivers in routes run (124) this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Titans WR Calvin Ridley “could be had for a late-round pick.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: The Titans are listening on Ridley, who could be had for a late-round pick, according to Schefter. The Chiefs, Steelers and 49ers are the most likely teams to be in the market for a wide receiver ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline. The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero also reported that multiple wide receivers could be traded before the deadline and listed Ridley as a name to watch.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer thinks the Titans might be willing to trade away Tony Pollard in exchange for a fourth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: Breer believes a fourth-round pick “seems like a lot” to give up for an aging running back who is set to enter free agency at the end of the year. So, Pollard might end up staying in Tennessee. Breer adds that the Titans could also consider trading away Calvin Ridley for a worse Day 3 pick, but he isn’t sure if the team is eager to get rid of pass catchers while they are attempting to develop their young quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins believes the Rams must find a way to trade for a wide receiver before the November 10th deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: The Rams’ resources are thin. They already traded away their 2027 first- and second-round picks, their 2028 second-round pick and their 2029 third-round pick. They also have just $8,000 in 2026 salary cap space, so restructuring the potential new add’s deal would be required. Atkins believes the Rams should consider Josh Downs as the top option due to his ability to beat man coverage and contribute as a returner. Other options, according to Atkins, include Calvin Ridley, Keenan Allen and Jauan Jennings, “for the likely cost of a Day 3 pick.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Calvin Ridley caught 1-of-3 targets for 20 yards in the Titans’ Week 8 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: Ridley was active after dealing with a hip injury this week, seeing the fourth-most snaps among Titans wide receivers. He finished the game with a drop and one reception. The veteran is a candidate to be traded but has not been offering much by way of fantasy production. Ridley can be left on fantasy benches heading into the Titans’ Week 9 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Calvin Ridley (hip) is active for Week 8 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: Ridley entered the week questionable due to a hip injury but will be active after getting in a full practice on Friday. The Titans declared WR Carnell Tate, RB Tyjae Spears, P Tommy Townsend, CB Jaylon Jones, OT Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson, TE Kylen Granson, and DT Jackie Marshall inactive for Week 8 against the Bengals. Ridley will be one of the Titans’ top pass-catchers with Carnell Tate (shoulder) already ruled out, but is not more than a touchdown-dependent fantasy WR4 this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter named Calvin Ridley as a potential trade candidate.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: Schefter threw out several names, many of whom have already been bandied about as trade candidates. Among the lesser-discussed options, he included Jerry Jeudy and Jauan Jennings in addition to Ridley. All three are veteran wideouts who have simply disappeared in the current iterations of their respective offenses. Even with new landing spots in the cards for the trio, none of them are worth holding onto in standard fantasy leagues. Ridley has five catches for 81 yards this year. He is expected to play through his hip injury today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Calvin Ridley (hip) is questionable for Tennessee’s Week 8 game against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: He got in a full session on Friday and would seem to be trending towards playing. With Carnell Tate down this week, Elic Ayomanor is probably the Titans dart throw wideout for the desperate against the Bengals if you’re choosing between him or Ridley.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.headline: Darius Cooper caught 4-of-5 targets for 59 yards in the Eagles’ Week 11 win against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.analysis: Cooper led all Eagles pass catchers in catches and receiving yards on a day that saw Joe Milton throw just 21 passes in a run-heavy game. Cooper played a full-time role because Dontayvian Wicks remained sidelined after practicing over the past week. Cooper would profile as an interesting flex play next week against Dallas if Wicks remains out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.headline: Darius Cooper caught 2-of-8 targets for 25 yards in the Eagles’ Week 9 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.analysis: One of Cooper’s missed connections in an inefficient performance was a drop on a potentially long score. So it goes when backup-level pass catchers are playing with No. 3 quarterbacks. Cooper has provided the Eagles with some desperately needed snaps and down-field ability, but there is extremely little chance his real life “value” translates to fantasy points in the second half of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.headline: Darius Cooper caught 1-of-2 targets for nine yards in the Eagles’ Week 6 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.analysis: With DeVonta Smith back, Cooper played just 39 of 64 snaps and ran a route on 26 of the team’s 52 dropbacks. Those were both fourth among wide receivers on the team. Cooper’s fantasy value is likely limited until there is another injury in the receiving room.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.headline: Darius Cooper caught 2-of-3 passes for 71 yards and a touchdown in the Eagles’ Week 5 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.analysis: Cooper has been a touchdown magnet this year, scoring three times on five catches before today’s explosion. He broke loose against the Jags in the second quarter with a 62-yard grab. Cooper beat his man deep and his adjustment to the throw, which was thrown back toward the center of the field, put him in open space with a full head of steam. He ran untouched into the end zone. Cooper’s absurd touchdown efficiency can’t be sustained, but he is developing into a meaningful deep threat for a struggling Philly passing attack. He will at least warrant some FLEX consideration if DeVonta Smith remains out for Week 6 against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.headline: Darius Cooper caught 3-of-7 targets for 33 yards and two touchdowns in the Eagles’ Week 4 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.analysis: Doing his best Isaac TesLaa impression, Cooper is now up to three touchdowns on only five catches this season. His first score today was a fluke 18-yarder where he turned a Jalen Hurts end zone interception into six after he wrestled the ball away from Quentin Lake. His second was a 10-yarder where the Rams somewhat understandably simply stopped covering him in the painted area. Cooper is one of the only Birds stepping up right now, but his paltry targets total through four appearances — 10 — means he’s not about to push for WR4 status even with DeVonta Smith (hamstring) on the shelf.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.headline: The Philly Voice’s Jimmy Kempski reports that Eagles WR Johnny Wilson had a “better” spring than WR Darius Cooper and could challenge for a roster spot.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.analysis: Wilson’s first two years in the NFL were riddled with injuries. A summer concussion and in-season hamstring injury slowed his rookie season development, and he was robbed of his second season after being rolled up on in an August practice. He underwent season-ending ankle and knee injuries and was replaced in the lineup by Cooper, who uninspiringly caught nine passes for 92 yards all year. Wilson, an oversized slot receiver, is unlikely to be fantasy-relevant, but it sounds like he has a chance to at least contribute this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.headline: The Athletic’s Zach Berman reports Darius Cooper “raised eyebrows” and “even pushed Jahan Dotson last year to be the No. 3 receiver.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.analysis: In trying to figure out how the Eagles could look if A.J. Brown gets traded, it’s possible Cooper pushes for a role in a three-wide set with Johnny Wilson also in the conversation. Cooper did manage a five-target, 33-yard game in meaningless Week 18 action with Tanner McKee starting. He’s on the deep dynasty radar.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.headline: Darius Cooper caught 3-of-5 targets for 33 yards in the Eagles’ Week 18 loss to the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.analysis: Cooper, an undrafted free agent rookie from Tarleton State, had six targets on the season heading into Week 18. He made a few chunk plays running the most routes he had all season with the Eagles resting starters. Also splitting WR4 looks for the Eagles was Britain Covey, who caught 2-of-4 targets for 20 yards. Neither Cooper nor Covey are relevant on offense when the Eagles are playing starters, which they will be doing in the Wild Card round against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.headline: Eagles placed OLB Nolan Smith on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.analysis: Smith reportedly re-injured the triceps muscle that he tore during Super Bowl LIX. He underwent surgery to repair the torn tissue this offseason. The Eagles believe Smith will not require surgery and hope to have him back “around” their Week 9 bye. Players placed on injured reserve are eligible to return after missing four games. The Eagles also placed CB Jakorian Bennett and WR Darius Cooper on injured reserve with undisclosed injuries. Both players are likewise expected to avoid surgery and are expected to return around Week 9. The Eagles signed S Marcus Epps, TE Cameron Latu, and CB Parry Nickerson to the active roster, and LB Lance Dixon, DB Eli Ricks, and WR Quez Watkins to the practice squad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.headline: Chimere Dike caught 6-of-7 targets for 69 yards in the Titans’ Week 11 loss to the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.analysis: Dike notched a 22-yard gain on a flea flicker on the Titans’ first play from scrimmage and went on to lead the team in receiving as it put up 30 points in a road loss. Good stuff, and Dike’s second pop-up effort in as many weeks, though it was Carnell Tate and Calvin Ridley who made the biggest plays. Second-year fourth-rounder Dike has been one of the biggest beneficiaries as fellow sophomore Cam Ward has finally started to play better, but he’s still having a difficult time cracking the top 48 at receiver. That is going to be especially true for Week 12 against the Jaguars as we get a rare November week with all 32 teams actually playing football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.headline: Chimere Dike caught 2-of-3 targets for 16 yards in the Titans’ Week 10 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.analysis: Coming off a 5-71-1 receiving line versus the Bengals, Dike appeared to be taking on a larger role in the absence of Carnell Tate. That wasn’t the case versus Jacksonville and he finished fifth on the team in targets. Even desperate fantasy managers can send him back to the waiver wire ahead of Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) will not play in Week 10 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.analysis: Head coach Robert Saleh said he is hopeful Tate will be able to return in Week 11 when the Titans visit the Cowboys, but his availability for that game will be determined once the Titans begin prepping for Dallas. In the meantime, the Titans will likely go with Wan’Dale Robinson and Chimere Dike as their top two wideouts after the pair led the team in routes run in Week 8 against the Bengals, with Elic Ayomanor also seeing some work (30 routes). Playing against a stout Jaguars defense will make all of the Titans’ receivers hard to trust as anything more than WR3/WR4 plays, while TE Gunnar Helm could also see more work after earning a season-high eight targets vs. the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.headline: Chimere Dike caught 5-of-6 targets for 71 yards and a touchdown in the Titans’ Week 8 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.analysis: Dike saw 58 snaps with Carnell Tate out, second among Titans wide receivers. He scored on an 11-yard reception in the fourth quarter. It was Dike’s first game with over three receptions and second game over one target this season. Dike is mostly utilized as a kick returner but is in line to see increased opportunities on offense if Tate misses additional time. For now, Dike should be off the fantasy radar heading into the Titans’ Week 9 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.headline: Chimere Dike caught 4-of-5 targets for 55 yards in the Titans’ Week 17 loss to the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.analysis: Dike also had a carry of seven yards and drew a 50-yard defensive pass interference. He finished the day tied for team-highs in catches and yards. With some help from his punt and kick returns, Dike set the record for all-purpose yards by a rookie at 2,344. Dike has his limitations as a receiver, but he is a force to be reckoned with when the ball is in his hands. He will be in the FLEX mix for his Week 18 date with the Jags.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.headline: Chimere Dike caught 3-of-5 targets for 40 yards and a touchdown in the Titans’ Week 16 win over the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.analysis: In addition to his fourth receiving score of the season, Dike set the Titans’ single-season record for kick return yardage. The 24-year-old has been a legitimate all-purpose weapon, even if it hasn’t quite translated to weekly WR4 value. Maybe that will be on tap for 2026, but Dike still lacks either the floor ceiling to be a trusted fantasy option for finals week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.headline: Chimere Dike caught 4-of-5 targets for 17 yards in the Titans’ Week 15 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.analysis: Dike had the most targets of any Titans wide receiver, but that’s not much to write home about. The Titans love to run screen passes, and Dike is really shifty after the catch, so you figure he’d be a good option on those plays. The Titans don’t seem to agree. The rookie also had a brutal drop in the fourth quarter on a play where Cam Ward evaded three rushers and escaped to the sideline before throwing a dart that hit Dike in the chest. He needs to make those catches, and the drop is a good example of why he’s hard to trust in fantasy leagues right now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.headline: Chimere Dike caught 5-of-8 targets for 24 yards and a touchdown in the Titans’ Week 14 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.analysis: That’s a highly disappointing yardage total considering Dike’s catches and targets, but the looks matched a season high. The score was also his second in three weeks. The Titans have followed through on their pledge to get Dike more involved down the stretch. It has been difficult for it to translate to real fantasy value because of Cam Ward’s ongoing struggles, but Dike is still looking like someone who could be an eventual fantasy WR3. That will not include for Week 15 against the 49ers. Fantasy managers simply have too many other higher-ceiling options with the playoffs beginning.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.headline: Titans WR Chimere Dike (quad) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 14 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.analysis: Dike has been quite the volatile scorer as of late. In his late six games, he has finished as the half-PPR WR15-18 three times. In his other three showings, he finished as the WR75 or worse. Facing the Browns’ elite defense, he makes for a very risky FLEX option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.headline: Titans WR Chimere Dike (quad) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.analysis: Dike had a calamitous Week 13 showing with just eight yards on four targets, as well as a fumbled kick return. He’s not a super desirable FLEX option against a strong Browns defense in Week 14.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ted-hurst/.headline: Ted Hurst caught 5-of-7 targets for 56 yards and two touchdowns in the Bucs’ Week 11 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ted-hurst/.analysis: Hurst brought down a beautiful deep shot right in the bread basket with four seconds left on the clock in the second quarter. He double-dipped near the end of the fourth quarter with a quick out at the goal line for his second touchdown of the day. Hurst led the Bucs in all receiving categories, including a 21 percent target share. Hurst has been a boom/bust receiver this year who mostly gives fantasy managers busts, but his Week 11 breakout gives him something to build on. He will be a high-risk FLEX play when the Bucs take on the Panthers next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ted-hurst/.headline: Ted Hurst failed to catch his only target in the Bucs’ Week 8 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ted-hurst/.analysis: Baker Mayfield only attempted three passes in this game. One of them was a deep shot for Hurst into the end zone. Hurst initially had the catch as he spun around for the back-shoulder ball, but Falcons corner Mike Hughes jarred the ball loose for an incompletion. It was Hurst’s second week in a row with zero catches on one target. Hurst has topped out at three catches for 40 yards in a single game this year. He isn’t on the fantasy radar for Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ted-hurst/.headline: Ted Hurst was held without a catch in the Bucs’ Week 7 win over the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ted-hurst/.analysis: A buzzy WR4 with Emeka Egbuka (foot, concussion) on the shelf, Hurst ended up drawing just one target in a game where the Bucs rode their run game and Panthers turnovers to a thumping road victory. Hugely disappointing if you threw the dart, but Hurst is still an upside bench stash for a team that finally has its starting quarterback back. That being said, Hurst is probably not going to find himself inside the top 50 for Week 8 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ted-hurst/.headline: Buccaneers head coach said Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) will be doubtful for Week 7’s game against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ted-hurst/.analysis: Bowles said Egbuka remains in concussion protocol and initially said “I’d say he’s out [for Week 7], too,” before saying the second-year receiver would be listed as doubtful. Fantasy managers holding out hope that Egbuka will suit up for Sunday’s game against the Panthers should ensure their backup plan is in place, as players listed as doubtful seldom end up playing on game day. Assuming he’s out, Ted Hurst could be tasked with operating as the Bucs’ WR1. Hurst has caught 11-of-22 targets for 168 yards and one touchdown this season but wouldn’t be viewed as anything more than a WR3/FLEX play even with Baker Mayfield (thumb) back under center.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ted-hurst/.headline: Ted Hurst caught 3-of-6 targets for 40 yards in the Bucs’ Week 6 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ted-hurst/.analysis: Hurst tied his season highs in catches and yards today. He also drew a defensive pass interference call that netted Tampa Bay 22 yards. Emeka Egbuka would score on the very next play. Hurst is looking like a solid field-stretcher, but the Bucs’ offense isn’t set up to support more than one fantasy-relevant pass-catcher. With Emeka Egbuka decisively taking that role, Hurst is buried in the WR6 ranks going forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ted-hurst/.headline: Ted Hurst was not targeted in the Buccaneers’ Week 5 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ted-hurst/.analysis: Hurst has seen his role eaten into by downfield threat Tez Johnson as the season has progressed, clearly not yet ready to take on a full workload in the offense as he enters the second month of his rookie season. Hurst brings the size and physicality to grow into a consistent producer at the NFL level, something fantasy managers could have to be patient with in the coming weeks. Hurst safely remains a bench stash ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ted-hurst/.headline: Ted Hurst caught 2-of-3 targets for 25 yards in the Bucs’ Week 4 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ted-hurst/.analysis: Hurst was the only Bucs pass-catcher to gain more than 20 yards on a single play. The passing game was otherwise relegated to intermediate throws and check-downs in Jalon Daniels’ first start. With Jalen McMillan on IR, Hurst has locked up a starting role. That simply is worth much for fantasy managers with a backup quarterback under center. Hurst will be a desperation FLEX play when he takes on the Cowboys next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ted-hurst/.headline: Ted Hurst caught his lone target for 40 yards and a touchdown in the Bucs’ Week 3 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ted-hurst/.analysis: Hurst caught a perfectly-placed 40-yard score down the seam in the first half and did not see another look from Baker Mayfield. It wasn’t a lack of playing time that limited Hurst: He ran a route on 39 of the team’s 43 drop backs on the day. His downfield profile will make Hurst a volatile weekly play in 12-team leagues. He should probably stay on benches next week against the Dolphins if Mayfield (hand) is sidelined, however.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ted-hurst/.headline: Ted Hurst caught 1-of-5 targets for 21 yards in the Bucs’ Week 2 loss against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ted-hurst/.analysis: Hurst was overthrown by Baker Mayfield a few times in the second half. It could have been a big day for the speedy rookie if his quarterback weren’t struggling so mightily with deep throws. Hurst had a solid role though, running a route on 29 of the team’s 37 drop backs. He will be a high-variance flex play for Week 3 against the Vikings if Mayfield can find a little accuracy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ted-hurst/.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Jalen McMillan (knee) is expected to play in Week 2 against the Browns, but not in a “full-time role just yet.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ted-hurst/.analysis: The Bucs are going to ease McMillan back into the lineup after he missed Week 1 with the knee injury. McMillan will take rookie Ted Hurst’s spot in the lineup once healthy, but that might not happen until Week 3. Until we see what their split looks like, neither Hurst nor McMillan should be in fantasy lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.headline: Devaughn Vele caught 7-of-7 targets for 76 yards in the Saints’ Week 11 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.analysis: Vele saw a decrease in opportunities last week with Jordyn Tyson’s activation off injured reserve. However, Tyson saw limited usage in Week 11 against the Bears, with Vele leading Saints receivers in snaps and ranking second in targets, receptions, and yards. Fantasy managers should wait to see if Tyson has any injury limitations moving forward, but Vele would be back in the WR3/4 ranks if Tyson is limited for Week 12 against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.headline: Devaughn Vele caught both of his targets for 14 yards in the Saints’ Week 10 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.analysis: Vele’s cold streak continued in a miserable game for Tyler Shough, who averaged 5.3 yards per attempt with an average depth of target of 4.5. The emergence of Jordyn Tyson, who led the Saints with 13 targets against Carolina, is going to take away targets from Vele. He might hold some PPR appeal in Week 11 against the Bears, but not much. Vele has more than four catches in a game just once in the past five weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.headline: Devaughn Vele caught 2-of-4 targets for 17 yards in the Saints’ Week 9 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.analysis: As expected, the return of Jordyn Tyson brought about the end of Vele’s time as a WR3 fantasy option. Though Vele got his normal complement of routes, Tyson out-targeted him 5-4. He also went for more yards on two extra catches. Tyson’s role is only going to grow as he gets more practice reps under his belt. Fantasy managers can thank Vele for the good times and send him to the waiver wire on this week’s run. He will be buried in the WR5/6 range for Week 10 versus the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.headline: NFL Insider Jordan Schultz reports Saints WR Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) “should be good to go” against the Browns in Week 9.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.analysis: The oft-injured Tyson hurt his hamstring in training camp and is yet to make his NFL debut. According to Schultz, he should be good to go Sunday against the Browns. A limited participant in practice throughout the week, it’s unclear how much Tyson might play in his first game. Eventually, though, he should settle in as the Saints’ WR2 behind Chris Olave. Tyson’s return also puts a damper on the fantasy prospects of Devaughn Vele and Juwan Johnson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.headline: Devaughn Vele caught 5-of-5 targets for 54 yards and a touchdown in the Saints’ Week 7 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.analysis: Vele brought in a one-yard touchdown on fourth-and-goal late in the second quarter to tie the game at 10-10. It would be the last points the Saints would score. Vele has hovered around these numbers through the first half of 2026, and while he provides Shough with a nice safety valve, it’s not exactly what fantasy managers should be chasing. He’ll be a WR4 in Week 9 against the Browns after the Saints “enjoy” their bye in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.headline: Devaughn Vele caught 3-of-6 targets for 42 yards in the Saints’ Week 6 win over the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.analysis: The Saints offense has not pushed the ball downfield over the past two weeks, leading to low-scoring outputs for Vele. He caught three passes on the day, and nearly reeled in a fourth catch on a Tyler Shough sideline overthrow in the second quarter. When the Saints aren’t in a pass-happy game script, Vele is relegated to touchdown-dependent FLEX value. He will be in the WR4 ranks against the Steelers for Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.headline: Devaughn Vele caught 4-of-6 targets for 26 yards in the Saints’ Week 5 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.analysis: Tyler Shough managed a dismal 96 passing yards in this game, so there simply wasn’t enough production for any New Orleans wideout to post usable fantasy numbers. Vele still tied Chris Olave for a team-high in targets. He has at least four catches and six targets in every game this year. Even after a quiet Week 5, Vele remains a solid WR4 option headed into a Week 6 date with the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.headline: Devaughn Vele caught 6-of-9 targets for 54 yards and a touchdown in the Saints’ Week 4 loss to the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.analysis: Vele’s nine targets ranked behind only alpha Chris Olave, although he was headed for another modest fantasy outing before a garbage time touchdown with less than two minutes remaining in the fourth quarter of the blowout loss. Vele has yet to eclipse 69 yards through the first month of play as he continues to operate in an intermediate role for a Saints team struggling to attack downfield. Fantasy managers could consider sitting Vele against the ferocious Vikings defense in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.headline: Devaughn Vele caught 3-of-6 targets for 39 yards in the Saints’ loss to the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.analysis: Vele nearly added a decent first-down pickup to his box score, but he was unable to secure the pass as he was diving to the ground. Aside from that, he had a nice 17-yard gain in which he ripped his leg away from a would-be tackler and scampered away for a few extra yards. Vele is a boom-bust FLEX against the Falcons next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.headline: Saints WR Barion Brown (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devaughn-v.analysis: It seems like Brown is very unlikely to play at this point. His agility and long speed define his game as a gadget player and return specialist. His absence could benefit WR2 Devaughn Vele and WR Bryce Lance.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brevyn-spann-f.headline: Brevyn Spann-Ford caught 2-of-2 targets for five yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 11 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brevyn-spann-f.analysis: The closest thing the Cowboys have to a No. 1 tight end during Jake Ferguson’s ongoing absence, Spann-Ford’s two-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter was just the second of his career. It’s what got the Cowboys to 50 points, which is both cool and also tells you all you need to know about Spann-Ford’s fantasy value. It took the Cowboys running it up late against one of the worst teams in the league for Spann-Ford to find the paint. He remains outside the top 30 in the weekly tight end rankings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brevyn-spann-f.headline: Brevyn Spann-Ford caught 2-of-3 targets for 20 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 9 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brevyn-spann-f.analysis: Spann-Ford played much of the game in the absence of Jake Ferguson, the latter of whom departed with a scary looking knee injury in the third quarter, and still managed only three targets in a game that saw alpha wide receiver CeeDee Lamb amass 16 targets on 34 Dak Prescott pass attempts. The secondary options in this offense are not worthy of weekly fantasy considering, of which Spann-Ford is one. He is not a streaming option ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brevyn-spann-f.headline: Brevyn Spann-Ford caught 4-of-5 targets for 31 yards in Dallas’ Week 8 loss to Arizona.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brevyn-spann-f.analysis: With Jake Ferguson (ankle) felled early, Spann-Ford played 65-of-74 snaps for the Cowboys and was second on the team in targets as Dallas tried to find a solution for the blitz. Spann-Ford would likely factor into the TE2 ranks next week if Ferguson were unable to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brevyn-spann-f.headline: Jake Ferguson caught 2-of-3 targets for 13 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 6 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brevyn-spann-f.analysis: Ferguson has now been out-targeted by the team’s WR3, Ryan Flournoy, in five of six games, even being out-targeted by fellow tight end Brevyn Span-Ford in this one. The latter caught 4-of-5 targets for 35 yards on a night quarterback Dak Prescott attempted 54 passes. Any fleeting fantasy value is quickly evaporating as the fourth option, at best, through the air. Ferguson can safely be left on fantasy benches ahead of a Week 7 meeting with the Eagles on the road.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brevyn-spann-f.headline: Cowboys signed TE Brevyn Spann-Ford to a three-year extension through 2029.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brevyn-spann-f.analysis: Spann-Ford initially signed on with the Cowboys as a 2024 undrafted free agent. He has caught 18 passes for 178 yards and one touchdown since then. The front office is evidently pleased with his development. He is not worth rostering in 12-team leagues. The deal is worth $18 million with $12.075 million guaranteed.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brevyn-spann-f.headline: Cowboys TE Brevyn Spann-Ford was taken to the locker room with an apparent leg injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brevyn-spann-f.analysis: ESPN’s Todd Archer described the play on which Spann-Ford was injured, saying, it “looked like he got rolled up on a run play.” Roll-up mechanisms can impact the knee and/or ankle, but specifics on the injury event are unknown and players are often sent for further examination during training camp out of an abundance of caution. The Cowboys should update Spann-Ford’s status in the near future.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brevyn-spann-f.headline: Cowboys ruled out Jake Ferguson (concussion) for Week 12 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brevyn-spann-f.analysis: Ferguson logged his third straight DNP on Friday and will be forced to try again next week. Backup tight ends Luke Schoonmaker and Brevyn Spann-Ford split repetitions in Week 11, with Schoonmaker astonishingly finishing second on the team in targets (10) and Spann-Ford respectably tying for third with five of his own. Schoonmaker can be streamed as a low-end TE1 if need be but be warned: The Commanders’ linebacker corps is one of the league’s best. This will not be an easy matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brevyn-spann-f.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Cowboys TE Jake Ferguson “could miss some time” with an MCL sprain.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brevyn-spann-f.analysis: Ferguson’s Week 1 injury against the Browns appeared much more serious. It looks like he avoided a season-ending injury and could return later this season, though a timeframe has yet to be detailed. Luke Schoonmaker and Brevyn Spann-Ford should split tight end pass-catching duties while Ferguson is sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brevyn-spann-f.headline: Cowboys sign Minnesota TE Brevyn Spann-Ford.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brevyn-spann-f.analysis: After redshirting his first season at Minnesota in 2018, Spann-Ford (6’7/260) caught five passes over his next two seasons. He rotated into the starter role during the 2021 season, starting all 24 of his games in his last two seasons. Spann-Ford finished his six years at Minnesota with a 25-239-2 line for the 2023 season. Though he struggles with drops and physicality, Spann-Ford’s size can allow him to be a mismatch in the passing game. Similarly, he can be a big blocker for the run game. His combine numbers show a subpar athletic profile, running a 4.77 40-yard dash and jumping a 31.5-inch vertical, both bottom-two among participating tight ends. Spann-Ford’s size will be an asset at the NFL level, though he will need to get more physical to make up for a lack of athleticism.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brevyn-spann-f.headline: Minnesota redshirt senior TE Ko Kieft (undisclosed) is available to play in Saturday’s game against Wisconsin.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brevyn-spann-f.analysis: Kieft (6'5/265) was among the many offensive linemen/tight ends who were sidelined in recent weeks, and the exact reason for those absences remains unknown. The redshirt senior is one of two tight ends who will be back in the fold, as Bryce Witham has also been cleared to play. Brevyn Spann-Ford is also in the mix, and that trio will split the tight end reps with Jake Paulson (undisclosed) being sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.headline: Ryan Flournoy caught an 11-yard pass in the Cowboys’ Week 11 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.analysis: Flournoy had his season-worst outing as the Cowboys had their season-best scoring effort. Go figure. Flournoy’s 11-yard grab came on the opening series only for him to draw zero more targets. That’s a rough development for WR3 desperados with six teams on bye. It is also a faceplant that is unlikely to repeat on Thanksgiving Day against the Eagles even with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens posting crazy usage numbers. The problem for Flournoy is, with all 32 teams active for Week 12, there’s simply no real way to get him into fantasy lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.headline: Ryan Flournoy caught 6-of-7 targets for 71 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 10 loss to the Niners.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.analysis: Flournoy’s seven targets were good for third-most among all Cowboys pass-catchers in this one. The third-year receiver hauled in a 23-yard catch in the third quarter, and broke free from his defender in the end zone on a fourth-and-six in the fourth quarter for an 11-yard touchdown as the Cowboys were hoping to mount a comeback. Flournoy continues to prove himself as a reliable option whenever Dak Prescott looks his way, but his usage remains hard to predict as long as CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens are healthy. Fantasy managers shouldn’t chase this performance entering Week 11 against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.headline: Ryan Flournoy caught 2-of-3 targets for 53 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 9 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.analysis: Flournoy had just one catch for seven yards until the final drive of the game, where he caught a 46-yard pass on the first play of the drive to instantly place the Cowboys into the red zone while trailing by three points. A Javonte Williams touchdown and Caleb Downs interception on the subsequent possession would be enough to send the Cowboys to 4-5 with a win. Fantasy managers must be left disappointed with the outing considering George Pickens was unable to go with a hamstring injury. Flournoy will be a shaky FLEX option in Week 10 against the 49ers, regardless of the status of Pickens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.headline: Ryan Flournoy caught 3-of-4 targets for 38 yards and a touchdown in Dallas’ Week 8 loss to the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.analysis: He added a DPI at the two-yard line to set up another score, and dropped another pass in the red zone. It’s clear that he’s cutting into George Pickens’ production at this point; Flournoy has gone over 90 yards or scored in three of his last four starts. He’ll be a reasonable FLEX play next week against the Colts, although the Cowboys may abandon the pass at some point in that one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.headline: Ryan Flournoy caught all four targets for 70 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 7 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.analysis: Flournoy is not typically going to see elite volume while playing alongside two true alphas in CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, but he continues to outproduce tight end Jake Ferguson as the preferred third option through the air. His big play potential showed against the Eagles as he caught a 35-yard dime early. Flournoy is, at minimum, worthy of a bench spot and could work his way into viable FLEX territory with another solid outing against the downtrodden Cardinals in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.headline: Ryan Flournoy caught 7-of-9 targets for 40 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 6 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.analysis: While the yardage totals continue to remain modest for the third-year receiver, his emergence as a trusted WR3 in the offense has led to him out-targeting tight end Jake Ferguson in five of six games through the first third of the season. That’s a role that can return usable FLEX production in the right matchups in the typically high-powered Cowboys offense, adding to his high-end handcuff value. Fantasy managers can continue to stash FLournoy ahead of a Week 7 meeting with the division rival Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.headline: Ryan Flournoy caught 3-of-4 targets for 90 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 5 loss to the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.analysis: Flournoy continues to operate as the clear WR3 behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, typically incapable of returning viable fantasy production in their shadows. He hit for a 48-yard reception at the end of the second quarter to set up a go-ahead field goal entering the break, otherwise remaining about as quiet as we would expect. This was the first game in 2026 over a modest 37 yards for Flournoy, who could be tasked with additional emphasis in the immediate future after Lamb departed with a quad injury in the fourth quarter. He could be worth a speculative add ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the reeling Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.headline: Ryan Flournoy caught 4-of-5 targets for 37 yards in Dallas’ Week 4 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.analysis: Flournoy has been held to exactly 22 or 23 yards in each of his first three games of the season, but the trend of Dallas passing more is pretty good for him. He’s got 21 targets over his last three games. It’s not anything beyond FLEX production yet but Thursday night games can be weird and that’s where Dallas will be next week against the Buccaneers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.headline: Ryan Flournoy caught 2-of-4 targets for 22 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 1 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.analysis: The veteran receiver inked a one-year contract extension this offseason to retain his supporting role in the high-powered Dallas offense, but the early returns were less than inspiring. Flournoy played 41 of 58 snaps, nearly every-down work, but the Cowboys just didn’t get enough play volume to let him spike a ceiling week. It’ll be hard for Flournoy to return consistent fantasy production for as long as both CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens remain healthy. He’ll be a boom-bust WR4 in a plus matchup against the Commanders in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.headline: Cowboys signed Ryan Flournoy to a one-year, $6 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.analysis: Flournoy is now under contract through the 2027 season. The 26-year-old receiver caught 40 passes for 475 yards and four touchdowns last season, while finishing third among Cowboys receivers in routes run (273) and fourth on the team in targets. It was reported earlier this summer that he was seeing more snaps in the slot, but it’s hard to imagine Flournoy making enough of an impact to be fantasy-relevant as long as CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, and Jake Ferguson are healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Jordan Tyson caught 1-of-2 targets for 6 yards in the Saints’ Week 11 loss to the Bears, adding one carry for four yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: Tyson saw the first offensive touch for the Saints, getting four-yard carry to start things off. He saw just one more touch the rest of the game and was barely on the field for the Saints’ final offensive drive. Though he was cleared off the injury report heading into the weekend, Tyson was dealing with a chest injury last week. Also coming back from a hamstring injury this season, Tyson’s compounding injury list may have played a role in him seeing just half of the offensive snaps against the Bears after getting 13 targets last week. He saw just two targets as Chris Olave took the alpha receiver role back. Fantasy managers should monitor Tyson’s injury status heading into Week 12; he is in the WR3 ranks against the Bengals next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Jordyn Tyson (chest) is not on New Orleans’ final Week 11 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: He got in a full session on Friday and was cleared off the report for Week 11’s game against the Bears. He’ll be an upside WR3 after last week’s 13-target breakout against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Jordyn Tyson (chest) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: It’s back-to-back limited sessions for Tyson, leaving him likely on the optimistic side of questionable heading into Friday’s practice sessions. Tyson will be an upside WR3 against the Bears in Week 11 based on the volume he was commanding last week so long as he avoids any unexpected setbacks on Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Jordyn Tyson (chest) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: Saints coach Kellen Moore told reporters that Tyson suffered the chest injury in Week 10 against the Panthers. The fact that he is limited is a great sign for his availability against the Bears. Tyson belongs in fantasy football lineups on a weekly basis at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Chris Olave caught 3-of-4 targets for 30 yards in the Saints’ Week 10 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: Jordyn Tyson, in his second NFL game, took over for at least one week as the team’s clear WR1, drawing 13 targets and finishing with 80 yards on 11 grabs. Olave, who did not record a reception until late in the third quarter, saw nothing downfield as Tyler Shough was under constant duress against a Carolina defense that entered the week with one of the lowest QB pressure rates in the NFL. Olave entered Week 10 with a 27 percent target share and a 47 percent air yards share. Tyson’s emergence could be a major issue for Olave if this sort of usage continues in Week 11 against the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Jordyon Tyson caught 11-of-13 targets for 80 yards in the Saints’ Week 10 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: The Saints ramped up Tyson’s snaps and routes in his second game of the season, as the rookie ran a route on 32 of the team’s 47 drop backs on the day and easily led all New Orleans pass catchers in targets and receiving yards. Chris Olave, meanwhile, was limited to three catches for 30 yards on five targets. Tyson was targeted both in the short and intermediate areas, and nearly came up with a couple downfield grabs on poorly-thrown balls from Tyler Shough. The Saints saw fit to target Tyson twice on backfield screen looks in the second half. That kind of usage suggests Tyson could be an outsized part of the Saints offense going forward. He’ll be a WR3 option in Week 11 against the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: New Orleans Football’s Mike Triplett reports that the Saints had Jordyn Tyson work with doctors at the University of Wisconsin to address his recurring hamstring issues.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: Tyson has dealt with recurring hamstring injuries since October 2025, and was most recently sidelined by a hamstring strain suffered on August 13th. According to Triplett, the Saints sent Tyson to be evaluated by Dr. Heiderscheit and his team, which received a $4 million research grant from the NFL in 2021 to study hamstring issues, twice during his three-month rehab program. Dr. Heiderscheit successfully treated Packers WR Christian Watson’s recurring hamstring injuries in 2024. According to Triplett, the specialists “determined that something was a little small” in Tyson’s hamstring fascia, which allowed the Saints’ training staff to update Tyson’s exercise regimen with needed alterations. Per Tyson, the changes have allowed the tissue “to fire better.” Given Dr. Heiderscheit’s track record, Tyson’s odds of remaining healthy for the rest of the season are trending upward. He warrants WR3/FLEX treatment at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Saints coach Kellen Moore said Jordyn Tyson should get “a healthy dose more” snaps in Week 10 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: Moore adds that the Saints will continue to increase Tyson’s usage over time, “to a point where he’s not limited.” This is great to read. Tyson isn’t even listed on the Saints’ injury report this week. He earned four targets on 16 snaps last week and should be expected to increase his workload this week, potentially to a FLEX-worthy level.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Jordyn Tyson caught 4-of-5 targets for 30 yards in the Saints’ Week 9 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: Tyson was activated from injured reserve over the weekend and made his NFL debut today. He got off to a nightmare start by fumbling his first career reception inside the five-yard line. The Saints didn’t go away from him after the rookie mistake and rotated him onto the field rather sporadically for the rest of the game. He was deployed as the team’s WR3, running 16 routes compared to 44 for Devaughn Vele. Those two numbers should converge in the coming weeks, but it might take some time for Tyson to overtake Vele as the team’s WR2. He will be a high-risk FLEX play for Week 10 against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is active for Week 9 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: Tyson will make his NFL debut after missing the first two months of the year with a hamstring injury. We’re expecting a snap count for him this week, making him an extremely risky FLEX play. Inactive for the Saints are QB Zach Wilson, S Mike Reid, RB C.J. Donaldson, DT Christen Miller, LB Jaylan Ford, OL Mason Murphy, and DL John Ridgeway III.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Chris Olave caught 9-of-15 targets for 102 yards in the Saints’ Week 11 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: Olave saw 15 targets against the Bears, taking back over as the alpha receiver after four targets last week. Tyler Shough had a steady pass funnel to Olave in the intermediate area against a softened Bears secondary. The 26-year-old receiver reeled in nine catches for 102 yards but did not get any targets in the red zone. The Saints often find themselves in pass-heavy game scripts and Olave’s steady diet of targets keeps him in the low-end WR1 ranks for Week 12 against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Chris Olave caught 3-of-4 targets for 30 yards in the Saints’ Week 10 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: Jordyn Tyson, in his second NFL game, took over for at least one week as the team’s clear WR1, drawing 13 targets and finishing with 80 yards on 11 grabs. Olave, who did not record a reception until late in the third quarter, saw nothing downfield as Tyler Shough was under constant duress against a Carolina defense that entered the week with one of the lowest QB pressure rates in the NFL. Olave entered Week 10 with a 27 percent target share and a 47 percent air yards share. Tyson’s emergence could be a major issue for Olave if this sort of usage continues in Week 11 against the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Chris Olave caught 7-of-12 targets for 98 yards in the Saints’ Week 9 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: It was business as usual for Olave, who has seen at least 10 targets in 6-of-8 games this year. He earned an astounding 38 percent target share today, and his 229 air yards are the second-most of the week, pending the two remaining games. The return of No. 8 overall pick Jorydn Tyson had no impact on his role, though Tyson was limited to 16 routes in his NFL debut. Tyson should see more work next week, but that will primarily come at the expense of Devaughn Vele. Olave will remain in the WR1 mix when he takes on the Panthers in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Chris Olave caught 6-of-10 targets for 57 yards in the Saints’ Week 7 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: Olave was once again a shorter-yardage target with a long gain of just 14 yards in the contest. Tyler Shough missed the 26-year-old on what would have been a walk-in touchdown from deep on a disappointing day for the top target in the Saints’ passing attack, at least based on expectations. He’ll remain one of the top fantasy receiving options in his next game, but that won’t come for two weeks as the Saints get a bye before facing the Browns in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Saints general manager Mickey Loomis said Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) won’t practice this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: Loomis said Tyson is “improving” in his long rehab from a major preseason hamstring injury. Tyson, who traveled with the Saints to France for their Week 7 game against the Steelers, could still be a couple weeks away as the team takes a cautious approach to his recovery. In the meantime, Bryce Lance will operate as the Saints’ No. 2 wideout behind Chris Olave. Lance over the past two weeks has a 13 percent target share and a 20 percent air yards share in the pass-first New Orleans offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Chris Olave caught 4-of-7 targets for 43 yards and a touchdown in the Saints’ Week 6 win over the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: Olave finished as the Saints’ leading receiver after coming into the weekend questionable with an illness. He was able to salvage his fantasy day with an 18-yard score at the beginning of the fourth quarter. Despite a season-low 43 yards receiving, Olave is still averaging just under 100 yards receiving per game this season. There is no question he belongs in the fantasy WR1 ranks heading into a Week 7 showdown against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Chris Olave (illness) is expected to play in Week 6 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: There was reportedly a bug going around the Saints’ locker room last weekend, and Olave seems to have caught the tail end of it. He missed the first two practices of the week but was back on the field for Friday’s session. The team listed him as questionable for Week 6. Barring any further updates, we’re expecting business as usual for the star wideout. He remains entrenched in the WR1 mix for his date with the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Chris Olave (illness) is questionable for New Orleans’ Week 6 game against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: Olave missed the first two days of practice this week with the illness, but we’d ultimately still expect him to play. He should be regarded as on the optimistic side of questionable. He’ll be an easy WR1, assuming he plays, against the Giants in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Chris Olave (illness) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: Unless we get word that it’s an exceptionally rough illness, we’d expect no worse than a questionable listing on Friday despite the two missed practices. Olave should remain a smash WR1 against the Giants in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Chris Olave (illness) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: We expect Olave to be fine for the Saints’ Week 6 game against the Giants. There is currently no cause for concern, but this is worth keeping an eye on. Olave experienced blood clots in his lung last season, and spent much of the offseason recovering. We are not doctors and cannot opine on the matter. For now, expect him to play, but keep an eye out for his hopeful return to practice tomorrow or Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.headline: Emeka Egbuka caught 2-of-5 targets for 18 yards in the Bucs’ Week 11 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.analysis: There’s not much to say here. It’s just not happening for Egbuka this year. He’s struggling to earn targets and doing nothing when the ball comes his way. Ted Hurst broke out with two scores and 56 yards on a team-high 56 yards today. Egbuka watched on with a measly 15 percent target share. He’s averaging a dismal five yards per target and has forced zero missed tackles. Egbuka will tumble into the WR4 ranks for his Week 12 game against Carolina. With no teams on bye, fantasy managers can feel comfortable sending him to the bench next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.headline: Emeka Egbuka caught 3-of-5 targets for 38 yards in the Buccaneers’ Week 9 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.analysis: It was Egbuka’s first game since Week 6 because of his foot injury, and it was pretty similar to his previous efforts in 2026. He was able to get lose for a 21-yard catch from the arm of Baker Mayfield, but once again, he was unable to eclipse 50 yards; a mark he hasn’t bested since Week 3. Egbuka is a high-floor, low-ceiling WR3 going forward, and the next chance will come after a bye in Week 11 against the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.headline: Emeka Egbuka (foot) is active for Week 9 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.analysis: As expected, Egbuka is back after missing two games with his foot injury. The wideout has been heavily targeted when healthy, but hasn’t been particularly effective with those opportunities with zero games over 65 yards in 2026. The Bucs’ inactives for Week 9 will be OLB Yaya Diaby, G Trevor Keegan, G Billy Schrauth, CB Ayden Garnes and DL DeMonte Capehart.

https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Emeka Egbuka (foot) will play in Week 9 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.analysis: Egbuka missed two games with the foot injury, though a concussion also kept him out for one of them. He practiced in full on Friday, so we’re not expecting much of a pitch count for the second-year wideout. Without anyone emerging as a viable replacement for Egbuka over the past two weeks, he should reclaim the No. 1 receiver role in Tampa Bay without much of a fight. Egbuka will be on the WR2/3 border for his first game back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.headline: Emeka Egbuka (foot) is listed as questionable for Week 9 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.analysis: Egbuka was able to get in another full practice Friday after getting the same Thursday, so it seems like he’s on the right side of the questionable tag, even with coach Todd Bowles suggesting he’ll be a game-time decision. The 24-year-old wideout is on the WR2/WR3 range for the Sunday Night Football showdown against Chicago if he is able to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.headline: Emeka Egbuka (foot) was a full participant in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.analysis: After only participating in drills on the side and being listed as a non-participant Wednesday, Egbuka was a full-go for Thursday’s session. The 24-year-old will likely need to get in one more full session before fantasy managers can fully trust the wideout for Week 9 against the Bears, but this is obviously a significant step in the right direction.

https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.headline: Emeka Egbuka (foot) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.analysis: Egbuka missed Week 7 with a concussion and a foot injury. He cleared the league’s concussion protocol last week, but the foot issue kept him on ice. A DNP today suggests he will miss another week. However, head coach Todd Bowles told reporters Egbuka worked off to the side today. The team will see how he feels tomorrow. That leaves the door open for him to play, but fantasy managers should at least have backup options in place. If he does suit up, Egbuka would be a high-risk WR3 versus Chicago.

https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.headline: Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said Emeka Egbuka (foot) will not play in Week 8 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.analysis: Bowles said Egbuka did clear concussion protocol, but the foot injury he has been dealing with for the last two weeks will officially sideline him for this week’s game against the Falcons. Hopefully this isn’t any kind of a major setback for Egbuka, who shed his non-contact jersey in Thursday’s practice and was limited in the first two practices to start the week. Ted Hurst will again operate as the Buccaneers’ primary outside target but shouldn’t be trusted as anything more than a risky WR4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.headline: Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) was not spotted at Friday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.analysis: After being limited in back-to-back practices to start the week, and shedding his non-contact jersey on Thursday, Egbuka being a DNP on Friday is a notable setback. Buccaneers beat writer Greg Auman speculated that Egbuka will “be ruled out again” for Week 8’s game against the Falcons, but we’ll wait for official word from the team before drawing conclusions. That said, the Bucs could again have Ted Hurst operating as their primary outside threat.

https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.headline: The Tampa Bay Times’ Rick Stroud reports Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) shed his non-contact jersey for Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.analysis: There’s a good chance Egbuka has been upgraded to a full participant in practice, meaning he is making his way through the league’s concussion protocol. He remains on track to play this week after missing Week 7. With Baker Mayfield back under center, Egbuka may be able to turn around his season after a rather quiet start to the year. He is in the WR2 mix for Week 8 versus the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.headline: Darnell Washington caught all three of his targets for 22 yards in the Steelers’ Week 11 loss to the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.analysis: Washington again ran fewer pass routes than Pat Freiermuth, who caught all five of his targets on the day. Washington won’t have much in the way of fantasy value until or unless Freiermuth misses time. Washington has five games this season with at least three catches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.headline: Darnell Washington caught 3-of-5 targets for 94 yards in the Steelers’ Week 8 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.analysis: Washington made a nice 58-yard catch where he broke two tackles, and then tight-rope walked down the sideline before being pushed out of bounds at the one-yard line. It was an impressive display of athleticism from a large human being. Washington was tied for second on the team in targets and played the third-most snaps of any non-offensive lineman or Aaron Rodgers today. However, early data says he ran a route on just five dropbacks, which means he was targeted every single time he ran a route. That type of production can’t hold up in that limited a role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.headline: Darnell Washington caught his only target for a four-yard touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 7 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.analysis: Washington used his massive — massive seems like a huge understatement — size to haul in a touchdown near the sideline. That’s his third touchdown in four games, and it’s pretty clear that he’s become a focal point once the Steelers get inside of the red zone. He just isn’t much of one outside of those opportunities, and that makes him the most touchdown dependent tight end to ever exist. Maybe a little bit of hyperbole there. Washington will try and score again in Week 8 against the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.headline: Darenll Washington caught 4-of-6 targets for 25 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 6 win over the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.analysis: Washington got in the end zone for the third time this year via an RPO toss from Rodgers near the goal line. His six targets were double the total of Pat Freiermuth, who was laboring through a calf injury in this contest. Muth should be healthier and earn more looks next week, making this minor spike game from Washington rather unsustainable. Washington will be a touchdown-or-bust TE2 for his Week 7 date with the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.headline: Pat Freiermuth caught 3-of-5 targets for 17 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 4 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.analysis: Freiermuth found the end zone late in the fourth quarter for his second touchdown of the season, tying fellow tight end Darnell Washington for fourth on the team with five targets. Washington managed to corral just two of his five targets but eclipsed the yardage total of Freiermuth with 27 yards while also adding a touchdown of his own. Both tight ends appear unlikely to contribute viable counting stats considering neither has seen more than five targets in a game during the first month of play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the Steelers are going to use Jaylen Warren “a lot” while frequently utilizing two-tight end sets in Week 4 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.analysis: It sounds like Warren is belongs on the RB1/2 border with Rico Dowdle (toe) sidelined again this week. The Steelers will try to control the line of scrimmage by frequently deploying TEs Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington, both in the run game and as receivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.headline: Darnell Washington caught 3-of-4 targets for 67 yards in the Steelers’ Week 3 win over the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.analysis: No, Washington can’t be trusted in fantasy, but he sure is fun when he gets a full head of steam. Washington caught a season-high three passes in Sunday’s win over the Bengals and led the Steelers in receiving yards, thanks largely to the 47-yard play he made in the fourth quarter. A true man among boys with the ball in his hands, Washington rumbled through and past multiple defenders on his way to the big gain. While he’s always good for an exciting play or two, Washington can be left on waivers for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.headline: The Athletic’s Mike DeFabo believes TE Pat Freiermuth will be the Steelers’ “go-to pass-catching tight end” this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.analysis: The Steelers notably signed TE Darnell Washington to a four-year, $42 million contract extension this offseason, but DeFabo believes Freiermuth is still the team’s TE1. He expects Washington to continue operating as a receiving threat, “especially in the red zone,” but he is apparently stuck in the TE2 role. Washington’s profile is certainly more intriguing, but he may be best viewed as a boom-bust backup option in best ball for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.headline: Steelers signed TE Darnell Washington to a four-year, $42 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.analysis: Washington’s contract includes $21 million in guaranteed money. A third-round pick in the 2023 NFL Draft from Georgia, he’s been as advertised so far in his pro career. Washington has only 57 catches, 625 yards and two touchdowns in three seasons, but is a tremendous blocker and extremely difficult to tackle when he has the ball. Listed at 6-foot-7 and 264 pounds, he’s one of the most physically imposing players in the NFL. With a $10.5 million average annual value, Washington is 12th in AAV among tight ends. That level of commitment could be a sign the Steelers plan to use a good amount of two tight end sets with Washington and Pat Freiermuth in head coach Mike McCarthy’s first season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.headline: Steelers TE Darnell Washington had surgery to repair his broken arm.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.analysis: Washington underwent surgery Monday and won’t return to the Steelers this season, even if they manage to beat the Ravens in Week 18 and make the playoffs. Washington ends the 2025 season with 31 receptions on 43 targets for 364 yards and one touchdown.
