He was third among Pittsburgh tight ends in catches, as Jonnu Smith and Pat Freiermuth remains involved in Arthur Smith’s tight end-heavy offensive scheme. With Washington sidelined, Freiermuth would seem to be the main beneficiary. Both Smith and Freiermuth have a 48 percent route participation rate through Week 17.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: CJ Donaldson rushed one time for five yards in the Saints’ Week 11 loss to the Bears, adding four receptions for 12 yards and a fumble.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: Donaldson is head coach Kellen Moore’s pride and joy as a passing-down back in the backfield. The undrafted rookie continues to run routes despite a lack of efficiency and production all season. He was used as a pass blocker and ran 25 routes on the day, more than rookie wideout Jordyn Tyson. Donaldson fumbled on one of his receptions in the second quarter, totaling 12 yards through the air and five on the ground. He has no fantasy value heading into Week 12.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: CJ Donaldson (shoulder) is not on New Orleans’ final Week 11 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: He’ll return to his pass-blocking role for the Saints, assuming they want him active, in Week 11. No fantasy value here for the moment.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: Taliese Fuaga (knee) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: Fuaga, the Saints’ right tackle, and backup OT Asim Richards (knee) were both sidelined today. Saints C Erik McCoy (biceps) is sidelined as well, though he was already expected to miss time. Hopefully, Fuaga can return in time to face the Bears this weekend. Backup RB CJ Donaldson (shoulder) is practicing in full.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: CJ Donaldson (shoulder) won’t play in New Orleans’ Week 10 game against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: The passing-down blocking back’s absence should create more opportunities for Alvin Kamara and, possibly, Travis Etienne in the passing game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: Alvin Kamara (NIR-rest/back) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: The Saints’ veteran running back is just having his reps managed. With Audric Estime playing well and Travis Etienne (hamstring) potentially returning, Kamara does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats at this time. Kamara will continue to chip in on passing downs, though. Backup RB CJ Donaldson (shoulder) remains sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: CJ Donaldson (shoulder) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: On the plus side, Donaldson is no longer listed with a concussion. Audric Estime played well last week and Travis Etienne (hamstring) is practicing now, though. Donaldson could be phased out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: CJ Donaldson (concussion/shoulder) has been ruled out for Week 9 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: Donaldson wasn’t able to practice again Friday, and the 22-year-old tailback won’t be available for the Week 9 skirmish against Cleveland. Alvin Kamara will likely be the top option — and would have been even if Donaldson could play — in that contest, assuming his back injury allows him to play, of course. This is not a great situation, folks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: Alvin Kamara (NIR-rest/back) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: The way the team listed Kamara indicates that the back injury will not keep him from playing, but he is clearly still hurt. Kamara has been entirely ineffective this season and can only be viewed as a touchdown-dependent FLEX. CJ Donaldson (concussion/shoulder) was unable to practice today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: CJ Donaldson (concussion/shoulder) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: Donaldson aggravated a shoulder injury in Week 7 against the Steelers and did not return. He also entered the league’s concussion protocol after the game. A limited session today means he’s making progress on both fronts. He should be good to go for Week 9. The same is true of Alvin Kamara, who got a rest day today, despite his back injury also being noted on the report. Both backs will mix in behind Kendre Miller on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: CJ Donaldson (shoulder) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: Donaldson is the third member of the Saints’ backfield committee. While he will get a few touches this week, he is not getting enough work for fantasy relevance.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.headline: Chris Godwin caught all three of his targets for 13 yards in the Bucs’ Week 11 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.analysis: The Bucs leaned on Godwin on third downs, using him to move the chains on two of his three targets. That, however, is a cold comfort for fantasy managers. Godwin hasn’t hit 50 yards in a game this year and is still looking for his first touchdown. If you somehow made it this far into the season with Godwin on your roster, it’s past time to cut bait. He’s somewhere beyond the WR5 ranks heading into Week 12.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.headline: Chris Godwin caught 2-of-3 targets for 16 yards in the Buccaneers’ Week 9 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.analysis: The only positive to take from this is every Tampa Bay receiver who caught a pass clobbered their production from the week before. Godwin did have a 12-yard rush, but it’s another clunker for the wideout in a year where Godwin has yet to reach 50 yards. It’s a mistake to bet that mark will be reached in Week 11 against the Lions after their bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.headline: Chris Godwin failed to catch his only target in the Bucs’ Week 8 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.analysis: Godwin has fallen off the map this year, but forces beyond his control caused this goose egg. The Bucs did not complete a pass and only attempted three in total. With their defense terrorizing Michael Penix, Tampa Bay leaned on their ground game to an absurd degree. Emeka Egbuka is working through a foot injury and didn’t play today. Godwin will return to the WR4/5 border if he’s back for Week 9. Godwin would have some FLEX appeal if the Bucs are without their No. 1 receiver versus the Bears next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.headline: Chris Godwin caught 4-of-5 targets for 27 yards in the Bucs’ Week 7 win over the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.analysis: That might not look like much, especially with Emeka Egbuka on the shelf, but it was actually a 45 percent target share in a game where the Bucs attempted just 11 passes in a 43-13 victory. Godwin also had a score called back by a Bucky Irving illegal shift. Promising in theory, we suppose, though Godwin has not cracked 40 yards receiving since Week 2. He has not reached 50 all year. It feels like he will have to get more involved at some point, but then again, this team has a lot of young receiving talent. Godwin’s WR4 prospects are hanging on by a thread heading into Week 8 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.headline: Chris Godwin caught 4-of-8 targets for 37 yards in the Bucs’ Week 6 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.analysis: Godwin’s eight targets today go down as a season-high, but he failed to make much of his opportunities, per usual. The veteran wideout hasn’t hit 50 receiving yards in a game this year and is still looking for his first touchdown of the season. With Emeka Egbuka pulling away as the team’s WR1, there isn’t much volume headed Godwin’s way. With Jalon Daniels likely to make another start next week, Godwin is tumbling down the WR4 ranks ahead of Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.headline: Chris Godwin caught all three targets for 37 yards in the Buccaneers’ Week 5 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.analysis: Godwin’s three targets finished tied for fourth on the team behind Emeka Egbuka, Cade Otton, and Kenny Gainwell on a night backup quarterback Jalon Daniels attempted only 25 passes. Week 5 now marks the fourth game in five tries in which Godwin was held to four targets or fewer, leaving the veteran wide receiver completely unusable in a fantasy setting, for the time being. He can safely be stashed on benches ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.headline: Chris Godwin caught 6-of-7 targets for 31 yards in the Bucs’ Week 4 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.analysis: UDFA rookie Jalon Daniels made his first career start and leaned on Godwin for some easy completions. Godwin led the team in catches and targets, though Cade Otton surprisingly led the way in yards with 37. Godwin set new season highs in targets and catches. The Bucs are operating an incredibly low-wattage offense without Baker Mayfield, but Godwin could continue to see enough work to return WR4 numbers in PPR leagues. He will put that to the test versus the Cowboys in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.headline: Chris Godwin (ankle) is not on Tampa Bay’s final Week 4 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.analysis: Godwin was a full participant for two straight days after a Wednesday DNP. The insertion of Jalon Daniels makes him (well, makes every Buccaneers player) hard to trust for Week 4, but Godwin is probably still in the FLEX conversation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.headline: Chris Godwin (ankle) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.analysis: Godwin should be expected to play in Week 4 against the Packers at this point, although he has mostly underperformed thus far. Buccaneers OC Zac Robinson said earlier that Godwin Jr. “is a stud and will continue to do his thing. The ball will find him.” That might be harder than one imagines with an undrafted free agent rookie at quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.headline: Chris Godwin (ankle) returned to practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.analysis: It will likely go down as a limited session for the veteran wideout, but Godwin should be on track to play in Week 4. The bad news is that he will do so with UDFA rookie Jalon Daniels as his quarterback. Godwin was already off to a slow start, and things aren’t likely to improve with a backup quarterback under center. He is low-wattage FLEX play for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard rushed 21 times for 110 yards in the Titans’ Week 11 loss to the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: Pollard was held without a catch on one target. Frustrating, though fantasy managers will take Pollard’s third 100-yard rushing effort in four weeks considering the Titans were down 27-9 at halftime. Pollard was “keeping the defense honest” as Cam Ward again showed increased play-making ability in the passing game. Pollard has now cleared 75 yards from scrimmage in five straight contests after doing so just once in the first five games of the season. He is amongst a number of Titans just genuinely playing better, though it is still not translating to victories. That will remain a pipe dream for Week 12, but Pollard will be rematching with a Jaguars defense he got for 99 yards from scrimmage in Week 10. It must be noted that was due in large part to a ridiculous eight receptions, which probably won’t be repeated seeing as Pollard has only 22 on the year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard rushed nine times for 33 yards in the Titans’ Week 10 loss to the Jaguars, adding eight catches for 66 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: Pollard was bottled up on the ground throughout this contest, but Cam Ward leaned on him for easy completions as the Titans played from behind. Pollard eventually cashed in on one of them with a 32-yard score on a simple checkdown. Pollard broke several tackle attempts from Jaguars defenders that could only be descried as effortless. The return of Tyjae Spear had no impact on his role, though that could change as Spears gets healthier. Pollard remains a volume-based RB2 for his Week 11 date with the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard (finger/rest) is not on Tennessee’s final Week 10 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: A Friday tradition unlike any other. Pollard, somehow still a Titan, will suit up as an fringe RB2 against the Jaguars on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard (finger/rest) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: Pollard practiced in full yesterday, despite the finger injury. The Titans added the rest label to his listing today, indicating his absence is simply load management. We do not expect his snaps to be impacted by the finger injury this weekend. Tyjae Spears (knee) resumed practicing, though, which could hurt Pollard’s snap share. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports the Titans are holding on to Tony Pollard at the trade deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: Keeping a 29-year-old running back on the final year of his contract on your 1-7 cellar franchise is certainly a choice a team is allowed to make. We don’t know if it’s the one we’d make, but Pollard will be here to hover around RB2 value in games the Titans are pesky and RB3 value in games where the Titans offense plays as we’ve come to expect.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Titans aren’t interested in trading RB Tony Pollard.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: A previous report from Albert Breer suggested the team might be willing to trade Pollard, who is in the last year of his contract, for a fourth-round pick. Schefter threw cold water on that theory, reporting Tennessee isn’t interested in trading the 29-year-old running back. Showing fresh legs in recent weeks, Pollard is a solid RB2 the rest of the way even on a struggling Titans offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer thinks the Titans might be willing to trade away Tony Pollard in exchange for a fourth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: Breer believes a fourth-round pick “seems like a lot” to give up for an aging running back who is set to enter free agency at the end of the year. So, Pollard might end up staying in Tennessee. Breer adds that the Titans could also consider trading away Calvin Ridley for a worse Day 3 pick, but he isn’t sure if the team is eager to get rid of pass catchers while they are attempting to develop their young quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard rushed 21 times for 117 yards and a touchdown in the Titans’ Week 8 loss to the Bengals, adding three receptions for 20 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: Pollard had his second-straight multi-touchdown game, scoring the first touchdown of the game on a 40-yard scamper with multiple missed tackles and a stiff-arm in the first quarter. With Tyjae Spears out, Pollard was the only Titans running back that got touches. He recovered his own fumble in the second half and added a one-yard score in the third quarter. He was also dropped for a safety in the third quarter on a head-scratching delayed hand-off to give the Bengals two points. Pollard enters the Titans’ Week 9 bye with several trade rumors swirling; if he is still in Tennessee, Pollard is a fantasy RB2 for Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: With two DNPs to start the week, Spears looks unlikely to play on Sunday. He also missed Week 7 with the knee issue. Tony Pollard racked up 28 touches and scored three rushing touchdowns. While we’re not banking on another multi-score outing anytime soon, his role alone is worth an RB2 ranking if Spears remains out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard had 25 rushes for 129 yards and three touchdowns in the Titans’ Week 7 loss to the Browns, adding three catches for 26 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: Pollard, whose last big game before Sunday was against these same Browns in 2025, scored two first quarter touchdowns against a Cleveland rush defense that seemed uninterested in tackling Pollard. He scored a third rushing touchdown in the fourth quarter, and could have had a fourth score if not for a Browns goal line stand. Pollard has seen big workloads with Tyjae Spears (knee) sidelined but hadn’t done much with the opportunity before Sunday. The Titans offense operated quickly, using no-huddle through much of the game. That created more play volume that benefited Pollard and the rest of the Titans offense. As long as Spears remains sidelined, Pollard should remain in 12-team lineups next week against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara rushed one time for one yard in the Saints’ Week 11 loss to the Bears, adding one reception for one yard and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: Kamara was the third running back in the Saints backfield, seeing just six total snaps. He came in for a fourth-and-goal pay at the one-yard line and caught a Tyler Shough pass for the touchdown. Kamara only received one carry for one yard. The Saints have a frustrating backfield committee, with Travis Etienne getting the bulk of the carries, CJ Donaldson running routes, and Kamara coming in for the occasional red zone target. Three touchdowns in his last two games keeps Kamara on the fantasy radar, though he is close to a zero without the red zone opportunities. Kamara is best left on benches for Week 12 against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara had two rushes for four yards and a touchdown in the Saints’ Week 10 loss to the Panthers, adding three catches for 10 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: Kamara somehow came up with both Saints touchdowns on the day even with Travis Etienne returning from injury and operating as the de facto RB1. Kamara didn’t even lead the backfield in routes, logging 13 pass routes to 14 for Etienne, who had three grabs for 20 yards. Fantasy managers would do well not to chase Kamara’s Week 10 touchdown production when the Saints take on the Bears in Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Travis Etienne had eight rushes for 14 yards in the Saints’ Week 10 loss to the Panthers, adding three catches for 20 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: The Saints wasted a few first half plays trying to get Etienne involved in his first game back from an extended injury absence. Those plays predictably went nowhere, and it was Alvin Kamara who had the big fantasy day, scoring both Saints touchdowns — one through the air, the other on the ground. Etienne logged 13 routes to 12 routes for Kamara. The Saints backfield is among the least appealing for fantasy purposes and has been for some time. Etienne will be a desperation deep league option in Week 11 against the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara (back) is not on New Orleans’ final Week 10 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: As usual, Kamara’s back listing has not prevented him in any real way from playing. A potential Travis Etienne activation off injured reserve could cut into his FLEX value in Week 10, but if Etienne stays on IR, Kamara will be a reasonable play against a rough Panthers run defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara (NIR-rest/back) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: The Saints’ veteran running back is just having his reps managed. With Audric Estime playing well and Travis Etienne (hamstring) potentially returning, Kamara does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats at this time. Kamara will continue to chip in on passing downs, though. Backup RB CJ Donaldson (shoulder) remains sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara (NIR-rest/back) was not seen practicing on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: We expect to see Kamara listed with his typical NIR-rest/back designation when the team’s official injury report is released later today. An update will be provided if this is not the case. With Travis Etienne (hamstring) now practicing and Audric Estime playing well, Kamara is barely fantasy-relevant.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara rushed six times for 32 yards in the Saints’ Week 9 win over the Browns, adding three catches for 17 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: The Saints added Audric Estime via waivers on Monday and he went on to lead the team in carries today. He saw 15 rushes plus one target. Estime also found the end zone after Kamara was tackled at the two-yard line. Kamara was the team’s primary back on passing downs, but his role between the tackles remained incredibly limited. With Travis Etienne potentially returning next week, his role could take another hit in Week 10. He remains a low-upside RB4 for his upcoming matchup with the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara has no injury designation for Week 9 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: Kamara was limited due to rest and a back injury, but unsurprisingly, he’ll be good to go for Sunday’s contest against the Browns. The Saints’ run game is a disaster, but Kamara should be involved enough in the pass game to make him a decent FLEX play for that contest.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara (NIR-rest/back) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: The way the team listed Kamara indicates that the back injury will not keep him from playing, but he is clearly still hurt. Kamara has been entirely ineffective this season and can only be viewed as a touchdown-dependent FLEX. CJ Donaldson (concussion/shoulder) was unable to practice today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: CJ Donaldson (concussion/shoulder) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: Donaldson aggravated a shoulder injury in Week 7 against the Steelers and did not return. He also entered the league’s concussion protocol after the game. A limited session today means he’s making progress on both fronts. He should be good to go for Week 9. The same is true of Alvin Kamara, who got a rest day today, despite his back injury also being noted on the report. Both backs will mix in behind Kendre Miller on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.headline: Travis Etienne rushed 14 times for 76 yards in the Saints’ Week 11 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.analysis: The good news is that Etienne started the game for the Saints backfield and received 14-of-16 running back carries. He led the backfield with 21 total snaps as Audric Estime was a healthy scratch against the Bears. Etienne’s best run of the day was a 46-yard carry in the second quarter, where he was chased down and tackled inside the five-yard line. He got two more opportunities and got the ball to the one-yard line, but did not get the touchdown on that drive. Etienne’s lack of passing-game usage and Alvin Kamara’s involvement as a touchdown scorer caps Etienne’s ceiling for fantasy purposes. He belongs in the RB3 ranks for Week 12 against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.headline: Travis Etienne had eight rushes for 14 yards in the Saints’ Week 10 loss to the Panthers, adding three catches for 20 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.analysis: The Saints wasted a few first half plays trying to get Etienne involved in his first game back from an extended injury absence. Those plays predictably went nowhere, and it was Alvin Kamara who had the big fantasy day, scoring both Saints touchdowns — one through the air, the other on the ground. Etienne logged 13 routes to 12 routes for Kamara. The Saints backfield is among the least appealing for fantasy purposes and has been for some time. Etienne will be a desperation deep league option in Week 11 against the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports the Saints plan to activate Travis Etienne (hamstring) from injured reserve ahead of Week 10’s game against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.analysis: Etienne practiced in full this week and now Pelissero reports he’s in line to return against the Panthers in Week 10. The 27-year-old running back deserves FLEX consideration in a plus matchup against Carolina, though he could be on a snap count in his first game in over a month.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.headline: Travis Etienne (hamstring) is questionable for New Orleans’ Week 10 game against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.analysis: He did practice again today, finally hitting a full session, so he at least has cleared a full week of practices if nothing else. If Etienne does play he could be a reasonable FLEX option. There are reports that he could be on a snap count if he does play, and that mixes with the early-season usage to create a situation that isn’t necessarily guaranteed to smash. That said, the Panthers are an enticing matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.headline: Travis Etienne (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.analysis: Etienne is firmly in the questionable camp for the Saints’ Week 10 game against the Panthers. New Orleans Football’s Nick Underhill believes that the Saints would keep Etienne on a snap count if he makes his return this weekend, noting “they took it easy” on Jordyn Tyson, who returned from a lengthy hamstring injury last week. If active, Etienne likely warrants low-end RB2 treatment.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.headline: Travis Etienne (hamstring) resumed practicing on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.analysis: Coming off injured reserve, Etienne can practice for 21 days before the Saints must officially either activate him or shut him down. The Saints’ No. 1 running back has been sidelined since unsuccessfully trying to play through a hamstring strain in Week 3 against the Raiders. Audric Estime could warrant RB2/FLEX treatment again this week if Etienne is not ready to face the Panthers on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.headline: Saints head coach Kellen Moore said the team is still deciding when it will open Travis Etienne’s (hamstring) 21-day return window.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.analysis: Etienne hasn’t played since suffering a hamstring injury in Week 3 against the Raiders. The 27-year-old back will need to have his 21-day return window opened before he can take the practice field, so we’ll see if Moore and the staff elect to designate him for a return ahead of Wednesday’s practice. Until that happens, Alvin Kamara, Kendre Miller, and CJ Donaldson will continue to operate as the Saints’ top options, with Kamara the likely leader in what has been an underwhelming backfield this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.headline: Saints placed Travis Etienne on injured reserve with a hamstring injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.analysis: This is a tough break. The Saints’ high-priced free agent signee will be sidelined for at least four games. Their Week 8 bye makes him eligible to return in Week 9. Veteran RB Alvin Kamara is the next man up, followed by RB Kendre Miller. Both should be rostered in 12-team leagues. Kamara will likely get the first crack at the starting job, but he has struggled to play efficiently this season, and coach Kellen Moore gave RB CJ Donaldson the backfield’s first green zone touch last week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.headline: Saints coach Kellen Moore said Travis Etienne Jr. (hamstring) “will miss time” and that a timeline for his return has not yet been determined.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.analysis: It’s unclear how much time Etienne will miss, but it wouldn’t be surprising if this became an injured reserve stint. Alvin Kamara could find himself in a more elevated role next week, perhaps with Kendre Miller joining him in a committee. Etienne exited Week 3’s loss to the Raiders with the injury after rushing for 57 yards on 13 carries. It had already been a tough scene for Etienne-reliant fantasy managers this year just based on how the results on the field were going; this won’t help.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.headline: Saints RB Travis Etienne exited Week 3 against the Raiders after suffering an apparent hamstring injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.analysis: Etienne entered the game with a hamstring injury and appears to have aggravated it on an explosive run. The Saints’ starting running back broke off a 16-yard gain in the third quarter, setting up a Saints passing touchdown on the following play. Etienne could be seen grabbing at his left hamstring at the end of the run. He had mostly been limited to modest single-digit gains before that, rushing 13 times for 57 yards and catching 2-of-2 targets for 13 yards on the day. He seems highly unlikely to return. Etienne and the other veteran running backs notably ceded the first backfield touch inside the green zone to RB CJ Donaldson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.headline: Cade Otton caught 1-of-3 targets for eight yards in the Bucs’ Week 11 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.analysis: Otton popped up with a four-catch, eight-target game before the Bucs’ Week 10 bye. He was unable to build on that box score and all but disappeared today. Otton hasn’t topped five catches or 56 yards in a game this year. He has also been held without a touchdown through nearly three months of action. He’s barely even a TE2 for Week 12 against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.headline: Cade Otton caught 4-of-6 targets for 25 yards in the Buccaneers’ Week 9 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.analysis: Otton was targeted a couple of times in the end zone, but Baker Mayfield wasn’t able to connect with the tight end on either attempt. The 25 yards are his most since Week 5, but it’s still a middling — at best — effort for the 27-year-old. Fantasy managers should look elsewhere in Week 11 against the Lions after Tampa Bay’s bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.headline: Cade Otton was not targeted in the Bucs’ Week 8 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.analysis: Otton has one catch over his past three appearances and hasn’t hit 40 yards since Week 3. The Bucs, who only attempted three passes today, will increase the pass volume in Week 9, but that alone won’t be enough to get Otton back into fantasy lineups. He is not even in the TE2 mix for Week 9 against the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.headline: Cade Otton was held without a catch in the Bucs’ Week 7 win over the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.analysis: What seemed like it could maybe be a pop-up performance for Otton in Emeka Egbuka’s (concussion, foot) absence instead turned into a one-target day as the Bucs rode their rushing attack and Panthers turnovers to a dominant road W. Otton typically comes with a 3-4 catch floor, but the same has been true of his “ceiling” this season. He will continue to struggle to get into the mix ahead of Week 8 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.headline: Cade Otton caught 1-of-2 targets for four yards in the Bucs’ Week 6 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.analysis: Otton had caught between three and five passes in every game this year until today, so this goes down as his first true bust of the season. On the other hand, he has peaked at five catches and 56 yards with zero touchdowns thus far, so the ceiling has been nonexistent. Otton could increase his production once Baker Mayfield is back in the lineup, but it doesn’t look like that will happen next week. He is barely in the TE2 conversation as long as Jalon Daniels remains under center.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.headline: Cade Otton caught 4-of-6 targets for 37 yards in the Bucs’ Week 4 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.analysis: Otton’s 37 yards were somehow enough to lead Tampa Bay, though that largely speaks to the ineffective nature of the team’s passing attack. With Jalon Daniels under center, there simply wasn’t much production to go around. He was intercepted twice and threw for just 148 yards. With Daniels likely to make his second start of the year on Week 5, Otton is a low-end TE2 for his upcoming matchup with Dallas.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.headline: Cade Otton caught 3-of-6 targets for 56 yards in the Bucs’ Week 3 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.analysis: As usual, Otton led the Bucs in pass routes and was second on the team in targets behind Emeka Egbuka. Most of Otton’s production came on a 37-yard catch in the first half. Baker Mayfield narrowly missed the tight end for another long gain later in the contest. Otton’s route involvement should keep him in deep league lineups next week against the Packers, unless Mayfield (hand) is sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.headline: Cade Otton caught 5-of-6 targets for 38 yards in the Bucs’ Week 2 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.analysis: Otton led the Bucs in targets while running nearly every route. This has been Otton’s role for quite some time. You know what you’re getting if you use Otton in fantasy lineups: He’s something of a PPR cheat code when the Bucs hit a negative game script. He’ll be a deep league option in Week 3 against the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.headline: Cade Otton caught 3-of-5 targets for 26 yards in the Bucs’ Week 1 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.analysis: This is about a standard Otton statline, though this one came on a day where Baker Mayfield attempted fewer than 30 passes. With Jalen McMillan sidelined, Otton probably would have exceeded five catches had the Bucs not kept killing drives with sacks and turnovers, alas. Otton is always good for a few PPR points on the back end of the TE2 ranks, but that appears to be his ceiling heading in to his age-27 campaign.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.headline: Buccaneers TE Cade Otton said there is “a lot of play action” in new OC Zac Robinson’s scheme.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.analysis: This is the kind of thing we like to hear for QB Baker Mayfield and his pass catchers. Robinson did not feature play action during his two seasons as the Falcons’ offensive coordinator, nor did former Buccaneers OC Josh Grizzard, so Otton’s comments are reassuring. Per PFF, NFL offenses averaged 7.76 yards per pass play with play action and just 6.72 without it. Upping the play action rate should help the Buccaneers run a more efficient offense in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.headline: Kenneth Gainwell rushed four times for 16 yards in the Bucs’ Week 11 loss to the Lions, adding four catches for 43 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.analysis: Bucs coach Todd Bowles told reporters on Monday that Gainwell could see more touches going forward to help keep Bucky Irving fresh. That couldn’t have been further from the truth today as Irving out-touched Gainwell 21-8. Gainwell did, however, post his second-best receiving line of the year. His only better game came two weeks ago, before Tampa’s bye, against the Bears. Gainwell might finally be developing a receptions-based floor, but a two-game sample can’t be taken as gospel. Gainwell will remain on the RB3/4 border when he takes on the Panthers next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.headline: Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said Bucky Irving’s touches could decrease in the second half of the season to preserve his health.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.analysis: As Bucs beat writer Greg Auman points out, Irving is on pace for 315 carries this season, which would have been the second most in the league last year. Irving has not missed a game yet this season, but after injuries limited him to 10 games in 2025, it’s not surprising to learn Bowles may want to dial things back a bit. The efficient play of Kenneth Gainwell in recent weeks has also earned him an expanded look, and it should instill a bit of confidence in OC Zac Robinson when asking him to spell Irving in certain situations. With the Bucs now entering their bye week, we will get our first look at how the team plans to deploy its backfield in Week 11 when they visit the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.headline: Kenny Gainwell rushed five times for 16 yards in the Buccaneers’ Week 9 loss to the Bears, adding three catches for 60 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.analysis: Most of Gainwell’s yardage came on a 44-yard busted coverage that set up the Bucs’ first score of the game. He found little room in the run game after gashing the Falcons for 140 yards. The 1A/1B talk that head coach Todd Bowles mentioned with Gainwell and Bucky Irving never really came to fruition, as Irving was much more effective with 97 yards on the ground and a pair of scores. Gainwell remains a RB3 going forward, with his next chance to contribute coming in Week 11 against the Lions after their bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.headline: Kenny Gainwell (hip) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.analysis: Gainwell has been a little more involved in recent weeks, and coach Todd Bowles recently told reporters that they are getting closer to the 1A/1B usage that they envisioned when they signed him. Gainwell will again play sidekick to Bucky Irving this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.headline: Kenny Gainwell was a full participant in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.analysis: Gainwell never seemed in danger of missing Week 9 against the Bears, but the 27-year-old should be just fine for the Week 9 bout against the Bears. He’s coming off a monster 140-yard performance against Atlanta, but keep in mind that Tampa Bay was basically a service academy school for that game with zero completions. He’s closer to FLEX than RB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.headline: Kenneth Gainwell (hip) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.analysis: Gainwell played through the hip injury last week to the tune of 25 carries. He starts out the week limited, but fantasy managers should expect to see the 27-year-old to play in Week 9 against the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.headline: Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said RB Kenneth Gainwell’s usage is getting closer to the “1A, 1B” usage the team envisioned when signing him.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.analysis: Gainwell saw 25 carries in a run-heavy game against the Falcons in Week 8. Bowles said, “I think we finally got to where we’re utilizing Kenny more and more, and that’s kind of the 1A, 1B we were talking about when we first signed him.” Gainwell saw 50-percent of the snaps for the first time all season last week and now has back-to-back weeks of at least 14 carries. He is still seeing low utilization in the passing game and game script has certainly played a role in his recent role, but it is notable that Bowles mentions the Bucs envisioned a 1A/1B backfield pairing between Bucky Irving and Gainwell. Despite Bowles’ comments, fantasy managers should anticipate Irving operating with the majority of backfield touches, like he did from Weeks 1-6. We will still have to see Gainwell’s usage in a more neutral game script to feel confident about him as a fantasy option moving forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.headline: Kenneth Gainwell rushed 25 times for 140 yards in the Bucs’ Week 8 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.analysis: Bucky Irving gave the Bucs a 16-0 lead entering the fourth quarter and passed the baton to Gainwell, who racked up 18 carries in the final frame. Irving only touched the ball once over the final 15 minutes. Gainwell’s late-game dominance got him up to career-highs in carries and yards. He also managed a season-high 14 attempts under similar circumstances last week. Unfortunately for Gainwell, the Bucs aren’t likely to be playing with a big lead in Week 9 against the Bears. Gainwell will return to the RB3/4 border next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.headline: Kenneth Gainwell (hip) is active for Week 8 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.analysis: Right tackle Luke Goedeke is also active. Gainwell will continue mixing in behind Bucky Irving this week. He has yet to hit a dozen fantasy points in a game this year and there’s no reason to expect that to change anytime soon. Gainwell is a low-end RB4 for Week 8. Inactive for the Bucs are DL DeMonte Capehart, WR Emeka Egbuka, CB Ayden Garnes, OT Luke Haggard, and OG Billy Schrauth.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Kenneth Gainwell (hip) is “good to go” for Week 8 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.analysis: Week 7 was Gainwell’s first game with more than seven touches all year. He handled 14 opportunities, all of which were carries, and they came in a 30-point blowout win over the Panthers. Unless the Bucs stay hot and roll over the Falcons, expect Gainwell’s touch total to return to the single digits. He is barely in the RB4 mix for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/zavion-thomas/.headline: Zavion Thomas caught 2-of-3 targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in the Bears’ Week 11 win over the Saints, adding one carry for 30 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/zavion-thomas/.analysis: Thomas was the subject of multiple explosive plays against the Saints. He saw just offensive 10 snaps, but Ben Johnson schemed up multiple plays to utilize the rookie receiver’s speed. A 40-yard reception in the third quarter and 30-yard rush in the second quarter highlighted a career-best day for Thomas. He is still not fantasy relevant, but his usage should be monitored as the Bears scheme up more plays for him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/zavion-thomas/.headline: Zavion Thomas caught all five of his targets for 140 yards and a touchdown in the Bears’ preseason win over the Titans on Saturday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/zavion-thomas/.analysis: The score and the bulk of the yardage came on one play, a 97-yard connection with Tyson Bagent. Thomas has some of the best speed of any rookie wideout — or any wideout regardless of age — and while he’s dealt with injuries in camp, the ability to grab and go is apparent. He’s not likely to be a significant contributor to begin the year, but he’s someone who has to be monitored in this Chicago passing attack.

https://www.nbcsports.com/zavion-thomas/.headline: Zavion Thomas (knee) returned to practice on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/zavion-thomas/.analysis: He missed about a week with a knee injury. Thomas has big-time speed and feels likely to connect on a few deep shots this year with Ben Johnson calling the plays, but he’ll likely need injuries in front of him to obtain fantasy relevancy. Especially now that he’s missed a chunk of training camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/zavion-thomas/.headline: Bears WR Zavion Thomas exited practice early after suffering an apparent knee injury on Sunday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/zavion-thomas/.analysis: According to CHGO Bears’ Adam Hoge, Thomas went down at practice on Sunday, “briefly grabbed his knee and then walked off with a slight limp.” Hopefully, the Bears’ speedy third-round rookie only suffered a minor injury. Bears coaches were likely hoping to get an extended look at Thomas in preseason play after he turned in a strong showing in spring practices. Bears WR Luther Burden (groin) is currently sidelined, leaving the wide receiver corps somewhat thin at the moment.

https://www.nbcsports.com/zavion-thomas/.headline: ESPN’s Courtney Cronin listed Bears WR Zavion Thomas as the team’s “biggest surprise” player in spring practices.
https://www.nbcsports.com/zavion-thomas/.analysis: Thomas turned in a 4.28-second 40 at the NFL Scouting Combine this year. Per Cronin, he has taken “ample reps as a punt returner this spring and showed that he can be more than a special teams star with his skill set on offense.” Bears coach Ben Johnson said Thomas was regularly making plays, but adds that they need to “make sure that we can trust him and he’s going to align where he needs to and run the route the way we need him to.” It sounds like Thomas is still in the developmental phase, but if he can refine his route running and prove himself reliable, he “could be a big weapon” for the Bears this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/zavion-thomas/.headline: The Athletic’s Kevin Fishbain believes the “expectation” is that Kalif Raymond will be the team’s No. 3 receiver.
https://www.nbcsports.com/zavion-thomas/.analysis: Jahdae Walker could position himself as the No. 3 with a second-year jump, and third-round pick Zavion Thomas is also in the mix. This room will probably split the snaps enough to make them unappealing from a fantasy perspective, but it’s possible someone emerges as a WR4-type.

https://www.nbcsports.com/zavion-thomas/.headline: Bears selected LSU WR Zavion Thomas with the No. 79 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/zavion-thomas/.analysis: Thomas ran the third-fastest 40 (4.28 seconds) at the NFL Scouting Combine. He made the Freshman All-American team as a punt returner at Mississippi State in 2022. After transferring to LSU in 2024, he bagged third-team All-SEC honors as a kick returner. Over the course of his college career, he found the end zone as a receiver, rusher, punt returner and kick returner. He posted career highs in receptions (41) and receiving touchdowns (four) last year, while totaling 488 receiving yards. Thomas (5’10/190) profiles as an impactful special teams player with the Bears as a rookie. He may have to wait until 2027 or later to earn much of a role as a wideout.

https://www.nbcsports.com/zavion-thomas/.headline: Louisville received a commitment from unrated 2022 WR Zavion Thomas.
https://www.nbcsports.com/zavion-thomas/.analysis: Thomas is unrated for now, but with a full scholarship from Louisville, he will certainly end up with a star rating soon. The 5-foot-11, 190-pound speedster reportedly runs in the low 4.30s for the 40-yard dash. That figure would be absurd for a soon-to-be pro, let alone someone who has yet to even leave high school. Thomas could eventually become a speed menace for the Louisville offense, similar to Tutu Atwell recently.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justice-hi.headline: Justice Hill rushed six times for 69 yards and a touchdown in the Ravens’ Week 11 loss to the Panthers, adding four receptions for 27 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justice-hi.analysis: Hill fell victim to one of the worst rules in football when he fumbled inside the Panthers’ five-yard line on a 36-yard run and watched the ball run out of the end zone. The turnover resulted in a touchback that rewarded the Panthers with the ball at Baltimore’s 20-yard line, but Hill would get his revenge on the following drive when he ran in a 19-yard touchdown to put the Ravens up 26-22 before halftime. Despite the gaffe early in the game, Hill was very efficient in this one, averaging a solid 9.6 yards per touch while being a difference-maker both on the ground and through the air. He has now seen double-digit opportunities in four straight weeks, but he remains difficult to trust as anything more than an RB4/Flex play, especially with Derrick Henry around to vulture any short-yardage touchdowns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justice-hi.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Giants inquired about Ravens RB Justice Hill.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justice-hi.analysis: Schefter reports that Hill rather than Derrick Henry was the running back the Giants called the Ravens about. While Henry is certainly the better back between the two, Schefter also reported that the Ravens won’t trade him. With Cam Skattebo (hamstring) doubtful and Tyrone Tracey on injured reserve, the Giants are looking for help in the backfield. Hill would help in that regard, but until a trade is consummated, he doesn’t have much standalone fantasy value behind Henry in Baltimore.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justice-hi.headline: Justice Hill rushed nine times for 85 yards and a touchdown in the Ravens’ Week 9 loss to the Jaguars, adding seven yards on three receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justice-hi.analysis: Hill became the first running back to amass more than 75 yards against the Jaguars since the start of the 2025 regular season with a 65-yard touchdown with the game well out of hand in the second half. It was an otherwise poor showing for the entirety of the Baltimore offense with a rookie undrafted free agent starting his first NFL game. Hill remains nothing more than a desperation FLEX ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justice-hi.headline: Justice Hill (groin) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justice-hi.analysis: Hill saw eight targets in a blowout loss last week. Third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano peppered him with check-downs, though Hill only managed four catches. With Fagnano making his first career start tomorrow, Hill should continue to rack up targets in Week 9. He’s in the RB4 mix in PPR leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justice-hi.headline: Justice Hill (groin) was listed as limited on Monday’s estimated practice report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justice-hi.analysis: The fact he was listed as limited and not a “DNP” likely signals a more modest injury and we would expect Hill to suit up when the Ravens take on the Jaguars on Thursday Night Football in Week 9. Either way, fantasy managers likely have better options at the position.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justice-hi.headline: Justice Hill rushed three times for 15 yards in the Ravens’ Week 8 loss to the Bills, adding four receptions for 20 yards on eight targets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justice-hi.analysis: Hill nearly turned into a surprise PPR scam this week with rookie UDFA Joe Fagnano under center for two-and-a-half quarters of play. Hill’s eight targets led all Ravens players, but his 20 receiving yards were largely buoyed by back-to-back receptions during a two-minute drill when the Ravens were facing second and third and longs. Despite the high-volume day, it’s hard to rely on anybody in this offense, which could have dark days ahead with Lamar Jackson (thumb) out for the foreseeable future and Tyler Huntley also dealing with a toe injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justice-hi.headline: Ravens placed Adam Randall on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justice-hi.analysis: Cornerback Bilhal Kone was also placed on IR. Both players can return after four games. Randall was likely parked behind Justice Hill as the Ravens’ RB3 heading into the season. That role now belongs to Rasheen Ali, at least until Randall is back in action. He played in the team’s final preseason game and the team has not said what this injury is yet.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justice-hi.headline: The Athletic’s Jeff Zrebiec believes the Ravens see Justice Hill “as a good complement to Derrick Henry and really value his ability out of the backfield and in blitz pickup.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justice-hi.analysis: Hill ended 2025 on injured reserve because of a neck issue. He was reportedly a cut candidate during the offseason and the team selected Clemson running back Adam Randall on Day Three of the draft. It seemed possible that the team planned on replacing Hill this year, but Zrebiec shot that idea down, at least for the start of the season. Zrebiec answered, “I can’t see that happening from the jump,” in reference to a question about Randall opening the season as Baltimore’s backup running back. Hill caught 21 passes for 169 yards and a touchdown in 10 games last year. He also punched in a pair of touchdowns on the ground despite running just 18 times. His ceiling is extremely limited, even in the event of a Henry injury, but Hill should have some standalone RB4 value in PPR leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justice-hi.headline: The Athletic’s Jeff Zrebiec reports Justice Hill has “been mentioned as a potential salary-cap cut.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justice-hi.analysis: Hill has a $3.8 million cap figure, of which the Ravens can save $3.1 million with a release. He missed the final six weeks of the season with a long-term neck injury, and turns 29 next November. Zrebiec brought up this idea in mentioning that the Ravens could chase a running back in the lower rounds of the draft to add to the room behind Derrick Henry.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justice-hi.headline: Ravens coach John Harbaugh said Justice Hill (neck) could return in “3-4 weeks.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justice-hi.analysis: Rasheen Ali will continue as the Ravens third-down back in the meantime, per Harbaugh. Keaton Mitchell is probably a better second Ravens back to roster at this point for most fantasy leagues than Ali. Hill can be dropped in all shallow formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Baker Mayfield completed 20-of-33 passes for 187 yards and two touchdowns in the Bucs’ 31-21, Week 11 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Mayfield appeared to be unlikely to suit up for today’s game when the week started, but a pair of limited practices was enough to get him on the field today. Things got off to a scary start when he was crushed for a sack-fumble on his first dropback of the day. He would go on to take four sacks for a total loss of 33 yards. Somehow, Mayfield looked more than willing as a runner, adding 36 yards on six carries. It was ultimately a solid fantasy outing from Mayfield, assisted by a garbage-time touchdown to Ted Hurst. A date with the Panthers next week will keep Mayfield in the QB2 mix next week, but he’s far from the best streaming option available to most fantasy managers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Baker Mayfield (foot) is active for Week 11 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Mayfield is going to try to play through the plantar fascia injury he suffered in Week 9 before the Bucs’ bye. Expect the Bucs to lean on their ground game for as long as possible to protect Mayfield. Even in a good matchup, it’s hard to treat him as anything better than a mid-range QB2. EDGE Yaya Diaby is also active. Inactive for the Bucs are DT DeMonte Capehart, CB Ayden Garnes, OG Trevor Keegan, OG Billy Schrauth, QB Easton Stick, and S Antoine Winfield Jr.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Baker Mayfield (foot) will play in Week 11 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Mayfield looked unlikely to play after missing Wednesday’s practice. He inexplicably returned for Thursday’s session before being listed as questionable the next day. He’s dealing with a plantar fascia injury that hobbled him in the team’s Week 9 loss to the Bears. A Week 10 bye was just enough time off to get him back on the field without any time missed. Even in a great matchup with the Lions, it’s hard to trust Mayfield as anything other than a mid-range QB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Buccaneers QB Baker Mayfield (foot) is dealing with a plantar fascia injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: While Mayfield remains on track to play against the Lions on Sunday, he’s dealing with a painful plantar fascia injury, according to Pelissero. If the 31-year-old gunslinger suits up in Week 11, he’ll wear a special orthotic and new cleats to help stabilize his foot. Mayfield looked doubtful to play earlier in the week and even missed practice Wednesday before getting in a pair of limited sessions. Jalon Daniels would start if Mayfield isn’t able to play this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Baker Mayfield (foot) is questionable for Tampa Bay’s Week 11 game against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Mayfield got in two limited sessions after missing Wednesday with the injury. Todd Bowles spoke to reporters earlier today and said that he was “trending in the right direction” to start this week. He seems to be on the optimistic side of questionable, Jalon Daniels would grab the start if Mayfield is unable to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said Baker Mayfield (foot) is “trending” in the right direction to start in Week 11 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Mayfield reportedly looked good in Friday’s practice and logged back-to-back practices to close out the week. We should have an update on his official game status soon, but all signs are pointing to him starting this week against a Lions team that has allowed the fifth-most passing yards this season. We will check back in with an official update when the team provides it.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Baker Mayfield (foot) was spotted at Friday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Mayfield will close out the week with back-to-back practices, which should give him a decent chance at playing in Week 11’s game against the Lions. Things looked doubtful for Mayfield earlier in the week, especially after the Bucs signed Cooper Rush to the practice squad on Monday. We should get official word on Mayfield’s status shortly, but it’s safe to say he is trending in the right direction at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Baker Mayfield (foot) returned to practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Mayfield did not practice Wednesday after injuring his foot ahead of the Bucs’ Week 10 bye. It initially looked like he would miss his Week 11 game against the Lions. Now he might be on the right side of questionable. Mayfield was spotted going through ball security drills and hopping over pads early in the practice. He certainly looked like a quarterback who was preparing to play in a few days. Mayfield hasn’t been all that productive this year, but he would still be an upgrade over Jalon Daniels. This is a situation to monitor heading into the weekend. After his limited practice today, Mayfield told reporters that he feels “ready” to play on Sunday, though the team has not made an official ruling. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Baker Mayfield (foot) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Fox Sports’ Greg Auman said Mayfield “came out in street clothes, shoes, no wrap or boot on foot” while Jalon Daniels took first-team reps ahead of Tampa’s Week 11 game against the Lions. If Mayfield is unable to log a practice tomorrow or Friday, Daniels will get another start for the Bucs in a plus matchup against Detroit. Daniels will be usable in superflex formats, while Bucs pass catchers will be nothing more than desperation options.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Baker Mayfield is dealing with a foot strain.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: He didn’t go as far as to rule out Mayfield this week, but between the Buccaneers signing Cooper Rush to the practice squad and elevating Easton Stick to the 53-man roster, they have already signaled that there’s a real chance Mayfield misses Week 11. Rapoport said it “seems to be trending towards” Jalon Daniels suiting up under center for the Bucs against Detroit on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Mitchell Evans caught 5-of-5 targets for 44 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 11 win over the Ravens.
Panthers TE Mitchell Evans (ankle) was carted off the field in practice Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Head coach Dave Canales spoke to media following the morning session specified the nature of the injury, calling it an ankle issue. The injury occurred in an 11-on-11 rep early in the day. The second-year tight end is behind both Tommy Tremble and Ja’Tavion Sanders on the depth chart but could work his way into more snaps with a strong showing this summer. This injury does not help on that front.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Mitchell Evans failed to catch his only target in Carolina’s Wild Card Round loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Evans was relegated to the background on the rare occasions when Ja’Tavion Sanders was healthy, finishing his rookie season with a 19/171/2 receiving line. He enters 2026 third on the Carolina tight end depth chart, but showed some flashes and wouldn’t be a bad TE2 flier if he had a non-trivial role in this offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Ja’Tavion Sanders caught both of his targets for nine yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 16 win over the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Sanders was targeted just twice, but one of those targets was a six-yard touchdown catch. The other one was an attempted hurdle for a three-yard gain in the first half. Rookie Mitchell Evans caught three passes for 23 yards as well. The tight end spot in Carolina is a mix of multiple players. Sanders ran 20 routes and saw 31 snaps, while Tommy Tremble saw 23 snaps and Evans saw 16 snaps. Sanders is the pass-catching tight end while Evans is more of the blocker, but neither should be on fantasy radars for Week 17.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Mitchell Evans caught his only target for four yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 5 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: That’s back-to-back games with a touchdown for the rookie tight end. Ja’Tavion Sanders was out with an ankle injury, so Evans split reps with Tommy Tremble this week. Neither player caught more than one pass. Evans’ game-winning score should earn him more work going forward, but fantasy managers shouldn’t count on a fantasy-relevant role in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Panthers signed No. 8 overall pick WR Tetairoa McMillan to a four-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Panthers officially bring their X-wide receiver into the fold via a $27.93 million deal. McMillan should immediately compete for the team lead in targets and should produce fantasy-friendly results in year one. The Panthers also signed third-round OLB Princely Umanmielen, fourth-round S Lathan Ransom, fifth-round DT Cam Jackson, fifth-round TE Mitchell Evans and sixth-round WR Jimmy Horn Jr.. Dynasty managers should take note of Horn, who could eventually work his way into three-wide receiver sets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Panthers selected Notre Dame TE Mitchell Evans with the No. 163 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Evans (6’5/258) spent four seasons at Notre Dame, totalling over 400 receiving yards in each of his last two. Injuries hampered his production as he suffered a broken foot as a sophomore and a partially torn ACL as a junior. Testing with a 1.55 10-yard split, No. 1 among tight ends at the NFL Combine, Evans is a good athlete who can work the middle of the field. His quickness to get open in the short area makes him a strong pass-catcher. As a blocker, he has the size and strength to be impactful in-line. Evans does not add much after the catch but is versatile enough to work out of both the slot and in-line positions. If he can stay healthy, Evans has the tools to be a secondary tight end option in the NFL.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Notre Dame TE Mitchell Evans (foot) to miss time this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Evans (6'5"/250) had surgery on his foot back on July 14th after injuring it during offseason training. The sophomore finished last season with two receptions for 21 yards and will play behind Michael Mayer when he returns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews caught 2-of-3 targets for 14 yards in the Ravens’ Week 11 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: Andrews’ disappointing performance comes a week after he caught eight targets for 82 yards in Jacoby Brissett’s debut with the Ravens. The Ravens worked to get all three tight ends involved in this one, as Andrews, Matthew Hibner, and Josh Cuevas combined to get eight targets, with Andrews and Cuevas both getting three looks. Andrews’ promising performance against the Chargers gave fantasy managers a reason to hope for more this week, especially with six teams on bye. With all 32 teams playing in Week 12, it’s safe to say Andrews shouldn’t be treated as anything more than a desperation play on the road against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews caught all eight targets for 82 yards in the Ravens’ Week 10 loss to the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: The presence of Jacoby Brissett and his elevated tight end target rate benefited Andrews, leading to a season-high 82 receiving yards on eight receptions. Andrews suddenly has the profile of a back end TE1 after nine weeks of poor performances and gets a solid matchup against the reeling Panthers in Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews caught both targets for 19 yards in the Ravens’ Week 9 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: Andrews, somewhat disgustingly, led the team in receiving with a modest 19 yards on a night undrafted free agent rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano threw for only 60 yards in his first career start. It remains difficult to start the veteran tight end, who has made more mental mistakes this season than he has receptions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews (hand) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: Andrews has been playing through the hand injury for a few weeks without any issues. He logged three full practices this week. With Joe Fagnano making his first career start for the Ravens tomorrow, we wouldn’t advise playing any Ravens outside of Derrick Henry and Zay Flowers this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews (hand) was listed as a full participant on Monday’s estimated injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: That keeps the veteran tight end on track to suit up in Week 9 against the Jaguars on Thursday Night Football. Andrews has struggled to return usable fantasy weeks throughout his age-31 season, with the team now down to their third, potentially fourth, quarterback for Thursday’s game. he can safely be left on fantasy benches on the short week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews caught 3-of-4 targets for 14 yards in the Ravens’ Week 8 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: It was another day at the office for Andrews, who has now gone six straight games with 28 or fewer receiving yards. Any hope that he might see a slight increase in production with Lamar Jackson back under center can be put aside after Jackson suffered a severe injury to his throwing hand that will require surgery and force him to go on injured reserve. Andrews isn’t on the fantasy radar heading into Week 9 against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews caught 3-of-4 targets for 23 yards in the Ravens’ Week 7 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: It was business as usual for Andrews, who can be consistently relied on for a solid 20-yard game. Andrews has gone for 28 or fewer yards in five straight games and will not be on the fantasy radar in Week 8 against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews caught 1-of-3 targets for four yards in the Ravens’ Week 6 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: Andrews ran 11 more routes than rookie tight end Josh Cuevas but was out-targeted by Cuevas 5-to-3. Andrews continues to underwhelm in the passing game and has now failed to surpass 28 yards in four straight games. He can be left on waivers ahead of Week 7’s game against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews caught 4-of-6 targets for 28 yards in the Ravens’ Week 5 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: Andrews dropped a would-be touchdown on the team’s opening possession on a ball that went through his hands in the end zone. He would then fumble on the following possession, which Jessie Bates returned for a touchdown to force the Ravens into catch-up mode for the remainder of the game. Luckily for him, late heroics from Tyler Huntley and Derrick Henry had the team escaping with a victory. Andrews has not looked great to start the 2026 season, having not eclipsed 50 yards through five games. He’ll remain a shaky fantasy start in Week 6 when the Ravens host the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews (hand) is practicing in full for Week 5 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: Andrews practiced in full with the hand injury last week before posting a 5/27/1 receiving line. He should be good to go again this week, though he is a low-end TE1, with backup QB Tyler Huntley likely starting in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Cam Ward completed 21-of-30 passes for 248 yards and two touchdowns in the Titans’ 51-30, Week 11 loss to the Cowboys, adding two rushes for three yards and a third score.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Recalled from fantasy benches for streamer duties vs. the defense-less Cowboys, Ward had his first three-score game of the year. It was also his third straight multi-score effort after managing just one in first seven starts. No. 3 was a 12-yard garbage time connection with Calvin Ridley, but that description doesn’t really do it justice. Flushed from the pocket and seemingly running out of bounds, Ward instead made like prime Aaron Rodgers and threw the ball across his body, across the middle of the field into Ridley’s arms like it was a loaf of bread. It was the most impressive play of his young NFL career, and an exclamation point on his recent improved play. Today was a soft matchup, but that was not the case for the Jaguars in Week 10, with whom Ward must now rematch in Week 12. Despite his hot streak, Ward will find himself outside the top 20 for Thanksgiving week because of his tough setup and all 32 teams being active for the holiday slate.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter believes that the Titans or Chargers would host “an auction” for the 2027 NFL Draft’s No. 1 overall pick if either team gets it.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Titans are currently in position to receive the No. 1 overall pick, and the Chargers are right behind them. Schefter spent much of the segment discussing the Titans, who Schefter says have “enough conviction” in Cam Ward that they would pass on the opportunity to draft Oklahoma State QB Drew Mestemaker. He cites the Dolphins, Jets, Cardinals and Browns as potential suitors. Poor play from Ward could still change minds in the Titans’ front office, but for now, it seems as though his job is secure.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Titans coach Robert Saleh said the Titans shifted the offensive philosophy to give Cam Ward “an opportunity” to prove he’s a franchise quarterback.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: “A few weeks ago we made a shift on how we’re letting Cam Ward run the offense, let him be a field general. ... He’s looking more comfortable, his footwork is improving, and he’s doing a nice job playing quarterback. Still things he can clean up,” Saleh added. Ward over the last two weeks has four touchdown passes and his two highest passing-attempt totals of the season. We’re not exactly excited to fire up Ward as a QB1 streamer at this point, even against the Cowboys in Week 11, but given how many NFL offenses are currently trending down it’s worth pointing out that the Titans are actually taking a step forward of late.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Cam Ward completed 28-of-39 passes for 231 yards, two touchdowns, and an interception in the Titans’ 40-23, Week 10 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ward also led the Titans with 39 rushing yards. He got off to an ugly start by throwing an interception to Travis Hunter. Ward attempted a throw across his body to a receiver with very little separation. He didn’t lead Elic Ayomanor enough and Hunter made a great play on the ball. Ward improved throughout the contest, but not enough to make this an awfully competitive game. Still, he threw two touchdown passes for the second time this year. The first was in Week 8 before Tennessee’s bye. Ward will be worth a look as a streamer when he takes on the Cowboys next week, though only as a low-end QB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Cam Ward completed 26-of-40 attempts for 304 yards, two touchdowns, and a fumble in the Titans’ 43-36, Week 8 loss to the Bengals, adding seven carries for 41 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ward also added a two-point conversion on the ground. The Titans offense got off to a fast start, leading 13-0 after one quarter. Ward finished the day passing for 304 yards, averaging 7.6 yards per attempt and surpassing 300 yards for the first time in his career. He made plays with his legs, scrambling for multiple first downs on short-yardage situations. A sack-fumble from Ward led to a Bengals score the other way in the third quarter and the 24-year-old also took a long sack towards the end of regulation to send the game into overtime. The Titans could not convert a fourth down in overtime to close the game. Ultimately, Ward had one of the best games of his season against the Bengals but came up short. For fantasy purposes, Ward’s work on the ground is encouraging for his elevated floor and an improved passing skillset makes him a fantasy QB2 heading into the Titans’ Week 9 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Cam Ward completed 20-of-31 attempts for 181 yards and an interception in the Titans’ Week 7 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ward did his best game manager impression in this one and made a handful of solid high-leverage throws using various arm angles. He had a positive EPA per drop back and was slightly over his expected completion rate, small victories at this point but still victories. The Titans deployed no-huddle for much of the game and operated at a quick pace — a strategy that seemed to get Ward into some sort of rhythm early on. Ward’s accuracy issues showed up on the fourth quarter when he sailed a pass over the head of a wide open tight end who had beaten the entire Cleveland secondary. It would’ve likely been a game-winning touchdown. Ward has now cracked 200 passing yards just once through Week 7 and should only be rostered in superflex formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Cam Ward completed 11-of-22 passes for 102 yards, one touchdown and an interception in the Titans’ 26-20, Week 6 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ward added just three carries for seven yards. Ward got the “quarterback win” as the Titans finally broke their five-game losing streak to begin the season, but this was more about the Colts imploding and setting up one short Titans field after another with turnovers. Ward did keep his connection with No. 4 overall rookie Carnell Tate going, finding him for 6/70/1 on seven targets. Ward didn’t find veteran Calvin Ridley for what would have been a wide open end zone grab, but we digress. His interception was a second quarter sail job as he was getting leveled by the blitz. Ward’s increasing chemistry with Tate is the Titans’ first real good news of the season, but today was not a particularly inspiring victory. They now get the Browns for a Week 7 home matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Titans head coach Robert Saleh said he had a “cool conversation” with Cam Ward.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ward’s head, per Saleh, is in a “good place” ahead of the Titans’ Week 6 game against the Colts. Ward has been dreadful through five weeks, ranking 24th in EPA per drop back and 27th in drop back success rate. Only five quarterbacks have a lower adjusted yards per attempt than Ward this season. Daniel Jones and Tyson Bagent are the only QBs who average fewer fantasy points per drop back. Saleh has defended his second-year QB at every turn and does not seem close to benching him in favor of journeyman backup Mitchell Trubisky.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Cam Ward completed 23-of-36 passes for 170 scoreless yards and an interception in Tennessee’s Week 5, 26-3 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Titans led off the day with a 58-yard field-goal drive that fell apart from a red zone first-and-5. They would not even flirt with crossing 30 yards in a drive for the rest of the game and crossed into Texans territory on only 11 more snaps all game, including just one inside the Houston 40. Ward took four sacks and avoided several others by turning Tyjae Spears into a PPR hero.
