https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.analysis: After being upgraded to a full participant on Thursday, Knight is officially off of the injury report and good to go for Sunday’s game against the Rams. Both Knight and Tyler Allgeier are expected to factor heavily into the Cardinals’ running game this weekend, especially with Carson Beck making his first career start with a depleted receiving corps. Both Knight and Allgeier will be fringe RB3/Flex plays in a game that could prove tough for the Cardinals’ banged-up offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.headline: Bam Knight (concussion) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.analysis: Knight is on track to resume his lead rushing role this week. Unfortunately, the Cardinals face the Seahawks, potentially rendering Knight a touchdown-dependent FLEX starter against their elite defense. Hopefully, Knight remains setback-free for the rest of the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.headline: Bam Knight (concussion) resumed practicing on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.analysis: Knight sat out in Week 9 against the Seahawks, but he is on track to resume his lead rushing role against the Rams this week. He was seen wearing a yellow non-contact jersey today, and will likely be listed as limited. The Rams’ defense is enjoying improved health and playing well. Knight will likely handle a FLEX-worthy role, but producing a ceiling game against this defense may be unlikely.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.headline: Cardinals declared RB Bam Knight, CB Starling Thomas V, LB Eku Leota, OL Jayden Williams, OL Jon Gaines III, and OL Albert Reese IV inactive for Week 9 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.analysis: Knight’s absence due to a concussion leaves Tyler Allgeier alone atop the running back depth chart with rookie Jeremiyah Love on injured reserve. The matchup is far from ideal against the Seahawks on the road, but Allgeier appears to be in line for a legitimate workhorse role and can be started as a viable RB2. The Cardinals press forward with veteran journeyman Gardner Minshew under center following the trade of Jacoby Brissett this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Bam Knight (concussion) will not play in Week 9 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.analysis: LaFleur also ruled out OL Jon Gaines II (ankle) and OT Jayden Williams (knee). Knight has been a DNP all week after suffering a concussion in Week 8’s win over the Cowboys and will officially be sidelined for Week 9. His absence, along with Jeremiyah Love’s (ankle) could create a bell cow role for Tyler Allgeier, who totaled 191 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns in last week’s win, while fourth-year vet Evan Hull could also work into the mix. Allgeier’s volume alone will put him in the RB2 conversation this week despite the tough matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.headline: Bam Knight (concussion) was not spotted at Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.analysis: It appears it’ll be another DNP for Knight as he entered the concussion protocol following Sunday’s win over the Cowboys in Week 8. The 25-year-old tailback seems unlikely to be able to go in Week 9 against the Seahawks, but there should be further updates on Knight’s status soon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.headline: Bam Knight (concussion) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.analysis: Knight entered concussion protocol after a hit to the head in Week 8 against the Cowboys. Starting out as a DNP this week means he still has a few steps to go to clear protocol by Sunday. Unless he can progress through protocol quickly, Knight is on the wrong side of questionable for Week 9 against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Bam Knight is in the league’s concussion protocol.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.analysis: Knight will need to clear protocol if he hopes to suit up in time to play in Week 9 against the Seahawks. The former UDFA has turned in a solid season thus far for the Cardinals, rushing for 28-168-0 while adding another six receptions for 43 additional yards. With Jeremiyah Love (ankle) likely to miss time, Knight could again find himself in a split with Tyler Allgeier when he returns. The Cardinals will likely need to address their running back room at some point in the week with Allgeier currently being the only healthy back on the roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.headline: Bucky Irving rushed 18 times for 68 yards and a touchdown in the Bucs’ Week 11 loss to the Lions, adding three catches for 32 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.analysis: It was a tumultuous day for fantasy managers who watched this one from start to finish. Irving broke off an 80-yard touchdown at the top of the third quarter, only for it to be called back via a holding penalty. Irving was leveled by Brian Banch a few plays later and appeared to suffer an injury. Trainers took the field to give him a look, but Irving eventually popped back up and was good to go a few plays later. Irving would go on to punch in a one-yard score later in the third quarter. Per usual, Irving operated as the unquestioned lead back, out-carrying Kenneth Gainwell 18-4. Irving has worked his way into the RB1 ranks ahead of his Week 12 game against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.headline: Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said Bucky Irving’s touches could decrease in the second half of the season to preserve his health.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.analysis: As Bucs beat writer Greg Auman points out, Irving is on pace for 315 carries this season, which would have been the second most in the league last year. Irving has not missed a game yet this season, but after injuries limited him to 10 games in 2025, it’s not surprising to learn Bowles may want to dial things back a bit. The efficient play of Kenneth Gainwell in recent weeks has also earned him an expanded look, and it should instill a bit of confidence in OC Zac Robinson when asking him to spell Irving in certain situations. With the Bucs now entering their bye week, we will get our first look at how the team plans to deploy its backfield in Week 11 when they visit the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.headline: Bucky Irving rushed 20 times for 97 yards and two scores in the Buccaneers’ Week 9 loss to the Bears, adding four catches for 28 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.analysis: Irving was held in check for the first three quarters outside of a short rushing touchdown, but broke several tackles to open the fourth quarter on a 25-yard gain. He scored again in the fourth quarter to tie the game at 24-24 and now has six rushing scores in 2026. It wasn’t quite the monster effort he produced against the Falcons (27/170/1) the week prior, but still a very strong fantasy day for the 24-year-old tailback. Irving should be considered as an RB1 against the Lions in Week 11 after a bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.headline: Bucky Irving rushed 27 times for 170 yards and a touchdown in the Bucs’ Week 8 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.analysis: The Bucs became the first team in over 50 years to not complete a pass for an entire game. In turn, Irving was able to rack up a career high in rush attempts. He then turned that into a career high in yards by averaging over six yards per carry. He could have posted even better numbers, but the Bucs put him on ice after his third-quarter touchdown. With the exception of one attempt from Irving, Gainwell saw 18 consecutive rush attempts to close the game. Gainwell wound up running for 140 yards on 25 attempts. To the Bucs’ credit, Gainwell was picking up chunk gain after chunk gain and Irving had already earned a massive workload. Irving failed to hit 100 yards on the ground in any of his first three games. He has since reached triple digits three times in his past four outings. Playing some of the best football of his career, Irving is pushing for an RB1 rank headed into Week 9 versus the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.headline: Bucky Irving (rest) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.analysis: Irving was absent from Thursday’s sessions with an official “rest” designation, allowing fantasy managers to breath a collective sigh of relief after the veteran back has morphed into a borderline workhorse in recent games. Managers can likely continue forward with Irving in their starting lineups as an upside RB2 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.headline: Kenneth Gainwell (hip) returned to practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.analysis: Gainwell missed Wednesday’s session with the hip issue. He will likely be listed as limited today, but that still puts him on track to play in Week 8 against the Falcons. Gainwell racked up 14 carries in a blowout win over the Panthers last week, but that hasn’t been the norm for him. Gainwell is averaging 6.4 touches per game and has topped out at three receptions in a week. He is buried in the RB4 ranks for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.headline: Kenneth Gainwell (hip) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.analysis: Gainwell suffered the hip injury while logging a season-high 14 rush attempts in Week 7. The Bucs blew out the Panthers and racked up 49 carries as a team. Bucky Irving would be in line for more work on passing downs if Gainwell is out for Week 8. Sean Tucker could also see an uptick in snaps, though his normal role has very little overlap with what Gainwell does. Per usual, Irving looks like a high-end RB2 this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.headline: Bucky Irving rushed 24 times for 106 yards and two touchdowns in the Bucs’ Week 7 win over the Panthers, adding a four-yard reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.analysis: The two-score day on the ground was somehow the first of Irving’s career. He led the way as the Bucs rolled up a ridiculous 258 yards rushing in a stunning road clobbering of the Panthers. That means Irving ceded plenty of work to Kenneth Gainwell and a little to Sean Tucker, but everyone got home as the Bucs simply dominated on the ground. Irving’s scores came from four and one yards out, meaning he had the goal-line advantage on Tucker while the game was still in doubt. It was a really strong performance, and a nice bounce-back effort after a rough Week 6. This figures to remain an up and down offense and rushing attack, but Irving has proven to be a high-end RB2 more weeks than not. That will include for Week 8 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.headline: Bucky Irving (illness) is not on the Buccaneers’ final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.analysis: As is typically the case with ill players, Irving is good to go for this week’s game. He upgraded to full participation today after getting a limited session in on Thursday. The Buccaneers’ No. 1 running back has been a volatile producer this season, yet even with last week’s flop, he still totaled 21 touches. That type of workload keeps him firmly in the RB2 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.headline: Bucky Irving (illness) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.analysis: The Buccaneers’ No. 1 running back is on track to play in Week 7 against the Panthers. The offense is expected to be led by Baker Mayfield (thumb), who will play with a protective plate on his hand to prevent re-injury. Irving should be good to go this week and can be treated as a high-end RB2, as usual.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kyle-mccord/00.headline: Kyle McCord completed 12-of-33 passes for 102 yards and an interception in the Dolphins’ 26-9, Week 11 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kyle-mccord/00.analysis: McCord didn’t look as bad as the stats suggest, but it was not a great game. He overthrew some receivers on key plays, but his receivers also had some drops, and the Buffalo secondary looked good as well. The rookie should find things a little easier next week against the Jets, but he’s still not a recommended option in fantasy leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kyle-mccord/00.headline: Kyle McCord completed 17-of-32 passes for 209 yards and a fumble in the Dolphins’ 24-22, Week 10 loss to the Colts, adding two carries for four yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kyle-mccord/00.analysis: Making his first career start in his NFL debut, McCord had a mix of explosive plays and turnover-worthy plays while taking three sacks on the day. The Dolphins offense committed a false start on the first snap and McCord briefly had his throwing hand looked at after hitting it on a helmet on the Dolphins’ first possession. He missed Greg Dulcich on a fourth down in the red zone in the first half and fumbled for a Colts touchdown to open the second half. McCord was able to hit more explosive plays in the fourth quarter with the Colts’ top two cornerbacks out with injury. He rushed for a touchdown to open the fourth quarter and get the Dolphins within two points. The Dolphins could not finish the comeback, mainly due to kicking woes. McCord showed the desire to put the ball in danger to hunt explosive plays in the second half, a good sign that he can keep a player like Caleb Douglas fantasy-relevant. With six teams on bye, McCord can be considered a QB2 against the Bills for Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kyle-mccord/00.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Kyle McCord is set to make his NFL debut against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kyle-mccord/00.analysis: McCord! Daniel Jones throwing to Ashton Dulin! All the stars are here in Week 10! Even in an elevated matchup, there’s little reason to believe that McCord will be more than a bottom-five superflex option this week. And this might wind up being one of his good starts, if indeed the Dolphins commit to giving him multiple cracks while Malik Willis is on injured reserve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kyle-mccord/00.headline: Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said the team traded for Kyle McCord to be the team’s No. 2 quarterback, but that he expects recently-claimed Brady Cook to “make a push.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/kyle-mccord/00.analysis: Riveting situation. The main fantasy takeaway here is probably something like “if Malik Willis gets hurt this year, all Dolphins pass-catchers will take major downgrades.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/kyle-mccord/00.headline: Dolphins acquired QB Kyle McCord from the Packers in exchange for a sixth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kyle-mccord/00.analysis: The news was first reported by ESPN’s Adam Schefter. The draft pick going to the Packers is a 2028 sixth-round pick. After trading Quinn Ewers to the Jaguars, the Dolphins acquired their new backup QB in McCord, who had an impressive preseason. The Dolphins new GM and HC came from Green Bay this offseason and so did both of the quarterbacks on their active roster in McCord and starter Malik Willis. McCord was a sixth-round pick by the Eagles in the 2025 NFL Draft and is yet to appear in a regular season game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kyle-mccord/00.headline: Eagles signed RB Audric Estime to their practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kyle-mccord/00.analysis: The second-year back will get a fresh start in Philadelphia, perhaps eventually pushing A.J. Dillon off the roster. Also on Philadelphia’s practice squad are: LB Chance Campbell, WR Elijah Cooks, G Kenyon Green, TE E.J. Jenkins, CB Brandon Johnson, OLB Patrick Johnson, TE Cameron Latu, WR Terrace Marshall, QB Kyle McCord, CB Parry Nickerson, T Hollin Pierce, OLB Antwaun Powell-Ryland, CB Eli Ricks and S Andre Sam.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kyle-mccord/00.headline: Ohio State freshman QB Kyle McCord completed 13-of-18 for 318 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in Saturday’s 59-7 win over Akron.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kyle-mccord/00.analysis: McCord (6'3"/210) got the start as CJ Stroud got the night off due to a shoulder injury. There is a reason why McCord was a five-star recruit, he looked great. He got the Buckeyes on the board when he hit Chris Olave in the back of the end zone for five yards. He later hit Jaxon Smith-Njigba a little short, but he was able to reach in front of the Akron defender and grab the 34-yard touchdown. His night was over midway through the third quarter as Jack Miller came in with OSU holding a comfortable lead. Even with the great performance by McCord, Stroud is still the guy. Ohio State will travel to Rutgers next Saturday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kyle-mccord/00.headline: Ohio State freshman QB Kyle McCord will start Saturday’s game against Akron, per Big Ten Network.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kyle-mccord/00.analysis: With freshman starter C.J. Stroud down due to a shoulder injury, either McCord (6'3/210) or Jack Miller was in line to start Saturday night. McCord won out in the end, but it would not come as a surprise if Miller got some reps as well. Stroud is available, but only in case of an emergency.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kyle-mccord/00.headline: Ohio State freshman QB Kyle McCord will compete in practice for the start against Akron.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kyle-mccord/00.analysis: Coach Ryan Day said backup QB McCord (6'3"/210) and third-string QB Jack Miller will compete in practice for the starting role against Akron on Saturday. Cj Stroud (shoulder) will be an emergency-only option. Whether it’s McCord or Miller who get the start this week for the Buckeyes, it’s a one-time deal.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kyle-mccord/00.headline: Ohio State HC Ryan Day has not made a decision on a backup quarterback as of now.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kyle-mccord/00.analysis: CJ Stroud is obviously this team’s starter and has been mentioned several times as early as this past offseason as a player who could become one of the top prospects at his position in the future granted that he shows to be what some have projected he can be as the season goes on. Buckeyes HC Ryan Day has said that he has not settled on a backup QB yet, though freshman Kyle McCord has largely been the projected favorite for the No. 2 spot. Ohio State also has junior QB J.P. Andrade, senior Jagger LaRoe and freshman Jack Miller are also on the depth chart at the position.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.headline: Noah Gray caught 3-of-5 targets for 21 yards in Kansas City’s Week 11 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.analysis: Gray played 45-of-70 snaps, more than any receiver or tight end but Travis Kelce and Rashee Rice. He remains just a low-end TE2 sort of bet, but it was Gray’s highest target total of the year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.headline: Noah Gray caught both of his targets for 15 yards and a touchdown in the Chiefs’ Week 8 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.analysis: Gray extended his streak of catching at least two (but no more than three) passes to five games. He also got in the end zone for the first time this year on a four-yard strike from Patrick Mahomes. Gray is a solid real-life tight end, but his role is too limited to be worth a look, even in deep fantasy leagues. He is not on the fantasy radar headed into Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.headline: Noah Gray caught all three targets for 44 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 7 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.analysis: The fact that the team’s top two tight ends tied for the most production through the air at a modest 44 yards tells the story of how the game went against the Seahawks, who limited the Chiefs to just 213 yards of total offense. The absences of the team’s top two receivers continue to place stress on an offense with no true vertical threat, although their primary downfield option was lost for the season prior to their bye. Gray remains unlikely to return weekly fantasy value for as long as Kelce remains healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.headline: Noah Gray caught all three of his targets for 53 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 6 win against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.analysis: The Chiefs used more two tight end sets with Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton sidelined. Gray ran a route on around half of KC’s drop backs and matched Travis Kelce with 53 yards. If Kelce struggles to play through the ankle injury he picked up against the Bolts, Gray could step in as the team’s TE1 in Week 7 against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.headline: Noah Gray caught 3-of-5 targets for 30 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 18 loss against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.analysis: Gray led the Chiefs in targets for 30 receiving yards in another miserable offensive outing for the Mahomes-less KC offense. It was a season-best game for Gray, who once again played behind Travis Kelce and had just five games with more than 20 receiving yards. He had 21 receptions for 178 yards in 2025. Gray, 26, is signed through the 2027 season and could have an increased role in the team’s passing offense if Kelce retires this offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.headline: Noah Gray (concussion/shoulder) practiced in full on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.analysis: Gray missed last week’s game with the concussion. The shoulder issue is a new addition to his practice report, though a full practice means it won’t stop him from suiting up this week. Gray isn’t on the fantasy radar for Week 14 but does bring plenty to the table as an extra blocker and a backup tight end for the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.headline: Chiefs TE Noah Gray (concussion) has been ruled out for Week 13 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.analysis: Gray sustained a head injury last week against the Colts and entered the league’s concussion protocol. He won’t suit up on a short week. It could mean a slight target bump for TE Travis Kelce. Gray had five receptions on seven targets over his past two games as a rotational tight end in the KC offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.headline: Chiefs TE Noah Gray (concussion) did not practice on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.analysis: Gray has slowly seen his role in the passing game grow over the past month, accumulating 12 targets in Kansas City’s last four games. It looks very unlikely he’ll be up for Thursday’s game against the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.headline: Noah Gray caught a two-yard pass in the Chiefs’ Super Bowl LIX loss to the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.analysis: Gray’s short grab was his lone target in a blowout loss. Coming off back-to-back solid seasons as the Chiefs’ No. 2 seam stretcher, Gray signed a new three-year deal on the eve of Week 1 and proceeded to post a career-best slash of 40/437/5 as Travis Kelce continued to decline. Gray’s five scores tied for ninth amongst tight ends, though his modest eight red zone targets suggest that number was a fluke. It was still an encouraging campaign for the 25-year-old with Kelce looking like a retirement candidate. Were that to transpire, Gray would suddenly be in the lower-end TE1 mix for a Chiefs skill corps that remains undermanned despite its continued Super Bowl appearances.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.headline: Noah Gray caught 1-of-1 targets for one yard and rushed once for negative-four yards in the Chiefs’ Week 18 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.analysis: Gray logged just four total snaps in this one, indicating the Chiefs value him as a capable passing-game contributor. Most skill position starters rested in this one though some, like Gray, remained active in a reserve capacity. Gray could be an interesting leverage option in playoff DFS tournaments.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/max-hurlem.headline: Max Hurleman caught 6-of-7 targets for 61 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 11 loss against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/max-hurlem.analysis: Hurleman, a converted quarterback who did not have a reception coming into Week 11, led all Steelers pass catchers in receptions and receiving yards, making an impressive touchdown grab late in the fourth quarter. Hurleman ran a route on just 15 of the team’s 58 drop backs on the day. He might have seen more playing time because DK Metcalf kept fighting with Eagles defenders until he was ejected in the third quarter. Hurleman remains a long way from fantasy relevance in any case.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/max-hurlem.headline: Steelers waived K Ben Sauls.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/max-hurlem.analysis: R.I.P. to the Ben Sauls trade candidate era, which lasted about 50 minutes. Pittsburgh also waived DL Kyler Baugh, LB Mark Robinson, LB Julius Welschof, DB D’Shawn Jamison, DB Daryl Porter, OL Steve Jones, OL Aiden Williams, TE JJ Galbreath, RB Lew Nichols, WR Max Hurleman and WR Lance McCutcheon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-ale.headline: Giants declared DL Darius Alexander, S Jason Pinnock, OL Josh Sills, OT J.C. Davis, RB Greg Desrosiers, CB Nic Jones, and TE Thomas Fidone inactive for Week 11 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-ale.analysis: Alexander is a surprising healthy scratch for Week 11. The Giants will take on the ultra-efficient Jaguars offense with several defensive starters sidelined. It should be a good setup for every fantasy-relevant Jacksonville player.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/robert-hai.headline: Jaguars declared C Robert Hainsey, DE Danny Striggow, DT Matt Dickerson, WR CJ Williams, and S Jalen Huskey inactive for Week 11 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/robert-hai.analysis: Hainsey will be out for a while with a knee issue, a blow for an otherwise-solid Jacksonville offensive line. The Jags are among the healthiest teams headed into Week 11. They face off today against a middling Giants pass rush.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/robert-hai.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Jaguars C Robert Hainsey (knee) is considered week to week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/robert-hai.analysis: Jacksonville could be without its starting center for at least a few weeks. Fowler said Hainsey’s knee issue is likely not the season-ending variety though. Through Week 10, the Jaguars rank 18th in run block win rate and 12th in pass block win rate. The Jags this week take on a Giants defense that ranks 23rd in sack rate.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/robert-hai.headline: Jaguars C Robert Hainsey (consussion) is active for Week 10 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/robert-hai.analysis: Hainsey cleared concussion protocol earlier this week and is good to go. Inactive for the Jags are S Jessie Bates III, WR CJ Williams, DT Jordan Davis, DE Wesley Williams, and DT Albert Regis.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/robert-hai.headline: Jaguars agreed to terms with C Robert Hainsey, formerly of the Buccaneers, on a three-year, $21 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/robert-hai.analysis: $13 million in guaranteed money for Hainsey, and the crowd goes wild citing Tommy Condon of CAA’s work on the deal. The last time we blurbed about Hainsey it was in the context of the 2023 Buccaneers, who had Hainsey ready to step in for Ryan Jensen at center. Hainsey was rough in 2023 and replaced by Graham Barton after he was selected in the first round of the 2024 NFL Draft. The 2021 third-round pick will, judging by the size of the contract, be the favorite to start over Luke Fortner at center in Jacksonville.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/robert-hai.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports OL Ryan Jensen’s knee injury is “likely career ending.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/robert-hai.analysis: Jensen was placed on IR and will miss the 2023 season. The 32-year-old has been dealing with knee injuries the last two seasons and opted to not have surgery last year. Jensen retiring would help the Bucs, who would leave $4.7 million in dead money to release Jensen as a post-June cut next offseason. Tampa will turn to Robert Hainsey as the starting center in 2023.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/robert-hai.headline: Bucs placed C Ryan Jensen (knee) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/robert-hai.analysis: Tampa Bay is holding out hope Jensen can return late in the year, but odds are his season is still over after suffering a knee injury in practice this month. The Bucs are handing the keys over to 2021 third-rounder Robert Hainsey at center.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/robert-hai.headline: Buccaneers C Robert Hainsey was carted off the field Wednesday due to “bad cramps,” not a leg injury as originally reported.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/robert-hai.analysis: It’s a huge sigh of relief for Buccaneers players, coaches, and fans. Hainsey is in line to start at center, following Ryan Jensen’s knee injury, and reportedly looks up to the challenge. As decades of television commentary have taught us, Tom Brady is susceptible to pressure up the middle. Having a reliable starter at center will be critical to the Buccaneers’ offensive success this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/robert-hai.headline: Buccaneers C Robert Hainsey (leg) was carted off the field Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/robert-hai.analysis: Hainsey was thrust into a critical role for the Buccaneers when Ryan Jenson suffered a knee injury on July 28th. The second-year player out of Notre Dame had reportedly been “looking great” per ESPN’s Jeff Darlington, to the point that the Buccaneers were not expected to look for an outside replacement for Jensen. That will need to change if Hainsey suffered a serious injury as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/robert-hai.headline: NBC Sports’ Peter King reports Robert Hainsey is getting the first-team reps at center in Bucs camp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/robert-hai.analysis: With Ryan Jensen facing a long-term absence after suffering a knee injury early in camp, the Bucs are scrambling a bit at center. A third-round pick last year, Hainsey is the next man up. “Every day he’s facing Akiem Hicks and Vita Vea,” coach Todd Bowles told King. “If that can’t get you ready for the season, I don’t know what will.” The coach added he is not particularly worried about the situation. Still, this is an uncertain situation for a team squarely in win-now mode. It would not be surprising if the Bucs look to a free agent like J.C. Tretter to shore up the depth chart.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/robert-hai.headline: Bucs HC Todd Bowles said “we’re not sure of anything yet” when asked about how the team plans to address the loss of Ryan Jensen.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/robert-hai.analysis: Bowles also added to his response, “We’ve been in shorts and t-shirts. That will work itself out as training camp goes, and depending on how that works out, we’ll see if we go outside of the house or not.” The Bucs currently has linemen Robert Hainsey and Nick Leverett on the roster, who have appeared in a combined 11 games and seen little time at center. Free agent J.C. Tretter remains another interesting option, as the 31-year-old remains on the market after spending the last five seasons with the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Benjamin Morrison (hamstring) will not return in Week 11 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Morrison went down late in the first half and was ruled out in the third quarter. Kevin Knowles has taken his place in the lineup. Knowles is primarily a special teamer, so we wouldn’t be surprised to see Jared Goff pick on him in the final 15 minutes of this game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Buccaneers CB Benjamin Morrison (leg) did not practice at organized team activities on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Morrison missed time in his 2024 college season after injuring the labrum in his hip. He almost missed time as a rookie last year, after suffering a hamstring injury in October. He totaled three pass breakups, 23 tackles and two quarterback pressures last year. Hopefully, he can return before long.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Bucs are not expected to have LT Tristan Wirfs (oblique) for Week 14 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The same is true of rookie corner Benjamin Morrison, who is dealing with a hamstring injury. Wrifs got in one limited practice this week before being listed as questionable. He was always going to be a long-shot to play after missing the first two practices of the week. The fact that he returned on Friday at least indicates that he could be back for Week 15 versus Atlanta. Graham Barton moved from center to left tackle when Wirfs missed time at the start of the year. The Bucs will likely make that move again this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Chris Godwin (fibula) will not play in Week 6 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Godwin is just one of a laundry list of players who will not be active for the Buccaneers’ Week 6 game against the Niners. Godwin’s fibula injury is likely due to a reaggravation of the fractured fibula that ended his 2024 campaign, although the team has yet to confirm this. His absence on Sunday could open the door for Sterling Shepard to serve as the Buccaneers’ no. 2 target in the passing game opposite Emeka Egbuka, which could be of use to fantasy managers in deeper leagues. In addition to Godwin, the Buccaneers also ruled out CBs Zyon McCollum (thumb) and Benjamin Morrison (hamstring).

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Buccaneers ruled out Jamel Dean (hip) for Week 5 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: In addition to Dean, the Buccaneers also ruled out CB Benjamin Morrison (hamstring) and S Christian Izien (quad). Dean is the most notable absence here. Having appeared on 175 defensive snaps this season, per PFF, Dean has been stingy in coverage thus far, allowing just six receptions on 16 targets to go with 43 scoreless yards. Backup corners Jacob Parrish and Kindle Vildor figure to see some extended work with Dean now out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Buccaneers CB Jamel Dean (hip) did not participate in Wednesday’s walkthrough practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Dean left the Bucs’ Week 4 loss to the Eagles with a groin injury that now seems to be more of a hip issue. Also not practicing were CB Benjamin Morrison (hamstring) and DB Christian Izien (quad). If none of the trio can practice the rest of the week, the Bucs’ secondary will look depleted against the Seahawks for Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Bucs selected Notre Dame CB Benjamin Morrison with the No. 53 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Bucs finally address their defense after Thursday’s surprising selection of WR Emeka Egbuka, and at a position of need. Morrison (6’0/193) had one of the great debuts in Irish history, earning Freshman All-American honors, recording an 82.2 cover grade and six interceptions which was the most by a ND defender since 2012. He allowed just seven plays of 15+ yards on 87 targets/39 receptions over the last two seasons, in addition to an excellent 18.4 QBR allowed last year. 63.3% of his cover snaps were in press man situations. Which he thrived in and was often left to fend for himself on an island by DC/HC Marcus Freeman. Morrison’s 2024 campaign was cut short due to a torn labrum in his left hip, which kept him from testing and somewhat clouds his profile in the short term. He transitions smoothly in go-ball situations as opposed to navigating short and intermediate routes, as he had some trouble with more shifty, deceptive receivers. He showed natural ball skills and is pretty clean in his fundamentals, which helps to minimize mistakes. However, he needs to add strength and improve leverage in order to handle alpha NFL wide receivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Notre Dame CB Benjamin Morrison (hip) will work out for teams prior to the draft on April 21st.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Morrison is recovering from hip surgery after his 2024 season ended early. The 21-year-old appeared in six games last season, totaling 20 tackles and four pass-breakups. He totaled nine interceptions between his first two college seasons and is considered one of the top cornerback prospects in the 2025 NFL Draft. Teams will get a chance to see Morrison work out a few days before the draft as he works his way back from the hip injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Notre Dame received a verbal commitment from four-star 2022 CB Benjamin Morrison.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Morrison (6'0/175) is considered the 31st cornerback and fourth overall player in Arizona, drawing a .8958 player rating on the 247Sports composite board. He had no shortage of high-profile suitors on the recruiting trail with Oregon, Alabama, Washington, Arizona State, Auburn and Florida State all pursuing the blue-chip defensive back. The Phoenix, AZ native is the 19th player to commit to the Irish from a loaded 2022 class that currently ranks second in the nation in terms of recruiting strength next year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-jo.headline: Broncos declared S Brandon Jones, QB Sam Ehlinger, WR Lil’Jordan Humphrey, OL Gavin Ortega, OL Kage Casey, TE Dallen Bentley, and DL Jordan Jackson inactive for Week 11 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-jo.analysis: Jones was the only Bronco listed as questionable for today’s game. The rest are healthy scratches. Jones has five pass breakups and two interceptions this year. He’s out with a hamstring issue.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-jo.headline: Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) is not on the Broncos’ final injury report and will play in Week 11 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-jo.analysis: Hufanga has not played since Week 5. He nearly returned in Week 9, pre-bye, but was unable to do so. His return could be helpful for a Broncos’ defense that struggles to cover tight ends. Broncos S Brandon Jones (hamstring) is questionable to play, and CB Riley Moss (concussion) is good to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-jo.headline: Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) is practicing on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-jo.analysis: Hufanga nearly played pre-bye in Week 9 against the Panthers, but he was unable to do so. He has been sidelined since injuring his ankle in Week 5 against the Chargers. Broncos S Brandon Jones (hamstring) and CB Riley Moss (concussion) are also practicing. Check back on Friday for their official statuses.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-jo.headline: Broncos S Brandon Jones suffered a hamstring injury and will not return in Week 8 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-jo.analysis: With Talanoa Hufanga also sidelined heading into this game, both of Denver’s starting safeties from Week 8 are out. Luckily for Denver, Pat Surtani is back this week, giving them some extra firepower in their secondary. Jones has two interceptions and five pass breakups this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-jo.headline: Broncos placed S Brandon Jones (pectoral) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-jo.analysis: Jones suffered the injury in Sunday’s win over the Packers. The decision to place Jones on IR came after an MRI, which could indicate something more serious, although the team has not suggested that at this time. Jones has totaled 78 tackles, seven pass breakups, and one interception in 14 games for the Broncos this season. Safety Devon Key is listed behind him on the depth chart and will presumably take over in Jones’ absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-jo.headline: Broncos CB Riley Moss and S Brandon Jones were listed at “DNP” on Monday’s estimated injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-jo.analysis: The team did not hold a practice on Monday ahead of their Week 10 meeting with the Raiders on Thursday Night Football, but the fact two additional members of the secondary appeared on the injury report as non-participants is concerning considering the absence of Pat Surtain. Absences from either could improve the schematic matchups for Jakobi Meyers and Tre Tucker, with tight end Brock Bowers expected to see a good deal of coverage from standout safety Talanoa Hufanga.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-jo.headline: Free agent S Nico Bolden will work out for the Broncos on Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-jo.analysis: The report comes from the Denver Gazette’s Chris Tomasson. The Broncos are now without three safeties following Brandon Jones’ Friday hamstring strain, though Jones is expected to return in two weeks. Bolden’s initial NFL dreams were dashed by a torn meniscus suffered at his 2023 pro day. He played in seven games with the UFL’s St. Louis Battlehawks this season, earning a 68.2 PFF defense grade for his efforts. Bolden functions primarily as a box safety but has some free safety versatility.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-jo.headline: Broncos S Brandon Jones suffered a hamstring strain at training camp on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-jo.analysis: The training staff has yet to determine the injury’s severity but the Broncos are already in a tough spot at safety. The front office released four-time second-team All-Pro S Justin Simmons this offseason and both S Caden Sterns (patellar tendon) and S Delarrin Turner-Yell (ACL) are currently on the active/physically unable to perform (PUP) list. P.J. Locke is the only active Broncos safety who logged triple-digit defensive snaps last year, though he worryingly earned a 55.2 PFF coverage grade.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-jo.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports the Broncos and S Brandon Jones have agreed to a three-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-jo.analysis: According to Bleacher Report’s Jordan Schultz, Jones’ deal is worth $20 million, with a chance for him to move up to $22.5 million. The former Dolphin totaled 48 tackles and two interceptions last season and should have a chance to step in and replace Justin Simmons, who the team made a cap casualty last week. Jones was a third-round pick of the Dolphins back in 2020 and has started 30 of the 54 games he’s appeared in for his career.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-jo.headline: Dolphins S Brandon Jones (ACL) is out for the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-jo.analysis: Jones suffered the injury Sunday night against the Steelers. It’s a blow to an injury-riddled Dolphins secondary graded by PFF as the league’s fifth worst. Miami’s secondary should be as vulnerable as any in the NFL for the remainder of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-ko.headline: Charlie Kolar (concussion) is active for Week 11 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-ko.analysis: Kolar, David Njoku and Oronde Gadsden will form a three-player committee this afternoon. None of them warrant TE1 treatment, though they provide Justin Herbert with safety-blanket options and should help out in the run game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-ko.headline: Charlie Kolar (concussion) is questionable for Los Angeles’ Week 11 game against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-ko.analysis: Kolar had not practiced either of the first two days of the week before this sudden Friday revival where he got in a limited session. We’d be surprised if he ultimately played coming off a short week, but no Chargers tight end is ultimately compelling with or without Kolar in the lineup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-ko.headline: Charlie Kolar (concussion) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-ko.analysis: Kolar seemingly came out of the Chargers’ first win of the season with a concussion, though he was on the field up until making the game-sealing catch on the last drive. He will need to clear concussion protocol in order to be eligible for Week 11 against the Jets. Also not practicing was WR Brenen Thompson (hamstring). Neither player has fantasy impact, though Kolar’s blocking is important for a Chargers team with a banged-up offensive line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-ko.headline: Oronde Gadsden caught 2-of-3 targets for 17 yards in the Chargers’ Week 9 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-ko.analysis: Justin Herbert gave Gadsden a chance to get going downfield early on, but the pass clanged off his hands. The incompletion may ultimately have been erased by a penalty. Herbert looked his way again later, on the Chargers’ late two-point conversion attempt, but it failed. Charlie Kolar, meanwhile, caught 3-of-3 targets for 31 yards and rushed once for three yards. Neither player needs to be rostered in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-ko.headline: Charlies Kolar caught 3-of-5 targets for 20 yards in the Chargers’ Week 6 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-ko.analysis: Kolar ran 28 routes on the day while Oronde Gadsden II ran 24 routes and also had five targets from Justin Herbert. The division of pass-catching duties for LA’s tight ends make both players unplayable for fantasy outside the deepest formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-ko.headline: Charlie Kolar caught 3-of-4 targets for 37 yards with a lost fumble in the Chargers’ Week 5 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-ko.analysis: Kolar tied for the team lead in catches, and finished with the most receiving yards. Unfortunately, 19 of those came on the first play, and were followed by a fumble. Oronde Gadsden didn’t catch his only target and Hayden Rucci had just one catch — for a touchdown, to be fair — so Kolar sadly appears to be the one “reliable” receiving target for the Chargers’ tight end room. That doesn’t mean he’s a great fantasy play for Week 6 against the Chiefs, however. On the contrary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-ko.headline: Chargers TE Charlie Kolar (forearm) is questionable for Los Angeles’ Week 5 game against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-ko.analysis: Kolar has missed a few weeks with a broken forearm after having surgery on it; he appears close to returning. The Chargers are perhaps wondering, looking at their offensive line, if he can play tackle.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-ko.headline: Quentin Johnston (chest) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-ko.analysis: Johnston and TE Charlie Kolar (forearm) both remained limited today, though WR Brenen Thompson (quad) downgraded. He did not practice, nor did Ladd McConkey (foot). Tre’ Harris could end up being the Chargers’ No. 1 wide receiver, but he would only be a FLEX against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-ko.headline: Chargers WR Quentin Johnston (chest) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-ko.analysis: In addition to Johnston, TE Charlie Kolar (forearm) and WR Brenen Thompson (quad) were also limited. Johnston has played in every game this season, but pops up on the practice report with a chest issue on Wednesday. He is not yet in danger of missing Week 5, barring setbacks later in the week. Neither Thompson nor Kolar have played since Week 2 but both have a chance to return this week against the Broncos. With Ladd McConkey (foot) not practicing, Johnston may have fantasy value as the Chargers’ No. 1 wideout this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-ko.headline: Chargers TE Charlie Kolar (forearm) won’t play in Los Angeles’ Week 4 game against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-ko.analysis: He did rejoin practice today, making it plausible he’ll be up for the Chargers’ Week 5 game against the Broncos. Second-year receiving TE Oronde Gadsden was unable to seize the moment with Kolar and TE David Njoku (knee) sidelined last week, catching 0-of-3 targets. The once-promising youngster must do something on Sunday if he wishes to remain re-draft-relevant in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dante-trad.headline: Dolphins declared S Dante Trader Jr., CB Jaylin Simpson, P Bradley Pinion, OL Christian Haynes, OL Caedan Wallace, TE Justin Joly, and WR Jared Wayne inactive for Week 11 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dante-trad.analysis: Trader Jr. is the Dolphins’ starting strong safety, but the rest of the inactives are depth pieces. Simpson does see the field as a backup cornerback, so the Dolphins will be down two members of the secondary in a game against Josh Allen, which is never great news.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyrell-sha.headline: Tyrell Shavers (knee) is active and will make his season debut in Week 11 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyrell-sha.analysis: Shavers has been sidelined all season after tearing his ACL in a playoff win over Jacksonville last year. The 27-year-old had emerged as the team’s best blocking wide receiver last year and had seen his snap count increase as the season went on. He’s unlikely to be a fantasy factor, but it would not be surprising to see him play a decent amount of snaps once he is fully ramped up because of the value he provides in the running game. This means rookie Skyler Bell is back to being a game-day inactive.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyrell-sha.headline: Bills activated WR Tyrell Shavers (knee) from the reserve/PUP list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyrell-sha.analysis: Shavers tore his ACL in the playoffs last year and began the season on the PUP list. He was active for all 17 games last year and played a mix of offense and special teams. Shavers caught 23 passes for 245 yards and a touchdown in 2025. He will mix in as a depth option for Buffalo over the second half of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyrell-sha.headline: Bills placed Tyrell Shavers (knee) on the reserve/PUP list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyrell-sha.analysis: He’ll miss at least the first four weeks of the season after tearing his ACL in the playoffs. No surprise there. Shavers will likely be a late-season reinforcement, if that, in 2026 after coming on strong when the Bills needed receiving help last year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyrell-sha.headline: Bills placed WR Tyrell Shavers (knee) on the active/PUP list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyrell-sha.analysis: After tearing his ACL in early January, Shavers is a good bet to wind up on reserve/PUP at the conclusion of training camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyrell-sha.headline: Bills coach Sean McDermott said WR Tyrell Shavers (knee) tore his ACL and will miss the remainder of the playoffs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyrell-sha.analysis: Shavers actually played 22 of the team’s snaps in the second half on the torn ACL, which is absurd. The 26-year-old heads to the offseason as unlikely to play early in the season due to how late this knee injury was suffered. He had a career-best 15/245/1 receiving line on 23 targets in the 2025 season, starting nine games and being sporadically useful when the team got annoyed with mercurial second-year receiver Keon Coleman. The Bills will need to rely on Coleman to give them something in the Divisional Round.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyrell-sha.headline: Tyrell Shavers (knee) returned to the Bills’ Wild Card Round game against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyrell-sha.analysis: Shavers left in the second quarter with the knee issue. He went to the locker room and the team listed him as questionable to return. Shavers was back on the field coming out of halftime, giving the Bills some extra receiver depth for the final two quarters.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyrell-sha.headline: Bills WR Tyrell Shavers (knee) is questionable to return in the Wild Card Round against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyrell-sha.analysis: Shavers injured his left knee while on punt coverage in the second quarter. He quickly left for the locker room and was listed as questionable to return. With Josh Palmer now on IR, the Bills would be forced to lean on Keon Coleman, Gabe Davis, and Brandin Cooks for wide receiver snaps if Shavers is done for the day. Bills S Jordan Poyer (hamstring) is also questionable to return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyrell-sha.headline: Tyrell Shavers caught 2-of-3 targets for 36 yards in the Bills’ 13-12, Week 17 loss to the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyrell-sha.analysis: Shavers made a massive 32-yard catch in traffic down the sideline to put the Bills in the red zone late in the third quarter. They would wind up getting stuffed on the one-yard line and turning the ball over on downs, but it was a really nice catch in traffic for the young receiver, who has emerged as a key part of the Bills’ wide receiver corps due to his run blocking and special teams ability. He may be the only receiver, in addition to Khalil Shakir, who feels like a lock to be on the Bills next season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyrell-sha.headline: Bills declared WR Keon Coleman, TE Dalton Kincaid, WR Curtis Samuel, DT Phidarian Mathis, OL Chase Lundt and DB Ja’Marcus Ingram inactive for Week 12 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyrell-sha.analysis: This will be Coleman’s fourth occasion missing game time due to disciplinary reasons in less than two years in the NFL. Kincaid (hamstring) and Samuel (elbow/neck) are both out due to injury. With Coleman out last week, the Bills relied on a wide receiver rotation including Khalil Shakir, Tyrell Shavers, Gabe Davis, Mecole Hardman, Joshua Palmer and Samuel. Hardman has since been placed on injured reserve. A heavy rotation is still expected against the Texans’ elite pass defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyrell-sha.headline: Tyrell Shavers caught 4-of-5 targets for 90 yards and a touchdown in a Week 11 win over the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyrell-sha.analysis: With Keon Coleman inactive for disciplinary reasons, it was Shavers who saw the biggest increase in playing time and usage. The 26-year-old did most of his damage on a 43-yard broken play touchdown, where he got behind the defense, but he also caught a few huge 20-plus yard passes throughout the game. We can’t expect this moving forward, but he’s certainly worth an add in deeper formats in case Keon Coleman’s disciplinary punishment lasts beyond one week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Saints declared LB Pete Werner, CB Martin Emerson Jr., RB Audric Estime, OT Asim Richards, OT Taliese Fuaga, C Erik McCoy, and QB Zach Wilson inactive for Week 11 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Estime was seeing nearly half of the Saints’ backfield snaps up to last week. With Travis Etienne ramping back up from injury, the Saints choose to deactivate Estime, keeping Etienne as the primary back, Alvin Kamara as the pass-catching back, and rookie CJ Donaldson as the third-string in what has been a frustrating committee for fantasy purposes. Zach Wilson is the emergency third quarterback while Werner (hamstring), Emerson (concussion), Richards (knee), Fuaga (knee), and McCoy (biceps) are all out with injury, leaving the offensive line and defense short-handed against the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Audric Estime had seven rushes for six yards in the Saints’ Week 10 loss to the Panthers, adding one catch for one yard.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Estime was shockingly ineffective a week after he led the Saints backfield with 15 rushing attempts for 72 yards and a touchdown. Travis Etienne returned from injury this week and operated as the nominal RB1 for the disastrous New Orleans offense. Estime won’t hold any fantasy value as long as Etienne is healthy and active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Travis Etienne (hamstring) resumed practicing on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Coming off injured reserve, Etienne can practice for 21 days before the Saints must officially either activate him or shut him down. The Saints’ No. 1 running back has been sidelined since unsuccessfully trying to play through a hamstring strain in Week 3 against the Raiders. Audric Estime could warrant RB2/FLEX treatment again this week if Etienne is not ready to face the Panthers on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Audric Estime rushed 15 times for 72 yards and a touchdown in the Saints’ Week 9 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Estime was waived by the Browns on Monday. The Saints claimed him on Tuesday and he was their starting back by Sunday. Life comes at you fast. Kellen Moore made it a point to get Estime going early with three carries for him on their first three plays of the game. He gashed the Browns 32 yards on those three attempts alone. He would later punch in a goal line touchdown to give the Saints the lead in the fourth quarter. Estime will be the Saints’ lead runner until Travis Etienne is activated from injured reserve. That could happen as soon as Week 10, so fantasy managers shouldn’t count on another usable week from Estime anytime soon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Audric Estime rushed nine times for 19 yards and a touchdown in the Browns’ Week 6 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: It wasn’t an overly impressive day for Estime, who was on the Vikings’ practice squad earlier in the week. But in the fourth quarter, with the Browns trailing 10-3, Estime took back-to-back carries for six yards, with his second resulting in a two-yard touchdown that would tie the game with just over eight minutes left in regulation. Estime could see a similar role in next week’s game against the Titans if Quinshon Judkins (ankle) misses another game, but he’ll be hard to trust as far as fantasy is concerned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Browns signed RB Audric Estime from the Vikings’ practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Estime’s signing comes as Quinshon Judkins is dealing with an ankle injury he suffered in Week 5. Estime, who is only 23 years old, already feels like an NFL journeyman as he now heads to his fifth team in three seasons after brief stints with the Broncos, Eagles, Saints, and Vikings. The former fifth-round pick has rushed for 508 yards and three touchdowns in his career and rushed for 76-310-2 as a rookie with the Broncos. Estime could see snaps in Week 6 against the Ravens if Judkins is unable to play, but we wouldn’t expect to see anything close to a meaningful workload at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Saints placed Kelvin Banks (ankle) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The team signed long snapper Cal Adomitis and reached an injury settlement with running back Audric Estime in corresponding moves. Banks is undergoing surgery for a severe high-ankle sprain. He could return later this year, but the team will be without their starting left tackle for at least four games, and likely much longer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Saints RB Alvin Kamara (knee) is questionable to play in Week 1 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Kamara logged two limited sessions to begin the week, and New Orleans Football’s Nick Underhill said he thinks Kamara will play, barring a setback. We do not yet know Kamara’s practice participation level on Friday, but he is traveling with the team, which is a good sign. Kamara would be a PPR FLEX if active. He is expected to play on passing downs while starting RB Travis Etienne leads the team in carries. Etienne is the best bet to handle the primary red zone role, but Kamara has been a prolific touchdown scorer over his career and could factor in. The Saints ruled out RB Audric Estime (thigh).

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Saints RB Kendre Miller (back) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Saints’ backup running back statuses continue to change. Veteran No. 2 RB Alvin Kamara (knee) is expected to be sidelined for at least one month, and RB Audric Estime is now sidelined with an undisclosed injury. Miller and RB Devin Neal (hamstring) both returned this week, though. Beat reporter Jeff Nowak notes that Miller, Neal and RB Ty Chandler were all allowed to rotate in for first-team reps today, as coach Kellen Moore presumably seeks out a viable primary backup for starting RB Travis Etienne. Per Nowak, Miller “looks sharp despite the time missed.” This is worth tracking for short-term bench stash purposes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Saints RB Kendre Miller (back) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The good news is that Miller was not listed with a knee injury after suffering a season-ending ACL tear in Week 7 last year. The bad news is that he evidently has a new injury, and the Saints have a fairly deep running back room right now. RBs Devin Neal, Audric Estime, Ty Chandler and CJ Donaldson are all vying for roster spots. Per Underhill, Neal is taking advantage of the extra reps. He could have the inside track to the RB3 role right now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nicholas-s.headline: Titans declared RB Nicholas Singleton, LB Mohamoud Diabate, CB Jaylon Jones, DT Jackie Marshall and OT Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson inactive for Week 11 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nicholas-s.analysis: With Tyjae Spears on injured reserve, it’s a poor sign for fifth-round rookie Singleton that he is still getting healthy scratched in Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nicholas-s.headline: Titans coach Robert Saleh said Michael Carter was active over rookie Nick Singleton because “Michael has three-down value with regards to protections and being able to understand how to play the game on third down.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nicholas-s.analysis: Nick Singleton is “still growing in that regard,” per Saleh. It sounds like Singleton may need to wait for a Tony Pollard trade to open up early-down carries if he’s going to be active this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nicholas-s.headline: Tyjae Spears (ankle) is questionable for Tennessee’s Week 3 game against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nicholas-s.analysis: He did return for a limited session on Friday, but it doesn’t look like it’s a sure thing he plays in Week 3. Titans head coach Robert Saleh said Nick Singleton could get more opportunities in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nicholas-s.headline: Titans RB Tony Pollard (ankle) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nicholas-s.analysis: We were told earlier today that Pollard and Spears are “dealing with some soreness.” Now we know what ails them. The Titans field an unexciting offense, but on the off chance that both Pollard and Spears are unable to play, rookie RB Nicholas Singleton would theoretically be in line for a sizable workload against the Giants this week. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nicholas-s.headline: Sports Illustrated’s Nick Arvin anticipates the Titans using “a more balanced committee approach” in the backfield this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nicholas-s.analysis: Arvin writes that Tony Pollard is expected to remain the lead back, but he thinks a committee approach could be in order, with the additions of fifth-round pick Nicholas Singleton and the continued presence of Tyjae Spears. On June 11, Titans coach Robert Saleh referred to Pollard and Spears as “the bellcows of this football team,” and said Singleton will have to “compete his way” into the rotation. The Titans have had just three practices since Saleh’s remarks. Pollard remains the top back in Tennessee. Spears is penciled in on passing downs and might get the chance to play a small role on early downs as well. Singleton’s role is murky. It would be reasonable for the Titans to limit a fifth-round rookie to special teams only.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nicholas-s.headline: The Nashville Post’s John Glennon believes Titans RB Tony Pollard and RB Tyjae Spears’ futures with the team, beyond 2026, are “uncertain.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nicholas-s.analysis: Both Pollard and Spears are entering contract years. Pollard, 29, has missed just one game over the past two seasons, while Spears, 24, has missed nine. Spears also entered the NFL with concerns regarding one of his knees, which has full thickness cartilage loss and is missing its ACL. Pollard has been far more productive than Spears, who acknowledges he needs to prove his consistency to the coaching staff, but Pollard’s age is working against him. Both players appear locked into the top-two spots on the depth chart, but Glennon thinks it’s “not a huge stretch to see” RB Nicholas Singleton becoming the team’s primary ball-carrier in 2027. Of course, we are a long way from having an answer to this. The Titans’ backfield developments in training camp are worth following, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nicholas-s.headline: Titans team reporter Jim Wyatt said RB Nicholas Singleton “has been getting more and more work” and is “impressed” by what he’s seen from Singleton so far.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nicholas-s.analysis: Singleton broke the fifth metatarsal in his right foot at the Senior Bowl, so the team has had to slowly add more to the rookie running back’s workload over the last few weeks. He reportedly worked more on Tuesday than he has at any point this offseason. That said, Titans coach Robert Saleh spoke with the media on Thursday and referred to RBs Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears as “the bellcows.” He adds that Singleton is big, fast and “learning it all,” but he must “compete his way” into the running back group.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nicholas-s.headline: Titans signed fifth-round pick RB Nicholas Singleton to a four-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nicholas-s.analysis: Singleton has decent odds of making the roster as the Titans’ RB3 and special teams returner. Where he goes from there remains to be seen. He flashed high-end, dual-threat traits in college, but ceded snaps to the reliable rusher, RB Kaytron Allen. Singleton’s boom-bust style has its strengths and weaknesses.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nicholas-s.headline: Titans selected Penn State RB Nicholas Singleton with the No. 165 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nicholas-s.analysis: The top running back recruit of the 2022 class, Singleton (6’/219) burst onto the scene as a true freshman with 1,061 yards at a staggering 6.8 yards per carry. He split work with fellow newcomer Kayton Allen and that would never change during his four years at Penn State. Though his role on the ground never improved much, Singleton exploded as a receiver in his sophomore and junior seasons. He caught 26 passes for 308 yards and two scores in 2023 and jumped to 41 grabs for 375 yards with five touchdowns in 2024. Penn State’s entire football program fell apart in Singleton’s final season and he was held to just 549 yards on the ground and 219 through the air. Singleton has the top gear you would expect from someone with over 1,100 career kick return yards, but he goes down on first contact rather easily. He’s a straight-line runner whose calling card in the NFL will be his speed and pass-catching prowess. At his size, that’s an interesting skill set to have.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nicholas-s.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that Penn State RB Nicholas Singleton (foot) “has been medically cleared and has resumed running.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nicholas-s.analysis: Singleton broke the fifth metatarsal in his right foot at the Senior Bowl, which required surgery and prevented him from participating in pre-draft workouts. Per Schefter, Singleton “projects to be a mid-round pick next week.” Hopefully for Singleton’s sake and fantasy purposes, that means Round 3 rather than Rounds 4 or 5. He is an explosive dual-threat player with good size, though analysts typically knock his vision.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.headline: Sione Vaki (ankle) is active for Week 11 against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.analysis: Vaki will continue to back up Jahmyr Gibbs, though that role hasn’t produced much fantasy value this year. He will only see a meaningful amount of touches if the Lions blow out the Bucs, which could happen. Vaki is buried in the RB5 ranks for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.headline: Sione Vaki rushed six times for 28 yards in the Lions’ Week 10 win over the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.analysis: Vaki operated as the RB2 once again. Three of his carries came on the Lions’ penultimate drive, though Jared Goff was still on the field. Dan Campbell pulled his starters for the team’s final possession and Jacob Saylors closed out the game. Vaki is the backup fantasy managers should roster as Jahmyr Gibbs insurance, but he doesn’t hold any standalone fantasy value.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ribs) is active for Week 10 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.analysis: No surprise here. St. Brown is good to go as a mid-range WR1 for Week 10. Sione Vaki is also active. Inactive for the Lions are CB D.J. Reed, C Cade Mays, DB Keith Abney II, LB Amen Ogbongbemiga, DT Mekhi Wingo, and EDGE Ahmed Hassanein.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.headline: Sione Vaki (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.analysis: Vaki sat out on Wednesday and Thursday before practicing in a limited capacity on Friday. He remains a worthwhile stash as the Lions’ No. 2 running back. His backup, Jacob Saylors (neck/hamstring), is good to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.headline: Sione Vaki (ankle) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.analysis: Vaki played through the injury last week, and should be expected to do so again against the Patriots this week. Fellow backup RB Jacob Saylors (neck/hamstring) is practicing in full. Vaki is the team’s top backup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ribs) is active for Week 9 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.analysis: No surprises here as this was reported earlier today. St. Brown remains a top-flight WR1 for his matchup with the Phins. Sione Vaki is also active and will serve as the team’s RB2. Inactive for the Lions are CB D.J. Reed, EDGE DJ Wonnum, C Cade Mays, RB Jacob Saylors, TE Jordan Meeks, DL Mekhi Wingo, and EDGE Ahmed Hassanein.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.headline: Sione Vaki (ankle) is questionable for Week 9 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.analysis: Vaki and Lions RB3 Jacob Saylors (neck) are both questionable. Vaki did not practice on Friday, having apparently suffered a new injury. Saylors was limited all week. Jahmyr Gibbs should handle his normal, sizable workload.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.headline: Sione Vaki had 11 rushes for 65 yards in the Lions’ Week 8 win against the Vikings, adding one catch for five yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.analysis: It was the first time this year Vaki has seen more than six carries. The Lions went ultra run-heavy in this one to combat the Vikings’ vexing blitz scheme, which led to 35 carries on the day. Vaki should be stashed in most formats in cae Jahmyr Gibbs misses any time in the coming weeks. Vaki would be a potential 20-touch weekly option in such a scenario.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs (shoulder) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.analysis: A DNP to open the week would normally be concerning, but Dan Campbell told reporters earlier today that he was going to get a lot of players “off their feet” during today’s practice. Gibbs appeared to injure his leg while awkwardly sliding to the ground on his final carry of Week 7. The fact that he isn’t listed with a leg injury on today’s report is also a good sign. Sione Vaki is the next man up if Gibbs can’t play this week, but we aren’t overly concerned quite yet. Tomorrow’s injury report will be more telling.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Isiah Pacheco (back) could return in early December.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.analysis: According to Rapoport, Pacheco “had surgery to remove a body that was pressing on a nerve in his back.” The 27-year-old back is looking at a 12-week recovery, but if all goes well, he could return for the final month of the season. If the Lions don’t add anybody to their backfield in the coming days/weeks, Sione Vaki and Jacob Saylors will continue to serve as the primary backups behind Jahmyr Gibbs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marlon-hum.headline: Ravens declared CB Marlon Humphrey, FS Jaylinn Hawkins, RB Adam Randall, OG Emery Jones, DT Nnamdi Madubuike, and QB Kedon Slovis inactive for Week 11 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marlon-hum.analysis: Humphrey, Madubuike, and Hawkins were all ruled out before the weekend. The Ravens will look to end a five-game skid in Jacoby Brissett’s second start with the team and face a Panthers defense that is near the bottom of the league at stopping the run, which could bode well for Derrick Henry and a ground game that has been stagnant in recent weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marlon-hum.headline: The Baltimore Ravens sent Marlon Humphrey home and he will be inactive for Week 11.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marlon-hum.analysis: Humphrey was asked what the city of Baltimore was good at making on his personal podcast, The Marlon Humphrey Show. He jokingly responded, “They’re the best at making criminals.” Humphrey has since apologized for the disparaging remark, but the team is dismissing him for the week after a wave of backlash. He could potentially return in Week 12 against Houston.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marlon-hum.headline: Cam Jurgens (concussion) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marlon-hum.analysis: Jurgens still has a chance to play, but we had hoped to see him upgrade to full participation. Ravens EDGE Mike Green (hamstring) was added to the injury report today as a limited participant. Ravens OG Andrew Vorhees (foot) joins him in the limited column. Ravens RT Roger Rosengarten (knee), LT Ronnie Stanley (rest/toe/ankle) and CB Marlon Humphrey (hamstring/calf) upgraded to full participation. Ravens OG John Simpson (groin) downgraded to a DNP.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marlon-hum.headline: Cam Jurgens (concussion) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marlon-hum.analysis: The Ravens’ new starting center is still recovering from his recent concussion, but he seemingly has a chance to face the Browns this week. Ravens EDGE Trey Hendrickson (finger) and S Kyle Hamilton (stinger) are practicing fully, while RT Roger Rosengarten (knee), OG John Simpson (groin), OG Andrew Vorhees (foot), LT Ronnie Stanley (rest/toe/ankle) and CB Marlon Humphrey (hamstring/calf) were limited.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marlon-hum.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Marlon Humphrey (hamstring/calf) is expected to play in Week 5 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marlon-hum.analysis: Humphrey logged one limited practice this week before being listed as questionable for Week 5. He’s one of several key defenders dealing with an injury heading into Sunday Night Football. EDGE Trey Hendrickson has already been ruled out, while S Kyle Hamilton is questionable with a groin injury. Even with some missing names, this defense still looks like a true test for Michael Penix.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marlon-hum.headline: Ravens coach Jesse Minter said CB Nate Wiggins and CB Marlon Humphrey “are trending very well to potentially be back next week.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marlon-hum.analysis: Wiggins was carted away on Tuesday, and Humphrey walked off with trainers on Wednesday. Minter’s phrasing is obviously non-committal, but it does seem like the Ravens’ starting cornerbacks will return before long.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marlon-hum.headline: Ravens WR Rashod Bateman (illness) is questionable for Baltimore’s Week 18 game against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marlon-hum.analysis: Bateman hasn’t practiced all week, but John Harbaugh said he believes both Bateman and Marlon Humphrey (illness — also questionable) to be cleared by game time on Sunday. Bateman has barely cracked the fantasy radar all season and would be hard to trust if he was healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marlon-hum.headline: Ravens CB Marlon Humphrey (finger) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 12 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marlon-hum.analysis: He didn’t even miss a practice after being sidelined ahead of Week 11’s game with the Browns. Humphrey will return and help limit the Jets’ new-look passing game in Week 12.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marlon-hum.headline: Ravens HC John Harbaugh said he is optimistic that Marlon Humphrey (finger) will be able to play in Week 12 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marlon-hum.analysis: Humphrey underwent a minor procedure last week that sidelined him for Week 11 against the Browns. He was never expected to miss more than a game or two, so Harbaugh’s early optimism that he could return in Week 12 doesn’t come as a surprise. Humphrey has played on 272 coverage snaps this season, per PFF, breaking up four passes while also forcing one interception.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marlon-hum.headline: Ravens HC John Harbaugh said Marlon Humphrey (finger) may need surgery.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marlon-hum.analysis: According to Harbaugh, Humphrey would likely miss one or two games if he did need surgery. The team is still weighing that decision, but with games against the Browns and Jets on tap over the next two weeks, it’s safe to say the Ravens can afford to be without Humphrey if he does opt for surgery. Humphrey has struggled in coverage this season, allowing 32 receptions for 461 yards and two touchdowns on 45 targets, but did notch his first interception of the season in Week 10’s win over the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Drake Maye (fractured fibula) is expected to miss at least six weeks.
