https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: A six-week absence would technically allow Maye to return late in the regular season, but Rapoport then followed up by saying he has an “outside chance” at playing if the Pats make the playoffs. We suspect the Patriots would, at most, use the final weeks of the regular season to get Maye back on the practice field. Tommy DeVito is currently their starting quarterback and they’re sitting at 5-5, so a playoff berth doesn’t appear to be in the cards. Rapoport also mentioned Daniel Jones as an option in Maye’s absence. We doubt he saves New England’s season, but he would be an upgrade over DeVito.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: ESPN’s Mike Reiss believes signing Daniel Jones could be an option for the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: Drake Maye has been diagnosed with a fractured fibula and is expected to be sidelined “deep” into the regular season. Tommy DeVito replaces him as the team’s starter. He is backed up by seventh-round rookie Behren Morton, who has reportedly “made a positive impression.” Jones has played poorly this year, prompting a surprise release earlier today. Despite the poor play, Jones still might be able to outplay DeVito and the late-Day 3 rookie. Assuming Jones passes through waivers, he could make sense as an affordable bridge option for the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Drake Maye fractured his fibula and it is expected to sideline him “deep into the regular season if he is able to return this year at all.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: Maye is being given the Jaxson Dart Memorial Puncher’s Chance of returning, but it doesn’t look likely that he’ll return this year and, if you were holding out hope for whatever reason, he can be dropped in most re-draft leagues at this time. Maye won’t have to undergo surgery and there was no additional ligament damage. The Patriots may choose to not put Maye on injured reserve because they are already near the limit of how many players they can designate to return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport believes “it would be a surprise” if Drake Maye (ankle) played again this year.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: Rapoport said that Maye would not play for the “foreseeable future” and noted that though the Patriots have not confirmed that Maye fractured his ankle, almost all of the reporting points to that reality. We’re all waiting for the Patriots to actually confirm this, which won’t happen any time soon because they’re on bye, but Maye can be dropped with little fear in shallow redraft leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Drake Maye is believed to have suffered a fractured ankle in Week 10’s loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: According to Schefter, Maye stayed overnight in Germany to undergo testing and determine whether or not he would need surgery. For now, Maye is out indefinitely, but the 24-year-old QB and 2025 MVP runner-up could be looking at missing the rest of the season for the now 5-5 Patriots. His absence would force the Patriots to start Tommy DeVito in Week 12 against the Chargers, which would all but spell disaster for all Patriots skill players from a fantasy perspective. DeVito completed 12-of-24 passes for 81 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in Sunday’s loss and has a career passing line of 1,450-9-4 in 15 career games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports it’s “possible” Drake Maye (lower leg) misses the rest of the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: Per Rapoport, Maye suffered a “significant lower leg injury that will keep him out an extended period of time.” It’s devastating news for Patriots fans and fantasy managers. While Maye has had his ups and downs this year, the team was nonfunctional without him on Sunday. Tommy DeVito took over for an injured Maye early in the first quarter and threw for 81 yards at 3.4 yards per attempt. The Pats also have seventh-round rookie Behren Morton on the roster. We suspect DeVito will get another shot at the starting job, but it wouldn’t be surprising to see Morton under center at some point this year. With A.J. Brown also banged up and Romeo Doubs still on IR, the Pats are shaping up to be a fantasy wasteland over the second half of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: NBC Sports’ Pro Football Talk’s Mike Florio reports that the Patriots expect Drake Maye (ankle) to be sidelined for “a while.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: Maye injured his ankle in the first quarter against the Lions today and was unable to return. We expect more updates to follow after Maye undergoes further testing once the team returns from Germany. The Patriots go on bye in Week 11, but it sounds like the early indications are that Maye will be sidelined beyond that. They face the Chargers in Week 12 and the division-rival Bills in Week 13.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: Drake Maye (ankle) will not return in Week 10 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: Aidan Hutchinson hip-drop tackled Maye for a sack early in the first quarter. Maye limped off the field and made his way to the locker room shortly after going down. He was initially listed as questionable to return but has since been downgraded to out. A dreaded high-ankle sprain appears to be on the table right now. The good news is that the Patriots get their bye next week, which will give Maye some extra time to recover. Tommy DeVito will close out Week 10 under center.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: Drake Maye (ankle) is questionable to return in Week 10 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: Maye’s ankle rolled while he was being sacked early in the first quarter. He initially appeared ready to play through it, but Maye walked to the locker room at the start of the Pats’ next drive. The fact that Maye was able to walk off under his own power, albeit with a slight limp, is at least a good sign. Tommy DeVito is under center for the Pats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: Drake Maye completed 21-of-38 passes for 299 yards, three touchdowns, and three interceptions in the Patriots’ 45-27, Week 9 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: Maye’s three first-half interceptions but the Patriots in the hole early, but the defenses’ inability to limit explosive plays also didn’t do them any favors. The Patriots saw three of their first six drives end in interceptions, but Maye did what he could to keep the game within reach. He completed his first touchdown pass of the day to Rhamondre Stevenson, who broke free down field for the 30-yard score in the second quarter. and on the following drive, Maye would complete passes of 19 and 28 yards to set up Efton Chism for an eight-yard touchdown with less than three minutes to go in the half. His third and final touchdown would come on a 22-yard pass to Mack Hollins, but Maye and the Patriots were under duress all afternoon and struggled to keep up with a Packers offense that didn’t slow down until it pulled it’s starters late in the fourth quarter. Maye also took four sacks in this one and has now been sacked nine times in his last three games. He’ll look to bounce back next week against the Lions in Munich.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Davante Adams sounds like a “long shot” to play in Week 13 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Adams isn’t expected to play in Week 12. The Rams get the Packers on Wednesday before Thanksgiving, and the tight turnaround makes a Week 12 return all but impossible. Head coach Sean McVay said Week 13 against Kansas City was a “possibility” earlier this week. That sounds unlikely now as well. Rapoport said Adams is eyeing a mid-December return. With Puka Nacua done for the year, the Rams are down to Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell as their top wide receivers for at least a few more weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Rams head coach Sean McVay said “there is a possibility” Davante Adams (hamstring) plays in Week 13 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins reported last week that the Rams were “hopeful” this would be the timeline for Adams’ return. McVay somewhat confirmed that optimism while speaking to the media on Friday, but noted that the star receiver isn’t “ready quite yet.” This follows McVay announcing that Puka Nacua (knee) will miss the next few months after MCL surgery, so it’s safe to assume the Rams will be thin at receiver in Week 12 when they take on the Packers on Thanksgiving Eve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins reports that the Rams are “hopeful” that Davante Adams (hamstring) will return for Week 13 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Over the next three weeks, the Rams face the Cardinals, go on bye and then face the Packers. While his potential return ahead of the fantasy football playoffs is helpful, we still have a long way to go before he returns, and even then, his status for Week 13 is still uncertain. Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell and CJ Daniels appear to be in line for 11 personnel duties at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said Davante Adams (hamstring) successfully underwent surgery, and his return timeline is “probably closer” to the shorter end of the expected 6-10 week timeline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: If Adams hit the absolute soonest return date, week-wise, he theoretically could face the Chiefs in Week 13, but that game takes place on Thursday night. We suspect facing the 49ers in Week 14 is more likely, though nothing is guaranteed for a 33-year-old player. Adams should be stashed in injured reserve spots, where possible. He makes for a tough cut in leagues without them.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said the team is still determining “the best time” to schedule Davante Adams’ (hamstring) “cleanup” procedure.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Surgeries are sometimes delayed to help reduce swelling. Occasionally, new information is gathered during this time and/or during the surgery. Adams is currently expected to be sidelined for 6-10 weeks. Perhaps the wide return-to-play timeline is due to the fact that the surgeon has not yet fully assessed the injury. We tentatively expect the team to share an updated recovery timeline once Adams undergoes the procedure on his ruptured hamstring tendon. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said the Rams have not had discussions about bringing in a receiver with Davante Adams (hamstring) sidelined for 6-10 weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Earlier today, ESPN’s Dan Graziano reported that the Rams “will at least explore the possibility of trading for a wide receiver.” Obviously, McVay doesn’t want to tip off other wide receiver-needy NFL teams about their potential entrance into the trade market, and he has no reason to be honest with us. Acquiring a new wide receiver makes sense, and the Rams were aggressive players in the trade market last offseason. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: ESPN’s Dan Graziano reports that the Rams “will at least explore the possibility of trading for a wide receiver.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Adams is set to undergo a procedure after rupturing his hamstring tendon in Week 6 against the Cardinals. He will be sidelined for 6-10 weeks. The Rams were already very thin at wide receiver and Puka Nacua has spent multiple weeks on the injury report as well. Acquiring a capable wide receiver makes sense, but as Graziano mentions, the Rams have already traded away a lot of their draft capital. Thus far, GM Les Snead has already given up their 2027 first- and third-round picks, and their 2028 second-round pick and their 2029 third-round pick. He notes that Rams QB Stetson Bennett played for Browns coach Todd Monken in college. Perhaps Monken would be interested in a reunion.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said Davante Adams (hamstring) will miss 6-10 weeks with a ruptured tendon.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Adams had a non-contact injury at the end of Week 6’s loss to the Cardinals and unfortunately is as serious as it appeared. He’ll likely be placed on injured reserve ahead of Week 7. His absence will further focus targets on Puka Nacua and likely elevate Konata Mumpfield into a bigger role. Adams had put together a 30/480/4 line in his first six games of the season. Adams will reportedly have surgery to “clean” out the tendon, per NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, in hopes he can return around the team’s bye week, which is scheduled for Week 11. It’s a major blow for a Rams team that is already reeling at 2-4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Davante Adams 3-of-4 targets for 39 yards in the Rams’ Week 6 loss to the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Adams appeared to injure his left knee while running a route in the red zone on the Rams’ final possession. He cut, turned upfield and quickly began limping his way to the back of the end zone, removing himself from the play while grabbing at the inside of his left knee. He subbed himself out after that. No word on his status, but we expect an update soon. Prior to that, the Cardinals’ pass rush made life tough on the Rams’ passing attack. Adams caught his first pass a minute and a half into the second quarter. Stafford was looking his way in the end zone later on the same drive, but Josh Sweat got to him for the strip-sack. Adams banked 16-yard receptions on the sixth and seventh drives, impressively getting wide open via a downfield out route on the second one. If Adams escaped with a minor injury, he would be a WR2 against the Raiders next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Davante Adams caught 5-of-7 targets for 51 yards and two touchdowns in the Rams’ Week 5 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Adams cashed in on a corner fade from four yards out in the second quarter and ran a beautiful route on a double move slant from five yards out for his second score in the fourth quarter, proving that he remains an elite red zone weapon for an offense that has now attempted 51 or more passes in three straight games. Adams is back to modest target rates following the Week 4 return of Puka Nacua but remains a weekly WR2 due to his red zone acumen, which remains true ahead of a much more forgiving matchup against the Cardinals in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Puka Nacua (MCL surgery) will be sidelined 4-5 months.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: This confirms Nacua will not only miss the remainder of the regular season, but would be unavailable for any potential Super Bowl run for the pre-season favorites. Schefter did add that Nacua’s knee “checked out clean aside from the MCL.” That’s good news heading into Nacua’s potential free agency, though he is nevertheless at a low ebb in his up-and-down Rams tenure. The ups have been any time Nacua takes the field. The downs have been how often he has been sidelined, as well as his off-the-field issues. Going on 26, Nacua would make a lot of sense as a franchise tag candidate, or perhaps a tag-and-trade for the cap-leveraged Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler described Rams WR Puka Nacua’s future with the team as “very uncertain.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: Nothing earth-shattering here from Fowler. Appearing on ESPN’s SportsCenter Saturday morning, the NFL Insider noted that Nacua is dealing with a significant MCL injury and a three-game suspension from the NFL. With Nacua unlikely to return this season, Fowler says this isn’t the kind of momentum the 25-year-old receiver wanted heading into free agency, where he’ll be the best player available. The Rams can extend him, franchise tag him or let him hit the open market this offseason. As Fowler says, it’s something the Rams have to sort out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Puka Nacua’s (knee/toe) recovery timeline “does not match up” with a potential return for Super Bowl LXI.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: Nacua is currently on injured reserve, recovering from MCL and PCL sprains, along with a turf toe injury. He will also serve a three-game suspension on injured reserve, following the Rams’ Week 11 bye. The superstar wide receiver underwent surgery to repair his MCL on Tuesday, and Rapoport believes we have “almost certainly” seen the last of Nacua in the 2026 season. He is set to enter free agency this offseason, and it is unclear whether the Rams will extend him, franchise tag him or allow him to walk.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: Rams head coach Sean McVay said Puka Nacua will undergo surgery on his MCL and will be out “a couple months.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: Shortly after it was reported that Nacua “will undergo” surgery, we learned that the star receiver actually had surgery on Tuesday. We don’t know exactly how long Nacua will miss, but it’s safe to assume his only path back for the 2026 season would be if the Rams make a run in the postseason. Even then, his recovery timeline could be too long for a late-January/early-February return. The 25-year-old receiver was in the midst of another stellar season for the Rams, catching 70 passes for 715 yards and four touchdowns in the seven games he appeared in. Nacua is in the final year of his four-year rookie contract and is on track to receive a lucrative payday this offseason, presumably from the Rams. An offseason marred by off-the-field issues and a stint at a rehab facility likely delayed the decision to extend him before training camp, but Nacua continues to play at an elite level on the field. If all goes well, it sounds like he should be healed well ahead of training camp next offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that Puka Nacua will serve a three-game suspension for violating the league’s personal conduct policy while on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: Schefter notes that the timing of Nacua’s suspension “could potentially save him a substantial amount of money.” Suspended players are not paid, and Nacua is in the final year of his rookie contract. Serving the suspension now “will cost him a lot less than serving it on his next contract, which is expected to be far more lucrative.” Schefter does not say whether he thinks the Rams will be the team that pays him, but a big payday is apparently still expected. Players are required to miss four games on injured reserve. Nacua has already missed one game. The Rams are on bye this week. He will spend the remainder of his injured reserve stint while also serving his suspension, and he will be eligible to return for Week 15 against the Cowboys. Nacua will be allowed to rehab his injuries at the Rams’ facility for the suspension’s final two weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said Puka Nacua’s (knee/toe) return timeline has not changed.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: A few days ago, McVay told reporters that Nacua would not be placed on injured reserve due to transaction limitations, so it was a bit surprising to see him land there yesterday. The move prompted some concern. He was initially expected to return in Week 14 or 15, and he will officially be eligible to return on the latter date against the Cowboys. As of today, he is on track to do so, just in time for the fantasy football playoffs. Nacua should not be dropped in any format. He will be a WR1 upon returning.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: Rams placed Puka Nacua on injured reserve with knee and toe injuries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: Nacua will be eligible to return for the Rams’ Week 15 game against the Cowboys. The Rams are on bye in Week 11, and he is required to miss at least four games. It was previously reported that Nacua was expected to return in Week 14 or 15. Shortly before the team made this announcement, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said that the team was “confident” Nacua would return in that timeframe. Rams coach Sean McVay previously said that the Rams would not place him on injured reserve due to transaction limitations. It is unclear whether anything has changed. Nacua suffered PCL and MCL sprains, along with a turf toe injury in Week 10 against the Commanders. ESPN’s Adam Schefter specifically cited Nacua’s MCL sprain after the move was made, adding that McVay said Nacua will miss “extended time.” Nacua should be stashed on fantasy football benches at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: Sean McVay said Puka Nacua (knee, toe) will not be placed on injured reserve for roster mechanics reasons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: The Rams are running out of return from IR designations. Putting Nacua on injured reserve would prevent another player from coming back later in the season, so he will simply take up a 53-man roster spot while he recovers. McVay made it clear that Nacua will still be out for a while. Nacua is expected to return at some point this year, though whether or not the Rams are still in the playoff hunt once he’s healthy could factor into the timeline.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: ESPN’s Dan Graziano reports Puka Nacua (knee, toe) will not miss the rest of the regular season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: Graziano said there’s an outside chance the Rams won’t put Nacua on injured reserve ahead of Week 10. Rams sources “were very adamant that Nacua’s injury isn’t season-ending and that they hope to get him back around that Week 14, Week 15 time.” With Davante Adams (hamstring) also sidelined, look for the Rams offense to be unusually run heavy in the coming weeks. That should mean more work for Kyren Williams and Blake Corum. Tyler Higbee and Colby Parkinson could see an uptick in targets too. If Terrance Ferguson (hamstring) is ever able to return to game action, he could profile as the team’s top target. Nacua had seen 44 percent of the Rams’ first-read targets this season, the highest rate in the NFL.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: Rams head coach Sean McVay said Puka Nacua (knee/turf toe) is likely headed to injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: An MRI on Monday revealed a sprained MCL and PCL for Nacua, who also suffered a turf toe injury on the Rams’ final offensive play in Sunday’s win over the Commanders. Nacua caught 14 passes for 150 yards and a touchdown in the win, drawing a target on 44.2 percent of Stafford’s pass attempts. It goes without saying that this creates a massive problem for a Rams passing game that has failed to find a serviceable WR2 sans Davante Adams (hamstring). Now, McVay and company will be faced with a new challenge as they try to replace Nacua with the likes of Tutu Atwell, Jordan Whittington, Konata Mumpfield, or a player not yet on the roster. Long believed to be buyers ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline, it seems like a foregone conclusion that GM Les Snead will do what he can to acquire a playmaker for Matthew Stafford with whatever draft picks he still has at his disposal. The Rams currently only hold one pick in the first three rounds of the 2027 NFL Draft but still hold their first-round picks in 2028 and 2029, per Spotrac.com.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.headline: Andrei Iosivas (thumb) is doubtful for Week 11 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.analysis: Iosivas was practicing in full throughout the week, making his designation somewhat puzzling as he attempts to return from injured reserve. The team will have another week to activate the young wide receiver before he will be forced to remain on injured reserve for the remainder of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.headline: Andrei Iosivas (thumb) is practicing in full for Week 11 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.analysis: Iosivas is seemingly on track to play in Week 11’s Monday Night Football game against the Commanders, but he does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats. Ja’Marr Chase, Tee Higgins (knee), Chase Brown and Mike Gesicki are playing very well in the receiving game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.headline: Andrei Iosivas (thumb) is doubtful to play in Week 10 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.analysis: Iosivas is still technically on injured reserve, although the team designated him to return this week. Fellow injured reserve players, CB Jalen Davis (hamstring) and OG Brian Parker (knee), are also listed as doubtful. Bengals S Kyle Dugger (quad) has been ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.headline: Bengals designated Andrei Iosivas (thumb) to return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.analysis: Iosivas will practice today for the first time since injuring his thumb in Week 2. The Bengals have 21 days to officially activate him from injured reserve, though he practiced in full today. He will likely reclaim his No. 3 role once healthy, though we don’t expect much fantasy value to come of it.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.headline: Bengals placed Andrei Iosivas (thumb) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.analysis: Head coach Zac Taylor said Iosivas is expected to return at some point this year. Colbie Young and Dohnte Meyers will both be in the running for the WR3 role, though it’s not a role that produces fantasy points unless one of Tee Higgins or Ja’Marr Chase goes down.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.headline: Andrei Iosivas caught his only target for seven yards in Cincinnati’s Week 2 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.analysis: He played 32-of-60 snaps as the Bengals have spread the ball around, letting Colvie Young (1/7 on one target) and Dohnte Meyers (0/0 on one target) also get involved against the Texans. Iosivas looks like a poor FLEX risk in Week 3 against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.headline: Bengals WR Andrei Iosivas caught 2-of-2 targets for 20 yards in Thursday’s preseason game against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.analysis: Iosivas was on the field for two drives, taking 10 of the first 13 snaps and playing alongside QB Joe Burrow. Fourth-round rookie WR Colbie Young subbed in, taking one snap on the second drive and remained on the field after the starters left. He looked good hauling in a 20-yard gain on 3rd-and-16 from QB Joe Flacco. The battle for the Bengals’ WR3 role continues with Iosivas seemingly ahead of the rookie.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.headline: The Athletic’s Paul Dehner Jr. reports that WR Colbie Young and WR Andrei Iosivas are still competing for the Bengals’ WR3 role.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.analysis: Young, the rookie, “has seemingly stacked at least one impressive catch per day.” Iosivas has had “a few notable drops,” but he reportedly “appears as polished and athletic as ever at getting open.” Both players could be worth late-round picks in best ball formats, but neither one is likely to return FLEX value in re-draft without WR1 Ja’Marr Chase or WR2 Tee Higgins missing time. Iosivas is entering a contract year, and the team just spent a fourth-round pick on Young. An in-season breakout from the rookie would make things easier from a salary cap perspective. Dehner also notes that former CFL WR Dohnte Meyers “has been a talk of camp” thus far.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.headline: ESPN’s Ben Baby reports that Bengals rookie WR Colbie Young is competing for OC Dan Pitcher’s “passing target No. 3" role.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.analysis: Baby’s practice notes indicate that incumbent No. 3 WR Andrei Iosivas and No. 1 TE Mike Gesicki are the other two competitors for the role, and both players “had productive springs.” Pitcher also said RB Chase Brown “can sometimes be viewed as a slot receiver,” but those types of comments are common in the summer and rarely pan out in the fall. Iosivas and Gesicki have been helpful contributors, but the fact that the team is searching for an answer at the No. 3 receiving role is indicative of their ceilings. Pitcher believes Young is “going to fight and battle” this summer, and thinks there are things Young “can do quickly and help us.” If he can actually become the team’s third-most voluminous target earner, he could pay off as a late-round best ball pick.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.headline: The Athletic’s Paul Dehner Jr. believes the Bengals will add competition for Andrei Iosivas’ No. 3 receiver role.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrei-ios.analysis: This isn’t a front-page headline or anything, but OC Dan Pitcher did say that Iosivas “would probably tell you that there were points last year that he was happy with his play and points where he felt he needed to be better.” Entering the final year of his rookie contract, Iosivas could be pushed by Mitchell Tinsley or a draft pick for playing time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Eagles placed WR Dontayvion Wicks (ankle/foot) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: Wicks has already missed the previous three games with an ankle injury and now finds himself sent to injured reserve, meaning he will miss at least seven games total with poorly timed injuries. He saw a “foot” designation added to his status during a week of limited showings, which is presumably the issue that lands him on injured reserve. DeVonta Smith, who returns from an extended absence this week, Makai Lemon, and Darius Cooper are likely to hold down the starting wide receiver positions in Wicks’ absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle/foot) will not play in Philadelphia’s Week 11 game against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: Wicks got in three limited sessions, but notably had the “foot” ailment attached to him after it only being listed as an “ankle” the last two days. It’s possible this is nothing major and the Eagles are just taking it easy with him, but a new injury should be on the radar. Wicks has little fantasy utility either way at this stage.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: Wicks is stuck in the questionable column, but he still has a chance to play. With QB3 Joe Milton at the helm, Wicks would only be a WR4/5 against the Steelers in Week 11. He does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Donatyvion Wicks (ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: Head coach Nick Sirianni told reporters he feels “pretty good” about Wicks and DeVonta Smith (hamstring) returning this week. Unfortunately for both wideouts, they will rejoin an offense now led by Joe Milton. With Smith commanding a massive target share and Makai Lemon in the mix for opportunities, Wicks will be relegated to the WR5 ranks if he suits up this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Eagles coach Nick Sirianni said he feels “pretty good” about Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) returning for Week 11 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: The bigger headline is that Sirianni said this about DeVonta Smith as well. Wicks was making the occasional splash play before going down with the ankle injury. That, however, was while Jalen Hurts was healthy. We don’t expect him to be a consistent fantasy option with Joe Milton now under center for the Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Eagles ruled out Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) for Week 9 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: Wicks and DeVonta Smith (hamstring) will both miss this weekend’s game, before taking the week off next week as well. The Eagles go on bye in Week 10. Hopefully, the added rest will allow Wicks to be healthy down the stretch.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: At this point, fantasy managers should expect Wicks to take the field next in Week 11, following the Eagles’ Week 10 bye. He does not need to be held on 12-team rosters at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) was not seen at the start of Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: Wicks hasn’t played or practiced since Week 6. It doesn’t look like he has much of a shot at suiting up this week. With a Week 10 bye up next, fantasy managers in even the deepest of leagues can cut Wicks loose.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) will not play in Philadelphia’s Week 8 game against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: He didn’t practice all week and has not practiced since the build up to Week 6. As with colleague DeVonta Smith, Wicks enters next week questionable to play and with the Eagles having a Week 10 bye, we wouldn’t be surprised if Wicks sat that game out as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) was not spotted at Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: Wicks has not practiced since before Week 6’s loss to the Panthers and should be seen as doubtful heading into Friday’s practice session. We’d be surprised if he played in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Titans placed RB Tyjae Spears (knee) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: Spears will now miss the next four games, at minimum, as he tends to a knee injury that has plagued him in recent weeks. Spears previously missed two games in Week 7 and Week 8 before returning to a modest workload in Week 9 after the team’s bye. Tony Pollard should continue operating in a true workhorse role and gets one of the top matchups in the league against the Cowboys in Week 11. Fantasy managers can continue to treat Pollard as a volume-driven RB1 after a slow start to the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) is questionable for Tennessee’s Week 11 game against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: Spears hit the questionable line with this knee injury in Week 10, Week 7 and Week 6 before this latest one. Given how similar the pathing looks to last week’s — as he also got in a full session ahead on Friday here — we think he’s more likely to play than not. He’s probably only a desperation FLEX play in a good matchup against the Cowboys busted run defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: It’s an upgrade from a Wednesday DNP. The Cowboys/Titans game has been looking like it’ll be a shootout if the Titans can keep up their end of the bargain, and six teams are on bye. Even with that, we still can’t muster much FLEX excitement for Spears as Tony Pollard’s backup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: It’s unclear if Spears aggravated his knee issue on Sunday or if this is just a maintenance day. Spears missed three weeks because of the knee issue before returning to action in week 10. He was held to five touches. Healthy or not, he is not on the fantasy radar ahead of Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears rushed four times for 28 yards in the Titans’ Week 10 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: Spears didn’t gain any yards on his only catch of the day. Tony Pollard, on the other hand, caught eight passes and rushed nine times. Spears missed three weeks with a knee issue and likely had his snaps limited by the team today.
